nodes.name: test_landcover_render.py
nodes.body_text: """WorldCover through the whole renderer: OSM wins, the rest grows by class.""" import contextlib import io import os import tempfile import unittest import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from generator import renderer from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.rendering import landcover as L from generator.rendering.projection import Projector SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST = 40.0, -85.0, 40.0040, -84.9948 if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: latlon
nodes.body_text: def latlon(proj, fx, fy): """The lat/lon of a fraction of the way across and down the map.""" lat = NORTH - (NORTH - SOUTH) * fy lon = WEST + (EAST - WEST) * fx return lat, lon

nodes.name: box
nodes.signature: def box(proj, x0, y0, x1, y1)
nodes.body_text: def box(proj, x0, y0, x1, y1): pts = [latlon(proj, x0, y0), latlon(proj, x1, y0), latlon(proj, x1, y1), latlon(proj, x0, y1)] return pts + [pts[0]]

nodes.name: features
nodes.body_text: def features(proj): return [ OSMFeature(1, "way", {"highway": "residential"}, [latlon(proj, 0.0, 0.5), latlon(proj, 1.0, 0.5)]), OSMFeature(2, "way", {"landuse": "residential"}, box(proj, 0.05, 0.05, 0.4, 0.4)), OSMFeature(3, "way", {"landuse": "farmland"}, box(proj, 0.6, 0.05, 0.95, 0.4)), ]

nodes.name: grid_for
nodes.body_text: def grid_for(width, height, bounds=None): grid = np.full((height, width), 30, dtype="uint8") grid[:, : width // 2] = 10 grid[height // 2:, width // 2:] = 40 return grid

nodes.name: render
nodes.body_text: def render(landcover_for, feats=None, **kw): proj = Projector.build(SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST, 1.0, 0.0) out = tempfile.mkdtemp() with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): renderer.render(features(proj) if feats is None else feats, SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST, meters_per_tile=1.0, output_dir=out, map_name="wc", landcover_for=landcover_for, **kw) land = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(out, "wc.bmp")).convert("RGB")) veg = np.asarray(Image.open(os.path.join(out, "wc_veg.bmp")).convert("RGB")) return proj, land, veg

nodes.name: is_
nodes.body_text: def is_(arr, *colours): out = np.zeros(arr.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for colour in colours: out |= np.all(arr == colour, axis=2) return out

nodes.name: region
nodes.signature: def region(proj, x0, y0, x1, y1)
nodes.body_text: def region(proj, x0, y0, x1, y1): (la0, lo0), (la1, lo1) = latlon(proj, x0, y0), latlon(proj, x1, y1) px0, py0 = proj.to_px(la0, lo0) px1, py1 = proj.to_px(la1, lo1) return slice(int(py0), int(py1)), slice(int(px0), int(px1))

nodes.name: RenderWorldCoverTest
nodes.body_text: class RenderWorldCoverTest(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.proj, cls.land, cls.veg = render(grid_for) def test_no_marker_left(self): self.assertFalse(is_(self.land, *L.MARKER.values()).any()) def test_tree_cover_is_a_wood(self): ys, xs = region(self.proj, 0.05, 0.6, 0.45, 0.95) trees = is_(self.veg[ys, xs], C.TREES, C.TREES_DARK_GRASS, C.SPARSE_TREES, C.TREE_BIG, C.TREE_HUGE, C.TREE_GIANT, C.TREE_SMALL) self.assertGreater(trees.mean(), 0.5) def test_osm_residential_is_not_a_wood(self): ys, xs = region(self.proj, 0.1, 0.1, 0.35, 0.35) trees = is_(self.veg[ys, xs], C.TREES, C.TREES_DARK_GRASS) self.assertLess(trees.mean(), 0.2) self.assertTrue(is_(self.land[ys, xs], C.MEDIUM_GRASS).mean() > 0.5) def test_cropland_and_osm_farmland_are_fields(self): for area in ((0.6, 0.6, 0.95, 0.95), (0.65, 0.1, 0.9, 0.35)): ys, xs = region(self.proj, *area) furrow = is_(self.land[ys, xs], C.DIRT_ROWS_H, C.DIRT_ROWS_V) self.assertGreater(furrow.mean(), 0.3, area) def test_road_stays_clear(self): road = is_(self.land, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE) # The road runs edge to edge of the bbox (the map is padded to whole # cells past it): no field or wood cut it. self.assertGreater(road.mean(axis=1).max(), 0.7) grown = is_(self.veg, C.CORN_1, C.CORN_2, C.TREES, C.TREES_DARK_GRASS, C.SPARSE_TREES, C.BUSHES, C.ROCKS, C.BOULDERS) self.assertFalse((grown & road).any()) def test_asks_for_what_the_image_covers(self): asked = {} def spy(width, height, bounds=None): asked["bounds"] = bounds return grid_for(width, height) proj, _, _ = render(spy) s, w, n, e = asked["bounds"] # Padded to whole cells: the image reaches past the bbox on every side. self.assertLess(s, SOUTH) self.assertLess(w, WEST) self.assertGreater(n, NORTH) self.assertGreater(e, EAST) self.assertEqual((s, w, n, e), proj.latlon_bbox()) def test_no_made_up_woods_on_worldcover_grass(self): def grass(width, height, bounds=None): return np.full((height, width), 30, dtype="uint8") proj, _, veg = render(grass) # Below the road nothing is mapped: only WorldCover's grassland. ys, xs = region(proj, 0.0, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0) trees = is_(veg[ys, xs], C.TREES, C.TREES_DARK_GRASS, C.TREE_BIG, C.TREE_HUGE, C.TREE_GIANT) self.assertFalse(trees.any()) def test_made_up_woods_without_worldcover(self): proj, _, veg = render(None) ys, xs = region(proj, 0.0, 0.55, 1.0, 1.0) trees = is_(veg[ys, xs], C.TREES, C.TREES_DARK_GRASS) self.assertTrue(trees.any()) def test_relief_bands_grass_but_not_water_or_cropland(self): # A slope rising to the east: its upper bands are flat ground colours, # which on WorldCover's lake or cropland would erase it. def lake_field_grass(width, height, bounds=None): grid = np.full((height, width), 30, dtype="uint8") grid[: height // 3, width // 2:] = 80 grid[height // 3: 2 * height // 3, width // 2:] = 40 return grid slope = np.tile(np.linspace(0, 200, 64, dtype="float32"), (64, 1)) proj, land, _ = render(lake_field_grass, feats=[], elevation=slope, elevation_span=(0.0, 200.0)) ys, xs = region(proj, 0.75, 0.05, 0.95, 0.25) self.assertGreater(is_(land[ys, xs], C.WATER).mean(), 0.95) ys, xs = region(proj, 0.75, 0.4, 0.95, 0.6) self.assertGreater(is_(land[ys, xs], C.DIRT_ROWS_H, C.DIRT_ROWS_V).mean(), 0.3) # ...while the grassland up there is banded. ys, xs = region(proj, 0.75, 0.7, 0.95, 0.95) self.assertLess(is_(land[ys, xs], C.MEDIUM_GRASS).mean(), 0.9) def test_broken_landcover_still_renders(self): def broken(w, h, bounds=None): raise RuntimeError("no data") _, land, _ = render(broken) self.assertFalse(is_(land, *L.MARKER.values()).any())

nodes.body_text: """WorldCover lands where it really is, on a turned map and an upright one.""" import unittest import numpy as np from generator.rendering import landcover as L from generator.rendering.projection import Projector SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST = 45.0, -69.0, 45.004, -68.994 if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: halves
nodes.body_text: def halves(width, height, bounds=None): """West of the bbox's middle meridian 10, east of it 30; north of its middle parallel adds 1 - so a tile's class says where it is.""" s, w, n, e = bounds lon = w + (np.arange(width) + 0.5) / width * (e - w) lat = n - (np.arange(height) + 0.5) / height * (n - s) grid = np.where(lon[None, :] < (WEST + EAST) / 2, 10, 30) grid = grid + (lat[:, None] > (SOUTH + NORTH) / 2) return grid.astype("uint8")

nodes.name: GridForMapTest
nodes.body_text: class GridForMapTest(unittest.TestCase): def check(self, rotation): proj = Projector.build(SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST, 1.0, rotation) grid = L.grid_for_map(halves, proj) self.assertEqual(grid.shape, (proj.height, proj.width)) rng = np.random.default_rng(1) px = rng.uniform(0, proj.width, 2000) py = rng.uniform(0, proj.height, 2000) lat, lon = proj.to_latlon_many(px, py) want = np.where(lon < (WEST + EAST) / 2, 10, 30) + (lat > (SOUTH + NORTH) / 2) got = grid[py.astype(int), px.astype(int)] # Off by a tile at most along the two dividing lines. self.assertGreater((got == want).mean(), 0.99) def test_upright(self): self.check(0.0) def test_turned(self): self.check(-11.5) self.check(30.0) def test_many_matches_one(self): proj = Projector.build(SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST, 1.0, 20.0) lat, lon = proj.to_latlon_many(np.array([10.0, 250.0]), np.array([30.0, 400.0])) for i, (x, y) in enumerate(((10.0, 30.0), (250.0, 400.0))): la, lo = proj.to_latlon(x, y) self.assertAlmostEqual(lat[i], la, places=9) self.assertAlmostEqual(lon[i], lo, places=9)

nodes.body_text: """What grows on each WorldCover class, on ground OSM left blank.""" import unittest import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from generator.rendering import landcover_veg as LV STRIPES = (10, 20, 30, 90, 60) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: setup
nodes.body_text: def setup(owned_all=True): grid = np.zeros((200, 250), dtype="uint8") for i, code in enumerate(STRIPES): grid[:, i * 50:(i + 1) * 50] = code owned = np.ones(grid.shape, dtype=bool) if not owned_all: owned[:100] = False land = Image.new("RGB", (250, 200), C.MEDIUM_GRASS) veg = Image.new("RGB", (250, 200), C.VEG_NOTHING) return grid, owned, land, veg

nodes.name: colours_in
nodes.body_text: def colours_in(img, cols): arr = np.asarray(img)[:, cols] return {tuple(int(v) for v in c) for c in np.unique(arr.reshape(-1, 3), axis=0)}

nodes.body_text: class PlantTest(unittest.TestCase): def test_each_class_gets_its_own(self): grid, owned, land, veg = setup() forest, counts = LV.plant_landcover(veg, land, grid, owned, P()) young = {C.TREE_SMALL, C.SPARSE_TREES} allowed = { 10: {C.VEG_NOTHING}, 20: {C.VEG_NOTHING, C.BUSHES} | young, 30: {C.VEG_NOTHING, C.SHORT_GRASS, C.BUSHES}, 90: {C.VEG_NOTHING, C.DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS, C.SPARSE_TREES}, 60: {C.VEG_NOTHING}, } for i, code in enumerate(STRIPES): got = colours_in(veg, slice(i * 50, (i + 1) * 50)) self.assertLessEqual(got, allowed[code], code) if code in (20, 30, 90): self.assertGreater(len(got), 1, code) self.assertTrue(forest[:, :50].all()) self.assertFalse(forest[:, 50:].any()) self.assertGreater(counts[20], 0) def test_marsh_sits_on_dark_grass(self): grid, owned, land, veg = setup() LV.plant_landcover(veg, land, grid, owned, P()) marsh = np.all(np.asarray(veg) == C.DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS, axis=2) self.assertTrue(np.all(np.asarray(land)[marsh] == C.DARK_GRASS)) def test_unowned_untouched(self): grid, owned, land, veg = setup(owned_all=False) forest, _ = LV.plant_landcover(veg, land, grid, owned, P()) self.assertFalse((np.asarray(veg)[:100] != 0).any()) self.assertFalse(forest[:100].any()) self.assertTrue(np.all(np.asarray(land)[:100] == C.MEDIUM_GRASS)) def test_density_zero(self): grid, owned, land, veg = setup() LV.plant_landcover(veg, land, grid, owned, P(), density=0.0) self.assertFalse((np.asarray(veg) != 0).any()) def test_keeps_what_is_there(self): grid, owned, land, veg = setup() veg.putpixel((60, 60), C.TREES) LV.plant_landcover(veg, land, grid, owned, P()) self.assertEqual(veg.getpixel((60, 60)), C.TREES) def test_deterministic(self): a = setup() b = setup() LV.plant_landcover(a[3], a[2], a[0], a[1], P()) LV.plant_landcover(b[3], b[2], b[0], b[1], P()) self.assertEqual(a[3].tobytes(), b[3].tobytes())

5, "N")]) _furnish(plan, random.Random(1)) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(plan.stalls), 2) compiled = buildtiles.parse_tbx(tbx.render_tbx(plan, "mall restroom")) tiles = buildtiles.level_tiles(compiled, 0) for x, y, facing in plan.stalls: front = (x, y + 1) if facing == "N" else (x + 1, y) door_sprite = "fixtures_bathroom_01_49" if facing == "N" else "fixtures_bathroom_01_48" self.assertIn(door_sprite, tiles[front]) def test_generated_mall_bathrooms_receive_stalls(self): for seed in range(3): plan = layout.build_building(79, 85, kind="mall", commercial=True, plan.stalls}, seed) def test_school_bathrooms_have_reachable_stalls(self): for seed in range(12): plan = layout.build_building(40, 32, kind="school", commercial=True, seed=seed).storeys[0] self.assertTrue(plan.stalls, seed) for x, y, facing in plan.stalls: room = plan.grid[y][x] self.assertIn(("toilet", x, y, facing), plan.furniture) dx, dy = (0, 1) if facing == "N" else (1, 0) front = (x + dx, y + dy) blocked = {cell for role, fx, fy, orient in plan.furniture if _blocks(role) for cell in _cells_for(role, fx, fy, orient)} self.assertNotIn(front, blocked) entrances = {cell for cell in _door_tiles(plan) if 0 <= cell[0] < plan.width and 0 <= cell[1] < plan.height and plan.grid[cell[1]][cell[0]] == room and cell not in blocked} reached = set(entrances) queue = deque(entrances) while queue: px, py = queue.popleft() for nx, ny in ((px-1, py), (px+1, py), (px, py-1), (px, py+1)): if (0 <= nx < plan.width and 0 <= ny < plan.height and plan.grid[ny][nx] == room and (nx, ny) not in blocked and (nx, ny) not in reached): reached.add((nx, ny)) queue.append((nx, ny)) self.assertIn(front, reached, (seed, x, y, facing)) def test_stall_walls_and_doors_compile_without_replacing_room_boundaries(self): for seed in range(6): building = layout.build_building(40, 32, kind="school", commercial=True, seed=seed) plan = building.storeys[0] parsed = buildtiles.parse_tbx(tbx.render_tbx(building, "school")) tiles = buildtiles.level_tiles(parsed, 0) for x, y, facing in plan.stalls: dx, dy = (0, 1) if facing == "N" else (1, 0) door = tiles[(x + dx, y + dy)] self.assertIn("fixtures_bathroom_01_49" if facing == "N" else "fixtures_bathroom_01_48", door) self.assertIn("fixtures_bathroom_01_42" if facing == "N" else "fixtures_bathroom_01_43", door) for obj in parsed.floors[0].objects: if obj.get("type") != "wall": continue x, y = int(obj["x"]), int(obj["y"]) ox, oy = (x - 1, y) if obj["dir"] == "N" else (x, y - 1) self.assertTrue(0 <= ox < plan.width and 0 <= oy < plan.height) self.assertEqual(plan.grid[y][x], plan.grid[oy][ox]) def test_homes_keep_regular_bathrooms(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 7, 5, kind="bathroom") plan = layout.Plan(8, 6, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 8 for _ in range(6)], kind="house", doors=[(4, 6, "N")]) _furnish(plan, random.Random(1)) self.assertFalse(plan.stalls) def test_large_public_bathroom_has_multiple_toilets_in_stalls(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 7, 5, kind="bathroom") plan = layout.Plan(8, 6, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 8 for _ in range(6)], kind="school", doors=[(4, 6, "N")]) _furnish(plan, random.Random(1)) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(plan.stalls), 2) self.assertEqual({(x, y) for role, x, y, orient in plan.furniture if role == "toilet"}, {(x, y) for nodes.name: app.py
nodes.body_text: """Knoxify — Flask entry point. Real-world areas → Project Zomboid maps. Run: source .venv/bin/activate python app.py Then open http://127.0.0.1:5000/ in a browser. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import sys import urllib.parse from flask import Flask, jsonify, render_template, request import knoxlog from web import (compiling, datasets, generation, geo, jobs, maps, presets, system, updates, zones) from web.common import _request_context, failed # Names the tests and tools/selftest.py reach through this module. The code # moved to web/; the old names still work for anything that reads them. from generator import osm # noqa: F401 from web.checks import (BIG_AREA_KM2, BIG_LANDMARK_KM2, BIG_TILES_PER_SIDE, # noqa: F401 MAX_METERS_PER_TILE, MIN_METERS_PER_TILE, RENDER_SETTINGS, _clean_shape, _too_big_for_memory, tidy_scale) from web.common import BASE_DIR # noqa: F401 from web.generation import generate # noqa: F401 from web.presets import MAX_PRESET_POINTS # noqa: F401 # Builds print place names in any script; a console on a legacy code page # would raise mid-request on the first one it cannot show. for _stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr): if hasattr(_stream, "reconfigure"): _stream.reconfigure(errors="replace") app = Flask(__name__, template_folder="templates", static_folder="static") # Only this PC may talk to the app. The server listens on 127.0.0.1, but a web # page in any browser on the PC can still point a hostname of its own at that # address ("DNS rebinding") and call the API as if it were the app's own page. # Such a request carries the attacker's hostname, so anything not addressed to # localhost is refused before it reaches a route. LOCAL_HOSTS = {"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "[::1]", "::1"} @app.errorhandler(Exception) @app.after_request @app.before_request @app.route("/") # ---- the routes: one blueprint per area, in web/ ---------------------------------- app.register_blueprint(jobs.bp) app.register_blueprint(updates.bp) app.register_blueprint(geo.bp) app.register_blueprint(system.bp) app.register_blueprint(presets.bp) app.register_blueprint(zones.bp) app.register_blueprint(compiling.bp) app.register_blueprint(generation.bp) app.register_blueprint(datasets.bp) app.register_blueprint(maps.bp) if __name__ == "__main__": port = int(os.environ.get("PORT", "5000")) app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=port, debug=False)

nodes.name: _api_error
nodes.body_text: def _api_error(exc): """Every failure as JSON the page can show, with the details in the log. Flask's default answer to an exception is an HTML page. The page reads every reply as JSON, so a crash anywhere in a request showed only "Unexpected token '<', "<!doctype"... is not valid JSON", which says nothing about what went wrong or where. """ from werkzeug.exceptions import HTTPException if isinstance(exc, HTTPException): if not request.path.startswith("/api/"): return exc return jsonify({"error": f"{exc.code} {exc.name}"}), exc.code return failed(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", 500, exc)

nodes.name: _log_refusals
nodes.body_text: def _log_refusals(response): """Every error the API answers with goes in the log, not just crashes: a "Missing or invalid bbox" is as much a clue as a traceback.""" if (request.path.startswith("/api/") and response.status_code >= 400 and response.is_json): data = response.get_json(silent=True) or {} if data.get("stopped"): return response # asked for; already in the log as a stop if not data.get("errorId"): eid = knoxlog.record(None, f"{request.method} {request.path} -> " f"{response.status_code}: {data.get('error')}", **_request_context()) data["errorId"] = eid response.set_data(json.dumps(data)) return response

nodes.name: _only_local
nodes.body_text: def _only_local(): host = (request.host or "").rsplit(":", 1)[0] if not (request.host or "").startswith("[") else (request.host or "").split("]")[0] + "]" if host not in LOCAL_HOSTS: return ("KnoxMap only answers requests from this computer.", 403) # A page open in the browser can send this server a plain POST with no body # (open the logs, restart for an update, change the language): the browser # allows it and the Host above is ours. Browsers say where such a request # came from, so one that came from somewhere else is refused. A request with # no Origin (the test client, curl) is not a browser's and passes. if request.method not in ("GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"): origin = request.headers.get("Origin") if origin is not None: try: origin_host = urllib.parse.urlparse(origin).hostname except ValueError: origin_host = None if origin_host not in LOCAL_HOSTS: return ("KnoxMap does not take requests from other websites.", 403) elif request.headers.get("Sec-Fetch-Site") == "cross-site": return ("KnoxMap does not take requests from other websites.", 403)

Adding a browser API to static/js means adding it here too - // which is the reminder that it is a browser API and not a KnoxMap one. module.exports = [ { files: ['static/js/**/*.js'], languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2022, // Scripts, not modules: index.html loads them in order and they share // globals through `window`. sourceType: 'script', globals: { // Libraries loaded by index.html before app.js. nodes.name: edits.py
nodes.body_text: """Changes to the features a map was built from, kept as a list of changes. A generated map is a reading of OpenStreetMap, and a reading is sometimes wrong: a shed the survey calls a house, a road that runs through where the mapper wants a square, a lake drawn round the wrong side of an island. Until now the only answer was to accept it, because the features came down from Overpass and went straight into the render. This holds what the mapper changed about them. Three kinds of change, each keyed by the feature's own OSM id: removed ids that are left out of the map altogether moved ids whose shape is replaced, as [(lat, lon), ...] tags ids whose tags are added to or overwritten They are kept as changes rather than as a copy of the edited features because a town is a hundred thousand features and almost all of them are untouched. The download stays exactly as it came, so an edit can be undone by dropping its line, and a re-download does not throw the editing away. Applying them is ordinary list work, so it costs nothing on a map with no edits and does not need the features to be in any particular order. """ from __future__ import annotations from dataclasses import replace from .osm import OSMFeature # What a page may set on an edited feature. The same list as a drawn one, plus # the tags that say what a building is: retagging a house as a shop is one of # the things this is for. Anything else is dropped - these tags reach # `classify` and the renderer, and a page should not be able to set whatever # it likes. EDITABLE_TAGS = { "building", "building:levels", "shop", "amenity", "leisure", "landuse", "natural", "highway", "railway", "waterway", "barrier", "name", "width", "bridge", "tunnel", "oneway", "layer", "surface", "area", }

nodes.name: empty
nodes.body_text: def empty() -> dict: return {"removed": [], "moved": {}, "tags": {}}

nodes.name: _as_list
nodes.body_text: def _as_list(value) -> list: return list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)) else []

nodes.name: _as_dict
nodes.body_text: def _as_dict(value) -> dict: return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}

nodes.name: clean
nodes.body_text: def clean(raw: dict | None) -> dict: """An edit list from untrusted input, with anything unusable left out. Untrusted means untrusted: this reads what the window posts and what is on disk beside the map, and a list where a table was expected - or a number where either was - threw rather than being left out, which is the one thing a cleaner must not do. """ raw = raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {} out = empty() for value in _as_list(raw.get("removed")): try: out["removed"].append(int(value)) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue for key, ring in _as_dict(raw.get("moved")).items(): try: osm_id = int(key) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue points = [] for point in _as_list(ring): try: lat, lon = float(point[0]), float(point[1]) except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError): points = [] break points.append((lat, lon)) # One point is not a way and two is not an area; either way there is # nothing to replace the original with. if len(points) >= 2: out["moved"][osm_id] = points for key, tags in _as_dict(raw.get("tags")).items(): try: osm_id = int(key) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue kept = {str(k): str(v) for k, v in _as_dict(tags).items() if k in EDITABLE_TAGS and v not in (None, "")} if kept: out["tags"][osm_id] = kept return out

nodes.name: count
nodes.body_text: def count(edits: dict | None) -> int: edits = edits or {} return (len(edits.get("removed") or []) + len(edits.get("moved") or {}) + len(edits.get("tags") or {}))

nodes.name: apply
nodes.signature: def apply(features: list[OSMFeature], edits: dict | None) -> tuple[list, dict]
nodes.body_text: def apply(features: list[OSMFeature], edits: dict | None) -> tuple[list, dict]: """The features as the mapper wants them, and what was actually used. What comes back is a new list; the features passed in are not touched, so the cached download stays the download. """ edits = clean(edits) removed = set(edits["removed"]) moved, tags = edits["moved"], edits["tags"] if not removed and not moved and not tags: return list(features), {"removed": 0, "moved": 0, "tags": 0} used = {"removed": 0, "moved": 0, "tags": 0} out = [] for feat in features: if feat.osm_id in removed: used["removed"] += 1 continue ring = moved.get(feat.osm_id) new_tags = tags.get(feat.osm_id) if ring is None and new_tags is None: out.append(feat) continue changed = feat if ring is not None: # A way that was closed stays closed: an area whose ring is left # open is not an area any more, and would be painted as a line. points = list(ring) was_closed = (len(feat.geometry) > 2 and feat.geometry[0] == feat.geometry[-1]) if was_closed and points[0] != points[-1]: points.append(points[0]) changed = replace(changed, geometry=points) used["moved"] += 1 if new_tags is not None: changed = replace(changed, tags={**feat.tags, **new_tags}) used["tags"] += 1 out.append(changed) return out, used

nodes.name: as_geojson
nodes.signature: def as_geojson(features: list[OSMFeature], bbox=None, limit: int = 0) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def as_geojson(features: list[OSMFeature], bbox=None, limit: int = 0) -> dict: """Features as GeoJSON for the window to edit, each carrying its own id. `bbox` is (south, west, north, east): only what touches it is sent, which is what keeps a town-sized map editable - a city is a hundred thousand features and a page cannot hold them. `limit` caps how many come back, largest first, so what arrives is what is worth editing. """ out = [] for feat in features: if feat.kind != "way" or len(feat.geometry) < 2: continue lats = [p[0] for p in feat.geometry] lons = [p[1] for p in feat.geometry] if bbox is not None: south, west, north, east = bbox if max(lats) < south or min(lats) > north: continue if max(lons) < west or min(lons) > east: continue closed = len(feat.geometry) > 2 and feat.geometry[0] == feat.geometry[-1] span = (max(lats) - min(lats)) * (max(lons) - min(lons)) ring = [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in feat.geometry] out.append((span, { "type": "Feature", "id": feat.osm_id, "properties": {"osm_id": feat.osm_id, "tags": dict(feat.tags)}, "geometry": ({"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [ring]} if closed else {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": ring}), })) total = len(out) if limit and total > limit: out.sort(key=lambda row: -row[0]) out = out[:limit] return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [row[1] for row in out], "total": total, "shown": len(out)}

nodes.name: extract.py
nodes.body_text: """Map data from a downloaded regional extract, not live Overpass queries. OpenStreetMap is published as flat files. Geofabrik cuts the planet into extracts by continent, country and state or province, and updates each one every day. Reading a map's worth of data out of one of those, on this PC, costs the shared Overpass servers nothing - which is what the people who run them ask of anything that fetches a whole town, a few hundred tiles at a time. The extract is downloaded once and kept (cache/extracts), checked for a newer copy at most every two weeks, and read with pyosmium using the same tag filters the Overpass query uses (generator.osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS). What comes out is the JSON Overpass would have answered with, so it goes through the same parser and nothing downstream can tell the difference. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import re import struct import tempfile import time import requests from shapely import from_wkb import knoxlog import knoxpaths import knoxstop GEOFABRIK_INDEX = "https://download.geofabrik.de/index-v1.json" INDEX_MAX_AGE_S = 30 * 86400.0 # How long an extract is used without asking Geofabrik whether it has a newer # one. They are rebuilt daily and nobody's map needs yesterday's changes. EXTRACT_MAX_AGE_S = 14 * 86400.0 # More extracts than this for one map means a box over half a continent. MAX_REGIONS = 6 # Above this a node-location table in memory would not fit; it goes to disk. BIG_EXTRACT_BYTES = 1_500_000_000 CHUNK = 1 << 20 CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S = 15 READ_TIMEOUT_S = 60 HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "KnoxMap/1.0 (+https://github.com/spytheeuclidean-a11y/knoxmap) " "local map generator (downloads regional extracts, cached)"} # ---- the Overpass filters, read back --------------------------------------------- _FILTER = re.compile(r'^(node|way|relation|nwr)((?:\[[^\]]+\])*)$') _COND = re.compile(r'\["([^"]+)"(?:(=|~)"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)")?\]') # ---- which extract covers a box ---------------------------------------------------- # ---- the download ------------------------------------------------------------------- # ---- reading it ---------------------------------------------------------------------

nodes.name: ExtractUnavailable
nodes.body_text: class ExtractUnavailable(RuntimeError): """The extract route cannot be taken here (no pyosmium, no extract covers the place, no way to download one). The caller may use Overpass instead."""

nodes.name: cache_dir
nodes.body_text: def cache_dir() -> str: return os.path.join(str(knoxpaths.BASE_DIR), "cache", "extracts")

nodes.name: _native_path
nodes.body_text: def _native_path(path: str) -> str: """Give libosmium an ASCII Windows path when the real path is Unicode.""" if os.name != "nt" or path.isascii(): return path import ctypes get_short = ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetShortPathNameW size = get_short(path, None, 0) if size: result = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(size) if get_short(path, result, size) and result.value.isascii(): return result.value raise ExtractUnavailable("Windows cannot provide a compatible path for the local extract; " "use Overpass or move KnoxMap to a folder with an ASCII path")

nodes.name: local_path
nodes.body_text: def local_path() -> str: """The extract a map developer picked, or "". `pbf_file` in knoxmap_config.json, or KNOXMAP_PBF_FILE in the environment. A regional extract is chosen for the map by asking Geofabrik which file covers the box; that is a guess about what the developer meant. Naming a file here takes the guess out: that file is read, and if it cannot be read the map stops rather than quietly asking the public servers instead. """ value = os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_PBF_FILE", "").strip() if not value: try: value = str(knoxpaths.load_config().get("pbf_file") or "").strip() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 value = "" if not value: return "" return os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(value))

nodes.name: local_region
nodes.body_text: def local_region() -> dict | None: """The picked extract as a region, or None when none is picked.""" path = local_path() if not path: return None return {"id": "local", "name": os.path.basename(path), "path": path, "local": True}

nodes.name: forced
nodes.body_text: def forced() -> bool: """True when a file was picked, so Overpass is not a fallback.""" return bool(local_path())

nodes.name: available
nodes.body_text: def available() -> bool: try: import osmium # noqa: F401 except ImportError: return False return True

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.body_text: class Filter: """One line of OVERPASS_FILTERS: which kinds, and the tag tests.""" def __init__(self, line: str): m = _FILTER.match(line.strip()) if not m: raise ValueError(f"unreadable filter: {line!r}") head = m.group(1) self.kinds = {"node", "way", "relation"} if head == "nwr" else {head} self.tests = [] for key, op, value in _COND.findall(m.group(2)): if op == "~": self.tests.append((key, re.compile(value))) elif op == "=": self.tests.append((key, value)) else: self.tests.append((key, None)) def matches(self, kind: str, tags) -> bool: if kind not in self.kinds: return False for key, want in self.tests: have = tags.get(key) if have is None: return False if want is None: continue if isinstance(want, str): if have != want: return False elif not want.search(have): return False return True

nodes.name: matches
nodes.signature: def matches(self, kind: str, tags) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def matches(self, kind: str, tags) -> bool: if kind not in self.kinds: return False for key, want in self.tests: have = tags.get(key) if have is None: return False if want is None: continue if isinstance(want, str): if have != want: return False elif not want.search(have): return False return True

nodes.name: parse_filters
nodes.body_text: def parse_filters(lines) -> list[Filter]: return [Filter(line) for line in lines]

nodes.name: wanted
nodes.signature: def wanted(filters: list[Filter], kind: str, tags) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def wanted(filters: list[Filter], kind: str, tags) -> bool: return any(f.matches(kind, tags) for f in filters)

nodes.name: _index
nodes.body_text: def _index(refresh_ok: bool = True) -> dict: path = os.path.join(cache_dir(), "geofabrik-index.json") fresh = os.path.exists(path) and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path) < INDEX_MAX_AGE_S if not fresh and refresh_ok: try: r = requests.get(GEOFABRIK_INDEX, headers=HEADERS, timeout=(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S, READ_TIMEOUT_S)) r.raise_for_status() data = r.json() os.makedirs(cache_dir(), exist_ok=True) with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(data, f) return data except (requests.RequestException, ValueError, OSError): pass try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f) except (OSError, ValueError): raise ExtractUnavailable("could not read Geofabrik's list of extracts " f"({GEOFABRIK_INDEX}) and none is saved") from None

nodes.name: regions_for
nodes.signature: def regions_for(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, index: dict) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def regions_for(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, index: dict) -> list[dict]: """The cheapest extract(s) that hold the whole box, as [{id, name, url}]: the smallest one that does, or - where a handful of smaller ones between them do it for less - those instead.""" from shapely.geometry import box, shape target = box(west, south, east, north) found = [] for feat in index.get("features", []): props = feat.get("properties") or {} url = (props.get("urls") or {}).get("pbf") geom = feat.get("geometry") if not url or not geom: continue try: poly = shape(geom).buffer(0) except (ValueError, TypeError): continue if poly.intersects(target): found.append({"id": props.get("id", ""), "name": props.get("name", ""), "parent": props.get("parent"), "url": url, "area": poly.area, "geom": poly, "covers": poly.covers(target)}) if not found: return [] # A box over a border is held by no single state, and the extract that does # hold it is the whole country: 12 GB of the United States for two counties # either side of the Ohio River, when Indiana and Kentucky (145 MB and # 148 MB) between them do it. So the children are weighed against the # parent: area stands in for bytes, which is close enough for the choice - # see the note below. parents = {r["parent"] for r in found} leaves = [r for r in found if r["id"] not in parents] or found leaves.sort(key=lambda r: r["area"]) together = _cover_with(leaves, target) covering = [r for r in found if r["covers"]] if covering: whole = min(covering, key=lambda r: r["area"]) if together and sum(r["area"] for r in together) < whole["area"]: return together return [whole] if together: return together # Nothing holds it all: the smallest few that touch it, as before. return leaves[:MAX_REGIONS] if len(leaves) <= MAX_REGIONS else []

nodes.name: _cover_with
nodes.body_text: def _cover_with(regions: list, target) -> list[dict]: """The few of `regions` - given smallest first - that between them hold the whole box, or [] if they cannot or it would take more than MAX_REGIONS. Greedy: take the smallest that adds anything, until nothing is left. It is not the optimal set, only a cheap one, and the areas are a stand-in for the files' sizes (the US polygon's runs far wider than its states' between them, which is the case this exists for).""" if not regions: return [] left = target chosen = [] for region in regions: if not region["geom"].intersects(left): continue chosen.append(region) left = left.difference(region["geom"]) if left.is_empty: return chosen if len(chosen) <= MAX_REGIONS else [] return []

nodes.name: _download
nodes.body_text: def _download(region: dict, say, should_stop) -> str: """The extract on disk, downloaded if there is none or it is two weeks old. A stale copy is used when Geofabrik cannot be reached. A region with a "path" is the file the developer picked: it is never downloaded.""" if region.get("path"): picked = os.path.abspath(region["path"]) if not os.path.isfile(picked): raise ExtractUnavailable(f"the extract you picked is not there: {picked}") if os.path.getsize(picked) == 0: raise ExtractUnavailable(f"the extract you picked is empty: {picked}") return picked os.makedirs(cache_dir(), exist_ok=True) safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "_", region["id"] or region["name"]) path = os.path.join(cache_dir(), f"{safe}.osm.pbf") have = os.path.exists(path) if have and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path) < EXTRACT_MAX_AGE_S: return path headers = dict(HEADERS) if have: headers["If-Modified-Since"] = time.strftime( "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT", time.gmtime(os.path.getmtime(path))) try: r = requests.get(region["url"], headers=headers, stream=True, timeout=(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S, READ_TIMEOUT_S)) if r.status_code == 304 and have: os.utime(path) # checked: good for another two weeks return path r.raise_for_status() total = int(r.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0) part = path + ".part" got = 0 with open(part, "wb") as f: for block in r.iter_content(CHUNK): knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the download") f.write(block) got += len(block) mb = got // (1 << 20) say(min(99, int(100 * got / total)) if total else 0, f"downloading the {region['name']} extract from Geofabrik, " f"{mb} of {total // (1 << 20)} MB" if total else f"downloading the {region['name']} extract from Geofabrik, {mb} MB") if total and got != total: raise OSError(f"the download stopped at {got} of {total} bytes") os.replace(part, path) return path except knoxstop.Stopped: raise except (requests.RequestException, OSError) as exc: if have: return path raise ExtractUnavailable( f"could not download the {region['name']} extract ({exc})") from None

nodes.name: _overlaps
nodes.signature: def _overlaps(b, south, west, north, east) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _overlaps(b, south, west, north, east) -> bool: return not (b[2] < south or b[0] > north or b[3] < west or b[1] > east)

nodes.name: _line_bounds
nodes.signature: def _line_bounds(hex_wkb: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]
nodes.body_text: def _line_bounds(hex_wkb: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]: """Bounds of the 2D LineString produced by osmium's WKBFactory. GEOS decoding a hex string for every distant way dominated a regional scan. Decode hex in C first; short lines need only four extrema, while long ones are faster in GEOS's binary reader. Neither creates point dicts. """ data = bytes.fromhex(hex_wkb) if len(data) < 9 or data[0] not in (0, 1): raise ValueError("invalid WKB LineString") order = "<" if data[0] else ">" kind, count = struct.unpack_from(order + "II", data, 1) if kind != 2 or not count or len(data) != 9 + count * 16: raise ValueError("expected a 2D WKB LineString") if count > 64: return from_wkb(data).bounds points = struct.unpack_from(f"{order}{count * 2}d", data, 9) xs, ys = points[::2], points[1::2] return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)

nodes.name: _read
nodes.signature: def _read(path: str, filters: list[Filter], bbox, say, should_stop) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def _read(path: str, filters: list[Filter], bbox, say, should_stop) -> list[dict]: """The elements of one extract that the filters want and that touch the box, as Overpass's `out geom` writes them.""" import osmium south, west, north, east = bbox big = os.path.getsize(path) > BIG_EXTRACT_BYTES path = _native_path(path) source = osmium.io.File(path, "pbf") index_file = None if big: index_file = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile( dir=cache_dir(), suffix=".nodes", delete=False) index_file.close() try: locations = f"sparse_file_array,{_native_path(index_file.name)}" except ExtractUnavailable: os.remove(index_file.name) raise else: locations = "flex_mem" elements: list[dict] = [] try: keys = sorted({key for f in filters for key, _want in f.tests}) factory = osmium.geom.WKBFactory() last_report = time.monotonic() def heartbeat(note): nonlocal last_report knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the download") now = time.monotonic() if now - last_report >= 1: # Object counts are not percentages of a compressed PBF. # The old estimate saturated at 70 (71 in the UI) and then # looked frozen for the rest of a hundred-million-node scan. say(None, note) last_report = now # 1. The relations, which come last in the file and are read on their # own: which ones the filters want, and which ways they are made of. say(None, "reading the relations") relations: dict[int, dict] = {} member_of: dict[int, list[int]] = {} for i, rel in enumerate(osmium.FileProcessor(source, osmium.osm.RELATION) .with_filter(osmium.filter.KeyFilter(*keys))): if i % 20000 == 0: knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the download") tags = dict(rel.tags) if not wanted(filters, "relation", tags): continue ways = [(m.ref, m.role) for m in rel.members if m.type == "w"] if not ways: continue relations[rel.id] = {"tags": tags, "members": ways} for ref, _role in ways: member_of.setdefault(ref, []).append(rel.id) # 2. Nodes and ways, with their places. A way is kept when it is wanted # and touches the box; a way a wanted relation is made of is kept for # the relation when it touches the box (the rest are fetched below if # the relation turns out to). say(None, "reading the map data") geometry: dict[int, list] = {} touches: set[int] = set() for i, obj in enumerate(osmium.FileProcessor(source, osmium.osm.NODE | osmium.osm.WAY) .with_locations(locations) .with_filter(osmium.filter.KeyFilter(*keys).enable_for(osmium.osm.NODE))): if i % 1000 == 0: heartbeat(f"reading the map data: {i:,} tagged nodes and ways checked") if obj.is_node(): if not obj.tags or not (south <= obj.location.lat <= north and west <= obj.location.lon <= east): continue if wanted(filters, "node", obj.tags): elements.append({"type": "node", "id": obj.id, "lat": obj.location.lat, "lon": obj.location.lon, "tags": {t.k: t.v for t in obj.tags}}) continue in_relation = obj.id in member_of if not obj.tags and not in_relation: continue # Reject distant ways in native code. Building a Python dict for # every vertex of every road/forest in the entire region used to # dominate this pass, even for a map of a few streets. try: min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat = _line_bounds(factory.create_linestring(obj)) except (RuntimeError, ValueError): pass # incomplete node locations: preserve the old fallback else: if not _overlaps((min_lat, min_lon, max_lat, max_lon), south, west, north, east): continue tags = dict(obj.tags) own = wanted(filters, "way", tags) if tags else False if not own and not in_relation: continue pts, lo_la, lo_lo, hi_la, hi_lo = [], 90.0, 180.0, -90.0, -180.0 for n in obj.nodes: if not n.location.valid(): continue la, lo = n.location.lat, n.location.lon pts.append({"lat": la, "lon": lo}) lo_la = min(lo_la, la) hi_la = max(hi_la, la) lo_lo = min(lo_lo, lo) hi_lo = max(hi_lo, lo) if not pts or not _overlaps((lo_la, lo_lo, hi_la, hi_lo), south, west, north, east): continue if own: elements.append({"type": "way", "id": obj.id, "tags": tags, "geometry": pts}) if in_relation: touches.add(obj.id) geometry[obj.id] = pts # 3. The relations that touch the box, with every member way in full: # the ones outside the box were not kept above. chosen = {rid for ref in touches for rid in member_of[ref]} missing = {ref for rid in chosen for ref, _r in relations[rid]["members"] if ref not in geometry} if missing: say(None, "reading the rest of the larger areas") # Nodes are read too, because the locations are built from them. for i, way in enumerate(osmium.FileProcessor(source, osmium.osm.NODE | osmium.osm.WAY) .with_locations(locations) .with_filter(osmium.filter.EntityFilter(osmium.osm.WAY)) .with_filter(osmium.filter.IdFilter(missing))): if i % 1000 == 0: knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the download") geometry[way.id] = [{"lat": n.location.lat, "lon": n.location.lon} for n in way.nodes if n.location.valid()] missing.discard(way.id) if not missing: break for rid in sorted(chosen): rel = relations[rid] members = [{"type": "way", "ref": ref, "role": role, "geometry": geometry[ref]} for ref, role in rel["members"] if geometry.get(ref)] if me

nodes.name: heartbeat
nodes.body_text: def heartbeat(note): nonlocal last_report knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the download") now = time.monotonic() if now - last_report >= 1: # Object counts are not percentages of a compressed PBF. # The old estimate saturated at 70 (71 in the UI) and then # looked frozen for the rest of a hundred-million-node scan. say(None, note) last_report = now

nodes.name: elements
nodes.signature: def elements(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, filters=None, progress=None, should_stop=None, regions=None) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def elements(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, filters=None, progress=None, should_stop=None, regions=None) -> list[dict]: """Everything the filters want inside the box, from the extract(s) that cover it - what Overpass would have answered with, as its JSON elements.""" from generator import osm if not available(): raise ExtractUnavailable("pyosmium is not installed (pip install osmium)") for name, value, limit in (("south", south, 90.0), ("north", north, 90.0), ("west", west, 180.0), ("east", east, 180.0)): if not -limit <= value <= limit: raise osm.OverpassError(f"{name}={value:g} is outside ±{limit:g}.") filters = parse_filters(filters if filters is not None else osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS) def say(pct: int | None, note: str) -> None: # File scans have no known object count; total=0 asks the UI for an # activity indicator instead of an invented completion percentage. osm._say(progress, pct + 1 if pct is not None else 0, 100 if pct is not None else 0, note) if regions is None: picked = local_region() if picked is not None: regions = [picked] # the developer named the file: use it else: say(None, "finding the OpenStreetMap extract that covers this place") regions = regions_for(south, west, north, east, _index()) if not regions: raise ExtractUnavailable("no Geofabrik extract covers this place") out: dict[tuple[str, int], dict] = {} for region in regions: path = _download(region, say, should_stop) say(None, f"reading the {region['name']} extract") try: found = _read(path, filters, (south, west, north, east), say, should_stop) except UnicodeDecodeError as exc: knoxlog.log.warning("osm: invalid UTF-8 in extract %s: %s", path, exc, exc_info=True) raise ExtractUnavailable( f"{os.path.basename(path)} contains text that is not valid UTF-8; " "download a fresh copy or use Overpass") from exc for el in found: out[(el["type"], el["id"])] = el return list(out.values())

nodes.name: features
nodes.signature: def features(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, progress=None, should_stop=None) -> list
nodes.body_text: def features(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, progress=None, should_stop=None) -> list: """OSMFeatures for the box, read from an extract (see the module docstring).""" from generator import osm return osm._parse({"elements": elements(south, west, north, east, progress=progress, should_stop=should_stop)})

nodes.name: msbuildings.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings from Microsoft's Global ML Building Footprints, where OSM has none. Overture's gap filling (generator/overture.py) draws on these same footprints but reaches them through DuckDB and two to three minutes of sifting metadata. Microsoft publishes them itself as plain files, one per quadkey tile, so this needs nothing installed: read the index, download only the tiles that cover the box, keep the footprints that touch it. Same ODbL licence as OSM. Everything after the fetch is shared with the Overture path: the rows become OSMFeatures through overture.to_features and are dropped where a mapped building already stands through overture.only_missing. A tile is about 30 MB gzipped (all of eastern Tennessee's Knox County sits in one), so the answer is cached beside the map like the Overpass one. """ from __future__ import annotations import csv import gzip import io import json import math import os import tempfile import time import urllib.request from . import overture from .osm import OSMFeature INDEX_URL = ("https://minedbuildings.z5.web.core.windows.net" "/global-buildings/dataset-links.csv") ZOOM = 9 # the index's tiles are level-9 quadkeys INDEX_MAX_AGE_S = 7 * 86400 # Microsoft re-publishes every few months TIMEOUT_S = 120 USER_AGENT = "KnoxMap (Project Zomboid map generator)"

nodes.name: cache_path
nodes.signature: def cache_path(output_dir: str, map_name: str) -> str
nodes.body_text: def cache_path(output_dir: str, map_name: str) -> str: return os.path.join(output_dir, f"{map_name}_microsoft.json.gz")

nodes.name: save_cache
nodes.signature: def save_cache(path: str, bbox, rows: list[dict]) -> None
nodes.body_text: def save_cache(path: str, bbox, rows: list[dict]) -> None: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or ".", exist_ok=True) with gzip.open(path, "wt", encoding="utf-8") as fh: json.dump({"source": "microsoft", "bbox": list(bbox), "buildings": rows}, fh)

nodes.name: load_cache
nodes.signature: def load_cache(path: str, bbox) -> list[dict] | None
nodes.body_text: def load_cache(path: str, bbox) -> list[dict] | None: if not os.path.exists(path): return None try: with gzip.open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8") as fh: payload = json.load(fh) except (OSError, ValueError): return None kept = payload.get("bbox") if not (isinstance(kept, list) and len(kept) == 4 and all(abs(a - b) < 1e-9 for a, b in zip(kept, bbox))): return None found = payload.get("buildings") return found if isinstance(found, list) else None

nodes.name: quadkeys
nodes.signature: def quadkeys(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, zoom: int = ZOOM) -> list[str]
nodes.body_text: def quadkeys(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, zoom: int = ZOOM) -> list[str]: """Every level-`zoom` Bing quadkey the box touches.""" def tile(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[int, int]: n = 2 ** zoom lat = max(-85.05112878, min(85.05112878, lat)) s = math.sin(math.radians(lat)) x = (lon + 180.0) / 360.0 * n y = (0.5 - math.log((1 + s) / (1 - s)) / (4 * math.pi)) * n return min(n - 1, max(0, int(x))), min(n - 1, max(0, int(y))) x0, y0 = tile(north, west) x1, y1 = tile(south, east) keys = [] for x in range(min(x0, x1), max(x0, x1) + 1): for y in range(min(y0, y1), max(y0, y1) + 1): key = "" for i in range(zoom, 0, -1): m = 1 << (i - 1) key += str((1 if x & m else 0) + (2 if y & m else 0)) keys.append(key) return keys

nodes.name: tile
nodes.signature: def tile(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def tile(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[int, int]: n = 2 ** zoom lat = max(-85.05112878, min(85.05112878, lat)) s = math.sin(math.radians(lat)) x = (lon + 180.0) / 360.0 * n y = (0.5 - math.log((1 + s) / (1 - s)) / (4 * math.pi)) * n return min(n - 1, max(0, int(x))), min(n - 1, max(0, int(y)))

nodes.name: _open
nodes.body_text: def _open(url: str): req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT}) return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT_S)

nodes.name: _index
nodes.body_text: def _index() -> dict[str, list[str]]: """quadkey -> tile urls, from the index, kept in the temp folder a week.""" path = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "knoxmap_ms_buildings_index.csv") fresh = (os.path.exists(path) and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path) < INDEX_MAX_AGE_S) if not fresh: with _open(INDEX_URL) as resp, open(path + ".part", "wb") as out: while chunk := resp.read(1 << 20): out.write(chunk) os.replace(path + ".part", path) table: dict[str, list[str]] = {} with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh: for row in csv.DictReader(fh): table.setdefault(row["QuadKey"], []).append(row["Url"]) return table

nodes.name: _touches
nodes.signature: def _touches(shape: dict, south, west, north, east) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _touches(shape: dict, south, west, north, east) -> bool: kind = shape.get("type") parts = ([shape.get("coordinates") or []] if kind == "Polygon" else shape.get("coordinates") or [] if kind == "MultiPolygon" else []) for part in parts: for lon, lat in (part[0] if part else []): # a corner inside is enough; a footprint spanning the whole box # without a corner in it is not a thing a town has if west <= lon <= east and south <= lat <= north: return True return False

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.signature: def fetch(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, should_stop=None) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def fetch(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, should_stop=None) -> list[dict]: """Every Microsoft footprint with a corner inside this box.""" table = _index() urls = [u for k in quadkeys(south, west, north, east) for u in table.get(k, [])] rows: list[dict] = [] for url in urls: with _open(url) as resp, gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=resp) as gz: for n, line in enumerate(io.TextIOWrapper(gz, encoding="utf-8")): if n % 20000 == 0 and should_stop is not None and should_stop(): import knoxstop raise knoxstop.Stopped("the Microsoft buildings download") try: feat = json.loads(line) shape = feat["geometry"] except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError): continue if not _touches(shape, south, west, north, east): continue height = (feat.get("properties") or {}).get("height") rows.append({"id": None, "height": height, "levels": None, "class": None, "geometry": shape}) return rows

nodes.name: add_missing
nodes.signature: def add_missing(features: list[OSMFeature], bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float], output_dir: str, map_name: str, should_stop=None) -> tuple[list[OSMFeature], dict]
nodes.body_text: def add_missing(features: list[OSMFeature], bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float], output_dir: str, map_name: str, should_stop=None) -> tuple[list[OSMFeature], dict]: """`features`, plus a building wherever Microsoft has one and OSM does not. Raises on a network failure; the caller decides what to fall back to. """ south, west, north, east = bbox stats = {"available": True, "fetched": 0, "added": 0, "cached": False} path = cache_path(output_dir, map_name) rows = load_cache(path, bbox) if rows is not None: stats["cached"] = True else: rows = fetch(south, west, north, east, should_stop=should_stop) try: save_cache(path, bbox, rows) except OSError: pass stats["fetched"] = len(rows) extra = overture.only_missing(overture.to_features(rows), features) stats["added"] = len(extra) return (features + extra) if extra else features, stats

nodes.name: octilinear.py
nodes.body_text: """Roads in long straight runs at 45-degree steps, the way Knox County's are. The game's own roads run along the tiles or on the diagonal, nothing between. A real street at 20 degrees drawn on tiles is a ragged staircase, its kerbs and markings chopped at every step, and a curving suburban crescent is a smear. With the "Knox County roads" setting the town is gently redrawn before anything is painted: 1. The road network becomes a graph: its junctions and the corners left once small wiggles are smoothed away. 2. Each stretch between two of those points picks the nearest of the four directions the game draws well - along either axis or either diagonal - and all the points are moved together, as little as they can be, until every stretch runs that way (a least-squares fit; junctions are shared, so every road still meets the ones it met). A crescent becomes a few straight sides with 45-degree corners; a long road at 10 degrees becomes straight. 3. Everything else - buildings, parks, car parks, water, paths - moves with the roads around it, by a smooth blend of how far the nearby roads moved, so houses still front their street instead of standing in it. What is left is a town that reads like the real one, laid out like the game's. The setting's other two choices route the roads instead (generator/roadgraph: vanilla's sixteen directions and its own street shapes). The renderer saves the result as <map>_roadgraph.json and every later step that needs the roads where the renderer drew them reads that file back (replay) rather than working them out again. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import math import os import numpy as np ROAD_CATEGORIES = {"road_major", "road_medium", "road_minor", "road_service", "pedestrian"} # Wiggles smaller than this, in tiles, are smoothed away first. SIMPLIFY_TILES = 3.0 # How strongly a point holds to where it really is, against how strongly each # stretch turns to its direction. Low: roads straighten, the town bends to fit. HOLD = 0.02 # How far, in tiles, the rest of the town feels a road's move. BLEND_TILES = 30 # How far straightening may drag a point from where the survey put it. The fit # on its own has no such limit, and on a big town it used it: a main road at a # slight angle straightened by moving its far end a couple of blocks, which # left the road beyond it cut off, and streets on the other side of town ended # up across the road they used to run beside. Anything that wants to move # further than this is pinned where it really is and the fit is run again, so # the straightening gives way rather than the map. MAX_MOVE_TILES = 24.0 # The hold on a point that has been pinned: large enough that the stretches # pulling on it cannot drag it anywhere. PINNED_HOLD = 50.0 # A closed loop smaller than this across is a roundabout, whatever it is # tagged. Fitting one to the eight directions turned it into a few crossed # triangles; it is left exactly as it is instead, with its junctions pinned so # every road still meets it. ROUNDABOUT_TILES = 60.0 # How far apart the points of one straight run may be across it and still be # rounded onto the same row, column or diagonal. ROUND_SPREAD = 2.0 FIELD_CELL = 4 # tiles per cell of the displacement field DIRECTIONS = [(1.0, 0.0), (math.sqrt(.5), math.sqrt(.5)), (0.0, 1.0), (-math.sqrt(.5), math.sqrt(.5))]

nodes.name: _key
nodes.signature: def _key(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _key(lat: float, lon: float) -> tuple[int, int]: return round(lat * 1e7), round(lon * 1e7)

nodes.name: _simplify_idx
nodes.signature: def _simplify_idx(pts: list[tuple[float, float]], tol: float) -> list[int]
nodes.body_text: def _simplify_idx(pts: list[tuple[float, float]], tol: float) -> list[int]: """Douglas-Peucker; the indices kept, both ends included.""" if len(pts) < 3: return list(range(len(pts))) keep = [False] * len(pts) keep[0] = keep[-1] = True stack = [(0, len(pts) - 1)] while stack: a, b = stack.pop() best, best_d = -1, tol for i in range(a + 1, b): d = _dist_to_line(pts[i], pts[a], pts[b]) if d > best_d: best, best_d = i, d if best >= 0: keep[best] = True stack += [(a, best), (best, b)] return [i for i, k in enumerate(keep) if k]

nodes.name: _dist_to_line
nodes.body_text: def _dist_to_line(p, a, b) -> float: (px, py), (ax, ay), (bx, by) = p, a, b dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay length = math.hypot(dx, dy) if length == 0: return math.hypot(px - ax, py - ay) return abs(dx * (ay - py) - (ax - px) * dy) / length

nodes.name: _legs
nodes.signature: def _legs(a: tuple[int, int], b: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _legs(a: tuple[int, int], b: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """From a to b along the grid and the diagonal: half the straight part, the diagonal, the other half.""" (ax, ay), (bx, by) = a, b dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay sx, sy = (dx > 0) - (dx < 0), (dy > 0) - (dy < 0) diag = min(abs(dx), abs(dy)) first = (max(abs(dx), abs(dy)) - diag) // 2 p1 = (ax + sx * first, ay) if abs(dx) >= abs(dy) else (ax, ay + sy * first) return [p1, (p1[0] + sx * diag, p1[1] + sy * diag), b]

nodes.name: _tidy
nodes.body_text: def _tidy(path: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """Without repeated points or points in the middle of a straight run.""" out: list[tuple[int, int]] = [] for p in path: if out and p == out[-1]: continue if len(out) >= 2: (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = out[-2], out[-1] if (x1 - x0) * (p[1] - y1) == (y1 - y0) * (p[0] - x1) and \ (x1 - x0) * (p[0] - x1) + (y1 - y0) * (p[1] - y1) >= 0: out[-1] = p continue out.append(p) return out

nodes.name: _rigid
nodes.body_text: def _rigid(f, px: list) -> bool: """Whether this road is left exactly as it was drawn: a roundabout, or any small closed loop, which has no straight sides to fit.""" if (f.tags.get("junction") or "").lower() in {"roundabout", "circular"}: return True if len(px) < 4 or math.dist(px[0], px[-1]) > 1e-6: return False xs = [x for x, _ in px] ys = [y for _, y in px] return max(max(xs) - min(xs), max(ys) - min(ys)) <= ROUNDABOUT_TILES

nodes.name: _fit
nodes.signature: def _fit(p0: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def _fit(p0: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray: """The points, straightened: once held firmly where they are, then again held only loosely to that, which is what takes the last of the slant out.""" def holds(value: float) -> np.ndarray: out = np.full((len(p0), 1), value) if pinned is not None: out[pinned] = PINNED_HOLD return out moved = _solve(p0, segs, normals, weights, hold=holds(HOLD)) return _solve(moved, segs, normals, weights, iterations=1500, hold=holds(HOLD / 50))

nodes.name: holds
nodes.body_text: def holds(value: float) -> np.ndarray: out = np.full((len(p0), 1), value) if pinned is not None: out[pinned] = PINNED_HOLD return out

nodes.name: _solve
nodes.signature: def _solve(p0: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, iterations: int = 400, hold=None) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def _solve(p0: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, iterations: int = 400, hold=None) -> np.ndarray: """Points as near p0 as they can be with every segment turned along its direction: minimise HOLD*|P - p0|^2 + sum w*(n . (P_j - P_i))^2, by conjugate gradients on the normal equations.""" hold = HOLD if hold is None else hold i, j = segs[:, 0], segs[:, 1] def apply(x): out = hold * x v = weights * np.einsum("ij,ij->i", normals, x[j] - x[i]) np.add.at(out, j, v[:, None] * normals) np.add.at(out, i, -v[:, None] * normals) return out b = hold * p0 x = p0.copy() r = b - apply(x) p = r.copy() rs = float((r * r).sum()) for _ in range(iterations): if rs < 1e-6: break ap = apply(p) alpha = rs / float((p * ap).sum()) x += alpha * p r -= alpha * ap rs_new = float((r * r).sum()) p = r + (rs_new / rs) * p rs = rs_new return x

nodes.name: apply
nodes.body_text: def apply(x): out = hold * x v = weights * np.einsum("ij,ij->i", normals, x[j] - x[i]) np.add.at(out, j, v[:, None] * normals) np.add.at(out, i, -v[:, None] * normals) return out

nodes.name: _blur
nodes.body_text: def _blur(a: np.ndarray, radius: int) -> np.ndarray: """Three box blurs, near enough a Gaussian, along both axes.""" for axis in (0, 1): for _ in range(3): pad = [(0, 0), (0, 0)] pad[axis] = (radius + 1, radius) c = np.cumsum(np.pad(a, pad, mode="edge"), axis=axis) hi = np.take(c, range(2 * radius + 1, c.shape[axis]), axis=axis) lo = np.take(c, range(0, c.shape[axis] - 2 * radius - 1), axis=axis) a = (hi - lo) / (2 * radius + 1) return a

nodes.name: _round_together
nodes.signature: def _round_together(moved: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, original: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray, clean: bool = False) -> list
nodes.body_text: def _round_together(moved: np.ndarray, segs: np.ndarray, normals: np.ndarray, original: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray, clean: bool = False) -> list: """Whole tiles for the points, the same row for every point along one east-west run, the same column along a north-south one and the same diagonal along a diagonal one - rounded one at a time, the ends of a long straight road can land either side of a tile edge, and it jogs.""" n = len(moved) cap = MAX_MOVE_TILES * (1.35 if clean else 1.0) reach = cap / math.sqrt(2) lower = np.ceil(original - reach).astype(int) upper = np.floor(original + reach).astype(int) orig_down = original[:, 0] - original[:, 1] orig_up = original[:, 0] + original[:, 1] down_lo = np.ceil(orig_down - cap).astype(int) down_hi = np.floor(orig_down + cap).astype(int) up_lo = np.ceil(orig_up - cap).astype(int) up_hi = np.floor(orig_up + cap).astype(int) if pinned is not None: lower[pinned] = upper[pinned] = np.rint(original[pinned]).astype(int) down_lo[pinned] = down_hi[pinned] = (lower[pinned, 0] - lower[pinned, 1]) up_lo[pinned] = up_hi[pinned] = (lower[pinned, 0] + lower[pinned, 1]) bounds = { "row": [list(lower[:, 1]), list(upper[:, 1])], "col": [list(lower[:, 0]), list(upper[:, 0])], "down": [list(down_lo), list(down_hi)], "up": [list(up_lo), list(up_hi)], } parent = {kind: list(range(n)) for kind in ("row", "col", "down", "up")} def find(kind, a): p = parent[kind] while p[a] != a: p[a] = p[p[a]] a = p[a] return a order = sorted(range(len(segs)), key=lambda i: -math.dist(original[segs[i, 0]], original[segs[i, 1]])) for edge in order: (a, b), (nx, ny) = segs[edge], normals[edge] if abs(nx) < 1e-9: kind = "row" # runs along x: normal is (0, ±1) elif abs(ny) < 1e-9: kind = "col" elif nx * ny < 0: kind = "down" # along (1, 1): x - y is constant else: kind = "up" # along (-1, 1): x + y is constant ra, rb = find(kind, int(a)), find(kind, int(b)) if ra != rb: if kind in bounds: lo, hi = bounds[kind] left, right = max(lo[ra], lo[rb]), min(hi[ra], hi[rb]) if left > right: continue lo[rb], hi[rb] = left, right parent[kind][ra] = rb def shared(kind, values): groups: dict[int, list[float]] = {} for k in range(n): groups.setdefault(find(kind, k), []).append(values[k]) mean = {g: round(sum(v) / len(v)) for g, v in groups.items()} # Axis and diagonal runs share a tile offset within their movement bounds. if kind in bounds: lo, hi = bounds[kind] mean = {g: min(hi[g], max(lo[g], m)) for g, m in mean.items()} together = {g: len(v) > 1 and (kind in bounds or max(abs(x - mean[g]) for x in v) <= ROUND_SPREAD) for g, v in groups.items()} return ([mean[find(kind, k)] for k in range(n)], [together[find(kind, k)] for k in range(n)]) xs, ys = moved[:, 0], moved[:, 1] row, in_row = shared("row", ys) col, in_col = shared("col", xs) down, in_down = shared("down", xs - ys) up, in_up = shared("up", xs + ys) out = [] for k in range(n): y = row[k] if in_row[k] else round(ys[k]) if in_col[k]: x = col[k] if not in_row[k]: if in_down[k]: y = x - down[k] elif in_up[k]: y = up[k] - x elif in_down[k]: if not in_row[k] and not in_up[k]: y = round((xs[k] + ys[k] - down[k]) / 2) lo_y = max(lower[k, 1], lower[k, 0] - down[k]) hi_y = min(upper[k, 1], upper[k, 0] - down[k]) if lo_y <= hi_y: y = min(hi_y, max(lo_y, y)) x = down[k] + y elif in_up[k]: if not in_row[k]: y = round((ys[k] - xs[k] + up[k]) / 2) lo_y = max(lower[k, 1], up[k] - upper[k, 0]) hi_y = min(upper[k, 1], up[k] - lower[k, 0]) if lo_y <= hi_y: y = min(hi_y, max(lo_y, y)) x = up[k] - y else: x = round(xs[k]) if not in_row[k] and not in_col[k] and in_down[k] and in_up[k]: # Where two diagonals cross, both hold. y = (up[k] - down[k]) // 2 x = down[k] + y x = min(upper[k, 0], max(lower[k, 0], x)) y = min(upper[k, 1], max(lower[k, 1], y)) out.append((int(x), int(y))) return out

nodes.name: find
nodes.body_text: def find(kind, a): p = parent[kind] while p[a] != a: p[a] = p[p[a]] a = p[a] return a

nodes.name: shared
nodes.body_text: def shared(kind, values): groups: dict[int, list[float]] = {} for k in range(n): groups.setdefault(find(kind, k), []).append(values[k]) mean = {g: round(sum(v) / len(v)) for g, v in groups.items()} # Axis and diagonal runs share a tile offset within their movement bounds. if kind in bounds: lo, hi = bounds[kind] mean = {g: min(hi[g], max(lo[g], m)) for g, m in mean.items()} together = {g: len(v) > 1 and (kind in bounds or max(abs(x - mean[g]) for x in v) <= ROUND_SPREAD) for g, v in groups.items()} return ([mean[find(kind, k)] for k in range(n)], [together[find(kind, k)] for k in range(n)])

nodes.name: _square_short_bends
nodes.signature: def _square_short_bends(p0, segs, normals, pinned, clean: bool = False)
nodes.body_text: def _square_short_bends(p0, segs, normals, pinned, clean: bool = False): """Square small kinks between long grid runs, keeping major diagonals.""" lengths = np.linalg.norm(p0[segs[:, 1]] - p0[segs[:, 0]], axis=1) axial = np.min(np.abs(normals), axis=1) < 1e-9 incident = {} all_incident = {} for i, (a, b) in enumerate(segs): all_incident.setdefault(a, []).append(i) all_incident.setdefault(b, []).append(i) if axial[i]: incident.setdefault(a, []).append(i) incident.setdefault(b, []).append(i) out = normals.copy() max_kink = MAX_MOVE_TILES * (2.0 if clean else 1.0) ratio = 1.5 if clean else 2.0 for i, (a, b) in enumerate(segs): if lengths[i] > max_kink or pinned[a] or pinned[b]: continue if not axial[i]: before = [j for j in incident.get(a, ()) if j != i and lengths[j] >= ratio * lengths[i]] after = [j for j in incident.get(b, ()) if j != i and lengths[j] >= ratio * lengths[i]] if before and after: j = max(before + after, key=lambda j: lengths[j]) out[i] = normals[j] continue # Also straighten a short kink (axial or diagonal) sandwiched between # two longer runs that share the same direction. for j in all_incident.get(a, ()): if j == i or lengths[j] < ratio * lengths[i]: continue for k in all_incident.get(b, ()): if k == i or lengths[k] < ratio * lengths[i]: continue if abs(float(np.dot(normals[j], normals[k]))) > 1.0 - 1e-6: out[i] = normals[j] break return out

nodes.name: _align_snapped_segments
nodes.signature: def _align_snapped_segments(snapped: list[tuple[int, int]], road_vertices: list[list[int]], rigid: list[bool], p0: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray, clean: bool = False) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _align_snapped_segments(snapped: list[tuple[int, int]], road_vertices: list[list[int]], rigid: list[bool], p0: np.ndarray, pinned: np.ndarray, clean: bool = False) -> None: """Eliminate 1-3 tile residual cross-axis shifts along straight and diagonal road segments when an unpinned internal vertex can sit on the exact line.""" v_uses: dict[int, int] = {} for held, verts in zip(rigid, road_vertices): if held: continue for idx, v in enumerate(verts): v_uses[v] = v_uses.get(v, 0) + (2 if idx in (0, len(verts) - 1) else 1) max_err = 4 if clean else 2 cap = MAX_MOVE_TILES for held, verts in zip(rigid, road_vertices): if held or len(verts) < 2: continue for u, v in zip(verts, verts[1:]): if u == v: continue ax, ay = snapped[u] bx, by = snapped[v] dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay adx, ady = abs(dx), abs(dy) if adx == 0 or ady == 0 or adx == ady: continue axial_err = min(adx, ady) diag_err = abs(adx - ady) if axial_err <= max_err and max(adx, ady) >= 3 * axial_err: for target, ref in ((v, (ax, ay)), (u, (bx, by))): if pinned[target] or (not clean and v_uses.get(target, 0) > 1): continue nx = ref[0] if adx < ady else snapped[target][0] ny = ref[1] if ady < adx else snapped[target][1] if math.hypot(nx - p0[target, 0], ny - p0[target, 1]) <= cap: snapped[target] = (int(nx), int(ny)) break elif diag_err <= max_err and min(adx, ady) >= 2 * diag_err: sx = 1 if dx > 0 else -1 sy = 1 if dy > 0 else -1 for target, origin, sign in ((v, (ax, ay), 1), (u, (bx, by), -1)): if pinned[target] or (not clean and v_uses.get(target, 0) > 1): continue tx, ty = snapped[target] step = round((abs(tx - origin[0]) + abs(ty - origin[1])) / 2) nx = origin[0] + sign * sx * step ny = origin[1] + sign * sy * step if math.hypot(nx - p0[target, 0], ny - p0[target, 1]) <= cap: snapped[target] = (int(nx), int(ny)) break

nodes.name: straighten_roads
nodes.signature: def straighten_roads(features: list, proj, classify, is_polygon, clean: bool = False) -> int
nodes.body_text: def straighten_roads(features: list, proj, classify, is_polygon, clean: bool = False) -> int: """Redraw the roads in `features` and move the rest of the town with them, in place. Returns how many roads were redrawn.""" roads = [f for f in features if f.kind == "way" and len(f.geometry) >= 2 and not is_polygon(f) and classify(f.tags) in ROAD_CATEGORIES] if not roads: return 0 # --- the graph: junctions shared, corners per road --------------------- uses: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {} for f in roads: for n, (lat, lon) in enumerate(f.geometry): k = _key(lat, lon) uses[k] = uses.get(k, 0) + (2 if n in (0, len(f.geometry) - 1) else 1) points: list[tuple[float, float]] = [] junction: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {} road_vertices: list[list[int]] = [] # per road, its graph points in order road_px: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = [] def vertex(xy, key=None): if key is not None and key in junction: return junction[key] points.append(xy) if key is not None: junction[key] = len(points) - 1 return len(points) - 1 simplify_tol = SIMPLIFY_TILES * (1.5 if clean else 1.0) rigid: list[bool] = [] # roads left exactly as they were drawn for f in roads: px = [proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lat, lon in f.geometry] road_px.append(px) rigid.append(_rigid(f, px)) keys = [_key(lat, lon) for lat, lon in f.geometry] cuts = [n for n, k in enumerate(keys) if n in (0, len(keys) - 1) or uses[k] >= 2] verts = [vertex(px[0], keys[0])] for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]): kept = _simplify_idx(px[a:b + 1], simplify_tol) for n in kept[1:-1]: verts.append(vertex(px[a + n])) verts.append(vertex(px[b], keys[b])) road_vertices.append(verts) p0 = np.array(points, dtype=float) pinned = np.zeros(len(points), dtype=bool) segs, normals, weights = [], [], [] for held, verts in zip(rigid, road_vertices): if held: # A roundabout holds its own shape and its junctions, so the roads # into it still meet it; nothing turns it to the eight directions. pinned[verts] = True continue for a, b in zip(verts, verts[1:]): if a == b: continue d = p0[b] - p0[a] length = float(np.hypot(*d)) if length < 1e-6: continue u = d / length best = max(DIRECTIONS, key=lambda t: abs(u[0] * t[0] + u[1] * t[1])) segs.append((a, b)) normals.append((-best[1], best[0])) # Long stretches turn firmly; a short one between two junctions # gives way to the roads around it. weights.append(min(length, 60.0) / 10.0) if not segs: return 0 segs, normals, weights = np.array(segs), np.array(normals), np.array(weights) normals = _square_short_bends(p0, segs, normals, pinned, clean=clean) moved = _fit(p0, segs, normals, weights, pinned) # Nothing may be dragged a block from where the survey put it. Whatever # wanted to be is pinned and the fit run again - the roads around it take # up the slack, and the ones that cannot simply stay as they were drawn. for _ in range(4): far = np.hypot(*(moved - p0).T) > MAX_MOVE_TILES if not (far & ~pinned).any(): break pinned |= far moved = _fit(p0, segs, normals, weights, pinned) # --- the roads, from the moved points --------------------------------- snapped = _round_together(moved, segs, normals, p0, pinned, clean=clean) _align_snapped_segments(snapped, road_vertices, rigid, p0, pinned, clean=clean) drawn: list = [] # each road as it now stands, in tiles for f, held, verts in zip(roads, rigid, road_vertices): if held: drawn.append(None) continue path = [snapped[verts[0]]] for v in verts[1:]: path += _legs(path[-1], snapped[v]) path = _tidy(path) if len(path) < 2: drawn.append(None) continue drawn.append(path) f.geometry = [proj.to_latlon(x, y) for x, y in path] # --- everything else moves with the roads near it --------------------- # Sampled along each road as it is drawn now, against the line it was # drawn on: a road that comes out as grid and 45-degree runs leaves that # line by up to MAX_MOVE_TILES, and the town has to go with the road that # is really there. Sampling the junctions alone said "nothing moved" # wherever the run between two junctions had been redrawn. samples = [] for held, px, path in zip(rigid, road_px, drawn): if held or path is None: continue for a, b in zip(path, path[1:]): qa, qb = np.array(a, dtype=float), np.array(b, dtype=float) steps = max(1, int(np.hypot(*(qb - qa)) / FIELD_CELL)) for t in np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, steps + 1): q = qa + (qb - qa) * t was = np.array(_on_line(px, q), dtype=float) samples.append((was, q - was)) _carry(features, roads, displacement(samples, proj)) return len(roads)

nodes.name: vertex
nodes.body_text: def vertex(xy, key=None): if key is not None and key in junction: return junction[key] points.append(xy) if key is not None: junction[key] = len(points) - 1 return len(points) - 1

nodes.name: _on_line
nodes.body_text: def _on_line(line: list, q) -> tuple[float, float]: """The point of `line` - a road's [(x, y), ...] before it was redrawn - nearest `q` in tiles, so a corner of the redrawn road knows where the road it replaced used to be.""" best, best_d = line[0], float("inf") for (ax, ay), (bx, by) in zip(line, line[1:]): dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay span = dx * dx + dy * dy t = 0.0 if not span else max(0.0, min(1.0, ((q[0] - ax) * dx + (q[1] - ay) * dy) / span)) p = (ax + dx * t, ay + dy * t) d = (q[0] - p[0]) ** 2 + (q[1] - p[1]) ** 2 if d < best_d: best, best_d = p, d return best

nodes.name: displacement
nodes.body_text: def displacement(samples, proj): """move(lat, lon) -> (lat, lon): the town's move at a point, from `samples` [(point before, its move)] in tiles along the roads - their moves blended over BLEND_TILES, fading out far from any road.""" gw, gh = proj.width // FIELD_CELL + 2, proj.height // FIELD_CELL + 2 weight = np.zeros((gh, gw)) shift = np.zeros((gh, gw, 2)) for q, d in samples: cx, cy = int(q[0] // FIELD_CELL), int(q[1] // FIELD_CELL) if 0 <= cx < gw and 0 <= cy < gh: weight[cy, cx] += 1.0 shift[cy, cx] += d radius = max(1, BLEND_TILES // FIELD_CELL) w_blur = _blur(weight, radius) field_x = _blur(shift[..., 0], radius) / (w_blur + 1e-3) field_y = _blur(shift[..., 1], radius) / (w_blur + 1e-3) # Far from any road the move fades out rather than jumping to nothing. fade = np.clip(w_blur / (w_blur.max() * 0.02 + 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0) field_x *= fade field_y *= fade def move(lat, lon): x, y = proj.to_px(lat, lon) cx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // FIELD_CELL))) cy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // FIELD_CELL))) return proj.to_latlon(x + field_x[cy, cx], y + field_y[cy, cx]) return move

nodes.name: move
nodes.body_text: def move(lat, lon): x, y = proj.to_px(lat, lon) cx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // FIELD_CELL))) cy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // FIELD_CELL))) return proj.to_latlon(x + field_x[cy, cx], y + field_y[cy, cx])

nodes.name: _carry
nodes.signature: def _carry(features: list, roads: list, move) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _carry(features: list, roads: list, move) -> None: """Everything in `features` but the roads moved by `move`, in place.""" road_ids = {id(f) for f in roads} for f in features: if id(f) in road_ids: continue if f.geometry and f.kind in ("way", "node"): f.geometry = [move(lat, lon) for lat, lon in f.geometry] if f.kind == "relation" and getattr(f, "role_geoms", None): f.role_geoms = [(role, [move(lat, lon) for lat, lon in ring]) for role, ring in f.role_geoms] if f.geometry and isinstance(f.geometry[0][0], (list, tuple)): f.geometry = [ring for _role, ring in f.role_geoms]

nodes.name: apply_road_graph
nodes.signature: def apply_road_graph(features: list, graph: dict, proj) -> int
nodes.body_text: def apply_road_graph(features: list, graph: dict, proj) -> int: """The roads as generator/roadgraph routed them, in place of straightening: graph {"ways": {osm id: {"geometry": [[lat, lon], ...], "tags": {...}}}, "drop": [osm id, ...], "shift": [[lat, lon, lat, lon], ...]}. Each routed way takes its new line (and any tags given); a dropped way (a lane folded into the road beside it, the second half of a dual carriageway) goes; "shift" - points along the roads, where they were and where they went - moves everything else with the roads near it, as straightening does.
