nodes.name: check
nodes.signature: def check(path: str, bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, limit: int = SAMPLE_LIMIT) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def check(path: str, bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, limit: int = SAMPLE_LIMIT) -> dict: """Everything wrong with this extract, and what is in it. `bbox` is (south, west, north, east) of the map about to be built; when given, the file has to cover it. """ result = {"path": os.path.abspath(path) if path else "", "ok": False, "problems": [], "warnings": [], "stats": {}, "tags": {}, "bbox": None, "version": 1} problems, warnings = result["problems"], result["warnings"] if not path: problems.append("No file given.") return result if not os.path.isfile(path): problems.append(f"There is no file at {path}.") return result size = os.path.getsize(path) if not size: problems.append("The file is empty (0 bytes): a download that never " "finished, or a shortcut with nothing behind it.") return result try: import osmium # noqa: F401 except ImportError: problems.append("pyosmium is not installed, so no extract can be read " "(run Setup again, or pip install osmium).") return result try: header = _header(path) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 problems.append(f"The file header cannot be read ({type(exc).__name__}: " f"{exc}). It is not an .osm.pbf, or it is truncated.") return result try: counted = _counts(path, limit) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 problems.append(f"The file breaks off while being read ({type(exc).__name__}: " f"{exc}). A download that stopped part way looks like this.") return result counts, tags = counted["counts"], counted["tags"] result["tags"] = tags result["stats"] = {**counts, "bytes": size, "modified": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d", time.localtime(os.path.getmtime(path))), "header": header, "sampled": counted["sampled"]} # A hand-cut file often carries no bounding box in its header; the nodes # themselves say what it covers just as well. result["bbox"] = header["bbox"] or counted["bbox"] if not counts["nodes"] or not counts["ways"]: problems.append("The file holds no nodes or no ways: there is nothing " "to draw a map from.") for key, what in NEEDED.items(): if not tags.get(key): problems.append(f"No {what} in the file (nothing tagged {key}: {what}).") missing = [key for key in NICE if not tags.get(key)] if missing: warnings.append("Nothing tagged " + ", ".join(missing) + ": those parts of the map will be plain.") if not result["bbox"]: warnings.append("The header gives no bounding box, so it cannot be " "checked against the area being drawn.") elif bbox: south, west, north, east = bbox hb = result["bbox"] if hb[2] < south or hb[0] > north or hb[3] < west or hb[1] > east: problems.append( f"The file covers {hb[0]:.4f},{hb[1]:.4f} to {hb[2]:.4f},{hb[3]:.4f}, " f"which does not overlap the area being drawn " f"({south:.4f},{west:.4f} to {north:.4f},{east:.4f}).") elif (hb[0] > south + 1e-6 or hb[2] < north - 1e-6 or hb[1] > west + 1e-6 or hb[3] < east - 1e-6): warnings.append("The area being drawn runs past the edge of this " "file: the part outside it will have no data.") age = time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path) if age > STALE_S: warnings.append(f"The file was last written {int(age // 86400)} days ago; " "Geofabrik rebuilds its extracts every day.") if size < 1 << 20: warnings.append(f"The file is only {size / 1024:.0f} KB, which is small " "for a regional extract.") if counted["sampled"]: warnings.append(f"Counts are a sample of the first {limit:,} objects.") result["ok"] = not problems return result

nodes.name: report_text
nodes.body_text: def report_text(result: dict) -> str: """The check as lines for a console.""" stats = result.get("stats") or {} lines = [f"{result['path']} — {'usable' if result['ok'] else 'NOT usable'}"] if stats: lines.append(f" {stats['bytes'] / 1048576:.1f} MB, written {stats['modified']}, " f"{stats['nodes']:,} nodes, {stats['ways']:,} ways, " f"{stats['relations']:,} relations") if result["bbox"]: b = result["bbox"] lines.append(f" covers {b[0]:.4f},{b[1]:.4f} to {b[2]:.4f},{b[3]:.4f}") for problem in result["problems"]: lines.append(f" ✗ {problem}") for warning in result["warnings"]: lines.append(f" ! {warning}") return "\n".join(lines)

nodes.name: places.py
nodes.body_text: """Finding places: search by name, and list landmarks inside a bbox. Two different services, for two different jobs: * Nominatim answers "where is Lexington High School" - free-text geocoding, used to jump the map somewhere and pre-set the selection rectangle. * Overpass answers "what is inside this rectangle" - the named schools, shops and civic buildings the area actually contains, which is what decides whether an area is worth turning into a map. Both are public OSM services with usage policies. They require a real User-Agent (the default python-requests string gets a 403), and Nominatim asks for at most one request per second, which `_throttle` enforces process-wide. """ from __future__ import annotations import threading import time import requests from generator import osm HEADERS = { "User-Agent": "KnoxMap/1.0 (+https://github.com/spytheeuclidean-a11y/knoxmap) local map generator", "Accept-Language": "en", } # Nominatim's public server is shared and has a usage policy every client must # follow: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ # One request a second (see _throttle), a real User-Agent (HEADERS), results # cached (web/geo.py), no autocomplete (the page searches only on Enter), no bulk use. NOMINATIM_URL = "https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search" # The same instances, in the same order, as the map download (generator/osm.py, # configurable in knoxmap_config.json). OVERPASS_ENDPOINTS = list(osm.ANSWERING_ENDPOINTS) _lock = threading.Lock() _last_call = 0.0 MIN_INTERVAL = 1.0 # Tags worth listing as landmarks. Anything named under these keys is something # a mapper would recognise on the ground. LANDMARK_KEYS = ("amenity", "shop", "leisure", "tourism", "historic", "office", "healthcare", "building") # Buildings are tagged building=yes in bulk, so only list named ones whose # value says something. BORING_BUILDING_VALUES = {"yes", "residential", "house", "detached", "garage", "shed", "hut", "roof", "apartments"} # How many landmarks a list holds, and how much of it any one kind of place # may take. A town with forty churches in it used to spend a quarter of the # list on them - they are ranked highly and there are a lot of them - and the # one theatre, the one market and the one graveyard were pushed out by the # cut. Each kind gets at most this share before anything is allowed seconds. LANDMARK_LIMIT = 600 VALUE_SHARE = 0.08 VALUE_MIN = 4 # What a player would navigate by. Weighted by key, raised for the values that # are landmarks in any town, and again when the place has its own Wikipedia or # Wikidata entry - a fair sign that people outside the street have heard of it. KEY_WEIGHT = {"historic": 6, "tourism": 5, "leisure": 3, "amenity": 3, "healthcare": 2, "building": 2, "office": 1, "shop": 1} NOTABLE_VALUES = { "place_of_worship": 4, "church": 4, "mosque": 4, "cathedral": 5, "synagogue": 4, "temple": 4, "school": 3, "university": 4, "college": 3, "hospital": 4, "townhall": 4, "police": 3, "fire_station": 3, "library": 3, "museum": 5, "attraction": 4, "castle": 5, "monument": 4, "park": 3, "stadium": 4, "marketplace": 3, "theatre": 3, "cinema": 2, "train_station": 4, "bus_station": 2, "supermarket": 2, "mall": 3, "department_store": 2, "fuel": 2, "pharmacy": 1, "post_office": 2, "prison": 4, "courthouse": 3, "hotel": 2, }

nodes.name: _throttle
nodes.body_text: def _throttle() -> None: """Nominatim's usage policy allows one request per second.""" global _last_call with _lock: wait = MIN_INTERVAL - (time.time() - _last_call) if wait > 0: time.sleep(wait) _last_call = time.time()

nodes.name: search
nodes.signature: def search(query: str, viewbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, bounded: bool = False, limit: int = 8) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def search(query: str, viewbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, bounded: bool = False, limit: int = 8) -> list[dict]: """Geocode `query`. viewbox is (south, west, north, east) to bias results.""" query = (query or "").strip() if not query: return [] params = { "q": query, "format": "jsonv2", "limit": str(max(1, min(limit, 20))), "addressdetails": "1", # Real outlines for towns, districts and parks, simplified to about ten # metres so a city boundary does not arrive as megabytes of points. "polygon_geojson": "1", "polygon_threshold": "0.0001", } if viewbox: s, w, n, e = viewbox # Nominatim wants <left>,<top>,<right>,<bottom>. params["viewbox"] = f"{w},{n},{e},{s}" if bounded: params["bounded"] = "1" _throttle() r = requests.get(NOMINATIM_URL, params=params, headers=HEADERS, timeout=20) r.raise_for_status() out = [] for item in r.json(): bb = item.get("boundingbox") or [] try: south, north, west, east = (float(bb[0]), float(bb[1]), float(bb[2]), float(bb[3])) except (ValueError, IndexError): continue out.append({ "name": item.get("name") or item.get("display_name", "").split(",")[0], "display_name": item.get("display_name", ""), "lat": float(item["lat"]), "lon": float(item["lon"]), "bbox": [south, west, north, east], "category": item.get("category") or item.get("class") or "", "type": item.get("type") or "", "outline": _outline(item.get("geojson")), }) return out

nodes.name: _outline
nodes.body_text: def _outline(geojson: dict | None) -> dict | None: """The place's own boundary, when it has one worth drawing a map in.""" if not geojson or geojson.get("type") not in ("Polygon", "MultiPolygon"): return None rings = geojson["coordinates"] if geojson["type"] == "Polygon" else \ [r for poly in geojson["coordinates"] for r in poly] if sum(len(r) for r in rings) > 20000: return None return geojson

nodes.name: _build_query
nodes.signature: def _build_query(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, timeout: int = 30) -> str

nodes.name: landmarks
nodes.signature: def landmarks(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, limit: int = LANDMARK_LIMIT) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def landmarks(south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, limit: int = LANDMARK_LIMIT) -> list[dict]: """Named landmarks inside the bbox, most specific category first.""" query = _build_query(south, west, north, east) last_err: Exception | None = None for endpoint in OVERPASS_ENDPOINTS: # The same manners as the map download: a server that is resting or # has refused us is not asked, and one request at a time to a host. if not osm.endpoint_ready(endpoint): last_err = RuntimeError(f"{endpoint} is resting") continue try: with osm._one_at_a_time(endpoint): r = requests.post(endpoint, data={"data": query}, headers=HEADERS, timeout=(osm.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S, 60)) payload = osm.response_payload(r) osm._note_up(endpoint) return _parse(payload, limit) except osm.OverpassError as exc: if exc.refused: osm._refuse(endpoint) elif exc.busy: osm._note_down(endpoint, exc.retry_after) last_err = RuntimeError(f"{endpoint}: {exc}") except (requests.RequestException, ValueError) as exc: osm._note_down(endpoint) last_err = RuntimeError(f"{endpoint}: {exc}") raise RuntimeError(f"All Overpass endpoints failed: {last_err}")

nodes.name: _parse
nodes.body_text: def _parse(payload: dict, limit: int) -> list[dict]: seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set() out: list[dict] = [] for el in payload.get("elements", []): tags = el.get("tags") or {} name = tags.get("name") if not name: continue if el.get("type") == "node": lat, lon = el.get("lat"), el.get("lon") else: centre = el.get("center") or {} lat, lon = centre.get("lat"), centre.get("lon") if lat is None or lon is None: continue kind = value = None for key in LANDMARK_KEYS: if key in tags: if key == "building" and tags[key] in BORING_BUILDING_VALUES: continue kind, value = key, tags[key] break if not kind: continue dedupe = (name, value) if dedupe in seen: continue seen.add(dedupe) out.append({ "name": name, "kind": kind, "value": value, "lat": float(lat), "lon": float(lon), "_rank": _notability(kind, value, tags), }) # Most notable first, then cut. Sorting by name of category before the # cut meant a busy street's alcohol shops, bakeries and bars filled the # list and every museum, church and school - later in the alphabet - was # silently dropped. out.sort(key=lambda d: (-d["_rank"], d["value"], d["name"].lower())) kept = _share_out(out, limit) for d in kept: del d["_rank"] kept.sort(key=lambda d: (d["value"], d["name"].lower())) return kept

nodes.name: _share_out
nodes.body_text: def _share_out(ranked: list[dict], limit: int) -> list[dict]: """The best `limit` landmarks, with no one kind of place taking the list. Two passes down the ranking. The first takes each kind up to its share, so the church, the school, the market and the theatre are all in before the fortieth church; the second fills whatever is left over from what was passed up, so a place that really is all churches still gets a full list rather than a short one. """ if len(ranked) <= limit: return list(ranked) share = max(VALUE_MIN, int(limit * VALUE_SHARE)) taken: dict[str, int] = {} kept, spare = [], [] for item in ranked: value = item["value"] if len(kept) < limit and taken.get(value, 0) < share: taken[value] = taken.get(value, 0) + 1 kept.append(item) else: spare.append(item) kept.extend(spare[:max(0, limit - len(kept))]) return kept

nodes.name: _notability
nodes.signature: def _notability(kind: str, value: str, tags: dict) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _notability(kind: str, value: str, tags: dict) -> int: score = KEY_WEIGHT.get(kind, 0) + NOTABLE_VALUES.get(value, 0) if "wikidata" in tags or "wikipedia" in tags: score += 4 return score

nodes.name: pz_colors.py
nodes.body_text: """Project Zomboid map color palette. Values taken directly from Thuztor's "Mapping Guide v0.2". These colors are interpreted pixel-for-pixel by WorldEd's BMP-to-TMX converter via the rules.txt that ships with the ZomboidMapTools. A PZ cell is 300x300 pixels/tiles. The landscape, vegetation, and zombie spawn bitmaps must all line up 1:1 (the spawn map is 10x smaller — one pixel per 10 world tiles). """ from __future__ import annotations # Landscape (floor) colors — used in the base landscape bitmap. DARK_GRASS = (90, 100, 35) MEDIUM_GRASS = (117, 117, 47) LIGHT_GRASS = (145, 135, 60) SAND = (210, 200, 160) # The road colours are named for what their tiles look like in Build 42, not # for the labels in Rules.txt, which are older than the textures and wrong: # Rules.txt calls 120 "Medium Asphalt" but its tiles (blends_street_01_96-103) # are pale concrete slabs, and 150 "Smooth Asphalt" is the grey asphalt. With # the labels believed, every residential street was paved in slabs and every # pavement in tarmac. DARK_ASPHALT = (100, 100, 100) # street2 — dark tarmac; no edge blends, so car parks MEDIUM_ASPHALT = (150, 150, 150) # street3 — smooth grey tarmac, blends at its edges LIGHT_ASPHALT = (165, 160, 140) # lightgravel — beige gravel: yards, track beds DARKEST_ASPHALT = (80, 80, 80) # street4 — speckled worn tarmac, blends PALE_CONCRETE = (120, 120, 120) # street — pale concrete slabs: pavements, kerbs PAVING = (170, 160, 130) # sandstone slabs — squares, plazas CLAY = (110, 80, 60) # clay — running tracks DIRT = (120, 70, 20) # Ground the relief and climate passes use (generator/renderer.py): "Dirt # Grass" and "Gravel Dirt" in the stock Rules.txt. DIRT_GRASS = (80, 55, 20) GRAVEL_DIRT = (140, 70, 15) WATER = (0, 138, 255) DARK_POTHOLE = (110, 100, 100) LIGHT_POTHOLE = (130, 120, 120) # Ploughed fields: furrowed dirt, rows running across the map (H) or down it # (V). Stock WorldEd Rules.txt has both ("Horizontal Dirt", "Vertical Dirt"). DIRT_ROWS_H = (120, 110, 95) DIRT_ROWS_V = (120, 100, 75) # Vegetation colors — used in the `_veg.bmp` bitmap. Several of these are # only valid when painted on top of a specific landscape color (see guide). TREES = (255, 0, 0) TREES_DARK_GRASS = (127, 0, 0) # fewer trees + more dark grass SPARSE_TREES = (64, 0, 0) # sparse trees + mostly dark grass GRASS_ON_DARK = (0, 255, 0) # long grass; Rules.txt has it for every grass SHORT_GRASS = (0, 250, 0) # short grass tufts, on any grass ground landscape LOT_OF_GRASS_AND_TREES = (0, 128, 0) BUSHES_TREES_DARK_GRASS = (255, 0, 255) BUSHES = (250, 0, 160) # bushes, any ground — hedges DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS = (200, 0, 200) # must sit on DARK_GRASS — wetland FLOWERS = (200, 100, 200) # flowers, any ground — cemeteries VEG_NOTHING = (0, 0, 0) # Standing corn, two kinds, for fields ("Farm Corn 1/2 (dead)" in the stock # Rules.txt: vegetation_farm_01_32..47, low bushes you push through). CORN_1 = (255, 128, 0) CORN_2 = (220, 100, 0) # Rock, for tundra and bare ground ("Boulders" and "Boulders (walkable)" in # the stock Rules.txt). BOULDERS block the way; ROCKS can be walked over. BOULDERS = (140, 160, 140) ROCKS = (100, 120, 100) # The big trees, each one a single tile whose picture is several tiles across. # Build 42's own world generator plants them as the ordinary tree of a wood - # in its maple forest a jumbo XL or XXL comes up thirty times more often than # a plain tree - and KnoxMap placed none at all, which is why generated woods # and parks read as scrub beside Knox County's. The rules for these colours # are written by worlded/patch_rules_b42_trees.py; the renderer keeps a clear # square around each (generator/rendering/vegetation.py), as the game does, # because the picture of one leans over its neighbours. TREE_BIG = (255, 0, 1) # jumbo: a 2x2 square to itself TREE_HUGE = (255, 0, 2) # jumbo XL: 3x3 TREE_GIANT = (255, 0, 3) # jumbo XXL: 5x5 # And the other end of it: a young tree, a quarter or half grown. TREES is # whatever the rule it falls under calls a tree, which in a wood or a park is # a grown one, so without this every tree in a park was the same height. BIG_TREE_ROOM = {TREE_BIG: 2, TREE_HUGE: 3, TREE_GIANT: 5} # Road details on the vegetation bitmap, placed by the rules that # worlded/patch_rules_roads.py adds: a kerb on each edge of a pavement tile # that meets the road, and centre lines along the edge between two lanes. KERB_W = (12, 34, 200) KERB_N = (12, 34, 201) KERB_S = (12, 34, 202) KERB_E = (12, 34, 203) KERB_NW = (12, 34, 204) KERB_SW = (12, 34, 205) KERB_NE = (12, 34, 206) KERB_SE = (12, 34, 207) LINE_YELLOW_N = (12, 35, 200) LINE_YELLOW_W = (12, 35, 201) LINE_WHITE_N = (12, 35, 202) LINE_WHITE_W = (12, 35, 203) EDGE_LINE_W = (12, 35, 204) EDGE_LINE_N = (12, 35, 205) EDGE_LINE_E = (12, 35, 206) EDGE_LINE_S = (12, 35, 207) # Street furniture and wear (worlded/patch_rules_roads.py). ASPHALT_GRIME = (12, 36, 200) ASPHALT_CRACKS = (12, 36, 201) LAMP_N = (12, 36, 202) LAMP_E = (12, 36, 203) LAMP_S = (12, 36, 204) LAMP_W = (12, 36, 205) HYDRANT = (12, 36, 206) STORM_DRAIN = (12, 36, 207) LITTER = (12, 36, 208) MAILBOX = (12, 36, 209) BIN = (12, 36, 210) # Speed limit signs from Erika's Tiles, painted only when that mod is set up: # (limit, facing) -> colour. A sign faces the traffic that drives past it. SPEED_SIGNS = {(25, "S"): (12, 38, 200), (25, "E"): (12, 38, 201), (35, "S"): (12, 38, 202), (35, "E"): (12, 38, 203), (45, "S"): (12, 38, 204), (45, "E"): (12, 38, 205)} # Back yards (knoxbuild/yards.py): a grill, patio table and chairs, a # clothesline and a raised planting bed, each tile of each its own colour. GRILL = (12, 37, 200) CHAIR_W = (12, 37, 201) CHAIR_N = (12, 37, 202) CHAIR_E = (12, 37, 203) CHAIR_S = (12, 37, 204) TABLE_X0 = (12, 37, 205) TABLE_X1 = (12, 37, 206) TABLE_Y0 = (12, 37, 207) TABLE_Y1 = (12, 37, 208) LINE_X0 = (12, 37, 209) LINE_XM = (12, 37, 210) LINE_X1 = (12, 37, 211) LINE_Y0 = (12, 37, 212) LINE_YM = (12, 37, 213) LINE_Y1 = (12, 37, 214) BED_NW = (12, 37, 215) BED_W = (12, 37, 216) BED_SW = (12, 37, 217) BED_N = (12, 37, 218) BED_S = (12, 37, 219) BED_NE = (12, 37, 220) BED_E = (12, 37, 221) BED_SE = (12, 37, 222) BED_SOIL = (12, 37, 223) # Works yards (knoxbuild/works.py): what stands along a works' walls, and its # dumpster, a two-tile piece set as two colours each way it faces. WORKS_PALLET = (12, 39, 200) WORKS_BRICKS = (12, 39, 201) WORKS_DRUM = (12, 39, 202) WORKS_BARREL = (12, 39, 203) WORKS_CRATE = (12, 39, 204) WORKS_TIRES = (12, 39, 205) DUMPSTER_BLUE_S0 = (12, 39, 206) DUMPSTER_BLUE_S1 = (12, 39, 207) DUMPSTER_BLUE_E0 = (12, 39, 208) DUMPSTER_BLUE_E1 = (12, 39, 209) DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S0 = (12, 39, 210) DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S1 = (12, 39, 211) DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E0 = (12, 39, 212) DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E1 = (12, 39, 213) # Ground: the stone slabs of a front path or a stoop (Rules.txt "Paving Stone 4"). PAVING_STONE = (190, 180, 180) # Track cross-sections: rail, sleepers, rail, over solid ballast. RAIL_NE_SW = (200, 30, 200) RAIL_NW_SE = (201, 31, 201) RAIL_NE_SW_W = (202, 32, 202) RAIL_NE_SW_E = (203, 33, 203) RAIL_NW_SE_N = (204, 34, 204) RAIL_NW_SE_S = (205, 35, 205) # Zombie spawn map: grayscale, 10x smaller than landscape/vegetation. # (0,0,0) = no spawns, (255,255,255) = max spawn density. # Valid color sets used for rules.txt-style validation if needed. LANDSCAPE_COLORS = { DARK_GRASS, MEDIUM_GRASS, LIGHT_GRASS, SAND, DARK_ASPHALT, MEDIUM_ASPHALT, LIGHT_ASPHALT, DARKEST_ASPHALT, PALE_CONCRETE, PAVING, CLAY, DIRT, RAIL_NE_SW, RAIL_NW_SE, RAIL_NE_SW_W, RAIL_NE_SW_E, RAIL_NW_SE_N, RAIL_NW_SE_S, WATER, DARK_POTHOLE, LIGHT_POTHOLE, DIRT_ROWS_H, DIRT_ROWS_V, DIRT_GRASS, GRAVEL_DIRT, } VEGETATION_COLORS = { TREES, TREES_DARK_GRASS, SPARSE_TREES, GRASS_ON_DARK, LOT_OF_GRASS_AND_TREES, BUSHES_TREES_DARK_GRASS, VEG_NOTHING, BUSHES, DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS, FLOWERS, TREE_BIG, TREE_HUGE, TREE_GIANT, CORN_1, CORN_2, BOULDERS, ROCKS, } CELL_SIZE = 300 # tiles per cell side — fixed by the game engine SPAWN_MAP_SCALE = 10 # spawn map is 1/10th the resolution

nodes.name: renderer.py
nodes.body_text: """Rasterize OSM features into Project Zomboid bitmaps. Output contract (per the Mapping Guide): <name>.bmp — landscape (11 palette colors) <name>_veg.bmp — vegetation (must be same size as landscape) <name>_road_hierarchy.bmp — grayscale OSM road class across right-of-way <name>_ZombieSpawnMap.bmp — grayscale, 1/10th resolution Dimensions are snapped up to the next multiple of 300 (PZ cell size). The requested real-world bbox is expanded symmetrically to fit that grid so the meters-per-tile scale stays consistent. """ from __future__ import annotations import logging import os from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Iterable import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw import knoxfiles import knoxstop from . import pz_colors as C from . import structures from .osm import (FENCE_BARRIERS, GATE_BARRIERS, OSMFeature, # noqa: F401 ROAD_HIERARCHY_BY_CODE, ROAD_HIERARCHY_CODES, classify, road_hierarchy) # Everything that moved out is still importable from here: the tests, the # tools and knoxbuild reach into this module by name. from .rendering.buildings import (ADDRESS_APART_M, ADDRESS_AVOIDS_ROADS, ADDRESS_CLEAR_M, ADDRESS_HOUSE_M, ADDRESS_PUSH_M, ADDRESS_SETBACK_M, BUILDING_TAGS, MAX_ADDRESS_HOUSES, _buildings_geojson, _houses_from_addresses, _off_the_road) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.infill import _back_sheds, _infill_frontage from .rendering.furniture import (CRACK_SHARE, DRAIN_EVERY, EDGE_LINE_MIN_WIDTH, GRIME_SHARE, HYDRANT_EVERY, LAMP_EVERY, LITTER_SHARE, ROAD_FURNITURE_INTERVALS, SPEED_BY_WIDTH, SPEED_SIGN_EVERY, _mod_tiles_ready, _paint_street_furniture) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.geometry import (_draw_line, _draw_roads, _draw_polygon, _feature_coords_px, _is_polygon, _paint_multipolygon, _pixel_width) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.gridangle import (ALIGN_MIN_STRENGTH, DISTRICT_CELL_M, DISTRICT_CLUSTER_DEG, DISTRICT_MIN_ROAD_M, GRID_ROADS, _grid_delta, dominant_road_angle) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.landcover import (AREA_CATEGORIES, DENSE_COVERAGE, GREEN_CATEGORIES, LANDSCAPE_FILL, LANDSCAPE_ORDER, VEG_CATEGORIES, WATERWAY_WIDTH_M, paint_markers, grid_for_map, refine_owned, resized_grid, settle_markers) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.fields import paint_fields, paint_pools, paint_rocks from .rendering.homesteads import clear_homesteads, keep_yards_clear from .rendering.landcover_veg import plant_landcover from .rendering.outputs import (AREA_TAGS, LINE_TAGS, OPENING_PATHS, _areas_geojson, _build_preview, _build_spawn_map, _lines_geojson, _openings_geojson, _places) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.projection import (Projector, _ceil_to, _inside, cover_bbox, shape_px) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.roads import (_paint_road_details, _pave_dense_ground, _real_kerbs, _road_hierarchy_image, _smooth_road_edges, _weather_roads, paint_rails) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.sea import sea_polygons # noqa: F401 from .rendering.shape import THROUGH_ROADS, _clip_to_shape # noqa: F401 from .rendering.vegetation import (BOX_STRIP_ROWS, GARDEN_CLEAR_OF_HOUSE, GARDEN_CLEAR_OF_PAVING, GARDEN_REACH_TILES, GARDEN_TREE_CHANCE, GARDEN_TREE_EVERY, GRASS_COLOURS, LONG_GRASS_SHARE, PARK_EDGE_M, SHORT_GRASS_SHARE, SHRUB_CHANCE, WILD_BUSH_SHARE, WILD_CLEAR_OF_PAVING, WILD_CLUMP_M, WILD_GROUND, WILD_TREE_CHANCE, WILD_TREE_EVERY_M, _box_any, _clear_building_vegetation, _clear_road_vegetation, _paint_gardens, _paint_groves, _paint_parks, _paint_vegetation, _paint_vegetation_extras, _paint_wild_growth, _paint_woodland, _plant_big_trees, tree_rules_ready) # noqa: F401 from .rendering.widths import (ROAD_WIDTHS_BY_HIERARCHY_M, ROAD_WIDTHS_M, SIDEWALK_BY_HIERARCHY_M, SIDEWALK_M, VERGE_BY_HIERARCHY_M, VERGE_M, _road_markings, _sidewalk_width_m, _verge_width_m, _way_width_m) # noqa: F401 # --- main entry point ------------------------------------------------------ @dataclass _log = logging.getLogger("knoxmap.renderer") # The Road layout setting (straight_roads) past Knox County's straight runs (1): # routed on vanilla's lattice (roadgraph/modes.py). ROAD_LAYOUTS = {2: "graph", 3: "cost"} # Ground tint multipliers per NOAA climate class: a gentle shift, never a # repaint. Project Zomboid's art is Kentucky-themed, so this only leans it. CLIMATE_TINT = { "arid": (1.10, 1.02, 0.80), "cold continental": (0.95, 1.00, 1.06), "humid": (0.95, 1.04, 0.95), "temperate": (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), } _WINTER_GROUND = (210, 214, 218) MIN_RELIEF_M = 30.0 SNOW_RELIEF_M = 400.0 # OSM wetland that gets pools: marsh, swamp, bog, reed bed, or untyped. Not # wet meadow, which is a field that floods. POOL_WETLANDS = {None, "marsh", "swamp", "bog", "reedbed"} # WorldCover classes relief may band: tree cover, shrubland, grassland, # built-up - grass ground that stays grass. RELIEF_CLASSES = (10, 20, 30, 50)

nodes.name: _paint_climate
nodes.signature: def _paint_climate(landscape: Image.Image, climate: dict, winter_look: str = "auto") -> None
nodes.body_text: def _paint_climate(landscape: Image.Image, climate: dict, winter_look: str = "auto") -> None: """Tint the ground for its real climate: dry, cold, lush or default.""" import numpy as np climate = climate or {} klass = str(climate.get("class") or "").strip().lower() mult = CLIMATE_TINT.get(klass) cold = klass == "cold continental" or float(climate.get("jan_c") or 0) < -3 winter = winter_look == "on" or (winter_look == "auto" and cold) if mult is None and not winter: return arr = np.asarray(landscape, dtype="float32") if mult: arr = arr * np.array(mult, dtype="float32") if winter: arr = arr * 0.80 + np.array(_WINTER_GROUND, dtype="float32") * 0.20 landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(np.clip(arr, 0, 255).astype("uint8"), "RGB"), (0, 0))

nodes.name: _paint_relief
nodes.signature: def _paint_relief(landscape: Image.Image, metres, span=None, strength: float = 0.30) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _paint_relief(landscape: Image.Image, metres, span=None, strength: float = 0.30) -> None: """Compressed relief: a hillshade and rock/snow bands, no z channel. The metres grid is one sample per tile (or a coarse DEM window); it is stretched to the ground image. Flat areas are left alone, so a map with no relief looks exactly as before. """ import numpy as np m = np.asarray(metres, dtype="float32") if m.ndim != 2 or m.size == 0: return if (m.shape[1], m.shape[0]) != landscape.size: m = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(m).resize(landscape.size, Image.BILINEAR)) if not np.isfinite(m).any(): return lo, hi = span if span else (float(np.nanmin(m)), float(np.nanmax(m))) relief = float(hi) - float(lo) if relief < MIN_RELIEF_M: return m = np.nan_to_num(m, nan=float(np.nanmin(m))) # Hillshade from the north-west, so slopes read the way paper maps do. gy, gx = np.gradient(m) shade = -(gx + gy) scale = float(np.percentile(np.abs(shade), 95)) or 1.0 shade = np.clip(shade / scale, -1.0, 1.0) * strength arr = np.asarray(landscape, dtype="float32") * (1.0 + shade[..., None]) rock = m >= np.percentile(m, 75) arr[rock] = arr[rock] * 0.85 + np.array([120, 110, 96], "float32") * 0.15 if relief >= SNOW_RELIEF_M: snow = m >= np.percentile(m, 92) arr[snow] = arr[snow] * 0.55 + np.array([238, 240, 244], "float32") * 0.45 landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(np.clip(arr, 0, 255).astype("uint8"), "RGB"), (0, 0))

nodes.name: _paint_climate_ground
nodes.signature: def _paint_climate_ground(landscape: Image.Image, climate: dict, winter_look: str = "auto") -> None
nodes.body_text: def _paint_climate_ground(landscape: Image.Image, climate: dict, winter_look: str = "auto") -> None: """Shift grass palette colours for climate while keeping exact Rules.txt RGBs.""" import numpy as np climate = climate or {} klass = str(climate.get("class") or "").strip().lower() cold = klass == "cold continental" or float(climate.get("jan_c") or 0) < -3 winter = winter_look == "on" or (winter_look == "auto" and cold) if klass not in ("arid", "humid") and not winter: return arr = np.array(landscape, dtype="uint8", copy=True) dark = ((arr[:, :, 0] == C.DARK_GRASS[0]) & (arr[:, :, 1] == C.DARK_GRASS[1]) & (arr[:, :, 2] == C.DARK_GRASS[2])) med = ((arr[:, :, 0] == C.MEDIUM_GRASS[0]) & (arr[:, :, 1] == C.MEDIUM_GRASS[1]) & (arr[:, :, 2] == C.MEDIUM_GRASS[2])) light = ((arr[:, :, 0] == C.LIGHT_GRASS[0]) & (arr[:, :, 1] == C.LIGHT_GRASS[1]) & (arr[:, :, 2] == C.LIGHT_GRASS[2])) if klass == "arid": arr[dark] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS arr[med] = C.LIGHT_GRASS arr[light] = C.DIRT_GRASS elif klass == "humid": arr[light] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS if winter: arr[dark & ~med] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(arr, "RGB"), (0, 0))

nodes.name: _paint_relief_ground
nodes.body_text: def _paint_relief_ground(landscape: Image.Image, metres, span=None) -> None: """Map relief bands to valid Rules.txt ground colours under OSM.""" import numpy as np m = np.asarray(metres, dtype="float32") if m.ndim != 2 or m.size == 0: return if (m.shape[1], m.shape[0]) != landscape.size: m = np.asarray(Image.fromarray(m).resize(landscape.size, Image.BILINEAR)) if not np.isfinite(m).any(): return lo, hi = span if span else (float(np.nanmin(m)), float(np.nanmax(m))) relief = float(hi) - float(lo) if relief < MIN_RELIEF_M: return m = np.nan_to_num(m, nan=float(np.nanmin(m))) arr = np.array(landscape, dtype="uint8", copy=True) upper = m >= np.percentile(m, 65) rock = m >= np.percentile(m, 88) arr[upper] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS arr[rock] = C.GRAVEL_DIRT if relief >= SNOW_RELIEF_M: arr[m >= np.percentile(m, 95)] = C.LIGHT_GRASS landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(arr, "RGB"), (0, 0))

nodes.name: _either
nodes.body_text: def _either(a, b): """The union of two optional bool masks.""" if a is None: return b return a if b is None else a | b

nodes.name: _polygon_mask
nodes.body_text: def _polygon_mask(feats, proj): """Bool array, True inside any of the features' polygons.""" mask = Image.new("L", (proj.width, proj.height), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(mask) for feat in feats: if not _is_polygon(feat): continue for ring in _feature_coords_px(feat, proj): if len(ring) >= 3: draw.polygon(ring, fill=255) return np.asarray(mask) > 0

nodes.name: _paint_landcover
nodes.body_text: def _paint_landcover(landscape: Image.Image, grid) -> None: """Paint the WorldCover base, one class per tile, under the OSM features. OSM is painted afterwards, so anything it knows wins; this only colours ground nothing else claimed. """ import numpy as np from .rendering.landcover import WORLDCOVER_PAINT height, width = grid.shape rgb = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype="uint8") for code, colour in WORLDCOVER_PAINT.items(): rgb[grid == code] = colour base = Image.fromarray(rgb, "RGB") if base.size != landscape.size: base = base.resize(landscape.size, Image.NEAREST) landscape.paste(base, (0, 0))

nodes.name: render
nodes.signature: def render(features: Iterable[OSMFeature], south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, meters_per_tile: float, output_dir: str, map_name: str, spawn_density: int = 10, tree_density: float = 1.0, forest_density: float = 1.0, rotation: float = 0.0, osm_cache: str | None = None, osm_bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, shape: dict | None = None, straight_roads: int = 4, include_proposed_roads: int = 0, fill_frontage: int = 0, landcover_for=None, climate=None, winter_look: str = "auto", elevation=None, elevation_span=None, should_stop=None, progress=None) -> RenderResult
nodes.body_text: def render(features: Iterable[OSMFeature], south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float, meters_per_tile: float, output_dir: str, map_name: str, spawn_density: int = 10, tree_density: float = 1.0, forest_density: float = 1.0, rotation: float = 0.0, osm_cache: str | None = None, osm_bbox: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, shape: dict | None = None, straight_roads: int = 4, include_proposed_roads: int = 0, fill_frontage: int = 0, landcover_for=None, climate=None, winter_look: str = "auto", elevation=None, elevation_span=None, should_stop=None, progress=None) -> RenderResult: proj = Projector.build(south, west, north, east, meters_per_tile, rotation) # Read more than once below - the buildings pass goes back over the # address points - so never leave this as a generator. features = list(features) road_layout = int(straight_roads or 0) if road_layout in (1, 4): # Every road in straight runs at 45-degree steps (octilinear.py). from .octilinear import straighten_roads straighten_roads(features, proj, classify, _is_polygon, clean=(road_layout == 4)) elif road_layout in ROAD_LAYOUTS: # Routed on vanilla's lattice (roadgraph/route.py), and saved: Build and # the paper map read the roads back rather than routing them again. from .octilinear import apply_road_graph, graph_path from .roadgraph.route import route def tick(done, total): knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the roads") if progress: progress(done, total) graph = route(features, proj, ROAD_LAYOUTS[road_layout], shape, tick=tick) knoxfiles.write(graph_path(output_dir, map_name), graph) apply_road_graph(features, graph, proj) # A drawn polygon, circle or real outline rather than a rectangle: the map # still covers its bounding box in whole cells, but only what lies inside # the shape is built. clip = shape_px(shape, proj) landscape = Image.new("RGB", (proj.width, proj.height), C.DARK_GRASS) landcover_grid = None if landcover_for is not None: # Optional WorldCover ground under everything OSM paints (knoxdata), # in marker colours until OSM has painted, so what OSM left blank can # be told apart (generator/rendering/landcover.py). try: # What the image covers, turned with the map if it is turned. landcover_grid = grid_for_map(landcover_for, proj) if landcover_grid is not None: landcover_grid = resized_grid(landcover_grid, landscape.size) paint_markers(landscape, landcover_grid) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - optional, never fatal _log.warning("worldcover skipped: %s: %s", type(exc).__name__, exc) landcover_grid = None if elevation is not None and landcover_grid is None: # Optional 3DEP relief (knoxdata): compressed into the ground under # OSM, since Project Zomboid's outdoor ground is flat by format. try: _paint_relief_ground(landscape, elevation, elevation_span) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - optional, never fatal pass vegetation = Image.new("RGB", (proj.width, proj.height), C.VEG_NOTHING) l_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(landscape) # Bucket features so we paint in a deterministic order. buckets: dict[str, list[OSMFeature]] = {} vegetation_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] building_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] indoor_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] fence_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] gate_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] place_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] monument_feats: list[OSMFeature] = [] for feat in features: # Fences and hedges are collected from any outline that carries one, # before and independently of what the outline is: the fence around a # schoolyard is still a fence when the way is also the schoolyard. if feat.kind == "node" and "population" in feat.tags and "place" in feat.tags: place_feats.append(feat) continue if structures.monument_kind(feat.tags): monument_feats.append(feat) if feat.kind == "node" and feat.tags.get("barrier") in GATE_BARRIERS: gate_feats.append(feat) if feat.kind == "node" and "natural" not in feat.tags: continue # shops and cafes inside buildings: knoxbuild/uses.py # Rooms a mapper drew inside a building. classify() has no colour for # them - they are walls, not ground - so they are taken aside here and # attached to their building when the geojson is written. if feat.kind == "way" and feat.tags.get("indoor") in ("room", "corridor"): indoor_feats.append(feat) continue barrier = feat.tags.get("barrier") if barrier in FENCE_BARRIERS and feat.kind == "way": fence_feats.append(feat) elif barrier == "hedge" and feat.kind == "way": vegetation_feats.append(feat) cat = classify(feat.tags, _is_polygon(feat)) if cat is None: continue if cat in {"fence", "hedge"}: continue # the line itself is collected below if cat in VEG_CATEGORIES: vegetation_feats.append(feat) if cat in {"forest", "scrub", "tree_single", "hedge"}: continue if cat == "building": if clip is not None and not _inside(feat, proj, clip): continue building_feats.append(feat) buckets.setdefault(cat, []).append(feat) # Bridges lifted over the roads they cross, and monuments. See # generator/structures.py; what they leave out of the ground is cut here. lifted = stru

nodes.name: tick
nodes.body_text: def tick(done, total): knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the roads") if progress: progress(done, total)

nodes.name: ground_rings
nodes.body_text: def ground_rings(feat: OSMFeature) -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]: rings = _feature_coords_px(feat, proj) cut = lifted.cut.get(id(feat)) if cut is None: return rings from shapely.geometry import LineString as _Line left = _Line(rings[0]).difference(cut) return [list(g.coords) for g in getattr(left, "geoms", [left]) if g.geom_type == "LineString" and not g.is_empty]
