nodes.name: buildings.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings from the OSM data: the tags that make one, houses invented from address points, and the buildings GeoJSON.""" from __future__ import annotations from ..osm import OSMFeature, classify from .geometry import _feature_coords_px, _is_polygon from .projection import Projector from .widths import _way_width_m # What survives into the geojson knoxbuild reads. amenity/shop/leisure carry # what a building actually is far more reliably than the building tag alone, # and they pick its materials and room plan. # # building:levels earns its place twice over: it is the only thing in OSM that # says how tall a building is, and dropping it meant every block of flats in a # town was rebuilt as a bungalow no matter what the mapper had recorded. # Houses where the map has an address but no building. # # In whole countries - and in most American suburbs - the houses are not drawn # at all; what the survey left behind is one node per home carrying # addr:housenumber. Those streets came out as roads through empty grass. A # node with an address on it is a building by definition, so one of a # household's size is put there, upright on the grid; the rest of the build # treats it like any other footprint, so it is skipped if a real building # already covers the spot and it moves off the road like the others do. # # Except where the numbers are the ends of an address interpolation: a line # along the street tagged addr:interpolation, whose end nodes say "2" and # "48" for every home between. Those two points are the ends of a range, not # two houses, and they stand at a corner or in the gap between real houses, # so a house made from them was wedged in among the ones Overture filled in. ADDRESS_HOUSE_M = (9.0, 11.0) # frontage, depth: a small detached house ADDRESS_CLEAR_M = 4.0 # keep this far off a mapped building ADDRESS_APART_M = 7.0 # and this far from the next address point MAX_ADDRESS_HOUSES = 40000 # How far the near wall of the house stands back from the edge of the road. # # An address is a point on a street, and mappers put it anywhere from the # doorstep to the middle of the carriageway. A house dropped where the point # is therefore sat on the road often enough to read as roads going missing. # Each one is pushed away from the nearest road until it is clear of it, and # dropped if it cannot be. ADDRESS_SETBACK_M = 2.0 ADDRESS_PUSH_M = 18.0 # as far as a house is moved to get clear # Every road a house has to stand clear of: the ones with a carriageway. A # footpath or a drive may run right past the door. ADDRESS_AVOIDS_ROADS = {"road_major", "road_medium", "road_minor", "road_service", "pedestrian"} BUILDING_TAGS = { "building", "building:levels", "building:part", "building:material", "building:use", "height", "levels", "roof:levels", "roof:shape", "name", "addr:housenumber", "addr:street", "addr:flats", "amenity", "shop", "leisure", "tourism", "industrial", "healthcare", "office", "craft", "man_made", "residential", "cuisine", }

nodes.name: _off_the_road
nodes.signature: def _off_the_road(x: float, y: float, need: float, roads, road_half, road_tree, push_limit: float, max_road_half: float | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def _off_the_road(x: float, y: float, need: float, roads, road_half, road_tree, push_limit: float, max_road_half: float | None = None): """Move a point away from the road nearest it until the house round it clears the carriageway. None when it cannot be cleared.""" from shapely.geometry import Point if max_road_half is None: max_road_half = max(road_half, default=0.0) reach = need + max_road_half for _ in range(6): here = Point(x, y) worst, gap = None, 0.0 for i in road_tree.query(here, predicate="dwithin", distance=reach): i = int(i) short = need + road_half[i] - roads[i].distance(here) if short > gap: worst, gap = i, short if worst is None: return x, y # Straight away from the road it is closest to. near = roads[worst].interpolate(roads[worst].project(here)) dx, dy = x - near.x, y - near.y length = (dx * dx + dy * dy) ** 0.5 if length < 1e-6: return None # on the centre line; no way to know step = gap + 0.5 if step > push_limit: return None x += dx / length * step y += dy / length * step push_limit -= step if push_limit <= 0: return None return None

nodes.name: _houses_from_addresses
nodes.signature: def _houses_from_addresses(feats: list["OSMFeature"], buildings: list["OSMFeature"], proj: "Projector") -> list["OSMFeature"]
nodes.body_text: def _houses_from_addresses(feats: list["OSMFeature"], buildings: list["OSMFeature"], proj: "Projector") -> list["OSMFeature"]: """A house-sized footprint for every address that has no building.""" from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon from shapely.strtree import STRtree # Overpass gives an interpolation line the same coordinates as its nodes, # so a node is found on one by where it is. ranges = {tuple(p) for f in feats if f.kind == "way" and f.tags.get("addr:interpolation") for p in f.geometry} points = [f for f in feats if f.kind == "node" and f.geometry and f.tags.get("addr:housenumber") and not f.tags.get("building") and tuple(f.geometry[0]) not in ranges] if not points: return [] shapes = [] for f in buildings: rings = _feature_coords_px(f, proj) for ring in rings: if len(ring) >= 3: poly = Polygon(ring) if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) if not poly.is_empty: shapes.append(poly) tree = STRtree(shapes) if shapes else None # The roads themselves, each as a band of its own width, so a house can # be pushed off the one it belongs to. roads, road_half = [], [] for f in feats: cat = classify(f.tags, _is_polygon(f)) if cat not in ADDRESS_AVOIDS_ROADS: continue for ring in _feature_coords_px(f, proj): if len(ring) >= 2: roads.append(LineString(ring)) road_half.append(_way_width_m(f, cat) / proj.meters_per_tile / 2) road_tree = STRtree(roads) if roads else None max_road_half = max(road_half, default=0.0) setback = ADDRESS_SETBACK_M / proj.meters_per_tile push_limit = ADDRESS_PUSH_M / proj.meters_per_tile clear = ADDRESS_CLEAR_M / proj.meters_per_tile apart = ADDRESS_APART_M / proj.meters_per_tile half_w = (ADDRESS_HOUSE_M[0] / proj.meters_per_tile) / 2 half_h = (ADDRESS_HOUSE_M[1] / proj.meters_per_tile) / 2 taken: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} cell = max(1.0, apart) made = [] for f in points: if len(made) >= MAX_ADDRESS_HOUSES: break lat, lon = f.geometry[0] x, y = proj.to_px(lat, lon) if not (-half_w <= x < proj.width + half_w and -half_h <= y < proj.height + half_h): continue here = Point(x, y) if tree is not None and len(tree.query(here, predicate="dwithin", distance=clear)) > 0: continue if road_tree is not None: spot = _off_the_road(x, y, max(half_w, half_h) + setback, roads, road_half, road_tree, push_limit, max_road_half=max_road_half) if spot is None: continue # nowhere off the road to put it if (x, y) != spot: x, y = spot here = Point(x, y) if tree is not None and len(tree.query(here, predicate="dwithin", distance=clear)) > 0: continue key = (int(x // cell), int(y // cell)) crowd = [p for dx in (-1, 0, 1) for dy in (-1, 0, 1) for p in taken.get((key[0] + dx, key[1] + dy), ())] if any(abs(px - x) < apart and abs(py - y) < apart for px, py in crowd): continue taken.setdefault(key, []).append((x, y)) ring = [(x - half_w, y - half_h), (x + half_w, y - half_h), (x + half_w, y + half_h), (x - half_w, y + half_h), (x - half_w, y - half_h)] tags = {k: v for k, v in f.tags.items() if k in BUILDING_TAGS} tags.setdefault("building", "house") made.append(OSMFeature(osm_id=f.osm_id, kind="way", tags=tags, geometry=[proj.to_latlon(px, py) for px, py in ring])) return made

nodes.name: _buildings_geojson
nodes.body_text: def _buildings_geojson(feats: list[OSMFeature], indoor: list[OSMFeature] = ()) -> dict: """Export building footprints so the user knows where to drop .tbx lots. Ways tagged indoor=room are attached to the building they stand in, as a "rooms" property: the mapper's own interior walls, which knoxbuild cuts the ground floor along instead of guessing at it (knoxbuild/build.py, knoxbuild/layout._mapped_rooms). """ from shapely.geometry import MultiPolygon, Polygon features = [] polys = [] # each building's shape, only built when rooms must fit for f in feats: if f.kind == "way": coords = [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in f.geometry] if len(coords) >= 3: features.append({ "type": "Feature", # amenity/shop/leisure carry what a building actually is # far more reliably than the building tag alone, and # knoxbuild uses them to pick materials and room plans. "properties": {k: v for k, v in f.tags.items() if k in BUILDING_TAGS}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [coords]}, }) if indoor: g = Polygon(coords) polys.append(g if g.is_valid else g.buffer(0)) elif f.kind == "relation": rings = [] for role, ring in f.role_geoms: if role == "inner": continue coords = [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in ring] if len(coords) >= 3: rings.append(coords) if rings: features.append({ "type": "Feature", "properties": {k: v for k, v in f.tags.items() if k in BUILDING_TAGS}, "geometry": {"type": "MultiPolygon", "coordinates": [[r] for r in rings]}, }) if indoor: g = MultiPolygon([Polygon(r) for r in rings]) polys.append(g if g.is_valid else g.buffer(0)) if indoor and features: import numpy as np # One representative point per room, against the bounding boxes of all # buildings first: a city can hold thousands of each, and only the # handful of buildings whose box holds the point are asked properly. boxes = np.array([g.bounds for g in polys]) for f in indoor: if len(f.geometry) < 3: continue ring = [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in f.geometry] room = Polygon(ring) if not room.is_valid: room = room.buffer(0) if room.is_empty: continue p = room.representative_point() near = np.flatnonzero((boxes[:, 0] <= p.x) & (p.x <= boxes[:, 2]) & (boxes[:, 1] <= p.y) & (p.y <= boxes[:, 3])) for i in near.tolist(): if polys[i].contains(p): features[i]["properties"].setdefault("rooms", []).append( {"ring": ring, "room": f.tags.get("room"), "amenity": f.tags.get("amenity")}) break return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}

nodes.name: furniture.py
nodes.body_text: """Street furniture and road wear: lamps, signs, hydrants, drains, cracks and litter.""" from __future__ import annotations import os from PIL import Image, ImageFilter from .. import pz_colors as C from ..osm import ROAD_HIERARCHY_BY_CODE # How often the vanilla streets have each, measured on their squares # (tools/building_stats.py's neighbourhoods): grime on 9% of the tarmac, cracks # on under 0.5%, a lamp per ~290 squares of street, and so on. Spacings are in # tiles along the kerb. # The grime was smooth dark patches on the road that read as shadows across it, # so it is off; set above 0 to bring it back. GRIME_SHARE = 0.0 # Roads at least this wide get a faded edge line down each side. EDGE_LINE_MIN_WIDTH = 5 CRACK_SHARE = 0.012 LITTER_SHARE = 0.002 LAMP_EVERY = 18 # A hydrant, a bin or a mailbox only stands where there is something for it to # serve: within this many tiles of a building. Out on open road they were # street furniture for nobody. NEAR_BUILDING_TILES = 12 # A speed limit sign every so many tiles along a main street's kerb (Erika's # Tiles only), with the limit going by how wide the carriageway is. SPEED_SIGN_EVERY = 80 SPEED_BY_WIDTH = ((12, 45), (8, 35), (0, 25)) BIN_EVERY = 28 MAILBOX_EVERY = 34 ROAD_FURNITURE_INTERVALS = { "motorway": {"lamp": 55, "hydrant": 1 << 30, "speed": 55, "drain": 40, "bin": 1 << 30, "mailbox": 1 << 30}, "trunk": {"lamp": 36, "hydrant": 80, "speed": 65, "drain": 32, "bin": 1 << 30, "mailbox": 1 << 30}, "primary": {"lamp": 20, "hydrant": 42, "speed": 75, "drain": 24, "bin": 24, "mailbox": 42}, "secondary": {"lamp": 18, "hydrant": 38, "speed": 85, "drain": 24, "bin": 26, "mailbox": 38}, "tertiary": {"lamp": 16, "hydrant": 35, "speed": 100, "drain": 24, "bin": 28, "mailbox": 34}, "residential": {"lamp": 14, "hydrant": 32, "speed": 120, "drain": 24, "bin": 28, "mailbox": 30}, "service": {"lamp": 30, "hydrant": 75, "speed": 1 << 30, "drain": 34, "bin": 36, "mailbox": 1 << 30}, "footway": {"lamp": 22, "hydrant": 1 << 30, "speed": 1 << 30, "drain": 1 << 30, "bin": 28, "mailbox": 1 << 30}, } HYDRANT_EVERY = 38 DRAIN_EVERY = 24

nodes.name: _mod_tiles_ready
nodes.body_text: def _mod_tiles_ready() -> bool: """Whether maps may use Erika's Tiles: installed and set up, and not turned off with KNOXMAP_NO_MOD_TILES=1.""" if os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_NO_MOD_TILES") == "1": return False try: import knoxpaths if not knoxpaths.erikas_tiles_ready(): return False # Tools set up before the signs existed have no rule for them, and a # colour without a rule is dropped with a warning: run Setup again. rules = knoxpaths.mapping_tools_dir() / "config" / "Rules.txt" return "KnoxMap road Speed limit 25 S" in rules.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no tools, no mod tiles return False

nodes.name: _paint_street_furniture
nodes.signature: def _paint_street_furniture(veg: Image.Image, landscape: Image.Image, road_hierarchy: Image.Image | None = None, buildings: Image.Image | None = None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def _paint_street_furniture(veg: Image.Image, landscape: Image.Image, road_hierarchy: Image.Image | None = None, buildings: Image.Image | None = None) -> dict: """Lamps, hydrants and drains along the kerbs; grime, cracks and litter. A generated street was clean tarmac, kerb and pavement and nothing else; Knox County's have all of these, and a road without them reads as a diagram. They go by the kerbs already painted: a lamp stands on the pavement one tile back from a straight kerb with its arm over the road, a hydrant likewise, a drain in the gutter in front of it. """ import numpy as np rng = np.random.default_rng(4321) ground = np.asarray(landscape.convert("RGB")) vp = np.array(veg.convert("RGB")) h, w = ground.shape[:2] road_classes = (np.asarray(road_hierarchy.convert("L")) if road_hierarchy is not None else None) def is_colour(arr, colours): mask = np.zeros(arr.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for c in colours: mask |= np.all(arr == c, axis=2) return mask empty = np.all(vp == 0, axis=2) asphalt = is_colour(ground, (C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT)) driveable = is_colour(ground, (C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT)) pavement = is_colour(ground, (C.PALE_CONCRETE,)) roadside = pavement | is_colour( ground, (C.DARK_GRASS, C.MEDIUM_GRASS, C.LIGHT_GRASS, C.PAVING, C.DIRT_ROWS_H, C.DIRT_ROWS_V)) # Hydrants, bins and mailboxes stand on the grass or paving beside the # sidewalk, never on the sidewalk itself, and only where there is a # building to serve: down an open stretch of road they were furniture for # nobody. verge = is_colour(ground, (C.DARK_GRASS, C.MEDIUM_GRASS, C.LIGHT_GRASS, C.PAVING)) near_buildings = None if buildings is not None: mask = buildings if buildings.mode == "L" else buildings.convert("L") reach = ImageFilter.MaxFilter(2 * NEAR_BUILDING_TILES + 1) near_buildings = np.asarray(mask.filter(reach)) > 0 counts = {} # Edge lines: tarmac with the road's edge on exactly one side and enough # road across from it to be a carriageway, not a car park aisle's end. # (Dark tarmac, 100, is car parks and yards, and is left out.) k = EDGE_LINE_MIN_WIDTH edge_lines = 0 diag_kerbs = {} for colour, (dx, dy) in ((C.EDGE_LINE_W, (-1, 0)), (C.EDGE_LINE_E, (1, 0)), (C.EDGE_LINE_N, (0, -1)), (C.EDGE_LINE_S, (0, 1))): outside = np.zeros_like(asphalt) across = np.ones_like(asphalt) if dx: if dx < 0: outside[:, 1:] = ~asphalt[:, :-1] for i in range(1, k): across[:, :-i] &= asphalt[:, i:] across[:, -i:] = False else: outside[:, :-1] = ~asphalt[:, 1:] for i in range(1, k): across[:, i:] &= asphalt[:, :-i] across[:, :i] = False side_a = np.zeros_like(asphalt); side_b = np.zeros_like(asphalt) side_a[1:, :] = asphalt[:-1, :]; side_b[:-1, :] = asphalt[1:, :] else: if dy < 0: outside[1:, :] = ~asphalt[:-1, :] for i in range(1, k): across[:-i, :] &= asphalt[i:, :] across[-i:, :] = False else: outside[:-1, :] = ~asphalt[1:, :] for i in range(1, k): across[i:, :] &= asphalt[:-i, :] across[:i, :] = False side_a = np.zeros_like(asphalt); side_b = np.zeros_like(asphalt) side_a[:, 1:] = asphalt[:, :-1]; side_b[:, :-1] = asphalt[:, 1:] # Straight edges only: the road continues along the line both ways. pick = asphalt & outside & across & side_a & side_b & empty diag_kerbs[colour] = asphalt & outside & across & (side_a | side_b) & ~pick vp[pick] = colour empty &= ~pick edge_lines += int(pick.sum()) counts["edge lines"] = edge_lines # Along each straight edge of the carriageway, road on one side: the lamp # stands a tile or two off the tarmac (past the kerb or on the verge) with # its arm reaching back over the road, the drain sits in the gutter. # (edge colour just painted, step away from the road, lamp colour) straight = [(C.EDGE_LINE_W, (-1, 0), C.LAMP_E), (C.EDGE_LINE_E, (1, 0), C.LAMP_W), (C.EDGE_LINE_N, (0, -1), C.LAMP_S), (C.EDGE_LINE_S, (0, 1), C.LAMP_N)] taken: dict[str, set] = { "lamp": set(), "hydrant": set(), "drain": set(), "speed": set(), "bin": set(), "mailbox": set(), } out = vp.copy() # Speed signs stand where drivers keeping right see their faces: on the # east kerb of a north-south road facing south, the north kerb of an # east-west one facing east. Erika's signs only face those two ways. speed_side = {C.EDGE_LINE_E: "S", C.EDGE_LINE_N: "E"} if _mod_tiles_ready() else {} def carriageway(gx, gy, sx, sy): n = 0 while n < 24 and 0 <= gx - n * sx < w and 0 <= gy - n * sy < h \ and asphalt[gy - n * sy, gx - n * sx]: n += 1 return n def hierarchy_at(gx, gy, sx, sy): if road_classes is None: return None for n in range(24): x, y = gx - n * sx, gy - n * sy if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): break if asphalt[y, x] and road_classes[y, x]: return ROAD_HIERARCHY_BY_CODE.get(int(road_classes[y, x])) return None def beside_the_pavement(gx, gy, sx, sy): """The first free grass or paving tile that touches the sidewalk.""" for n in range(2, 6): x, y = gx + n * sx, gy + n * sy if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): return None if not (empty[y, x] and not driveable[y, x] and verge[y, x]): continue for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1

nodes.name: is_colour
nodes.body_text: def is_colour(arr, colours): mask = np.zeros(arr.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for c in colours: mask |= np.all(arr == c, axis=2) return mask

nodes.name: carriageway
nodes.body_text: def carriageway(gx, gy, sx, sy): n = 0 while n < 24 and 0 <= gx - n * sx < w and 0 <= gy - n * sy < h \ and asphalt[gy - n * sy, gx - n * sx]: n += 1 return n

nodes.name: hierarchy_at
nodes.body_text: def hierarchy_at(gx, gy, sx, sy): if road_classes is None: return None for n in range(24): x, y = gx - n * sx, gy - n * sy if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): break if asphalt[y, x] and road_classes[y, x]: return ROAD_HIERARCHY_BY_CODE.get(int(road_classes[y, x])) return None

nodes.name: beside_the_pavement
nodes.body_text: def beside_the_pavement(gx, gy, sx, sy): """The first free grass or paving tile that touches the sidewalk.""" for n in range(2, 6): x, y = gx + n * sx, gy + n * sy if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): return None if not (empty[y, x] and not driveable[y, x] and verge[y, x]): continue for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)): nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and pavement[ny, nx]: return x, y return None

nodes.name: geometry.py
nodes.body_text: """Small geometry helpers and the pixel drawing primitives the passes share.""" from __future__ import annotations import math from PIL import Image, ImageDraw from ..osm import OSMFeature from .projection import Projector # A road that comes back to where it started is a ring road, a roundabout or a # loop of lane - not a plot of ground. Filled as an area it paved everything # inside it: a road drawn round a town, or a closed loop of roads, turned the # whole town to tarmac. Only a mapper who says it is an area makes it one. _LINEAR_HIGHWAYS = frozenset({ "motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary", "tertiary", "residential", "unclassified", "living_street", "service", "track", "path", "cycleway", "bridleway", "steps", "motorway_link", "trunk_link", "primary_link", "secondary_link", "tertiary_link"})

nodes.name: _pixel_width
nodes.body_text: def _pixel_width(metres: float, metres_per_tile: float) -> int: """Convert a real width to the nearest whole bitmap tile, never zero.""" return max(1, int(math.floor(metres / max(0.05, metres_per_tile) + 0.5)))

nodes.name: _feature_coords_px
nodes.signature: def _feature_coords_px(feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector) -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]
nodes.body_text: def _feature_coords_px(feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector) -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]: """Project every ring/linestring in this feature to pixel space.""" if feat.kind == "way": return [[proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in feat.geometry]] if feat.kind == "relation": rings: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = [] for _role, coords in feat.role_geoms: rings.append([proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in coords]) return rings if feat.kind == "node": la, lo = feat.geometry[0] return [[proj.to_px(la, lo)]] return []

nodes.name: _is_polygon
nodes.body_text: def _is_polygon(feat: OSMFeature) -> bool: """Treat as polygon if first/last point match (way) or it's a relation - unless it is a road, which stays a line however it loops.""" if feat.kind == "relation": return True if feat.kind == "way" and len(feat.geometry) >= 3: # Drawn on the map as a line, so a line it stays when it closes. if feat.tags.get("knox:line") == "yes": return False if (feat.geometry[0] == feat.geometry[-1] and feat.tags.get("highway") in _LINEAR_HIGHWAYS and feat.tags.get("area") != "yes" and "area:highway" not in feat.tags): return False return feat.geometry[0] == feat.geometry[-1] return False

nodes.name: _paint_multipolygon
nodes.signature: def _paint_multipolygon(image: Image.Image, feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector, fill: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _paint_multipolygon(image: Image.Image, feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector, fill: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None: """Fill a relation's outer rings and leave its inner rings as they were. An island in a lake or a clearing in a wood is an inner ring. Drawn like the outers it was flooded or planted over; here it is cut out of a mask the size of the relation, so whatever lies under it shows through. """ rings = [(role, [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in ring]) for role, ring in feat.role_geoms if len(ring) >= 3] if not rings: return xs = [x for _r, ring in rings for x, _y in ring] ys = [y for _r, ring in rings for _x, y in ring] x0, y0 = max(0, int(min(xs))), max(0, int(min(ys))) x1, y1 = min(image.width, int(max(xs)) + 2), min(image.height, int(max(ys)) + 2) if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0: return mask = Image.new("L", (x1 - x0, y1 - y0), 0) md = ImageDraw.Draw(mask) for role, ring in sorted(rings, key=lambda r: r[0] == "inner"): md.polygon([(x - x0, y - y0) for x, y in ring], fill=0 if role == "inner" else 255) image.paste(Image.new("RGB", mask.size, fill), (x0, y0), mask)

nodes.name: _draw_polygon
nodes.signature: def _draw_polygon(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, rings: list[list[tuple[float, float]]], fill: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _draw_polygon(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, rings: list[list[tuple[float, float]]], fill: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None: for ring in rings: if len(ring) >= 3: draw.polygon(ring, fill=fill)

nodes.name: _draw_line
nodes.signature: def _draw_line(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, rings: list[list[tuple[float, float]]], fill: tuple[int, int, int], width_px: int) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _draw_line(draw: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, rings: list[list[tuple[float, float]]], fill: tuple[int, int, int], width_px: int) -> None: w = max(1, int(round(width_px))) for ring in rings: if len(ring) >= 2: draw.line(ring, fill=fill, width=w, joint="curve") # Round line caps so intersections look right. r = w // 2 if r > 0: for x, y in ring: draw.ellipse((x - r, y - r, x + r, y + r), fill=fill)

nodes.name: _draw_roads
nodes.body_text: def _draw_roads(image: Image.Image, strokes, fill) -> None: """Constant-width road strokes, joined across OSM ways with 45-degree bevels.""" from shapely.geometry import LineString from shapely.ops import linemerge, unary_union groups = {} for width, rings in strokes: width = max(1, int(round(width))) for ring in rings: points = [(round(x, 6), round(y, 6)) for x, y in ring] if len(set(points)) > 1: groups.setdefault(width, []).append(points) for width, rings in groups.items(): if width == 1: _draw_line(ImageDraw.Draw(image), rings, fill, width) continue # Pillow includes both polygon boundaries: subtract one to keep even widths exact. shift = 0.5 if width % 2 == 0 else 0.0 lines = [LineString([(x + shift, y + shift) for x, y in ring]) for ring in rings] network = unary_union(lines) if network.geom_type == "MultiLineString": network = linemerge(network) surface = network.buffer((width - 1) / 2, cap_style="round", join_style="bevel") if surface.is_empty: continue x0, y0, x1, y1 = surface.bounds left, top = max(0, math.floor(x0)), max(0, math.floor(y0)) right, bottom = min(image.width, math.ceil(x1) + 1), min(image.height, math.ceil(y1) + 1) if right <= left or bottom <= top: continue mask = Image.new("L", (right - left, bottom - top), 0) draw = ImageDraw.Draw(mask) for poly in getattr(surface, "geoms", None) or [surface]: draw.polygon([(round(x - left), round(y - top)) for x, y in poly.exterior.coords], fill=255) for hole in poly.interiors: draw.polygon([(round(x - left), round(y - top)) for x, y in hole.coords], fill=0) image.paste(fill, (left, top, right, bottom), mask)

nodes.name: gridangle.py
nodes.body_text: """Which way the street grid runs, so a town can be turned square to the map.""" from __future__ import annotations import math from typing import Iterable from ..osm import OSMFeature, classify from .geometry import _is_polygon from .projection import Projector # Roads that count towards a town's street grid. Paths wander, and a motorway # slicing through at its own angle should not turn the town around it. GRID_ROADS = {"road_minor", "road_medium", "road_service", "pedestrian"} # How strongly the streets must agree on a direction before the map is turned # to it: 1 is a perfect grid, 0 no preference. This is measured against *all* # road in the box, so a town with a second phase, or rural lanes round it, # scores low even when its winning district is a perfectly good grid: measured # maps whose roads were left staircased scored 0.135 (a clear -38.9 degree # grid), 0.223 and 0.234, while a single-phase town scored 0.281. The old 0.25 # cut-off turned none of the first three, so every street stayed at its # real-world angle. The district clustering already rejects a town with no # grid; this only has to reject a stray lane. ALIGN_MIN_STRENGTH = 0.12 # Per-district street grid (dominant_road_angle). The map is one tile grid and # is turned by one angle, but the angle is chosen *per neighbourhood* now: the # bbox is cut into cells of this many metres, each cell measures its own local # grid, and the cells vote. Averaging a town that grew in two or three phases # used to land the rotation halfway between them - a compromise angle that # straightens none of the districts - and a long avenue at its own angle used # to sway the whole town because it carried more length than it deserved. # 400 m is a few blocks: small enough that two grids a street apart are told # apart, big enough that a local grid can be measured inside one cell. DISTRICT_CELL_M = 400.0 # A cell with less road than this in it has nothing to vote with - a park # edge, a stub - and abstains rather than letting one corner decide the turn. DISTRICT_MIN_ROAD_M = 60.0 # Two local grids whose angles are this close (degrees, ignoring the # 90-degree period of a grid) are the same district and vote together. DISTRICT_CLUSTER_DEG = 12.0

nodes.name: _grid_delta
nodes.body_text: def _grid_delta(a: float, b: float) -> float: """How far two grid angles are apart in degrees, ignoring the 90-degree period: 44 degrees and -44 degrees are the same grid, two degrees off.""" d = abs(a - b) % 90.0 return min(d, 90.0 - d)

nodes.name: dominant_road_angle
nodes.signature: def dominant_road_angle(features: Iterable[OSMFeature], south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float) -> tuple[float, float]
nodes.body_text: def dominant_road_angle(features: Iterable[OSMFeature], south: float, west: float, north: float, east: float) -> tuple[float, float]: """The main direction of a town's streets, and how strongly they share it. Tiles are square, so a street at 20 degrees becomes a staircase with a step every few tiles - kerbs zigzagging along it and blends failing at every corner. Most towns have a grid, even a loose one; turning the whole map so that grid runs along the tiles straightens every street on it. Buildings, fences and the paper map are projected the same way, so nothing is misaligned - only north is no longer straight up. The angle is measured per district, not once over the whole town. Each DISTRICT_CELL_M cell of the bbox measures its own local grid (directions averaged with a 90-degree period, segments weighed by length, as before), and cells whose local grid is within DISTRICT_CLUSTER_DEG of one another vote together as one district. The district holding the most street wins, and the rotation is its angle. This matters where a town grew in phases: an old core on one grid and an extension on another used to average into an angle that belonged to neither, so both districts stayed staircases. Now the district with the most street runs straight. The rotation is still one angle for the whole map - the game's tile grid is global - so streets on the losing grid keep their offset; "Knox County roads" is the setting that bends those. Returns (angle, strength): the angle in degrees in (-45, 45], counter- clockwise from east, and the strength in [0, 1] - how much of the town's grid road the winning district's straightened direction accounts for. A town with no district big enough to vote falls back to the plain town-wide mean, which is what it always did. """ proj = Projector.build(south, west, north, east, 1.0) # (sin sum, cos sum, length) per district cell, plus the town-wide totals. cells: dict[tuple[int, int], list[float]] = {} sin_sum = cos_sum = total = 0.0 for feat in features: if feat.kind != "way" or classify(feat.tags, _is_polygon(feat)) not in GRID_ROADS: continue pts = [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in feat.geometry] for (ax, ay), (bx, by) in zip(pts, pts[1:]): dx, dy = bx - ax, ay - by # tile y grows south; flip to north-up length = math.hypot(dx, dy) if length < 1: continue # Only the street that is on the map has a say. The features include # what was fetched beyond it (a turned map downloads a margin all the # way round, and a long way is whole however far it runs), and a # bigger grid in that margin used to decide how the map was turned. mid_x, mid_y = (ax + bx) / 2, (ay + by) / 2 if not (0 <= mid_x < proj.width and 0 <= mid_y < proj.height): continue a = 4 * math.atan2(dy, dx) s, c = length * math.sin(a), length * math.cos(a) sin_sum += s cos_sum += c total += length key = (math.floor(mid_x / DISTRICT_CELL_M), math.floor(mid_y / DISTRICT_CELL_M)) slot = cells.get(key) if slot is None: cells[key] = [s, c, length] else: slot[0] += s slot[1] += c slot[2] += length if total == 0: return 0.0, 0.0 # Every cell with enough road in it is one district's vote: its local # angle, weighted by how much street stands behind it and how well those # streets agree (a cell of crossed lanes has little to say). votes: list[tuple[float, float, float, float]] = [] # angle, weight, sin, cos for s, c, length in cells.values(): if length < DISTRICT_MIN_ROAD_M: continue agree = math.hypot(s, c) / length weight = length * agree if weight <= 0: continue votes.append((math.degrees(math.atan2(s, c) / 4), weight, s, c)) if not votes: # Only stubs and scattered lanes: no district to ask, so the town as a # whole answers, exactly as it did before districts were measured. return (math.degrees(math.atan2(sin_sum, cos_sum) / 4), math.hypot(sin_sum, cos_sum) / total) # Cluster the votes greedily from the strongest district outwards. Each # cell joins the strongest unassigned seed it is within DISTRICT_CLUSTER_DEG # of, so one grid can gather its own phase and the next seed starts a new # one; the cluster with the most street wins. votes.sort(key=lambda v: (-v[1], v[0])) assigned = [False] * len(votes) best: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None # magnitude, sin, cos for i, (seed_angle, _weight, _s, _c) in enumerate(votes): if assigned[i]: continue assigned[i] = True members = [i] for j in range(i + 1, len(votes)): if not assigned[j] and _grid_delta(seed_angle, votes[j][0]) <= DISTRICT_CLUSTER_DEG: assigned[j] = True members.append(j) m_sin = sum(votes[m][2] for m in members) m_cos = sum(votes[m][3] for m in members) magnitude = math.hypot(m_sin, m_cos) if best is None or magnitude > best[0]: best = (magnitude, m_sin, m_cos) _magnitude, m_sin, m_cos = best angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(m_sin, m_cos) / 4) # How much of the town's grid road the winning district accounts for: a # second phase on the far side of the map lowers it, as disagreement did # before, but no longer drags the angle off the grid it belongs to. return angle, _magnitu

nodes.name: infill.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings for the gaps along a street that has buildings either side of them. OpenStreetMap is traced by hand, so a high street can have its first six shops drawn, the seventh missing and the next four drawn again. The generated map then has a hole in the row where anyone can see a building belongs. This fills those holes, and only those: it looks at what stands along each street, finds a stretch of frontage with nothing on it between buildings that are there, and puts buildings in it that are built like their neighbours. What "like their neighbours" means is measured, not assumed, from the buildings on either side of the gap: width how much street each one takes up depth how far back it goes set back how far its front wall stands from the edge of the pavement kind house, shop, flats ... and how many storeys A street wall (shops standing on the pavement) is filled wall to wall; a row of houses with gardens is filled with houses with a gap between. A lot is dropped rather than squeezed in wherever it would touch a building, a road, water, a park, a wood or the edge of the drawn map, and a stretch with a building on neither side is left alone: this extends a street that is there, it does not found a town. `houses_from_addresses` (buildings.py) and Overture (generator/overture.py) are the other two ways a map gets buildings OSM does not have; this one needs no data from anywhere. """ from __future__ import annotations import statistics from collections import Counter from ..osm import OSMFeature, classify from .buildings import ADDRESS_AVOIDS_ROADS from .geometry import _feature_coords_px, _is_polygon from .landcover import WATERWAY_WIDTH_M from .projection import Projector from .widths import _sidewalk_width_m, _way_width_m # Streets that get frontage looked at. Service lanes and drives do not: a # building beside one is a shed or a back door, not a street front. FRONTAGE_ROADS = ("road_major", "road_medium", "road_minor") STEP_M = 2.0 # how often the frontage is looked at REACH_BUILDING_M = 20.0 # a building this close behind the pavement fronts the street REACH_M = 40.0 # how far back the probe looks for anything at all MIN_DEPTH_M = 7.0 # less room than this and nothing fits REAR_CLEAR_M = 2.5 # kept clear behind a new building MIN_NEIGHBOUR_M2 = 40.0 # sheds and garages say nothing about the street MIN_LOT_M = 5.0 # narrowest new building MAX_LOT_M = 28.0 # widest; a longer gap is cut into more lots SIDE_STEPS = 4 # stations of side gap a row is carried across SIDE_GAP_M = 3.0 # between detached houses EDGE_SLACK_M = 0.05 # so a side gap never rounds to under SIDE_GAP_M # on its way through lat/lon and back STREET_WALL_M = 3.5 # set back less than this and the row is a street wall MAX_GAP_BOTH_M = 140.0 # longest gap filled with a building on both sides MAX_GAP_ONE_M = 45.0 # and with one: the row is carried a little further MAX_PER_GAP = 12 MAX_INFILL = 20000 FIRST_ID = -2_000_000_000 # below Overture's (generator/overture.py) # What may be copied from a neighbour. Anything else beside the gap - a church, # a school, a warehouse, a garage - does not say what stands next to it. FILL_KINDS = {"yes", "house", "detached", "semidetached_house", "terrace", "residential", "apartments", "retail", "commercial", "office", "hotel", "dormitory", "mixed_use"} # Ground that is not for building on, drawn as areas. BLOCKING_AREAS = {"water", "pool", "park", "sports", "playground", "cemetery", "wetland", "track", "parking", "plaza", "sand", "orchard", "farmland", "pier", "military", "schoolyard", "worship_grounds", "hospital_grounds", "pedestrian"} BLOCKING_VEGETATION = {"forest", "scrub"} CHOP_M = 200.0 # Sheds and garages behind the houses along a street: what a yard has in it. SHED_HOUSE_KINDS = {"house", "detached", "semidetached_house", "residential", "yes"} SHED_HOUSE_M2 = (70.0, 300.0) # smaller is a shed already, bigger is not a house SHED_NEAR_STREET_M = 30.0 # a house this close to a street stands on it SHED_SHARE = 35 # per cent of the houses that have one SHED_SIZE_M = ((3.0, 6.0), (3.0, 5.0)) # across, deep SHED_BEHIND_M = 2.0 # clear of the house's back wall SHED_CLEAR_M = 3.0 # kept clear of any outbuilding already there MAX_SHEDS = 20000

nodes.name: _polys
nodes.signature: def _polys(feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector, scale: float)
nodes.body_text: def _polys(feat: OSMFeature, proj: Projector, scale: float): """A feature's outlines as shapely polygons in metres.""" from shapely.geometry import Polygon out = [] for ring in _feature_coords_px(feat, proj): if len(ring) < 3: continue poly = Polygon([(x * scale, y * scale) for x, y in ring]) if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) for part in getattr(poly, "geoms", [poly]): if part.geom_type == "Polygon" and part.area > 0: out.append(part) return out

nodes.name: _chopped
nodes.body_text: def _chopped(geoms): """The same ground in pieces no bigger than CHOP_M across. A wood or a lake can have a thousand vertices and the extent of the map, and every probe that lands in its bounding box is tested against all of them: minutes on a county. In squares each test is against a few. """ import numpy as np import shapely from shapely.geometry import box out = [] for g in shapely.simplify(np.array(geoms, dtype=object), 0.5): x0, y0, x1, y1 = g.bounds if (x1 - x0 <= CHOP_M and y1 - y0 <= CHOP_M) or g.geom_type != "Polygon": out.append(g) continue shapely.prepare(g) for cx in range(int(x0 // CHOP_M), int(x1 // CHOP_M) + 1): for cy in range(int(y0 // CHOP_M), int(y1 // CHOP_M) + 1): square = box(cx * CHOP_M, cy * CHOP_M, (cx + 1) * CHOP_M, (cy + 1) * CHOP_M) if not g.intersects(square): continue piece = g.intersection(square) out.extend(p for p in getattr(piece, "geoms", [piece]) if p.geom_type == "Polygon" and not p.is_empty) return np.array(out, dtype=object)

nodes.name: _Grid
nodes.body_text: class _Grid: """New lots, found again by where they are, so a lot is only checked against the ones near it.""" CELL = 40.0 def __init__(self): self.cells: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} def near(self, poly): x0, y0, x1, y1 = poly.bounds seen, out = set(), [] for cx in range(int(x0 // self.CELL), int(x1 // self.CELL) + 1): for cy in range(int(y0 // self.CELL), int(y1 // self.CELL) + 1): for p in self.cells.get((cx, cy), ()): if id(p) not in seen: seen.add(id(p)) out.append(p) return out def add(self, poly): x0, y0, x1, y1 = poly.bounds for cx in range(int(x0 // self.CELL), int(x1 // self.CELL) + 1): for cy in range(int(y0 // self.CELL), int(y1 // self.CELL) + 1): self.cells.setdefault((cx, cy), []).append(poly)

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.body_text: def __init__(self): self.cells: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {}

nodes.name: near
nodes.body_text: def near(self, poly): x0, y0, x1, y1 = poly.bounds seen, out = set(), [] for cx in range(int(x0 // self.CELL), int(x1 // self.CELL) + 1): for cy in range(int(y0 // self.CELL), int(y1 // self.CELL) + 1): for p in self.cells.get((cx, cy), ()): if id(p) not in seen: seen.add(id(p)) out.append(p) return out

nodes.name: add
nodes.body_text: def add(self, poly): x0, y0, x1, y1 = poly.bounds for cx in range(int(x0 // self.CELL), int(x1 // self.CELL) + 1): for cy in range(int(y0 // self.CELL), int(y1 // self.CELL) + 1): self.cells.setdefault((cx, cy), []).append(poly)

nodes.name: _side_scan
nodes.signature: def _side_scan(line, half_edge, sign, buildings, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree)
nodes.body_text: def _side_scan(line, half_edge, sign, buildings, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree): """Look along one side of a street, every STEP_M. Returns the stations (position, tangent, normal) and, for each, its state: ("B", building index, distance) where a building stands in front of it, ("E", free depth) where nothing does, and ("X",) where it is blocked. """ import numpy as np import shapely length = line.length s = np.arange(STEP_M / 2, length, STEP_M) if len(s) < 3: return None pts = shapely.line_interpolate_point(line, s) ahead = shapely.line_interpolate_point(line, np.minimum(s + 1.0, length)) behind = shapely.line_interpolate_point(line, np.maximum(s - 1.0, 0.0)) px, py = shapely.get_x(pts), shapely.get_y(pts) tx = shapely.get_x(ahead) - shapely.get_x(behind) ty = shapely.get_y(ahead) - shapely.get_y(behind) norm = np.hypot(tx, ty) norm[norm == 0] = 1.0 tx, ty = tx / norm, ty / norm nx, ny = -ty * sign, tx * sign # out from the road, on this side ax, ay = px + nx * half_edge, py + ny * half_edge anchors = shapely.points(ax, ay) probes = shapely.linestrings(np.stack( [np.stack([ax, ay], axis=1), np.stack([ax + nx * REACH_M, ay + ny * REACH_M], axis=1)], axis=1)) n = len(s) hard = np.full(n, REACH_M) if hard_tree is not None: pi, gi = hard_tree.query(probes, predicate="intersects") if len(pi): d = shapely.distance(anchors[pi], hard_geoms[gi]) np.minimum.at(hard, pi, d) near_b = np.full(n, np.inf) which = np.full(n, -1) if b_tree is not None: pi, gi = b_tree.query(probes, predicate="intersects") if len(pi): d = shapely.distance(anchors[pi], buildings[gi]) order = np.lexsort((d, pi)) pi, gi, d = pi[order], gi[order], d[order] first = np.unique(pi, return_index=True)[1] near_b[pi[first]] = d[first] which[pi[first]] = gi[first] return {"s": s, "x": px, "y": py, "tx": tx, "ty": ty, "nx": nx, "ny": ny, "ax": ax, "ay": ay, "hard": hard, "near_b": near_b, "which": which}

nodes.name: _states
nodes.body_text: def _states(scan): """B (built on), E (free, with room), X (no room) for each station.""" out = [] for hard, nb in zip(scan["hard"], scan["near_b"]): if nb <= REACH_BUILDING_M and nb < hard: out.append("B") elif min(hard, nb) < MIN_DEPTH_M: out.append("X") else: out.append("E") return out

nodes.name: _neighbours
nodes.signature: def _neighbours(scan, states, i, step, info, limit=3)
nodes.body_text: def _neighbours(scan, states, i, step, info, limit=3): """The buildings (up to `limit`) in the unbroken stretch of built frontage that starts next to station `i` and goes in direction `step`, and whether that stretch is more than one building: a row joined wall to wall.""" seen: list[int] = [] joined = False j = i while 0 <= j < len(states): if states[j] != "B": # The side gap between two detached houses is not the end of the # row: step over it to the next building. k = j while (0 <= k < len(states) and states[k] != "B" and abs(k - j) <= SIDE_STEPS): k += step if not (0 <= k < len(states) and states[k] == "B" and seen): break j = k continue b = int(scan["which"][j]) if b not in seen: if len(seen) == limit: break if seen and states[j - step] == "B": joined = True # wall to wall, no gap between seen.append(b) j += step return ([info[b] for b in seen if info[b] and info[b]["area"] >= MIN_NEIGHBOUR_M2], joined)

nodes.name: _describe
nodes.body_text: def _describe(scan, states, bi, poly, tags): """How one neighbouring building sits on the street: the metres of frontage it takes up, how deep it is, how far back it stands.""" idx = [k for k, (st, w) in enumerate(zip(states, scan["which"])) if st == "B" and int(w) == bi] if not idx: return None width = (idx[-1] - idx[0] + 1) * STEP_M k = idx[len(idx) // 2] nx, ny = scan["nx"][k], scan["ny"][k] tx, ty = scan["tx"][k], scan["ty"][k] ox, oy = scan["ax"][k], scan["ay"][k] proj_d = [(x - ox) * nx + (y - oy) * ny for x, y in poly.exterior.coords] # Where its side walls are along the street. The stations are STEP_M # apart, so one can land on a side wall and fall either way by rounding; # a gap is measured from these instead. proj_s = [(x - ox) * tx + (y - oy) * ty for x, y in poly.exterior.coords] return {"width": width, "depth": max(proj_d) - min(proj_d), "setback": max(0.0, min(proj_d)), "area": poly.area, "s_lo": scan["s"][k] + min(proj_s), "s_hi": scan["s"][k] + max(proj_s), "kind": (tags.get("building") or "yes").lower(), "levels": tags.get("building:levels")}

nodes.name: _modal_kind
nodes.body_text: def _modal_kind(near): kinds = Counter(n["kind"] for n in near) return max(kinds, key=lambda k: (kinds[k], k != "yes"))

nodes.name: _levels
nodes.body_text: def _levels(near): vals = [] for n in near: try: v = int(float(str(n["levels"]).split(";")[0])) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue if 0 < v < 60: vals.append(v) return str(int(round(statistics.median(vals)))) if vals else None

nodes.name: _lots_for_gap
nodes.signature: def _lots_for_gap(scan, i0, i1, left, right, hard_free, joined=False, lo=None, hi=None)
nodes.body_text: def _lots_for_gap(scan, i0, i1, left, right, hard_free, joined=False, lo=None, hi=None): """Footprints (as lists of four metre corners) for the free frontage between stations i0 and i1, built like the buildings beside it. `joined` says the row beside it stands wall to wall; `lo` and `hi` are the side walls of the buildings at either end, along the street, where there are any.""" near = left + right # One side only is a row carried on, and a row is two buildings at least; # a lone house in the country does not found a street. if not near or (not (left and right) and len(near) < 2): return [] kinds = {n["kind"] for n in near} if not kinds <= FILL_KINDS: return [] width = statistics.median(n["width"] for n in near) depth = statistics.median(n["depth"] for n in near) setback = statistics.median(n["setback"] for n in near) # Close to the pavement is not enough: detached houses can stand there # too, and a hole in their row gets their side gaps, not a terrace. wall = setback <= STREET_WALL_M and joined gap = 0.0 if wall else SIDE_GAP_M length = (i1 - i0 + 1) * STEP_M both = bool(left and right) limit = min(MAX_GAP_BOTH_M, max(40.0, 10 * width)) if both else \ min(MAX_GAP_ONE_M, max(20.0, 2.5 * width)) if length < MIN_LOT_M: return [] if length > limit: # Too long to fill whole: carry the row on from each neighbour as far # as a row is carried (half the limit from each end when both stand), # and leave the middle as it is. reach = int((limit / 2 if both else limit) // STEP_M) done = [] for part in ((i0, i0 + reach - 1, left, [], lo, None) if left else None, (i1 - reach + 1, i1, [], right, None, hi) if right else None): if part is None or reach < 1: continue got = _lots_for_gap(scan, part[0], part[1], part[2], part[3], hard_free, joined, part[4], part[5]) if got: done.append(got) if not done: return [] return ([lot for g in done for lot in g[0]], done[0][1], done[0][2]) # The pavement edge of the gap; ends against a neighbour keep a garden's # width from it, ends against a road or nothing keep a little less. inset_l = 0.4 if wall else (SIDE_GAP_M + EDGE_SLACK_M if left else 1.5) inset_r = 0.4 if wall else (SIDE_GAP_M + EDGE_SLACK_M if right else 1.5) # A neighbour's wall is trusted only within a station of the gap's end: # that is the rounding it is there to settle. Further off, the building # meets the street at a corner - a bend, a slanted outline - and its wall # can lie twenty metres past the gap. edge0, edge1 = i0 * STEP_M, (i1 + 1) * STEP_M if lo is not None and abs(lo - edge0) <= STEP_M: edge0 = lo if hi is not None and abs(hi - edge1) <= STEP_M: edge1 = hi start = edge0 + inset_l end = edge1 - inset_r span = end - start if span < MIN_LOT_M: return [] target = min(max(width, 6.0), MAX_LOT_M) # Room for a building about as wide as its neighbours or it is a yard, not # a gap: the garden between two houses is not a house that was not drawn. if span < 0.7 * target: return [] n = max(1, int(round((span + gap) / (target + gap)))) n = min(n, MAX_PER_GAP) while n > 1 and (span - (n - 1) * gap) / n < MIN_LOT_M: n -= 1 while (span - (n - 1) * gap) / n > MAX_LOT_M and n < MAX_PER_GAP: n += 1 bw = (span - (n - 1) * gap) / n if bw < MIN_LOT_M: return [] out = [] for k in range(n): a = start + k * (bw + gap) b = a + bw # which stations this lot spans, for the room behind it and the angle k0 = min(max(i0, int(a // STEP_M)), i1) k1 = max(min(i1, int(b // STEP_M)), k0) room = min(hard_free[k0:k1 + 1]) d = min(depth, room - setback - REAR_CLEAR_M) if d < MIN_DEPTH_M: continue mid = min(max(int(((a + b) / 2) // STEP_M), i0), i1) tx, ty = scan["tx"][mid], scan["ty"][mid] nx, ny = scan["nx"][mid], scan["ny"][mid] # the pavement point opposite the lot's middle off = (a + b) / 2 - scan["s"][mid] cx = scan["ax"][mid] + tx * off cy = scan["ay"][mid] + ty * off cx += nx * (max(setback, 0.3) + d / 2) cy += ny * (max(setback, 0.3) + d / 2) hw, hd = bw / 2, d / 2 out.append([(cx - tx * hw - nx * hd, cy - ty * hw - ny * hd), (cx + tx * hw - nx * hd, cy + ty * hw - ny * hd), (cx + tx * hw + nx * hd, cy + ty * hw + ny * hd), (cx - tx * hw + nx * hd, cy - ty * hw + ny * hd)]) return out, _modal_kind(near), _levels(near)

nodes.name: _world
nodes.signature: def _world(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector)
nodes.body_text: def _world(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector): """What stands, what cannot be built on and which streets are looked along, or None when there is nothing to look at.""" import numpy as np import shapely from shapely.geometry import LineString, Polygon from shapely.strtree import STRtree from .projection import _inside k = proj.meters_per_tile # Everything already standing. b_polys, b_tags = [], [] for f in building_feats: for poly in _polys(f, proj, k): b_polys.append(poly) b_tags.append(f.tags) if not b_polys: return None b_geoms = np.array(b_polys, dtype=object) b_tree = STRtree(b_geoms) # Everything a building cannot stand on: the roads' own width and pavement # (every kind of street, not only the ones looked along), railways, water, # parks and woods. hard: list = [] fronts = [] for cat in ADDRESS_AVOIDS_ROADS | {"railway"}: for f in buckets.get(cat, []): if _is_polygon(f): continue half = _way_width_m(f, cat) / 2 + _sidewalk_width_m(f, cat) for ring in _feature_coords_px(f, proj): if len(ring) < 2: continue line = LineString([(x * k, y * k) for x, y in ring]) if line.length < 0.5: continue hard.append(line.buffer(half, cap_style="flat")) if (cat in FRONTAGE_ROADS and line.length >= 3 * STEP_M and not f.tags.get("bridge") and not f.tags.get("tunnel") and f.tags.get("access") != "private"): fronts.append((line, half)) for cat in BLOCKING_AREAS: for f in buckets.get(cat, []): if _is_polygon(f): hard.extend(_polys(f, proj, k)) elif cat == "water": reach = WATERWAY_WIDTH_M.get(f.tags.get("waterway"), 3.0) / 2 + 1 for ring in _feature_coords_px(f, proj): if len(ring) >= 2: hard.append(LineString([(x * k, y * k) for x, y in ring]).buffer(reach)) for f in vegetation_feats: if _is_polygon(f) and classify(f.tags, True) in BLOCKING_VEGETATION: hard.extend(_polys(f, proj, k)) hard_geoms = _chopped(hard) if hard else None hard_tree = STRtree(hard_geoms) if hard else None if not fronts: return None return (k, b_polys, b_tags, b_geoms, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree, fronts)

nodes.name: _infill_frontage
nodes.signature: def _infill_frontage(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector, clip=None) -> list[OSMFeature]
nodes.body_text: def _infill_frontage(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector, clip=None) -> list[OSMFeature]: """New buildings for the gaps along streets. See the module docstring.""" from shapely.geometry import Polygon from .projection import _inside world = _world(buckets, vegetation_feats, building_feats, proj) if world is None: return [] k, b_polys, b_tags, b_geoms, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree, fronts = world width_m, height_m = proj.width * k, proj.height * k grid = _Grid() made: list[OSMFeature] = [] ident = FIRST_ID for line, half in fronts: for sign in (1, -1): if len(made) >= MAX_INFILL: break scan = _side_scan(line, half + 0.3, sign, b_geoms, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree) if scan is None: continue states = _states(scan) if "E" not in states or "B" not in states: continue info: dict[int, dict | None] = {} for bi in {int(w) for st, w in zip(states, scan["which"]) if st == "B"}: info[bi] = _describe(scan, states, bi, b_polys[bi], b_tags[bi]) free = [min(h, nb) for h, nb in zip(scan["hard"], scan["near_b"])] i = 0 while i < len(states): if states[i] != "E": i += 1 continue j = i while j + 1 < len(states) and states[j + 1] == "E": j += 1 left, joined_l = (_neighbours(scan, states, i - 1, -1, info) if i > 0 else ([], False)) right, joined_r = (_neighbours(scan, states, j + 1, 1, info) if j + 1 < len(states) else ([], False)) # the side walls of the buildings at either end of the gap end_l = info.get(int(scan["which"][i - 1])) if i > 0 else None end_r = info.get(int(scan["which"][j + 1])) if j + 1 < len(states) else None lo = end_l["s_hi"] if end_l and states[i - 1] == "B" else None hi = end_r["s_lo"] if end_r and states[j + 1] == "B" else None run = (i, j) i = j + 1 if not (left or right): continue got = _lots_for_gap(scan, run[0], run[1], left, right, free, joined_l or joined_r, lo, hi) if not got: continue lots, kind, levels = got for corners in lots: poly = Polygon(corners) if not poly.is_valid or poly.is_empty: continue x0, y0, x1, y1 = poly.bounds if x0 < 0 or y0 < 0 or x1 > width_m or y1 > height_m: continue core = poly.buffer(-0.4) if core.is_empty: continue if b_tree.query(core, predicate="intersects").size: continue if hard_tree is not None and hard_tree.query(core, predicate="intersects").size: continue if any(core.intersects(p) for p in grid.near(poly)): continue tags = {"building": kind} if levels: tags["building:levels"] = levels feat = OSMFeature( osm_id=ident, kind="way", tags=tags, geometry=[proj.to_latlon(x / k, y / k) for x, y in corners + [corners[0]]]) if clip is not None and not _inside(feat, proj, clip): continue grid.add(poly) made.append(feat) ident -= 1 return made

nodes.name: _back_sheds
nodes.signature: def _back_sheds(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector, clip=None) -> list[OSMFeature]
nodes.body_text: def _back_sheds(buckets: dict, vegetation_feats: list, building_feats: list, proj: Projector, clip=None) -> list[OSMFeature]: """A shed or garage behind some of the houses on each street. Only where there is room: nothing on it, nothing within SHED_CLEAR_M of it that is a building already, no road, water, park or wood. Which houses get one is a function of where they stand, so the same map comes out the same. """ import numpy as np from shapely.geometry import Point, Polygon from shapely.strtree import STRtree from .projection import _inside world = _world(buckets, vegetation_feats, building_feats, proj) if world is None: return [] k, b_polys, b_tags, b_geoms, b_tree, hard_geoms, hard_tree, fronts = world lines = np.array([line for line, _half in fronts], dtype=object) line_tree = STRtree(lines) width_m, height_m = proj.width * k, proj.height * k grid = _Grid() made: list[OSMFeature] = [] ident = FIRST_ID - MAX_INFILL - 1 # below the lots' ids for me, (poly, tags) in enumerate(zip(b_polys, b_tags)): if len(made) >= MAX_SHEDS: break if (tags.get("building") or "yes").lower() not in SHED_HOUSE_KINDS: continue if not SHED_HOUSE_M2[0] <= poly.area <= SHED_HOUSE_M2[1]: continue c = poly.centroid # which way is the street, and which way is back near = line_tree.nearest(c) line = lines[near] at = line.interpolate(line.project(c)) dx, dy = c.x - at.x, c.y - at.y dist = (dx * dx + dy * dy) ** 0.5 if dist == 0 or dist - 0.5 * poly.length / 4 > SHED_NEAR_STREET_M: continue nx, ny = dx / dist, dy / dist tx, ty = -ny, nx # a function of the house's place: 35% of them, and the shape h = (int(c.x * 10) * 73856093) ^ (int(c.y * 10) * 19349663) if h % 100 >= SHED_SHARE: continue r1, r2, r3 = (h >> 7) % 100 / 100, (h >> 14) % 100 / 100, (h >> 21) % 100 / 100 w = SHED_SIZE_M[0][0] + r1 * (SHED_SIZE_M[0][1] - SHED_SIZE_M[0][0]) d = SHED_SIZE_M[1][0] + r2 * (SHED_SIZE_M[1][1] - SHED_SIZE_M[1][0]) back = max((x - c.x) * nx + (y - c.y) * ny for x, y in poly.exterior.coords) side = (r3 - 0.5) * min(poly.length / 4, 8.0) cx = c.x + nx * (back + SHED_BEHIND_M + d / 2) + tx * side cy = c.y + ny * (back + SHED_BEHIND_M + d / 2) + ty * side corners = [(cx - tx * w / 2 - nx * d / 2, cy - ty * w / 2 - ny * d / 2), (cx + tx * w / 2 - nx * d / 2, cy + ty * w / 2 - ny * d / 2), (cx + tx * w / 2 + nx * d / 2, cy + ty * w / 2 + ny * d / 2), (cx - tx * w / 2 + nx * d / 2, cy - ty * w / 2 + ny * d / 2)] shed = Polygon(corners) x0, y0, x1, y1 = shed.bounds if x0 < 0 or y0 < 0 or x1 > width_m or y1 > height_m: continue if any(i != me for i in b_tree.query(shed.buffer(SHED_CLEAR_M), predicate="intersects")): continue if hard_tree is not None and hard_tree.query(shed.buffer(0.4), predicate="intersects").size: continue if any(shed.intersects(p) for p in grid.near(shed)): continue feat = OSMFeature( osm_id=ident, kind="way", tags={"building": "garage" if w >= 5.0 else "shed"}, geometry=[proj.to_latlon(x / k, y / k) for x, y in corners + [corners[0]]]) if clip is not None and not _inside(feat, proj, clip): continue grid.add(shed) made.append(feat) ident -= 1 return made

nodes.name: landcover.py
nodes.body_text: """What each kind of ground is: the draw order, the fill colours and the category sets.""" from __future__ import annotations from .. import pz_colors as C # ESA WorldCover class -> ground colour, painted under every OSM feature. # The table is data (knoxdata/worldcover.py reads it), but the colours are the # renderer's, so they live here with the rest of the palette. WORLDCOVER_PAINT = { 10: C.DARK_GRASS, # tree cover -> forest ground 20: C.MEDIUM_GRASS, # shrubland 30: C.MEDIUM_GRASS, # grassland 40: C.LIGHT_GRASS, # cropland -> farmland 50: C.MEDIUM_GRASS, # built-up: yards, not pavement; roads/buildings over it 60: C.DIRT, # bare / sparse 70: C.SAND, # snow and ice (the tile palette has no snow) 80: C.WATER, # permanent water 90: C.DARK_GRASS, # herbaceous wetland -> marsh 95: C.DARK_GRASS, # mangroves 100: C.DIRT, # moss and lichen -> rocky tundra } # While OSM paints, WorldCover's ground stands in these colours, one per class, # none of them a ground colour. Whatever is still a marker once OSM has painted # is ground OSM left blank - which comparing colours after the fact cannot # tell, since OSM's grass over WorldCover's grass is the same grass. MARKER = {code: (3, 7, code) for code in WORLDCOVER_PAINT} assert not set(MARKER.values()) & C.LANDSCAPE_COLORS _STRIP = 1024 # --- feature painting ------------------------------------------------------ # Paint order for landscape: later categories overwrite earlier ones, so this # is effectively painted bottom-to-top. LANDSCAPE_ORDER = [ # Broad land use first, so anything more specific inside it - a pitch in a # schoolyard, a car park on an industrial estate - is painted over it. "residential", # gardens and yards "commercial", # pavement in front of shops "industrial", # rough grass; the works' yards are paved later "military", "schoolyard", "hospital_grounds", "worship_grounds", "cemetery", "orchard", "farmland", # light grass "grass", # medium grass "park", # medium grass w/ trees added by vegetation pass "sports", "wetland", "sand", "dirt", "playground", "track", # Water under the ways that cross it: a river polygon painted last erased # every bridge, leaving no way over. Above land use, which it still wins. "water", "pool", "railway", # gravel track bed; roads cross it at level crossings "dirt_path", # thin dirt line "paved_path", # footway, pavement, cycleway "pier", # jetties and breakwaters, over the water "parking", # car park tarmac "plaza", # paved pedestrian square "pedestrian", # pedestrian zone, paved wall to wall "road_service", # alleys and driveways "road_minor", "road_medium", "road_major", # widest, so it wins at junctions # Building footprints are not painted at all. They used to be dirt, which # showed as a brown fringe wherever the placed building and the painted # footprint disagreed by a tile - and the building's own floor covers the # ground under it anyway. ] # Waterways drawn from a centre line, when no area is mapped around them. # A river is usually mapped with its banks too, which paints over this. WATERWAY_WIDTH_M = {"river": 12.0, "canal": 8.0, "stream": 2.0} LANDSCAPE_FILL = { "water": C.WATER, "sand": C.SAND, "dirt": C.DIRT, "dirt_path": C.DIRT, "paved_path": C.PALE_CONCRETE, "pier": C.PALE_CONCRETE, # Dirt, not lightgravel: a rail bed is bare earth and gravel, and the pale # gravel strip read as a sandy footpath across the whole map. "railway": C.DIRT, "grass": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "park": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "farmland": C.LIGHT_GRASS, # street/street2/street4 in Rules.txt. road_minor used to paint # lightgravel, which put a gravel track through the middle of every # residential street in town. # Service lanes were gravel, which next to slab pavements read as more # pavement. Main roads get the worn speckled tarmac so they stand apart # from the smooth tarmac of ordinary streets; both blend at the edges. "road_service": C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, "pedestrian": C.PAVING, "road_minor": C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, "road_medium": C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, "road_major": C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, "parking": C.DARK_ASPHALT, "plaza": C.PAVING, "residential": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "commercial": C.PALE_CONCRETE, # Rough grass: each works gets its own tarmac yard round it # (knoxbuild/works.py). Gravel from fence to fence was a beige plain. "industrial": C.LIGHT_GRASS, "military": C.DIRT, "schoolyard": C.PALE_CONCRETE, "hospital_grounds": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "worship_grounds": C.PAVING, "cemetery": C.LIGHT_GRASS, "orchard": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "sports": C.MEDIUM_GRASS, "wetland": C.DARK_GRASS, "playground": C.SAND, "track": C.CLAY, "pool": C.WATER, } # Categories knoxbuild needs as areas, to tell what a building standing in # them probably is: an untagged building on an industrial estate is a works, # not a house. AREA_CATEGORIES = {"residential", "commercial", "industrial", "military", "schoolyard", "hospital_grounds", "worship_grounds", "cemetery", "parking", "sports", "park", "playground"} # Drawn onto the vegetation bitmap rather than the ground. VEG_CATEGORIES = {"forest", "scrub", "tree_single", "hedge", "orchard", "cemetery", "wetland"} # A city block is paved when buildings cover at least this share of it - the # same line knoxbuild draws between a city and a suburb. # Measured: central Paris, Kadikoy and a Tokyo neighbourhood sit at 0.4-0.5, a # US suburb and a French village around 0.16. Set to the bottom of that # downtown band: at 0.28 every old town got slabs of concrete two blocks wide, # standing where the yards and trees should be. DENSE_COVERAGE = 0.40 # And a block whose area is bigger than this is not a city block at all. A # rural road grid throws blocks a kilometre across - one farm, one works and a # couple of houses clear the coverage line easily - and paving the whole of one # is the big concrete field that reads as ground nobody landscaped. 200 x 200 # tiles is a long Manhattan block; past that the yards stay grass. MAX_PAVED_BLOCK = 200 * 200 # Mapped green space keeps its grass however built-up the area around it is. GREEN_CATEGORIES = {"park", "grass", "sports", "cemetery", "orchard", "farmland", "wetland", "hospital_grounds"}

nodes.name: grid_for_map
nodes.body_text: def grid_for_map(landcover_for, proj): """WorldCover's class for every tile of the map, `(height, width)`. The map's image covers more than the bbox (it is padded to whole cells), so the grid is read for what the image covers. A turned map's tiles do not run along lines of latitude: the grid is read for the box round the whole turned map, and each tile takes the class at its own position.""" import math import numpy as np bounds = proj.latlon_bbox() if not proj.rotation: return landcover_for(proj.width, proj.height, bounds=bounds) a = math.radians(proj.rotation) c, s_ = abs(math.cos(a)), abs(math.sin(a)) gw = max(1, int(math.ceil(proj.width * c + proj.height * s_))) gh = max(1, int(math.ceil(proj.width * s_ + proj.height * c))) source = landcover_for(gw, gh, bounds=bounds) if source is None: return None source = np.asarray(source) gh, gw = source.shape south, west, north, east = bounds out = np.zeros((proj.height, proj.width), dtype=source.dtype) xs = np.arange(proj.width, dtype=np.float64) + 0.5 for top in range(0, proj.height, _STRIP): bottom = min(proj.height, top + _STRIP) ys = np.arange(top, bottom, dtype=np.float64) + 0.5 px, py = np.meshgrid(xs, ys) lat, lon = proj.to_latlon_many(px, py) col = np.clip(((lon - west) / (east - west) * gw).astype(np.int64), 0, gw - 1) row = np.clip(((north - lat) / (north - south) * gh).astype(np.int64), 0, gh - 1) out[top:bottom] = source[row, col] return out

nodes.name: resized_grid
nodes.body_text: def resized_grid(grid, size): """The class grid at the image's size (width, height), nearest class.""" import numpy as np from PIL import Image grid = np.asarray(grid, dtype="uint8") if (grid.shape[1], grid.shape[0]) == tuple(size): return grid return np.asarray(Image.fromarray(grid, "L").resize(tuple(size), Image.NEAREST))

nodes.name: paint_markers
nodes.body_text: def paint_markers(landscape, grid) -> None: """Paint each classified tile in its class's marker colour.""" import numpy as np from PIL import Image grid = resized_grid(grid, landscape.size) w = landscape.size[0] for top in range(0, grid.shape[0], _STRIP): g = grid[top:top + _STRIP] if not g.any(): continue rgb = np.array(landscape.crop((0, top, w, top + g.shape[0]))) for code, colour in MARKER.items(): rgb[g == code] = colour landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(rgb, "RGB"), (0, top))

nodes.name: settle_markers
nodes.body_text: def settle_markers(landscape, grid): """Turn marker colours into the classes' ground colours. Returns `owned`: a bool array, True where the tile is still WorldCover's (OSM left it).""" import numpy as np from PIL import Image grid = resized_grid(grid, landscape.size) w, h = landscape.size owned = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool) for top in range(0, h, _STRIP): g = grid[top:top + _STRIP] if not g.any(): continue rgb = np.array(landscape.crop((0, top, w, top + g.shape[0]))) for code, colour in MARKER.items(): hit = (g == code) & np.all(rgb == colour, axis=2) if hit.any(): rgb[hit] = WORLDCOVER_PAINT[code] owned[top:top + g.shape[0]] |= hit landscape.paste(Image.fromarray(rgb, "RGB"), (0, top)) return owned

nodes.name: refine_owned
nodes.body_text: def refine_owned(landscape, grid, owned) -> None: """Drop from `owned` (in place) any tile no longer its class's colour: dense paving and the drawn shape's clipping repaint after OSM.""" import numpy as np grid = resized_grid(grid, landscape.size) w, h = landscape.size for top in range(0, h, _STRIP): o = owned[top:top + _STRIP] if not o.any(): continue g = grid[top:top + o.shape[0]] rgb = np.asarray(landscape.crop((0, top, w, top + o.shape[0]))) same = np.zeros(o.shape, dtype=bool) for code, colour in WORLDCOVER_PAINT.items(): same |= (g == code) & np.all(rgb == colour, axis=2) o &= same

nodes.name: outputs.py
nodes.body_text: """What a render writes besides the two bitmaps: place names, area, line and opening GeoJSON, the zombie spawn map and the preview picture.""" from __future__ import annotations import random from PIL import Image from .. import pz_colors as C from ..osm import OSMFeature from .geometry import _is_polygon from .landcover import AREA_CATEGORIES from .projection import Projector AREA_TAGS = {"landuse", "amenity", "leisure", "name", "religion"} LINE_TAGS = {"barrier", "fence_type", "material", "height", "wall"} # Ways people walk through a fence on: the path to the playing field, the # track to the yard. A fence drawn across one is drawn with a gap. OPENING_PATHS = {"paved_path", "dirt_path", "pedestrian"}

nodes.name: _places
nodes.body_text: def _places(feats: list[OSMFeature], proj: Projector) -> list[dict]: """Named places with an official population, and where they sit.""" out = [] for f in feats: raw = str(f.tags.get("population", "")).replace(",", "").replace(" ", "") try: population = int(float(raw.split(";")[0])) except (ValueError, OverflowError): # OverflowError: "inf", "1e999" continue la, lo = f.geometry[0] x, y = proj.to_px(la, lo) out.append({"name": f.tags.get("name", ""), "place": f.tags.get("place"), "population": population, "tile_x": round(x), "tile_y": round(y), "inside": 0 <= x < proj.width and 0 <= y < proj.height}) return out

nodes.name: _areas_geojson
nodes.body_text: def _areas_geojson(buckets: dict[str, list[OSMFeature]]) -> dict: """Land-use polygons, with the category each was painted as.""" features = [] for cat in AREA_CATEGORIES: for f in buckets.get(cat, []): if not _is_polygon(f): continue if f.kind == "way": rings = [[[lon, lat] for lat, lon in f.geometry]] else: rings = [[[lon, lat] for lat, lon in ring] for role, ring in f.role_geoms if role != "inner"] polys = [[r] for r in rings if len(r) >= 3] if not polys: continue features.append({ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"category": cat, **{k: v for k, v in f.tags.items() if k in AREA_TAGS}}, "geometry": {"type": "MultiPolygon", "coordinates": polys}, }) return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}

nodes.name: _lines_geojson
nodes.body_text: def _lines_geojson(feats: list[OSMFeature]) -> dict: """Fence and wall lines for knoxbuild to turn into fence tiles.""" features = [] for f in feats: if f.kind != "way" or len(f.geometry) < 2: continue features.append({ "type": "Feature", "properties": {k: v for k, v in f.tags.items() if k in LINE_TAGS}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in f.geometry]}, }) return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}

nodes.name: _openings_geojson
nodes.body_text: def _openings_geojson(gates: list[OSMFeature], buckets: dict) -> dict: """Where a fence should have a way through it: gates, and the paths that cross one. The crossing itself is worked out where the fence is built (knoxbuild/fences.py), which is the only place that knows where the line ended up on the grid.""" features = [] for f in gates: if not f.geometry: continue lat, lon = f.geometry[0] features.append({ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"opening": "gate", "barrier": f.tags.get("barrier") or "gate"}, "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [lon, lat]}, }) for cat in sorted(OPENING_PATHS): for f in buckets.get(cat, ()): if f.kind != "way" or len(f.geometry) < 2 or _is_polygon(f): continue features.append({ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"opening": "path", "category": cat}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[lon, lat] for lat, lon in f.geometry]}, }) return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}

nodes.name: _build_spawn_map
nodes.signature: def _build_spawn_map(landscape: Image.Image, w: int, h: int, max_density: int) -> Image.Image
nodes.body_text: def _build_spawn_map(landscape: Image.Image, w: int, h: int, max_density: int) -> Image.Image: """Grayscale spawn map. Dense in built-up areas, zero over water. The red channel is read as a raw zombie density, and Build 42 reads it on a much smaller scale than you would guess from a 0-255 byte. Sampling the vanilla Knox County spawn map: values run 1..10 and 97% of the map is 0. Writing 96 here - a quarter of the byte range - buries the map in thousands of zombies. Everything below is expressed as a fraction of `max_density`, which now defaults to vanilla's ceiling of 10. """ scaled = landscape.resize((w, h), Image.Resampling.BILINEAR) out = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), (0, 0, 0)) sp = scaled.load() op = out.load() rng = random.Random(0xABBA) def band(chance: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> int: """Density between two fractions of the ceiling, `chance` of the time. Sparsity matters as much as the ceiling. Vanilla leaves 97% of the map at zero and averages about 0.06 per pixel; filling every pixel with a mid value - even a small one - still produces a wall of zombies. Town maps are denser than county-wide wilderness, but the shape should be the same: crowds on the streets, almost nothing in the fields. """ if rng.random() > chance: return 0 return int(round(rng.uniform(max_density * lo, max_density * hi))) for y in range(h): for x in range(w): r, g, b = sp[x, y] if r == C.WATER[0] and g == C.WATER[1] and b == C.WATER[2]: v = 0 elif (75 <= r <= 175 and abs(r - g) < 30 and abs(g - b) < 30) or (r, g, b) == C.PAVING: # Asphalt, pavement and paved squares: where crowds belong. # The low end has to reach 75 now that the widest roads are # painted street4 at 80,80,80 - a range starting at 95 left # every main road through town as quiet as a field. v = band(0.40, 0.4, 1.0) elif r > g and r > 90 and g < 110: # Dirt tracks, yards, building footprints. v = band(0.15, 0.2, 0.5) elif g > r and g > 80: # Open grass: the odd wanderer, nothing more. v = band(0.03, 0.1, 0.2) else: v = band(0.08, 0.1, 0.3) op[x, y] = (v, v, v) return out

Vanilla leaves 97% of the map at zero and averages about 0.06 per pixel; filling every pixel with a mid value - even a small one - still produces a wall of zombies. Town maps are denser than county-wide wilderness, but the shape should be the same: crowds on the streets, almost nothing in the fields. """ if rng.random() > chance: return 0 return int(round(rng.uniform(max_density * lo, max_density * hi)))

nodes.name: _build_preview
nodes.body_text: def _build_preview(landscape: Image.Image, vegetation: Image.Image) -> Image.Image: """Human-friendly PNG: landscape with trees painted dark green.""" import numpy as np arr = np.array(landscape, dtype=np.uint8, copy=True) veg = np.asarray(vegetation, dtype=np.uint8) h, w = arr.shape[:2] key = ((veg[:, :, 0].astype(np.uint32) << 16) | (veg[:, :, 1].astype(np.uint32) << 8) | veg[:, :, 2]) def code(c): return (c[0] << 16) | (c[1] << 8) | c[2] other_trees = [code(c) for c in (C.TREES_DARK_GRASS, C.SPARSE_TREES, C.BUSHES_TREES_DARK_GRASS, C.TREE_SMALL)] arr[np.isin(key, other_trees)] = (65, 95, 45) arr[key == code(C.TREES)] = (40, 75, 35) # Fields, rocks and scrub, so a field reads as a field and a marsh as a # marsh rather than as the bare ground under them. for c, rgb in ((C.CORN_1, (200, 170, 60)), (C.CORN_2, (185, 150, 55)), (C.ROCKS, (150, 150, 145)), (C.BOULDERS, (115, 115, 110)), (C.BUSHES, (80, 110, 50)), (C.DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS, (70, 100, 60))): arr[key == code(c)] = rgb # A big tree covers more ground than its one tile, so the preview gives it # the square it keeps clear - otherwise a wood of them reads as a clearing. for c, side in C.BIG_TREE_ROOM.items(): ys, xs = np.nonzero(key == code(c)) if len(xs) == 0: continue reach = side // 2 if side % 2 else 0 for y, x in zip(ys.tolist(), xs.tolist()): arr[max(0, y - reach):min(h, y - reach + side), max(0, x - reach):min(w, x - reach + side)] = (25, 60, 25) return Image.fromarray(arr, "RGB")
