nodes.name: _plant_big_trees
nodes.signature: def _plant_big_trees(veg: Image.Image, landscape: Image.Image, wood_feats: list[OSMFeature], park_feats: list[OSMFeature], building_feats: list[OSMFeature], proj: Projector, density: float = 1.0) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def _plant_big_trees(veg: Image.Image, landscape: Image.Image, wood_feats: list[OSMFeature], park_feats: list[OSMFeature], building_feats: list[OSMFeature], proj: Projector, density: float = 1.0) -> dict: """Grow some of the trees already planted into big ones. Every tree on the vegetation bitmap is one tile, and so was every tree in a KnoxMap map. The ones that make a wood look like a wood are several tiles across and need a square kept clear around them, so they are chosen here, out of the trees the passes above planted, once all of them are down and it can be seen what stands next to what. Returns how many of each kind went in.""" import numpy as np counts: dict[str, int] = {} if density <= 0 or not tree_rules_ready(): return counts w, h = veg.size # Build tree and blocked masks in strips rather than holding duplicate # 3-channel RGB arrays for the entire map in RAM. tree = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool) blocked = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool) for top in range(0, h, BOX_STRIP_ROWS): bottom = min(h, top + BOX_STRIP_ROWS) veg_s = np.asarray(veg.crop((0, top, w, bottom))) for col in PLANTABLE: tree[top:bottom] |= np.all(veg_s == col, axis=2) for col in (C.BUSHES, C.DENSE_BUSHES_GRASS, C.FLOWERS): blocked[top:bottom] |= np.all(veg_s == col, axis=2) ground_s = np.asarray(landscape.crop((0, top, w, bottom))) blocked[top:bottom] |= np.all(ground_s == C.WATER, axis=2) if not tree.any(): return counts canopy = _Canopy(tree.shape) canopy.blocked = blocked woods = _polygon_mask(veg.size, [f for f in wood_feats if _is_polygon(f) and classify(f.tags, True) == "forest"], proj) parks = _polygon_mask(veg.size, park_feats, proj) gardens = _polygon_mask(veg.size, building_feats, proj) if gardens is not None: gardens = _box_any(gardens, GARDEN_REACH_TILES) # Each kind of ground gets its own mix, and the ground already spoken for # is left out of the next: a wood inside a park is park. rest = np.ones(tree.shape, dtype=bool) rounds = [] if parks is not None: deep = max(1, int(round(PARK_EDGE_M / proj.meters_per_tile))) belt = parks & _box_any(~parks, deep) rounds.append((belt, PARK_BELT_BIG_TREES)) rounds.append((parks & ~belt, PARK_BIG_TREES)) rest &= ~parks if woods is not None: rounds.append((woods & rest, WOOD_BIG_TREES)) rest &= ~woods if gardens is not None: rounds.append((gardens & rest, GARDEN_BIG_TREES)) rest &= ~gardens rounds.append((rest, WILD_BIG_TREES)) rng = np.random.default_rng(0x7E3E5) px = veg.load() for where, mix in rounds: here = tree & where if not here.any(): continue for colour, every, chance in mix: side = C.BIG_TREE_ROOM[colour] for x, y in _block_picks(here, every, rng, min(1.0, chance * density)): box = canopy.room(x, y, side) if box is None: continue canopy.taken[box] = True # The rest of the square is bare ground under the tree, the # way the game's own features leave it. rows, cols = box for fy in range(rows.start, rows.stop): for fx in range(cols.start, cols.stop): px[fx, fy] = C.VEG_NOTHING px[x, y] = colour counts[str(colour)] = counts.get(str(colour), 0) + 1 return counts

nodes.name: tree_rules_ready
nodes.body_text: def tree_rules_ready() -> bool: """Whether the map tools have the rules for trees of a size we choose. They are written by worlded/patch_rules_b42_trees.py when Setup runs, and a colour with no rule behind it is dropped with a warning - so on an install set up before the big trees existed, every tree stays the size its own rule says until Setup is run again. KNOXMAP_NO_BIG_TREES=1 turns them off. """ import os if os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_NO_BIG_TREES") == "1": return False try: import knoxpaths rules = knoxpaths.mapping_tools_dir() / "config" / "Rules.txt" text = rules.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") return all(f"KnoxMap tree {what}" in text for what in ("Small tree", "Giant tree")) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no tools, no trees of our own return False

nodes.name: widths.py
nodes.body_text: """How wide roads, pavements and verges are drawn, and how a road is marked.""" from __future__ import annotations import math from ..osm import OSMFeature, road_hierarchy # Road widths in meters. Converted to pixels by dividing by meters_per_tile. # # These are the fallbacks. A way carrying lanes= or width= is measured from # those instead, because every street in a class being identically wide is what # made the towns read as a printed circuit rather than a place - real ones have # a four-lane high street feeding two-lane side roads feeding one-car alleys. ROAD_WIDTHS_M = { "road_major": 12.0, "road_medium": 8.0, "road_minor": 6.0, "road_service": 3.5, # A pedestrian zone is as wide as the square it paves, not as wide as # a lane; mapped as lines with no area round them, this is what fills # the space between the buildings. "pedestrian": 9.0, "dirt_path": 2.5, "paved_path": 2.5, "pier": 3.0, "railway": 4.0, } ROAD_WIDTHS_BY_HIERARCHY_M = { "motorway": 24.0, "trunk": 16.0, "primary": 12.0, "secondary": 9.0, "tertiary": 7.0, "residential": 6.0, "service": 3.5, "footway": 2.5, } # Metres of kerb either side. Town streets in the vanilla game sit in a band of # pale concrete; without it the asphalt runs straight into grass and every road # looks like it was dropped on the landscape rather than built into it. SIDEWALK_M = { "road_major": 2.5, "road_medium": 3.5, "road_minor": 3.0, } # Of that, the strip of grass between the kerb and the pavement on a # residential street - Knox County's streets run kerb, verge, pavement, lawn. # In a built-up block the verge is paved over with the rest of the ground. VERGE_M = { "road_medium": 1.5, "road_minor": 1.5, } SIDEWALK_BY_HIERARCHY_M = { "motorway": 0.0, "trunk": 1.5, "primary": 2.5, "secondary": 2.5, "tertiary": 2.5, "residential": 2.5, "service": 0.5, } VERGE_BY_HIERARCHY_M = { "motorway": 0.0, "trunk": 0.0, "primary": 0.0, "secondary": 0.5, "tertiary": 1.0, "residential": 1.5, "service": 0.0, }

nodes.name: _sidewalk_width_m
nodes.body_text: def _sidewalk_width_m(feat: OSMFeature, cat: str) -> float: return SIDEWALK_BY_HIERARCHY_M.get(road_hierarchy(feat.tags), SIDEWALK_M.get(cat, 0.0))

nodes.name: _verge_width_m
nodes.body_text: def _verge_width_m(feat: OSMFeature, cat: str) -> float: return VERGE_BY_HIERARCHY_M.get(road_hierarchy(feat.tags), VERGE_M.get(cat, 0.0))

nodes.name: _way_width_m
nodes.body_text: def _way_width_m(feat: OSMFeature, cat: str) -> float: """Carriageway width for this way, from its own tags where it has them.""" base = ROAD_WIDTHS_BY_HIERARCHY_M.get(road_hierarchy(feat.tags), ROAD_WIDTHS_M[cat]) raw = feat.tags.get("width") or feat.tags.get("est_width") if raw: # OSM widths are metres unless suffixed; "7", "7 m" and "7.5" all occur. try: given = float(str(raw).split()[0].replace(",", ".")) # "nan" is a number to float(), and min(30.0, nan) is 30.0: a road # tagged width=nan came out thirty metres wide. if math.isfinite(given): return max(2.0, min(30.0, given)) except (ValueError, IndexError): # IndexError: a width of " " pass lanes = feat.tags.get("lanes") if lanes: try: n = max(1, min(8, int(str(lanes).split(";")[0]))) except ValueError: n = 0 if n: # 3.2 m a lane, plus a little for the shoulder and markings. width = n * 3.2 + 1.0 if feat.tags.get("oneway") == "yes": width = max(width, 3.5) return width return base

nodes.name: _road_markings
nodes.signature: def _road_markings(feat: OSMFeature, cat: str) -> list[tuple[str, float]]
nodes.body_text: def _road_markings(feat: OSMFeature, cat: str) -> list[tuple[str, float]]: """(color, offset in metres) for lane markings across a road centerline.""" width = _way_width_m(feat, cat) if any(str(feat.tags.get(key, "")).lower() == "no" for key in ("centreline", "centerline", "road_marking")): return [] raw_lanes = str(feat.tags.get("lanes") or "").split(";")[0].strip() try: lanes = max(1, min(8, int(float(raw_lanes)))) if raw_lanes else max( 1, min(8, int(round(width / 3.2)))) except ValueError: lanes = max(1, min(8, int(round(width / 3.2)))) if lanes < 2: return [] oneway = (str(feat.tags.get("oneway") or "").lower() in ("yes", "1", "-1") or feat.tags.get("junction") == "roundabout") lane_width = width / lanes if oneway: return [("white", -width / 2 + lane_width * lane) for lane in range(1, lanes)] markings = [("yellow", 0.0)] lanes_per_direction = lanes // 2 if lanes >= 4: for lane in range(1, lanes_per_direction): offset = lane_width * lane markings.extend((("white", -offset), ("white", offset))) return markings

nodes.name: woodland.py
nodes.body_text: """Bounded woodland pixel batches through the existing native terrain worker.""" import logging import struct import subprocess import time from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, TimeoutError as FutureTimeout from PIL import Image import knoxstop from .. import pz_colors as C from ..roadgraph.rustsearch import exe MAX_PIXELS = 1_048_576 MIN_PIXELS = 1_048_576 TIMEOUT_S = 30

nodes.name: _exchange
nodes.body_text: def _exchange(proc, data, expected): view = memoryview(data) while view: sent = proc.stdin.write(view) if not sent: raise RuntimeError('woodland worker input closed') view = view[sent:] proc.stdin.flush() reply = proc.stdout.read(expected) if len(reply) != expected or reply[:4] != b'KWD1': raise RuntimeError('invalid woodland worker reply') return reply[4:]

nodes.name: paint
nodes.signature: def paint(veg, landscape, mask, eroded, scrub, edge, inside, should_stop=None)
nodes.body_text: def paint(veg, landscape, mask, eroded, scrub, edge, inside, should_stop=None): """Apply strips, or return False so the idempotent Python loop can finish.""" binary = exe() width, height = veg.size if binary is None or not 0 < width <= MAX_PIXELS or not height: return False if veg.mode != 'RGB' or landscape.mode != 'RGB': return False colours = (C.WATER, C.MEDIUM_GRASS, C.LIGHT_GRASS, C.DARK_GRASS, C.BUSHES_TREES_DARK_GRASS, edge, inside, C.VEG_NOTHING) palette = bytes(v for colour in colours for v in colour) rows = min(256, MAX_PIXELS // width) try: with subprocess.Popen([binary, '--woodland'], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, creationflags=getattr(subprocess, 'CREATE_NO_WINDOW', 0)) as proc: with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool: try: for top in range(0, height, rows): knoxstop.check(should_stop, 'the woodland') box = (0, top, width, min(top+rows, height)) size = (width, box[3]-top) n = size[0]*size[1] data = (b'KWD1'+struct.pack('<I', (height+rows-1)//rows)) if top == 0 else b'' data += struct.pack('<II', *size) + palette data += b''.join(im.crop(box).tobytes() for im in (veg, landscape, mask, eroded, scrub)) future = pool.submit(_exchange, proc, data, 4+6*n) deadline = time.monotonic() + TIMEOUT_S while True: knoxstop.check(should_stop, 'the woodland') if time.monotonic() >= deadline: raise TimeoutError('native woodland worker timed out') try: result = future.result(timeout=.1) break except FutureTimeout: continue veg.paste(Image.frombytes('RGB', size, result[:3*n]), box) landscape.paste(Image.frombytes('RGB', size, result[3*n:]), box) finally: if proc.poll() is None: proc.kill() proc.wait() except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc: logging.getLogger(__name__).warning('native woodland unavailable; using Python: %s', exc) return False return True

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.body_text: """Roads routed on vanilla B42's lattice (route.py): the Road layout setting's vanilla choices."""

nodes.name: modes.py
nodes.body_text: """How built-up streets are routed. graph vanilla's sixteen directions everywhere cost a frontage-density field (snap.COST): a step off the grid costs more the more building outline is near it - 45 degrees a little, 2:1 a lot - and where it is dense a road turns only at a junction or a gap in the frontage (snap.JOG); each building square under the carriageway costs too (snap.OCC), so a road keeps off the buildings it runs past prepare() sets snap up for a mode; reset() puts it back. The fields are worked out from the map's own OSM buildings. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw from . import snap LOW = {"grid": 0.0, "45": 0.25, "2:1": 0.75} PRESETS = { "graph": ("graph", {}), "cost": ("cost", {"DIR_PENALTY": LOW, "OCC_WEIGHT": 1.0}), } # The density field: building outline (tiles of it) near a square, smoothed over # DENSITY_SIGMA tiles, as a share of DENSITY_FULL - about what a street lined both # sides with buildings has (a high street reads about 0.7; capped at 1). DENSITY_SIGMA = 6.0 DENSITY_FULL = 0.10 DIST_CAP = 16 # tiles: building distances past this are all "far" (the jog rule # asks up to half the widest road plus snap.JOG_GAP) _SAVED: dict = {} # snap's constants as they were before a run's params

nodes.name: building_rings
nodes.body_text: def building_rings(features, proj) -> list: """The map's OSM buildings: each outline's points in tiles.""" return [[proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lat, lon in f.geometry] for f in features if f.kind == "way" and f.tags.get("building") and f.geometry and len(f.geometry) >= 3]

nodes.name: buildings
nodes.signature: def buildings(rings, H: int, W: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
nodes.body_text: def buildings(rings, H: int, W: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: """(footprints, outlines): the buildings filled, and their outlines as lines a tile wide.""" fill, edge = Image.new("1", (W, H), 0), Image.new("1", (W, H), 0) df, de = ImageDraw.Draw(fill), ImageDraw.Draw(edge) for pts in rings: df.polygon(pts, fill=1) de.line(pts + [pts[0]], fill=1, width=1) return np.array(fill, bool), np.array(edge, bool)

nodes.name: gaussian
nodes.signature: def gaussian(a: np.ndarray, sigma: float) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def gaussian(a: np.ndarray, sigma: float) -> np.ndarray: """a blurred by a gaussian of `sigma` tiles (to 4 sigma; zeros beyond the edge).""" r = int(math.ceil(4 * sigma)) x = np.arange(-r, r + 1) k1 = np.exp(-x * x / (2 * sigma * sigma)) k1 /= k1.sum() return snap.convolve(a.astype(float), np.outer(k1, k1))

nodes.name: density
nodes.signature: def density(outlines: np.ndarray, sigma: float = DENSITY_SIGMA, full: float = DENSITY_FULL) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def density(outlines: np.ndarray, sigma: float = DENSITY_SIGMA, full: float = DENSITY_FULL) -> np.ndarray: """0-1: building outline near each square (gaussian, sigma tiles), over `full`.""" return np.clip(gaussian(outlines, sigma) / full, 0.0, 1.0)

nodes.name: distance
nodes.signature: def distance(fill: np.ndarray, cap: int = DIST_CAP) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def distance(fill: np.ndarray, cap: int = DIST_CAP) -> np.ndarray: """Each square's distance in tiles to the nearest filled one, exact up to `cap` (beyond it, cap + 1): the nearest along each column, then across the row.""" H, W = fill.shape far = cap + 1 rows = np.arange(H)[:, None] above = np.maximum.accumulate(np.where(fill, rows, -10 ** 9), axis=0) below = np.minimum.accumulate(np.where(fill, rows, 10 ** 9)[::-1], axis=0)[::-1] g = np.minimum(np.minimum(rows - above, below - rows), far).astype(float) best = g * g for dx in range(1, far): for src, dst in ((slice(dx, None), slice(None, -dx)), (slice(None, -dx), slice(dx, None))): best[:, dst] = np.minimum(best[:, dst], g[:, src] ** 2 + dx * dx) return np.minimum(np.sqrt(best), far)

nodes.name: fields
nodes.signature: def fields(rings, H: int, W: int) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def fields(rings, H: int, W: int) -> dict: """Everything the cost mode needs, worked out once: footprints, density, and each square's distance in tiles to the nearest building.""" fill, edge = buildings(rings, H, W) return {"footprints": fill, "density": density(edge), "building_dist": distance(fill)}

nodes.name: reset
nodes.body_text: def reset() -> None: """snap as it was: no mode, its constants back.""" snap.COST = None snap.JOG = None snap.OCC = None for k, v in _SAVED.items(): setattr(snap, k, v) _SAVED.clear()

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.signature: def prepare(mode: str, rings, H: int, W: int) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def prepare(mode: str, rings, H: int, W: int) -> dict: """snap set up for `mode` ("graph" or "cost"). Returns {"mode", "params"} for the map's info.json.""" if mode not in PRESETS: raise ValueError(f"road mode {mode!r}: one of {', '.join(PRESETS)}") kind, params = PRESETS[mode] reset() for k, v in params.items(): _SAVED.setdefault(k, getattr(snap, k)) setattr(snap, k, v) used = dict(params) if kind == "cost": f = fields(rings, H, W) snap.COST = f["density"] snap.JOG = {"dist": f["building_dist"], "plots": None} if snap.OCC_WEIGHT > 0: snap.OCC = f["footprints"] used = {k: getattr(snap, k) for k in ("DIR_PENALTY", "COST_SCALE", "ARM_COST", "JOG_DENSITY", "JOG_GAP", "JOG_END", "JOG_RUN", "OCC_WEIGHT")} used.update(DENSITY_SIGMA=DENSITY_SIGMA, DENSITY_FULL=DENSITY_FULL) return {"mode": mode, "params": used}

nodes.name: network.py
nodes.body_text: """The road graph from OpenStreetMap, in a map's tiles: junction-to-junction links, each with a class and a width in whole tiles. The map's frame is the renderer's (its Projector, turned as the map is), so what comes out lines up with the map as built. Footways and paths are left for their own pass; tunnels are left out (the ground is flat). A way's ends and every node it shares with another way are graph nodes; a node where just two ways of one class meet end to end is merged away, so a link runs junction to junction. Then generalised: a small turning loop is a dead end, a dual carriageway one wide road, a lane hugging a bigger road part of it. """ from __future__ import annotations import math from dataclasses import dataclass, field import numpy as np import shapely from shapely.ops import substring # OSM highway -> (class, default width in tiles at 1 m a tile; whole tiles, odd # ones too as vanilla's streets.xml has them - 5 and 7 wide are common). The # width shapes the routing (the run between bends, a curve's radius, how far # apart two roads keep); Generate still draws each road at its own width. CLASSES = { "motorway": ("motorway", 14), "motorway_link": ("motorway", 8), "trunk": ("primary", 8), "trunk_link": ("primary", 6), "primary": ("primary", 8), "primary_link": ("primary", 6), "secondary": ("secondary", 6), "secondary_link": ("secondary", 6), "tertiary": ("minor", 6), "tertiary_link": ("minor", 6), "unclassified": ("minor", 6), "residential": ("local", 6), "living_street": ("local", 6), "road": ("local", 6), "service": ("service", 4), "track": ("track", 2), } # Routed highest first (snap.py): the main roads get the straightest runs. RANK = {"motorway": 0, "primary": 1, "secondary": 2, "minor": 3, "local": 4, "service": 5, "track": 6} LOOP_MAX = 80 # tiles round: a loop shorter than this is a turning loop DUAL_MAX = 16 # tiles apart at most, the two ways of a dual carriageway ABSORB_GAP = 2 # tiles: a lane no further than this from a bigger road's edge is part of it ATTACH_MAX = 10 # tiles a junction of an absorbed lane may move to a bigger road's WIDTH_RANGE = {"motorway": (10, 16), "primary": (6, 10), "secondary": (6, 8), "minor": (4, 10), "local": (4, 8), "service": (2, 6), "track": (2, 4)} @dataclass # Sites whose service ways are their own car parks and drives, not streets # (a school's one-way aisles). SITE_AMENITIES = {"parking", "school", "college", "university", "hospital", "clinic", "kindergarten", "community_centre", "place_of_worship", "fuel", "supermarket"} SITE_LANDUSE = {"retail", "commercial", "industrial"} SITE_SHARE = 0.6 # of a service way's length inside a site for it to be the site's CAR_PARK_SHARE = 0.5 # ...and of any minor road's inside a car park for it to be the car park's MINOR_IN_CAR_PARK = ("unclassified", "residential", "living_street")

nodes.name: Link
nodes.body_text: class Link: u: int # node ids at its ends v: int pts: list # polyline in tiles, u to v cls: str width: int # tiles, whole tags: dict = field(default_factory=dict) ways: list = field(default_factory=list)

nodes.name: _key
nodes.body_text: def _key(lat, lon): return round(lat * 1e7), round(lon * 1e7)

nodes.name: whole
nodes.body_text: def whole(w: float) -> int: return max(2, int(round(w)))

nodes.name: build
nodes.signature: def build(features: list, proj, shape: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, list[Link], dict]
nodes.body_text: def build(features: list, proj, shape: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, list[Link], dict]: """(nodes {id: (x, y) in tiles}, links, pins) for a map's OSM features, the roads as they really are (not straightened), cut at the map's edge. Pins {node: the way into the map, (dx, dy)} are the nodes where a road leaves the map: worked out from the real road alone, so a neighbouring map built in the same frame finds the same point and the roads meet. A roundabout is not routed (roundabouts()): it stays as drawn, and the roads into it are pinned where they meet it, leaving it outwards.""" ways = road_ways(features) rings = roundabouts(features) if shape: ways = _in_shape(ways, shape, proj) mpt = getattr(proj, "meters_per_tile", 1.0) or 1.0 # Graph nodes: way ends, and nodes shared by more than one way. uses: dict = {} for f in ways: for n, (lat, lon) in enumerate(f.geometry): k = _key(lat, lon) uses[k] = uses.get(k, 0) + (2 if n in (0, len(f.geometry) - 1) else 1) node_of: dict = {} nodes: dict = {} def node(k, lat, lon): if k not in node_of: node_of[k] = len(node_of) nodes[node_of[k]] = proj.to_px(lat, lon) return node_of[k] links: list[Link] = [] for f in ways: cls, w = CLASSES[f.tags["highway"].lower()] tagged = _width_tag(f.tags) lo, hi = WIDTH_RANGE[cls] width = min(hi, max(lo, whole(tagged / mpt))) if tagged else max(2, whole(w / mpt)) start = 0 geo = f.geometry for n in range(1, len(geo)): k = _key(*geo[n]) if n == len(geo) - 1 or uses[k] >= 3: a, b = geo[start], geo[n] links.append(Link(node(_key(*a), *a), node(k, *b), [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in geo[start:n + 1]], cls, width, dict(f.tags), [f.osm_id])) start = n links = _merge_through(links) # A loop drawn as one way back to its own junction: a turning loop if # short (dropped: the road ends where it starts), else two links split at # its middle by a new node. links = [l for l in links if l.u != l.v or _length(l.pts) >= LOOP_MAX] for k, l in enumerate(links): if l.u == l.v and len(l.pts) > 2: half = _length(l.pts) / 2 m = next(n for n in range(1, len(l.pts)) if _length(l.pts[:n + 1]) >= half) mid = len(nodes) + 1_000_000 nodes[mid] = l.pts[m] links[k] = Link(l.u, mid, l.pts[:m + 1], l.cls, l.width, l.tags, l.ways) links.append(Link(mid, l.v, l.pts[m:], l.cls, l.width, l.tags, l.ways)) links = _merge_through(_absorb_lanes(_dual_carriageways(links))) links, pins = _clip(links, nodes, proj.width, proj.height) # Nodes no link uses any more (merged away) go. used = {l.u for l in links} | {l.v for l in links} nodes = {k: v for k, v in nodes.items() if k in used} for ring in _whole_rings(rings): px = [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in ring] cx, cy = sum(x for x, _y in px) / len(px), sum(y for _x, y in px) / len(px) for lat, lon in ring: n = node_of.get(_key(lat, lon)) if n in nodes: x, y = nodes[n] d = math.hypot(x - cx, y - cy) or 1.0 pins[n] = ((x - cx) / d, (y - cy) / d) return nodes, links, pins

nodes.name: node
nodes.body_text: def node(k, lat, lon): if k not in node_of: node_of[k] = len(node_of) nodes[node_of[k]] = proj.to_px(lat, lon) return node_of[k]

nodes.name: car_park_ways
nodes.body_text: def car_park_ways(feats) -> list: """The ways that are a car park or a site's own drives, not streets: service ways tagged a parking aisle, or mostly (SITE_SHARE) inside a car park, or private or one-way and mostly inside a site (a school, a hospital, a retail park); and any minor road (MINOR_IN_CAR_PARK) mostly (CAR_PARK_SHARE) inside a car park, whatever its highway tag (a supermarket's car park mapped as a loop of highway=unclassified). Left where they are and moved with the roads, not routed.""" sites = [] for f in feats: t = f.tags if (t.get("amenity") in SITE_AMENITIES or t.get("landuse") in SITE_LANDUSE) and f.kind == "way" \ and len(f.geometry) > 3 and f.geometry[0] == f.geometry[-1]: try: poly = shapely.Polygon([(lo, la) for la, lo in f.geometry]) except Exception: continue if poly.is_valid and poly.area > 0: sites.append((poly, t.get("amenity") == "parking")) tree = shapely.STRtree([p for p, _c in sites]) if sites else None out = [] for f in feats: t = f.tags hw = (t.get("highway") or "").lower() if f.kind != "way" or len(f.geometry) < 2 or hw not in ("service",) + MINOR_IN_CAR_PARK: continue if hw != "service": if tree is not None: line = shapely.LineString([(lo, la) for la, lo in f.geometry]) if any(sites[k][1] and line.intersection(sites[k][0]).length >= CAR_PARK_SHARE * line.length for k in tree.query(line)): out.append(f) continue if t.get("service") == "parking_aisle": out.append(f) continue if tree is None or t.get("service") in ("driveway", "alley"): continue line = shapely.LineString([(lo, la) for la, lo in f.geometry]) private = t.get("access") in ("private", "customers", "permissive", "destination", "no") or t.get("oneway") == "yes" for k in tree.query(line): poly, is_car_park = sites[k] if (is_car_park or private) and line.intersection(poly).length >= SITE_SHARE * line.length: out.append(f) break return out

nodes.name: _is_roundabout
nodes.body_text: def _is_roundabout(f) -> bool: return (f.tags.get("junction") or "").lower() in ("roundabout", "circular")

nodes.name: roundabouts
nodes.body_text: def roundabouts(feats) -> list: """The roundabouts among the roads: left as drawn, as Knox County straight leaves them.""" return [f for f in feats if f.kind == "way" and len(f.geometry) >= 2 and _is_roundabout(f) and (f.tags.get("highway") or "").lower() in CLASSES]

nodes.name: _whole_rings
nodes.body_text: def _whole_rings(ways) -> list: """Each roundabout's nodes [(lat, lon)], once each: its ways joined where they share a node (one is often mapped as several arcs, and an arc's own middle is not the roundabout's).""" parent = list(range(len(ways))) def find(a): while parent[a] != a: parent[a] = parent[parent[a]] a = parent[a] return a first: dict = {} for k, f in enumerate(ways): for lat, lon in f.geometry: j = first.setdefault(_key(lat, lon), k) parent[find(k)] = find(j) rings: dict = {} for k, f in enumerate(ways): ring = rings.setdefault(find(k), {}) for lat, lon in f.geometry: ring.setdefault(_key(lat, lon), (lat, lon)) return [list(r.values()) for r in rings.values()]

nodes.name: find
nodes.body_text: def find(a): while parent[a] != a: parent[a] = parent[parent[a]] a = parent[a] return a

nodes.name: road_ways
nodes.body_text: def road_ways(feats) -> list: """The OSM ways the graph is made of: roads of a class it knows, not areas, tunnels, roundabouts, or car parks and sites' own drives (car_park_ways).""" parks = {id(f) for f in car_park_ways(feats)} out = [] for f in feats: if id(f) in parks or _is_roundabout(f): continue h = (f.tags.get("highway") or "").lower() if f.kind != "way" or h not in CLASSES or len(f.geometry) < 2: continue if f.tags.get("area") == "yes" or f.tags.get("tunnel") in ("yes", "culvert"): continue out.append(f) return out

nodes.name: _in_shape
nodes.signature: def _in_shape(ways: list, shape: dict, proj) -> list
nodes.body_text: def _in_shape(ways: list, shape: dict, proj) -> list: """A map cut to a drawn outline keeps its main roads whole, as Generate does (rendering/shape.THROUGH_ROADS: the town is not an island), and of every other road only the part inside the outline; outside, Generate's ground is grass.""" from dataclasses import replace from generator.renderer import classify from generator.rendering.projection import shape_px from generator.rendering.shape import THROUGH_ROADS clip = shape_px(shape, proj) out = [] for f in ways: if classify(f.tags, False) in THROUGH_ROADS: out.append(f) continue px = [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in f.geometry] line = shapely.LineString(px) if clip.contains(line): out.append(f) continue # The way's own nodes keep their exact lat/lon (junctions are matched # on them); only the new end at the outline is worked out. real = {(round(x, 6), round(y, 6)): ll for (x, y), ll in zip(px, f.geometry)} part = line.intersection(clip) for piece in getattr(part, "geoms", [part]): if piece.geom_type == "LineString" and piece.length >= 1: geo = [real.get((round(x, 6), round(y, 6))) or tuple(proj.to_latlon(x, y)) for x, y in piece.coords] out.append(replace(f, geometry=geo)) return out

nodes.name: _clip
nodes.signature: def _clip(links: list[Link], nodes: dict, W: int, H: int) -> tuple[list[Link], dict]
nodes.body_text: def _clip(links: list[Link], nodes: dict, W: int, H: int) -> tuple[list[Link], dict]: """Links cut to the map (0..W, 0..H); a new node, a pin, where one crosses the edge. A road leaving and coming back is two pieces.""" frame = shapely.box(0, 0, W, H) out, pins = [], {} def end_node(p, own, own_pos): if math.dist(p, own_pos) < 1e-6: return own nid = len(nodes) + 2_000_000 nodes[nid] = p x, y = p pins[nid] = (0, 1) if y < 1e-6 else (0, -1) if y > H - 1e-6 else (1, 0) if x < 1e-6 else (-1, 0) return nid for l in links: line = shapely.LineString(l.pts) if frame.contains(line): out.append(l) continue part = line.intersection(frame) for piece in getattr(part, "geoms", [part]): if piece.is_empty or piece.geom_type != "LineString" or piece.length < 1: continue pts = [tuple(c) for c in piece.coords] if line.project(shapely.Point(pts[0])) > line.project(shapely.Point(pts[-1])): pts = pts[::-1] # the piece the link's way round u = end_node(pts[0], l.u, l.pts[0]) v = end_node(pts[-1], l.v, l.pts[-1]) out.append(Link(u, v, pts, l.cls, l.width, l.tags, l.ways)) return out, pins

nodes.name: end_node
nodes.body_text: def end_node(p, own, own_pos): if math.dist(p, own_pos) < 1e-6: return own nid = len(nodes) + 2_000_000 nodes[nid] = p x, y = p pins[nid] = (0, 1) if y < 1e-6 else (0, -1) if y > H - 1e-6 else (1, 0) if x < 1e-6 else (-1, 0) return nid

nodes.name: _samples
nodes.body_text: def _samples(pts, every=2.0): line = shapely.LineString(pts) n = max(2, int(line.length / every) + 1) return shapely.line_interpolate_point(line, np.linspace(0, line.length, n))

nodes.name: _dual_carriageways
nodes.body_text: def _dual_carriageways(links: list[Link]) -> list[Link]: """A dual carriageway (two one-way ways of a class side by side, running opposite ways) made one road: the centreline between them, as wide as both and the reservation. The second way's end junctions become the first's.""" alias: dict = {} gone = set() for i, a in enumerate(links): if i in gone or a.tags.get("oneway") != "yes": continue la = shapely.LineString(a.pts) for j, b in enumerate(links): if j <= i or j in gone or b.tags.get("oneway") != "yes" or b.cls != a.cls: continue lb = shapely.LineString(b.pts) da, db = shapely.distance(_samples(a.pts), lb), shapely.distance(_samples(b.pts), la) heading_a = np.subtract(a.pts[-1], a.pts[0]) heading_b = np.subtract(b.pts[-1], b.pts[0]) if np.quantile(da, 0.8) > DUAL_MAX or np.quantile(db, 0.8) > DUAL_MAX or heading_a @ heading_b >= 0: continue sep = float(np.median(np.concatenate([da, db]))) mid = [((x + p.x) / 2, (y + p.y) / 2) for (x, y), p in zip(a.pts, shapely.get_point(shapely.shortest_line(shapely.points(a.pts), lb), 1))] links[i] = a = Link(a.u, a.v, mid, a.cls, min(16, whole(a.width + sep)), dict(a.tags, dual_carriageway="yes"), a.ways + b.ways) la = shapely.LineString(a.pts) for old, new in ((b.v, a.u), (b.u, a.v)): if old != new: alias[old] = new gone.add(j) out = [] for k, l in enumerate(links): if k not in gone: l.u, l.v = alias.get(l.u, l.u), alias.get(l.v, l.v) if l.u != l.v: out.append(l) return out

nodes.name: _absorb_lanes
nodes.body_text: def _absorb_lanes(links: list[Link]) -> list[Link]: """A service lane or track that never leaves the reach of bigger roads (a parking strip along the High Street) is part of them: dropped, one at a time. A junction of it other roads still use moves to the nearest junction of a bigger road (within ATTACH_MAX), or it stays. On a big city each sample is measured only against roads within reach (an index a pass), and a lane that failed is not tried again until something that could change its answer has: dropping a road only takes reach away, so only a lane beside the one dropped (one arm fewer at a junction), a lane whose line moved, or one ranked below a road that moved, is tried again - in the same order, so the same lanes go as when every lane was tried after every drop.""" failed: set = set() # id() of lanes that cannot go yet line_of: dict = {} # id(link) -> (its pts, its line) def line(m): got = line_of.get(id(m)) if got is None or got[0] is not m.pts: got = line_of[id(m)] = (m.pts, shapely.LineString(m.pts)) return got[1] while True: arms: dict = {} pos: dict = {} for l in links: for n, p in ((l.u, l.pts[0]), (l.v, l.pts[-1])): arms.setdefault(n, []).append(l) pos[n] = p all_lines = [line(m) for m in links] tree = shapely.STRtree(all_lines) widest = max((m.width for m in links), default=0.0) for k, l in enumerate(links): if RANK[l.cls] < RANK["service"] or id(l) in failed: continue big = [m for m in links if RANK[m.cls] < RANK[l.cls]] reach = l.width / 2 + ABSORB_GAP def covered(p): near = tree.query(p, predicate="dwithin", distance=reach + widest / 2) return any(RANK[links[j].cls] < RANK[l.cls] and shapely.distance(p, all_lines[j]) - links[j].width / 2 <= reach for j in near) if not big or not all(covered(p) for p in _samples(l.pts)): failed.add(id(l)) continue alias = {} for n in (l.u, l.v): if len(arms[n]) == 1 or any(RANK[m.cls] < RANK[l.cls] for m in arms[n]): continue d, to = min((math.dist(pos[n], pos[b]), b) for m in big for b in (m.u, m.v)) if d > ATTACH_MAX: break alias[n] = to else: kept, moved = [], [] for j, m in enumerate(links): if j == k: continue if m.u in alias or m.v in alias: moved.append(m) if m.u in alias: m.u, m.pts = alias[m.u], [pos[alias[m.u]]] + m.pts[1:] if m.v in alias: m.v, m.pts = alias[m.v], m.pts[:-1] + [pos[alias[m.v]]] if m.u != m.v: kept.append(m) links = kept failed -= {id(m) for n in (l.u, l.v) for m in arms[n]} failed -= {id(m) for m in moved} if moved: low = min(RANK[m.cls] for m in moved) failed -= {id(m) for m in links if RANK[m.cls] > low} line_of.pop(id(l), None) break failed.add(id(l)) else: return links

nodes.name: line
nodes.body_text: def line(m): got = line_of.get(id(m)) if got is None or got[0] is not m.pts: got = line_of[id(m)] = (m.pts, shapely.LineString(m.pts)) return got[1]

nodes.name: covered
nodes.body_text: def covered(p): near = tree.query(p, predicate="dwithin", distance=reach + widest / 2) return any(RANK[links[j].cls] < RANK[l.cls] and shapely.distance(p, all_lines[j]) - links[j].width / 2 <= reach for j in near)

nodes.name: _width_tag
nodes.body_text: def _width_tag(tags: dict) -> float | None: raw = tags.get("width") or tags.get("est_width") if not raw: return None try: return float(str(raw).split()[0].replace(",", ".").rstrip("m")) except ValueError: return None

nodes.name: _length
nodes.body_text: def _length(pts) -> float: return sum(math.dist(a, b) for a, b in zip(pts, pts[1:]))

nodes.name: _merge_through
nodes.body_text: def _merge_through(links: list[Link]) -> list[Link]: """Links joined end to end at a node only they meet at, of one class and width, made one (a road drawn as several ways is one link).""" while True: at: dict = {} for i, l in enumerate(links): at.setdefault(l.u, []).append(i) at.setdefault(l.v, []).append(i) merged = False for nid, ids in at.items(): if len(ids) != 2 or ids[0] == ids[1]: continue a, b = links[ids[0]], links[ids[1]] if (a.cls, a.width) != (b.cls, b.width): continue pa = a.pts if a.v == nid else a.pts[::-1] ua = a.u if a.v == nid else a.v pb = b.pts if b.u == nid else b.pts[::-1] vb = b.v if b.u == nid else b.u if ua == vb: # A loop back to where it started: a turning loop at a road's # end is a dead end (half of it kept); a bigger one is a real # loop road, left two links. if _length(pa + pb[1:]) < LOOP_MAX: links = [l for i, l in enumerate(links) if i != ids[1]] merged = True break continue new = Link(ua, vb, pa + pb[1:], a.cls, a.width, a.tags, a.ways + b.ways) links = [l for i, l in enumerate(links) if i not in ids] + [new] merged = True break if not merged: return links

nodes.name: way_lines
nodes.signature: def way_lines(links, paths, real: dict) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def way_lines(links, paths, real: dict) -> dict: """{OSM way id: (its snapped line in tiles, the widest link it is part of)}: each way of a routed link its stretch of the link's path, found by where the way's points lie along the link's real line (within the link's width, 3 tiles at least), carried over in proportion along the path; a way over several links their stretches joined in the way's own order and direction. real: {way id: its real points in tiles}.""" pieces: dict = {} for i, path in paths.items(): l = links[i] line_r = shapely.LineString(l.pts) line_p = shapely.LineString(path) k = line_p.length / max(line_r.length, 1e-9) tol = max(3.0, float(l.width)) for w in dict.fromkeys(l.ways): pts = real.get(w) if not pts: continue near = [(n, line_r.project(shapely.Point(p))) for n, p in enumerate(pts) if line_r.distance(shapely.Point(p)) <= tol] if not near: continue s = [d for _n, d in near] sub = substring(line_p, min(s) * k, max(s) * k) coords = list(sub.coords) if sub.geom_type == "LineString" else [sub.coords[0]] if near[0][1] > near[-1][1]: coords = coords[::-1] # the way's own direction pieces.setdefault(w, []).append((near[0][0], coords, l)) out = {} for w, ps in pieces.items(): ps.sort(key=lambda t: t[0]) geo = [] for _n, coords, _l in ps: for c in coords: if not geo or (abs(geo[-1][0] - c[0]) > 1e-6 or abs(geo[-1][1] - c[1]) > 1e-6): geo.append(c) if len(geo) < 2: continue out[w] = (geo, max((t[2] for t in ps), key=lambda l: l.width)) return out

nodes.name: raster.py
nodes.body_text: """Snapped roads to tiles. Every vertex is a tile corner and every edge a multiple of 45 degrees. Each road is drawn from one outline, its edges the centreline offset to each side: - along the grid by half the road's width (an odd width is drawn half a tile over, on a line of tile centres, so its edges are tile edges too); - on the diagonal by half an even horizontal span (span_of), so the edge runs through tile corners; - on a 2:1 slope by as near half the width as keeps the edge on a line through tile corners (lattice_k), where vanilla's 2:1 kerbs meet; - at a bend the two offsets meet where they cross - a straight edge meets a diagonal one at a tile corner, so the outline is the same road width all the way round the bend, with no spike or notch; - at the path's ends it runs on by half its width, into the junction (a dead end ends square). A tile is road if the outline covers three or all of its four quarter triangles (the quarters between its diagonals), half road if two beside one another (kept in a mask of their own with the corner of the tile the road half is in: NE/NW/SE/SW). A full tile wins over a half one; two halves of a tile make it full. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import numpy as np import shapely import shapely.affinity # Quarter-triangle centroids of a tile (y down) and the halves two of them make. QUARTERS = {"N": (0.5, 1 / 6), "E": (5 / 6, 0.5), "S": (0.5, 5 / 6), "W": (1 / 6, 0.5)} HALVES = {"NE": ("N", "E"), "NW": ("N", "W"), "SE": ("S", "E"), "SW": ("S", "W")} # Vanilla's junctions (the lot files at its right-angled Ts in Muldraugh, # Rosewood and Riverside): the two roads crossing, each inner # corner square or cut at 45 degrees by a tile or two (a 1-tile cut 74 times, # square 67, 2 tiles 32, 4 tiles 12). JUNCTION_CUT = 2 # tiles along each road's edge the cut takes CUT_ANGLES = (60.0, 120.0) # degrees between two neighbouring roads for their corner to be cut

nodes.name: span_of
nodes.body_text: def span_of(width: int) -> int: """A diagonal road's horizontal span in tiles, even: the proposal's table (2 -> 4, 4 -> 6, 6 -> 8, 8 -> 12, 14 -> 20).""" return max(int(round(width * math.sqrt(2) / 2)) * 2, width + 2)

nodes.name: _span
nodes.signature: def _span(a: int, b: int, n: int) -> slice
nodes.body_text: def _span(a: int, b: int, n: int) -> slice: """a..b clipped to 0..n (a road off the map's edge has negative corners: an unclipped negative stop counts from the far end).""" return slice(min(n, max(0, a)), min(n, max(0, b)))

nodes.name: _unit
nodes.body_text: def _unit(a, b) -> tuple: """The step of a run from corner a to corner b (its direction in lowest terms).""" dx, dy = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1] g = math.gcd(dx, dy) or 1 return dx // g, dy // g

nodes.name: _heading
nodes.body_text: def _heading(a, b) -> int: from .snap import STEP return STEP.index(_unit(a, b))

nodes.name: vertices
nodes.body_text: def vertices(path): """The corners where a path turns (and its ends).""" path = [p for k, p in enumerate(path) if k == 0 or p != path[k - 1]] # a corner given twice once if len(path) < 2: return list(path) * 2 out = [path[0]] for a, b, c in zip(path, path[1:], path[2:]): if (b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]) != (c[0] - b[0], c[1] - b[1]): out.append(b) out.append(path[-1]) return out

nodes.name: lattice_k
nodes.body_text: def lattice_k(width: int) -> float: """The offset factor of a 2:1 run's edges (offset (-dy, dx) * k, d its step in lowest terms): each edge on a line through tile corners - two tiles along to one across, through the middle of a tile edge between - as vanilla's 2:1 kerbs (street_curbs_01_diag_2, in pairs corner to corner) are drawn. The offset moves the line's x - 2y (or 2x - y) by 5k, which must be whole (half and a half for an odd width, drawn half a tile over): the nearest to half the width.""" frac = 0.5 if width % 2 else 0.0 return (round(width / 2 * math.sqrt(5) - frac) + frac) / 5

nodes.name: _cross
nodes.body_text: def _cross(p, d, q, e): """Where the line p + t d meets q + s e.""" det = d[0] * -e[1] - d[1] * -e[0] if abs(det) < 1e-9: # parallel (a run split in two): join where the next begins return q t = ((q[0] - p[0]) * -e[1] - (q[1] - p[1]) * -e[0]) / det return (p[0] + t * d[0], p[1] + t * d[1])

nodes.name: _beyond
nodes.body_text: def _beyond(n: float, d) -> float: """The offset factor for at least n tiles more beyond an edge in direction d (step in lowest terms), so the edge stays on its lattice: the offset moves the edge's line value by k |d|^2, which must stay whole. Rounded up: a 1-tile pavement by a 2:1 road rounded to 0.89 tiles lay wholly in the part-road squares at the kerb, and was lost.""" n2 = d[0] ** 2 + d[1] ** 2 return math.ceil(n * math.sqrt(n2) - 1e-9) / n2

nodes.name: outline
nodes.body_text: def outline(path, width: int, extra=(0, 0)): """The road's outline (a shapely polygon) round a snapped path; with `extra`, that many tiles more on each side (its left - the side of (-dy, dx) - and right), each edge still on its lattice.""" vs = vertices(path) half_w, half_s = width / 2, span_of(width) / 2 segs = [] for a, b in zip(vs, vs[1:]): if a == b: continue d = _unit(a, b) diag = abs(d[0]) == abs(d[1]) # Offset to the left: along the grid half the width; on the diagonal # half the span measured across x (the normal (-dy, dx) is sqrt 2 long); # on a 2:1 slope as near half the width as keeps the edge on the 2:1 # lattice through tile corners (lattice_k). k = half_s / 2 if diag else lattice_k(width) if abs(d[0]) + abs(d[1]) == 3 else half_w / math.hypot(*d) segs.append((a, b, d, [(-d[1] * ks, d[0] * ks) for ks in (k + _beyond(extra[0], d), k + _beyond(extra[1], d))])) if not segs: return shapely.Polygon() left, right = [], [] for side, out in ((1, left), (-1, right)): # Set on the first segment of the run and read from the second on; the # `else` below is the only reader, and it is never reached for n == 0. out_prev = None for n, (a, b, d, offs) in enumerate(segs): off = offs[0 if side == 1 else 1] pa = (a[0] + side * off[0], a[1] + side * off[1]) if n == 0: run_on = half_w / math.hypot(*d) out.append((pa[0] - d[0] * run_on, pa[1] - d[1] * run_on)) else: pa2, d2 = out_prev out.append(_cross(pa2, d2, pa, d)) out_prev = (pa, d) a, b, d, offs = segs[-1] off = offs[0 if side == 1 else 1] pb = (b[0] + side * off[0], b[1] + side * off[1]) run_on = half_w / math.hypot(*d) out.append((pb[0] + d[0] * run_on, pb[1] + d[1] * run_on)) # One quadrilateral a run, joined: a sharp inner corner can fold back on # itself, which a single ring would not survive. quads = [shapely.make_valid(shapely.Polygon([left[n], left[n + 1], right[n + 1], right[n]])) for n in range(len(segs))] shape = shapely.union_all(quads) # An odd width centred on corners would have its edges mid-tile: half a tile over. return shapely.affinity.translate(shape, 0.5, 0.5) if width % 2 else shape

nodes.name: junction_cuts
nodes.signature: def junction_cuts(paths: dict, links: list) -> list
nodes.body_text: def junction_cuts(paths: dict, links: list) -> list: """[(link index, triangle)]: at each junction, the corner between two neighbouring roads meeting near square, cut JUNCTION_CUT tiles along each road's edge.""" arms: dict = {} # corner -> [(link, unit direction, half width)] for i, path in paths.items(): vs = vertices(path) if len(vs) < 2 or vs[0] == vs[-1]: continue for end, nxt in ((vs[0], vs[1]), (vs[-1], vs[-2])): d = np.subtract(nxt, end, dtype=float) arms.setdefault(tuple(end), []).append((i, d / np.hypot(*d), links[i].width / 2)) out = [] for j, arm in arms.items(): if len(arm) < 2: continue arm.sort(key=lambda a: math.atan2(a[1][1], a[1][0])) for (ia, da, ha), (ib, db, hb) in zip(arm, arm[1:] + arm[:1]): turn = math.degrees(math.atan2(da[0] * db[1] - da[1] * db[0], da @ db)) % 360 if not CUT_ANGLES[0] <= turn <= CUT_ANGLES[1]: continue # Arm a's edge on b's side, arm b's edge on a's side; the corner where they cross. na, nb = np.array([-da[1], da[0]]), np.array([db[1], -db[0]]) pa, pb = np.array(j, float) + na * ha, np.array(j, float) + nb * hb det = da[0] * -db[1] - da[1] * -db[0] if abs(det) < 1e-9: continue t = ((pb[0] - pa[0]) * -db[1] - (pb[1] - pa[1]) * -db[0]) / det corner = pa + t * da tri = shapely.Polygon([corner, corner + da * JUNCTION_CUT, corner + db * JUNCTION_CUT]) if tri.area > 0: out.append((ia, tri)) return out

nodes.name: rasterise
nodes.signature: def rasterise(paths: dict, links: list, H: int, W: int)
nodes.body_text: def rasterise(paths: dict, links: list, H: int, W: int): """(owner: link index + 1 of each full tile, -1 a tile two halves make, 0 none; half: {(x, y): set of the road corners of a half tile}). Each road's outline, then its junctions' corner cuts.""" owner = np.zeros((H, W), np.int32) half: dict = {} shapes = [(i, outline(path, links[i].width)) for i, path in paths.items()] + junction_cuts(paths, links) for i, shape in shapes: if shape.is_empty: continue bx0, by0, bx1, by1 = shape.bounds x0, y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(bx0))), max(0, int(math.floor(by0))) x1, y1 = min(W, int(math.ceil(bx1))), min(H, int(math.ceil(by1))) if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0: continue ty, tx = np.mgrid[y0:y1, x0:x1] q = {k: shapely.contains_xy(shape, tx + ox, ty + oy) for k, (ox, oy) in QUARTERS.items()} count = sum(q.values()) sub = owner[y0:y1, x0:x1] sub[(count >= 3) & (sub == 0)] = i + 1 for name, (a, b) in HALVES.items(): for yy, xx in zip(*np.nonzero((count == 2) & q[a] & q[b])): half.setdefault((x0 + xx, y0 + yy), set()).add(name) # Two halves of one tile (opposite corners) make it road. for (x, y), cs in list(half.items()): if owner[y, x] or {"NE", "SW"} <= cs or {"NW", "SE"} <= cs: if not owner[y, x]: owner[y, x] = -1 del half[(x, y)] return owner, half

nodes.name: route.py
nodes.body_text: """The roads routed on vanilla's lattice, for the renderer: the "Road layout" setting's vanilla choices (straight_roads 2 and 3). route(features, proj, mode) -> graph 1. The road graph from the map's OSM ways (network.py): junction-to-junction links with a class and a width; dual carriageways made one road, lanes that hug a bigger road folded into it, turning loops dropped. 2. Every link routed on the tile-corner lattice in vanilla B42's sixteen directions - along the grid, 2:1, 45 and 1:2 - fitted where it can be to one of the street shapes vanilla's own map draws between junctions (snap.py, templates.py). Main roads first and whole; streets straight in OSM squared exactly. 3. The graph octilinear.apply_road_graph reads: each OSM way's new line (cut to its corners), the ways the graph dropped, and points along the roads before and after, by which everything else moves with the roads near it. "graph" routes every road the same way; "cost" keeps built-up streets on the grid, as the buildings along them are, and off the buildings (modes.py). It is slow beside straightening - minutes on a town of a few hundred streets, the time going on the search for each link (snap.MAX_STATES) - so it runs once, in Generate, and the result is saved beside the map for every later step. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import threading import numpy as np import shapely from PIL import Image, ImageDraw from . import modes, network, raster, snap TOWN_REACH = 40 # tiles from a building: in town (the narrower band) SHIFT_EVERY = 4 # tiles between the points along a road that say how far it moved # snap and modes keep the routing's settings in module globals: one routing at a time. _LOCK = threading.Lock()

nodes.name: town_mask
nodes.signature: def town_mask(rings, H: int, W: int, reach: int = TOWN_REACH) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def town_mask(rings, H: int, W: int, reach: int = TOWN_REACH) -> np.ndarray: """Within `reach` tiles of a building's centre.""" img = Image.new("1", (W, H), 0) d = ImageDraw.Draw(img) for pts in rings: x = sum(p[0] for p in pts) / len(pts) y = sum(p[1] for p in pts) / len(pts) if 0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H: cx, cy = int(x) + 0.5, int(y) + 0.5 d.ellipse((cx - reach, cy - reach, cx + reach, cy + reach), fill=1) return np.array(img, bool)

nodes.name: shift_samples
nodes.body_text: def shift_samples(links, paths, proj) -> list: """[[lat, lon, lat, lon]]: points every SHIFT_EVERY tiles along each routed link, where they really are and where the routed road put them (the same share of the way along it).""" out = [] for i, path in paths.items(): real, snapped = shapely.LineString(links[i].pts), shapely.LineString(path) if real.length == 0 or snapped.length == 0: continue for t in np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, max(1, int(real.length // SHIFT_EVERY)) + 1): p, q = real.interpolate(t, normalized=True), snapped.interpolate(t, normalized=True) out.append([*proj.to_latlon(p.x, p.y), *proj.to_latlon(q.x, q.y)]) return out

nodes.name: route
nodes.signature: def route(features: list, proj, mode: str = "graph", shape: dict | None = None, log=print, tick=None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def route(features: list, proj, mode: str = "graph", shape: dict | None = None, log=print, tick=None) -> dict: """The map's roads routed (see the module's notes). `features` is not changed. tick(done, total) is called as links are routed (it may raise to stop).""" with _LOCK: H, W = proj.height, proj.width nodes, links, pins = network.build(features, proj, shape) rings = modes.building_rings(features, proj) town = town_mask(rings, H, W) used = modes.prepare(mode, rings, H, W) try: paths, _corner, _merged, failed = snap.snap(nodes, links, town, log=log, pins=pins, tick=tick) finally: modes.reset() snap.close_router() # one search process per map: none left behind on a stop log(f"roads routed ({mode}): {len(paths)} of {len(links)} links, {len(failed)} left as drawn") road = network.road_ways(features) real = {f.osm_id: [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in f.geometry] for f in road} lines = network.way_lines(links, paths, real) # Each way cut to its corners, keeping every point another way ends on: a side # road's end is a node of the road it joins, as in OSM. ends = {tuple(geo[k]) for geo, _l in lines.values() for k in (0, -1)} ways = {} for w, (geo, l) in lines.items(): corners = set(raster.vertices(geo)) keep = [p for k, p in enumerate(geo) if (p in corners or tuple(p) in ends) and (k == 0 or p != geo[k - 1])] # A dual carriageway's two ways share the one line and are drawn at their own # width: one ordinary road, as vanilla draws most of its own. ways[str(w)] = {"geometry": [list(proj.to_latlon(x, y)) for x, y in keep], "tags": {}} # Roundabouts as drawn; a road routed into one ends exactly on its node (the # route ends on the tile corner nearest it). ring_nodes = [] for f in network.roundabouts(features): ways[str(f.osm_id)] = {"geometry": [list(p) for p in f.geometry], "tags": {}} ring_nodes += [(proj.to_px(*p), list(p)) for p in f.geometry] for g in ways.values(): for k in (0, -1): at = proj.to_px(*g["geometry"][k]) near = min(ring_nodes, key=lambda n: math.dist(n[0], at), default=None) if near is not None and 0 < math.dist(near[0], at) <= 1.0: g["geometry"][k] = near[1] # The ways the graph left out (folded into another road, a turning loop) go; # a link that could not be routed keeps its ways as drawn. unrouted = {w for i in failed for w in links[i].ways} drop = [f.osm_id for f in road if str(f.osm_id) not in ways and f.osm_id not in unrouted] return {"ways": ways, "drop": drop, "shift": shift_samples(links, paths, proj), "road_mode": used}

nodes.name: rustsearch.py
nodes.body_text: """Road and railway searches, run out of the interpreter (``rust/knoxroute``). Python still works out the ground - the band's costs, the way the real line runs, the frontage density, the buildings, which corners a road may turn on - because that is shapely's and numpy's work and it is fast. The *search* is the part that cost ~50 microseconds a state, so it lives in the Rust binary beside ``rust/knoxlots``: ``search()`` takes what ``snap._search`` takes once the ground is known, sends it, and gets the corners back. The binary is found the way ``knoxlots`` is (see ``tools/compile_map.py``): the ``KNOXROUTE`` environment variable, else ``rust/knoxroute/target/release``. Build it with:: cargo build --release --manifest-path rust/knoxroute/Cargo.toml A search that has no worked-out turn field (`turnable`) is the "graph" mode: this client leaves that to the interpreter's own search rather than guess. ``rail_search`` uses the same binary's ``--rails`` mode with an independent versioned frame, so older road workers still work and rails can fall back. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import logging import struct import subprocess import threading import time import numpy as np import knoxstop from ..rail_tiles import RAIL_END_RADIUS, RailFitError from . import snap BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) VERSION = 1 NO_HEADING = -2 ** 31 _HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

nodes.name: exe
nodes.body_text: def exe() -> str | None: """The knoxroute binary: KNOXROUTE, else one a release ships beside KnoxMap.exe, else the local release build - the same order knoxlots is looked for in (tools/compile_map.py).""" named = os.environ.get("KNOXROUTE") if named: return named if os.path.exists(named) else None name = "knoxroute.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "knoxroute" for path in (os.path.join(BASE_DIR, name), os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "rust", "knoxroute", "target", "release", name)): if os.path.exists(path): return path return None

nodes.name: available
nodes.body_text: def available() -> bool: return exe() is not None

nodes.name: Router
nodes.body_text: class Router: """One knoxroute process: the handshake once, then a search per link.""" def __init__(self, binary: str | None = None): binary = binary or exe() if binary is None: raise FileNotFoundError("knoxroute not built: cargo build --release --manifest-path " "rust/knoxroute/Cargo.toml") self.proc = subprocess.Popen([binary], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, bufsize=0) self._moves: dict = {} self._lock = threading.Lock() # one search at a time on this pipe self._timer: threading.Timer | None = None self._hello() # --- handshake ------------------------------------------------------------------------- def _hello(self) -> None: parts = [b"KRTE", struct.pack("<i", VERSION)] # Per heading, in the order rust/knoxroute/src/main.rs reads them. for h in range(snap.N): parts.append(struct.pack("<ii", snap.STEP[h][0], snap.STEP[h][1])) parts.append(struct.pack("<dd", snap.ANGLE[h], snap.LENGTH[h])) parts.append(struct.pack("<i", ("grid", "45", "2:1").index(snap.SLOPE[h]))) parts.append(struct.pack("<dd", snap.SLOPE_COST[snap.SLOPE[h]], snap.DIR_PENALTY[snap.SLOPE[h]])) # A notch of turn costs beta x this, and beta is the search's own. parts.append(struct.pack("<dd", snap.TURN_SHARE, snap.REVERSE)) parts.append(struct.pack("<i", len(snap.SWING_BOUNDS))) parts.append(np.asarray(snap.SWING_BOUNDS, "<f8").tobytes()) swing = np.asarray(snap.SWING_TABLE, "<u1") parts.append(swing.tobytes()) self._send(b"".join(parts)) # --- one search ------------------------------------------------------------------------ def search(self, **kw) -> tuple: """One search at a time: the pipe carries a request and its reply whole.""" with self._lock: return self._search(**kw) def _search(self, *, x0, y0, w, h, s, g, h_start, h_arrive, reach, run_min, cap, end_run, end_r, road_width, beta, lean, limit, weight, way, dens, occ, turnable, run_here, taken_idx, taken_owner, me=0, end_short=None, jog_end=None, stops=(), trace=0) -> tuple: """(path or None, states). `weight`, `way`, `dens`, `occ`, `turnable` and `run_here` are the window's arrays; `taken` comes as the corners and their owners.""" packing = self._moves.get((run_min, beta)) if packing is None: chunks = [] for hd in range(snap.N): # A curve's radius is the search's own width (run_min in snap._search), not # the road's painted width. for moves in (snap._sharp_moves(hd, beta), snap._curved_moves(hd, run_min, 1.0, beta), snap._curved_moves(hd, run_min, 2.0, beta)): chunks.append(struct.pack("<i", len(moves))) for steps, nh, nr, sign, cost in moves: chunks.append(struct.pack("<i", len(steps))) for sh, count in steps: chunks.append(struct.pack("<ii", sh, count)) chunks.append(struct.pack("<iiid", nh, nr, sign, cost)) packing = self._moves[(run_min, beta)] = b"".join(chunks) flat = (np.asarray(weight) != np.inf).ravel() idx = np.nonzero(flat)[0].astype("<i4") head = [b"\x00\x00\x00\x00", struct.pack("<iiii", w, h, x0, y0), struct.pack("<iiii", s[0], s[1], g[0], g[1]), struct.pack("<ii", NO_HEADING if h_start is None else h_start, NO_HEADING if h_arrive is None else h_arrive), struct.pack("<iiiii", reach, run_min, cap, end_run, end_r), struct.pack("<iii", road_width, int(jog_end if jog_end is not None else snap.JOG_END), me), struct.pack("<i", len(stops)), b"".join(struct.pack("<ii", int(q[0]), int(q[1])) for q in stops), struct.pack("<d", snap.END_SHORT if end_short is None else end_short), struct.pack("<dd", lean, beta), struct.pack("<q", -1 if limit is None else int(limit)), struct.pack("<i", trace), packing, struct.pack("<ii", dens is not None, occ is not None), struct.pack("<i", idx.size)] bulk = [idx.tobytes(), np.asarray(weight).ravel()[flat].astype("<f8").tobytes(), np.asarray(way).ravel()[flat].astype("<f8").tobytes()] if dens is not None: bulk.append(np.asarray(dens).ravel()[flat].astype("<f8").tobytes()) if occ is not None: bulk.append(np.asarray(occ).ravel()[flat].astype("<f8").tobytes()) bulk.append(np.asarray(turnable, "<u1").ravel()[flat].tobytes()) bulk.append(np.asarray(run_here, "<i4").ravel()[flat].tobytes()) taken_idx = np.asarray(taken_idx, "<i4") taken_owner = np.asarray(taken_owner, "<i4") bulk.append(struct.pack("<i", taken_idx.size)) bulk.append(taken_idx.tobytes()) bulk.append(taken_owner.tobytes()) self._arm() try: self._send(b"".join(head) + b"".join(bulk)) return self._read() finally: self._disarm() # --- the pipe -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # A wedged search used to hang the generate thread with both processes idle. # After this long with no reply the router is killed; _exact sees EOF and # snap falls back to the interpreter's search. SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S = float(os.environ.get("KNOXROUTE_TIMEOUT") or 600) def _arm(self) -> None: self._disarm() self._timer = threading.Timer(self.SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S, self.proc.kill) self._timer.daemon = True self._timer.start() def _disarm(self) -> None: if self._timer is not None: self._timer.cancel() self._timer = None def _send(self, blob: bytes) -> None: # RawIOBase.write

nodes.name: _send
nodes.signature: def _send(self, blob: bytes) -> None: # RawIOBase.write may write only part of the blob; the router waits for # the whole request before it answers, so a lost tail deadlocks both # ends (it happened on a large request at link 390 of 1771).
nodes.body_text: def _send(self, blob: bytes) -> None: # RawIOBase.write may write only part of the blob; the router waits for # the whole request before it answers, so a lost tail deadlocks both # ends (it happened on a large request at link 390 of 1771). view = memoryview(blob) while view: sent = self.proc.stdin.write(view) if not sent: raise RuntimeError("knoxroute stopped (its input closed)") view = view[sent:] self.proc.stdin.flush()

nodes.name: _read
nodes.body_text: def _read(self) -> tuple: ok, states, n = struct.unpack("<iqi", self._exact(16)) if ok == 2: # a trace, for the equivalence harness raw = self._exact(36 * n) if n else b"" return [struct.unpack_from("<ddiiiii", raw, 36 * k) for k in range(n)], states pts = [] if n: raw = self._exact(8 * n) vals = struct.unpack(f"<{2 * n}i", raw) pts = list(zip(vals[0::2], vals[1::2])) return (pts if ok else None), states

nodes.name: _exact
nodes.body_text: def _exact(self, n: int) -> bytes: chunks = [] got = 0 while got < n: piece = self.proc.stdout.read(n - got) if not piece: raise RuntimeError("knoxroute stopped (its output closed)") chunks.append(piece) got += len(piece) return b"".join(chunks)

nodes.name: close
nodes.body_text: def close(self) -> None: for pipe in (self.proc.stdin, self.proc.stdout): try: pipe.close() except OSError: pass try: self.proc.wait(timeout=10) except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: self.proc.kill()

nodes.name: rail_search
nodes.signature: def rail_search(guide, x0, y0, start, target, last_dir, assemblies, should_stop=None)
nodes.body_text: def rail_search(guide, x0, y0, start, target, last_dir, assemblies, should_stop=None): """Connected rail sections, or None when the native worker is unavailable. KRL2: origin/dimensions, start state, target, endpoint radius, last heading, assembly ports, then Pillow's L raster. Reply: KRL2, signed count (-1: no route), then (tile_x, tile_y, assembly_index) triples. Start/target/ports use half tiles; raster origin and result origins use whole tiles. The existing no-argument road protocol is unchanged. """ binary = exe() if binary is None: return None knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the railways") header = b"KRL2" + struct.pack("<8i3d3i", x0, y0, *guide.size, *start, *target, RAIL_END_RADIUS, *last_dir, len(assemblies)) ports = b"".join(struct.pack("<8i", *a, *b, *incoming, *outgoing) for a, b, incoming, outgoing, _pieces in assemblies) deadline = time.monotonic() + Router.SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S try: with subprocess.Popen([binary, "--rails"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0)) as proc: pending = header + ports + guide.tobytes() try: while True: knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the railways") if time.monotonic() >= deadline: raise TimeoutError("native railway search timed out") try: reply, error = proc.communicate(pending, timeout=0.1) break except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: pending = None # communicate retains partially written input finally: if proc.poll() is None: proc.kill() proc.communicate() if proc.returncode: raise RuntimeError(error.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").strip() or "worker failed") if len(reply) < 8 or reply[:4] != b"KRL2": raise RuntimeError("invalid railway worker reply") count, = struct.unpack_from("<i", reply, 4) if count < -1 or count == 0 or len(reply) != 8 + 12 * max(count, 0): raise RuntimeError("invalid railway worker result length") sections = list(struct.iter_unpack("<iii", reply[8:])) if any(not 0 <= row[2] < len(assemblies) for row in sections): raise RuntimeError("invalid railway worker assembly") except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc: logging.getLogger(__name__).warning("native rail fitter unavailable; using Python: %s", exc) return None if count == -1: raise RailFitError("Railway cannot fit connected vanilla track within its mapped corridor") return sections

nodes.name: snap.py
nodes.body_text: """The road graph snapped to sixteen directions on the tile-corner lattice, vanilla B42's: along the grid, 2:1, 45 degrees and 1:2 - Muldraugh's curves are runs on these, turning a notch at a time. 1. Junctions to the nearest tile corner; two junctions joined by a link shorter than the half-widths of their side roads plus JUNCTION_GAP are one (the side roads could not be drawn apart). 2. Every arm of a junction a heading of the sixteen, at least 90 degrees from its neighbours (45 where a junction has more arms than that allows), the least total deviation from the arms' true bearings (brute force). 2b. A main road (minor or above) routed whole: its links chained through the junctions where it goes straight on (a stroke), routed in one go against its line with small wiggles smoothed away (SMOOTH_TILES), turns dearer (BETA_MAIN) and room to stray in town (STROKE_BAND); its side roads' junctions slide onto it (STROKE_MOVE at most). Elsewhere a through road's two arms at a junction are kept opposite (THROUGH_WEIGHT). 2c. Streets straight in OSM squared: each a few degrees off one of the eight directions gets it, and the junctions all move together, as little as they can (least squares; the main roads' and pins' held; STRAIGHT_MOVE at most, STRAIGHT_MOVE_END for a dead end), until every such street runs exactly on its direction - then it is one straight run, not a jog. 3. A link leaving and arriving on one heading whose corners are a little apart sideways (less than its minimum run) has its lesser junction moved onto the line, by ALIGN_MAX at most: otherwise it needs a jog. 4. Each link routed between its two corners by A*: state (corner, heading, run since the last turn, in tiles); a move is a step along the heading, or, once the run reaches the minimum (min_run, twice it out of town, half for the first and last runs), one of vanilla's turns taken whole (SHARP corners of one, two or four notches; CURVES: a right angle as three pieces 2:1-45-1:2 at the road width's radius, or a corner cut by one 45 piece; a 45 as one 2:1 piece - twice the size out of town). Step cost length x (1 + ALPHA d^2), d the corner's distance in tiles from the real centreline (its ends moved to the snapped corners), plus BETA a turn and REVERSE more for an S-bend (a turn back within twice the minimum run). Out of town (the town mask, corner by corner) a road may stray far further for far less (BAND_OPEN, ALPHA_OPEN): a gentle angle there is a long straight, not a staircase. Hard limits: within the band, leaving and arriving on the arms' headings, and not through a road already routed. A dead end has no heading and may stop within DEAD_END_REACH of its real end; a pin (a road leaving the map) is fixed in place and heading. Routed by class, highest first; a link with no path tries a wider band, then a shorter minimum run, and is logged. Headings 0-15 step (1,0), (2,1), (1,1), (1,2), (0,1), ... anticlockwise on screen being clockwise in tiles (x right, y down); 8 notches is the opposite way. A 2:1 step goes two tiles along and one across. """ from __future__ import annotations import bisect import heapq import itertools import math import time import numpy as np import shapely from .network import RANK STEP = [(1, 0), (2, 1), (1, 1), (1, 2), (0, 1), (-1, 2), (-1, 1), (-2, 1), (-1, 0), (-2, -1), (-1, -1), (-1, -2), (0, -1), (1, -2), (1, -1), (2, -1)] N = len(STEP) ANGLE = [math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx)) % 360 for dx, dy in STEP] SPAN = [max(abs(dx), abs(dy)) for dx, dy in STEP] # tiles a step goes along the grid LENGTH = [math.hypot(dx, dy) for dx, dy in STEP] SLOPE = ["grid" if dx == 0 or dy == 0 else "45" if abs(dx) == abs(dy) else "2:1" for dx, dy in STEP] # The road's turns, as vanilla's streets.xml draws them: sharp corners of one notch, two (45 degrees) or four (a # right angle); a right angle curved as three pieces - 2:1, 45, 1:2, near # equal, each RIGHT_PIECE of the radius - or cut by one 45 piece on a tight # corner; a 45 curved as one 2:1 piece. Costs are shares of a turn's (beta). SHARP = {1: 0.5, 2: 0.7, 4: 1.0} CURVE_COST = {"right": 0.9, "cut": 1.1, "half": 0.8} RIGHT_PIECE = math.pi / 6 # each of a curved right angle's three pieces: radius x this CUT_RADIUS = 5.0 # a corner cut by one 45 piece: radius (its piece is radius x pi/2 long) _CURVES: dict = {} # (heading, width, scale) -> what curves() gives back # The turns the search may take from a heading, once per heading and beta: # [(steps [(heading, count)], new heading, run after, last turn, turn cost)]. _MOVES: dict = {} # Cost a tile on each slope, beside along the grid: vanilla runs 65-72% of its # kerb along the grid, 10-12% at 2:1 and 4% at 45 (measured from streets.xml), # 2:1 mostly round curves - so a long 2:1 road pays its way. 45 is let be # (Knox County's own roads use it). SLOPE_COST = {"grid": 1.0, "2:1": 1.15, "45": 1.0} TURN_SHARE = min(min(c / k for k, c in SHARP.items()), CURVE_COST["right"] / 4, CURVE_COST["half"] / 2) # the least a notch of turn can cost (for the search's estimate) ALPHA, BETA = 0.05, 10.0 REVERSE = 10.0 # more for a turn back the other way soon after one (an S-bend) BAND, BAND_OPEN = 6, 40 # tiles a road may stray from its line, in town and out of it ALPHA_OPEN = 0.005 # out of town straying costs little: nobody sees it FREE_OPEN = 20.0 # ...and nothing within this many tiles of the line: a gentle # angle is then a few long straights, not a staircase FREE_MAIN = 0.0 # tiles a main road may stray in town for nothing (4 made more bends) TIE = 0.001 # within the free distance, a whisper of cost toward the line: the # fewest bends first, then the closest of the routes with that many MIN_RUN_TILES = 4 JUNCTION_GAP = 2 # tiles of verge at least between two side roads ARM_LOOK = 8.0 # tiles along a link its arm's bearing is read over THROUGH_LOOK = 25.0 # ...and a through road's, over a longer stretch (past its wiggles) THROUGH_DEFLECT = 30.0 # degrees: two arms this near straight on are one road THROUGH_WEIGHT = 6.0 # cost of a through road turning by 45 degrees at a junction # Main roads are routed against their line with wiggles under this many tiles # smoothed away, and pay more for a turn: a long straight, not every wobble. SMOOTH_TILES = {"motorway": 6.0, "primary": 6.0, "secondary": 5.0, "minor": 5.0, "local": 2.0} BETA_MAIN = 20.0 MAIN = ("motorway", "primary", "secondary", "minor") STROKE_BAND, STROKE_ALPHA = 15, 0.01 # a main road routed whole may stray this far in town, for this STROKE_MOVE = 20 # tiles a junction may slide to sit on its main road STRAIGHT_TOL = 2.0 # tiles (or 2% of its length if more): a street no further than this # from its chord is straight STRAIGHT_MIN = 15.0 # ...and at least this long STRAIGHT_MAX_DEG = 15.0 # ...and this near one of the sixteen directions, to be squared to it STRAIGHT_MOVE = 15.0 # tiles a junction may move to square its streets STRAIGHT_MOVE_END = 30.0 # ...a dead end (nothing else hangs on it) CLEAR_PAD = 4 # tiles beyond a routed road's edge another road pays to come within CLEAR_COST = 3.0 # ...a tile (a cost, not a wall: a tight spot can still be routed) TEMPLATE_MIN_END = 40.0 # tiles: a dead end shorter than this is routed, not fitted to a vanilla shape # (it would hook to land exactly on its end; routed it may stop short) MAX_STATES = 500_000 # a search this big gives up (and the link tries again looser) EXACT_STATES = 250_000 # ...but first: an exact search this big, then one leaning on its LEAN_MID, MID_STATES = 1.5, 250_000 # estimate a little harder, then GREEDY = 2.0 # estimate this much harder (cost at most this times the best; # a long road out of town with room to stray is too big to search exactly) # Why the exact search is not given millions: a search that will not fit runs to # its limit and is thrown away, and its link then searches again looser. On a # town whose main roads are long and crooked those searches fill the window # (a diagonal main road's is the whole map) and take a minute each, so a town of # 1,655 links sat at 0 routed for the best part of an hour. A road that cannot be # searched exactly in a quarter of a million states is one whose exact route # nobody can see either; leaning on the estimate at 1.5 finds nearly the same # road in a few thousand, and the looser tries behind it bound the worst case. LADDER = ((1.0, EXACT_STATES), (LEAN_MID, MID_STATES), (GREEDY, MAX_STATES)) # a full link's tries in order - exact, leaning a little, leaning # hard - and the first that finds a path wins RETRY_STATES = 200_000 # the looser tries after the first (wider band, shorter runs, headings # let go) give up at this: a failing search runs to its limit, and at # 1.5 million a try a town's 9 unroutable links took 40+ minutes; a # road needing more than this in a widened band would not look right # anyway SLOW_LINK_S = 5.0 # a link taking longer than this to route is logged, with its states ALIGN_MAX = 6 # tiles a junction may move to line up a straight road DEAD_END_REACH = 3 # tiles from its real end a dead end may stop END_SHORT = 2.0 # cost a tile a dead end stops short BACK_LIMIT = 101.25 # degrees a step may turn from the way the real line runs DONE = -1 # heading of the search's finished state # Roads by frontage density (mode "cost", modes.py): COST, a 0-1 field of building # outline near each square (None: off). A step costs, on top, its length x COST_SCALE x # the density there x DIR_PENALTY of its slope - nothing along the grid, a little at 45, # much at 2:1 - so a built-up street keeps to the grid, as the buildings along it are. COST: np.ndarray | None = None DIR_PENALTY = {"grid": 0.0, "45": 0.5, "2:1": 1.5} COST_SCALE = 1.0 ARM_COST = 1.0 # a junction's arm off the grid where it is dense: density x # DIR_PENALTY x this, beside its deviation (squared, in 45s) # ...and where the density is JOG_DENSITY or more (JOG: {"dist": each square's distance to # a building, "plots": each square's land parcel number, or None}; None: off) a road turns # only at a junction (within JOG_END tiles, or its width, of its ends), a gap in the # frontage (no building within JOG_GAP tiles of the road's edge, both sides) or a parcel # boundary (the squares JOG_SIDE tiles out from the road's edge a tile and a half before # and after the turn in two parcels, either side), and runs JOG_RUN x the minimum between # turns there. JOG: dict | None = None JOG_DENSITY = 0.5 JOG_GAP = 4.0 JOG_SIDE = 3.0 JOG_END = 6 JOG_RUN = 2 JOG_LET_GO_BAND = 1.5 # a link routed with the jog rule let go (its last try): its band x this # Occupancy (mode "cost"): OCC, the buildings' footprints (None: off). A # step costs, on top, OCC_WEIGHT x the building squares under the carriageway there (a disc # the road's width across, per tile of road): a road drawn over buildings pays for each. OCC: np.ndarray | None = None OCC_WEIGHT = 0.0 _OCC_FIELDS: dict = {} # (id(src), width) -> (src, its field) (worked out once a width) JOG_LET_GO: list = [] # links the last snap() routed only with the jog rule let go GRID_HEADINGS = (0, 4, 8, 12) SWING_BOUNDS, SWING_TABLE = _swing_table() SWING_SET = frozenset(SWING_BOUNDS) # a bearing exactly on one: see h, its strictness STATES = {"searched": 0} # states searched, for the slow-link log # Which engine runs the search: "rust" (the same search in rust/knoxroute - see # rustsearch.py) or "python" (the loop in _search). Python works out the ground # either way; this only picks who searches it. Rust is the default and the # interpreter's own search the fallback: no binary built, a trace wanted, or a # turn rule the port does not carry, and it runs here instead. BACKEND = "rust" TRACE_TO = None # a list: the equivalence harness's window on the rust search's pops _UNAVAILABLE = object() # the rust search could not run: use the python one _ROUTER = None

nodes.name: curve_radius
nodes.body_text: def curve_radius(width: int) -> float: """A curved right angle's radius on a road this wide (vanilla's medians: about 12 up to 6 wide, 20 from 8).""" return 12.0 if width <= 6 else 20.0 if width >= 8 else 16.0

nodes.name: _piece_steps
nodes.body_text: def _piece_steps(h: int, length: float) -> int: """Steps on heading h making a piece about `length` tiles long.""" return max(1, int(round(length / LENGTH[h])))

nodes.name: curves
nodes.signature: def curves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float = 1.0) -> list
nodes.body_text: def curves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float = 1.0) -> list: """The curved turns leaving heading hd (a grid or 45 heading): [(kind, turn in notches, [(heading, steps), ...])] - the pieces, then the road goes on at hd + turn. The same for a heading, a width and a scale, so it is worked out once: the search used to do it again at every corner.""" key = (hd, width, scale) out = _CURVES.get(key) if out is None: out = _CURVES[key] = _built_curves(hd, width, scale) return out

nodes.name: _built_curves
nodes.signature: def _built_curves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float = 1.0) -> list
nodes.body_text: def _built_curves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float = 1.0) -> list: out = [] if hd % 2: return out # from a 2:1 run, only sharp turns r = curve_radius(width) * scale for sign in (1, -1): out.append(("right", 4 * sign, [((hd + k * sign) % N, _piece_steps((hd + k * sign) % N, r * RIGHT_PIECE)) for k in (1, 2, 3)])) cut = (hd + 2 * sign) % N out.append(("cut", 4 * sign, [(cut, _piece_steps(cut, CUT_RADIUS * scale * math.pi / 2))])) half = (hd + sign) % N out.append(("half", 2 * sign, [(half, _piece_steps(half, r * math.pi / 4))])) return out

nodes.name: _sharp_moves
nodes.body_text: def _sharp_moves(hd: int, beta: float) -> tuple: """Vanilla's sharp turns leaving heading hd, at this beta.""" key = ("sharp", hd, beta) out = _MOVES.get(key) if out is None: out = [] for k, share in SHARP.items(): for sign in (1, -1): turn = k * sign nh = (hd + turn) % N out.append(([(nh, 1)], nh, SPAN[nh], sign, beta * share)) out = _MOVES[key] = tuple(out) return out

nodes.name: _curved_moves
nodes.signature: def _curved_moves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float, beta: float) -> tuple
nodes.body_text: def _curved_moves(hd: int, width: int, scale: float, beta: float) -> tuple: """The curved turns leaving heading hd (a 2:1 run takes none of them).""" key = ("curve", hd, width, scale, beta) out = _MOVES.get(key) if out is None: out = _MOVES[key] = tuple( (pieces, (hd + turn) % N, 0, 1 if turn > 0 else -1, beta * CURVE_COST[kind]) for kind, turn, pieces in curves(hd, width, scale)) return out

nodes.name: occ_field
nodes.signature: def occ_field(width: int, src: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray
