nodes.body_text: def _lay_run(plan: Plan, line: LineString, h, level: int, width: float, cat: str, proj) -> None: half = width / 2 area = line.buffer(half, cap_style=2) x0, y0, x1, y1 = (int(math.floor(v)) for v in area.bounds) deck: dict[int, set] = {} ramps: set = set() tops: list = [] for x, y in _covered_tiles(area, max(0, x0), max(0, y0), min(proj.width, x1 + 1), min(proj.height, y1 + 1)): centre = Point(x + 0.5, y + 0.5) s = line.project(centre) height = h(s) if height <= 0: continue steps = int(round(height * RAMP_STEPS)) z, seg = divmod(steps, RAMP_STEPS) if steps == 0: continue plan.clear_veg.add((x, y)) if seg == 0: plan.put(x, y, z, "Floor", DECK_FLOOR) deck.setdefault(z, set()).add((x, y)) continue ahead = line.interpolate(min(line.length, s + 1)).coords[0] behind = line.interpolate(max(0.0, s - 1)).coords[0] dx, dy = ahead[0] - behind[0], ahead[1] - behind[1] if h(min(line.length, s + 1)) < h(max(0.0, s - 1)): dx, dy = -dx, -dy if abs(dx) >= abs(dy): direction = "E" if dx > 0 else "W" else: direction = "S" if dy > 0 else "N" plan.put(x, y, z, "Floor", ramp_tile(direction, seg)) ramps.add((x, y)) if seg == RAMP_STEPS - 1: tops.append((x, y, z, direction)) _cap_tops(plan, tops, deck, proj) footprint = set(ramps).union(*deck.values()) if deck else set(ramps) for z, tiles in deck.items(): _rail(plan, tiles, footprint, z) _posts(plan, tiles, footprint, z)

nodes.name: _cap_tops
nodes.signature: def _cap_tops(plan: Plan, tops: list, deck: dict, proj) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _cap_tops(plan: Plan, tops: list, deck: dict, proj) -> None: """Lay the deck a ramp climbs to when rounding left it short. A last segment at 19/20 storey with nothing at the next level is a ramp that tops out in mid-air: the player walks up and cannot step off. """ ahead = {"N": (0, -1), "S": (0, 1), "W": (-1, 0), "E": (1, 0)} for x, y, z, direction in tops: if any((x + dx, y + dy) in deck.get(z + 1, ()) for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))): continue dx, dy = ahead[direction] nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy if not (0 <= nx < proj.width and 0 <= ny < proj.height): nx, ny = x, y plan.put(nx, ny, z + 1, "Floor", DECK_FLOOR) deck.setdefault(z + 1, set()).add((nx, ny)) plan.clear_veg.add((nx, ny))

nodes.name: _rail
nodes.signature: def _rail(plan: Plan, tiles: set, footprint: set, z: int) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _rail(plan: Plan, tiles: set, footprint: set, z: int) -> None: edges: dict = {} for x, y in tiles: if (x - 1, y) not in footprint: edges.setdefault((x, y), set()).add("W") if (x + 1, y) not in footprint: edges.setdefault((x + 1, y), set()).add("W") if (x, y - 1) not in footprint: edges.setdefault((x, y), set()).add("N") if (x, y + 1) not in footprint: edges.setdefault((x, y + 1), set()).add("N") for (x, y), sides in edges.items(): tile = RAIL_NW if len(sides) == 2 else RAIL_W if "W" in sides else RAIL_N plan.put(x, y, z, "Furniture", tile)

nodes.name: _posts
nodes.signature: def _posts(plan: Plan, tiles: set, footprint: set, z: int) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _posts(plan: Plan, tiles: set, footprint: set, z: int) -> None: edge = sorted((x, y) for x, y in tiles if any(n not in footprint for n in ((x - 1, y), (x + 1, y), (x, y - 1), (x, y + 1)))) for x, y in edge: if (x * 7 + y * 13) % POST_EVERY: continue plan.posts.append((x, y, z))

nodes.name: rail_water
nodes.signature: def rail_water(plan: Plan, landscape, water_colour) -> None
nodes.body_text: def rail_water(plan: Plan, landscape, water_colour) -> None: """Railings along the sides of bridges over water, and posts that would stand in a road taken back out.""" px = landscape.load() w, h = landscape.size for shape in plan.water_rails: x0, y0, x1, y1 = (int(math.floor(v)) for v in shape.bounds) tiles = set(_covered_tiles(shape, max(0, x0), max(0, y0), min(w, x1 + 1), min(h, y1 + 1))) for x, y in tiles: for (nx, ny), (ex, ey, side) in (((x - 1, y), (x, y, "W")), ((x + 1, y), (x + 1, y, "W")), ((x, y - 1), (x, y, "N")), ((x, y + 1), (x, y + 1, "N"))): if (nx, ny) in tiles or not (0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h): continue if px[nx, ny] != water_colour: continue prev = plan.tiles.get((ex, ey, 0, "Furniture")) sides = {side} if prev in (RAIL_W, RAIL_NW): sides.add("W") if prev in (RAIL_N, RAIL_NW): sides.add("N") tile = RAIL_NW if len(sides) == 2 else RAIL_W if "W" in sides else RAIL_N plan.put(ex, ey, 0, "Furniture", tile)

nodes.name: settle_posts
nodes.body_text: def settle_posts(plan: Plan, is_clear) -> None: """Stand the posts under the decks, except where one would land in the road, railway or water beneath.""" for x, y, top in plan.posts: if not is_clear(x, y): continue for level in range(top): plan.put(x, y, level, "Furniture2", POST)

nodes.name: tower_kind
nodes.body_text: def tower_kind(tags: dict) -> str | None: """water_tower, lighthouse, windmill or tower; None for anything else.""" made = (tags.get("man_made") or "").lower() if made not in TOWER_MAN_MADE: made = (tags.get("building") or "").lower() if made not in TOWER_MAN_MADE: return None if made == "tower" and (tags.get("tower:type") or "").lower() not in TOWER_TYPES: return None return made

nodes.name: monument_kind
nodes.body_text: def monument_kind(tags: dict) -> str | None: """arch, column, statue, fountain, stone or tower; None for anything else.""" historic = tags.get("historic") memorial = (tags.get("memorial") or tags.get("monument") or "").lower() artwork = (tags.get("artwork_type") or "").lower() name = (tags.get("name") or "").lower() building = tags.get("building") if tags.get("amenity") == "fountain": return "fountain" if tower_kind(tags): return "tower" if tags.get("man_made") == "obelisk" or memorial in {"obelisk", "column"}: return "column" if building == "triumphal_arch" or memorial == "arch" or ( historic in {"monument", "memorial"} and ("arch" in name.split() or " arch" in name)): return "arch" if historic in {"monument", "memorial"}: if memorial in NOT_MONUMENT_MEMORIALS: return None if memorial in {"statue", "bust", "sculpture"}: return "statue" if memorial in {"stone", "war_memorial", "stele", "cross"}: return "stone" return "statue" if tags.get("tourism") == "artwork" and artwork in {"statue", "bust", "sculpture", "stone", ""}: if tags.get("leisure") or tags.get("landuse"): return None return "statue" if artwork != "stone" else "stone" return None

nodes.name: _storeys
nodes.signature: def _storeys(tags: dict, default: int, meters_per_level: float = 3.0) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _storeys(tags: dict, default: int, meters_per_level: float = 3.0) -> int: try: metres = float(str(tags.get("height", "")).split()[0]) return max(1, min(8, int(round(metres / meters_per_level)))) except (ValueError, IndexError, OverflowError): # "inf" and "1e999" read as numbers return default

nodes.name: plan_piers
nodes.signature: def plan_piers(buckets: dict, proj, meters_per_tile: float, way_width, plan: Plan) -> None
nodes.body_text: def plan_piers(buckets: dict, proj, meters_per_tile: float, way_width, plan: Plan) -> None: """Railings along a pier, where it stands over the water. A jetty is painted onto the ground like a path and left there, as the game's own bridges over water are - the terrain bitmap is one storey, and a deck raised over water in a game with no swimming is a deck nobody can reach the underneath of. What it was missing is the railing: a pier ran out into a river with nothing along either side, so it read as a concrete strip laid on the water rather than as something built over it, and you walked off the end of it without a thing in the way. The same pass that rails a bridge over water does this one (rail_water): it puts a rail on every edge whose neighbour is water, so the landward end where the pier meets the bank is left open by itself. """ for feat in buckets.get("pier", []): line = _line_px(feat, proj) if line is None or line.length < 2: continue width = max(1.0, way_width(feat, "pier") / meters_per_tile) plan.water_rails.append(line.buffer(width / 2, cap_style=2))

nodes.name: plan_monuments
nodes.signature: def plan_monuments(feats: list, proj, meters_per_tile: float, plan: Plan) -> None
nodes.body_text: def plan_monuments(feats: list, proj, meters_per_tile: float, plan: Plan) -> None: for feat in feats: kind = monument_kind(feat.tags) if kind is None: continue if feat.kind == "node": x, y = proj.to_px(*feat.geometry[0]) shape = box(x - 1.5, y - 1.5, x + 1.5, y + 1.5) elif feat.kind == "way" and len(feat.geometry) >= 4 and feat.geometry[0] == feat.geometry[-1]: shape = Polygon([proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in feat.geometry]) if not shape.is_valid or shape.area * meters_per_tile ** 2 > MAX_MONUMENT_M2: continue levels = feat.tags.get("building:levels") if levels and kind not in ("arch", "tower"): try: if float(levels) > 1: continue except ValueError: pass else: continue if not (0 <= shape.centroid.x < proj.width and 0 <= shape.centroid.y < proj.height): continue if kind == "fountain" and feat.kind == "way": # A fountain drawn as its basin is painted as water already; the # tiers stand in the middle of it. c = shape.centroid if shape.area >= 9: plan.put(int(c.x), int(c.y), 0, "Furniture", FOUNTAIN) plan.monuments += 1 continue if "building" in feat.tags: plan.not_buildings.add(id(feat)) plan.paving.append(shape.buffer(1.0, join_style=2)) {"arch": _arch, "column": _column, "statue": _statue, "fountain": _fountain, "stone": _stone, "tower": _tower}[kind](plan, shape, feat.tags) plan.monuments += 1

nodes.name: _cells
nodes.body_text: def _cells(shape) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: x0, y0, x1, y1 = (int(math.floor(v)) for v in shape.bounds) cells = list(_covered_tiles(shape, x0, y0, x1 + 1, y1 + 1)) if not cells: c = shape.centroid cells = [(int(c.x), int(c.y))] return cells

nodes.name: _arch
nodes.signature: def _arch(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _arch(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: cells = _cells(shape) xs = [x for x, _ in cells] ys = [y for _, y in cells] x0, x1, y0, y1 = min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys) along_x = (x1 - x0) >= (y1 - y0) length = (x1 - x0 + 1) if along_x else (y1 - y0 + 1) pier = max(2, min(4, length // 3)) # Tall enough that the opening reads as one: a storey of span over at # least two of open air. height = max(3, min(6, _storeys(tags, 4, 3.0))) for x, y in cells: t = (x - x0) if along_x else (y - y0) in_pier = t < pier or t >= length - pier for z in range(height): if in_pier or z == height - 1: plan.put(x, y, z, "Floor", BLOCK) if not in_pier: plan.put(x, y, 0, "Floor", PAVING)

nodes.name: _column
nodes.signature: def _column(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _column(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: c = shape.centroid cx, cy = int(c.x), int(c.y) for dx in (-1, 0, 1): for dy in (-1, 0, 1): plan.put(cx + dx, cy + dy, 0, "Floor", PLINTH) height = max(2, min(8, _storeys(tags, 4))) for z in range(height): plan.put(cx, cy, z, "Floor", BLOCK)

nodes.name: _tower
nodes.signature: def _tower(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _tower(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: """A shaft rising from its footprint, topped the way its kind is known by. A water tower is a tank on legs, so the shaft is narrow all the way and the last two storeys spread back out to the whole footprint. The rest stand on their base: the shaft rises from the middle and what is left of the footprint is a low plinth around it, which is a lighthouse or a mill seen from across a town. """ kind = tower_kind(tags) or "tower" cells = _cells(shape) cx, cy = int(shape.centroid.x), int(shape.centroid.y) half = TOWER_SHAFT // 2 shaft = [(x, y) for x, y in cells if abs(x - cx) <= half and abs(y - cy) <= half] or [(cx, cy)] height = max(2, min(8, _storeys(tags, TOWER_LEVELS.get(kind, 5)))) for z in range(height): for x, y in shaft: plan.put(x, y, z, "Floor", BLOCK) if kind == "water_tower": # The tank, wider than the legs it stands on. for z in range(max(0, height - 2), height): for x, y in cells: plan.put(x, y, z, "Floor", BLOCK) else: for x, y in cells: if (x, y) not in shaft: plan.put(x, y, 0, "Floor", PLINTH)

nodes.name: _statue
nodes.signature: def _statue(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _statue(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: c = shape.centroid cx, cy = int(c.x), int(c.y) plan.put(cx, cy, 0, "Furniture", STATUES[(cx * 3 + cy) % len(STATUES)])

nodes.name: _fountain
nodes.signature: def _fountain(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _fountain(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: c = shape.centroid cx, cy = int(c.x), int(c.y) plan.put(cx, cy, 0, "Furniture", FOUNTAIN)

nodes.name: _stone
nodes.signature: def _stone(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _stone(plan: Plan, shape, tags: dict) -> None: c = shape.centroid cx, cy = int(c.x), int(c.y) plan.put(cx, cy, 0, "Floor", ramp_tile("N", 10))

nodes.body_text: """Generate furnished Project Zomboid buildings from Knoxify footprints.""" from PIL import Image as _Image # Pillow refuses images past ~179 Mpx as a decompression-bomb guard. The # bitmaps read here are KnoxMap's own output, and web.checks._too_big_for_memory # already guards how big a map may get, so the guard only blocks big maps. _Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None

nodes.name: areas.py
nodes.body_text: """What a building's surroundings say it is. OSM rarely tags what a building is used for: in the town this was built on, 3015 of 3079 buildings were plain building=yes. The land they stand on is tagged far more often - an industrial estate, a school's grounds, a hospital site, a cemetery - and a building inside one of those is almost always part of it. Reading that turns an anonymous box on an industrial estate into a works, and the shed in a schoolyard into part of the school, instead of the suburban house every untagged building used to become. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import knoxfiles from shapely import STRtree from shapely.geometry import Point, Polygon # Area category -> building kind, for buildings OSM says nothing about. # Residential and parking are left out on purpose: a building in a # residential area is exactly what the house and flats logic already decides, # and one in a car park is a kiosk not worth guessing at. KIND_FOR_AREA = { "industrial": "industrial", "commercial": "shop", "schoolyard": "school", "hospital_grounds": "medical", "military": "military", "worship_grounds": "church", "cemetery": "church", "sports": "civic", } # Below this many tiles, a building on institutional grounds is an outbuilding # rather than the institution itself. OUTBUILDING = 120

nodes.name: parts
nodes.body_text: def parts(shape) -> list[Polygon]: """Every plain polygon in a geometry. A ring that touches or crosses itself - a landuse boundary drawn as one way round two yards, or a relation the download cut in half - is mended with buffer(0), and what comes back is then several polygons rather than one. Kept whole, a shape with no outline of its own sat in the index, and whatever asked it for one fell over; the parts go in as themselves. """ if shape is None or shape.is_empty: return [] if isinstance(shape, Polygon): return [shape] out = [] for part in getattr(shape, "geoms", ()) or (): out.extend(parts(part)) return out

nodes.name: AreaIndex
nodes.body_text: class AreaIndex: def __init__(self, polygons: list[tuple[Polygon, dict]]): self._items = polygons self._tree = STRtree([p for p, _ in polygons]) if polygons else None # How big each area is all told. An outline that came in in several # pieces is still one area, and "the smallest one here wins" has to # weigh the whole of it: half an industrial estate is smaller than # the school inside it, and would have answered for its ground. self._whole: dict[int, float] = {} for shape, props in polygons: self._whole[id(props)] = self._whole.get(id(props), 0.0) + shape.area @classmethod def load(cls, out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj) -> "AreaIndex": path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_areas.geojson") data = knoxfiles.read(path, "the land use") if not data: return cls([]) items = [] for feat in data.get("features", []): # One table of properties for every piece of this feature, so the # pieces are known below to be pieces of one area. props = feat.get("properties") or {} geom = feat.get("geometry") or {} polys = geom.get("coordinates") or [] if geom.get("type") == "Polygon": polys = [polys] for poly in polys: if not poly or len(poly[0]) < 3: continue ring = [proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lon, lat in poly[0]] shape = Polygon(ring) if not shape.is_valid: shape = shape.buffer(0) for part in parts(shape): if part.area <= 0: continue items.append((part, props)) return cls(items) def around(self, x: float, y: float) -> dict | None: """The most specific area containing a point: the smallest one. Areas nest - a school inside a residential district - and the inner one is the one that says what is actually there. """ best = self._smallest(x, y) return best[1] if best else None def shape_around(self, x: float, y: float): """The polygon around() reads its answer from: the site a military base's basement spreads under (knoxbuild/basements.py).""" best = self._smallest(x, y) return best[0] if best else None def _smallest(self, x: float, y: float): if self._tree is None: return None point = Point(x, y) best = None for i in self._tree.query(point): shape, props = self._items[int(i)] size = self._whole.get(id(props), shape.area) if shape.contains(point) and (best is None or size < best[0]): best = (size, shape, props) return best[1:] if best else None def kind_for(self, x: float, y: float, tiles: int) -> str | None: props = self.around(x, y) if not props: return None category = props.get("category") kind = KIND_FOR_AREA.get(category) if kind in {"school", "medical"} and tiles < OUTBUILDING: return "civic" return kind def mask(self, categories: set[str], width: int, height: int): """These areas as a bitmap of the map, for asking about ground rather than about one point. Nothing drawn is an empty mask, not no mask.""" import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw sheet = Image.new("1", (width, height), 0) pen = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet) for shape, props in self._items: if props.get("category") not in categories: continue # An outline mended with buffer(0) can be several polygons. for part in parts(shape): ring = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in part.exterior.coords] if len(ring) >= 3: pen.polygon(ring, fill=1) return np.asarray(sheet, dtype=bool) def category_at(self, x: float, y: float) -> str | None: props = self.around(x, y) return props.get("category") if props else None

nodes.name: basements.py
nodes.body_text: """Basements: a cellar under a house, a plant room under a school, levels of bunker under a military base. A basement is its own lot, `<parent>_bsmt.tbx`, laid at a level below 0 with its top floor at -1, and the room tables keep it a building of its own, apart from the one above, as the game's own maps do (buildheader.placed_rooms). Where each one goes is settled here, in build order, before the buildings are laid out across processes: one map of the squares already taken underground, so no two basements share a square on any level. Build 42's levels run from -32 to 31 (zombie.iso.IsoChunkMap, read for analysis). """ from __future__ import annotations import random from dataclasses import dataclass import numpy as np BOTTOM_LEVEL = -32 LARGE_KINDS = {"school", "medical", "civic", "police", "mall", "industrial"} CHURCH_MIN_M2 = 600 LARGE_TWO_LEVELS_M2 = 3_000 INSTALLATION_SITE_M2 = 50_000 # an industrial site this big goes deep SITE_M2_PER_LEVEL = 20_000 # A works' plant rooms, not a bunker: an estate's levels added a third of a big # port city's save buffer (the game's room table, tools/make_map_mod.save_bytes). INDUSTRIAL_MAX_LEVELS = 2 # ponytail: a square crop centred on the parent; follow the site's own shape if # a big base's basement looks cut off. INSTALLATION_MAX_TILES = 40_000 # per level, so a base is not one building of thousands of rooms EAST_ASIA = {"cn", "jp", "kr"} # houses there rarely have a cellar BLOCK = 32 @dataclass # --- laying one out ---------------------------------------------------------- # Where the stairs down may start, best first: through a hall, past the # laundry, and only then out of a kitchen. A big building also takes a stair in # any room but a bathroom or a bedroom. STAIR_ROOMS = ("hall", "corridor", "lobby", "laundry", "storage", "office", "kitchen", "dining", "livingroom") NOT_STAIR_ROOMS = {"bathroom", "bedroom", "kidsbedroom"} # A house with no wall in any other room to stand a stairwell against goes # down through a bedroom before the flight comes up open in the middle of one. LAST_RESORT_ROOMS = {"bedroom", "kidsbedroom"} # What a house's cellar is, as (layout kind, weight, finished). A finished one # keeps the house's own walls and floors; the rest are bare concrete. HOUSE_BASEMENTS = (("basement_house", 35, False), ("basement_house_rec", 20, True), ("basement_house_workshop", 15, False), ("basement_house_shelter", 10, True), ("basement_house_cellar", 20, False)) @dataclass # What each kind of well tries, in order, as (lane, against a wall): a home's # cellar stairs behind a door at the top (lane None), other buildings' open # stairs in a hall with a lane beside the flight (-1, 1), and "open", the # flight in the room as it is, last. Along a wall first; the shaft below has # to be inside the basement, a tile in from the outside walls, so a small # house's flight often has no wall to stand by and is walled in on both sides. WELL_TRIES = {"stairwell": [[(None, True)], [(None, False)], [(-1, True), (1, True)], ["open"]], "hall": [[(-1, True), (1, True)], [(-1, False), (1, False)], [(None, True)], [(None, False)], ["open"]]}

nodes.body_text: def tier(kind: str | None, footprint_m2: float, site_m2: float) -> str | None: """"house", "large", "installation", or None for a building with no basement.""" if kind is None or kind in ("house", "apartment"): return "house" if kind == "military": return "installation" if kind == "industrial" and site_m2 >= INSTALLATION_SITE_M2: return "installation" if kind in LARGE_KINDS or (kind == "church" and footprint_m2 >= CHURCH_MIN_M2): return "large" return None

nodes.name: levels_for
nodes.signature: def levels_for(tier: str, footprint_m2: float, site_m2: float, max_depth: int, kind: str | None = None) -> int
nodes.body_text: def levels_for(tier: str, footprint_m2: float, site_m2: float, max_depth: int, kind: str | None = None) -> int: if tier == "house": return 1 if tier == "large": return 2 if footprint_m2 >= LARGE_TWO_LEVELS_M2 else 1 deepest = min(max_depth, -BOTTOM_LEVEL) if kind == "industrial": deepest = min(deepest, INDUSTRIAL_MAX_LEVELS) return max(2, min(1 + int(site_m2 // SITE_M2_PER_LEVEL), deepest))

nodes.name: Underground
nodes.body_text: class Underground: """The squares basements have taken, level by level, in 32 x 32 blocks.""" def __init__(self): self._levels: dict[int, dict[tuple[int, int], np.ndarray]] = {} def _blocks(self, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray): """(block key, block slice, mask slice) for each block the mask covers.""" h, w = mask.shape for by in range(y0 // BLOCK, (y0 + h - 1) // BLOCK + 1): for bx in range(x0 // BLOCK, (x0 + w - 1) // BLOCK + 1): ax, ay = max(x0, bx * BLOCK), max(y0, by * BLOCK) bx1, by1 = min(x0 + w, (bx + 1) * BLOCK), min(y0 + h, (by + 1) * BLOCK) yield ((bx, by), (slice(ay - by * BLOCK, by1 - by * BLOCK), slice(ax - bx * BLOCK, bx1 - bx * BLOCK)), (slice(ay - y0, by1 - y0), slice(ax - x0, bx1 - x0))) def fits(self, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, levels: int) -> bool: for z in range(-1, -levels - 1, -1): taken = self._levels.get(z, {}) for key, there, here in self._blocks(x0, y0, mask): block = taken.get(key) if block is not None and (block[there] & mask[here]).any(): return False return True def take(self, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, levels: int) -> None: for z in range(-1, -levels - 1, -1): taken = self._levels.setdefault(z, {}) for key, there, here in self._blocks(x0, y0, mask): block = taken.setdefault(key, np.zeros((BLOCK, BLOCK), dtype=bool)) block[there] |= mask[here]

nodes.body_text: def take(self, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, levels: int) -> None: for z in range(-1, -levels - 1, -1): taken = self._levels.setdefault(z, {}) for key, there, here in self._blocks(x0, y0, mask): block = taken.setdefault(key, np.zeros((BLOCK, BLOCK), dtype=bool)) block[there] |= mask[here]

nodes.name: BasementSpec
nodes.body_text: class BasementSpec: tier: str kind: str levels: int dx: int # the basement lot's corner, from the parent lot's corner dy: int mask: np.ndarray # its squares, in its own lot

nodes.name: _inside
nodes.body_text: def _inside(mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """The footprint less its outer ring: the walls of two units of one building stand side by side, and their basements must not touch.""" m = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool) out = m.copy() out[0, :] = out[-1, :] = False out[:, 0] = out[:, -1] = False out[1:, :] &= m[:-1, :] out[:-1, :] &= m[1:, :] out[:, 1:] &= m[:, :-1] out[:, :-1] &= m[:, 1:] return out

nodes.name: _site_mask
nodes.signature: def _site_mask(shape, row: dict, inside: np.ndarray, size: tuple[int, int])
nodes.body_text: def _site_mask(shape, row: dict, inside: np.ndarray, size: tuple[int, int]): """(dx, dy, mask) of a site's squares around the parent, within the map and INSTALLATION_MAX_TILES, joined to the parent's own.""" import shapely x0, y0, w, h = row["x0"], row["y0"], row["w"], row["h"] side = int(INSTALLATION_MAX_TILES ** 0.5) cx, cy = x0 + w // 2, y0 + h // 2 a, b, c, d = shape.bounds lx = max(int(a), cx - side // 2, 0) ly = max(int(b), cy - side // 2, 0) hx = min(int(c) + 1, lx + side, size[0]) hy = min(int(d) + 1, ly + side, size[1]) xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(lx, hx) + 0.5, np.arange(ly, hy) + 0.5) mask = shapely.contains_xy(shape, xs, ys) # The parent's own squares, wherever the crop or the site's edge falls. ux0, uy0 = min(lx, x0), min(ly, y0) ux1, uy1 = max(hx, x0 + w), max(hy, y0 + h) out = np.zeros((uy1 - uy0, ux1 - ux0), dtype=bool) out[ly - uy0:hy - uy0, lx - ux0:hx - ux0] = mask out[y0 - uy0:y0 - uy0 + h, x0 - ux0:x0 - ux0 + w] |= inside return ux0 - x0, uy0 - y0, out

nodes.name: reserve
nodes.signature: def reserve(rows: list[dict], settings, region: str | None, areas, rng: random.Random, size: tuple[int, int], m2_per_tile: float = 1.0, underground: Underground | None = None) -> list[BasementSpec | None]
nodes.body_text: def reserve(rows: list[dict], settings, region: str | None, areas, rng: random.Random, size: tuple[int, int], m2_per_tile: float = 1.0, underground: Underground | None = None) -> list[BasementSpec | None]: """Where each building's basement goes, in build order, or None. A row is {"kind", "x0", "y0", "w", "h", "mask"}: the parent lot and its footprint. `areas` answers shape_around(x, y) with the site a building stands in (areas.AreaIndex), or is None. `size` is the map, in tiles.""" underground = underground or Underground() share = settings.basement_share * (0.25 if region in EAST_ASIA else 1.0) out: list[BasementSpec | None] = [None] * len(rows) if settings.max_basement_depth < 1: return out # Bases first, biggest building first, so the bunker under a site goes to # its barracks and not to a guard hut too small to take the stairs; the # rest in build order. The house share is rolled in build order regardless. rolls = [rng.random() for _ in rows] def first(i): r = rows[i] return (0, -int(np.count_nonzero(r["mask"]))) if r["kind"] in ("military", "industrial") else (1, 0) for i in sorted(range(len(rows)), key=first): row = rows[i] kind = row["kind"] or "house" fitted = np.zeros((row["h"], row["w"]), dtype=bool) m = np.asarray(row["mask"], dtype=bool)[:row["h"], :row["w"]] fitted[:m.shape[0], :m.shape[1]] = m row = {**row, "mask": fitted} footprint_m2 = float(np.count_nonzero(row["mask"])) * m2_per_tile site = None if areas is not None and kind in ("military", "industrial"): site = areas.shape_around(row["x0"] + row["w"] / 2, row["y0"] + row["h"] / 2) site_m2 = site.area * m2_per_tile if site is not None else 0.0 t = tier(kind, footprint_m2, site_m2) if t is None or (t == "house" and rolls[i] >= share): continue levels = levels_for(t, footprint_m2, site_m2, settings.max_basement_depth, kind) inside = _inside(row["mask"]) # Under its own footprint an installation's building has a building's # basement: the first one on a site takes the bunker under all of it, # and an estate of warehouses is not a stack of bunkers. tries = [(t, levels, 0, 0, inside) if t != "installation" else ("large", levels_for("large", footprint_m2, 0, settings.max_basement_depth), 0, 0, inside)] if t == "installation": whole = _site_mask(site, row, inside, size) if site is not None else (0, 0, inside) tries.insert(0, (t, levels, *whole)) spec = None for got, deep, dx, dy, mask in tries: if mask.any() and underground.fits(row["x0"] + dx, row["y0"] + dy, mask, deep): underground.take(row["x0"] + dx, row["y0"] + dy, mask, deep) spec = BasementSpec(got, kind, deep, dx, dy, mask) break out[i] = spec return out

nodes.name: first
nodes.body_text: def first(i): r = rows[i] return (0, -int(np.count_nonzero(r["mask"]))) if r["kind"] in ("military", "industrial") else (1, 0)

nodes.name: _house_basement
nodes.body_text: def _house_basement(seed: int) -> tuple[str, bool]: """(layout kind, finished) of a house's cellar, a function of its seed.""" pick = random.Random(seed ^ 0x5BD1E995).uniform(0, sum(w for _k, w, _f in HOUSE_BASEMENTS)) for kind, weight, finished in HOUSE_BASEMENTS: pick -= weight if pick <= 0: return kind, finished return HOUSE_BASEMENTS[0][0], False

nodes.name: Basement
nodes.body_text: class Basement: building: object # layout.Building, its storeys bottom first dx: int dy: int levels: int finished: bool = False

nodes.name: _run
nodes.signature: def _run(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _run(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """The squares a flight and its landings take (layout.STAIR_RUN).""" from .layout import STAIR_RUN return [(x, y + i) if d == "N" else (x + i, y) for i in range(STAIR_RUN)]

nodes.name: _top
nodes.signature: def _top(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _top(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """What a flight from below takes of the floor it rises to: the square a player steps off at, then the three over the steps (buildtiles._stair_squares).""" return _run(x, y, d)[:4]

nodes.name: _core
nodes.signature: def _core(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _core(x: int, y: int, d: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]: """The shaft around a flight, as layout._stairs_in_core reads one back.""" from .layout import STAIR_RUN if d == "N": return (x - 1, y - 1, x + 1, y + STAIR_RUN - 1) return (x - 1, y - 1, x + STAIR_RUN - 1, y + 1)

nodes.name: _well
nodes.signature: def _well(x: int, y: int, d: str, lane: int | None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _well(x: int, y: int, d: str, lane: int | None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """The squares of the room a flight comes up in: the step-off square and the three over the steps, and with `lane` (-1 or 1) the squares beside them to walk round by.""" run = _top(x, y, d) if lane is None: return run ox, oy = (lane, 0) if d == "N" else (0, lane) return run + [(a + ox, b + oy) for a, b in run]

nodes.name: find_stair_spot
nodes.signature: def find_stair_spot(ground, under: np.ndarray, kinds: tuple[str, ...] | None, avoid: set, well: str | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def find_stair_spot(ground, under: np.ndarray, kinds: tuple[str, ...] | None, avoid: set, well: str | None = None): """(x, y, dir, lane, door) on the ground floor where a flight can come up from below. The square a player steps off at and the three left open over the steps (_top) lie in one room of `kinds` (None: any room but a bathroom or a bedroom), off every door and `avoid`; the shaft below lies inside `under` (the basement's squares, in the ground floor's tiles). `well` ("stairwell" or "hall", WELL_TRIES) asks for a room of the flight's own, cut out of that room along one of its walls, with `door` its way in beside the step-off square and `lane` the hall's side. Left in the room as it was, the stairs had furniture standing across them. With no well, or none that fits, `lane` and `door` are None: the flight comes up in the room as it is. The first spot that moves no furniture wins, rooms taken in the order of `kinds`.""" from .layout import _cells_for, _is_wall_piece grid = ground.grid h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0]) if grid else 0 blocked = set(avoid) | set(ground.void) | set(ground.holes) for x, y, d in ground.doors: blocked |= {(x, y), (x, y - 1) if d == "N" else (x - 1, y)} furnished = {c for f in ground.furniture if not _is_wall_piece(f[0]) for c in _cells_for(f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3])} def room_kind(x, y): v = grid[y][x] return ground.rooms[v - 1].kind if v else None def ok(x, y, d): run = _top(x, y, d) if any(not (0 <= a < w and 0 <= b < h) or (a, b) in blocked for a, b in run): return False first = grid[run[0][1]][run[0][0]] if first == 0 or any(grid[b][a] != first for a, b in run): return False x0, y0, x1, y1 = _core(x, y, d) uh, uw = under.shape return (0 <= x0 and 0 <= y0 and x1 < uw and y1 < uh and bool(under[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1].all())) def at(a, b): return grid[b][a] if 0 <= a < w and 0 <= b < h else 0 def walled_in(x, y, d, lane, along): """(squares, door, square before the door) of a room for the flight, along a wall of its room if `along`, or None.""" sq = _well(x, y, d, lane) r = grid[y][x] if any(at(a, b) != r or (a, b) in blocked for a, b in sq): return None # One long side against a wall the room already has. if d == "N": lo, hi = min(a for a, _ in sq) - 1, max(a for a, _ in sq) + 1 sides = [[(lo, b) for _, b in _top(x, y, d)], [(hi, b) for _, b in _top(x, y, d)]] else: lo, hi = min(b for _, b in sq) - 1, max(b for _, b in sq) + 1 sides = [[(a, lo) for a, _ in _top(x, y, d)], [(a, hi) for a, _ in _top(x, y, d)]] if along and not any(all(at(*p) != r for p in side) for side in sides): return None # What is left of the room still hangs together. rest = {(a, b) for b in range(h) for a in range(w) if grid[b][a] == r} - set(sq) if not rest: return None start = min(rest) seen, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: a, b = todo.pop() for n in ((a + 1, b), (a - 1, b), (a, b + 1), (a, b - 1)): if n in rest and n not in seen: seen.add(n) todo.append(n) if seen != rest: return None # The way in, beside the step-off square: off the end of the flight # first, then its side. landing = [sq[0]] + ([sq[4]] if lane else []) ends = [(0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)] if d == "N" else [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)] for la, lb in landing: for ex, ey in ends: o = (la + ex, lb + ey) if o in sq or at(*o) != r or o in blocked: continue door = (la, max(lb, o[1]), "N") if ex == 0 else (max(la, o[0]), lb, "W") return sq, door, o return None spots = [(x, y, d) for y in range(h) for x in range(w) for d in ("N", "W") if room_kind(x, y) and ok(x, y, d)] order = kinds or STAIR_ROOMS def place(spot, loose=False): kind = room_kind(spot[0], spot[1]) if loose: if kind in order: return order.index(kind) return len(order) if kind in LAST_RESORT_ROOMS else None if kinds is None and kind in NOT_STAIR_ROOMS: return None return order.index(kind) if kind in order else (len(order) if kinds is None else None) def best(lanes, loose=False): ranked = [] for spot in spots: p = place(spot, loose) if p is None: continue for way in lanes: if way == "open": ranked.append(((p, bool(set(_top(*spot)) & furnished)), (*spot, None, None))) continue lane, along = way got = walled_in(*spot, lane, along) if got: sq, door, o = got ranked.append(((p, bool((set(sq) | {o}) & furnished), lane or 0), (*spot, lane, door))) return min(ranked)[1] if ranked else None for lanes in WELL_TRIES.get(well, [["open"]]): got = best(lanes) if got: return got # Not in a room it was meant for: in a bedroom, behind a door, still # against a wall if there is one. if lanes != ["open"] and kinds is not None: got = best(lanes, loose=True) if got: return got return None

nodes.name: room_kind
nodes.body_text: def room_kind(x, y): v = grid[y][x] return ground.rooms[v - 1].kind if v else None

nodes.name: ok
nodes.body_text: def ok(x, y, d): run = _top(x, y, d) if any(not (0 <= a < w and 0 <= b < h) or (a, b) in blocked for a, b in run): return False first = grid[run[0][1]][run[0][0]] if first == 0 or any(grid[b][a] != first for a, b in run): return False x0, y0, x1, y1 = _core(x, y, d) uh, uw = under.shape return (0 <= x0 and 0 <= y0 and x1 < uw and y1 < uh and bool(under[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1].all()))

nodes.name: at
nodes.body_text: def at(a, b): return grid[b][a] if 0 <= a < w and 0 <= b < h else 0

nodes.name: walled_in
nodes.signature: def walled_in(x, y, d, lane, along)
nodes.body_text: def walled_in(x, y, d, lane, along): """(squares, door, square before the door) of a room for the flight, along a wall of its room if `along`, or None.""" sq = _well(x, y, d, lane) r = grid[y][x] if any(at(a, b) != r or (a, b) in blocked for a, b in sq): return None # One long side against a wall the room already has. if d == "N": lo, hi = min(a for a, _ in sq) - 1, max(a for a, _ in sq) + 1 sides = [[(lo, b) for _, b in _top(x, y, d)], [(hi, b) for _, b in _top(x, y, d)]] else: lo, hi = min(b for _, b in sq) - 1, max(b for _, b in sq) + 1 sides = [[(a, lo) for a, _ in _top(x, y, d)], [(a, hi) for a, _ in _top(x, y, d)]] if along and not any(all(at(*p) != r for p in side) for side in sides): return None # What is left of the room still hangs together. rest = {(a, b) for b in range(h) for a in range(w) if grid[b][a] == r} - set(sq) if not rest: return None start = min(rest) seen, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: a, b = todo.pop() for n in ((a + 1, b), (a - 1, b), (a, b + 1), (a, b - 1)): if n in rest and n not in seen: seen.add(n) todo.append(n) if seen != rest: return None # The way in, beside the step-off square: off the end of the flight # first, then its side. landing = [sq[0]] + ([sq[4]] if lane else []) ends = [(0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)] if d == "N" else [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)] for la, lb in landing: for ex, ey in ends: o = (la + ex, lb + ey) if o in sq or at(*o) != r or o in blocked: continue door = (la, max(lb, o[1]), "N") if ex == 0 else (max(la, o[0]), lb, "W") return sq, door, o return None

nodes.name: place
nodes.body_text: def place(spot, loose=False): kind = room_kind(spot[0], spot[1]) if loose: if kind in order: return order.index(kind) return len(order) if kind in LAST_RESORT_ROOMS else None if kinds is None and kind in NOT_STAIR_ROOMS: return None return order.index(kind) if kind in order else (len(order) if kinds is None else None)

nodes.name: best
nodes.body_text: def best(lanes, loose=False): ranked = [] for spot in spots: p = place(spot, loose) if p is None: continue for way in lanes: if way == "open": ranked.append(((p, bool(set(_top(*spot)) & furnished)), (*spot, None, None))) continue lane, along = way got = walled_in(*spot, lane, along) if got: sq, door, o = got ranked.append(((p, bool((set(sq) | {o}) & furnished), lane or 0), (*spot, lane, door))) return min(ranked)[1] if ranked else None

nodes.name: plan_basement
nodes.signature: def plan_basement(parent, spec: BasementSpec, seed: int, settings) -> Basement | None
nodes.body_text: def plan_basement(parent, spec: BasementSpec, seed: int, settings) -> Basement | None: """Lay out `spec` under `parent` (a layout.Building), or None when the ground floor has nowhere for the stairs. On success the parent's ground floor is cleared over the flight and opened (Plan.holes).""" from .layout import Building, _cells_for, _clear_for_stairs, _is_wall_piece, build_plan ground = parent.storeys[0] h, w = spec.mask.shape # The basement's squares in the parent's tiles. under = np.zeros((parent.height, parent.width), dtype=bool) for y in range(parent.height): by = y - spec.dy if 0 <= by < h: for x in range(parent.width): bx = x - spec.dx if 0 <= bx < w: under[y, x] = spec.mask[by, bx] avoid = {c for s in parent.stairs for c in _run(*s)} kinds = STAIR_ROOMS if spec.tier == "house" else None # Homes and works go down behind a door at the top of the stairs; other # buildings' stairs come up in a stair hall of their own. well = ("stairwell" if spec.tier == "house" or (spec.tier == "large" and spec.kind == "industrial") else "hall") spot = find_stair_spot(ground, under, kinds, avoid, well) if spot is None: return None sx, sy, d, lane, door = spot here = (sx - spec.dx, sy - spec.dy, d) core = _core(*here) mask = spec.mask.tolist() kind, finished = (f"basement_{spec.kind}", False) if spec.tier == "house" and spec.kind in ("house", None): kind, finished = _house_basement(seed) storeys = [build_plan(w, h, seed=seed + 977 * i, kind=kind, mask=mask, ground=False, settings=settings, core=core, level=i, levels=spec.levels + 1, stairs=here, corridor=spec.tier == "installation") for i in range(spec.levels)] for st in storeys: st.windows = [] _clear_for_stairs(st, *here) building = Building(width=w, height=h, storeys=storeys, stairs=[here] * spec.levels) clear = set(_top(sx, sy, d)) if door is not None: clear = _wall_off(ground, _well(sx, sy, d, lane), door) ground.furniture = [f for f in ground.furniture if _is_wall_piece(f[0]) or not (set(_cells_for(f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3])) & clear)] ground.holes |= set(_top(sx, sy, d)[1:]) return Basement(building, spec.dx, spec.dy, spec.levels, finished)

nodes.name: _wall_off
nodes.signature: def _wall_off(ground, squares: list[tuple[int, int]], door: tuple[int, int, str]) -> set
nodes.body_text: def _wall_off(ground, squares: list[tuple[int, int]], door: tuple[int, int, str]) -> set: """Make `squares` a hall of their own, of the same flat as the room they are cut from, with `door` into that room. Returns what has to be cleared of furniture: the hall, and the squares either side of its door.""" from .layout import Room a, b = squares[0] was = ground.rooms[ground.grid[b][a] - 1] xs, ys = [p[0] for p in squares], [p[1] for p in squares] ground.rooms.append(Room(min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys), kind="hall", unit=was.unit)) for x, y in squares: ground.grid[y][x] = len(ground.rooms) ground.doors.append(door) x, y, e = door return set(squares) | {(x, y), (x, y - 1) if e == "N" else (x - 1, y)}

nodes.name: basement_style
nodes.signature: def basement_style(style: dict | None, finished: bool = False) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def basement_style(style: dict | None, finished: bool = False) -> dict: """The building's style with concrete walls and floors: the industrial kit. A finished cellar keeps the house's own interior walls and floor.""" from . import catalog as C plant = C.SPECIAL_STYLES["industrial"] out = dict(style or {}) out.update(exterior=plant["exterior"], roof=None, trim=None, shutters=None, grime=None, windows_by_levels=None) if not (finished and out.get("interior") and out.get("floor")): out.update(interior=plant["interior"], floor=plant["floor"]) out.setdefault("name", "basement") return out

nodes.name: render_basement
nodes.signature: def render_basement(b: Basement, label: str, style: dict | None) -> str
nodes.body_text: def render_basement(b: Basement, label: str, style: dict | None) -> str: from .tbx import render_tbx return render_tbx(b.building, label, basement_style(style, b.finished), roof=False)

nodes.name: bitmaps.py
nodes.body_text: """Read the map's bitmaps without holding three copies of them. ``np.array(Image.open(p).convert("RGB"))`` decodes the file into a PIL image, converts it into a second one and copies that into an array: about three times the bitmap at once. A 285 Mpx map is 855 MB as an array, so that was 2.5 GB before the building step had done anything. The renderer writes plain 24-bit (landscape, vegetation) and 8-bit (road hierarchy) BMPs. For those the pixels are read straight off the disk a strip of rows at a time into one preallocated array, so the peak is the array and a strip. Any other BMP, or a file this cannot make sense of, goes through Pillow as before. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import struct import numpy as np from PIL import Image STRIP_ROWS = 256

nodes.name: _bmp_header
nodes.body_text: def _bmp_header(path: str): """(width, height, bottom_up, bits, data_offset) of a plain BMP, else None.""" try: with open(path, "rb") as fh: head = fh.read(54) except OSError: return None if len(head) < 54 or head[:2] != b"BM": return None offset, = struct.unpack_from("<I", head, 10) size, width, height, planes, bits, compression = struct.unpack_from( "<IiiHHI", head, 14) if size < 40 or compression != 0 or planes != 1 or width <= 0 or height == 0: return None return width, abs(height), height > 0, bits, offset

nodes.name: _fast
nodes.signature: def _fast(path: str, bits_wanted: int, crop, step: int = 1)
nodes.body_text: def _fast(path: str, bits_wanted: int, crop, step: int = 1): hdr = _bmp_header(path) if hdr is None or hdr[3] != bits_wanted: return None width, height, bottom_up, bits, offset = hdr bpp = bits // 8 stride = (width * bpp + 3) // 4 * 4 if os.path.getsize(path) < offset + stride * height: return None out_h, out_w = height, width if crop is not None: out_h, out_w = min(crop[0], height), min(crop[1], width) if step > 1: # Every step-th pixel in each direction: a picture to look at, not to # measure, so the full bitmap is never held. rows = range(0, out_h, step) cols = slice(0, out_w, step) shape = (len(rows), len(range(0, out_w, step))) + ((3,) if bpp == 3 else ()) out = np.empty(shape, dtype=np.uint8) raw = np.memmap(path, dtype=np.uint8, mode="r", offset=offset, shape=(height, stride)) try: for n, y in enumerate(rows): line = raw[height - 1 - y] if bottom_up else raw[y] if bpp == 3: out[n] = line[:out_w * 3].reshape(out_w, 3)[cols][:, ::-1] else: out[n] = line[:out_w][cols] finally: del raw return out shape = (out_h, out_w, 3) if bpp == 3 else (out_h, out_w) out = np.empty(shape, dtype=np.uint8) raw = np.memmap(path, dtype=np.uint8, mode="r", offset=offset, shape=(height, stride)) try: for top in range(0, out_h, STRIP_ROWS): bottom = min(top + STRIP_ROWS, out_h) if bottom_up: # File row 0 is the bottom of the picture. src = raw[height - bottom:height - top][::-1] else: src = raw[top:bottom] if bpp == 3: px = src[:, :out_w * 3].reshape(bottom - top, out_w, 3) out[top:bottom] = px[:, :, ::-1] # BGR -> RGB else: out[top:bottom] = src[:, :out_w] finally: del raw return out

nodes.name: read_rgb
nodes.signature: def read_rgb(path: str, crop: tuple[int, int] | None = None, step: int = 1) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def read_rgb(path: str, crop: tuple[int, int] | None = None, step: int = 1) -> np.ndarray: """The picture as a (height, width, 3) uint8 array. `crop` is (rows, cols); `step` keeps every step-th pixel, for a smaller picture of a big map.""" arr = _fast(path, 24, crop, step) if arr is not None: return arr with Image.open(path) as img: arr = np.array(img.convert("RGB")) arr = arr[:crop[0], :crop[1]] if crop else arr return arr[::step, ::step] if step > 1 else arr

nodes.name: read_gray
nodes.signature: def read_gray(path: str, crop: tuple[int, int] | None = None) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def read_gray(path: str, crop: tuple[int, int] | None = None) -> np.ndarray: """The picture as a (height, width) uint8 array of grey levels.""" arr = _fast(path, 8, crop) if arr is not None: # An 8-bit BMP is palette indices; the renderer writes a grey ramp, so # they are the grey levels. Check, rather than trust it. with Image.open(path) as img: pal = img.getpalette() if pal is None or all(pal[i * 3] == i for i in range(256) if i * 3 < len(pal)): return arr with Image.open(path) as img: arr = np.array(img.convert("L")) return arr[:crop[0], :crop[1]] if crop else arr

nodes.name: same_colour
nodes.body_text: def same_colour(rgb: np.ndarray, colour) -> np.ndarray: """Boolean mask of the pixels equal to `colour`, without the (h, w, 3) boolean that ``np.all(rgb == colour, axis=2)`` builds.""" r, g, b = colour[:3] mask = rgb[:, :, 0] == r mask &= rgb[:, :, 1] == g mask &= rgb[:, :, 2] == b return mask

nodes.name: cell_hashes
nodes.signature: def cell_hashes(path: str, cell: int) -> dict[tuple[int, int], str]
nodes.body_text: def cell_hashes(path: str, cell: int) -> dict[tuple[int, int], str]: """A fingerprint of each cell x cell square of a picture, keyed (column, row). For telling which squares of a big bitmap changed between two builds without keeping the old bitmap: only the picture's bytes are read, a band of rows at a time. Two pictures give the same fingerprint for a square exactly when its pixels are the same. A square at the edge is just smaller. """ import hashlib out: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {} hdr = _bmp_header(path) if hdr is not None and hdr[3] in (8, 24): width, height, bottom_up, bits, offset = hdr bpp = bits // 8 stride = (width * bpp + 3) // 4 * 4 if os.path.getsize(path) >= offset + stride * height: raw = np.memmap(path, dtype=np.uint8, mode="r", offset=offset, shape=(height, stride)) try: for cy, y0 in enumerate(range(0, height, cell)): y1 = min(y0 + cell, height) band = raw[height - y1:height - y0] if bottom_up else raw[y0:y1] for cx, x0 in enumerate(range(0, width, cell)): part = band[:, x0 * bpp:min(x0 + cell, width) * bpp] out[(cx, cy)] = hashlib.blake2b( np.ascontiguousarray(part).tobytes(), digest_size=12).hexdigest() finally: del raw return out with Image.open(path) as img: arr = np.array(img.convert("RGB")) for cy, y0 in enumerate(range(0, arr.shape[0], cell)): for cx, x0 in enumerate(range(0, arr.shape[1], cell)): out[(cx, cy)] = hashlib.blake2b( np.ascontiguousarray(arr[y0:y0 + cell, x0:x0 + cell]).tobytes(), digest_size=12).hexdigest() return out

nodes.name: read_rgb_rows
nodes.signature: def read_rgb_rows(path: str, top: int, bottom: int, width: int | None = None) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def read_rgb_rows(path: str, top: int, bottom: int, width: int | None = None) -> np.ndarray: """Rows top..bottom (exclusive) of the picture, as a (rows, width, 3) array. For working down a big bitmap a strip at a time: only that strip is read, where opening the picture and converting it holds all of it, twice.""" hdr = _bmp_header(path) if hdr is not None and hdr[3] == 24: w, height, bottom_up, _bits, offset = hdr bottom = min(bottom, height) top = max(0, min(top, bottom)) cols = min(width, w) if width else w stride = (w * 3 + 3) // 4 * 4 if os.path.getsize(path) >= offset + stride * height: raw = np.memmap(path, dtype=np.uint8, mode="r", offset=offset, shape=(height, stride)) try: band = raw[height - bottom:height - top][::-1] if bottom_up else raw[top:bottom] return np.ascontiguousarray( band[:, :cols * 3].reshape(bottom - top, cols, 3)[:, :, ::-1]) finally: del raw with Image.open(path) as img: w, h = img.size cols = min(width, w) if width else w return np.array(img.convert("RGB").crop((0, top, cols, min(bottom, h))))

nodes.name: blends.py
nodes.body_text: """Edge blends: overlay tiles where one kind of ground meets another (Blends.txt). Blends.txt is a data file that ships with the mapping tools. Each rule names a ground kind (`mainTile`), the overlay that goes on the square beside it (`blendTile`), the direction the main ground lies in (`dir`), the layer the overlay goes on, and kinds of ground that do not get it (`exclude`). Kinds are tiles or aliases from Rules.txt. What the rules mean was worked out from WorldEd's own output (see tools/blend_check.py): - A square that is not itself the main kind, not excluded and has a tile, gets the cardinal overlay (n, e, s, w) when the neighbour in that direction is the main kind. - A corner overlay (nw, ne, sw, se) goes on a square whose two neighbours either side of that corner are both the main kind, and then replaces those two cardinal overlays. A main neighbour on a diagonal alone gives nothing. - Rules share four overlay layers. Where several fit one square and layer, the one later in the file wins (a pothole's overlay beats a grass corner). - Which of the overlay's tiles is used is picked from its alias by position, like any other tile. """ from __future__ import annotations from dataclasses import dataclass, field import numpy as np from .rules import Ruleset from .terrain import Palette, mix CARDINAL = {"n": (0, -1), "s": (0, 1), "e": (1, 0), "w": (-1, 0)} CORNER = {"nw": ("n", "w"), "ne": ("n", "e"), "sw": ("s", "w"), "se": ("s", "e")} @dataclass

nodes.name: Blend
nodes.body_text: class Blend: layer: str main: str tile: str dir: str exclude: list[str] exclude2: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)

nodes.name: parse_blends
nodes.body_text: def parse_blends(text: str) -> list[Blend]: out: list[Blend] = [] cur: dict | None = None lines = [ln.split("//")[0].strip() for ln in text.splitlines()] i = 0 while i < len(lines): s = lines[i] if s == "blend": cur = {} elif s == "}" and cur is not None: out.append(Blend(cur["layer"], cur["mainTile"], cur["blendTile"], cur["dir"], cur.get("exclude", "").split(), [tuple(p.split()) for p in cur.get("exclude2", [])])) cur = None elif cur is not None and "=" in s: k, v = (t.strip() for t in s.split("=", 1)) if v == "[": items = [] i += 1 while i < len(lines) and lines[i] != "]": if lines[i]: items.append(lines[i]) i += 1 cur[k] = items else: cur[k] = v i += 1 return out

nodes.name: load_blends
nodes.body_text: def load_blends(path: str) -> list[Blend]: with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: return parse_blends(f.read())

nodes.name: _members
nodes.signature: def _members(rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, kind: str) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def _members(rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, kind: str) -> np.ndarray: """Which palette entries are `kind` (a tile, or an alias of tiles). Kept on the palette and only extended as it grows.""" cache = pal.__dict__.setdefault("_kinds", {}) have = cache.get(kind) if have is None or len(have) < len(pal.names): wanted = set(rules.aliases.get(kind, [kind])) new = np.array([n in wanted for n in pal.names[0 if have is None else len(have):]], bool) have = new if have is None else np.concatenate([have, new]) cache[kind] = have return have

nodes.name: _neighbour
nodes.signature: def _neighbour(mask: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def _neighbour(mask: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray: """For every square, `mask` at the square (+dx, +dy) from it (False off the edge).""" h, w = mask.shape out = np.zeros_like(mask) ys, yd = (slice(0, h - dy), slice(dy, h)) if dy >= 0 else (slice(-dy, h), slice(0, h + dy)) xs, xd = (slice(0, w - dx), slice(dx, w)) if dx >= 0 else (slice(-dx, w), slice(0, w + dx)) out[ys, xs] = mask[yd, xd] return out

nodes.name: blend_layers
nodes.signature: def blend_layers(floor: np.ndarray, rules: Ruleset, blends: list[Blend], pal: Palette, seed: int, x0: int = 0, y0: int = 0, seam: int | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
nodes.body_text: def blend_layers(floor: np.ndarray, rules: Ruleset, blends: list[Blend], pal: Palette, seed: int, x0: int = 0, y0: int = 0, seam: int | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]: """{layer: (h, w) palette numbers} of overlay tiles for a window of floor tiles. `floor` is (h, w) of palette numbers, 0 where there is no tile. Squares past the window's edge are taken to have no ground, so a window should include a one-square margin of its neighbours (cut away by the caller) to blend correctly at its edge. `seam`, if given, makes squares on either side of every multiple of that many tiles (300 for WorldEd) see nothing of each other, as WorldEd does when it blends each 300 x 300 map on its own. Left out, blends run across the whole world.""" h, w = floor.shape gy, gx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w] gx = gx.astype(np.int64) + x0 gy = gy.astype(np.int64) + y0 has_tile = floor > 0 reach: dict[tuple[int, int], np.ndarray | None] = {} def look(mask: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray: """`mask` at the neighbour (+dx, +dy), unseen across a seam.""" out = _neighbour(mask, dx, dy) if seam: key = (dx, dy) if key not in reach: reach[key] = (gx // seam == (gx + dx) // seam) & (gy // seam == (gy + dy) // seam) out &= reach[key] return out layers: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {} main_cache: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {} takes_cache: dict[tuple, np.ndarray] = {} seen_cache: dict[tuple, np.ndarray] = {} for n, b in enumerate(blends): is_main = main_cache.get(b.main) if is_main is None: is_main = main_cache[b.main] = _members(rules, pal, b.main)[floor] & has_tile if not is_main.any(): continue # none of this ground in the window tkey = (b.main, tuple(b.exclude)) takes = takes_cache.get(tkey) if takes is None: excl_tab = np.zeros(len(pal.names), bool) for e in b.exclude: excl_tab = excl_tab | _members(rules, pal, e)[: len(pal.names)] takes = takes_cache[tkey] = has_tile & ~is_main & ~excl_tab[floor] def see(dx, dy, main=b.main, mask=is_main): k = (main, dx, dy) if k not in seen_cache: seen_cache[k] = look(mask, dx, dy) return seen_cache[k] if b.dir in CARDINAL: dx, dy = CARDINAL[b.dir] cond = takes & see(dx, dy) # dropped where a corner overlay of the same ground takes over for corner, (a, c) in CORNER.items(): if b.dir in (a, c): ax, ay = CARDINAL[a] cx, cy = CARDINAL[c] cond &= ~(see(ax, ay) & see(cx, cy)) else: a, c = CORNER[b.dir] cond = takes & see(*CARDINAL[a]) & see(*CARDINAL[c]) if not cond.any(): continue layer = layers.setdefault(b.layer, np.zeros((h, w), np.int64)) free = cond # one overlay to a layer: the last rule in the file that fits keeps it tiles = rules.aliases.get(b.tile, [b.tile]) ids = np.array([pal.of(t) for t in tiles], np.int64) pick = (mix(gx[free], gy[free], seed * 1000003 + 5000 + n) % np.uint64(len(ids))).astype(np.int64) layer[free] = ids[pick] return layers

nodes.name: look
nodes.signature: def look(mask: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def look(mask: np.ndarray, dx: int, dy: int) -> np.ndarray: """`mask` at the neighbour (+dx, +dy), unseen across a seam.""" out = _neighbour(mask, dx, dy) if seam: key = (dx, dy) if key not in reach: reach[key] = (gx // seam == (gx + dx) // seam) & (gy // seam == (gy + dy) // seam) out &= reach[key] return out

nodes.name: see
nodes.body_text: def see(dx, dy, main=b.main, mask=is_main): k = (main, dx, dy) if k not in seen_cache: seen_cache[k] = look(mask, dx, dy) return seen_cache[k]

nodes.name: build.py
nodes.body_text: """Turn a Knoxify output folder into furnished .tbx buildings + a WorldEd project. python -m knoxbuild output/mytown Reads <name>_info.json and <name>_buildings.geojson, reprojects every OSM footprint with Knoxify's own Projector so the buildings line up with the landscape BMP exactly, generates a floor plan for each, and writes: <dir>/buildings/<name>_NNN.tbx <dir>/<name>.pzw WorldEd project with every building placed <dir>/<name>_placements.csv """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import collections import csv import json import math import random import re import os import sys import time import numpy as np from shapely.geometry import Polygon from generator.renderer import Projector import knoxfiles import knoxstop from .areas import AreaIndex from .bitmaps import read_gray, read_rgb, same_colour from .fences import build_fences from . import footprint from .footprint import place from .layout import build_building, thin_building from .uses import USE_KEYS, is_hotel, uses_of from .context import Context, style_fits from .population import build_spawn_map, official_population, save_footprints from . import hospitals from .profile import BuildingProfile from .settings import PRESETS, Settings from .tbx import render_tbx from .world import Placement, render_pzw from . import worldmap # OSM building tags that should get a commercial room mix rather than a house. COMMERCIAL_TAGS = { "retail", "commercial", "industrial", "warehouse", "office", "shop", "supermarket", "school", "hospital", "church", "civic", "public", "government", "hotel", "service", "garage", "garages", "kiosk", } # building=* values that are not walled buildings at all. A carport or a petrol # station canopy is a roof on posts; ruins and tanks have no rooms. Built as # houses they would be solid boxes standing where the real place is open. NOT_BUILDINGS = { "roof", "carport", "canopy", "ruins", "collapsed", "demolished", "no", "bridge", "storage_tank", "tank", "silo", "transformer_tower", "chimney", "tower", "grandstand", "construction", } # Outbuildings: one room, one storey, nobody living there. SHED_VALUES = { "shed", "garage", "garages", "hut", "service", "toilets", "boathouse", "allotment_house", "bunker", "garbage_shed", "guardhouse", "gatehouse", } # An untagged building this small is a shed, a garage or a kiosk, not a home: # 30 square metres of house would be one living room with a sofa filling it. # Mappers tag the small houses that do exist (building=house), and those # stay houses. Real square metres, so a map drawn at 4 m a tile does not turn # its houses into sheds. SHED_MAX_M2 = 30 HOUSE_TAGS = ("house", "detached", "bungalow", "semidetached_house", "cabin") # An untagged building among tagged blocks of flats is taken for one when it # is at least this big, in square metres; smaller ones are the shops and # garages between them. NEIGHBOUR_FLATS_M2 = 60 # Kinds whose height follows the tagged buildings around them. A school or a # church is its own shape whatever the street is like. FOLLOWS_NEIGHBOURS = {"house", "apartment", "shop", "civic", "restaurant"} HOUSE_MAX_LEVELS = 3 # Named buildings worth a label on the paper map: the public ones people give # directions by. Hotels, banks and offices are "civic" for their room plan, # but a label on each buries the map in brand names. NOTABLE_AMENITY = {"townhall", "police", "fire_station", "library", "courthouse", "post_office", "community_centre", "theatre", "hospital", "school", "university", "college", "place_of_worship", "marketplace", "prison", "arts_centre"} # Theatres are a hall a few storeys high. THEATRE_MAX_LEVELS = 3 # OSM values that identify a building as something other than a house. Checked # against the building/amenity/shop/leisure/tourism/healthcare tags in turn. SPECIAL_BY_VALUE = { "school": "school", "kindergarten": "school", "college": "school", "university": "school", "childcare": "school", "library": "library", "church": "church", "chapel": "church", "cathedral": "church", "mosque": "church", "synagogue": "church", "temple": "church", "place_of_worship": "church", "restaurant": "restaurant", "fast_food": "restaurant", "cafe": "restaurant", "bar": "restaurant", "pub": "restaurant", "food_court": "restaurant", "retail": "shop", "commercial": "shop", "supermarket": "shop", "convenience": "shop", "kiosk": "shop", "shop": "shop", "marketplace": "shop", # A shopping centre is not a big corner shop. As "shop" it took the shop # recipe - one sales floor the width of the front, stockrooms behind - # and a 92x72 one came out as a single room of 5,670 tiles with an # office block on top. Knox County's mall is a concourse with units off # it: Muldraugh 54_22 is 33.6% hall by floor, and the rest clothes, # department, furniture, gift, toy and book stores of 150 to 400 tiles. "mall": "mall", "department_store": "mall", "industrial": "industrial", "warehouse": "industrial", "factory": "industrial", "works": "industrial", "manufacture": "industrial", "garage": "garage", "garages": "garage", "car_repair": "garage", "barn": "barn", "farm": "barn", "farm_auxiliary": "barn", "greenhouse": "barn", "stable": "barn", "cowshed": "barn", "hospital": "medical", "clinic": "medical", "doctors": "medical", "dentist": "medical", "pharmacy": "medical", "veterinary": "medical", "apartments": "apartment", "residential": "apartment", "dormitory": "apartment", "terrace": "apartment", "civic": "civic", "public": "civic", "government": "civic", "townhall": "civic", # A police station, a library and a fire station have rooms of their own # in the game, with the loot that goes in them. As "civic" they came out # as an office block with a storeroom, which is what players reported # when a station they knew had nothing in it. "police": "police", "prison": "police", "fire_station": "fire", "hotel": "civic", "office": "civic", "courthouse": "civic", "museum": "civic", "bank": "civic", "post_office": "civic", "theatre": "civic", "cinema": "civic", "arts_centre": "civic", # Bases: barracks, armouries, the offices and stores of a military site. "military": "military", "barracks": "military", "bunker": "military", "armory": "military", "armoury": "military", # The buildings a town is known by, which had no kind at all and so were # ordinary housing: thinned like a house, grown like a house and given a # sofa and two bedrooms. A castle keeps its great hall and its chapel; a # ground is a concourse, changing rooms and a kit store. "castle": "castle", "fort": "castle", "fortress": "castle", "citadel": "castle", "manor": "castle", "palace": "castle", "city_gate": "castle", "stadium": "stadium", "sports_centre": "stadium", "sports_hall": "stadium", "grandstand": "stadium", "pavilion": "stadium", "arena": "stadium", } # Last resort when the tags say nothing useful but the name is obvious. SPECIAL_BY_NAME = [ ("school", "school"), ("academy", "school"), ("college", "school"), ("university", "school"), ("church", "church"), ("chapel", "church"), ("cathedral", "church"), ("hospital", "medical"), ("clinic", "medical"), ("pharmacy", "medical"), ("warehouse", "industrial"), ("factory", "industrial"), ("mill", "industrial"), ("plant", "industrial"), ("market", "shop"), ("mall", "mall"), ("store", "shop"), ("shop", "shop"), ("diner", "restaurant"), ("restaurant", "restaurant"), ("grill", "restaurant"), ("cafe", "restaurant"), ("bar ", "restaurant"), ("barn", "barn"), ("library", "library"), ("bibliot", "library"), ("kütüphane", "library"), ("police", "police"), ("polizei", "police"), ("polic", "police"), ("karakol", "police"), ("politie", "police"), ("gendarm", "police"), ("fire station", "fire"), ("feuerwehr", "fire"), ("itfaiye", "fire"), ("caserne de pompiers", "fire"), ("brandweer", "fire"), ("bank", "civic"), ("city hall", "civic"), ("apartment", "apartment"), ("apartmani", "apartment"), ("residence", "apartment"), ("towers", "apartment"), ("blok", "apartment"), ] # Storeys, when OSM does not say and the area tables in regional.py do not # cover the kind either. A town of nothing but bungalows reads as a film set # - the skyline is what tells you whether you are downtown or in the suburbs. DEFAULT_LEVELS = { "industrial": (1, 1), "garage": (1, 1), "barn": (1, 1), "shed": (1, 1), "church": (1, 1), "apartment": (3, 5), "civic": (2, 3), "school": (2, 3), "medical": (2, 4), "shop": (1, 2), "restaurant": (1, 2), "military": (1, 2), "police": (1, 2), "library": (1, 2), "fire": (1, 1), # A keep is tall and a stand is not. Kept short because the mix is dealt # again on every storey: at four levels a castle had four chapels. "castle": (2, 3), "stadium": (1, 2), # Knox County's mall runs to five storeys; two is the common one. "mall": (1, 2), } # Rows of units under one outline. # # OpenStreetMap maps a parade of shops, a strip mall or a terrace of houses as # one polygon more often than not - the mapper drew the block, not the seven # front doors in it - and built as one building it came out as a single shed # with one door and one enormous room, whatever country the map was of. A # footprint this much longer than it is deep, and no deeper than a shop unit # is, is cut into units instead (footprint.split_row). # # Everything here is in metres, not tiles, so a map drawn at 2 m a tile splits # the same row the same way as one drawn at half a metre. ROW_KINDS = {None, "house", "apartment", "shop", "restaurant"} ROW_RATIO = 2.2 # long side over short side ROW_MIN_DEPTH_M = 5.0 # any shallower and a unit has no room in it ROW_MAX_DEPTH_M = 32.0 # any deeper and it is a big shop, not a row ROW_MIN_LENGTH_M = 22.0 # Frontages: a terraced house is narrower than a shop unit. UNIT_FRONTAGE_M = {"house": 9.0, "apartment": 9.0} SHOP_FRONTAGE_M = 13.0 # building=* values that say "row of houses" outright, in the countries whose # mappers use them. TERRACE_TAGS = {"terrace", "terraced", "semidetached_house", "row_house"} # OpenStreetMap room= and amenity= values the game furnishes under a name of # their own. Rooms a mapper drew inside a building (indoor=room) arrive with # their tags, and where the tag names something Knox County knows, the room is # built as that instead of guessed from its size (layout._mapped_rooms). MAPPED_ROOM_KINDS = { "bedroom": "bedroom", "bathroom": "bathroom", "toilet": "bathroom", "kitchen": "kitchen", "living_room": "livingroom", "corridor": "hall", "hallway": "hall", "hall": "hall", "lobby": "lobby", "classroom": "classroom", "office": "office", "storage": "storage", "utility": "storage", "laundry": "laundry", "closet": "closet", "wardrobe": "closet", "library": "library", "laboratory": "schoollab", "stairs": "hall", } # And a building too big to be one building whatever it is. # # A room may be no bigger than the game will fill (layout.MAX_ROOM_AREA), so a # footprint of forty thousand tiles came out as five hundred rooms in one # .tbx - more than any hand-made building in the game has, and slow to lay # out. Past this it is cut into blocks that stand wall to wall, which is what # a shopping centre or a works of that size is anyway. BIG_BUILDING_M2 = 6000.0 # A footprint past settings.max_size is kept and cut into units instead of # dropped, but not without limit: a polygon this many tiles in area (about a # square kilometre at one metre a tile) comes to hundreds of units, each laid # out as a building of its own, and is a campus or an airfield mapped as one # building rather than a building. Past it the old answer stands: left out. MAX_OVERSIZE_TILES = 1_200_000 # ...except a mall. A real one is 10,000-60,000 m2, and cut at the blocks # above Piqua Center came out as eleven mini-malls side by side, each with # a concourse of its own and nothing joining them. Up to this it is one # building (layout._mall_plan); past it it is a campus mapped as one outline. MALL_MAX_M2 = 60000.0 # A mall mapped with no mall tag on it: "Piqua Center" with the shops drawn # as points inside. The name alone is not enough - a medical centre has a # pharmacy, an office tower called a Plaza has a cafe in its lobby, and a # strip of shops is a Plaza too - so it takes this many different shops or # places to eat, no offices, a low building and a real mall's floor area. MALL_NAME_MIN_SHOPS = 3 MALL_NAME_MIN_M2 = 10000.0 MALL_NAME_MAX_LEVELS = 2 MALL_NAME = re.compile(r"\b(center|centre|plaza)\s*$", re.I) # Kinds with no walls and windows of their own (knoxbuild/catalog.py # SPECIAL_STYLES), dressed as the nearest kind that has: an army base is # built like a works, a station or a library like any other public building. STYLE_AS = {"military": "industrial", "fire": "industrial", "garage": "industrial", "police": "civic", "library": "civic"} # A footprint this big, with nothing but building=yes on it, is a block of # flats rather than somebody's house. # # This has to be a guess because the data gives nothing else to go on: of 3079 # buildings in a real Turkish town, 3015 were tagged building=yes and not one # carried building:levels. Taking those at face value produced 2902 detached # houses and two apartment blocks - a suburb where a town should be. # Metres of building per storey, for turning a height= into a floor count. # OSM's own convention, and close enough to the game's floor spacing. METRES_PER_LEVEL = 3.0 # A public building has no wall style of its own, so it fell through to the # house styles and a police station could come out in clapboard. These borrow # another kind's, which is what such a building is built of. BORROWED_STYLE = {"police": "civic", "library": "civic", "fire": "civic", "military": "civic", # Stone, not clapboard: a castle has no style of its own and # the house styles would have built one out of weatherboard. "castle": "church", "stadium": "civic", "mall": "civic"} # Kinds that shipped with a single style, so every church in a county was the # same church. The exterior wall is taken from a house style instead, whole - # the entry carries its own window and door tiles, so nothing is mixed. MORE_WALLS = { "church": ("brick", "stucco", "render", "painted"), "industrial": ("brick", "panel", "stucco"), "barn": ("timber", "panel", "clapboard"), } # ...and the walls inside. Every variant of a kind shared one interior wall, # so a whole county of schools was painted the same colour indoors however # many materials the outside came in. The house styles carry nine different # ones between them and each is taken whole, window and door tiles with it. MORE_INSIDE = { "school": ("brick", "painted", "stucco"), "church": ("timber", "painted", "clapboard"), "civic": ("painted", "stucco", "panel"), "shop": ("painted", "panel"), "apartment": ("brick", "painted", "stucco", "render"), "industrial": ("panel", "stucco"), "barn": ("timber", "panel"), "medical": ("painted", "stucco"), "restaurant": ("painted", "panel"), } # Of the buildings in a block, how many keep the block's own style. A street # built at one time is mostly one material with later infills between; every # house in 110 tiles being identical is what read as an estate rather than a # street. BLOCK_SHARE = 55 STALL_W, STALL_H = 3, 5 CAR_PARK_LANE = 17 # two rows of 5, and a 7-tile lane STREET_LOOK_TILES = 40 # How far off a wall counts as standing at the water's edge. A building this # close to water on one side has its door on another. SHORE_LOOK_TILES = 6 RETAIL_DENSITY = 0.28 # Land whose ground is painted in a road's colours but is not a road: an # industrial estate's gravel yard. A car park is left out - a building in the # middle of one is a kiosk nobody mapped, and keeping footprints off car parks # is right. YARD_AREAS = {"industrial"} # A job's fields up to its party walls; a BasementSpec (or None) follows. JOB_FIELDS = 21 # Below this many buildings, starting worker processes costs more than it saves. PARALLEL_FROM = 60 # What the last build made, kept beside its files so that building again - a new # zombie setting, a few footprints moved - lays out only the buildings whose # inputs changed. A building's .tbx depends

nodes.name: is_notable
nodes.signature: def is_notable(tags: dict, kind: str | None) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def is_notable(tags: dict, kind: str | None) -> bool: if kind in ("school", "church", "medical"): return True return (tags.get("amenity") in NOTABLE_AMENITY or tags.get("tourism") in ("museum", "attraction") or tags.get("historic") not in (None, "", "no") or tags.get("heritage") not in (None, "", "no") or tags.get("building") in ("government", "public", "civic", "townhall") or "wikidata" in tags or "wikipedia" in tags)

nodes.name: mall_by_name
nodes.signature: def mall_by_name(special: str | None, tags: dict, uses: list[tuple[str, str]], real_m2: float) -> str | None
nodes.body_text: def mall_by_name(special: str | None, tags: dict, uses: list[tuple[str, str]], real_m2: float) -> str | None: """"mall" for a Center, Centre or Plaza with shops in it, else `special`.""" from .uses import FOOD_FRONTS, OFFICE_USE, SHOP_USES if special not in (None, "shop", "civic"): return special if not MALL_NAME.search(tags.get("name") or "") or real_m2 < MALL_NAME_MIN_M2: return special if OFFICE_USE in uses or tags.get("building") == "office": return special try: if float(tags.get("building:levels") or 0) > MALL_NAME_MAX_LEVELS: return special except ValueError: pass retail = {front for front, _back in SHOP_USES.values()} | FOOD_FRONTS shops = sum(1 for front, _back in uses if front in retail) return "mall" if shops >= MALL_NAME_MIN_SHOPS else special

nodes.name: _cut_big
nodes.signature: def _cut_big(units: list, metres_per_tile: float, max_side: int | None = None) -> list
nodes.body_text: def _cut_big(units: list, metres_per_tile: float, max_side: int | None = None) -> list: """Cut anything left that is still too big to be one building. `max_side`, passed only for a footprint placed past settings.max_size (build.py, the "large" retry), is a hard cap on either side: the gate that used to throw such a building away no longer ran, so it is cut down to what the gate would have allowed instead. split_row leaves a piece whole when round(length / unit) comes to 1, so the cut target is 2/3 of the cap - a side over the cap is then always over 1.5 targets, which always divides, and every piece lands inside the cap. """ import math from .footprint import split_row side = max(8, int(math.sqrt(BIG_BUILDING_M2) / max(0.05, metres_per_tile))) limit = side * side cut = side if max_side is None else min(side, max(4, (2 * max_side) // 3)) def needs_cut(u) -> bool: return (u.width * u.height > limit or (max_side is not None and max(u.width, u.height) > max_side)) out = list(units) for _ in range(4): if all(not needs_cut(u) for u in out): break nxt = [] for u in out: nxt.extend(split_row(u, cut) if needs_cut(u) else [u]) if len(nxt) == len(out): break out = nxt return out

nodes.name: needs_cut
nodes.body_text: def needs_cut(u) -> bool: return (u.width * u.height > limit or (max_side is not None and max(u.width, u.height) > max_side))

nodes.name: row_units
nodes.signature: def row_units(fp, special: str | None, btag: str, n_uses: int, metres_per_tile: float, max_side: int | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def row_units(fp, special: str | None, btag: str, n_uses: int, metres_per_tile: float, max_side: int | None = None): """One footprint per unit of a row, or the footprint as it stands. `max_side` (see _cut_big) is passed only for a footprint that was too wide for settings.max_size and placed anyway, to be cut into units that fit rather than dropped. """ from .footprint import split_row if special == "mall" and max_side is None and \ fp.tiles * metres_per_tile * metres_per_tile <= MALL_MAX_M2: return [fp] if special not in ROW_KINDS and btag not in TERRACE_TAGS: return _cut_big([fp], metres_per_tile, max_side) long_side = max(fp.width, fp.height) * metres_per_tile short_side = min(fp.width, fp.height) * metres_per_tile if short_side < ROW_MIN_DEPTH_M or long_side < ROW_MIN_LENGTH_M: return _cut_big([fp], metres_per_tile, max_side) terrace = btag in TERRACE_TAGS if not terrace: if short_side > ROW_MAX_DEPTH_M or long_side < short_side * ROW_RATIO: return _cut_big([fp], metres_per_tile, max_side) frontage = UNIT_FRONTAGE_M.get(special or "house", SHOP_FRONTAGE_M) if n_uses > 1: # The shops mapped inside it say how many units there really are; # keep the frontage sane so two shops in a long parade do not become # two units of fifty metres. frontage = min(max(frontage, long_side / n_uses), frontage * 2) return _cut_big(split_row(fp, max(5, int(round(frontage / metres_per_tile)))), metres_per_tile, max_side)

nodes.name: looks_like_apartment
nodes.signature: def looks_like_apartment(tags: dict, area_tiles: int, rng, settings: Settings) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def looks_like_apartment(tags: dict, area_tiles: int, rng, settings: Settings) -> bool: """Whether an untagged building should be treated as a block of flats.""" # A mapper who recorded a height or a floor count has told us something, # but not everything.
