Three storeys up is a block of flats and one storey # is not; two says nothing, because a terraced row is two storeys and so # is a bungalow with an attic, and the footprint is what separates them. # # Taking two at face value made every large 2-storey building one house, # at any size: a 1200-tile terrace came out as a single dwelling with 25 # rooms, six bedrooms and five bathrooms. measured = levels_from_tags(tags, settings) if measured is not None and measured >= 3: return True if measured == 1: return False if area_tiles < settings.apartment_footprint: return False if (tags.get("building") or "").lower() in ("house", "detached", "bungalow"): return False return rng.random() < settings.apartment_chance

nodes.name: flats_by_height
nodes.signature: def flats_by_height(special: str | None, levels: int, btag: str, area_tiles: int, settings: Settings) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def flats_by_height(special: str | None, levels: int, btag: str, area_tiles: int, settings: Settings) -> bool: """Whether a building left a house turns out a block of flats once its storeys are known. looks_like_apartment rolls for a big untagged building with no height, and one the roll left a house still got its storeys from its footprint: Piqua had 154 houses three and four storeys up, the biggest 54 x 35, each floor sixteen offices, sixteen storerooms and eight laundries. Three storeys up is flats, as a measured height already is.""" return (special is None and levels >= 3 and btag not in HOUSE_TAGS and area_tiles >= settings.apartment_footprint)

nodes.name: _number
nodes.body_text: def _number(raw: str | None) -> float | None: """A leading number out of an OSM measurement, in metres. Values in the wild are "12", "12 m", "12.5", "12,5" and occasionally "40'" or "3;4" where two mappers disagreed. Feet are converted; a semicolon list takes the first entry. """ if not raw: return None text = str(raw).strip().split(";")[0].strip().replace(",", ".") feet = text.endswith("'") or text.endswith("ft") text = text.rstrip("'").removesuffix("ft").removesuffix("m").strip() try: value = float(text) except ValueError: return None # float() reads "inf", "Infinity", "nan" and "1e999" as numbers. None of them # is a height, and each one raised in the int() a few lines on - outside the # per-building handling, so one such tag stopped the whole build. if not math.isfinite(value): return None return value * 0.3048 if feet else value

nodes.name: levels_from_tags
nodes.signature: def levels_from_tags(tags: dict, settings: Settings) -> int | None
nodes.body_text: def levels_from_tags(tags: dict, settings: Settings) -> int | None: """Storeys according to OSM, or None where it does not say. Preference order is how confident each source is. building:levels is a mapper counting floors, so it is taken as given. height is a measurement - of the roof ridge, not the top floor - so it is divided by a nominal storey and rounded down, which is why a 10 m building comes out as three floors rather than four. """ for key in ("building:levels", "levels"): value = _number(tags.get(key)) if value is not None and value >= 1: levels = int(value) # A roof level is habitable space in OSM's model, so an attic # conversion counts - but only when the mapper recorded one. roof = _number(tags.get("roof:levels")) if roof and roof >= 1: levels += int(roof) return max(1, min(settings.max_levels, levels)) for key in ("height", "building:height", "est_height"): metres = _number(tags.get(key)) if metres and metres > 0: # A building:part sitting on a podium starts partway up. base = _number(tags.get("min_height")) or 0.0 usable = max(metres - base, metres * 0.5) return max(1, min(settings.max_levels, int(usable // METRES_PER_LEVEL))) return None

nodes.name: building_levels
nodes.signature: def building_levels(tags: dict, kind: str | None, area_tiles: int, rng, settings: Settings, metres_per_tile: float = 1.0, region: str | None = None) -> tuple[int, bool]
nodes.body_text: def building_levels(tags: dict, kind: str | None, area_tiles: int, rng, settings: Settings, metres_per_tile: float = 1.0, region: str | None = None) -> tuple[int, bool]: """How many storeys this building gets, and whether OSM said so. OSM's own height and level tags come first, as ever. Where it says nothing, the guess is the Arnis way: the kind and the real footprint together (knoxbuild/regional.py) - a 90 m2 footprint is a shop unit or somebody's house whatever country it is in, and a 2,500 m2 one is not a bungalow - with the region's own housing tables where the map is of somewhere whose housing does not run to Knox County's shapes. """ from .regional import area_level_pool measured = levels_from_tags(tags, settings) if measured is not None: return measured, True lo, hi = DEFAULT_LEVELS.get(kind or "", (1, 2)) if region == "cn": from .regional import CN_DEFAULT_LEVELS lo, hi = CN_DEFAULT_LEVELS.get(kind or "", (lo, hi)) real_m2 = area_tiles * metres_per_tile * metres_per_tile pool = area_level_pool(kind, real_m2, region) def draw() -> int: if pool: return max(1, min(settings.max_levels, rng.choice(pool))) return rng.randint(min(lo, settings.max_levels), min(hi, settings.max_levels)) return _mixed_levels(draw, settings, rng), False

nodes.name: draw
nodes.body_text: def draw() -> int: if pool: return max(1, min(settings.max_levels, rng.choice(pool))) return rng.randint(min(lo, settings.max_levels), min(hi, settings.max_levels))

nodes.name: _mixed_levels
nodes.body_text: def _mixed_levels(draw, settings: Settings, rng) -> int: """Shape an unmapped building's height to the skyline that was asked for. The guess itself (the kind and the footprint) is what knows a factory from a bungalow, so it is kept and leaned on rather than replaced: two draws and the lower of them for a low town, the higher for a tall one, the mean for one that gathers in the middle. "Even" is the exception and means what it says - every height up to the tallest, equally often - because that is what was asked for and no guess survives it. """ mix = getattr(settings, "height_mix", "auto") if mix == "even": return rng.randint(1, max(1, settings.max_levels)) first = draw() if mix == "auto": return first if mix == "middle": # The middle of three, not the mean of two: averaging a pool of 2, 3 # and 4 rounds its halves outwards and came out wider than the guess # it was supposed to gather in. return sorted((first, draw(), draw()))[1] second = draw() if mix == "low": return min(first, second) if mix == "tall": return max(first, second) return first

nodes.name: classify_building
nodes.body_text: def classify_building(tags: dict) -> str | None: """The special kind for this building, or None for an ordinary one.""" for key in ("amenity", "shop", "healthcare", "leisure", "tourism", "office", "industrial", "craft", "military", "historic", "building"): value = (tags.get(key) or "").strip().lower() if not value: continue if value in SPECIAL_BY_VALUE: return SPECIAL_BY_VALUE[value] # shop=* with an unlisted value is still a shop. if key == "shop" and value not in ("no", "vacant"): return "shop" if key == "healthcare": return "medical" # military=* is the key mappers use for everything on a base - # armory, barracks, checkpoint, office, hangar, depot - and it was # not read at all, so an armoury came out as somebody's house. if key == "military" and value != "no": return "military" name = (tags.get("name") or "").lower() for needle, kind in SPECIAL_BY_NAME: if needle in name: return kind return None

nodes.name: _business_kind
nodes.signature: def _business_kind(special: str | None, uses: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str | None
nodes.body_text: def _business_kind(special: str | None, uses: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str | None: """Promote retail outlines containing a mapped car-repair business to a garage.""" if special in (None, "shop") and ("mechanic", "storage") in uses: return "garage" return special

nodes.name: _wall_pool
nodes.body_text: def _wall_pool(kind: str | None) -> list[dict]: """The styles a building of this kind is really built in, or none. A kind that borrows another's walls - a police station is built of what a civic building is built of - is asked about under the kind it borrows from, which is what pick_style does; a kind with no walls of its own at all has none, rather than raising. """ from . import catalog as C kind = BORROWED_STYLE.get(kind or "", kind) if not kind or kind not in C.SPECIAL_STYLES: return [] return wall_variants(kind)

nodes.name: style_names
nodes.signature: def style_names(kind: str | None = None) -> list[str]
nodes.body_text: def style_names(kind: str | None = None) -> list[str]: """Every wall style a zone may pin its buildings to, by name.""" from . import catalog as C names = [style["name"] for style in C.HOUSE_STYLES] names += [v["name"] for v in _wall_pool(kind) if v.get("name")] seen, out = set(), [] for name in names: if name and name not in seen: seen.add(name) out.append(name) return out

nodes.name: style_named
nodes.signature: def style_named(name: str, kind: str | None) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def style_named(name: str, kind: str | None) -> dict | None: """The style of that name for this kind of building, or None. A kind with walls of its own is asked first, so pinning "brick" on a church gets the church's brick rather than a house's; a name nothing answers to gets None, and the caller keeps the style it had. """ from . import catalog as C wanted = (name or "").strip().lower() if not wanted: return None pools = [] own = _wall_pool(kind) if own: pools.append(own) pools.append(C.HOUSE_STYLES) for pool in pools: for style in pool: if (style.get("name") or "").lower() == wanted: return style # "brick" against a church's "church_brick", which is what a mapper # pinning a style by its plain name means. for pool in pools: for style in pool: if wanted in (style.get("name") or "").lower().split("_"): return style return None

nodes.name: wall_variants
nodes.body_text: def wall_variants(kind: str) -> list[dict]: """Every style a building of this kind may be built in.""" from . import catalog as C base = C.SPECIAL_STYLES[kind] out = list(getattr(C, "SPECIAL_STYLE_VARIANTS", {}).get(kind) or [base]) houses = {s["name"]: s for s in C.HOUSE_STYLES} for name in MORE_WALLS.get(kind, ()): donor = houses.get(name) if not donor: continue variant = dict(base) variant["exterior"] = donor["exterior"] variant["name"] = f"{base['name']}_{name}" out.append(variant) inside = [(n, houses[n]["interior"]) for n in MORE_INSIDE.get(kind, ()) if n in houses] if inside: grown = [] for variant in out: grown.append(variant) for name, entry in inside: other = dict(variant) other["interior"] = entry other["name"] = f"{variant['name']}~{name}" grown.append(other) out = grown return out

nodes.name: pick_style
nodes.signature: def pick_style(kind: str | None, tile_x: int, tile_y: int, rng, settings: Settings, density: float = 0.0, profile: BuildingProfile | None = None, region: str | None = None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def pick_style(kind: str | None, tile_x: int, tile_y: int, rng, settings: Settings, density: float = 0.0, profile: BuildingProfile | None = None, region: str | None = None) -> dict: """Materials for one building: its own if special, else its block's. Only styles that suit how built-up the place is are in the running, so the old town gets render and brick and the log cabins stay in the countryside. A Chinese map (or one set to Chinese) builds its houses from the flat-roofed masonry pool instead - unless the building is a dated prewar one, which keeps its pitched roof and era materials: the temple and the 1920s shophouse are the last things a regional pool should flatten. """ from . import catalog as C from . import regional kind = BORROWED_STYLE.get(kind or "", kind) if kind and kind in C.SPECIAL_STYLES: variants = wall_variants(kind) if profile: picker = random.Random(profile.seed ^ 0xA37E) weights = [profile.style_weight(variant["name"]) for variant in variants] return picker.choices(variants, weights=weights, k=1)[0] # By the building's own position, so neighbours differ and a rebuild # picks the same again. return variants[(tile_x * 73856093 ^ tile_y * 19349663) % len(variants)] if region == "cn" and not (profile and profile.dated and profile.era == "prewar"): pool = regional.cn_house_styles() styles = [s for s in pool if style_fits(s["name"], density)] or pool else: styles = [s for s in C.HOUSE_STYLES if style_fits(s["name"], density)] \ or C.HOUSE_STYLES size = settings.neighbourhood_tiles block = (tile_x // size, tile_y // size) # Deterministic per block, so re-running gives the same town. idx = (block[0] * 73856093 ^ block[1] * 19349663) % len(styles) # ...and then per building, so a block is a street rather than one house # built over and over. own = (tile_x * 83492791 ^ tile_y * 297121507) & 0x7FFFFFFF if len(styles) > 1 and own % 100 >= BLOCK_SHARE: idx = (own // 100) % len(styles) if len(styles) > 1 and rng.random() < settings.style_oddity: idx = (idx + 1 + rng.randrange(len(styles) - 1)) % len(styles) if profile: weights = [profile.style_weight(style["name"]) * (1.4 if i == idx else 1.0) for i, style in enumerate(styles)] picker = random.Random(profile.seed ^ 0xA37E) return picker.choices(styles, weights=weights, k=1)[0] return styles[idx]

nodes.name: car_park_stalls
nodes.signature: def car_park_stalls(bounds: tuple[int, int, int, int], w: int, h: int)
nodes.body_text: def car_park_stalls(bounds: tuple[int, int, int, int], w: int, h: int): """Where a stall could go in a car park with these bounds, as (x, y, sw, sh), in the order they are tried - only the ones that lie on the map. This used to walk the whole bounding box of the car park and throw away what was off the map afterwards. A car park a few hundred metres past the edge costs nothing; a polygon of the whole country mapped as one (it happens) was hundreds of millions of steps. Starting each run at the first position that can be on the map visits the same stalls in the same order.""" x0, y0, x1, y1 = bounds across = (x1 - x0) >= (y1 - y0) # rows run along the long side sw, sh = (STALL_W, STALL_H) if across else (STALL_H, STALL_W) # b runs along the rows, a across them; a + row is the offset of a stall's row. b_origin, b_len, b_map = (x0, x1 - x0, w) if across else (y0, y1 - y0, h) a_origin, a_len, a_map = (y0, y1 - y0, h) if across else (x0, x1 - x0, w) lane = CAR_PARK_LANE a_lo = max(0, -a_origin - STALL_H) a_start = -(-a_lo // lane) * lane a_stop = min(a_len, a_map - STALL_H - a_origin + 1) b_lo = max(0, -b_origin) b_start = -(-b_lo // STALL_W) * STALL_W b_stop = min(b_len, b_map - STALL_W - b_origin + 1) for a in range(a_start, a_stop, lane): for row in (0, STALL_H): for b in range(b_start, b_stop, STALL_W): x, y = (x0 + b, y0 + a + row) if across else (x0 + a + row, y0 + b) if 0 <= x and x + sw <= w and 0 <= y and y + sh <= h: yield x, y, sw, sh

nodes.name: _detect_zones
nodes.signature: def _detect_zones(landscape_path: str, placements, rng_seed: int = 7, settings: Settings | None = None, areas=None, drives=(), keep_clear=(), road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def _detect_zones(landscape_path: str, placements, rng_seed: int = 7, settings: Settings | None = None, areas=None, drives=(), keep_clear=(), road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None): """Parking stalls along the roads, town zones over built-up ground. Without these the streets are bare: vehicles only ever spawn inside ParkingStall zones, and TownZone is what marks ground as urban. Vanilla Knox County ships 9694 of the former and 2715 of the latter. Stalls are found by scanning the landscape bitmap for asphalt that sits on a road *edge* — a stall in the middle of a carriageway would block it. """ import random from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from .world import Zone ASPHALT = {C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE} settings = settings or Settings() rng = random.Random(rng_seed) zones: list[Zone] = [] with Image.open(landscape_path) as source: img = source.convert("RGB") w, h = img.size px = img.load() if road_hierarchy is not None: road_hierarchy = road_hierarchy[:h, :w] def is_asphalt(x: int, y: int) -> bool: """Carriageway or car park, as opposed to the pavement beside it.""" if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): return False # The three street shades plus the two pothole shades that weather # them. Kerbs and paving slabs are deliberately out: parking a car on # the pavement is where stalls ended up once roads grew kerbs, because # any grey pixel in a wide range counted as road. return px[x, y] in ASPHALT STALL_W, STALL_H = 3, 5 step = 14 # how often to consider a spot taken: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() # A car on most drives, as in Knox County. for x, y, sw, sh in drives: if rng.random() <= min(1.0, 0.6 * settings.parking_density): taken.add((x // 8, y // 8)) zones.append(Zone("ParkingStall", x, y, sw, sh)) # Car parks OpenStreetMap maps as such: rows of stalls across the whole of # each, two rows back to back and then a lane, the way a real one is laid # out. Sampling the tarmac every 14 tiles found at most a stall or two in # anything smaller than a supermarket's, so most car parks had no cars. if areas is not None: from shapely.geometry import box buildings = [box(p.tile_x, p.tile_y, p.tile_x + p.width, p.tile_y + p.height) for p in placements] from shapely import STRtree built = STRtree(buildings) if buildings else None lots = [shape for shape, props in areas._items if props.get("category") == "parking"] hard = ASPHALT | {C.PALE_CONCRETE, C.PAVING} for lot in lots: bounds = tuple(int(v) for v in lot.bounds) for x, y, sw, sh in car_park_stalls(bounds, w, h): stall = box(x, y, x + sw, y + sh) if not lot.contains(stall): continue if any(px[i, j] not in hard for i in (x, x + sw - 1) for j in (y, y + sh - 1)): continue if built is not None and any(buildings[int(i)].intersects(stall) for i in built.query(stall)): continue if rng.random() > min(1.0, 0.55 * settings.parking_density): continue taken.add((x // 8, y // 8)) zones.append(Zone("ParkingStall", x, y, sw, sh)) for y in range(4, h - STALL_H - 4, step): for x in range(4, w - STALL_W - 4, step): if not is_asphalt(x, y): continue kerbside = not (is_asphalt(x - 4, y) and is_asphalt(x + 4, y) and is_asphalt(x, y - 4) and is_asphalt(x, y + 4)) # Deep inside a wide expanse of tarmac: no carriageway is 16 tiles # across, so this is a car park, and its middle is exactly where # the cars go. The old rule skipped every interior spot to avoid # blocking a road, which left car parks themselves empty. car_park = (is_asphalt(x - 8, y) and is_asphalt(x + 8, y) and is_asphalt(x, y - 8) and is_asphalt(x, y + 8)) if not kerbside and not car_park: continue if car_park: rate = 0.75 elif road_hierarchy is None or not road_hierarchy[y, x]: rate = 0.45 else: rate = { 1: 0.0, 2: 0.18, 3: 0.55, 4: 0.38, 5: 0.28, 6: 0.16, 7: 0.08, 8: 0.02, }.get(int(road_hierarchy[y, x]), 0.45) chance = rate * settings.parking_density if rng.random() > chance: continue vertical = is_asphalt(x, y - 2) or is_asphalt(x, y + 2) sw, sh = (STALL_W, STALL_H) if vertical else (STALL_H, STALL_W) # Not on a petrol station's forecourt, where the pumps stand. if any(x < fx + fw and fx < x + sw and y < fy + fh and fy < y + sh for fx, fy, fw, fh in keep_clear): continue key = (x // 8, y // 8) if key in taken: continue taken.add(key) zones.append(Zone("ParkingStall", x, y, sw, sh)) # One town zone per cell that holds buildings, covering their extent with a # margin so gardens and the street frontage count as town too. by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} for p in placements: by_cell.setdefault((p.cell_x, p.cell_y), []).append(p) for (cx, cy), group in by_cell.items(): x0 = max(0, min(p.tile_x for p in group) - 8) y0 = max(0, min(p.tile_y for p in group) - 8) x1 = min(w, max(p.tile_x + p.width for p in group) + 8) y1 = min(h, max(p.tile_y + p.height for p in group) + 8) # Clamp into the owning cell so the rectangle stays where it is written. x0 = max(x0, cx * 300) y0 = max(y0, cy * 300) x1 = min(x1, (cx + 1) * 300) y1 = min(y1, (cy +

nodes.name: is_asphalt
nodes.signature: def is_asphalt(x: int, y: int) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def is_asphalt(x: int, y: int) -> bool: """Carriageway or car park, as opposed to the pavement beside it.""" if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h): return False # The three street shades plus the two pothole shades that weather # them. Kerbs and paving slabs are deliberately out: parking a car on # the pavement is where stalls ended up once roads grew kerbs, because # any grey pixel in a wide range counted as road. return px[x, y] in ASPHALT

nodes.name: _ring_points
nodes.body_text: def _ring_points(geom: dict) -> list[list[float]]: """Every [lon, lat] in a Polygon or MultiPolygon outer ring.""" if geom["type"] == "Polygon": return geom["coordinates"][0] pts: list[list[float]] = [] for poly in geom["coordinates"]: pts.extend(poly[0]) return pts

nodes.name: _street_finder
nodes.signature: def _street_finder(out_dir: str, map_name: str, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def _street_finder(out_dir: str, map_name: str, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None): """A function giving the side ("N", "S", "W" or "E") of a footprint that faces the nearest pavement or road, or None if none is near.""" import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as PC path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_ground_base.bmp") if not os.path.exists(path): path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.bmp") if not os.path.exists(path): return lambda *a: None g = read_rgb(path) paved = np.zeros(g.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for c in (PC.PALE_CONCRETE, PC.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, PC.DARKEST_ASPHALT): paved |= same_colour(g, c) water = same_colour(g, PC.WATER) H, W = paved.shape def side(x0: int, y0: int, w: int, h: int) -> str | None: best, best_score = None, STREET_LOOK_TILES + 1 wet = {} for name, (dx, dy) in (("N", (0, -1)), ("S", (0, 1)), ("W", (-1, 0)), ("E", (1, 0))): if dx == 0: starts = [(x0 + w * f // 4, y0 if dy < 0 else y0 + h - 1) for f in (1, 2, 3)] else: starts = [(x0 if dx < 0 else x0 + w - 1, y0 + h * f // 4) for f in (1, 2, 3)] near_water = SHORE_LOOK_TILES + 1 for sx, sy in starts: for d in range(1, STREET_LOOK_TILES + 1): x, y = sx + dx * d, sy + dy * d if not (0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H): break if d <= SHORE_LOOK_TILES and water[y, x]: near_water = min(near_water, d) if paved[y, x]: rank = (int(road_hierarchy[y, x]) if road_hierarchy is not None else 0) score = d - min(5.0, rank * 0.6) if score < best_score: best, best_score = name, score break wet[name] = near_water if best is not None: return best # Nothing paved within reach. If the building stands over or beside # water - a boathouse, a hut on a pier - the way in is whichever side # is not water; without this every door on a pier faced the lake, # because a building with no street found gets its door on the south # wall by default. if min(wet.values()) <= SHORE_LOOK_TILES: away = {"N": "S", "S": "N", "W": "E", "E": "W"}[ min(wet, key=lambda name: (wet[name], name))] return max(wet, key=lambda name: (wet[name], name == away, name)) return None return side

nodes.name: side
nodes.signature: def side(x0: int, y0: int, w: int, h: int) -> str | None
nodes.body_text: def side(x0: int, y0: int, w: int, h: int) -> str | None: best, best_score = None, STREET_LOOK_TILES + 1 wet = {} for name, (dx, dy) in (("N", (0, -1)), ("S", (0, 1)), ("W", (-1, 0)), ("E", (1, 0))): if dx == 0: starts = [(x0 + w * f // 4, y0 if dy < 0 else y0 + h - 1) for f in (1, 2, 3)] else: starts = [(x0 if dx < 0 else x0 + w - 1, y0 + h * f // 4) for f in (1, 2, 3)] near_water = SHORE_LOOK_TILES + 1 for sx, sy in starts: for d in range(1, STREET_LOOK_TILES + 1): x, y = sx + dx * d, sy + dy * d if not (0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H): break if d <= SHORE_LOOK_TILES and water[y, x]: near_water = min(near_water, d) if paved[y, x]: rank = (int(road_hierarchy[y, x]) if road_hierarchy is not None else 0) score = d - min(5.0, rank * 0.6) if score < best_score: best, best_score = name, score break wet[name] = near_water if best is not None: return best # Nothing paved within reach. If the building stands over or beside # water - a boathouse, a hut on a pier - the way in is whichever side # is not water; without this every door on a pier faced the lake, # because a building with no street found gets its door on the south # wall by default. if min(wet.values()) <= SHORE_LOOK_TILES: away = {"N": "S", "S": "N", "W": "E", "E": "W"}[ min(wet, key=lambda name: (wet[name], name))] return max(wet, key=lambda name: (wet[name], name == away, name)) return None

nodes.name: _load_road_hierarchy
nodes.signature: def _load_road_hierarchy(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj) -> np.ndarray | None
nodes.body_text: def _load_road_hierarchy(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj) -> np.ndarray | None: from PIL import Image path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_road_hierarchy.bmp") if not os.path.exists(path): return None return read_gray(path, crop=(proj.height, proj.width))

nodes.name: _road_weight
nodes.signature: def _road_weight(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None, areas=None) -> np.ndarray | None
nodes.body_text: def _road_weight(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None, areas=None) -> np.ndarray | None: """2 on carriageway, 1 on pavement, 0 elsewhere, from the ground as the renderer drew it. The ground alone cannot always tell a road from a yard: an industrial estate is painted in the same beige gravel as a track bed, so every footprint inside one was refused as standing on the road and the estate came out as empty gravel in the exact shape of its polygon. Where the land is what made the ground look like that, and no real road runs over it, it is ground a building may stand on. """ from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_ground_base.bmp") if not os.path.exists(path): path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.bmp") if not os.path.exists(path): return None ground = read_rgb(path, crop=(proj.height, proj.width)) weight = np.zeros(ground.shape[:2], dtype=np.int8) for colour in (C.PALE_CONCRETE,): weight[same_colour(ground, colour)] = 1 for colour in (C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.LIGHT_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE): weight[same_colour(ground, colour)] = 2 classified = None if road_hierarchy is not None: # The mask includes each road's sidewalk width. Larger road classes # carry a stronger cost so footprints settle behind local streets. classified = road_hierarchy[:proj.height, :proj.width] weight[classified > 0] = classified[classified > 0] if areas is not None: yards = areas.mask(YARD_AREAS, weight.shape[1], weight.shape[0]) if classified is not None: yards = yards & (classified == 0) weight[yards] = 0 # Rail beds are transport corridors too; rooms must not erase their track tiles. from generator.rail_tiles import RAIL_RULES rail = (ground[:, :, 0] == 206) & np.isin(ground[:, :, 1], (1, 2)) for colour in {colour for label, colour, tile in RAIL_RULES if colour[0] != 206}: rail |= same_colour(ground, colour) # An exterior wall can stand one square outside its room footprint. padded = np.pad(rail, 1) rail_clear = rail.copy() for dy in range(3): for dx in range(3): rail_clear |= padded[dy:dy + rail.shape[0], dx:dx + rail.shape[1]] weight[rail_clear] = 8 return weight

nodes.name: _drawn_features
nodes.body_text: def _drawn_features(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> list: """What was drawn by hand for this map, as OSM features. The sheet from the drawing board, if there is one, and whatever was drawn over the world map. Both are stored as drawn so they can be drawn on again, and converted here the same way the generator converts them. """ from generator import sketch # The sheet first, and only the sheet where there is one: building from a # sheet writes the drawing it becomes out as well, so reading both counted # every drawn thing twice - one petrol station came out as two. # A half-written one of these is said out loud rather than skipped: the # drawing is the whole map on a hand-drawn one, and a build that quietly # left it out handed back empty ground with no word of why. for name, convert, what in ( (f"{map_name}_design.json", sketch.design_to_drawn, "the map you drew"), (f"{map_name}_sketch.geojson", lambda d: d, "what you added to the area")): drawn = knoxfiles.read(os.path.join(out_dir, name), what) if drawn is None: continue return sketch.features(convert(drawn)) return []

nodes.name: _points_of_use
nodes.signature: def _points_of_use(out_dir: str, info: dict, map_name: str, proj) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def _points_of_use(out_dir: str, info: dict, map_name: str, proj) -> dict: """Point features from OSM, bucketed by tile for nearby-footprint lookup.""" from generator import osm bbox = info.get("bbox") or {} cache = os.path.join(out_dir, info["osm_cache"]) if info.get("osm_cache") else osm.cache_path(out_dir, map_name) wanted = tuple(info["osm_bbox"]) if info.get("osm_bbox") else (bbox.get("south"), bbox.get("west"), bbox.get("north"), bbox.get("east")) grid: dict = {} # As the paper map does: this reads the download, it never fetches one. feats = osm.load_cache(cache, wanted, filters=None) or [] feats = osm.proposed_roads(feats, info.get("include_proposed_roads", 0)) # Points drawn by hand count too. They are kept beside the map rather than # in the download (web/mapfiles.py, _save_sketch), so reading only the cache left a # petrol station somebody placed themselves with no forecourt and no # pumps: "0 pumps at 0 stations, 0 canopies and 0 points". feats = feats + _drawn_features(out_dir, map_name) if info.get("straight_roads") and feats: # Where the renderer moved them to, with the roads straightened or routed. from generator.octilinear import replay from generator.renderer import _is_polygon, classify replay(feats, proj, classify, _is_polygon, info, out_dir, map_name) for feat in feats: if feat.kind != "node" or not ( any(k in feat.tags for k in USE_KEYS) or "entrance" in feat.tags): continue lat, lon = feat.geometry[0] x, y = proj.to_px(lat, lon) grid.setdefault((int(x) // 16, int(y) // 16), []).append((x, y, feat.tags)) return grid

nodes.name: _points_inside
nodes.signature: def _points_inside(grid: dict, px: list, taken: set) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def _points_inside(grid: dict, px: list, taken: set) -> list[dict]: """The tags of the points inside a footprint (or just outside its wall, where a mapper put the shop's entrance), each point used once.""" if not grid: return [] from shapely.geometry import Point poly = Polygon(px) if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) zone = poly.buffer(1.0) minx, miny, maxx, maxy = zone.bounds out = [] for gx in range(int(minx) // 16, int(maxx) // 16 + 1): for gy in range(int(miny) // 16, int(maxy) // 16 + 1): for x, y, tags in grid.get((gx, gy), ()): key = (x, y) if (any(k in tags for k in USE_KEYS) and key not in taken and zone.contains(Point(x, y))): taken.add(key) out.append((x, y, tags)) return [tags for _x, _y, tags in out]

nodes.name: _entrances_inside
nodes.signature: def _entrances_inside(grid: dict, px: list) -> list[tuple[float, float, dict]]
nodes.body_text: def _entrances_inside(grid: dict, px: list) -> list[tuple[float, float, dict]]: """Entrance nodes on or just outside a building outline, in map tiles.""" if not grid: return [] from shapely.geometry import Point poly = Polygon(px) if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) zone = poly.buffer(1.5) minx, miny, maxx, maxy = zone.bounds out = [] for gx in range(int(minx) // 16, int(maxx) // 16 + 1): for gy in range(int(miny) // 16, int(maxy) // 16 + 1): for x, y, tags in grid.get((gx, gy), ()): if "entrance" in tags and zone.contains(Point(x, y)): out.append((x, y, tags)) return out

nodes.name: _entrances_by_unit
nodes.signature: def _entrances_by_unit(entrances: list[tuple[float, float, dict]], units ) -> list[list[tuple[float, float, dict]]]
nodes.body_text: def _entrances_by_unit(entrances: list[tuple[float, float, dict]], units ) -> list[list[tuple[float, float, dict]]]: """Assign each mapped entrance to its closest unit and make it local.""" assigned = [[] for _ in units] for x, y, tags in entrances: closest = None for i, unit in enumerate(units): lx, ly = x - unit.x0, y - unit.y0 ix0, iy0 = math.floor(lx), math.floor(ly) distance = float("inf") for iy in range(max(0, iy0 - 1), min(unit.height, iy0 + 2)): for ix in range(max(0, ix0 - 1), min(unit.width, ix0 + 2)): if not unit.mask[iy, ix]: continue dx = max(ix - lx, 0.0, lx - ix - 1) dy = max(iy - ly, 0.0, ly - iy - 1) distance = min(distance, dx * dx + dy * dy) if closest is None or distance < closest[0]: closest = (distance, i, lx, ly) if closest is not None and closest[0] <= 2.25: _distance, i, lx, ly = closest assigned[i].append((lx, ly, tags)) return assigned

nodes.name: _rooms_by_unit
nodes.body_text: def _rooms_by_unit(entries, fp, units, proj) -> list: """The building's mapped rooms (renderer._buildings_geojson), moved with the placed footprint and shared out between the units it was cut into. Returns one list per unit of (ring, kind): the ring in that unit's own tiles, kind from the OSM room tag where the game knows it (None = cut as drawn but furnished by the usual rules). A room whose centre falls in no unit - outside the footprint after squaring up - is left out. """ out: list = [[] for _ in units] if not entries: return out turned = fp.point_rotation or fp.point_offset != (0.0, 0.0) for entry in entries: ring = entry.get("ring") or [] if len(ring) < 3: continue pts = [proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lon, lat in ring] if turned: pts = [fp.transform_point(x, y) for x, y in pts] room = str(entry.get("room") or "").strip().lower() amenity = str(entry.get("amenity") or "").strip().lower() kind = MAPPED_ROOM_KINDS.get(room) or MAPPED_ROOM_KINDS.get(amenity) cx = sum(p[0] for p in pts) / len(pts) cy = sum(p[1] for p in pts) / len(pts) for n, unit in enumerate(units): if unit.x0 <= cx < unit.x0 + unit.width \ and unit.y0 <= cy < unit.y0 + unit.height: local = [(int(round(x - unit.x0)), int(round(y - unit.y0))) for x, y in pts] out[n].append((local, kind)) break return out

nodes.name: _party_walls
nodes.signature: def _party_walls(owner: np.ndarray, me: int, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, levels: list[int]) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def _party_walls(owner: np.ndarray, me: int, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, levels: list[int]) -> dict: """{(x, y, "N" or "W"): storeys of the neighbour} for each outside wall of building `me` with another building's tile beyond it, in the building's own coordinates, as doors and windows name wall edges.""" out: dict = {} h, w = mask.shape mh, mw = owner.shape sub = owner[max(0, y0 - 1):min(mh, y0 + h + 1), max(0, x0 - 1):min(mw, x0 + w + 1)] if not ((sub >= 0) & (sub != me)).any(): return out for ly in range(h): for lx in range(w): if not mask[ly, lx]: continue for dx, dy, edge in ((0, -1, (lx, ly, "N")), (0, 1, (lx, ly + 1, "N")), (-1, 0, (lx, ly, "W")), (1, 0, (lx + 1, ly, "W"))): nx, ny = lx + dx, ly + dy if 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and mask[ny, nx]: continue wx, wy = x0 + nx, y0 + ny if 0 <= wx < mw and 0 <= wy < mh: other = owner[wy, wx] if other >= 0 and other != me: out[edge] = max(out.get(edge, 0), levels[other]) return out

nodes.name: _make_one
nodes.signature: def _make_one(job: tuple, room_limit: int | None = None) -> tuple
nodes.body_text: def _make_one(job: tuple, room_limit: int | None = None) -> tuple: """Lay out one building and write its .tbx. Returns (storeys, rooms, furniture, error, escalators, basement): a building that cannot be laid out is left out with the reason, instead of stopping the other two thousand. `basement` is what basements.plan_basement made of the job's last element (a BasementSpec), written beside the building as <name>_bsmt.tbx, or None. `room_limit`, when given, is how many rooms this building may have: the map needed thinning to fit the game's save buffer (layout.thin_building).""" (w, h, levels, commercial, seed, kind, mask, settings, style, label, path, street, retail, uses, hotel, entrances, profile, mapped, garage_door, preset_file, party, *rest) = job basement = rest[0] if rest else None job = job[:JOB_FIELDS] # what the room solver reads, without the basement if preset_file: # A building somebody built by hand, used as it was built. Nothing is # re-rendered and nothing is stretched: the file that was saved is the # file that is written, which is the whole point of hand-building one. try: with open(preset_file, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: text = f.read() with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(text) except OSError as exc: return (0, 0, 0, f"{os.path.basename(path)}: the preset " f"{os.path.basename(preset_file)} could not be " f"read ({exc})", [], None) from . import presets as P about = P.measure(text) or {"storeys": 1, "rooms": 0} return (about["storeys"], about["rooms"], 0, None, [], None) try: # a house planned whole by the room solver (Settings.room_solver), when # it is on and the house fits; anything else is laid out as always from . import room_solver plan = None if room_solver.wanted(settings): try: plan = room_solver.plan_for_job(job) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - that house keeps Build's own layout plan = None if plan is None: plan = build_building(w, h, levels=levels, commercial=commercial, seed=seed, kind=kind, mask=mask, settings=settings, street=street, retail=retail, uses=uses, hotel=hotel, party=party, entrances=entrances, profile=profile, mapped=mapped, garage_door=garage_door) if room_limit: # Fewer, larger rooms: the map would otherwise be past the buffer # the game saves room state through, and none of it would be kept. # Before the basement is planned, so its stair opens into a room # that is still there. thin_building(plan, room_limit) below = None if basement is not None: from . import basements # Before the house is written: the stairs down open its ground floor. below = basements.plan_basement(plan, basement, seed, settings) text = render_tbx(plan, label, style) below_text = (basements.render_basement(below, f"{label} basement", style) if below is not None else None) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 import traceback return (0, 0, 0, f"{os.path.basename(path)} ({kind or 'house'}, {w}x{h}, " f"{levels} storeys): {traceback.format_exc()}", [], None) with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(text) info = None if below is not None: below_path = path[:-len(".tbx")] + "_bsmt.tbx" with open(below_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(below_text) info = {"file": os.path.basename(below_path), "tier": basement.tier, "dx": below.dx, "dy": below.dy, "w": below.building.width, "h": below.building.height, "levels": below.levels, "rooms": len(below.building.rooms)} return (len(plan.storeys), len(plan.rooms), sum(len(s.furniture) for s in plan.storeys), None, list(plan.escalators), info)

nodes.name: _code_fingerprint
nodes.body_text: def _code_fingerprint() -> str: """Changes whenever the code that lays a building out does, or the tiles it may use. A cache from other code is not trusted: the same job would come out differently.""" import hashlib from .layout import _erika_ready h = hashlib.sha1() here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) for name in sorted(os.listdir(here)): # room_solver.json: the room solver's programmes lay houses out too if name.endswith(".py") or name == "room_solver.json": h.update(name.encode()) with open(os.path.join(here, name), "rb") as f: h.update(f.read()) layout_dir = os.path.join(here, "layout") for name in sorted(os.listdir(layout_dir)): if name.endswith(".py"): h.update(("layout/" + name).encode()) with open(os.path.join(layout_dir, name), "rb") as f: h.update(f.read()) h.update(b"erika" if _erika_ready() else b"vanilla") from . import room_solver h.update(os.environ.get(room_solver.ENV, "").encode()) # it overrides the setting return h.hexdigest()

nodes.name: _job_key
nodes.body_text: def _job_key(job: tuple) -> str: """A building's inputs as one string. The file name (index 10) is left out: numbers shift when a footprint is added, and the building does not change.""" import hashlib import pickle return hashlib.sha1(pickle.dumps(job[:10] + job[11:], protocol=4)).hexdigest()

nodes.name: _rooms_that_fit
nodes.signature: def _rooms_that_fit(buildings: int, info: dict, out_dir: str) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _rooms_that_fit(buildings: int, info: dict, out_dir: str) -> int: """How many rooms this map may have and still be saved by the game. map_meta.bin is written through one 10 MB buffer and holds the whole world: this map's cells, every room and every building in it - Knox County's own rooms as well, unless this map stands alone (tools/make_map_mod.py). What is left of the buffer is what this map's rooms may take, in the 10 bytes a room costs. """ from tools.make_map_mod import (KNOX_COUNTY_META, META_BUDGET, META_BUILDING, META_CELL, META_ROOM) from . import placement left = META_BUDGET - META_BUILDING * buildings left -= META_CELL * int(info["cells_x"]) * int(info["cells_y"]) if not placement.standalone(out_dir): left -= KNOX_COUNTY_META return max(0, left // META_ROOM)

nodes.name: _read_cache
nodes.body_text: def _read_cache(out_dir: str, code: str) -> dict: try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, CACHE_FILE), encoding="utf-8") as f: data = json.load(f) except (OSError, ValueError): return {} if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("code") != code: return {} return data.get("buildings") or {}

nodes.name: _write_cache
nodes.signature: def _write_cache(out_dir: str, code: str, entries: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _write_cache(out_dir: str, code: str, entries: dict) -> None: try: tmp = os.path.join(out_dir, CACHE_FILE + ".tmp") with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"code": code, "buildings": entries}, f) os.replace(tmp, os.path.join(out_dir, CACHE_FILE)) except OSError: pass # no cache means the next build lays everything out again

nodes.name: _make_batch
nodes.body_text: def _make_batch(jobs: list[tuple]) -> list[tuple]: return [_make_one(job) for job in jobs]

nodes.name: _make_thin_batch
nodes.body_text: def _make_thin_batch(pairs: list[tuple]) -> list[tuple]: """Buildings that have to lose rooms to fit the game's save buffer: each is (job, how many rooms it may have).""" return [_make_one(job, limit) for job, limit in pairs]

nodes.name: _make_all
nodes.signature: def _make_all(jobs: list[tuple], tick=None, should_stop=None, on_result=None, make_batch=_make_batch, prepare_solver: bool = True) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _make_all(jobs: list[tuple], tick=None, should_stop=None, on_result=None, make_batch=_make_batch, prepare_solver: bool = True) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]: """Every building, in order, across processes when there are enough. KNOXBUILD_WORKERS=1 forces one process. If worker processes cannot start at all - some locked-down PCs refuse them - the work simply runs here. `tick(done, total)` is called as results come in, for a progress readout; `on_result(i, result)` with each building's result as soon as it is made. A stop asked for while it runs (`should_stop`) drops the work not yet started and raises knoxstop.Stopped. `make_batch` makes a list of jobs; the tests hand it something quicker than laying out buildings, and a second run over buildings that must lose rooms hands `_make_thin_batch` (`prepare_solver` is off then: they were solved on the first run). """ out: list = [None] * len(jobs) done = 0 def keep(i: int, result) -> None: nonlocal done out[i] = result done += 1 if on_result: on_result(i, result) def run_here() -> list: for i, job in enumerate(jobs): if out[i] is not None: continue # made before the pool gave out knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the buildings") keep(i, make_batch([job])[0]) if tick and done % 25 == 0: tick(done, len(jobs)) return out # the room solver's houses solved before the pool starts, so each worker # only reads its cache (nothing when the room_solver setting is off) if prepare_solver: from . import room_solver room_solver.prepare([job[:JOB_FIELDS] for job in jobs]) workers = int(os.environ.get("KNOXBUILD_WORKERS") or max(1, min(12, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 2))) if workers <= 1 or len(jobs) < PARALLEL_FROM: return run_here() from concurrent.futures import FIRST_COMPLETED, ProcessPoolExecutor, wait from concurrent.futures.process import BrokenProcessPool pool = None try: pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) pending = {pool.submit(make_batch, jobs[s:s + MAKE_BATCH]): s for s in range(0, len(jobs), MAKE_BATCH)} last_tick = 0 while pending: # Woken at least every second, so a stop is seen while the big # buildings are still being made. finished, _ = wait(pending, timeout=1.0, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED) for fut in finished: start = pending.pop(fut) for k, result in enumerate(fut.result()): keep(start + k, result) if tick and done - last_tick >= 25: last_tick = done tick(done, len(jobs)) knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the buildings") pool.shutdown() return out except (BrokenProcessPool, OSError) as exc: if pool is not None: pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) print(f" (worker processes unavailable: {exc}; building in one process)") return run_here() except BaseException: # Stopped, or the window closed: the work not started is dropped # rather than finished first, which on a city was hours. if pool is not None: pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) raise

nodes.name: keep
nodes.body_text: def keep(i: int, result) -> None: nonlocal done out[i] = result done += 1 if on_result: on_result(i, result)

nodes.name: run_here
nodes.body_text: def run_here() -> list: for i, job in enumerate(jobs): if out[i] is not None: continue # made before the pool gave out knoxstop.check(should_stop, "the buildings") keep(i, make_batch([job])[0]) if tick and done % 25 == 0: tick(done, len(jobs)) return out

nodes.name: build
nodes.signature: def build(out_dir: str, seed: int | None = None, min_size: int | None = None, max_size: int | None = None, settings: Settings | None = None, should_stop=None, progress=None) -> int
nodes.body_text: def build(out_dir: str, seed: int | None = None, min_size: int | None = None, max_size: int | None = None, settings: Settings | None = None, should_stop=None, progress=None) -> int: """Generate every building for a rendered map. The explicit seed/min_size/max_size arguments are kept so the command line can override one value without composing a whole Settings. `progress(text, fraction)`, when given, is called as the work moves on: a short account of the stage, and how far through the whole run it is (0 to 1, or None when that is not known). The fractions are rough: where each stage starts, not a measured share of the time. """ def say(text: str, fraction: float | None = None) -> None: if progress: progress(text, fraction) say("Reading the map", 0.0) settings = settings or Settings() overrides = {k: v for k, v in (("seed", seed), ("min_size", min_size), ("max_size", max_size)) if v is not None} if overrides: settings = Settings.from_dict({**settings.to_dict(), **overrides}) # Before any building is laid out: the mod-tile check is asked once and # remembered, so saying this afterwards would be too late for the first. from .layout import use_mod_tiles use_mod_tiles(not settings.vanilla_tiles) seed = settings.seed min_size = settings.min_size max_size = settings.max_size names = [f for f in os.listdir(out_dir) if f.endswith("_info.json")] if not names: print(f"no <name>_info.json in {out_dir}", file=sys.stderr) return 2 map_name = names[0][: -len("_info.json")] info = knoxfiles.read(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_info.json"), "what the map is", default={}) geo = knoxfiles.read(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_buildings.geojson"), "the buildings") if not info or geo is None: print(f"{out_dir} is missing what the map is or its buildings - " f"generate the map again", file=sys.stderr) return 2 bbox = info["bbox"] proj = Projector.build(bbox["south"], bbox["west"], bbox["north"], bbox["east"], info["meters_per_tile"], info.get("rotation") or 0.0) if (proj.width, proj.height) != (info["width_tiles"], info["height_tiles"]): print("projection does not match the rendered BMP - is this folder " "from a different Knoxify version?", file=sys.stderr) return 2 road_hierarchy = _load_road_hierarchy(out_dir, map_name, proj) # What part of the world the survey is of, read from the names on its own # buildings (knoxbuild/regional.py). Only Chinese housing is built its own # way for now; anywhere else keeps the game's shapes, and `arch_style` # forces the question either way. from . import regional region = None if settings.arch_style == "cn": region = "cn" elif settings.arch_style != "off": region = regional.detect_region(geo, bbox) # Where this map stands in the world, beside any other KnoxMap map on # this PC rather than on top of it (knoxbuild/world.py). Everything # below - the paper map, the zones, the compiled cells - is written from # here on, so it is settled first. from .world import origin, set_origin from . import placement as _placement set_origin(_placement.settled_origin( out_dir, info.get("map_name") or os.path.basename(out_dir.rstrip("\\/")), info["cells_x"], info["cells_y"])) # Keep the saved choice in step with the project, so the window and the # compiled cells never disagree about where the map is. _placement.save(out_dir, origin()) # Record what this build actually used, whoever started it. Without this # a map generated from the command line cannot be reproduced, and the app # and the CLI disagree about what a folder was built with. try: knoxfiles.write(os.path.join(out_dir, "settings.json"), settings.to_dict(), indent=2) except OSError: pass bdir = os.path.join(out_dir, "buildings") os.makedirs(bdir, exist_ok=True) # What the last build left. Building numbers follow the footprints, so a # rebuild does not overwrite the same set of files, and leftovers from an # earlier run would sit in the folder looking like part of the map: the # ones this build does not write are removed once it has finished (below), # and the ones it can reuse are left alone until then. earlier_files = {f for f in os.listdir(bdir) if f.endswith(".tbx")} code = _code_fingerprint() earlier = _read_cache(out_dir, code) # The cache stays as it is until the buildings start being written: nothing # before that touches their files. Then it is cut down to what this build # reuses and grows as each building is made (below), so a build that stops # or crashes half way picks up where it was. Deleting it here instead - a # half-written set of files must not be vouched for by the old record - # cost a 232,000-building map its whole two and a half hours to a crash. # WorldEd writes into these but will not create them: BMP to TMX fails with # "Could not open file for writing" if the export directory is absent. os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "tmx"), exist_ok=True) os.makedirs(os.path.join(out_dir, "lots"), exist_ok=True) import random as _random style_rng = _random.Random(seed ^ 0x5EED) placements: list[Placement] = [] rows = [] skipped = {"
