nodes.name: overlay_tile
nodes.signature: def overlay_tile(entry: dict, dname: str, variant: str) -> str
nodes.body_text: def overlay_tile(entry: dict, dname: str, variant: str) -> str: """An overlay's (trim, grime) tile for a wall with a window. The trim and grime tables name one window tile - WestWindow, NorthWindow - however many cut-out walls a style carries, so a numbered wall variant (NorthWindow12) is not a key there. Asking only for the variant dropped the trim band and the grime from every window square, which left a clean, bare patch under the windows of a weathered wall. """ return entry.get(variant) or entry.get(dname + "Window") or entry.get(dname, "")

nodes.name: opening_wall
nodes.body_text: def opening_wall(x, y, dname): """The wall tiles of edge dname of square (x, y), with its door or window variant.""" o = opening_dir.get((x, y, dname)) if o is None: return wall_tiles(x, y, dname) if o["type"] == "door": return wall_tiles(x, y, dname + "Door") v = _window_variant(_entry(b, o.get("Tile", b.attrs.get("Window", 0))).get(dname, "")) variant = f"{dname}Window{v}" if v else dname + "Window" if room(x, y) > 0: return wall_tiles(x, y, variant, fallback=dname + "Window") k = variant if ext.get(variant) else dname + "Window" return outside_tiles(ext.get(k, ""), overlay_tile(trim, dname, variant), overlay_tile(grime, dname, variant))

nodes.name: preserve_corner
nodes.body_text: def preserve_corner(tiles): if kind_at[(x, y)] != "NorthWest": return tiles # The square's other wall keeps its own opening (a door on the west edge and a # window on the north edge of one corner square): its Door/Window variant, not # the solid wall, or the second opening would wall the first one up. other = opening_wall(x, y, "West" if d == "N" else "North") if r == 0 and len(tiles) == 3 and len(other) == 3: return other[:2] + tiles + other[2:] return other + tiles

nodes.name: level_tiles
nodes.signature: def level_tiles(b: Building, z: int) -> dict[tuple[int, int], list[str]]
nodes.body_text: def level_tiles(b: Building, z: int) -> dict[tuple[int, int], list[str]]: """Building tiles in drawing order; retains the original flat-stack interface.""" return {pos: [tile for _, tile in items] for pos, items in level_layers(b, z).items()}

nodes.name: _structure
nodes.body_text: def _structure(tile: str) -> bool: return tile.startswith(STRUCTURE_PREFIXES) or tile in HEDGE_TILES

nodes.name: _yields
nodes.body_text: def _yields(tile: str) -> bool: return tile.startswith(YIELDING_PREFIXES) and not _structure(tile)

nodes.name: compose_lots
nodes.signature: def compose_lots(lots) -> dict[tuple[int, int, int], list[str]]
nodes.body_text: def compose_lots(lots) -> dict[tuple[int, int, int], list[str]]: """Compose (building, x, y, base level) placements in project order. Rooms replace earlier lot squares. Outside rooms, only populated layers replace matching earlier layers; empty squares preserve the underlying lot - except that an earlier wall, fence, gate, railing or hedge is not replaced by a later lot's prop, and a square holding one drops the lamps, trees, bushes and flowers on it. """ world = {} for b, tx, ty, base in lots: for z, floor in enumerate(b.floors): layers = level_layers(b, z) rooms = {(x, y) for y, row in enumerate(floor.rooms) for x, r in enumerate(row) if r > 0} for x, y in rooms | layers.keys(): pos = (tx + x, ty + y, base + z) new = layers.get((x, y), []) if (x, y) in rooms: world[pos] = new else: channels = {layer for layer, _ in new} old = world.get(pos, []) if "floor" in channels: # a floor tile (a flat roof is one) takes the square old = [] replaced = set().union(*(WALL_REPLACES.get(c, {c}) for c in channels)) if channels else set() # An earlier wall survives a later lot's prop on its square, but a later # lot's own wall replaces it, as WorldEd does where two buildings overlap. walled = any(_structure(tile) for _, tile in new) keep = [(layer, tile) for layer, tile in old if layer not in replaced or (_structure(tile) and not walled)] world[pos] = keep + [item for item in new if item not in keep] out = {} for pos, items in world.items(): tiles = [tile for _, tile in items] if any(_structure(t) for t in tiles): tiles = [t for t in tiles if not _yields(t)] if tiles: out[pos] = tiles return out

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.body_text: """What a building's surroundings say about it. OSM describes a few buildings well and the rest barely at all. The ones it does describe say a lot about their neighbours: a street where every mapped block is six storeys tall is not lined with bungalows in between, and a quarter packed wall to wall with buildings is not the place for a log cabin. This looks at all the footprints at once, before any building is placed, so each untagged one can borrow what its neighbours make plain. The road hierarchy adds a smaller signal: a connected street grid is urban even before buildings fill the block. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import numpy as np # Coverage is measured on a coarse grid and averaged over a 3x3 window of it, # so a building sees roughly the 120 m around it - a block or two. Distances # here are real metres, whatever the map's scale: the question is what the # street is like, not how many tiles it became. DENSITY_CELL_M = 40 # Share of the ground under buildings. Measured on real places: central # Paris, Kadikoy and a Tokyo neighbourhood put most buildings at 0.4-0.5; # Levittown and a French village both sit around 0.16, so density cannot tell # a suburb from a village - but it does pick out the farmstead or the house at # the end of the lane, below SPARSE, which is where a log cabin belongs. DENSE = 0.28 SPARSE = 0.06 # Wall styles that belong only in some places. A log cabin or a trailer in the # middle of a city reads as a mistake at first glance, and clapboard or timber # framing looks lost among blocks of flats. RURAL_ONLY = {"logs", "trailer"} NOT_DENSE = {"clapboard", "timber", "siding_blue", "siding_yellow", "siding_green", "siding_pink", "siding_grey"} # Tagged heights count within this distance of a building, and only when # enough of them agree to be a pattern rather than one tower. NEIGHBOUR_RADIUS_M = 120 NEIGHBOUR_SAMPLES = 4

nodes.name: Context
nodes.body_text: class Context: def __init__(self, width: int, height: int, buildings: list[tuple[float, float, float, int | None]], metres_per_tile: float = 1.0, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None): """`buildings` holds (centre x, centre y, area in tiles, storeys or None).""" self.cell = max(1.0, DENSITY_CELL_M / metres_per_tile) self.radius = NEIGHBOUR_RADIUS_M / metres_per_tile gw = max(1, math.ceil(width / self.cell)) gh = max(1, math.ceil(height / self.cell)) covered = np.zeros((gh, gw), dtype=float) for x, y, area, _levels in buildings: gx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // self.cell))) gy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // self.cell))) covered[gy, gx] += area # 3x3 window sums, divided by the ground each window really spans so # the map's edges are not read as empty countryside. padded = np.pad(covered, 1) ground = np.pad(np.ones_like(covered), 1) sums = sum(padded[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) spans = sum(ground[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) self.coverage = np.clip(sums / (spans * self.cell * self.cell), 0, 1) if road_hierarchy is not None: road_urbanity = np.zeros(9, dtype=float) road_urbanity[1:] = (0.08, 0.18, 0.58, 0.76, 0.86, 0.90, 0.72, 0.48) road = np.asarray(road_hierarchy[:height, :width], dtype=np.uint8) road = np.minimum(road, len(road_urbanity) - 1) road_cells = np.zeros_like(covered) for gy in range(gh): y0, y1 = int(gy * self.cell), min(height, int((gy + 1) * self.cell)) for gx in range(gw): x0, x1 = int(gx * self.cell), min(width, int((gx + 1) * self.cell)) if x1 > x0 and y1 > y0: road_cells[gy, gx] = road_urbanity[road[y0:y1, x0:x1]].mean() road_padded = np.pad(road_cells, 1) road_sums = sum(road_padded[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) self.coverage = np.clip(self.coverage + 0.45 * road_sums / spans, 0, 1) tagged = [(x, y, lv) for x, y, _a, lv in buildings if lv is not None] self._tagged = np.array(tagged, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3) def density(self, x: float, y: float) -> float: gh, gw = self.coverage.shape gx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // self.cell))) gy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // self.cell))) return float(self.coverage[gy, gx]) def neighbour_levels(self, x: float, y: float) -> float | None: """Median tagged storey count nearby, or None when too few say.""" if len(self._tagged) < NEIGHBOUR_SAMPLES: return None d2 = (self._tagged[:, 0] - x) ** 2 + (self._tagged[:, 1] - y) ** 2 near = self._tagged[d2 <= self.radius ** 2, 2] if len(near) < NEIGHBOUR_SAMPLES: return None return float(np.median(near))

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.signature: def __init__(self, width: int, height: int, buildings: list[tuple[float, float, float, int | None]], metres_per_tile: float = 1.0, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def __init__(self, width: int, height: int, buildings: list[tuple[float, float, float, int | None]], metres_per_tile: float = 1.0, road_hierarchy: np.ndarray | None = None): """`buildings` holds (centre x, centre y, area in tiles, storeys or None).""" self.cell = max(1.0, DENSITY_CELL_M / metres_per_tile) self.radius = NEIGHBOUR_RADIUS_M / metres_per_tile gw = max(1, math.ceil(width / self.cell)) gh = max(1, math.ceil(height / self.cell)) covered = np.zeros((gh, gw), dtype=float) for x, y, area, _levels in buildings: gx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // self.cell))) gy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // self.cell))) covered[gy, gx] += area # 3x3 window sums, divided by the ground each window really spans so # the map's edges are not read as empty countryside. padded = np.pad(covered, 1) ground = np.pad(np.ones_like(covered), 1) sums = sum(padded[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) spans = sum(ground[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) self.coverage = np.clip(sums / (spans * self.cell * self.cell), 0, 1) if road_hierarchy is not None: road_urbanity = np.zeros(9, dtype=float) road_urbanity[1:] = (0.08, 0.18, 0.58, 0.76, 0.86, 0.90, 0.72, 0.48) road = np.asarray(road_hierarchy[:height, :width], dtype=np.uint8) road = np.minimum(road, len(road_urbanity) - 1) road_cells = np.zeros_like(covered) for gy in range(gh): y0, y1 = int(gy * self.cell), min(height, int((gy + 1) * self.cell)) for gx in range(gw): x0, x1 = int(gx * self.cell), min(width, int((gx + 1) * self.cell)) if x1 > x0 and y1 > y0: road_cells[gy, gx] = road_urbanity[road[y0:y1, x0:x1]].mean() road_padded = np.pad(road_cells, 1) road_sums = sum(road_padded[dy:dy + gh, dx:dx + gw] for dy in range(3) for dx in range(3)) self.coverage = np.clip(self.coverage + 0.45 * road_sums / spans, 0, 1) tagged = [(x, y, lv) for x, y, _a, lv in buildings if lv is not None] self._tagged = np.array(tagged, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3)

nodes.name: density
nodes.signature: def density(self, x: float, y: float) -> float
nodes.body_text: def density(self, x: float, y: float) -> float: gh, gw = self.coverage.shape gx = min(gw - 1, max(0, int(x // self.cell))) gy = min(gh - 1, max(0, int(y // self.cell))) return float(self.coverage[gy, gx])

nodes.name: neighbour_levels
nodes.signature: def neighbour_levels(self, x: float, y: float) -> float | None
nodes.body_text: def neighbour_levels(self, x: float, y: float) -> float | None: """Median tagged storey count nearby, or None when too few say.""" if len(self._tagged) < NEIGHBOUR_SAMPLES: return None d2 = (self._tagged[:, 0] - x) ** 2 + (self._tagged[:, 1] - y) ** 2 near = self._tagged[d2 <= self.radius ** 2, 2] if len(near) < NEIGHBOUR_SAMPLES: return None return float(np.median(near))

nodes.name: style_fits
nodes.signature: def style_fits(style_name: str, density: float) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def style_fits(style_name: str, density: float) -> bool: if style_name in RURAL_ONLY: return density < SPARSE if style_name in NOT_DENSE: return density < DENSE return True

nodes.name: render_line
nodes.signature: def render_line(text: str, scale: int = 1) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def render_line(text: str, scale: int = 1) -> np.ndarray: """One line of text as a boolean bitmap, one letter space between letters.""" cols = [] for ch in text.upper(): glyph = _FONT.get(ch) cell = np.zeros((GLYPH_H, GLYPH_W + 1), dtype=bool) if glyph: for y, row in enumerate(glyph): for x, c in enumerate(row): cell[y, x] = c == "#" cols.append(cell) if not cols: return np.zeros((GLYPH_H * scale, 0), dtype=bool) line = np.concatenate(cols, axis=1)[:, :-1] # no space after the last letter return np.kron(line, np.ones((scale, scale), dtype=bool))

nodes.name: render
nodes.body_text: def render(lines=LINES) -> np.ndarray: """All the lines, centred on each other, as one bitmap.""" parts = [render_line(text, scale) for text, scale in lines] width = max(p.shape[1] for p in parts) rows = [] for i, p in enumerate(parts): pad = width - p.shape[1] rows.append(np.pad(p, ((0, 0), (pad // 2, pad - pad // 2)))) if i < len(parts) - 1: rows.append(np.zeros((GAP, width), dtype=bool)) return np.concatenate(rows, axis=0)

nodes.name: find_patch
nodes.signature: def find_patch(free: np.ndarray, size: tuple[int, int], near: tuple[int, int], margin: int = MARGIN) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def find_patch(free: np.ndarray, size: tuple[int, int], near: tuple[int, int], margin: int = MARGIN) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """The top-left (x, y) of the free rectangle of `size` (height, width), with `margin` clear tiles round it, nearest `near`; None when there is none.""" h, w = free.shape bh, bw = size[0] + 2 * margin, size[1] + 2 * margin if bh > h or bw > w: return None # A summed-area table: how many free tiles in any rectangle, in one lookup. table = np.zeros((h + 1, w + 1), dtype=np.int32) table[1:, 1:] = free.astype(np.int32).cumsum(axis=0).cumsum(axis=1) count = (table[bh:, bw:] - table[:-bh, bw:] - table[bh:, :-bw] + table[:-bh, :-bw]) ok = count == bh * bw if not ok.any(): return None ys, xs = np.nonzero(ok) cx, cy = xs + bw / 2, ys + bh / 2 d2 = (cx - near[0]) ** 2 + (cy - near[1]) ** 2 best = int(np.argmin(d2)) if d2[best] > MAX_DISTANCE ** 2: return None return int(xs[best]) + margin, int(ys[best]) + margin

nodes.name: spawn_house
nodes.signature: def spawn_house(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def spawn_house(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """The middle of the home nearest the middle of all the homes: where tools/make_map_mod.py's first spawn point goes.""" homes = [r for r in rows if r.get("kind") in ("house", "apartment")] if not homes: return None centres = np.array([(r["tile_x"] + r["width"] / 2, r["tile_y"] + r["height"] / 2) for r in homes]) mid = centres.mean(axis=0) x, y = centres[int(np.argmin(((centres - mid) ** 2).sum(axis=1)))] return int(x), int(y)

nodes.name: paint
nodes.signature: def paint(ground: np.ndarray, veg, free: np.ndarray, rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def paint(ground: np.ndarray, veg, free: np.ndarray, rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """Spell the credit on a clear patch near the first spawn house; where it went (top-left tile), or None when the map has no room for it.""" near = spawn_house(rows) or (free.shape[1] // 2, free.shape[0] // 2) for layout in LAYOUTS: letters = render(layout) at = find_patch(free, letters.shape, near) if at is not None: break else: return None x0, y0 = at ys, xs = np.nonzero(letters) ground[y0 + ys, x0 + xs] = C.PALE_CONCRETE if veg is not None: veg[y0 + ys, x0 + xs] = C.VEG_NOTHING return at

nodes.name: credits.py
nodes.body_text: """Who made KnoxMap, in one place: the credit every map carries. A map's ATTRIBUTION.txt and its Steam Workshop page (tools/make_map_workshop.py) both read this, so a name added here shows up in both. Names are the authors' own, as they appear on the project's commits. """ from __future__ import annotations KNOXMAP_URL = "https://github.com/spytheeuclidean-a11y/knoxmap" # The person who made KnoxMap. MAKER = "euclid80tr" # Everyone else who has worked on it, in the order they began. CONTRIBUTORS = ["PonSky", "SolarisMare", "yoruvell", "hamurabi11", "spongebobik", "Soner Kochan", "Tom N", "Zombaxx"] # What KnoxMap stands on. BUILT_ON = [ ("Knoxify", "arytek", "https://github.com/arytek/knoxify", "the original OpenStreetMap-to-Project-Zomboid terrain generator KnoxMap is built on"), ("PZ Mapping Tools", "Alree / Unjammer", "https://github.com/Unjammer/PZ_Mapping_Tools", "built on Tim Baker's TileZed and WorldEd"), ]

nodes.name: plain
nodes.body_text: def plain() -> str: """The credit as lines of text, for ATTRIBUTION.txt.""" lines = [f"Made with KnoxMap ({KNOXMAP_URL}) by {MAKER}, with work from " + ", ".join(CONTRIBUTORS) + ".", "KnoxMap is built on:"] lines += [f" - {name} by {who} ({url}): {what}" for name, who, url, what in BUILT_ON] return "\n".join(lines)

nodes.name: dataset_lines
nodes.signature: def dataset_lines(used, retrieved: str | None = None) -> list[str]
nodes.body_text: def dataset_lines(used, retrieved: str | None = None) -> list[str]: """Attribution for the optional data layers a map actually used. Delegates to knoxdata so each layer's own module owns its wording; the lazily imported package keeps a bare knoxbuild import cheap. """ if not used: return [] try: import knoxdata return knoxdata.attribution_lines(used, retrieved=retrieved) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - credit is never fatal return []

nodes.name: bbcode
nodes.body_text: def bbcode() -> str: """The same, for a Steam Workshop page.""" out = [f"[b]Made with [url={KNOXMAP_URL}]KnoxMap[/url][/b] by [b]{MAKER}[/b], with work " "from " + ", ".join(CONTRIBUTORS) + ".", "", "KnoxMap is a free program that turns a real place into a Project Zomboid map. " "It is built on:", "[list]"] out += [f"[*] [url={url}]{name}[/url] by {who}: {what}" for name, who, url, what in BUILT_ON] out.append("[/list]") return "\n".join(out)

nodes.name: designer.py
nodes.body_text: """A building drawn by hand in the window, as a plan and as a .tbx. The generator lays out every building from scratch, and a preset (knoxbuild/presets.py) is the way out of that: a hand-built .tbx stamped onto a plot instead of a generated one. Until now the only way to make one was BuildingEd, which means leaving KnoxMap, learning another editor and knowing which of the game's three thousand tiles a police station is built of. This is the other half: rooms drawn on a sheet in the window, and everything else - walls, doors, windows, the staircase, the roof, the furniture, the tile for each of them - done by the same code that builds the rest of the map. So a hand-drawn police station is a real police station: its lockers, its gun storage and its cells hold what the game puts in those rooms, because they are the same rooms the generator would have made, laid out where the mapper wanted them instead of where the splitter happened to cut. A design is plain data (`clean`), kept beside the preset it was saved as, so a preset can be opened and changed again. What comes out of it is an ordinary .tbx, written by knoxbuild/tbx.py: once saved, nothing can tell it from a building made in BuildingEd. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import math import os import random import zlib from . import layout as L from . import presets as P from .settings import Settings # A building smaller than this has no room in it; bigger than this is not a # building but a district, and the editor draws every tile of it. MIN_SIDE, MAX_SIDE = 4, 150 MAX_STOREYS = 8 # The rooms of a house, which no SPECIAL_MIXES entry covers because a house is # what the generator builds when a building is nothing in particular. HOUSE_ROOMS = ("livingroom", "openplan", "kitchen", "dining", "bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bathroom", "hall", "closet", "laundry", "storage", "garage", "shed") # ---- the design itself ------------------------------------------------------ # ---- from a design to a building -------------------------------------------- # Laying a storey out and furnishing it costs about a second per 20,000 tiles, # which is nothing for a house and seven seconds for 150x150 over eight floors # - too long to wait for after every drag. Past this much, only the storey # being looked at is built for the picture; the whole building is still built # when it is saved. PREVIEW_BUDGET = 40000 # ---- what it is made of ----------------------------------------------------- # ---- a picture of it -------------------------------------------------------- OUTSIDE = (232, 231, 226) WALL = (58, 56, 54) DOOR = (196, 120, 40) WINDOW = (96, 170, 220) PIECE = (74, 70, 66) GRID = (214, 212, 206) # The sheet under the drawing. Asked for in #suggestions: the grid only # appeared under a room once one had been drawn, and a floor you are about to # draw is exactly when it is worth seeing - it is how you judge how big to # make the room. Every fifth line is darker so tiles can be counted without # following one across the whole sheet. EMPTY_GRID = (223, 222, 216) EMPTY_GRID_FIFTH = (209, 207, 200) GRID_EVERY = 5 # ---- keeping one ------------------------------------------------------------

nodes.name: room_label
nodes.body_text: def room_label(kind: str) -> str: style = L.ROOM_STYLE.get(kind) return style[1] if style else kind

nodes.name: _mix_for
nodes.body_text: def _mix_for(kind: str | None) -> list[str]: """The rooms the generator itself would put in this kind of building.""" if not kind or kind in ("house", "shed"): return [name for name in HOUSE_ROOMS if name in L.ROOM_STYLE] mix, fill = L.SPECIAL_MIXES.get(kind, ((), ())) out = [] for name in list(mix) + list(fill): if name not in out and name in L.ROOM_STYLE: out.append(name) return out

nodes.name: room_kinds
nodes.signature: def room_kinds(kind: str | None = None) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def room_kinds(kind: str | None = None) -> list[dict]: """Every room that can be drawn, the ones this building has first. Taken from the room table itself rather than listed here, so a room the game knows and this window does not cannot happen; and ordered by what is being built, because a police station has 113 rooms to choose from and seven of them are the ones it is made of. """ def entry(name: str, group: str) -> dict: # The colour it is drawn in on the plan, so the palette and the # picture agree about which room is which. return {"id": name, "label": room_label(name), "group": group, "colour": "#%02x%02x%02x" % room_colour(name)} first = _mix_for(kind) # With no kind chosen the rooms a house is made of are the ones offered # first, so saying they are "in this kind of building" would be saying # nothing: they are named for what they are. out = [entry(name, "In this kind of building" if kind else "Rooms of a house") for name in first] house = [name for name in HOUSE_ROOMS if name not in first and name in L.ROOM_STYLE] out += [entry(name, "Rooms of a house") for name in house] # A room with nothing to put in it is not a room anybody draws: the lift # shaft is machinery the builder fits where the stairs are, and drawn by # hand it is a sealed box with no way in and no lift in it. rest = sorted((name for name in L.ROOM_STYLE if name not in first and name not in house and L.ROOM_STYLE[name][2]), key=room_label) out += [entry(name, "Every other room") for name in rest] return out

nodes.name: entry
nodes.signature: def entry(name: str, group: str) -> dict: # The colour it is drawn in on the plan, so the palette and the # picture agree about which room is which.
nodes.body_text: def entry(name: str, group: str) -> dict: # The colour it is drawn in on the plan, so the palette and the # picture agree about which room is which. return {"id": name, "label": room_label(name), "group": group, "colour": "#%02x%02x%02x" % room_colour(name)}

nodes.name: _listed
nodes.body_text: def _listed(value) -> list: """A list of whatever was sent, or nothing. A cleaner never throws: this reads what the window posts and what is on disk, and a number where a list was expected used to come back as a Python TypeError.""" return list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) else []

nodes.name: _table
nodes.body_text: def _table(value) -> dict: return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}

nodes.name: _int
nodes.body_text: def _int(value, low, high, fallback): try: number = float(value) except (TypeError, ValueError): return fallback # float() takes "NaN" and "inf" and int() takes neither: a sheet whose # width arrived as one of those ended in "cannot convert float infinity # to integer" rather than in the size it was supposed to fall back to. if not math.isfinite(number): return fallback return min(max(int(number), low), high)

nodes.name: _stable_seed
nodes.body_text: def _stable_seed(*parts) -> int: return zlib.crc32(repr(parts).encode("utf-8")) & 0x7FFFFFFF

nodes.name: blank
nodes.signature: def blank(kind: str | None = None, width: int = 20, height: int = 16) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def blank(kind: str | None = None, width: int = 20, height: int = 16) -> dict: return clean({"kind": kind or "", "width": width, "height": height, "storeys": 1, "rooms": []})

nodes.name: clean
nodes.body_text: def clean(raw) -> dict: """A design from untrusted input, with its rooms made to not overlap. Rooms are drawn one over another, as in any paint program: the newest wins and whatever was under it keeps the rest of itself. The pieces are worked out here rather than in the window because the rest of the pipeline is built on rectangular rooms (knoxbuild/layout.py) and this is the one place that has to be true. A room with no kind is the eraser: it takes its rectangle out of whatever is under it and leaves nothing behind, which is also how a footprint is cut to an L or a T. """ raw = raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {} width = _int(raw.get("width"), MIN_SIDE, MAX_SIDE, 20) height = _int(raw.get("height"), MIN_SIDE, MAX_SIDE, 16) storeys = _int(raw.get("storeys"), 1, MAX_STOREYS, 1) kind = str(raw.get("kind") or "").strip().lower()[:40] if kind and kind not in {entry["id"] for entry in P.kinds()}: kind = "" # a kind the generator cannot recognise is no kind style = str(raw.get("style") or "").strip()[:60] name = P.safe_name(raw.get("name") or "") seed = _int(raw.get("seed"), 0, 2 ** 31 - 1, 0) or _stable_seed(name or "x") # Level by level, so a room drawn upstairs cannot cut one downstairs. by_level: dict[int, list[tuple[tuple, str]]] = {} for item in _listed(raw.get("rooms")): if not isinstance(item, dict): continue level = _int(item.get("level"), 0, storeys - 1, 0) x0 = _int(item.get("x"), 0, width - 1, 0) y0 = _int(item.get("y"), 0, height - 1, 0) x1 = min(width - 1, x0 + _int(item.get("w"), 1, MAX_SIDE, 1) - 1) y1 = min(height - 1, y0 + _int(item.get("h"), 1, MAX_SIDE, 1) - 1) room_kind = str(item.get("kind") or "").strip().lower()[:40] if room_kind and room_kind not in L.ROOM_STYLE: continue kept = [] for box, had in by_level.get(level, []): for piece in L._subtract(box, [(x0, y0, x1, y1)]): kept.append((piece, had)) if room_kind: kept.append(((x0, y0, x1, y1), room_kind)) by_level[level] = kept rooms = [] for level in sorted(by_level): for (x0, y0, x1, y1), room_kind in by_level[level]: rooms.append({"level": level, "x": x0, "y": y0, "w": x1 - x0 + 1, "h": y1 - y0 + 1, "kind": room_kind}) return {"name": name, "kind": kind, "style": style, "seed": seed, "width": width, "height": height, "storeys": storeys, "rooms": rooms}

nodes.name: painted
nodes.signature: def painted(design: dict, level: int = 0) -> int
nodes.body_text: def painted(design: dict, level: int = 0) -> int: """How many tiles of this storey are inside the building.""" return sum(r["w"] * r["h"] for r in design["rooms"] if r["level"] == level)

nodes.name: tally
nodes.signature: def tally(design: dict, level: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, int]]
nodes.body_text: def tally(design: dict, level: int | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, int]]: """The rooms of a storey, most floor first, for the window's list.""" area: dict[str, int] = {} for room in design["rooms"]: if level is not None and room["level"] != level: continue area[room["kind"]] = area.get(room["kind"], 0) + room["w"] * room["h"] return sorted(area.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))

nodes.name: _mask
nodes.body_text: def _mask(design: dict, level: int) -> list[list[bool]]: mask = [[False] * design["width"] for _ in range(design["height"])] for room in design["rooms"]: if room["level"] != level: continue for y in range(room["y"], room["y"] + room["h"]): for x in range(room["x"], room["x"] + room["w"]): mask[y][x] = True return mask

nodes.name: _rooms_of
nodes.body_text: def _rooms_of(design: dict, level: int) -> list[L.Room]: return [L.Room(r["x"], r["y"], r["x"] + r["w"] - 1, r["y"] + r["h"] - 1, kind=r["kind"]) for r in design["rooms"] if r["level"] == level]

nodes.name: _split_by
nodes.signature: def _split_by(box: tuple[int, int, int, int], core: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _split_by(box: tuple[int, int, int, int], core: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> int: """How badly a staircase cuts a room: 2 if it leaves two pieces, 1 if it takes a bite out of one, 3 if it eats the room whole. A strip two tiles thick is not a room - the layout folds anything that thin into its neighbour (_mend_fragments) - so a shaft that leaves only strips has eaten the room, whatever the arithmetic says. """ pieces = [piece for piece in L._subtract(box, [core]) if min(piece[2] - piece[0], piece[3] - piece[1]) + 1 >= 3] if not pieces: return 3 if len(pieces) == 1: return 1 # _subtract gives rectangles, not regions: two of them along the same side # of the shaft are still one room. Walk them to see which really touch. seen = {0} edge = [0] while edge: i = edge.pop() ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1 = pieces[i] for j, (bx0, by0, bx1, by1) in enumerate(pieces): if j in seen: continue if (ax0 <= bx1 + 1 and bx0 <= ax1 + 1 and ay0 <= by1 + 1 and by0 <= ay1 + 1): seen.add(j) edge.append(j) return 1 if len(seen) == len(pieces) else 2

nodes.name: _core_for
nodes.body_text: def _core_for(design: dict, rng: random.Random): """Where the staircase goes in a building somebody drew. The generator puts its shaft in the middle of the floor, which is right for a plan it laid out itself around one. Over a drawing it is wrong: the shaft landed in the middle of a drawn room and cut it in two, and in a room barely bigger than the shaft it ate the whole thing - draw a 6x6 room on a two-storey building and what came back was two rooms. So it is put where it takes the least out of what was drawn: a corner of one room rather than its middle, against an outside wall where a house really keeps its stairs. It must stand on painted floor on every storey, because a shaft over the garden upstairs is a flight into the air. """ width, height = design["width"], design["height"] levels = design["storeys"] masks = [_mask(design, level) for level in range(levels)] rooms = [(level, (r["x"], r["y"], r["x"] + r["w"] - 1, r["y"] + r["h"] - 1)) for level in range(levels) for r in design["rooms"] if r["level"] == level] best, best_score = [], None for cw, ch in ((L.CORE_WIDE, L.STAIR_RUN + 1), (L.STAIR_RUN + 1, L.CORE_WIDE)): if cw > width or ch > height: continue for y0 in range(height - ch + 1): for x0 in range(width - cw + 1): core = (x0, y0, x0 + cw - 1, y0 + ch - 1) if not all(mask[y][x] for mask in masks for y in range(y0, y0 + ch) for x in range(x0, x0 + cw)): continue harm = eaten = 0 for _level, box in rooms: if (box[0] > core[2] or box[2] < core[0] or box[1] > core[3] or box[3] < core[1]): continue cut = _split_by(box, core) harm += cut eaten += cut == 3 # Against a wall: how much of the shaft's own edge has nothing # painted beyond it. outside = 0 for y in range(y0, y0 + ch): for x, step in ((x0, -1), (x0 + cw - 1, 1)): at = x + step outside += at < 0 or at >= width or not masks[0][y][at] for x in range(x0, x0 + cw): for y, step in ((y0, -1), (y0 + ch - 1, 1)): at = y + step outside += at < 0 or at >= height or not masks[0][at][x] score = (eaten, harm, -outside, round(abs((x0 + cw / 2) - width / 2) + abs((y0 + ch / 2) - height / 2), 3)) if best_score is None or score < best_score: best, best_score = [core], score elif score == best_score: best.append(core) # Every place the stairs could stand would swallow a room whole, which is # to say the drawing has no room for stairs: one storey of it, then, the # same answer as a building with nowhere to put a shaft at all. if not best or best_score[0]: return None return rng.choice(best)

nodes.name: style_for
nodes.body_text: def style_for(design: dict) -> dict: """The materials this building is built of. A style named in the design is looked up for the kind being built, so "brick" on a church is the church's brick; a design that names none is built in whatever the generator would have picked for that kind, which is also what makes a one-click preset look like the rest of the map. """ from . import build as B kind = design.get("kind") or None if design.get("style"): found = B.style_named(design["style"], kind) if found: return found return B.pick_style(kind, 0, 0, random.Random(design.get("seed") or 0), Settings())

nodes.name: style_choices
nodes.signature: def style_choices(kind: str | None = None) -> list[str]
nodes.body_text: def style_choices(kind: str | None = None) -> list[str]: from . import build as B return B.style_names(kind or None)

nodes.name: stack
nodes.signature: def stack(design: dict, settings: Settings | None = None, only: int | None = None) -> L.Building
nodes.body_text: def stack(design: dict, settings: Settings | None = None, only: int | None = None) -> L.Building: """The design as a finished building: walls, doors, windows, furniture. Everything that is not the room plan is done by the generator's own passes, in the order build_building does them - doors between rooms, a way in on the ground floor, the furniture, then the windows for the whole facade at once so they stack in columns. A hand-drawn building is therefore furnished to the same rules as every other building on the map. `only` builds that storey alone, for drawing a big building quickly; what is saved is always the whole stack. """ settings = settings or Settings() design = clean(design) kind = design.get("kind") or None levels = design["storeys"] seed = design["seed"] rng = random.Random(seed ^ 0x5745) core = stairs = None if levels > 1: core = _core_for(design, rng) if core is None: levels = 1 # nowhere for a staircase, so one storey it is else: stairs = L._stairs_in_core(core) wanted = range(levels) if only is None else [min(max(only, 0), levels - 1)] storeys = [] for level in wanted: plan = L.Plan(width=design["width"], height=design["height"], rooms=_rooms_of(design, level), core=core, kind=kind, drawn=True) L._paint(plan) if not plan.rooms: storeys.append(plan) continue floor_rng = random.Random(seed + 977 * level) L._doors(plan, floor_rng) if level == 0: L._exterior_door(plan, floor_rng, avoid=L._stair_foot(stairs)) if kind in (None, "house"): L._back_door(plan) L._furnish(plan, floor_rng, stairs) storeys.append(plan) building = L.Building(width=design["width"], height=design["height"], storeys=storeys) if stairs is not None and only is None: for level in range(levels - 1): building.stairs.append(stairs) L._clear_for_stairs(storeys[level], *stairs) L._clear_for_stairs(storeys[level + 1], *stairs) elif stairs is not None: # One storey on its own still has the staircase standing in it. L._clear_for_stairs(storeys[0], *stairs) L._place_windows(building, kind) L._clear_the_way(building) return building

nodes.name: tbx_text
nodes.signature: def tbx_text(design: dict, name: str | None = None) -> str
nodes.body_text: def tbx_text(design: dict, name: str | None = None) -> str: """The design as the .tbx a preset is.""" from .tbx import render_tbx design = clean(design) label = P.safe_name(name or design.get("name") or "") or "Hand-built" return render_tbx(stack(design), label, style_for(design))

nodes.name: autofill
nodes.signature: def autofill(design: dict, settings: Settings | None = None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def autofill(design: dict, settings: Settings | None = None) -> dict: """Rooms laid out by the generator, to start from or to fill a storey. Drawing a 30-room school by hand is work nobody should have to do twice. This is the building the map would have got, handed over as a design to change: the rooms it would have cut, where it would have cut them. """ design = clean(design) built = L.build_building(design["width"], design["height"], levels=design["storeys"], kind=design.get("kind") or None, seed=design["seed"], settings=settings or Settings()) rooms = [] for level, storey in enumerate(built.storeys): for room in storey.rooms: if room.is_shaft or room.kind not in L.ROOM_STYLE: continue rooms.append({"level": level, "x": room.x0, "y": room.y0, "w": room.w, "h": room.h, "kind": room.kind}) out = dict(design) out["rooms"] = rooms out["storeys"] = max(1, len(built.storeys)) return clean(out)

nodes.name: _tile_names
nodes.body_text: def _tile_names(entry, limit: int = 6) -> list[str]: if not isinstance(entry, dict): return [] tiles = entry.get("tiles") if not isinstance(tiles, dict): return [] return sorted({str(t) for t in tiles.values() if t})[:limit]

nodes.name: tiles_used
nodes.body_text: def tiles_used(design: dict) -> list[dict]: """The game tiles this building is built of, for the window to show. "Which tiles" is the question BuildingEd answers with a tile picker and three thousand thumbnails. A preset is built of its style's walls, its rooms' floors and the fittings those rooms carry, so that is what is listed: the walls by name, and each room's floor and furniture. """ design = clean(design) style = style_for(design) out = [{"what": "Outside walls", "name": style.get("name") or "", "tiles": _tile_names(style.get("exterior"))}, {"what": "Inside walls", "name": style.get("name") or "", "tiles": _tile_names(style.get("interior"))}] for room_kind, _area in tally(design): entry = L.ROOM_STYLE.get(room_kind) if not entry: continue out.append({"what": room_label(room_kind), "name": room_kind, "tiles": _tile_names(entry[0], 3), "fittings": sorted(set(entry[2] or ()))[:12]}) return out

nodes.name: room_colour
nodes.signature: def room_colour(kind: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]
nodes.body_text: def room_colour(kind: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]: """A colour per room kind, the same one every time. Worked out from the name rather than listed, because there are 113 rooms and a table of them would be a table to forget to add to. """ import colorsys hue = (zlib.crc32(kind.encode("utf-8")) % 997) / 997.0 sat = 0.30 + ((zlib.crc32(kind[::-1].encode("utf-8")) >> 3) % 20) / 100.0 r, g, b = colorsys.hls_to_rgb(hue, 0.78, sat) return int(r * 255), int(g * 255), int(b * 255)

nodes.name: one_storey_at_a_time
nodes.body_text: def one_storey_at_a_time(design: dict) -> bool: """Whether this design is too big to build whole for every change.""" return (design["storeys"] > 1 and design["width"] * design["height"] * design["storeys"] > PREVIEW_BUDGET)

nodes.name: scale_for
nodes.signature: def scale_for(design: dict, longest: int = 760) -> int
nodes.body_text: def scale_for(design: dict, longest: int = 760) -> int: side = max(design["width"], design["height"], 1) return max(4, min(26, longest // side))

nodes.name: _sheet_grid
nodes.signature: def _sheet_grid(pen, width: int, height: int, px: int) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _sheet_grid(pen, width: int, height: int, px: int) -> None: """One square a tile, over the whole sheet, under whatever is drawn.""" for x in range(width + 1): pen.line([x * px, 0, x * px, height * px], fill=EMPTY_GRID_FIFTH if x % GRID_EVERY == 0 else EMPTY_GRID) for y in range(height + 1): pen.line([0, y * px, width * px, y * px], fill=EMPTY_GRID_FIFTH if y % GRID_EVERY == 0 else EMPTY_GRID)

nodes.name: preview
nodes.signature: def preview(design: dict, level: int = 0, scale: int | None = None, building: L.Building | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def preview(design: dict, level: int = 0, scale: int | None = None, building: L.Building | None = None): """A picture of one storey: rooms, walls, doors, windows, furniture. Drawn from the finished building rather than from the drawing, so what is on the screen is what the .tbx will hold - the doors the generator put in, the windows it put in the facade, the furniture standing in each room - and not only the rectangles that were drawn. """ from PIL import Image, ImageDraw design = clean(design) built = building if building is not None else stack(design) width, height = design["width"], design["height"] px = scale or scale_for(design) img = Image.new("RGB", (width * px + 1, height * px + 1), OUTSIDE) pen = ImageDraw.Draw(img) _sheet_grid(pen, width, height, px) if not built.storeys: return img level = min(max(level, 0), len(built.storeys) - 1) plan = built.storeys[level] if not plan.grid: return img def room_at(x, y): if 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height: return plan.grid[y][x] return 0 for y in range(height): for x in range(width): idx = room_at(x, y) if not idx: continue pen.rectangle([x * px, y * px, x * px + px, y * px + px], fill=room_colour(plan.rooms[idx - 1].kind), outline=GRID) thick = max(1, px // 5) for y in range(height + 1): for x in range(width + 1): # A wall stands wherever two different rooms meet, and round the # outside of the building: the rule tbx.py writes them by. if room_at(x, y) != room_at(x - 1, y): pen.line([x * px, y * px, x * px, y * px + px], fill=WALL, width=thick) if room_at(x, y) != room_at(x, y - 1): pen.line([x * px, y * px, x * px + px, y * px], fill=WALL, width=thick) for x, y, d in plan.windows: if d == "W": pen.line([x * px, y * px + 2, x * px, y * px + px - 2], fill=WINDOW, width=thick + 1) else: pen.line([x * px + 2, y * px, x * px + px - 2, y * px], fill=WINDOW, width=thick + 1) # Doors last of the wall things: a doorway is a gap in the wall, so it has # to be drawn over the wall rather than under it. for x, y, d in plan.doors: if d == "W": pen.line([x * px, y * px + 1, x * px, y * px + px - 1], fill=DOOR, width=thick + 1) else: pen.line([x * px + 1, y * px, x * px + px - 1, y * px], fill=DOOR, width=thick + 1) spot = max(2, px // 3) for _role, x, y, _d in plan.furniture: cx, cy = x * px + px // 2, y * px + px // 2 pen.ellipse([cx - spot // 2, cy - spot // 2, cx + spot // 2, cy + spot // 2], fill=PIECE) return img

nodes.name: room_at
nodes.body_text: def room_at(x, y): if 0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height: return plan.grid[y][x] return 0

nodes.name: design_path
nodes.body_text: def design_path(base_dir, name: str) -> str: return os.path.join(P.folder(base_dir), f"{P.safe_name(name)}{P.DESIGN_SUFFIX}")

nodes.name: save_design
nodes.signature: def save_design(base_dir, name: str, design: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def save_design(base_dir, name: str, design: dict) -> None: """Keep the drawing beside the preset, so it can be opened and changed.""" clean_name = P.safe_name(name) if not clean_name: raise ValueError("A preset needs a name.") os.makedirs(P.folder(base_dir), exist_ok=True) path = design_path(base_dir, clean_name) out = dict(clean(design)) out["name"] = clean_name tmp = path + ".part" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(out, f) os.replace(tmp, path)

nodes.name: load_design
nodes.signature: def load_design(base_dir, name: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def load_design(base_dir, name: str) -> dict | None: """The drawing a preset was made from: somebody's own, or a shipped one. A building that ships with KnoxMap keeps its drawing beside it, so one can be opened, changed and saved - which saves it as a building of their own and leaves the shipped one alone (knoxbuild/presets.py, library). """ clean_name = P.safe_name(name) for where in (P.folder(base_dir), P.library_folder(base_dir)): try: with open(os.path.join(where, f"{clean_name}{P.DESIGN_SUFFIX}"), encoding="utf-8") as f: return clean(json.load(f)) except (OSError, ValueError): continue return None

nodes.name: drop_design
nodes.body_text: def drop_design(base_dir, name: str) -> bool: try: os.remove(design_path(base_dir, name)) return True except OSError: return False

nodes.name: keep
nodes.signature: def keep(base_dir, name: str, design: dict) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def keep(base_dir, name: str, design: dict) -> dict: """Save a design as a preset: the drawing, and the .tbx it builds into.""" design = _table(design) clean_name = P.safe_name(name or design.get("name") or "") if not clean_name: raise ValueError("A preset needs a name.") design = clean(design) if not design["rooms"]: raise ValueError("Draw at least one room first.") about = P.save(base_dir, clean_name, tbx_text(design, clean_name), kind=design.get("kind") or "") save_design(base_dir, clean_name, design) about["editable"] = True return about

nodes.name: fences.py
nodes.body_text: """Turn OSM fence and wall lines into Project Zomboid fence tiles. A fence in the game is a tile on a tile's west or north edge, the way a wall is. The styles below are copied from the mapping tools' Fences.txt, which is what WorldEd's own fence tool draws with, and placed by the same rule that tool uses (FenceTool::getWestEdgeTiles and its north twin in TileZed): along a west edge, west1 and west2 alternate; along a north edge, north1 and north2; a tile carrying both takes the corner piece; a loose end gets a post. The fences are written as furniture in a building with no rooms, one per map cell, so they compile into the lots like anything else in a .tbx. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import os from xml.sax.saxutils import quoteattr import knoxfiles from . import catalog as C CELL = 300 # From PZ_Mapping_Tools/config/Fences.txt. Names are zero-padded to three # digits, the form BuildingFurniture.txt uses; both parse to the same tile. STYLES = { "short_wooden": dict(west1=35, west2=34, north1=32, north2=33, nw=36, post=37), "tall_wooden": dict(west1=11, west2=10, north1=8, north2=9, nw=12, post=13), "short_chainlink": dict(west1=27, west2=26, north1=24, north2=25, nw=28, post=29), "tall_chainlink": dict(west1=59, west2=58, north1=56, north2=57, nw=60, post=61), "white_picket": dict(west1=4, west2=4, north1=5, north2=5, nw=6, post=7), "cattle": dict(west1=20, west2=20, north1=21, north2=21, nw=18, post=19), "black_metal": dict(west1=2, west2=2, north1=1, north2=1, nw=3, post=0), # The full-height bars of the Rosewood base wall. The game has both and # OSM says which: metal bars two metres tall came out half that, because # a fence's height was never read. "tall_metal": dict(west1=67, west2=66, north1=64, north2=65, nw=68, post=69), "short_picket": dict(west1=121, west2=121, north1=120, north2=120, nw=122, post=123), "tall_concrete": dict(west1=40, west2=40, north1=41, north2=41, nw=42, post=43), } # Which of a pair is the taller, and the height in metres at which a fence # becomes it. OSM fence heights are mostly 0.9 to 2.4; the game's short # fences are waist high and its tall ones are over your head. TALLER = { "short_wooden": ("tall_wooden", 1.4), "short_chainlink": ("tall_chainlink", 1.7), "black_metal": ("tall_metal", 1.7), "short_picket": ("white_picket", 1.0), } SHORTER = {tall: short for short, (tall, _m) in TALLER.items()} # Gates, for the fences drawn round back yards: (west-edge tile, north-edge tile). GATES = { "short_wooden": ("fixtures_doors_fences_01_004", "fixtures_doors_fences_01_005"), "tall_wooden": ("fixtures_doors_fences_01_012", "fixtures_doors_fences_01_013"), "white_picket": ("fixtures_doors_fences_01_008", "fixtures_doors_fences_01_009"), "short_chainlink": ("fixtures_doors_fences_01_016", "fixtures_doors_fences_01_017"), "black_metal": ("fixtures_doors_fences_01_000", "fixtures_doors_fences_01_001"), } # Land uses that are fenced off in real life, and their smallest size in # tiles - a hundred-tile "base" is a war memorial, not a barracks. FENCED_SITES = {"military": 400} # How far either side of a gate or a crossing path the fence is looked at, in # tiles: the fence line and the node or path it meets rarely land on the same # tile once both are on the grid. OPENING_REACH = 1

nodes.name: height_m
nodes.body_text: def height_m(tags: dict) -> float | None: """A fence's height in metres, from however the mapper wrote it. "2", "2 m", "2.5m" and "6'" all occur; anything else is no answer rather than a guess. """ raw = str(tags.get("height") or tags.get("est_height") or "").strip().lower() if not raw: return None if "'" in raw or "ft" in raw: feet = raw.replace("ft", "").split("'")[0].strip() try: return float(feet) * 0.3048 except ValueError: return None for suffix in (" m", "m", " metres", " meters"): if raw.endswith(suffix): raw = raw[: -len(suffix)].strip() break try: metres = float(raw.replace(",", ".")) except ValueError: return None return metres if 0.2 <= metres <= 12.0 else None

nodes.name: by_height
nodes.signature: def by_height(style: str, metres: float | None) -> str
nodes.body_text: def by_height(style: str, metres: float | None) -> str: """The same fence at the height the mapper gave it.""" if metres is None: return style short = SHORTER.get(style, style) taller, at = TALLER.get(short, (None, 0.0)) if taller is None: return style return taller if metres >= at else short

nodes.name: _tile
nodes.body_text: def _tile(n: int) -> str: return f"fencing_01_{n:03d}"

nodes.name: _fenced_sites
nodes.body_text: def _fenced_sites(areas) -> list: """The land-use polygons that get a fence of their own.""" out = [] for shape, props in getattr(areas, "_items", []) or (): least = FENCED_SITES.get((props.get("category") or "")) if least is None or shape.is_empty or shape.area < least: continue if getattr(shape, "exterior", None) is not None: out.append(shape) return out

nodes.name: _mapped_lines
nodes.body_text: def _mapped_lines(runs: list[list]): """The fences somebody put there, as one geometry to ask about.""" if not runs: return None from shapely.geometry import LineString from shapely.ops import unary_union kept = [LineString(pts) for pts in runs if len(pts) >= 2] return unary_union(kept) if kept else None

nodes.name: _crosses
nodes.body_text: def _crosses(pts: list, drawn) -> bool: """Whether this run of fence meets one that was mapped or drawn.""" if drawn is None or len(pts) < 2: return False from shapely.geometry import LineString try: return LineString(pts).intersects(drawn) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a line that is not a line return False

nodes.name: style_for
nodes.signature: def style_for(tags: dict, area: str | None) -> str
nodes.body_text: def style_for(tags: dict, area: str | None) -> str: """Which fence a line gets: from its own tags first, its surroundings next. Where the mapper gave a height, that decides between the short and the tall version of the fence they asked for - the game has both of most of them, and two-metre metal bars used to come out as the waist-high railing. """ barrier = tags.get("barrier") if barrier in {"wall", "retaining_wall", "city_wall"}: return "tall_concrete" metres = height_m(tags) kind = (tags.get("fence_type") or tags.get("material") or "").lower() if kind in {"chain_link", "chain", "mesh"}: if metres is not None: return by_height("short_chainlink", metres) return "tall_chainlink" if area in {"industrial", "military"} else "short_chainlink" if kind in {"wood", "wooden", "split_rail", "board", "panel"}: return by_height("tall_wooden", metres) if kind in {"picket", "pales"}: return by_height("white_picket", metres) if kind in {"metal", "railing", "metal_bars", "bars", "iron", "steel"}: return by_height("black_metal", metres) if kind in {"barbed_wire", "electric", "wire"}: return "cattle" if kind in {"concrete", "brick", "stone", "masonry"}: return "tall_concrete" return by_height({ "industrial": "tall_chainlink", "military": "tall_chainlink", "schoolyard": "short_chainlink", "sports": "short_chainlink", "residential": "tall_wooden", "cemetery": "black_metal", "worship_grounds": "black_metal", "hospital_grounds": "black_metal", }.get(area or "", "short_wooden"), metres)

nodes.name: _grid_path
nodes.body_text: def _grid_path(points: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """A polyline as a walk along tile corners, one grid step at a time. Diagonal runs become staircases along tile edges - a fence can only stand on an edge - choosing at each corner the step that keeps closer to the real line. """ path: list[tuple[int, int]] = [] for (ax, ay), (bx, by) in zip(points, points[1:]): steps = max(1, int(math.ceil(math.hypot(bx - ax, by - ay) * 4))) for i in range(steps + 1): t = i / steps v = (int(round(ax + (bx - ax) * t)), int(round(ay + (by - ay) * t))) if not path: path.append(v) continue px, py = path[-1] if v == (px, py): continue if v[0] != px and v[1] != py: # Two corners apart diagonally: go through whichever of the two # in-between corners sits nearer the true line. opt1, opt2 = (v[0], py), (px, v[1]) mx, my = ax + (bx - ax) * t, ay + (by - ay) * t mid = min((opt1, opt2), key=lambda o: math.hypot(o[0] - mx, o[1] - my)) path.append(mid) path.append(v) return path

nodes.name: _tarmac_mask
nodes.signature: def _tarmac_mask(bmp_path: str, width: int, height: int)
nodes.body_text: def _tarmac_mask(bmp_path: str, width: int, height: int): """True where the ground is a road, service lane or car park.""" import numpy as np from generator import pz_colors as C from .bitmaps import read_rgb if not os.path.exists(bmp_path): return None ground = read_rgb(bmp_path) if ground.shape[:2] != (height, width): return None mask = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=bool) for colour in (C.LIGHT_ASPHALT, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE): same = ground[:, :, 0] == colour[0] same &= ground[:, :, 1] == colour[1] same &= ground[:, :, 2] == colour[2] mask |= same return mask

nodes.name: _openings
nodes.body_text: def _openings(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj): """Where people get through a fence: gate nodes, and the paths that cross one. Points in tiles, with the paths as lines to be crossed with each fence where it is built.""" path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_fence_openings.geojson") feats = (knoxfiles.read(path, "the gates and paths through the fences", default={}) or {}).get("features", []) if not feats: return [], [] gates, paths = [], [] for feat in feats: geom = feat.get("geometry") or {} coords = geom.get("coordinates") or [] if geom.get("type") == "Point" and len(coords) == 2: gates.append(proj.to_px(coords[1], coords[0])) elif geom.get("type") == "LineString" and len(coords) >= 2: paths.append([proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lon, lat in coords]) return gates, paths

nodes.name: _path_crossings
nodes.body_text: def _path_crossings(fence: list, paths) -> list: """Where a footpath or a track crosses this fence, in tiles.""" if paths is None or len(fence) < 2: return [] from shapely.geometry import LineString try: line = LineString(fence) hit = line.intersection(paths) except Exception: # a fence that is not a line: nothing crosses it return [] if hit.is_empty: return [] out = [] for part in getattr(hit, "geoms", [hit]): if part.geom_type == "Point": out.append((part.x, part.y)) elif not part.is_empty: middle = part.centroid out.append((middle.x, middle.y)) return out

nodes.name: _way_through
nodes.signature: def _way_through(openings: dict, gated: set, gates: dict, at: tuple[int, int], style: str) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _way_through(openings: dict, gated: set, gates: dict, at: tuple[int, int], style: str) -> bool: """Whether the fence is built on this tile at all. True builds it as usual, False leaves a hole. A gate node hangs one gate on the first tile of its opening the fence actually reaches and the fence carries on either side of it, so a gate is a gate and not a gateway; a fence the game has no gate for gets the hole instead. """ mark = openings.get(at) if mark is None: return True if mark: # a gate the mapper put there if style not in GATES: return False # no gate for this fence: a gap if mark not in gated: gated.add(mark) gates[at] = style # swapped for the gate below return True return False # a path through: a gap

nodes.name: build_fences
nodes.signature: def build_fences(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, occupied, areas, bdir: str, extra: list | None = None, keep_clear: set | None = None) -> tuple[list, int]
nodes.body_text: def build_fences(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, occupied, areas, bdir: str, extra: list | None = None, keep_clear: set | None = None) -> tuple[list, int]: """Write one fence .tbx per map cell that has fences. Returns placements. `keep_clear` is a set of (x, y) tiles - the ground in front of each door - that no fence edge may touch: a fence across a doorway is a gap in the fence instead.""" clear = keep_clear or () from .world import Placement path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_fences.geojson") lines = (knoxfiles.read(path, "the fences", default={}) or {}).get("features", []) sites = _fenced_sites(areas) if not lines and not extra and not sites: return [], 0 map_h, map_w = occupied.shape def building_at(x: int, y: int) -> bool: return 0 <= x < map_w and 0 <= y < map_h and bool(occupied[y, x]) # Mappers draw a fence as one line and put the gate in as a separate point, # so a schoolyard fence crosses its own driveway and a factory fence the # road into the works. Built as drawn, the fence walls the road off. An # edge with tarmac on both sides is a road crossing, and is left open; a # fence along the side of a car park has tarmac on one side only and stays. tarmac = _tarmac_mask(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.bmp"), map_w, map_h) def crossing(ax: int, ay: int, bx: int, by: int) -> bool: if tarmac is None: return False inside = (0 <= ax < map_w and 0 <= ay < map_h and 0 <= bx < map_w and 0 <= by < map_h) return inside and bool(tarmac[ay, ax]) and bool(tarmac[by, bx]) # (x, y) -> {"W": style, "N": style} edges: dict[tuple[int, int], dict[str, str]] = {} ends: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {} # Mapped fences, then the ones drawn round back yards (knoxbuild/yards.py), # which come as tile points with their style. Each carries whether it is a # fence somebody put there - mapped in OpenStreetMap or drawn in the # editor - or one made up here, because where the two meet the real one # wins. todo: list[tuple[list, str, bool]] = [] for feat in lines: coords = feat.get("geometry", {}).get("coordinates") or [] if len(coords) < 2: continue pts = [proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lon, lat in coords] mid = pts[len(pts) // 2] todo.append((pts, style_for(feat.get("properties") or {}, areas.category_at(*mid) if areas else None), True)) # Sites that are fenced in the world whether or not anyone drew the fence. # OpenStreetMap maps an army base as landuse=military far more often than # it maps the wire round it, so a base was open ground you could walk # across; the outline of the site is the fence. Road crossings are left # open by the rule above, which is what makes the gates. for shape in sites: ring = list(shape.exterior.coords) if len(ring) >= 4: todo.append(([(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in ring], "tall_chainlink", True)) gates: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {} # A yard fence is this program's guess at what is round a house. Where # somebody has mapped or drawn a fence or a hedge that crosses it, theirs # is what is there, and the guess is dropped rather than laid over it. drawn = _mapped_lines([pts for pts, _style, real in todo if real]) for item in extra or (): pts, style = item[0], item[1] if _crosses(pts, drawn): continue todo.append((pts, style, False)) for gx, gy in (item[2] if len(item) > 2 else ()): gates[(gx, gy)] = style # A gate on the fence, or a footpath through it: the mapper drew the way # in, and a fence built from the line alone stood across it. Each opening # takes its tiles out of the fence; where the game has a gate for that # fence, one of those tiles becomes the gate rather than a hole. gate_points, path_lines = _openings(out_dir, map_name, proj) paths = None if path_lines: from shapely.geometry import LineString from shapely.ops import unary_union paths = unary_union([LineString(line) for line in path_lines if len(line) >= 2]) openings: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {} def open_up(points, kind_gate: bool) -> None: for px, py in points: mark = len(openings) + 1 if kind_gate else 0 for dx in range(-OPENING_REACH, OPENING_REACH + 1): for dy in range(-OPENING_REACH, OPENING_REACH + 1): key = (int(round(px)) + dx, int(round(py)) + dy) openings.setdefault(key, mark) open_up(gate_points, True) gated: set[int] = set() for pts, style, real in todo: if paths is not None: open_up(_path_crossings(pts, paths), False) walk = _grid_path(pts) for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(walk, walk[1:]): if y1 == y2: # along a north edge x = min(x1, x2) # A fence never runs through a building: that edge is a wall. if building_at(x, y1) or building_at(x, y1 - 1): continue if (x, y1) in clear or (x, y1 - 1) in clear: continue if crossing(x, y1, x, y1 - 1): continue if not _way_through(openings, gated, gates, (x, y1), style): continue side = edges.setdefault((x, y1), {}) if real or "N" not in side: side["N"] = style else: # along a west edge y = min(y1, y2) if building_at(x1, y) or building_at(x1 - 1, y): continue if (x1, y) in clear or (x1 - 1, y) in clear: continue if crossing(x1, y, x1 - 1, y): continue if not _way_through(ope

Each distinct fence tile is its own single-tile furniture piece, defined for all four facings so the reader accepts it, and placed facing west. """ tiles = sorted(set(pieces.values())) index = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(tiles)} out = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>'] attrs = [("version", 4), ("width", width), ("height", height), ("ExteriorWall", C.EXTERIOR_WALL), ("ExteriorWallTrim", 0), ("Door", C.DOOR), ("DoorFrame", C.DOOR_FRAME), ("Window", C.WINDOW), ("Curtains", C.CURTAINS), ("Shutters", 0), ("Stairs", C.STAIRS), ("RoofCap", C.ROOF_CAP), ("RoofSlope", C.ROOF_SLOPE), ("RoofTop", C.ROOF_TOP), ("GrimeWall", 0)] out.append("<building" + "".join(f" {k}={quoteattr(str(v))}" for k, v in attrs) + ">") for entry in C.TILE_ENTRIES: out.append(f' <tile_entry category={quoteattr(entry["category"])}>') for enum_name, tile in entry["tiles"].items(): out.append(f' <tile enum={quoteattr(enum_name)} tile={quoteattr(tile)}/>') out.append(" </tile_entry>") for tile in tiles: out.append(" <furniture>") for orient in ("W", "N", "E", "S"): out.append(f' <entry orient="{orient}">') out.append(f' <tile x="0" y="0" name={quoteattr(tile)}/>') out.append(" </entry>") out.append(" </furniture>") out.append(" <used_tiles>" + " ".join(str(i) for i in range(1, len(C.TILE_ENTRIES) + 1)) + "</used_tiles>") out.append(" <used_furniture>" + " ".join(str(i) for i in range(len(tiles))) + "</used_furniture>") out.append(" <floor>") for (x, y), tile in sorted(pieces.items()): out.append(f' <object type="furniture" FurnitureTiles="{index[tile]}" ' f'orient="W" x="{x}" y="{y}"/>') grid = "
" + "

nodes.name: footprint.py
nodes.body_text: """Fit real OSM building outlines to the game's axis-aligned tile grid. Real rasterizes the mapped polygon. Smart straightens near-grid footprints, rectifying nonrectangular shapes and boxing only near-rectangles. Rectilinear aligns every footprint's dominant wall direction while preserving its L-shapes and notches. Rectangle uses the minimum rotated rectangle as a clean box. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import numpy as np import shapely from shapely.affinity import rotate as rotate_geometry from shapely.geometry import Polygon # Within this many degrees of the grid, square the building up. SNAP_DEGREES = 8.0 # A footprint filling this share of its rotated rectangle is a rectangle. RECTANGULAR_ENOUGH = 0.86 MIN_TILES = 16 RECTILINEAR_SIMPLIFY_TOLERANCE = 1.0 BUILDING_ALIGNMENT_OPTIONS = {"real", "smart", "rectilinear", "rectangle"} # A unit narrower than this is not a building anyone can walk into: three # tiles of room plus its walls. MIN_ROOM_SIDE = 5 # A building reaches the game as a lot, and a lot is a rectangle: the .pzw # says <lot x y width height> and WorldEd writes that whole rectangle of # squares into the cell. A footprint off the grid owns a staircase of tiles # inside its rectangle and nothing else, so most of that rectangle is ground # the building never claimed - and the next building along claims it, because # `occupied` only ever held the tiles. On Brugge that came to 5004 pairs of # lots standing on top of each other among 4202 buildings, overlapping by # whole rows rather than the single shared column a terrace wants. Where two # lots cover a square, one is written over the other and a wall goes missing. # # So a footprint claims its rectangle as well as its tiles, and a later one is # cut back to the biggest part of itself whose rectangle is still free. Real # neighbours still stand wall to wall: their rectangles meet along an edge, # and the wall between them is the one column both of them draw. NUDGE_TILES = 5 # A building may stand on at most this share of road; it is moved out of the road as far as # WIDE_NUDGE_TILES to get there, and the road squares it still has are cut away. One that # cannot be got under the share is refused ("road"): 63 of 957 buildings of a real town sat # on roads, 25 of them mostly, before this. ROAD_SHARE_MAX = 0.10 WIDE_NUDGE_TILES = 12 ROAD_WEIGHT = 2 # `avoid` at or above this is road; 1 is pavement, which a building may front

nodes.name: _polygon
nodes.signature: def _polygon(px: list[tuple[float, float]]): # One or two points are not a shape; Shapely raises on them, and place() # says "small" for an empty one. The build already skips these before it # gets here, so this is for whoever calls place() next.
nodes.body_text: def _polygon(px: list[tuple[float, float]]): # One or two points are not a shape; Shapely raises on them, and place() # says "small" for an empty one. The build already skips these before it # gets here, so this is for whoever calls place() next. if len(px) < 3: return Polygon() poly = Polygon(px) if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) if poly.geom_type == "MultiPolygon": poly = max(poly.geoms, key=lambda g: g.area) return poly

nodes.name: grid_angle
nodes.body_text: def grid_angle(poly, rect=None) -> float: """How far the building's long side is from the nearest grid axis, 0..45. `rect` is the polygon's minimum rotated rectangle when the caller already has it: working it out is the dearest thing Shapely does per building. """ if rect is None: rect = poly.minimum_rotated_rectangle if not hasattr(rect, "exterior"): return 0.0 c = list(rect.exterior.coords) e1 = (c[1][0] - c[0][0], c[1][1] - c[0][1]) e2 = (c[2][0] - c[1][0], c[2][1] - c[1][1]) long_edge = e1 if math.hypot(*e1) >= math.hypot(*e2) else e2 a = abs(math.degrees(math.atan2(long_edge[1], long_edge[0]))) % 90.0 return min(a, 90.0 - a)

nodes.name: _orthogonal_rotation
nodes.body_text: def _orthogonal_rotation(poly, rect=None) -> float: """Rotation that takes the dominant wall direction to the nearest grid axis. `rect` is the polygon's minimum rotated rectangle when the caller has it. """ if rect is None: rect = poly.minimum_rotated_rectangle coords = list(rect.exterior.coords) if hasattr(rect, "exterior") else [] if len(coords) < 4: return 0.0 edge1 = (coords[1][0] - coords[0][0], coords[1][1] - coords[0][1]) edge2 = (coords[2][0] - coords[1][0], coords[2][1] - coords[1][1]) long_edge = edge1 if math.hypot(*edge1) >= math.hypot(*edge2) else edge2 angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(long_edge[1], long_edge[0])) return -((angle + 45.0) % 90.0 - 45.0)

nodes.name: rectilinearize_polygon
nodes.body_text: def rectilinearize_polygon(poly): """Align a footprint's dominant axis to the tile grid and simplify small survey jogs without replacing its outline with a bounding rectangle. The map itself is rotated before footprints reach this function, so this aligns a building to that frame (and thus to the selected road grid) while keeping L-shaped and notched footprints recognizable. """ rotation = _orthogonal_rotation(poly) aligned = rotate_geometry(poly, rotation, origin="centroid") \ if abs(rotation) > 1e-6 else poly aligned = aligned.simplify(RECTILINEAR_SIMPLIFY_TOLERANCE, preserve_topology=True) if not aligned.is_valid: aligned = aligned.buffer(0) if aligned.geom_type == "MultiPolygon": aligned = max(aligned.geoms, key=lambda part: part.area) return aligned

nodes.name: _largest_component
nodes.body_text: def _largest_component(mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """Keep only the biggest 4-connected piece of a mask.""" # A full mask is one piece. Squared-up buildings are always full, and # walking every tile of a large one to learn that is the slow part. if mask.all(): return mask h, w = mask.shape seen = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=bool) best: list[tuple[int, int]] = [] for y in range(h): for x in range(w): if not mask[y, x] or seen[y, x]: continue piece = [] stack = [(y, x)] seen[y, x] = True while stack: cy, cx = stack.pop() piece.append((cy, cx)) for ny, nx in ((cy + 1, cx), (cy - 1, cx), (cy, cx + 1), (cy, cx - 1)): if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and mask[ny, nx] and not seen[ny, nx]: seen[ny, nx] = True stack.append((ny, nx)) if len(piece) > len(best): best = piece out = np.zeros_like(mask, dtype=bool) for y, x in best: out[y, x] = True return out

nodes.name: Footprint
nodes.body_text: class Footprint: """Where one building goes: its bounding box and which tiles it owns.""" def __init__(self, x0: int, y0: int, mask: np.ndarray, angle: float, short_side: float, long_side: float, point_origin: tuple[float, float] | None = None, point_rotation: float = 0.0, point_offset: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0)): self.x0, self.y0 = x0, y0 self.mask = mask self.angle = angle self.short_side = short_side self.long_side = long_side self.point_origin = point_origin self.point_rotation = point_rotation self.point_offset = point_offset @property def width(self) -> int: return self.mask.shape[1] @property def height(self) -> int: return self.mask.shape[0] @property def tiles(self) -> int: return int(self.mask.sum()) def mask_list(self) -> list[list[bool]] | None: """The mask as layout.py takes it, or None when it fills its box.""" if self.mask.all(): return None return self.mask.tolist() def transform_point(self, x: float, y: float) -> tuple[float, float]: """Move a mapped point with the geometry transform used by this mask.""" if self.point_origin is None or not self.point_rotation: return x + self.point_offset[0], y + self.point_offset[1] cx, cy = self.point_origin angle = math.radians(self.point_rotation) dx, dy = x - cx, y - cy return (cx + dx * math.cos(angle) - dy * math.sin(angle) + self.point_offset[0], cy + dx * math.sin(angle) + dy * math.cos(angle) + self.point_offset[1])
