nodes.body_text: def transform_point(self, x: float, y: float) -> tuple[float, float]: """Move a mapped point with the geometry transform used by this mask.""" if self.point_origin is None or not self.point_rotation: return x + self.point_offset[0], y + self.point_offset[1] cx, cy = self.point_origin angle = math.radians(self.point_rotation) dx, dy = x - cx, y - cy return (cx + dx * math.cos(angle) - dy * math.sin(angle) + self.point_offset[0], cy + dx * math.sin(angle) + dy * math.cos(angle) + self.point_offset[1])

nodes.name: split_row
nodes.signature: def split_row(fp: "Footprint", unit_tiles: int, min_tiles: int = MIN_TILES) -> list["Footprint"]
nodes.body_text: def split_row(fp: "Footprint", unit_tiles: int, min_tiles: int = MIN_TILES) -> list["Footprint"]: """Cut a long footprint into one footprint per unit along its length. A row of shops or a terrace of houses is usually one polygon in OpenStreetMap - the mapper drew the block, not the seven doors in it - and built as one building it came out as a single cavernous shed with one front door, the "uber building" players kept reporting. Cut into units of about a shop's frontage it becomes what it is: separate buildings standing wall to wall, which is a case the rest of the build already handles (the shared walls lose their windows, see _party_walls). The cuts are made on tile boundaries with no gap between units, so the row still covers exactly the tiles the real building covers. """ along_x = fp.width >= fp.height length = fp.width if along_x else fp.height units = max(1, int(round(length / max(1, unit_tiles)))) if units < 2: return [fp] out: list[Footprint] = [] edges = [round(length * k / units) for k in range(units + 1)] for a, b in zip(edges, edges[1:]): if b - a < MIN_ROOM_SIDE: continue part = fp.mask[:, a:b] if along_x else fp.mask[a:b, :] if part.sum() < min_tiles: continue part = _largest_component(part) rows = np.where(part.any(axis=1))[0] cols = np.where(part.any(axis=0))[0] if len(rows) == 0 or len(cols) == 0: continue part = part[rows[0]:rows[-1] + 1, cols[0]:cols[-1] + 1] if part.sum() < min_tiles: continue x0 = fp.x0 + (a if along_x else 0) + int(cols[0]) y0 = fp.y0 + (0 if along_x else a) + int(rows[0]) out.append(Footprint(x0, y0, part, fp.angle, fp.short_side, fp.long_side / units, fp.point_origin, fp.point_rotation, fp.point_offset)) return out or [fp]

nodes.name: _hug
nodes.signature: def _hug(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _hug(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int, int]: """The mask's biggest piece, in a box trimmed to hold only that.""" mask = _largest_component(mask) rows = np.where(mask.any(axis=1))[0] cols = np.where(mask.any(axis=0))[0] if len(rows) == 0: return mask[:0, :0], x0, y0 return (mask[rows[0]:rows[-1] + 1, cols[0]:cols[-1] + 1], x0 + int(cols[0]), y0 + int(rows[0]))

nodes.name: _clear_box
nodes.signature: def _clear_box(mask: np.ndarray, blocked: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _clear_box(mask: np.ndarray, blocked: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]: """The box holding most of `mask` and no `blocked` tile, half open. Cutting a row off the near side, as a nudge would, is no use when the lot in the way sits along the middle of the footprint, so every rectangle of free ground is measured - the row-by-row histogram scan that finds them - and the one keeping the most of the building wins. A footprint therefore gives up whichever end of itself is emptiest, and one that has nowhere left to stand gives up altogether. """ h, w = mask.shape # Squeeze runs of identical rows and columns of `blocked` into one. A # rectangle's edge can always slide to the end of such a run without # touching a blocked tile or losing any of the building, so the best box # is found on the squeezed grid and gives the same count of tiles. A large # building with a lot or two clipping its corner is a handful of runs, not # tens of thousands of tiles. cuts_x = np.flatnonzero((blocked[:, 1:] != blocked[:, :-1]).any(axis=0)) + 1 cuts_y = np.flatnonzero((blocked[1:] != blocked[:-1]).any(axis=1)) + 1 cb = np.concatenate(([0], cuts_x, [w])) rb = np.concatenate(([0], cuts_y, [h])) small = blocked[rb[:-1]][:, cb[:-1]] sh, sw = small.shape # How much of the building any box holds, in one subtraction. held = np.zeros((h + 1, w + 1), dtype=np.int32) held[1:, 1:] = mask.cumsum(0).cumsum(1) best = (0, 0, 0, 0, 0) heights = np.zeros(sw, dtype=np.int32) for y in range(sh): # Free runs standing one above another, counting up to this row. heights = np.where(small[y], 0, heights + 1) stack: list[tuple[int, int]] = [] for x, tall in enumerate(heights.tolist() + [0]): start = x while stack and stack[-1][1] >= tall: start, high = stack.pop() top = y + 1 - high tiles = int(held[rb[y + 1], cb[x]] - held[rb[top], cb[x]] - held[rb[y + 1], cb[start]] + held[rb[top], cb[start]]) if tiles > best[0]: best = (tiles, int(rb[top]), int(rb[y + 1]), int(cb[start]), int(cb[x])) stack.append((start, tall)) return best[1:]

nodes.name: _road_share
nodes.signature: def _road_share(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int, avoid: np.ndarray) -> float
nodes.body_text: def _road_share(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int, avoid: np.ndarray) -> float: """The share of the footprint's tiles that are road, with the footprint at (x0, y0).""" map_h, map_w = avoid.shape h, w = mask.shape cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1 = max(0, x0), max(0, y0), min(map_w, x0 + w), min(map_h, y0 + h) if cx1 <= cx0 or cy1 <= cy0 or not mask.sum(): return 0.0 m = mask[cy0 - y0:cy1 - y0, cx0 - x0:cx1 - x0] return float((avoid[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1][m] >= ROAD_WEIGHT).sum()) / float(mask.sum())

nodes.name: _clear_of
nodes.signature: def _clear_of(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int, avoid: np.ndarray, occupied: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _clear_of(mask: np.ndarray, x0: int, y0: int, avoid: np.ndarray, occupied: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, int]: """Where to put a footprint so it stands off the roads. `avoid` weighs each tile: the bigger the road the more it costs, pavement costs 1 and free ground 0. With roads straightened and buildings squared up, a building can come out a tile or three into the street; it is moved the least distance, up to NUDGE_TILES, that takes it out. A spot clear of the road altogether is taken when there is one. Where there is not, the building stands on the least road it can rather than being dropped: demanding a clear spot threw away every footprint that fronts a pavement, which in a town is most of them - the selftest's school, shop and medical building all came out "0 laid out".""" map_h, map_w = avoid.shape h, w = mask.shape def cost(ox, oy): ax0, ay0 = x0 + ox, y0 + oy cx0, cy0 = max(0, ax0), max(0, ay0) cx1, cy1 = min(map_w, ax0 + w), min(map_h, ay0 + h) if cx1 <= cx0 or cy1 <= cy0: return None m = mask[cy0 - ay0:cy1 - ay0, cx0 - ax0:cx1 - ax0] return (int(avoid[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1][m].sum()), int(occupied[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1][m].sum())) here = cost(0, 0) if here is None or here[0] == 0: return x0, y0 clear, clear_score = None, float("inf") best, best_score = (0, 0), here[0] * 4 + here[1] for ox in range(-NUDGE_TILES, NUDGE_TILES + 1): for oy in range(-NUDGE_TILES, NUDGE_TILES + 1): c = cost(ox, oy) if c is None: continue moved = (abs(ox) + abs(oy)) * 0.5 if c[0] == 0 and c[1] + moved < clear_score: clear, clear_score = (ox, oy), c[1] + moved score = c[0] * 4 + c[1] + moved if score < best_score: best, best_score = (ox, oy), score ox, oy = clear if clear is not None else best if _road_share(mask, x0 + ox, y0 + oy, avoid) > ROAD_SHARE_MAX: # Still on the road: look further for a spot that is off it, nearest first. found = None for r in range(NUDGE_TILES + 1, WIDE_NUDGE_TILES + 1): for ox2 in range(-r, r + 1): for oy2 in range(-r, r + 1): if max(abs(ox2), abs(oy2)) != r: continue c = cost(ox2, oy2) if c is None: continue if _road_share(mask, x0 + ox2, y0 + oy2, avoid) <= ROAD_SHARE_MAX: if found is None or c[1] < found[0]: found = (c[1], ox2, oy2) if found: ox, oy = found[1], found[2] break return x0 + ox, y0 + oy

nodes.name: cost
nodes.body_text: def cost(ox, oy): ax0, ay0 = x0 + ox, y0 + oy cx0, cy0 = max(0, ax0), max(0, ay0) cx1, cy1 = min(map_w, ax0 + w), min(map_h, ay0 + h) if cx1 <= cx0 or cy1 <= cy0: return None m = mask[cy0 - ay0:cy1 - ay0, cx0 - ax0:cx1 - ax0] return (int(avoid[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1][m].sum()), int(occupied[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1][m].sum()))

nodes.name: place
nodes.signature: def place(px: list[tuple[float, float]], occupied: np.ndarray, min_side: float = 0, max_side: float = 1e9, snap_degrees: float = SNAP_DEGREES, avoid: np.ndarray | None = None, lots: np.ndarray | None = None, alignment: str = "smart" ) -> tuple[Footprint | None, str]
nodes.body_text: def place(px: list[tuple[float, float]], occupied: np.ndarray, min_side: float = 0, max_side: float = 1e9, snap_degrees: float = SNAP_DEGREES, avoid: np.ndarray | None = None, lots: np.ndarray | None = None, alignment: str = "smart" ) -> tuple[Footprint | None, str]: """Rasterise a projected footprint, claiming its tiles in `occupied`. Returns the footprint and why not when there is none: "small", "large", "outside" or "taken". Size is judged on the real building's sides, before anything is claimed, so a rejected building never blocks its neighbours. Tiles another building already owns are left to it. Real neighbours share walls; two buildings claiming the same tile would put one wall inside the other. `lots` is the ground already covered by a building's lot rectangle rather than by its tiles (_clear_box). Passed in, the footprint is cut back until its own rectangle stands clear of every other, and its rectangle is claimed there in turn. """ map_h, map_w = occupied.shape poly = _polygon(px) if poly.is_empty or poly.area <= 0: return None, "small" rect = poly.minimum_rotated_rectangle c = list(rect.exterior.coords) if hasattr(rect, "exterior") else [] if len(c) >= 4: sides = sorted((math.dist(c[0], c[1]), math.dist(c[1], c[2]))) else: minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds sides = sorted((maxx - minx, maxy - miny)) if sides[0] < min_side: return None, "small" if sides[1] > max_side: return None, "large" angle = grid_angle(poly, rect) rectangular = rect.area > 0 and poly.area / rect.area >= RECTANGULAR_ENOUGH point_origin = (poly.centroid.x, poly.centroid.y) point_rotation = 0.0 if alignment not in BUILDING_ALIGNMENT_OPTIONS: alignment = "smart" box_alignment = alignment == "rectangle" or ( alignment == "smart" and angle <= snap_degrees and (rectangular or snap_degrees >= 30)) rectilinear_alignment = (alignment == "rectilinear" or (alignment == "smart" and not box_alignment and angle <= snap_degrees and not rectangular)) if rectilinear_alignment: point_rotation = _orthogonal_rotation(poly, rect) poly = rectilinearize_polygon(poly) # Rectangle discards nonrectangular details; Smart only boxes near-grid # footprints that are already close to rectangular. if box_alignment: point_rotation = _orthogonal_rotation(poly, rect) # Square it up: an upright rectangle of the true side lengths, centred. cx, cy = poly.centroid.x, poly.centroid.y horizontal = (angle == 0.0 and (poly.bounds[2] - poly.bounds[0]) >= (poly.bounds[3] - poly.bounds[1])) if len(c) >= 4: dx = abs(c[1][0] - c[0][0]) + abs(c[2][0] - c[1][0]) dy = abs(c[1][1] - c[0][1]) + abs(c[2][1] - c[1][1]) horizontal = dx >= dy w, h = (sides[1], sides[0]) if horizontal else (sides[0], sides[1]) w, h = max(1, int(round(w))), max(1, int(round(h))) x0 = int(round(cx - w / 2)) y0 = int(round(cy - h / 2)) mask = np.ones((h, w), dtype=bool) else: minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds x0, y0 = int(math.floor(minx)), int(math.floor(miny)) x1, y1 = int(math.ceil(maxx)), int(math.ceil(maxy)) xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1) + 0.5, np.arange(y0, y1) + 0.5) mask = shapely.contains_xy(poly, xs, ys) before_nudge = (x0, y0) if avoid is not None: x0, y0 = _clear_of(mask, x0, y0, avoid, occupied) point_offset = (x0 - before_nudge[0], y0 - before_nudge[1]) if avoid is not None: if _road_share(mask, x0, y0, avoid) > ROAD_SHARE_MAX: return None, "road" # What little is left on the road is cut away: no room stands on the carriageway. map_h2, map_w2 = avoid.shape h2, w2 = mask.shape cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1 = max(0, x0), max(0, y0), min(map_w2, x0 + w2), min(map_h2, y0 + h2) if cx1 > cx0 and cy1 > cy0: mask = mask.copy() mask[cy0 - y0:cy1 - y0, cx0 - x0:cx1 - x0] &= ~(avoid[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1] >= ROAD_WEIGHT) # Clip to the map, then give up tiles already owned by a neighbour. h, w = mask.shape cx0, cy0 = max(0, x0), max(0, y0) cx1, cy1 = min(map_w, x0 + w), min(map_h, y0 + h) if cx1 <= cx0 or cy1 <= cy0: return None, "outside" mask = mask[cy0 - y0:cy1 - y0, cx0 - x0:cx1 - x0].copy() mask &= ~occupied[cy0:cy1, cx0:cx1] if mask.sum() < MIN_TILES: return None, "taken" # Trim empty rows and columns so the box hugs what is left. mask, fx0, fy0 = _hug(mask, cx0, cy0) if mask.sum() < MIN_TILES: return None, "taken" # ...and cut it back again where the box that hugs it would stand on a # lot already placed, even though the tiles under it are free. if lots is not None: blocked = lots[fy0:fy0 + mask.shape[0], fx0:fx0 + mask.shape[1]] if blocked.any(): by0, by1, bx0, bx1 = _clear_box(mask, blocked) mask, fx0, fy0 = _hug(mask[by0:by1, bx0:bx1], fx0 + bx0, fy0 + by0) if mask.sum() < MIN_TILES: return None, "taken" occupied[fy0:fy0 + mask.shape[0], fx0:fx0 + mask.shape[1]] |= mask if lots is not None: lots[fy0:fy0 + mask.shape[0], fx0:fx0 + mask.shape[1]] = True return Footprint(fx0, fy0, mask, angle, sides[0], sides[1], point_origin, point_rotation, point_offset), "ok"

nodes.name: furnish_rules.py
nodes.body_text: """Furnishing rules: what matters most in a room, where people walk, and whether a new piece would cut the free floor in two. No import of layout.""" import heapq from collections import deque ESSENTIAL, SECONDARY, DECORATION = 0, 1, 2 DECORATION_ROLES = ( "plant", "erika_plant", "lamp", "shelf", "bookshelf", "erika_shelves", "painting", "mirror", "erika_art", "erika_ad", "rug", "shag_rug", "bath_mat", "corkboard", "bin", "box", "hamper", "coat_rack", "sale_sign", "door_mat") _KITCHEN = ("fridge", "stove", "kitchen_sink", "counter") _BED = ("double_bed", "bed", "bunk_bed") ESSENTIALS = { "bathroom": ("toilet", "sink", "bath", "shower"), "kitchen": _KITCHEN, "openplan": _KITCHEN + ("sofa",), "livingroom": ("sofa",), "bedroom": _BED, "kidsbedroom": _BED, "motelroom": _BED, "laundry": ("washer",), "dining": ("dining_table", "round_table"), "closet": ("wardrobe",), } _WALKWAYS: dict = {}

nodes.name: priority
nodes.body_text: def priority(role, room_kind): """0 essential, 1 secondary, 2 decoration. Decoration is checked first so bath_mat is never read as bath.""" if role.startswith(DECORATION_ROLES): return DECORATION if role.startswith(ESSENTIALS.get(room_kind, ())): return ESSENTIAL return SECONDARY

nodes.name: in_priority_order
nodes.body_text: def in_priority_order(roles, room_kind): return sorted(roles, key=lambda r: priority(r, room_kind))

nodes.name: _near
nodes.body_text: def _near(t): x, y = t return ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1))

nodes.name: _depth
nodes.body_text: def _depth(cells): """1 for a tile with a 4-neighbour outside cells, +1 per step inward.""" depth = {t: 1 for t in cells if any(n not in cells for n in _near(t))} todo = deque(sorted(depth)) while todo: t = todo.popleft() for n in _near(t): if n in cells and n not in depth: depth[n] = depth[t] + 1 todo.append(n) return depth

nodes.name: _path
nodes.body_text: def _path(cells, depth, sources, goal): """Cheapest path from any source until goal(tile) is first popped: fewest tiles, ties away from walls. Returns the path tiles (source excluded from cost, included in the list), or None. A cost is tiles << 20 plus the wall tiles among them: one int sorts as the pair did, and faster.""" best = {s: 0 for s in sources} parent = {} heap = [(0, y, x) for x, y in sources] heapq.heapify(heap) pop, push, step = heapq.heappop, heapq.heappush, 1 << 20 while heap: cost, y, x = pop(heap) t = (x, y) if cost != best[t]: continue if t not in sources and goal(t): path = [t] while path[-1] in parent: path.append(parent[path[-1]]) return path for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): d = depth.get(n) # depth has a value for every tile of cells if d is None: continue c = cost + step + (d == 1) b = best.get(n) if b is None or c < b: best[n] = c parent[n] = t push(heap, (c, n[1], n[0])) return None

nodes.name: walkway
nodes.body_text: def walkway(cells, entries): """Tiles that stay free: a path joining the room's ways in, or for a single way in a spine to the farthest tile that is off every wall, where the floor off the walls is at least two tiles across. Remembered by room and ways in: the window pass asks again for most rooms the furnishing already asked about, and a mall's concourse costs a search per shop door.""" terminals = sorted({e for e in entries if e in cells}) if not terminals: return set() key = (frozenset(cells), tuple(terminals)) if key not in _WALKWAYS: if len(_WALKWAYS) > 512: # ponytail: crude cap, an LRU if it ever matters _WALKWAYS.clear() _WALKWAYS[key] = frozenset(_walkway(cells, terminals)) return set(_WALKWAYS[key])

nodes.name: _walkway
nodes.body_text: def _walkway(cells, terminals): depth = _depth(cells) if len(terminals) == 1: start = terminals[0] steps = {start: 0} todo = deque([start]) while todo: t = todo.popleft() for n in _near(t): if n in cells and n not in steps: steps[n] = steps[t] + 1 todo.append(n) inner = {t for t in steps if depth[t] >= 2} # Only where the inner floor is two tiles across: a spine down the one # inner row of a three-wide room left nothing two deep (a double bed) # room on either side, and 117 of 176 such bedrooms lost their bed. inner = [(x, y) for x, y in inner if {(x + 1, y), (x - 1, y)} & inner and {(x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)} & inner] if not inner: return {start} target = min(inner, key=lambda t: (-steps[t], t[1], t[0])) return set(_path(cells, depth, {start}, lambda t: t == target)) tree = {terminals[0]} pending = set(terminals[1:]) while pending: path = _path(cells, depth, tree, pending.__contains__) if path is None: # unreachable (split cells): leave the rest out break tree.update(path) pending -= tree return tree

nodes.name: keeps_floor_open
nodes.signature: def keeps_floor_open(cells, blocked, walk, new, pocket)
nodes.body_text: def keeps_floor_open(cells, blocked, walk, new, pocket): """True if placing `new` leaves the walkway untouched and the cut-off patches of free floor hold at most `pocket` tiles between them. Counted one patch at a time, a dresser that shut a bedroom off from its doorway passed: it left pockets of 2, 2 and 1 behind.""" if new & walk: return False free = cells - blocked - new seen, comps = set(), [] for start in sorted(free): if start in seen: continue comp, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: for n in _near(todo.pop()): if n in free and n not in comp: comp.add(n) todo.append(n) seen |= comp comps.append(comp) if not comps: return True anchor = walk & free if anchor: main = min(anchor) keep = next(c for c in comps if main in c) else: keep = max(comps, key=len) # comps are in min-tile order: ties go to the smallest return sum(len(c) for c in comps if c is not keep) <= pocket

nodes.name: OpenFloor
nodes.body_text: class OpenFloor: """keeps_floor_open for one room as its pieces go in. The free floor's patches are kept as pieces are put down (block), and both a piece put down and a query flood the room only when the new tiles might cut a patch in two: when the free tiles beside them do not join up through the free ring of tiles about them. The answers are keeps_floor_open's, so a seed lays out the same room.""" def __init__(self, cells, walk, pocket): self.cells, self.walk, self.pocket = cells, walk, pocket self.blocked = set() self.free = None def block(self, tiles): tiles = set(tiles) - self.blocked if not tiles: return self.blocked |= tiles if self.free is None: return gone = tiles & self.free if gone & self.walk or self._splits(gone, tiles): self.free = None return self.free -= gone for t in gone: n = self.patch.pop(t) self.size[n] -= 1 if n != self.keep: self.off -= 1 def _splits(self, gone, new): """Whether taking `new` off the free floor might cut a patch in two.""" free = self.free edge = {n for t in gone for n in _near(t) if n in free and n not in new} if not edge: return False ring = {(x + dx, y + dy) for x, y in gone for dx in (-1, 0, 1) for dy in (-1, 0, 1)} & free ring -= new start = min(edge) seen, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: for t in _near(todo.pop()): if t in ring and t not in seen: seen.add(t) todo.append(t) return not edge <= seen def _patches(self): self.free = free = self.cells - self.blocked self.patch, self.size = {}, [] for start in sorted(free): if start in self.patch: continue n = len(self.size) self.patch[start], todo, k = n, [start], 1 while todo: for t in _near(todo.pop()): if t in free and t not in self.patch: self.patch[t] = n todo.append(t) k += 1 self.size.append(k) anchor = self.walk & free self.keep = self.patch[min(anchor)] if anchor else None self.off = sum(k for n, k in enumerate(self.size) if n != self.keep) def keeps_open(self, new): new = set(new) if new & self.walk: return False if self.free is None: self._patches() if self.keep is None: return keeps_floor_open(self.cells, self.blocked, self.walk, new, self.pocket) gone = new & self.free if not gone: return self.off <= self.pocket if self._splits(gone, new): return keeps_floor_open(self.cells, self.blocked, self.walk, new, self.pocket) # No patch is cut in two: each one the new tiles touch just shrinks. return self.off - sum(self.patch[t] != self.keep for t in gone) <= self.pocket

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.body_text: def __init__(self, cells, walk, pocket): self.cells, self.walk, self.pocket = cells, walk, pocket self.blocked = set() self.free = None

nodes.name: block
nodes.body_text: def block(self, tiles): tiles = set(tiles) - self.blocked if not tiles: return self.blocked |= tiles if self.free is None: return gone = tiles & self.free if gone & self.walk or self._splits(gone, tiles): self.free = None return self.free -= gone for t in gone: n = self.patch.pop(t) self.size[n] -= 1 if n != self.keep: self.off -= 1

nodes.name: _splits
nodes.body_text: def _splits(self, gone, new): """Whether taking `new` off the free floor might cut a patch in two.""" free = self.free edge = {n for t in gone for n in _near(t) if n in free and n not in new} if not edge: return False ring = {(x + dx, y + dy) for x, y in gone for dx in (-1, 0, 1) for dy in (-1, 0, 1)} & free ring -= new start = min(edge) seen, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: for t in _near(todo.pop()): if t in ring and t not in seen: seen.add(t) todo.append(t) return not edge <= seen

nodes.name: _patches
nodes.body_text: def _patches(self): self.free = free = self.cells - self.blocked self.patch, self.size = {}, [] for start in sorted(free): if start in self.patch: continue n = len(self.size) self.patch[start], todo, k = n, [start], 1 while todo: for t in _near(todo.pop()): if t in free and t not in self.patch: self.patch[t] = n todo.append(t) k += 1 self.size.append(k) anchor = self.walk & free self.keep = self.patch[min(anchor)] if anchor else None self.off = sum(k for n, k in enumerate(self.size) if n != self.keep)

nodes.name: keeps_open
nodes.body_text: def keeps_open(self, new): new = set(new) if new & self.walk: return False if self.free is None: self._patches() if self.keep is None: return keeps_floor_open(self.cells, self.blocked, self.walk, new, self.pocket) gone = new & self.free if not gone: return self.off <= self.pocket if self._splits(gone, new): return keeps_floor_open(self.cells, self.blocked, self.walk, new, self.pocket) # No patch is cut in two: each one the new tiles touch just shrinks. return self.off - sum(self.patch[t] != self.keep for t in gone) <= self.pocket

nodes.name: guns.py
nodes.body_text: """One military rifle, somewhere, whatever the map turned out to be. Knox County is a county under martial law: there are checkpoints on the roads, an army surplus store, a gun shop in most towns and a police armoury, and the game's loot tables lean on all of them. A real town does not have any of that. Generate Reading, or Antalya, or a Dutch suburb, and the map may contain no army building at all and no gun shop, so `Base.AssaultRifle` - the M16, which spawns from army and police loot and almost nowhere else - has no container on the whole map it could ever appear in. Players read that as the map being broken rather than as the town being peaceful. So one is placed by hand. Where it goes follows what the map actually has: an army building, if the map has one - a barracks, an armoury, a bunker the police station, whose gun locker is where the town's rifles were the gun shop, if somebody mapped one a house out on the edge of town, as the survivor who had it The choice is written to <map>_guncache.json and shipped as a Lua file with the mod (knoxbuild/lua/guncache.lua), which puts the rifle into the first container the game fills inside that building and then never does it again. It has to be done at fill time rather than baked into the .tbx, because a .tbx has walls, floors and furniture in it and no items: what is inside a container is rolled by the game the first time anybody walks in. """ from __future__ import annotations import math import os import knoxfiles # The M16 and enough to fire it. Checked against the game's own scripts: # AssaultRifle takes MagazineType Base.556Clip and AmmoType base:bullets_556 # (media/scripts/generated/items/weapon.txt). ITEMS = ["Base.AssaultRifle", "Base.556Clip", "Base.556Clip", "Base.556Box"] # Where to look, best first. A kind from the placements CSV; "gunshop" is not # a kind but a use, and is matched separately. PRIORITY = ("military", "police", "gunshop", "house") # A survivor's house is on the edge of town, not in the middle of the high # street: of the houses big enough to be worth the walk, the one furthest out. # This is the share of houses, by size, considered at all. SURVIVOR_TOP_SHARE = 0.25 SURVIVOR_MIN_HOUSES = 8

nodes.name: _centre
nodes.body_text: def _centre(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float]: if not rows: return 0.0, 0.0 xs = sum(r["tile_x"] + r["width"] / 2 for r in rows) / len(rows) ys = sum(r["tile_y"] + r["height"] / 2 for r in rows) / len(rows) return xs, ys

nodes.name: _biggest
nodes.body_text: def _biggest(candidates: list[dict]) -> dict: """The largest, and the same one every time two are the same size.""" return max(candidates, key=lambda r: (r["width"] * r["height"], r["file"]))

nodes.name: _survivor
nodes.body_text: def _survivor(rows: list[dict]) -> dict | None: """A house on the edge of town, big enough to be somebody's home.""" houses = [r for r in rows if r["kind"] in ("house", "apartment")] if not houses: return None houses.sort(key=lambda r: (-(r["width"] * r["height"]), r["file"])) top = houses[:max(SURVIVOR_MIN_HOUSES, int(len(houses) * SURVIVOR_TOP_SHARE))] cx, cy = _centre(rows) return max(top, key=lambda r: ( math.dist((r["tile_x"] + r["width"] / 2, r["tile_y"] + r["height"] / 2), (cx, cy)), r["file"]))

nodes.name: choose
nodes.signature: def choose(rows: list[dict], gunshops: set[str]) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def choose(rows: list[dict], gunshops: set[str]) -> dict | None: """The building to put the rifle in, or None when there is nowhere at all. `rows` is the placements the build just made; `gunshops` the file names of the buildings OSM said sell weapons. """ if not rows: return None for want in PRIORITY: if want == "gunshop": here = [r for r in rows if r["file"] in gunshops] elif want == "house": pick = _survivor(rows) here = [pick] if pick else [] else: here = [r for r in rows if r["kind"] == want] if here: return dict(_biggest(here) if want != "house" else here[0], _found_as=want) # No army base, no station, no gun shop and no house: a map of nothing but # warehouses still gets one, in the biggest thing standing. return dict(_biggest(rows), _found_as="any")

nodes.name: write
nodes.signature: def write(out_dir: str, map_name: str, pick: dict | None, world_origin: tuple[int, int], cell_size: int) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def write(out_dir: str, map_name: str, pick: dict | None, world_origin: tuple[int, int], cell_size: int) -> dict | None: """Record the choice in world coordinates, for the mod builder to ship. The tile coordinates in `rows` are this map's own; the game knows the map by where it was placed in the world (knoxbuild/world.py), so they are moved by the origin here, once, rather than everywhere that reads them. """ path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_guncache.json") if pick is None: try: os.remove(path) # a rebuild that found nowhere leaves nothing except OSError: pass return None ox, oy = world_origin[0] * cell_size, world_origin[1] * cell_size out = { "map": map_name, "kind": pick.get("_found_as", pick.get("kind")), "building": pick["file"], "name": pick.get("name") or "", "x": int(ox + pick["tile_x"]), "y": int(oy + pick["tile_y"]), "w": int(pick["width"]), "h": int(pick["height"]), "items": ITEMS, } knoxfiles.write(path, out, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) return out

nodes.name: hospitals.py
nodes.body_text: """HIFLD hospital identity: how a real facility shapes its game building. The knoxdata layer writes a facility's fields onto the OSM building's tags (hifld_beds, hifld_type, hifld_status, helipad). This turns them into the numbers the builder uses: a size class, a medical occupancy scale and loot scale, and whether the place is closed. The room-mix table is data (knoxdata/data/hospital_types.json), the same one DATASETS.md documents. """ from __future__ import annotations import json from pathlib import Path _DATA = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "knoxdata" / "data" / "hospital_types.json") # A 200-bed hospital holds several times the people a generic medical # building does; clamp so a bad field cannot empty the map. MAX_OCCUPANCY = 4.0 CLOSED_OCCUPANCY = 0.25

nodes.name: _types
nodes.body_text: def _types() -> dict: try: with open(_DATA, encoding="utf-8") as fh: table = json.load(fh) except (OSError, ValueError): return {} return table if isinstance(table, dict) else {}

nodes.name: _int
nodes.body_text: def _int(value) -> int: try: return max(0, int(float(value))) except (TypeError, ValueError): return 0

nodes.name: is_hospital
nodes.body_text: def is_hospital(tags) -> bool: tags = tags or {} return (str(tags.get("healthcare") or "").lower() == "hospital" or str(tags.get("amenity") or "").lower() == "hospital")

nodes.name: profile
nodes.body_text: def profile(tags) -> dict | None: """Per-building numbers from HIFLD tags, or None when it is not one.""" tags = tags or {} if not is_hospital(tags): return None beds = _int(tags.get("hifld_beds")) staff = _int(tags.get("hifld_staff")) kind = str(tags.get("hifld_type") or "").strip().upper() status = str(tags.get("hifld_status") or "").strip().upper() table = _types() return { "beds": beds, "staff": staff, "type": kind, "mix": table.get(kind) or table.get("") or "generalacute", "status": status, "closed": status == "CLOSED", "helipad": str(tags.get("helipad") or "").lower() == "yes", "occupancy": round(min(MAX_OCCUPANCY, max(0.5, (beds + staff) / 400.0)), 3), "loot": round(min(3.0, max(0.5, 0.5 + beds / 400.0)), 3), }

nodes.name: occupancy_kind
nodes.signature: def occupancy_kind(kind: str, prof: dict | None) -> str
nodes.body_text: def occupancy_kind(kind: str, prof: dict | None) -> str: """Encode the medical occupancy scale in the kind the spawn map reads. ``medical:2.5`` / ``medical:closed`` are understood by knoxbuild/population.occupants; every other kind is left alone. """ if not prof or kind != "medical": return kind if prof.get("closed"): return "medical:closed" return f"medical:{prof.get('occupancy', 1.0)}"

nodes.name: interiors.py
nodes.body_text: """Shops, offices and homes furnished the way Knox County's own are. A room used to be furnished from a wishlist pushed against its walls, so a grocery was a ring of bookcases round an empty floor and an office a table and a chair - and since every flat drew on the same sofa, bed and wardrobe, a block of flats was one flat repeated. What the game's own buildings do instead, read off their compiled rooms (tools/building_stats.py and renders of Muldraugh, West Point and Louisville): - a shop's sales floor has rows of shelving standing out into the room, their ends to the shop front so you see down the aisles from the door, shelves or fridges along the other walls, and a counter with the till just inside the door; clothes shops have rails in rows and mannequins in the window; - an office is desks with their chairs in rows, filing cabinets along a wall, a water cooler and a board on the wall; - a home's living room is a sofa facing the television across a coffee table, a bedroom a bed with its head to the wall between bedside tables, and the furniture differs from home to home. """ from __future__ import annotations import random from . import catalog as C OPPOSITE = {"N": "S", "S": "N", "W": "E", "E": "W"} STEP = {"N": (0, -1), "S": (0, 1), "W": (-1, 0), "E": (1, 0)} # What each kind of shop is fitted with. "rows" stand in the middle, one piece # after another in lines running back from the shop front; "wall" goes along # the side walls, "back" along the wall facing the front; "front" stands just # inside the shop front; "counter" is the till counter by the door. STORES = { "grocery": {"rows": "shop_aisle", "wall": ["shop_shelf", "shop_shelf_white"], "tills": 2, "back_counter": "shop_counter", "back": ["shop_fridge_open", "shop_fridge_double", "shop_freezer"], "counter": "shop_counter", "front": ["shop_bin"]}, "conveniencestore": {"rows": "shop_aisle", "wall": ["shop_shelf_red", "shop_fridge"], "back": ["shop_fridge", "shop_fridge", "shop_fridge_double"], "counter": "shop_counter_red", "front": ["vending", "vending_snacks"], "produce": 2}, "generalstore": {"rows": "shop_aisle", "wall": ["shop_shelf_wood", "shop_shelf"], "back": ["shop_shelf", "shop_fridge_double"], "counter": "shop_counter", "front": ["shop_bin"]}, "liquorstore": {"rows": "shop_aisle", "wall": ["shop_shelf_wood"], "back": ["shop_fridge", "shop_fridge_white"], "counter": "shop_counter", "front": []}, "pharmacy": {"rows": "shop_aisle", "wall": ["shop_shelf_white"], "back_counter": "shop_counter", "back": ["shop_display", "shop_shelf_white"], "counter": "shop_counter", "front": ["shop_case"]}, "clothingstore": {"rows": "clothes_rack", "wall": ["clothes_rack", "shop_shelf_wood"], "back": ["shop_shelf_wood", "mirror"], "counter": "shop_counter", "front": ["mannequin", "mannequin_male", "mannequin_dark"]}, "bookstore": {"rows": "bookcases", "wall": ["bookshelf"], "back": ["bookshelf"], "nook": True, "counter": "shop_counter", "front": []}, "toolstore": {"rows": "metal_rack", "wall": ["metal_rack", "shop_shelf_wood"], "back": ["metal_rack"], "counter": "shop_display", "front": ["shop_bin"]}, } # Pieces that stand against a wall on any side, used where a piece above only # has north and west sprites and the wall is a south or east one. # The other shops OpenStreetMap names (knoxbuild/uses.py), fitted out like # one of the above with a few pieces of their own. _LIKE = { "giftstore": ("generalstore", {"front": ["plant"]}), "toystore": ("generalstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf", "bookshelf"]}), "candystore": ("conveniencestore", {"front": ["shop_case"]}), # A forecourt shop: the drinks coolers along the back wall, snack shelving # down the sides and in short aisles, the counter by the door where the # cashier can see the pumps. Coolers on every wall was a cold room. "gasstore": ("conveniencestore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf_red", "shop_shelf_red", "shop_fridge"], "front": ["vending", "vending_snacks"], "produce": 1}), "butcher": ("grocery", {"back_counter": "shop_counter", "rows": "shop_display_butcher", "back": ["shop_fridge_double", "shop_freezer"]}), "bakery": ("generalstore", {"back_counter": "shop_counter", "rows": "shop_display_bakery", "back": ["shop_shelf_white"], "front": ["shop_case"]}), "departmentstore": ("clothingstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf", "clothes_rack"]}), "sportstore": ("clothingstore", {"wall": ["metal_rack", "shop_shelf"], "front": ["mannequin_male"]}), "jewelrystore": ("pharmacy", {"rows": "shop_display", "wall": ["shop_case"], "front": ["mirror"]}), "camerastore": ("pharmacy", {"rows": "shop_display", "wall": ["shop_shelf_white"]}), "musicstore": ("bookstore", {"front": ["shop_case"]}), "movierental": ("bookstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf"]}), "gunstore": ("toolstore", {"rows": "shop_display", "wall": ["metal_rack"]}), "gardenstore": ("toolstore", {"front": ["plant", "plant"], "wall": ["shop_shelf_wood", "plant"]}), "armysurplus": ("toolstore", {"rows": "metal_rack", "wall": ["clothes_rack", "metal_rack"], "front": ["shop_display"]}), "hunting": ("toolstore", {"rows": "metal_rack", "wall": ["clothes_rack", "shop_shelf_wood"], "front": ["shop_display"]}), "artstore": ("generalstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf_wood", "metal_rack"], "front": ["painting"]}), "petstore": ("generalstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf", "shop_shelf_wood"], "front": ["shop_bin"]}), "furniturestore": ("generalstore", {"rows": "bookcases", "wall": ["wardrobe", "dresser", "sofa"], "back": ["double_bed", "wardrobe2"], "front": ["armchair"]}), # The units Knox County's mall is let out to. clothesstore is the game's # own spelling - 158 rooms across the county against 9 for the # clothingstore we were writing - so it carries the better loot table. "clothesstore": ("clothingstore", {}), "shoestore": ("clothingstore", {"rows": "shop_shelf_wood", "wall": ["shop_shelf_wood", "shop_display"], "front": ["mirror"]}), "sewingstore": ("clothingstore", {"rows": "shop_display", "wall": ["shop_shelf_wood"]}), "electronicsstore": ("camerastore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf", "shop_case"]}), "housewarestore": ("generalstore", {"wall": ["shop_shelf_wood", "dresser"]}), "cornerstore": ("conveniencestore", {"produce": 2}), "optometrist": ("pharmacy", {"front": ["mirror"]}), } # Hanging rails: wall fittings, not aisle ones. RACKS = {"clothes_rack", "clothes_rack_small"} # What may stand in an aisle, besides the piece "rows" names. # # Every aisle used to be the same piece, so a supermarket or a mall came out # as a perfectly regular grid of one shelf repeated forty times - "shopping # malls generate repeated patterns of clothing racks and food shelves". Real # shops mix their fittings, and a long aisle changes what it holds partway # along, so the rows are drawn from these instead. AISLE_MIX = { "grocery": ["shop_aisle", "shop_aisle", "shop_shelf"], "conveniencestore": ["shop_aisle", "shop_aisle_red", "shop_shelf_red"], "generalstore": ["shop_aisle", "shop_shelf", "shop_shelf_wood"], "liquorstore": ["shop_aisle", "shop_shelf_wood", "shop_shelf"], "pharmacy": ["shop_aisle", "shop_shelf_white"], "clothingstore": ["shop_shelf_wood", "shop_display", "shop_shelf_wood"], "toolstore": ["metal_rack", "shop_shelf_wood"], } for _kind, _mix in AISLE_MIX.items(): STORES[_kind]["aisles"] = _mix for _kind, (_base, _over) in _LIKE.items(): STORES[_kind] = {**STORES[_base], **_over} # Fresh produce only where it is said: a candy store is not a greengrocer. if "produce" not in _over: STORES[_kind].pop("produce", None) # A shop given rows of its own does not keep the mix it was based on. if "rows" in _over and "aisles" not in _over: STORES[_kind]["aisles"] = [_over["rows"]] ANY_WALL = {"shop_aisle": "shop_shelf", "shop_aisle_red": "shop_shelf_red", "shop_shelf_wood": "shop_shelf", "shop_fridge_open": "shop_fridge_double", "clothes_rack": "shop_shelf", "metal_rack": "shop_shelf", "mirror": "shop_shelf", "shop_display": "shop_counter"} # The shops a ground floor may hold when OpenStreetMap does not say which, # weighted roughly as Knox County's are. STORE_WEIGHTS = {"generalstore": 3, "grocery": 2, "conveniencestore": 3, "clothingstore": 3, "liquorstore": 1, "pharmacy": 2, "bookstore": 1, "toolstore": 1} # Rows of shelving need this much floor, and the rows this much space apart # (the shelf and a two-tile aisle). MIN_SALES_FLOOR = 20 ROW_EVERY = 3 BOOKCASE_ROW_EVERY = 4 CROSS_AISLE_EVERY = 8 # Mannequins, drinks machines or bins inside the shop front, at most. FRONT_PIECES = 3 # Produce stands just inside the door of a grocery: as many as fit, to this. MAX_STANDS = 6 # A bank of coolers takes this share of its wall; display cases, this many rows. BANK_SHARE = 0.6 MAX_CASE_ROWS = 2 OFFICE_DESKS = ["desk", "desk_dark", "desk_long", "desk_long_pale"] # Workstations stand a tile apart along a row, and the rows a tile of aisle # apart; the room's edge is left a tile clear to walk round. STATION_GAP = 1 STATION_AISLE = 1 # A classroom's desks face the board. Students sit at a table two wide with a # chair to each place, in rows with an aisle between; what is left of the # walls is bookshelves and a teacher's desk. CLASS_DESK = [("dining_table", 0, 0, "W"), ("chair", 0, 1, "S"), ("chair", 1, 1, "S")] _TURNED = {"W": "N", "N": "W", "E": "S", "S": "E"} SALON_TILES_PER_CHAIR = 25 # A home's own furniture: one choice per flat (or per storey of a house) for # each of these, so the flat next door has a different sofa, bed, wardrobe and # kitchen. The sofa and armchair come as a matching pair. SOFA_SETS = [("sofa", "armchair")] + [(f"sofa_{i}", f"armchair_{i}") for i in range(1, 15)] CHOICES = { "double_bed": ["double_bed", "double_bed_alt", "double_bed_black"], "bed": ["bed", "bed_alt", "bed_plain"], "wardrobe": ["wardrobe", "wardrobe2", "wardrobe_pale", "wardrobe_black", "wardrobe_oak", "wardrobe_tan"], "dresser": ["dresser", "dresser_alt", "dresser_black", "dresser_tan"], "counter": ["counter"] + [f"counter_{i}" for i in range(1, 8)], # Every kitchen in a town had the same steel double sink and every # bathroom the same white basin, which is what reads as institutional. # Vanilla spreads across nine sets; these are the ones whose facings we # could confirm off the map itself. "sink": ["sink", "sink_cream"], "kitchen_sink": ["kitchen_sink", "kitchen_sink_steel", "kitchen_sink_dark"], } # A home's wooden furniture is all one wood. The palette above picks the # wardrobe, dresser and beds on their own, and the bookcase, tables and # bedside chest were the same for everyone, so one bedroom had a black table, # dark dressers and a pale bookcase. A house gets one wood throughout; a # block of flats one per flat. Each kind of piece maps to the one in this # home's wood; a kind a wood has no piece for is left as it is. # # A piece only changes to one of the same height (the game's Surface), or a # lamp stood on it floats or sinks: a bedside chest is a 34 chest of drawers # in every wood, never the 15 low table furniture_storage_01 also has. TONE_KIND = { **{r: "wardrobe" for r in CHOICES["wardrobe"]}, **{r: "dresser" for r in CHOICES["dresser"]}, "nightstand": "nightstand", "bookshelf": "bookshelf", "shelf_1": "bookshelf", "shelf_2": "bookshelf", **{r: "double_bed" for r in CHOICES["double_bed"]}, **{r: "bed" for r in CHOICES["bed"]}, "coffee_table": "low_table", "sidetable": "low_table", "dining_table": "dining_table", # The mirrored vanity is light wood: in any other home it is that home's # chest of drawers, the same height. "vanity": "vanity", } TONES = { "white": {"wardrobe": "wardrobe", "dresser": "dresser", "nightstand": "dresser", "vanity": "dresser", "bookshelf": "shelf_2", "low_table": "low_table_white", "dining_table": "dining_table_white", # No bed is white: a painted room has the black metal frame. "double_bed": "double_bed_black", "bed": "bed"}, "light": {"wardrobe": "wardrobe_tan", "dresser": "dresser_tan", "nightstand": "nightstand", "bookshelf": "shelf_2", "low_table": "low_table_tan", "dining_table": "dining_table_oak", "double_bed": "double_bed_alt", "bed": "bed_alt"}, "dark": {"wardrobe": "wardrobe_pale", "dresser": "dresser_alt", "nightstand": "dresser_alt", "vanity": "dresser_alt", "bookshelf": "bookshelf", "double_bed": "double_bed", "bed": "bed_plain"}, "black": {"wardrobe": "wardrobe_black", "dresser": "dresser_black", "nightstand": "dresser_black", "low_table": "low_table_black", "vanity": "dresser_black", "double_bed": "double_bed_black", "bed": "bed", # The game has no black bookcase: a black chest of drawers on # the same tile instead of a dark one in a black room. "bookshelf": "dresser_black"}, } # Dark wood is drawn twice as often as each of the others. L = _layout() counts = {s: 0 for s in STEP} edge = {"N": lambda x, y: (x, y, "N"), "S": lambda x, y: (x, y + 1, "N"), "W": lambda x, y: (x, y, "W"), "E": lambda x, y: (x + 1, y, "W")} for x, y in cells: for s, (dx, dy) in STEP.items(): # A wall shared with the next building is no shop front. if not L._room_at(plan, x + dx, y + dy) and edge[s](x, y) not in plan.party: counts[s] += 1 if street in counts and counts[street] >= 3: return street for x, y, d in plan.doors: for inside, outside, side in (((x, y), (x - 1, y) if d == "W" else (x, y - 1), "W" if d == "W" else "N"), ((x - 1, y) if d == "W" else (x, y - 1), (x, y), "E" if d == "W" else "S")): if inside in cells and not L._room_at(plan, *outside): return side return max(counts, key=lambda s: counts[s])

nodes.name: Frame
nodes.body_text: class Frame: """Room coordinates as (along the front, depth in from the front).""" def __init__(self, cells: set, front: str): self.front = front xs = [x for x, _ in cells] ys = [y for _, y in cells] self.x0, self.x1, self.y0, self.y1 = min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys) self.along_x = front in ("N", "S") self.length = (self.x1 - self.x0 + 1) if self.along_x else (self.y1 - self.y0 + 1) self.depth = (self.y1 - self.y0 + 1) if self.along_x else (self.x1 - self.x0 + 1) def xy(self, a: int, d: int) -> tuple[int, int]: if self.front == "S": return self.x0 + a, self.y1 - d if self.front == "N": return self.x0 + a, self.y0 + d if self.front == "W": return self.x0 + d, self.y0 + a return self.x1 - d, self.y0 + a

L = _layout() cells = _cells(plan, idx, room) if len(cells) < MIN_SALES_FLOOR or min(room.w, room.h) < 6: return False front = _front_side(plan, idx, cells, None) frame = Frame(cells, front) blocked = set(keep_clear) | set(door_tiles) for x, y in door_tiles: if (x, y) in cells: blocked.update((x + dx, y + dy) for dx in (-1, 0, 1) for dy in (-1, 0, 1)) placed: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() def put(role: str, along: int, depth: int, wall: str) -> bool: x, y = frame.xy(along, depth) orient = L._facing(role, wall) got = _fits(plan, idx, role, x, y, orient, blocked | placed) if got is None: return False plan.furniture.append((role, x, y, orient)) placed.update(got) return True left, right = (("W", "E") if frame.along_x else ("N", "S")) for depth in range(4, frame.depth - 2, 4): for along, side in ((0, left), (frame.length - 1, right)): put(rng.choice(("metal_rack", "crate")), along, depth, side) back = OPPOSITE[front] rear_depth = frame.depth - 1 if mechanic: put("counter_2", frame.length // 2, rear_depth, back) for along, role in ((max(1, frame.length // 4), "metal_rack"), (min(frame.length - 2, 3 * frame.length // 4), "crate")): put(role, along, rear_depth, back) return True

nodes.body_text: def furnish_store(plan, idx: int, room, rng: random.Random, door_tiles: set, keep_clear: set, street: str | None) -> bool: """Fit out a shop's sales floor. False if the room is too small to.""" L = _layout() spec = STORES[room.kind] cells = _cells(plan, idx, room) if len(cells) < MIN_SALES_FLOOR: return False front = _front_side(plan, idx, cells, street) frame = Frame(cells, front) blocked = set(keep_clear) # A tile's clearance round every door into the room. for dx, dy in door_tiles: if (dx, dy) in cells: blocked |= {(dx + i, dy + j) for i in (-1, 0, 1) for j in (-1, 0, 1)} placed: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() def put(role, x, y, orient, ring=False) -> bool: got = _fits(plan, idx, role, x, y, orient, blocked | placed) if got is None: return False plan.furniture.append((role, x, y, orient)) placed.update(got) if ring: placed.update((cx + i, cy + j) for cx, cy in got for i in (-1, 0, 1) for j in (-1, 0, 1)) return True # The till counter: just inside the door, in a short run parallel to the # shop front, with its register, and room behind it for the cashier. doors_in = [(x, y) for x, y in door_tiles if (x, y) in cells] front_tiles = [(a, frame.xy(a, 0)) for a in range(frame.length)] door_along = next((a for a, xy in front_tiles if xy in doors_in), frame.length // 2) counter = spec["counter"] back_to = OPPOSITE[front] run = 3 if frame.length >= 9 else 2 # A wide supermarket has more than one till open. tills_wanted = 2 if spec.get("tills", 1) > 1 and frame.length >= 16 else 1 tills = 0 for start in (door_along + 2, door_along - 1 - run, 1, frame.length - run - 1): spots = [frame.xy(start + k, 2) for k in range(run)] orient = L._facing(counter, back_to) if all(_fits(plan, idx, counter, x, y, orient, blocked | placed) for x, y in spots): for x, y in spots: put(counter, x, y, orient) mx, my = spots[len(spots) // 2] plan.furniture.append(("register", mx, my, L._facing("register", back_to))) # The cashier's tile behind, and a tile in front for customers. placed.update(frame.xy(start + k, d) for k in range(-1, run + 1) for d in (1, 3)) tills += 1 if tills >= tills_wanted: break # A service counter along the back wall - the deli, the pharmacist's, the # butcher's - with the staff's tile behind it and the customers' in front. service = spec.get("back_counter") if service and frame.length >= 10 and frame.depth >= 9 and service in C.FURNITURE: orient = L._facing(service, back_to) done = False # As long a counter as the back wall's doors leave room for. for span in (min(6, frame.length // 3), 4, 3): for start in [frame.length - span - 1, 1] + list(range(2, frame.length - span - 1)): spots = [frame.xy(start + k, frame.depth - 3) for k in range(span)] if all(_fits(plan, idx, service, x, y, orient, blocked | placed) for x, y in spots): for x, y in spots: put(service, x, y, orient) placed.update(frame.xy(start + k, d) for k in range(-1, span + 1) for d in (frame.depth - 2, frame.depth - 4)) done = True break if done: break # Along the walls. Each wall is walked tile by tile, fitting one piece after # another so they stand in a line. def fill_wall(side: str, roles: list[str]): if not roles: return # Coolers are not shelves: one kind, side by side along the wall, as in # a real shop, then the rest of the wall is shelving. coolers = [r for r in roles if is_cooler(r)] roles = [r for r in roles if not is_cooler(r)] bank_role = rng.choice(coolers) if coolers else None line = sorted((c for c in cells if L._room_at(plan, c[0] + STEP[side][0], c[1] + STEP[side][1]) != idx), key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1])) on_wall = set(line) ix, iy = STEP[OPPOSITE[side]] def put_on_wall(role, x, y, orient) -> bool: # A cooler is opened, and a shelf is browsed, from the tile in # front of it: that tile must be this room's floor, and it stays # free - no drinks machine in front of a fridge door, no fridge # facing the wall of a notch in the outline. front = [(cx + ix, cy + iy) for cx, cy in L._cells_for(role, x, y, orient)] if any(c not in cells or c in placed for c in front): return False if not put(role, x, y, orient): return False placed.update(front) return True bank_left = (len(line) if not roles else round(len(line) * BANK_SHARE)) if bank_role else 0 k = 0 i = 0 while i < len(line): x, y = line[i] if bank_left <= 0 and not roles: break role = bank_role if bank_left > 0 else roles[k % len(roles)] if role not in C.FURNITURE or side not in C.FURNITURE[role]: role = ANY_WALL.get(role, role) if role not in C.FURNITURE: i += 1 continue orient = side if side in C.FURNITURE[role] else None if orient is None: i += 1 continue # Pieces grow east or south from their anchor; on a south or east # wall the anchor is the piece's own first tile all the same. if _layout()._is_wall_piece(role): if _layout()._wall_edge(x, y, side) not in plan.wall_pieces and \ put(role, x, y, orient): plan.wall_pieces.add(_layout()._wall_edge(x, y, side)) k += 1 i += 1 continue # The whole piece against this wall: past a corner or a doorway # it would stand out into the room. if all(c

nodes.body_text: def fill_wall(side: str, roles: list[str]): if not roles: return # Coolers are not shelves: one kind, side by side along the wall, as in # a real shop, then the rest of the wall is shelving. coolers = [r for r in roles if is_cooler(r)] roles = [r for r in roles if not is_cooler(r)] bank_role = rng.choice(coolers) if coolers else None line = sorted((c for c in cells if L._room_at(plan, c[0] + STEP[side][0], c[1] + STEP[side][1]) != idx), key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1])) on_wall = set(line) ix, iy = STEP[OPPOSITE[side]] def put_on_wall(role, x, y, orient) -> bool: # A cooler is opened, and a shelf is browsed, from the tile in # front of it: that tile must be this room's floor, and it stays # free - no drinks machine in front of a fridge door, no fridge # facing the wall of a notch in the outline. front = [(cx + ix, cy + iy) for cx, cy in L._cells_for(role, x, y, orient)] if any(c not in cells or c in placed for c in front): return False if not put(role, x, y, orient): return False placed.update(front) return True bank_left = (len(line) if not roles else round(len(line) * BANK_SHARE)) if bank_role else 0 k = 0 i = 0 while i < len(line): x, y = line[i] if bank_left <= 0 and not roles: break role = bank_role if bank_left > 0 else roles[k % len(roles)] if role not in C.FURNITURE or side not in C.FURNITURE[role]: role = ANY_WALL.get(role, role) if role not in C.FURNITURE: i += 1 continue orient = side if side in C.FURNITURE[role] else None if orient is None: i += 1 continue # Pieces grow east or south from their anchor; on a south or east # wall the anchor is the piece's own first tile all the same. if _layout()._is_wall_piece(role): if _layout()._wall_edge(x, y, side) not in plan.wall_pieces and \ put(role, x, y, orient): plan.wall_pieces.add(_layout()._wall_edge(x, y, side)) k += 1 i += 1 continue # The whole piece against this wall: past a corner or a doorway # it would stand out into the room. if all(c in on_wall for c in L._cells_for(role, x, y, orient)) and \ put_on_wall(role, x, y, orient): if role == bank_role and bank_left > 0: bank_left -= len(C.FURNITURE[role][orient]) else: k += 1 i += len(C.FURNITURE[role][orient]) else: i += 1

nodes.name: pack_stations
nodes.signature: def pack_stations(plan, idx: int, room, group, occupied: set, keep_clear: set, keeps_open=None, gap: int = STATION_GAP, aisle: int = STATION_AISLE)
nodes.body_text: def pack_stations(plan, idx: int, room, group, occupied: set, keep_clear: set, keeps_open=None, gap: int = STATION_GAP, aisle: int = STATION_AISLE): """Copies of `group` - [(role, dx, dy, orient)] - in rows across the room, stepping round the walkway and doorways, leaving the room's edge clear when that still holds some and its walls otherwise. Returns the rows as [row_y, x, x, ...] of the group's anchors, and the group's measures (gx0, gy0, gw, gh, pieces).""" L = _layout() pieces = [(role, dx, dy, L._facing(role, o)) for role, dx, dy, o in group] shape = [(dx + cx, dy + cy) for role, dx, dy, o in pieces for cx, cy in L._cells_for(role, 0, 0, o)] gx0, gy0 = min(x for x, _ in shape), min(y for _, y in shape) gw = max(x for x, _ in shape) - gx0 + 1 gh = max(y for _, y in shape) - gy0 + 1 solid = {(dx + cx, dy + cy) for role, dx, dy, o in pieces if C.FURNITURE_LAYERS.get(role, "Furniture") == "Furniture" for cx, cy in L._cells_for(role, 0, 0, o)} def clear(ox: int, oy: int) -> bool: cells = {(ox + x, oy + y) for x, y in shape} if any(L._room_at(plan, x, y) != idx or (x, y) in occupied for x, y in cells): return False return not ({(ox + x, oy + y) for x, y in solid} & keep_clear) def station_at(ox: int, oy: int) -> bool: mine = {(ox + x, oy + y) for x, y in solid} if not clear(ox, oy) or (keeps_open and not keeps_open(mine)): return False for role, dx, dy, o in pieces: plan.furniture.append((role, ox + dx, oy + dy, o)) occupied.update((ox + x, oy + y) for x, y in shape) return True def lay(margin: int, shift: int, commit: bool): x_lo, x_hi = room.x0 + margin, room.x1 - margin y_lo, y_hi = room.y0 + margin, room.y1 - margin pitch = gw + gap slack = (x_hi - x_lo + 1 + gap) % pitch out = [] oy = y_lo + shift - gy0 while oy + gy0 + gh - 1 <= y_hi: row = [] ox = x_lo + slack // 2 - gx0 while ox + gx0 + gw - 1 <= x_hi: if (station_at(ox, oy) if commit else clear(ox, oy)): row.append(ox) ox += pitch else: ox += 1 if row: out.append([oy] + row) oy += gh + aisle return out def pack(margin: int): best = max(range(gh + aisle), key=lambda sh: sum(len(r) - 1 for r in lay(margin, sh, False))) return lay(margin, best, True) rows = pack(1) or pack(0) return rows, (gx0, gy0, gw, gh, pieces)
