Clearance that does not touch the path is left out: the second tile in front of a door across a one-tile hall lands in the room beyond, cut off from its walkway. door_tiles keeps it clear all the same.""" r = plan.rooms[idx - 1] if r.is_core or r.is_shaft: return set() cells = {(x, y) for y in range(r.y0, r.y1 + 1) for x in range(r.x0, r.x1 + 1) if plan.grid[y][x] == idx} entries = [] shop = r.kind in SHOP_FLOOR_KINDS() for x, y, d in list(plan.doors) + sorted(plan.open_edge): inside, other = (((x, y), (x - 1, y)) if d == "W" else ((x, y), (x, y - 1))) if inside not in cells: inside, other = other, inside # A shop's customers do not walk to its staff doors: the way through # joins the street to the rest of the sales floor, and the stock room # and office doors open onto whatever aisle is beside them. Counting # them put the walkway along the back wall, where the coolers go. if shop and (x, y, d) in plan.doors and _room_at(plan, *other) and plan.rooms[_room_at(plan, *other) - 1].kind in SHOP_STAFF_ROOMS: continue entries += [(x, y), (x - 1, y) if d == "W" else (x, y - 1)] if stairs is not None: sx, sy, sd = stairs dx, dy = (0, 1) if sd == "N" else (1, 0) entries += [(sx - dx, sy - dy), (sx + dx * STAIR_RUN, sy + dy * STAIR_RUN)] walk = FR.walkway(cells, entries) clear = door_tiles & cells todo = sorted(walk) while todo: x, y = todo.pop() for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if n in clear and n not in walk: walk.add(n) todo.append(n) return walk

nodes.name: _furnish
nodes.signature: def _furnish(plan: Plan, rng: random.Random, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None, street: str | None = None) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _furnish(plan: Plan, rng: random.Random, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None, street: str | None = None) -> None: """Push furniture against room walls, skipping tiles a door needs clear. Every room, the corridor and stair hall included, first gets a light switch on the wall beside its door. The game hangs a room's ceiling light off its switch, so a room without one has no light at all - which is why so many rooms were pitch dark: the switch was only on some rooms' wishlists, and even there it was written to the floor rather than a wall. """ door_tiles = _door_tiles(plan) door_edges = set(plan.doors) | set(plan.open_edge) # The lift doors take their stretch of wall: nothing hangs on it. for _rect, (lx, ly, ld) in plan.shafts: door_edges |= {(lx, ly + i, "W") if ld == "W" else (lx + i, ly, "N") for i in range(SHAFT_SIZE)} # Tiles of the flight. A switch hung there would be deleted along with the # furniture cleared off the staircase, leaving the stair hall dark. stair_tiles: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() if stairs is not None: sx, sy, sd = stairs dx, dy = (0, 1) if sd == "N" else (1, 0) stair_tiles = {(sx + dx * i, sy + dy * i) for i in range(STAIR_RUN)} for _rect, (lx, ly, ld) in plan.shafts: plan.furniture.append(("elevator_door", lx, ly, ld)) from .. import interiors # Each home its own furniture: one palette per flat, or per storey of a # house, drawn from a seed of this storey's own. home_seed = rng.random() palettes: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {} # Who lives in each home (interiors.household), and which of its rooms # are a child's so far, for a teenager to be given one. households: dict[int, dict] = {} kid_rooms: dict[int, int] = {} for idx, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, start=1): # A lift car has no switch and no furniture: it is a sealed box. if r.is_shaft: continue start = len(plan.furniture) # Walls this room has, as (x, y, facing) for a piece standing on the # tile with its back to that wall. slots = [] for y in range(r.y0, r.y1 + 1): for x in range(r.x0, r.x1 + 1): if plan.grid[y][x] != idx or (x, y) in stair_tiles: continue for facing, nx, ny in (("N", x, y - 1), ("S", x, y + 1), ("W", x - 1, y), ("E", x + 1, y)): if _room_at(plan, nx, ny) != idx: slots.append((x, y, facing)) used_walls: set[tuple[int, int, str]] = set() # Outside walls are where the windows go, and the windows are laid out # last, in columns up the facade: a painting or switch hung there took # the bay and left a hole in the column. Hang things inside first. step = {"N": (0, -1), "S": (0, 1), "W": (-1, 0), "E": (1, 0)} def on_facade(slot: tuple[int, int, str]) -> bool: x, y, facing = slot ox, oy = step[facing] return not _room_at(plan, x + ox, y + oy) def hang(role: str, x: int, y: int, facing: str) -> bool: if role in NORTH_WEST_ONLY and facing in ("S", "E"): return False edge = _wall_edge(x, y, facing) if edge in door_edges or edge in used_walls: return False orient = _facing(role, facing) # Every tile of the piece in this room: a two-tile mirror hung at # the end of a wall reached through the outside wall. if any(_room_at(plan, cx, cy) != idx for cx, cy in _cells_for(role, x, y, orient)): return False plan.furniture.append((role, x, y, orient)) used_walls.add(edge) plan.wall_pieces.add(edge) return True # The switch: on a wall one tile from this room's door, the way people # actually fit them, or on any wall if the door is awkward. mine = [(x, y) for x, y in door_tiles if _room_at(plan, x, y) == idx] by_reach = sorted( slots, key=lambda s: min((abs(s[0] - dx) + abs(s[1] - dy) for dx, dy in mine), default=0) + (4 if on_facade(s) else 0)) # The game hangs one ceiling light off each switch, and that light # only reaches so far, so a sales floor or a warehouse lit by the one # switch beside its door was dark everywhere else - "lighting seems # somewhat broken". A big room gets a switch every so often, spread # out along its walls, the way a real shop is wired. # Every room keeps one. The game lights a room from the switch in # it, so a room without one is dark whatever the sprite count says - # tools/audit_layouts.py fails a plan for it. Thinning these out to # match Knox County's 0.12 per 10 m2 left 1,945 rooms unlit, and it # was chasing the wrong thing anyway: the round fittings that read as # clocks were school_desk, not these. floor_switch = 1 want_switches = max(floor_switch, min(MAX_SWITCHES, r.area // LIGHT_EVERY_TILES)) lit: list[tuple[int, int]] = [] for x, y, facing in by_reach: if len(lit) >= want_switches: break if (x, y) in mine and _wall_edge(x, y, facing) in door_edges: continue if lit and min(abs(x - lx) + abs(y - ly) for lx, ly in lit) < SWITCHES_APART: continue if hang(SWITCH, x, y, facing): lit.append((x, y)) if not lit and want_switches: for x, y, facing in by_reach: if hang(SWITCH, x, y, facing): break # The walkway: a path joining this room's ways in, or a spine from its # one door, that nothing standing may cover. Placed round it rather # than cleared afterwards, which deleted toilets and beds alo

nodes.name: on_facade
nodes.signature: def on_facade(slot: tuple[int, int, str]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def on_facade(slot: tuple[int, int, str]) -> bool: x, y, facing = slot ox, oy = step[facing] return not _room_at(plan, x + ox, y + oy)

nodes.name: hang
nodes.signature: def hang(role: str, x: int, y: int, facing: str) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def hang(role: str, x: int, y: int, facing: str) -> bool: if role in NORTH_WEST_ONLY and facing in ("S", "E"): return False edge = _wall_edge(x, y, facing) if edge in door_edges or edge in used_walls: return False orient = _facing(role, facing) # Every tile of the piece in this room: a two-tile mirror hung at # the end of a wall reached through the outside wall. if any(_room_at(plan, cx, cy) != idx for cx, cy in _cells_for(role, x, y, orient)): return False plan.furniture.append((role, x, y, orient)) used_walls.add(edge) plan.wall_pieces.add(edge) return True

nodes.name: keeps_open
nodes.body_text: def keeps_open(tiles) -> bool: """Whether a new blocking piece on `tiles` leaves the walkway clear and cuts off no patch of floor bigger than a pocket. Only this room's pieces have gone in since `start`, and only by appending (_stand_on_something inserts once the room is done).""" for role, x, y, o in plan.furniture[counted[0]:]: if _blocks(role): floor.block(_cells_for(role, x, y, o)) counted[0] = len(plan.furniture) return floor.keeps_open(tiles)

nodes.name: slot_order
nodes.body_text: def slot_order(slot): x, y, facing = slot distance = min((abs(x - dx) + abs(y - dy) for dx, dy in door_frontier), default=0) return side_rank[facing], -distance, y, x

nodes.name: centre
nodes.signature: def centre(): # The middle, with an aisle round it the wall pieces must leave # free; placed after them, it almost never found room.
nodes.body_text: def centre(): # The middle, with an aisle round it the wall pieces must leave # free; placed after them, it almost never found room. before = len(plan.furniture) if not office and not eatery and not trade_fitted: _furnish_middle(plan, idx, r, occupied, keep_clear, pal, keeps_open) if r.kind == "livingroom" and not any( role == "tv" for role, *_ in plan.furniture[before:]): wishlist[:] = [role for role in wishlist if role != "tv"] # The center group already supplied its focal pieces; do not add # them again from the room wishlist. for role, *_ in plan.furniture[before:]: consumed = (_once(role) or (r.kind == "church" and role == "table") or (r.kind == "livingroom" and role.startswith("armchair")) or (r.kind in ("clinic", "medical") and role.startswith("bed")) or (r.kind == "motelroom" and role == "sidetable") or (r.kind == "lobby" and (plan.kind in CIVIC_KINDS or plan.kind == "apartment") and role == "shop_counter")) if role in wishlist and consumed: wishlist.remove(role)

nodes.name: place
nodes.body_text: def place(role): if role == "bath_mat": # A mat is walked over, so it may lie on the walkway. mat = _bath_mat_spot(plan, idx, r, occupied, door_tiles | stair_tiles) if mat is not None: mx, my, mat_orient, mat_cells = mat plan.furniture.append((role, mx, my, mat_orient)) occupied.update(mat_cells) return if role == "mirror" and r.kind == "bathroom": basin = next(((x, y, orient) for basin_role, x, y, orient in plan.furniture if _is_sink(basin_role) and _room_at(plan, x, y) == idx), None) if basin is not None: bx, by, facing = basin near_basin = sorted( (slot for slot in slots if slot[2] == facing), key=lambda slot: abs(slot[0] - bx) + abs(slot[1] - by)) for slot in near_basin: if not hang("mirror", *slot): continue mirror_orient = _facing("mirror", slot[2]) occupied.update(_cells_for("mirror", slot[0], slot[1], mirror_orient)) return if _is_wall_piece(role): # A picture goes on bare wall before it goes behind a dresser, # and on the north wall before the west one. Both are the same # drawing question: the game draws a floor piece after the # thing on the wall of its own tile, so a picture hung where a # wardrobe or a piano stands is drawn over the piece instead of # behind it - a framed print floating across a bookshelf. Bare # wall first; then the north wall, which is drawn first. for x, y, facing in sorted( floor_slots, key=lambda s: ((s[0], s[1]) in occupied, 0 if s[2] == "N" else 1, on_facade(s))): if hang(role, x, y, facing): break return # A toilet is sat on from the square before it, and a dresser once # stood there. Only the room's essentials may take it: in a tight # bathroom the basin has nowhere else, and kept off it the basin # went onto the window square and was cleared away. toilet_fronts = set() if FR.priority(role, r.kind) == FR.ESSENTIAL else { (tx - _STEP[o][0], ty - _STEP[o][1]) for t, tx, ty, o in plan.furniture if t == "toilet" and o in _STEP and _room_at(plan, tx, ty) == idx} for (x, y, wanted) in floor_slots: if role in NORTH_WEST_ONLY and wanted in ("S", "E"): continue orient = _facing(role, wanted) ax, ay = _wall_anchor(role, x, y, orient, wanted) cells = _cells_for(role, ax, ay, orient) if any(c in occupied or c in no_go or c in toilet_fronts for c in cells): continue # A bed or a stove may stand in the sleeve round the way # through; a dresser or a plant may not, or the way through # is a needle's eye between two tall pieces. if (sleeve and FR.priority(role, r.kind) != FR.ESSENTIAL and any(c in sleeve for c in cells)): continue if any(_room_at(plan, cx, cy) != idx for cx, cy in cells): continue front = set() if _needs_front(role): # A fridge, a stove or a wardrobe is opened from the tile # in front of it; that tile stays floor. fx, fy = {"N": (0, 1), "S": (0, -1), "W": (1, 0), "E": (-1, 0)}[wanted] front = {(cx + fx, cy + fy) for cx, cy in cells} - set(cells) if any(c in occupied or _room_at(plan, *c) != idx for c in front): continue if role == "crate" and (len(crates) >= crate_cap or any( n in crates for cx, cy in cells for n in ((cx + 1, cy), (cx - 1, cy), (cx, cy + 1), (cx, cy - 1)))): continue # Nothing standing that shuts off a patch of the floor. if _blocks(role) and not keeps_open(cells): continue occupied.update(cells) occupied.update(front) plan.furniture.append((role, ax, ay, orient)) if role == "crate": crates.update(cells) if rng.random() < CRATE_STACKED: plan.furniture.append(("crate_top", ax, ay, orient)) return

nodes.name: _is_sink
nodes.body_text: def _is_sink(role: str) -> bool: return role != "sink_public" and role.startswith(("sink", "kitchen_sink"))

nodes.name: _needs_front
nodes.signature: def _needs_front(role: str) -> bool: # A shop's coolers and drinks machines too: one moved off a window used to # land in a corner with a shelf across its door.
nodes.body_text: def _needs_front(role: str) -> bool: # A shop's coolers and drinks machines too: one moved off a window used to # land in a corner with a shelf across its door. return role in FRONT_CLEAR_ROLES or role.startswith( ("wardrobe", "dresser", "fridge", "shop_fridge", "shop_freezer", "vending"))

nodes.name: _needs_surface
nodes.body_text: def _needs_surface(role: str) -> bool: return role in SURFACE_ROLES or _is_sink(role) or role.startswith("erika_plant")

nodes.name: _stand_on_something
nodes.signature: def _stand_on_something(plan: Plan, idx: int, room: Room, palette: dict) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _stand_on_something(plan: Plan, idx: int, room: Room, palette: dict) -> None: """A counter, a chest or a table under every piece of this room that needs one and does not have one - and a taller one under anything left standing on a piece too low to reach it.""" standing: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() low: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {} mine = [] for n, (role, x, y, o) in enumerate(plan.furniture): if _room_at(plan, x, y) != idx or _is_wall_piece(role): continue mine.append(n) if _needs_surface(role): continue cells = _cells_for(role, x, y, o) if role in LOW_TABLES: for cell in cells: low[cell] = n else: standing.update(cells) added, swapped = [], [] for n in mine: role, x, y, o = plan.furniture[n] if not _needs_surface(role) or (x, y) in standing: continue if room.kind in WORKTOP_ROOMS or _is_sink(role) or role == "register": support = palette.get("counter", "counter") elif role == "tv": support = "dresser" else: support = ("filing_cabinet" if plan.kind in CIVIC_KINDS and "filing_cabinet" in C.FURNITURE else NIGHTSTANDS[(x + y) % len(NIGHTSTANDS)]) if support not in C.FURNITURE: continue # A lamp already sitting on a coffee table: the table goes, the chest # takes its place, rather than two pieces on the one tile. under = low.pop((x, y), None) if under is not None: swapped.append((under, (support, x, y, _facing(support, o)))) else: added.append((n, (support, x, y, _facing(support, o)))) standing.add((x, y)) for n, piece in swapped: plan.furniture[n] = piece # Each support goes in just before its piece, so it is drawn underneath. for n, piece in sorted(added, reverse=True): plan.furniture.insert(n, piece)

nodes.name: _counter_runs
nodes.signature: def _counter_runs(plan: Plan, idx: int, slots, occupied: set, door_tiles: set, stair_tiles: set, counter: str = "counter", cabinets: bool = True, area: int = 0, rng: random.Random | None = None, keeps_open=None) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _counter_runs(plan: Plan, idx: int, slots, occupied: set, door_tiles: set, stair_tiles: set, counter: str = "counter", cabinets: bool = True, area: int = 0, rng: random.Random | None = None, keeps_open=None) -> None: """Fitted counters along a kitchen's two longest walls, up to what the floor is worth. Knox County sets the sink and stove into a run of worktop rather than standing them against bare wall, so the gaps along the two longest walls fill with counters - but only as far as COUNTER_PER_M2, and never in front of a door. Whatever the wishlist placed stays and counts against the same budget. """ rng = rng or random.Random(idx) # One budget for the whole tileset, counters and cupboards together, since # that is how the 3.9 was counted. Spending it on counters first and then # hanging cupboards on top of it is what left ours at 6.6. budget = max(3, round(area * COUNTER_PER_M2)) if area else 99 # A commercial kitchen asks for no cupboards and for the worktop to run # wall to wall (area=0). Taking the cupboard share out of that budget all # the same left it at 99 - 99 = 0, so no run was ever drawn: a restaurant # kitchen had the one counter off its wishlist and bare wall beside it. if not cabinets: room_cabinets = 0 elif area: room_cabinets = max(1, round(budget * CABINET_SHARE)) else: room_cabinets = 99 already = sum(1 for role, x, y, _o in plan.furniture if role.startswith("counter") and _room_at(plan, x, y) == idx) left = max(0, budget - room_cabinets - already) placed = [] by_wall: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, str]]] = {} for x, y, facing in slots: by_wall.setdefault(facing, []).append((x, y, facing)) for facing in sorted(by_wall, key=lambda f: -len(by_wall[f]))[:2]: for x, y, _f in by_wall[facing]: if len(placed) >= left: break orient = _facing(counter, facing) ax, ay = _wall_anchor(counter, x, y, orient, facing) cells = _cells_for(counter, ax, ay, orient) if any(c in occupied or c in door_tiles or c in stair_tiles for c in cells): continue if any(_room_at(plan, cx, cy) != idx for cx, cy in cells): continue if keeps_open and not keeps_open(cells): continue # A corner tile is on two walls; one counter is enough. occupied.update(cells) plan.furniture.append((counter, ax, ay, orient)) placed.append((ax, ay, orient)) # Cupboards on the wall above the counters, and sometimes a microwave on # one. North and west walls only, as for everything fixed to a wall; the # windows then keep off those tiles. if not cabinets: return hung = 0 microwave = rng.random() >= MICROWAVE_SHARE # True means: already done for role, x, y, orient in list(plan.furniture): if hung >= room_cabinets: break if role != counter or orient not in ("N", "W") or _room_at(plan, x, y) != idx: continue edge = _wall_edge(x, y, orient) if edge in plan.wall_pieces or _room_at(plan, *((x, y - 1) if orient == "N" else (x - 1, y))) == idx: continue plan.furniture.append(("wall_cabinet", x, y, _facing("wall_cabinet", orient))) plan.wall_pieces.add(edge) hung += 1 if not microwave: plan.furniture.append(("microwave", x, y, _facing("microwave", orient))) microwave = True

nodes.name: Building
nodes.body_text: class Building: """One or more storeys stacked into a single .tbx. A .tbx holds a list of <floor> elements and one building-wide room list; a floor's grid indexes into that shared list. So each storey is laid out as its own plan and the room lists are concatenated, with every storey's grid shifted by the rooms that came before it. """ width: int height: int storeys: list[Plan] = field(default_factory=list) # Per storey below the top: where its staircase rises from. stairs: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = field(default_factory=list) # Where a mall's escalators stand, in this building's own tiles: the top # of the run, the end that lands on the upper floor. They are packed as # their own lot (knoxbuild/structures.pack_loose), not written into this # .tbx, because a square of one carries two tiles. escalators: list[tuple[int, int]] = field(default_factory=list) profile: object | None = None # A large house (Plan.grand): its rooms take a mansion's finishes. grand: bool = False @property def rooms(self) -> list[Room]: return [r for s in self.storeys for r in s.rooms] def grid_for(self, level: int) -> list[list[int]]: """That storey's grid, renumbered into the shared room list.""" offset = sum(len(s.rooms) for s in self.storeys[:level]) grid = self.storeys[level].grid return [[v + offset if v else 0 for v in row] for row in grid]

nodes.name: rooms
nodes.body_text: def rooms(self) -> list[Room]: return [r for s in self.storeys for r in s.rooms]

nodes.name: grid_for
nodes.body_text: def grid_for(self, level: int) -> list[list[int]]: """That storey's grid, renumbered into the shared room list.""" offset = sum(len(s.rooms) for s in self.storeys[:level]) grid = self.storeys[level].grid return [[v + offset if v else 0 for v in row] for row in grid]

nodes.name: _pick_corridor
nodes.signature: def _pick_corridor(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random, widths=CORRIDOR_WIDTHS ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def _pick_corridor(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random, widths=CORRIDOR_WIDTHS ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None: """A corridor through the floor, with room for the stairs inside it. Flats need something to open onto, and it has to reach all of them: a compact shaft in the middle leaves the flats in the corners touching nothing. A strip along the building's length touches the flats either side of it by construction. The strip used to have to span the bounding box end to end. Placed on its real footprint, a block of flats turned 30 degrees has triangles of empty box at every corner, so no such strip ever fitted and the block fell back to one flat per floor. Now the longest strip that lies wholly inside the footprint is taken, as long as it runs most of the building's length; flats beyond its ends are folded into neighbours that do reach it. """ along_y = height >= width span = height if along_y else width across = width if along_y else height # This building's corridor width, narrowing if the floor is too thin # for the one drawn. wide = rng.choice(widths) while wide > CORRIDOR_WIDE and across < wide + 2 * MIN_ROOM: wide -= 1 if span < STAIR_RUN + 2 or across < wide + 2 * MIN_ROOM: return None def inside(a: int, b: int) -> bool: x, y = (b, a) if along_y else (a, b) return mask is None or mask[y][x] # How far the building actually extends along its length. extent = [a for a in range(span) if any(inside(a, b) for b in range(across))] if not extent: return None needed = max(STAIR_RUN + 2, int(0.6 * (extent[-1] - extent[0] + 1))) best = None for start in range(MIN_ROOM, across - wide - MIN_ROOM + 1): run_start = None for a in range(span + 1): ok = a < span and all(inside(a, b) for b in range(start, start + wide)) if ok and run_start is None: run_start = a if not ok and run_start is not None: length = a - run_start if length >= needed: centre = abs((start + wide / 2) - across / 2) score = (-length, centre) if best is None or score < best[0]: if along_y: rect = (start, run_start, start + wide - 1, a - 1) else: rect = (run_start, start, a - 1, start + wide - 1) best = (score, rect) run_start = None return best[1] if best else None

nodes.name: inside
nodes.signature: def inside(a: int, b: int) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def inside(a: int, b: int) -> bool: x, y = (b, a) if along_y else (a, b) return mask is None or mask[y][x]

nodes.name: _pick_core
nodes.signature: def _pick_core(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random, street: str | None = None, min_gap: int = 1 ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def _pick_core(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random, street: str | None = None, min_gap: int = 1 ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None: """Reserve a stair shaft: the same rectangle on every storey. Returned as (x0, y0, x1, y1) inclusive, oriented either way round, and always wholly inside the footprint - a shaft half outside an L-shaped building would put the flight in the garden. With the street known the stairs go at the back against a side wall, where a shop or a restaurant keeps its stairs; in the middle of the floor, a terrace of narrow shops had a flight of stairs in the middle of every one. The floor left on each side of the shaft is none or at least `min_gap` tiles: a house five tiles wide had its stairs down the middle and every room a one-tile strip round them, with nowhere to put a single piece. """ shapes = [(CORE_WIDE, STAIR_RUN + 1), (STAIR_RUN + 1, CORE_WIDE)] best: list[tuple[int, int, int, int]] = [] best_score = None for cw, ch in shapes: if cw > width or ch > height: continue for y0 in range(height - ch + 1): for x0 in range(width - cw + 1): if mask is not None and not all( mask[y][x] for y in range(y0, y0 + ch) for x in range(x0, x0 + cw)): continue if any(0 < g < min_gap for g in (x0, width - (x0 + cw), y0, height - (y0 + ch))): continue # Central, so the flight is not jammed against the windows. score = (abs((x0 + cw / 2) - width / 2) + abs((y0 + ch / 2) - height / 2)) if street in STEP_OF: # Back and side: distance from the wall opposite the # street, then from the nearer side wall. back = {"S": y0, "N": height - (y0 + ch), "E": x0, "W": width - (x0 + cw)}[street] side = min(x0, width - (x0 + cw)) if street in ("N", "S") \ else min(y0, height - (y0 + ch)) score = back * 2 + side if best_score is None or score < best_score - 1e-9: best_score, best = score, [(x0, y0, x0 + cw - 1, y0 + ch - 1)] elif abs(score - best_score) < 1e-9: best.append((x0, y0, x0 + cw - 1, y0 + ch - 1)) return rng.choice(best) if best else None

nodes.name: _pick_shaft
nodes.signature: def _pick_shaft(core: tuple[int, int, int, int], width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None ) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int, int], tuple[int, int, str]] | None
nodes.body_text: def _pick_shaft(core: tuple[int, int, int, int], width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None ) -> tuple[tuple[int, int, int, int], tuple[int, int, str]] | None: """A 2x2 elevator shaft beside the stair hall, and the wall its doors go in. The Elevators mod finds a lift by its door tiles - vanilla fixtures_escalators_01_48-51 - repeated at the same square on every floor it serves, with a small sealed box behind them. So the shaft is fixed once for the whole building, like the stairs, and sits against the long side of the stair hall so its doors open onto the landing on every storey. """ cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1 = core s = SHAFT_SIZE stair_cells = set() if stairs is not None: sx, sy, d = stairs stair_cells = {(sx, sy + i) if d == "N" else (sx + i, sy) for i in range(STAIR_RUN)} def inside(x0, y0): if x0 < 0 or y0 < 0 or x0 + s > width or y0 + s > height: return False return mask is None or all(mask[y][x] for y in range(y0, y0 + s) for x in range(x0, x0 + s)) options = [] if (cy1 - cy0) >= (cx1 - cx0): # Hall runs north-south: shafts to its west or east, doors in a W wall. mid = (cy0 + cy1) / 2 for y0 in range(cy0, cy1 - s + 2): for x0, door_x, side_col in ((cx0 - s, cx0, cx0), (cx1 + 1, cx1 + 1, cx1)): if not inside(x0, y0): continue if any((side_col, y0 + i) in stair_cells for i in range(s)): continue options.append((abs(y0 + s / 2 - 1 - mid), (x0, y0, x0 + s - 1, y0 + s - 1), (door_x, y0, "W"))) else: mid = (cx0 + cx1) / 2 for x0 in range(cx0, cx1 - s + 2): for y0, door_y, side_row in ((cy0 - s, cy0, cy0), (cy1 + 1, cy1 + 1, cy1)): if not inside(x0, y0): continue if any((x0 + i, side_row) in stair_cells for i in range(s)): continue options.append((abs(x0 + s / 2 - 1 - mid), (x0, y0, x0 + s - 1, y0 + s - 1), (x0, door_y, "N"))) if not options: return None options.sort(key=lambda o: (o[0], o[1])) return options[0][1], options[0][2]

nodes.name: _cut_off_by_the_shaft
nodes.body_text: def _cut_off_by_the_shaft(plan: Plan) -> None: """Take out any part of the storey the shaft has just walled off. Nothing opens into a lift shaft - it is a sealed box - so where the shaft lands in the neck of an L or a T it is a wall across it, and the rooms up the arm are rooms with no door anywhere: their only neighbour is the shaft. One fire station in a few thousand came out with four of them. Those tiles are better off not being part of the storey at all, which is what the arm is from the outside: roof. """ sealed = {i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if r.is_shaft} if not sealed: return touching: dict[int, set[int]] = {} for (a, b) in _boundary_edges(plan): if a in sealed or b in sealed: continue touching.setdefault(a, set()).add(b) touching.setdefault(b, set()).add(a) rooms = [i for i in range(1, len(plan.rooms) + 1) if i not in sealed] if not rooms: return # Out from the biggest room, which is the body of the building. start = max(rooms, key=lambda i: plan.rooms[i - 1].area) seen, stack = {start}, [start] while stack: for nxt in touching.get(stack.pop(), ()): if nxt not in seen: seen.add(nxt) stack.append(nxt) gone = [i for i in rooms if i not in seen] if not gone: return for y in range(plan.height): for x in range(plan.width): if plan.grid[y][x] in gone: plan.grid[y][x] = 0 _renumber(plan) _refit(plan)

nodes.name: _carve_shaft
nodes.signature: def _carve_shaft(plan: Plan, shaft: tuple[int, int, int, int], door: tuple[int, int, str]) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _carve_shaft(plan: Plan, shaft: tuple[int, int, int, int], door: tuple[int, int, str]) -> None: """Paint the elevator shaft over the storey as a sealed room of its own.""" x0, y0, x1, y1 = shaft plan.rooms.append(Room(x0, y0, x1, y1, kind="elevator", unit=0, is_shaft=True)) idx = len(plan.rooms) for y in range(y0, y1 + 1): for x in range(x0, x1 + 1): plan.grid[y][x] = idx if plan.shaft is None: plan.shaft = shaft plan.shaft_door = door plan.shafts.append((shaft, door)) _renumber(plan) _mend_fragments(plan) _refit(plan)

Set one tile in from the end so the corridor is still walkable past it. """ x0, y0, x1, y1 = core if (y1 - y0) >= (x1 - x0): start = min(y0 + 1, y1 - (STAIR_RUN - 1)) return x0 + (x1 - x0) // 2, max(y0, start), "N" start = min(x0 + 1, x1 - (STAIR_RUN - 1)) return max(x0, start), y0 + (y1 - y0) // 2, "W"

nodes.body_text: def _clear_for_stairs(plan: Plan, x: int, y: int, d: str) -> None: """Drop furniture standing where the staircase goes.""" dx, dy = (0, 1) if d == "N" else (1, 0) blocked = {(x + dx * i, y + dy * i) for i in range(STAIR_RUN)} plan.furniture = [ f for f in plan.furniture if _is_wall_piece(f[0]) or not (set(_cells_for(f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3])) & blocked) ]

nodes.name: _ways_in
nodes.body_text: def _ways_in(building: "Building", level: int, storey: "Plan") -> set: """The tiles a player arrives on: the outside doors on the ground floor, the stairs on every floor above.""" w, h = storey.width, storey.height def room(x, y): return storey.grid[y][x] if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h else 0 out = set() if level == 0: for (x, y, d) in storey.doors: a = (x - 1, y) if d == "W" else (x, y - 1) if room(*a) and not room(x, y): out.add(a) elif room(x, y) and not room(*a): out.add((x, y)) for lvl, (sx, sy, sd) in enumerate(building.stairs): if lvl not in (level - 1, level): continue dx, dy = (0, 1) if sd == "N" else (1, 0) out |= {(sx + dx * i, sy + dy * i) for i in range(STAIR_RUN) if room(sx + dx * i, sy + dy * i)} return out

Moved off # their window squares in full bedrooms and living rooms, they had nowhere # to go and were the pieces the clear-up threw out most.

Moved off # their window squares in full bedrooms and living rooms, they had nowhere # to go and were the pieces the clear-up threw out most. return (role in {"bath", "bath_mat", "sofa", "table", "coffee_table", "sidetable", "desk", "bench", "nightstand", "lamp", "radio", "coffee_maker", "toaster", "bin", "phone", "box", "box_battered", "hamper", "sale_sign"} or role.startswith(("bed", "double_bed", "sofa_", "counter", "dresser", "low_table_")))

nodes.name: _open_up
nodes.body_text: def _open_up(storey: "Plan", starts: set) -> set: """Which pieces have to go for every room to be walked into.""" w, h, grid = storey.width, storey.height, storey.grid doors = set(storey.doors) at: dict = {} # What standing on a tile costs: the pieces that would have to go, counted # (essentials, secondary, decoration) by the room each one stands in, so # the search below gives up any number of plants before one toilet. weight: dict = {} for i, (role, fx, fy, orient) in enumerate(storey.furniture): if not _blocks(role): continue idx = grid[fy][fx] if 0 <= fx < w and 0 <= fy < h else 0 rank = FR.priority(role, storey.rooms[idx - 1].kind if idx else "") for tile in _tiles_under(role, fx, fy, orient): at.setdefault(tile, set()).add(i) weight[tile] = weight.get(tile, ZERO) + RANK_COST[rank] def step(ax, ay, bx, by) -> bool: """Whether you can walk from one tile to the next: same room, or a doorway in the wall between them.""" if not (0 <= bx < w and 0 <= by < h) or not grid[by][bx]: return False if grid[ay][ax] == grid[by][bx]: return True if bx == ax + 1: return (bx, by, "W") in doors if ax == bx + 1: return (ax, ay, "W") in doors if by == ay + 1: return (bx, by, "N") in doors return (ax, ay, "N") in doors # A search out from the way in: stepping onto an empty tile is free, # stepping onto an occupied one costs the pieces standing there. What # comes back is the fewest essentials, then secondary pieces, then # decoration that have to move for each room to open. best: dict = {} back: dict = {} heap: list = [] for tile in sorted(starts): cost = weight.get(tile, ZERO) if cost < best.get(tile, NONE): best[tile], back[tile] = cost, None heapq.heappush(heap, (cost, tile)) while heap: here, (x, y) = heapq.heappop(heap) if here != best[(x, y)]: continue for nxt in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if not step(x, y, *nxt): continue cost = here + weight.get(nxt, ZERO) if cost < best.get(nxt, NONE): best[nxt], back[nxt] = cost, (x, y) heapq.heappush(heap, (cost, nxt)) walked = {grid[y][x] for (x, y), cost in best.items() if cost == ZERO} want: dict = {} for (x, y), cost in best.items(): idx = grid[y][x] if not idx or idx in walked or storey.rooms[idx - 1].is_shaft: continue if cost < want.get(idx, (NONE, None))[0]: want[idx] = (cost, (x, y)) goals = [tile for _cost, tile in want.values()] # A room is not walkable just because one corner of it can be reached: the # floor you are left standing on should hang together, and both sides of a # door and the square at a window have to be reachable or they cannot be # used. A tile or two you cannot step onto, though - behind the bed, beside # the bath - is how a furnished room works, and insisting on every bare # square took out 78 baths and 247 beds in 200 houses, three times what # this pass used to clear. Only a pocket bigger than that is opened up. for x, y, facing in doors | set(storey.windows): sides = ((x - 1, y), (x, y)) if facing == "W" else ((x, y - 1), (x, y)) for tx, ty in sides: if not (0 <= tx < w and 0 <= ty < h) or not grid[ty][tx]: continue if best.get((tx, ty), NONE) == ZERO: continue if (x, y, facing) not in doors and all( _under_a_window(storey.furniture[n][0]) for n in at.get((tx, ty), ())): continue goals.append((tx, ty)) shut = {(x, y) for y in range(h) for x in range(w) if grid[y][x] and (x, y) not in at and best.get((x, y), NONE) > ZERO} seen: set = set() for tile in shut: if tile in seen: continue seen.add(tile) pocket, edge = [], deque([tile]) while edge: cx, cy = edge.popleft() pocket.append((cx, cy)) for nxt in ((cx + 1, cy), (cx - 1, cy), (cx, cy + 1), (cx, cy - 1)): if nxt in shut and nxt not in seen and step(cx, cy, *nxt): seen.add(nxt) edge.append(nxt) if len(pocket) > POCKET_TILES: goals.append(min(pocket, key=lambda t: best.get(t, NONE))) gone: set = set() for tile in goals: while tile is not None: gone |= at.get(tile, set()) tile = back.get(tile) return gone

nodes.body_text: def step(ax, ay, bx, by) -> bool: """Whether you can walk from one tile to the next: same room, or a doorway in the wall between them.""" if not (0 <= bx < w and 0 <= by < h) or not grid[by][bx]: return False if grid[ay][ax] == grid[by][bx]: return True if bx == ax + 1: return (bx, by, "W") in doors if ax == bx + 1: return (ax, ay, "W") in doors if by == ay + 1: return (bx, by, "N") in doors return (ax, ay, "N") in doors

nodes.body_text: def _stay_reachable(cells: set, blocked: set, walk: set, squares: set) -> bool: """Whether each of `squares` can still be walked to from the walkway, over the room's bare floor. A room with no walkway has nothing to join.""" start = [t for t in walk if t in cells and t not in blocked] if not start or not squares: return True seen, todo = set(start), list(start) while todo: x, y = todo.pop() for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if n in cells and n not in blocked and n not in seen: seen.add(n) todo.append(n) return squares <= seen

nodes.body_text: def _make_way_for_windows(storey: "Plan", stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None) -> int: """Stand whatever blocks a window square against another wall of its room. Windows go in after the rooms are furnished, so nobody knew where they would land, and the square inside one had to be cleared for the window to be opened, climbed through and seen out of. Deleting what stood there was nine in ten of everything the clear-up took out. A one-tile piece, and what stands on it, moves to the nearest free wall tile of the same room that keeps the floor in one piece; with no such tile it trades places with a one-tile piece of the same room that may stand at a window. Only what cannot move is left for _open_up. Returns the number of pieces moved. A door slid off a corner after furnishing (_doors_off_corners) can land with a piece in its clearance; that clearance is cleared the same way, with no exception for what may stand at a window.""" w, h, grid = storey.width, storey.height, storey.grid squares = set() for x, y, d in storey.windows: for tx, ty in (((x - 1, y), (x, y)) if d == "W" else ((x, y - 1), (x, y))): if 0 <= tx < w and 0 <= ty < h and grid[ty][tx]: squares.add((tx, ty)) door_tiles = _door_tiles(storey) at_door = {(x, y) for x, y in door_tiles if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and grid[y][x]} if not squares and not at_door: return 0 off = squares | door_tiles for x, y, facing in storey.stalls: off.add((x, y)) off.add((x, y + 1) if facing == "N" else (x + 1, y)) if stairs is not None: sx, sy, sd = stairs dx, dy = (0, 1) if sd == "N" else (1, 0) off |= {(sx + dx * i, sy + dy * i) for i in range(STAIR_RUN)} furniture = storey.furniture cells_of = [_cells_for(role, x, y, o) for role, x, y, o in furniture] on_floor: dict = {} for i, f in enumerate(furniture): if not _is_wall_piece(f[0]): for c in cells_of[i]: on_floor.setdefault(c, []).append(i) hung = {(f[1], f[2]) for f in furniture if f[0] in ("wall_cabinet", "microwave")} def fits(pieces, x, y, face) -> bool: """Whether each piece, turned to face that wall, still covers one tile: a side table is one tile one way and two the other.""" return all(_cells_for(furniture[i][0], x, y, _facing(furniture[i][0], face)) == [(x, y)] for i in pieces) def put(pieces, x, y, face) -> None: for i in pieces: for c in cells_of[i]: on_floor[c].remove(i) role = furniture[i][0] furniture[i] = (role, x, y, _facing(role, face)) cells_of[i] = [(x, y)] on_floor.setdefault((x, y), []).append(i) def wall_of(t, facings): return next((f for f in facings if (t[0] + _STEP[f][0], t[1] + _STEP[f][1]) not in cells), None) def nearest(tiles): return sorted(tiles, key=lambda d: (abs(d[0] - t[0]) + abs(d[1] - t[1]), d[1], d[0])) rooms: dict = {} moved = 0 for t in sorted(squares | at_door): stack = sorted(on_floor.get(t, ())) roles = [furniture[i][0] for i in stack] if (not any(_blocks(r) for r in roles) or (t not in at_door and all(_under_a_window(r) for r in roles)) or any(len(cells_of[i]) > 1 for i in stack) or t in hung): continue idx = grid[t[1]][t[0]] if idx not in rooms: r = storey.rooms[idx - 1] cells = {(x, y) for y in range(r.y0, r.y1 + 1) for x in range(r.x0, r.x1 + 1) if grid[y][x] == idx} rooms[idx] = cells, _room_walkway(storey, idx, door_tiles, stairs) cells, walk = rooms[idx] blocked = {c for i, f in enumerate(furniture) if _blocks(f[0]) for c in cells_of[i]} & cells blocked.discard(t) # The tile something is opened from stays floor. fronts = {(cx - _STEP[f[3]][0], cy - _STEP[f[3]][1]) for i, (f, cs) in enumerate(zip(furniture, cells_of)) if _needs_front(f[0]) and f[3] in _STEP and i not in stack for cx, cy in cs} nw_only = any(r in NORTH_WEST_ONLY for r in roles) facings = ("N", "W") if nw_only else ("N", "W", "S", "E") front = any(_needs_front(r) for r in roles) def opened(d, face) -> bool: ahead = (d[0] - _STEP[face][0], d[1] - _STEP[face][1]) return not front or (ahead in cells and ahead not in blocked) covered = {c for cs in cells_of for c in cs} floor = FR.OpenFloor(cells, walk, POCKET_TILES) floor.block(blocked) # Every window square of the room that is bare floor, this one once # it is cleared: each has to stay joined to the walkway. opens = (squares & cells) - blocked opens.add(t) for d in nearest(cells - off - walk - covered - fronts): face = wall_of(d, facings) if (face is None or not opened(d, face) or not fits(stack, *d, face) or not floor.keeps_open({d}) or not _stay_reachable(cells, blocked | {d}, walk, opens - {d})): continue put(stack, *d, face) moved += len(stack) break else: # No free wall: trade places with a one-tile piece that may stand # at a window - a bare counter for the sink, a table for the # dresser. Both tiles stay taken, so the floor is as it was. if t in at_door: continue here = wall_of(t, "NWSE") # A wall cabinet keeps a counter under it. keep = off if any(r.startswith("counter") for r in roles) else off | hung for c in nearest(set(on_floor) & cells - keep): other = sorted(on_floor[c]) if not any(_blocks(furniture[j][0]) for j in other) or any( len(cells_of

nodes.name: _doors_off_stairs
nodes.body_text: def _doors_off_stairs(building: "Building") -> int: """Move a door that opens onto the steps of a flight to somewhere else on the same wall between the same two rooms. The steps between the two landings cannot be walked across, so a door hung on one - or on the wall beside one - leads nowhere, and the rooms behind it are cut off. Left where it is only when no other clean stretch of that boundary exists. """ if not building.stairs: return 0 x, y, d = building.stairs[0] dx, dy = (0, 1) if d == "N" else (1, 0) steps = {(x + dx * i, y + dy * i) for i in range(1, STAIR_RUN - 1)} def on_steps(door) -> bool: dxx, dyy, dd = door before = (dxx - 1, dyy) if dd == "W" else (dxx, dyy - 1) return (dxx, dyy) in steps or before in steps moved = 0 for storey in building.storeys: bad = [i for i, door in enumerate(storey.doors) if on_steps(door)] if not bad: continue edges = {(ex, ey, ed) for _side, wall in _facade_runs(storey.grid) for ex, ey, ed, _ix, _iy in wall} | _room_edges(storey.grid) corners = {(ex, ey) for ex, ey, ed in edges if (ex, ey, "N" if ed == "W" else "W") in edges} keep_off = set(storey.party) | set(getattr(storey, "wall_pieces", ())) for i in bad: door = storey.doors[i] want = _sides_of(storey.grid, *door) taken = set(storey.doors) spots = [e for e in edges if e not in taken and e not in keep_off and (e[0], e[1]) not in corners and not on_steps(e) and _sides_of(storey.grid, *e) == want] if spots: spots.sort(key=lambda e: (abs(e[0] - door[0]) + abs(e[1] - door[1]), e)) storey.doors[i] = spots[0] moved += 1 else: # Nowhere else on that wall. Where the rooms are reached # another way the door only has to go; where it was the one # way in, a door to some other neighbour takes its place. if not _joined_without(storey, i): for e in sorted(edges, key=lambda e: (abs(e[0] - door[0]) + abs(e[1] - door[1]), e)): pair = _sides_of(storey.grid, *e) if (e in taken or e in keep_off or (e[0], e[1]) in corners or on_steps(e) or 0 in pair or pair[0] == pair[1] or not set(pair) & set(want) or set(pair) == set(want) or any(storey.rooms[r - 1].is_shaft for r in pair)): continue ua, ub = (storey.rooms[r - 1].unit for r in pair) if ua and ub and ua != ub: continue storey.doors.append(e) if _joined_without(storey, i): taken.add(e) break storey.doors.pop() if _joined_without(storey, i): storey.doors[i] = None moved += 1 storey.doors = [d for d in storey.doors if d is not None] return moved

nodes.name: _joined_without
nodes.body_text: def _joined_without(storey, skip: int) -> bool: """Whether the two rooms either side of door `skip` still meet through the other doors and open edges, so that door can go without shutting one in.""" adj: dict[int, set] = {} links = [d for j, d in enumerate(storey.doors) if j != skip and d is not None] for x, y, d in list(links) + list(getattr(storey, "open_edge", ())): a, b = _sides_of(storey.grid, x, y, d) if a and b and a != b: adj.setdefault(a, set()).add(b) adj.setdefault(b, set()).add(a) a, b = _sides_of(storey.grid, *storey.doors[skip]) seen, stack = {a}, [a] while stack: for nxt in adj.get(stack.pop(), ()): if nxt not in seen: seen.add(nxt) stack.append(nxt) return b in seen

nodes.name: _thin_clutter
nodes.body_text: def _thin_clutter(building: "Building") -> int: """Take the decoration, then the secondary pieces, out of a room that is more furniture than floor. Essentials stay whatever the room.""" removed = 0 for storey in building.storeys: w, h, grid = storey.width, storey.height, storey.grid area: dict = {} for row in grid: for v in row: if v: area[v] = area.get(v, 0) + 1 by_room: dict = {} for i, (role, fx, fy, orient) in enumerate(storey.furniture): if not _blocks(role) or not (0 <= fx < w and 0 <= fy < h) or not grid[fy][fx]: continue by_room.setdefault(grid[fy][fx], []).append( (i, role, sum(1 for _ in _tiles_under(role, fx, fy, orient)))) gone: set = set() for idx, pieces in by_room.items(): room = storey.rooms[idx - 1] cap = CLUTTER_CAP.get(room.kind) if cap is None or room.is_core or area[idx] < MIN_ROOM * MIN_ROOM: continue fill = sum(t for _i, _r, t in pieces) order = sorted((p for p in pieces if FR.priority(p[1], room.kind) != FR.ESSENTIAL), key=lambda p: (-FR.priority(p[1], room.kind), p[2], p[0])) for i, _role, tiles in order: if fill <= cap * area[idx]: break gone.add(i) fill -= tiles if gone: # What stood on a piece goes with it: a lamp left over bare floor # hangs in the air, a cabinet over nothing is on a bare wall. cells = {c for i in gone for c in _tiles_under(*storey.furniture[i])} for i, (role, fx, fy, _o) in enumerate(storey.furniture): if (fx, fy) in cells and (_needs_surface(role) or role in ("wall_cabinet", "microwave")): gone.add(i) storey.furniture = [f for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if i not in gone] removed += len(gone) return removed

nodes.name: _narrow
nodes.signature: def _narrow(grid, x: int, y: int) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _narrow(grid, x: int, y: int) -> bool: """A room tile with its own room on neither side across one axis: a strip one tile wide, or a single square sticking out of the room.""" idx = grid[y][x] h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0]) def mine(nx, ny): return 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and grid[ny][nx] == idx return (not mine(x - 1, y) and not mine(x + 1, y)) or \ (not mine(x, y - 1) and not mine(x, y + 1))

nodes.name: mine
nodes.body_text: def mine(nx, ny): return 0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h and grid[ny][nx] == idx

nodes.name: _off_narrow_spots
nodes.body_text: def _off_narrow_spots(building: "Building") -> int: """Nothing stands on a tile of a room that is one tile wide. A kitchen with a one-tile tail had its counters and sink run down it, with the outside on one side and the hall wall on the other, and a bathroom's one-square nub took the toilet: nowhere to stand to use either, and the spot read as a mistake in the game (Piqua, 2026-10-31). What hangs on the walls stays; what stood on a piece that goes, goes with it.""" removed = 0 for storey in building.storeys: grid, w, h = storey.grid, storey.width, storey.height gone = {i for i, (role, fx, fy, orient) in enumerate(storey.furniture) if _blocks(role) and not role.startswith("elevator") and any(0 <= cx < w and 0 <= cy < h and grid[cy][cx] and _narrow(grid, cx, cy) for cx, cy in _tiles_under(role, fx, fy, orient))} if not gone: continue cells = {c for i in gone for c in _tiles_under(*storey.furniture[i])} gone |= {i for i, (role, fx, fy, _o) in enumerate(storey.furniture) if (fx, fy) in cells and (_needs_surface(role) or role in ("wall_cabinet", "microwave"))} storey.furniture = [f for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if i not in gone] removed += len(gone) return removed

nodes.name: _seat_the_desks
nodes.body_text: def _seat_the_desks(building: "Building") -> int: """Put each desk's office chair at it, as if someone sat there. A desk too big for the middle of a room goes against a wall, and its chair was then placed on its own wherever a wall had room, two tiles off or across the office. A chair not already at a desk moves to a free tile on the desk's open side, facing it; no chair is added.""" moved = 0 # The flight and the tile at either end of it, on every floor it touches. stairs = set() for x, y, d in building.stairs: dx, dy = (0, 1) if d == "N" else (1, 0) stairs |= {(x + dx * i, y + dy * i) for i in range(-1, STAIR_RUN + 1)} for storey in building.storeys: grid, w, h = storey.grid, storey.width, storey.height furn = storey.furniture taken = {c for role, x, y, o in furn if _blocks(role) for c in _tiles_under(role, x, y, o)} doors = _door_tiles(storey) # The squares either side of a window are kept clear to open it. doors |= {t for x, y, d in storey.windows for t in ((x, y), (x, y - 1) if d == "N" else (x - 1, y))} def room(x, y): return grid[y][x] if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h else 0 def fronts(i): role, x, y, o = furn[i] sx, sy = _STEP[_OPPOSITE[o]] return [(cx + sx, cy + sy) for cx, cy in _tiles_under(role, x, y, o)] desks = [i for i, f in enumerate(furn) if f[0] in DESK_ROLES and f[3] in _STEP] seated = {c for i in desks for c in fronts(i)} chairs = [i for i, f in enumerate(furn) if f[0] == "office_chair"] for d in desks: if any((furn[c][1], furn[c][2]) in fronts(d) for c in chairs): continue here = room(furn[d][1], furn[d][2]) loose = [c for c in chairs if (furn[c][1], furn[c][2]) not in seated and room(furn[c][1], furn[c][2]) == here] spot = next((t for t in fronts(d) if room(*t) == here and t not in taken and t not in doors and t not in stairs), None) if not loose or spot is None: continue c = min(loose, key=lambda c: abs(furn[c][1] - spot[0]) + abs(furn[c][2] - spot[1])) taken.discard((furn[c][1], furn[c][2])) furn[c] = ("office_chair", spot[0], spot[1], _OPPOSITE[furn[d][3]]) taken.add(spot) seated.add(spot) moved += 1 return moved

nodes.name: room
nodes.body_text: def room(x, y): return grid[y][x] if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h else 0

nodes.name: fronts
nodes.body_text: def fronts(i): role, x, y, o = furn[i] sx, sy = _STEP[_OPPOSITE[o]] return [(cx + sx, cy + sy) for cx, cy in _tiles_under(role, x, y, o)]

nodes.name: _off_the_doorways
nodes.body_text: def _off_the_doorways(storey: Plan) -> int: """Nothing standing on the tiles a door keeps clear. Furnishing keeps off them, but a door can be moved or added afterwards - when the flight is in the way of the door first chosen - and it can land on a bed already in place: a bedroom whose only way in was a bed's foot. """ clear = _door_tiles(storey) gone = {i for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if _blocks(f[0]) and set(_cells_for(f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3])).intersection(clear)} if gone: storey.furniture = [f for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if i not in gone] return len(gone)

nodes.name: _clear_the_way
nodes.body_text: def _clear_the_way(building: "Building") -> int: """Take out whatever stands between a doorway and the rooms behind it. Rooms are furnished one at a time, so nothing stopped a shelf landing in the only doorway or a counter spanning the only way through. The plan was connected - every audit of it passed - but the furnished building was not. """ _doors_off_stairs(building) removed = sum(_off_the_doorways(storey) for storey in building.storeys) stairs = building.stairs[0] if building.stairs else None for level, storey in enumerate(building.storeys): _make_way_for_windows(storey, stairs) starts = _ways_in(building, level, storey) if not starts: continue for _round in range(6): gone = _open_up(storey, starts) if not gone: break # What hangs over a counter goes with it: a wall cabinet left over # bare floor was a cupboard on a wall with nothing beneath. under = {(f[1], f[2]) for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if i in gone and f[0].startswith("counter")} gone |= {i for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if f[0] in ("wall_cabinet", "microwave") and (f[1], f[2]) in under} storey.furniture = [f for i, f in enumerate(storey.furniture) if i not in gone] removed += len(gone) # Last, after the windows have moved pieces off their squares: a piece stood # against another wall can land on a one-tile spot. removed += _off_narrow_spots(building) _thin_clutter(building) # Last, so nothing moves a chair away again; it only takes a free tile that # is not a doorway's or a window's, so the way through stays open. _seat_the_desks(building) return removed

nodes.name: houses.py
nodes.body_text: """Houses: room budgets by floor, wings, spare rooms, and the house mix.""" from __future__ import annotations from ..sizing import SIZES from ..sizing import capacity from ..sizing import programme_for_house_floor from ..sizing import split_by_targets import random from .core import HOUSE_OVERSIZE, Plan, Room, STAIR_RUN from .openings import _room_at from .malls import _renumber from .dwellings import _graph_distance, _neighbours, _pieces, _too_small # Knox County's houses (546 measured) have per house about 1.4 bedrooms, 0.4 # children's bedrooms, 0.5 closets and 0.2 laundries - and ours had three # bedrooms and an office apiece, every spare room another bedroom. A room this # small is a closet; the rest take turns down these lists. # A room this size or under is a closet rather than a bedroom. It was 8, # which no room can ever be: MIN_ROOM and MIN_SPLIT put the smallest room # the splitter can make at 9 tiles, so the rule never once fired and Knox # County's commonest small room - 5,397 closets - was one we never built. SMALL_ROOM_TILES = 10 # Upstairs. The game's houses have 1.39 bedrooms and 0.42 children's rooms # each; ours had 2.15 and 1.21, an upstairs of nothing but beds. A closet on # the landing is what it really has - 0.50 a house, and none of ours had one. # A separate dining room, in Knox County, is in 13% of houses. DINING_ROOM_SHARE = 0.13 HOUSE_SLEEPING = ["bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bedroom", "storage"] # What is left of a floor once its bedrooms, its bathroom and its one office # are dealt out. Everything past them used to become storage, which turned a # fourteen-room house into five bedrooms and nine store cupboards - 2747 # storerooms in 200 houses against 321 before, and storage the commonest room # in a house by three times over. These are the rooms a house has more than # one of, and they are dealt round in turn. HOUSE_SPARE = ["storage", "laundry", "office", "storage", "closet", "office"] UPSTAIRS = ["bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bedroom", "laundry", "bedroom", "office", "storage"] # Some two-storey houses keep a bedroom downstairs as well - for a guest or # a grandparent - with a bathroom beside it, when the house has bedrooms # enough upstairs and the ground floor room for both. All of them had one # before bedrooms went upstairs; then none, and ground-floor bathrooms went # with them (18 in 203 multi-storey houses to 5). GROUND_BEDROOM_SHARE = 0.2 GROUND_EXTRA_TILES = 60 # A house floor cut by kind gets spare rooms while it is bigger than its # rooms can fill (sizing.capacity: the big ones at their hi), so a big floor # gets more rooms rather than a living room of 90 tiles - up to one room per # HOUSE_ROOM_TILES of floor and HOUSE_MAX_SPARE spares. HOUSE_ROOM_TILES = 22 HOUSE_MAX_SPARE = 40 # A floor this many tiles or more is a large house and takes more rooms of the # kinds that fill a floor. HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR = 260 # A house whose storeys add up to that much floor is a mansion: it takes the # finishes and the dressing of an old, rich house rather than a bigger version # of a small one. The same line, measured over the whole house, so two storeys # of 130 count where one floor of 130 does not. MANSION_FLOOR_TILES = HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR # And the floors it lays: dark wood and red carpet underfoot, white tile in the # wet rooms. A kind it does not list keeps the house's own floor. These are # EXTRA_FLOORS names (tbx.floor_options). MANSION_FLOORS = { "livingroom": ["wood_dark", "carpet_red", "carpet_blue"], "dining": ["wood_dark", "carpet_red"], "hall": ["wood_dark", "tile_white"], "office": ["wood_dark", "carpet_red"], "bedroom": ["carpet_red", "carpet_blue", "wood_dark"], "kidsbedroom": ["carpet_blue", "carpet_red"], "kitchen": ["tile_white", "tile_cream"], "bathroom": ["tile_white", "tile_cream"], } # On a floor that size the bedrooms still stay bedrooms, not suites: the wings # give the other rooms the space. BIG_FLOOR_BEDROOM_OVERSIZE = 1.2 HOUSE_TOP_UP = ["storage", "office"] HOUSE_GROW_TRIES = 10 BIG_HOUSE_FILL = ["closet", "livingroom", "laundry", "office", "storage", "office", "storage", "livingroom"] # Rooms a cut may clip away: what is left of one is folded into the room # beside it or kept as a closet. The hall too, unless it is the landing. HOUSE_LOSABLE = {"hall", "laundry", *HOUSE_TOP_UP} # What a too-big closet is called instead, smallest first. CLOSET_GROWS_INTO = ("storage", "office") # Shuffles of a programme cut as a whole box before it sheds a room, and of # the bare programme before the floor falls back: a 3x3 bathroom lands # clear of a turned footprint's corners only so often. HOUSE_TRIES = 3 HOUSE_LAST_TRIES = 10 # A footprint filling less of its box than this - a turned or L-shaped # house - is cut as it always was. The cut is drawn on the whole box, so # every room the footprint does not clip came out the box's share of it: # twice its size on a turned house, living rooms of 500 tiles. HOUSE_MIN_FILL = 0.8 # The rooms of a large house's day wing; the rest sleep. _DAY_ROOMS = {"hall", "livingroom", "openplan", "kitchen", "dining", "laundry", "office", "storage"} # Where you walk when you are not in a room. Knox County's houses have a hall # in 42% of them and a living room in nearly all, and everything opens off one # or the other; ours had no circulation upstairs at all, so a floor of bedrooms # was a chain of them - the commonest door in the whole town was one bedroom # into the next. CIRCULATION = {"hall", "lobby", "livingroom", "openplan", "concourse"} # One more hall per this many rooms on a floor, on top of the corridor and the # landing. It is a balance between two ways of being wrong, and the number was # picked by measuring both against Knox County. Too few and rooms chain: at # one per twelve, 230 doors in 300 buildings went bedroom into bedroom. Too # many and the plan is corridor: at one per six, a house was a third # circulation where the game's are a quarter by room. One per eight puts a # house at 23.3% of its rooms against the game's 23.7%, and bedroom-to-bedroom # doors at 120 where the old plan had 771. ROOMS_PER_HALL = 8

nodes.name: _footprint
nodes.body_text: def _footprint(plan: Plan) -> int: return (sum(sum(row) for row in plan.mask) if plan.mask is not None else plan.width * plan.height)

nodes.name: _house_room_budgets
nodes.signature: def _house_room_budgets(plan: Plan, levels: int) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _house_room_budgets(plan: Plan, levels: int) -> tuple[int, int]: floor_area = _footprint(plan) * max(1, levels) bedrooms = min(5, max(1, (floor_area + 89) // 90)) bathrooms = 2 if floor_area >= 900 else 1 return bedrooms, bathrooms

nodes.name: _house_bedrooms_on_floor
nodes.signature: def _house_bedrooms_on_floor(bedrooms: int, levels: int, level: int) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _house_bedrooms_on_floor(bedrooms: int, levels: int, level: int) -> int: each, remainder = divmod(bedrooms, max(1, levels)) return each + (level < remainder)

nodes.name: _house_floor_bedrooms
nodes.signature: def _house_floor_bedrooms(bedrooms: int, levels: int, level: int) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _house_floor_bedrooms(bedrooms: int, levels: int, level: int) -> int: """A house's bedrooms on one floor: all of them in a bungalow, none on the ground floor of a house with an upstairs, the rest shared upstairs.""" if levels <= 1: return bedrooms return _house_bedrooms_on_floor(bedrooms, levels - 1, level - 1) if level else 0

nodes.name: _ground_bedroom
nodes.signature: def _ground_bedroom(bedrooms: int, levels: int, floor: int, rng: random.Random) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _ground_bedroom(bedrooms: int, levels: int, floor: int, rng: random.Random) -> bool: """Whether a house's ground floor keeps a bedroom of its own.""" return (levels == 2 and bedrooms >= 2 and floor >= GROUND_EXTRA_TILES and rng.random() < GROUND_BEDROOM_SHARE)

nodes.name: _house_spares
nodes.signature: def _house_spares(profile, rng: random.Random, upstairs: bool = False, big: bool = False)
nodes.body_text: def _house_spares(profile, rng: random.Random, upstairs: bool = False, big: bool = False): """Rooms for a floor past its bedrooms, in turn: a study (or storage, by the household's _house_study_share), then storage and offices. The laundry is in the programme, the closets are the pieces a cut leaves. Only those: a house has a study and a store room, not a row of them, so past that an upper floor takes bedrooms, which are big enough to fill it, rather than filling with cupboards; a ground floor's rooms grow.""" first = "office" if rng.random() < _house_study_share(profile) else "storage" yield first yield from (k for k in HOUSE_TOP_UP if k != first) if big: # A large house keeps its bedroom and bathroom budget; the extra # floor goes to a dining room and the rooms beside it. if not upstairs: yield "dining" # And past those, the rooms a big house really has more of, dealt # round: a floor of four hundred tiles is not seven rooms of sixty. while True: yield from BIG_HOUSE_FILL elif upstairs: yield from ("bedroom", "bedroom")

nodes.name: _wall_shared
nodes.body_text: def _wall_shared(a, b, run: int = 2) -> bool: """Whether two rectangles (anything with x0 y0 x1 y1) share a wall of at least `run` tiles.""" ox = min(a.x1, b.x1) - max(a.x0, b.x0) + 1 oy = min(a.y1, b.y1) - max(a.y0, b.y0) + 1 return ((ox >= run and (a.y1 + 1 == b.y0 or b.y1 + 1 == a.y0)) or (oy >= run and (a.x1 + 1 == b.x0 or b.x1 + 1 == a.x0)))

nodes.name: _cut_in_wings
nodes.signature: def _cut_in_wings(box, kinds: list[str], rng: random.Random, floor, core, landing) -> list[Room] | None
nodes.body_text: def _cut_in_wings(box, kinds: list[str], rng: random.Random, floor, core, landing) -> list[Room] | None: """A big house floor cut in two wings, each with a hall of its own. One cut over four hundred tiles has to put every bedroom beside a hall, and cannot, so a large house came out as rooms that open into rooms. Two wings are two small houses side by side: the stairs and the day rooms in one, the bedrooms in the other, and the halls meet. Returns None when the floor will not split (the caller cuts it whole).""" from ..sizing import capacity rest = kinds[1:] day = [k for k in rest if k in _DAY_ROOMS] night = [k for k in rest if k not in _DAY_ROOMS] if len(day) < 2 or len(night) < 2: # Upstairs is all bedrooms: share them out, the second wing gets a hall. half = max(2, len(rest) // 2) day, night = rest[:half], rest[half:] if len(night) < 2: return None wing_a, wing_b = ["hall"] + day, ["hall"] + night # Split by what each wing can hold, not by its rooms' targets: a floor cut # in proportion to the targets gave a wing of three bedrooms the room of # five, and bedrooms of fifty tiles. ta = capacity(wing_a) tb = capacity(wing_b) x0, y0, x1, y1 = box wide = (x1 - x0) >= (y1 - y0) lo, hi = (x0, x1) if wide else (y0, y1) cut = lo + round((hi - lo + 1) * ta / (ta + tb)) cut = min(max(cut, lo + 6), hi - 5) if core is not None: # The stairs stay in the first wing: the line goes past them, or in # front of them if that is nearer the ideal. c0, c1 = (core[0], core[2]) if wide else (core[1], core[3]) if c0 < cut <= c1: cut = c1 + 1 if c1 + 1 <= hi - 5 else c0 a_box = (x0, y0, cut - 1, y1) if wide else (x0, y0, x1, cut - 1) b_box = (cut, y0, x1, y1) if wide else (x0, cut, x1, y1) def tiles(b): return sum(1 for y in range(b[1], b[3] + 1) for x in range(b[0], b[2] + 1) if floor[y][x]) out = [] for sub, wing in ((a_box, wing_a), (b_box, wing_b)): holds_core = core is not None and not ( core[2] < sub[0] or core[0] > sub[2] or core[3] < sub[1] or core[1] > sub[3]) got = split_by_targets(sub, wing, rng, area=tiles(sub), touch=landing if holds_core else None) if got is None: return None out += got return out

nodes.name: tiles
nodes.body_text: def tiles(b): return sum(1 for y in range(b[1], b[3] + 1) for x in range(b[0], b[2] + 1) if floor[y][x])

nodes.name: _house_by_kind
nodes.signature: def _house_by_kind(plan: Plan, level: int, levels: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[Room] | None
nodes.body_text: def _house_by_kind(plan: Plan, level: int, levels: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[Room] | None: """A house floor's rooms cut to its programme's sizes, kinds fixed. The whole box is cut, sized for the floor inside the walls, and kept only where every room keeps one piece of its kind's least floor inside the walls and clear of the stair shaft (painted over whatever is beneath it) - a bathroom the shaft lands on is not a bathroom - and none comes out far bigger than its kind. The hall is cut beside the stairs, so they arrive in it. A programme no cut fits sheds its extra rooms. None when the floor is too small, the footprint fills too little of its box, or nothing fits: the caller falls back to _split. """ if _footprint(plan) < HOUSE_MIN_FILL * plan.width * plan.height: return None core = plan.core floor = [[(plan.mask is None or plan.mask[y][x]) and not (core and core[0] <= x <= core[2] and core[1] <= y <= core[3]) for x in range(plan.width)] for y in range(plan.height)] area = sum(map(sum, floor)) kinds = programme_for_house_floor(area, level, levels, rng) if kinds is None: return None need = 5 if levels == 1 else 3 # rooms no floor of its kind goes without # An open-plan house has one room for living and cooking, cut as one. if level == 0 and rng.random() < _house_open_plan_share(plan.profile): kinds[kinds.index("livingroom")] = "openplan" kinds.remove("kitchen") need -= 1 # A dining room as often as households have one (_house_dining_share). if (level == 0 and area >= (70 if levels == 1 else 45) and rng.random() < _house_dining_share(plan.profile)): kinds.append("dining") bedrooms, bathrooms = _house_room_budgets(plan, levels) quota = _house_floor_bedrooms(bedrooms, levels, level) spares = _house_spares(plan.profile, rng, level > 0, area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR) beds = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom")] for i in beds[quota:]: # past the house's bedroom budget kinds[i] = next(spares, "storage") spare = ["bedroom"] * (quota - len(beds)) if level == 0: if _ground_bedroom(bedrooms, levels, area, rng): kinds += ["bedroom", "bathroom"] elif levels > 1 and bathrooms > levels - 1: spare.insert(0, "bathroom") if "laundry" not in kinds: spare.append("laundry") n = 0 while (area > capacity(kinds) and n < HOUSE_MAX_SPARE and len(kinds) < area // HOUSE_ROOM_TILES): more = spare[n] if n < len(spare) else next(spares, None) if more is None: break kinds.append(more) n += 1 box = (0, 0, plan.width - 1, plan.height - 1) landing = core if core is not None and kinds[0] == "hall" else None losable = HOUSE_LOSABLE - {"hall"} if landing else HOUSE_LOSABLE def keeps(room: Room) -> bool: ps = _pieces(room, floor) return bool(ps) and SIZES[room.kind].lo <= len(ps[0]) and not ( _too_small(ps[0]) or (len(ps) > 1 and not _too_small(ps[1]))) def _on_circulation(room: Room, rooms: list, core) -> bool: """A bedroom opens onto a hall, the stairs or the living room, else it is reached through another bedroom.""" if room.kind not in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom"): return True if core is not None: c = Room(*core) if _wall_shared(room, c): return True return any(o is not room and o.kind in ("hall", "livingroom", "openplan") and _wall_shared(room, o) for o in rooms) # A big floor has more of everything, and each room may be bigger too. oversize = HOUSE_OVERSIZE def too_big(room: Room) -> bool: return (room.kind != "hall" and sum(map(len, _pieces(room, floor))) > (BIG_FLOOR_BEDROOM_OVERSIZE if room.kind in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom") and area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR else oversize) * SIZES[room.kind].hi) grown = 0 while True: always_big = True for _ in range(HOUSE_TRIES if len(kinds) > need else HOUSE_LAST_TRIES): rooms = (_cut_in_wings(box, kinds, rng, floor, core, landing) if area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR else None) if rooms is None: rooms = split_by_targets(box, kinds, rng, area=area, touch=landing) for r in rooms or (): if r.kind == "closet" and too_big(r): # A closet the cut made room-sized is the spare room it # looks like: a big floor failed on these more than on # anything else, and went to the plain splitter. tiles = sum(map(len, _pieces(r, floor))) r.kind = next((k for k in CLOSET_GROWS_INTO if tiles <= HOUSE_OVERSIZE * SIZES[k].hi), r.kind) kept = [r for r in rooms or () if r.kind not in losable] big = any(map(too_big, kept)) # One hall cannot touch every bedroom of a large house, and the # wings already give each half its own, so only a smaller floor # is held to it. if rooms and not big and all(map(keeps, kept)) and ( area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR or all(_on_circulation(r, rooms, core) for r in rooms)): return rooms always_big &= big # Every cut had a room too big for its kind. On a large floor that # means too few rooms, not too many: add some and cut again, a few # times, before the floor is given up to the plain splitter. if always_big and area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR and grown < HOUSE_GROW_TRIES: grown += 1 kinds.extend(k for k in (next(spares, None) for _ in range(2)) if k) continue # Fewer rooms would only come out bigger.

nodes.name: keeps
nodes.body_text: def keeps(room: Room) -> bool: ps = _pieces(room, floor) return bool(ps) and SIZES[room.kind].lo <= len(ps[0]) and not ( _too_small(ps[0]) or (len(ps) > 1 and not _too_small(ps[1])))

nodes.name: _on_circulation
nodes.signature: def _on_circulation(room: Room, rooms: list, core) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _on_circulation(room: Room, rooms: list, core) -> bool: """A bedroom opens onto a hall, the stairs or the living room, else it is reached through another bedroom.""" if room.kind not in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom"): return True if core is not None: c = Room(*core) if _wall_shared(room, c): return True return any(o is not room and o.kind in ("hall", "livingroom", "openplan") and _wall_shared(room, o) for o in rooms)

nodes.name: too_big
nodes.body_text: def too_big(room: Room) -> bool: return (room.kind != "hall" and sum(map(len, _pieces(room, floor))) > (BIG_FLOOR_BEDROOM_OVERSIZE if room.kind in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom") and area >= HOUSE_BIG_FLOOR else oversize) * SIZES[room.kind].hi)

nodes.name: _house_open_plan_share
nodes.body_text: def _house_open_plan_share(profile) -> float: if profile is None: return 0.0 era_share = {"prewar": 0.03, "midcentury": 0.12, "modern": 0.28} share = era_share.get(profile.era, 0.08) * (0.75 + 0.5 * profile.wealth) return min(0.38, share + (0.04 if profile.setting == "urban" else 0.0))

nodes.name: _house_dining_share
nodes.body_text: def _house_dining_share(profile) -> float: if profile is None: return DINING_ROOM_SHARE era_factor = {"prewar": 1.45, "midcentury": 1.0, "modern": 0.65} return min(0.3, DINING_ROOM_SHARE * era_factor.get(profile.era, 1.0) * (0.75 + 0.5 * profile.wealth))

nodes.name: _house_study_share
nodes.body_text: def _house_study_share(profile) -> float: if profile is None: return 1.0 share = 0.25 + 0.45 * profile.wealth if profile.era == "modern": share += 0.12 if profile.wear >= 0.75: share -= 0.08 return max(0.1, min(0.9, share))

nodes.name: _merge_house_open_plan
nodes.signature: def _merge_house_open_plan(plan: Plan, living_id: int, kitchen_id: int) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _merge_house_open_plan(plan: Plan, living_id: int, kitchen_id: int) -> bool: living, kitchen = plan.rooms[living_id - 1], plan.rooms[kitchen_id - 1] side_by_side = (living.y0 == kitchen.y0 and living.y1 == kitchen.y1 and (living.x1 + 1 == kitchen.x0 or kitchen.x1 + 1 == living.x0)) stacked = (living.x0 == kitchen.x0 and living.x1 == kitchen.x1 and (living.y1 + 1 == kitchen.y0 or kitchen.y1 + 1 == living.y0)) if not (side_by_side or stacked): return False living.x0, living.y0 = min(living.x0, kitchen.x0), min(living.y0, kitchen.y0) living.x1, living.y1 = max(living.x1, kitchen.x1), max(living.y1, kitchen.y1) living.kind = "openplan" for y in range(plan.height): for x in range(plan.width): if plan.grid[y][x] == kitchen_id: plan.grid[y][x] = living_id kitchen.kind = None _renumber(plan) return True

nodes.name: _landing
nodes.signature: def _landing(plan: Plan, adj: dict, free: list, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None) -> int | None
nodes.body_text: def _landing(plan: Plan, adj: dict, free: list, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None) -> int | None: """The room a floor is walked through: where the stairs arrive, or failing that whichever room touches the most others.""" if stairs is not None: x, y, d = stairs dx, dy = (0, 1) if d == "N" else (1, 0) for i in range(STAIR_RUN): room = _room_at(plan, x + dx * i, y + dy * i) if room in free: return room if not free: return None return max(free, key=lambda i: (len([n for n in adj.get(i, ()) if n in free]), plan.rooms[i - 1].area))

nodes.name: _more_halls
nodes.signature: def _more_halls(plan: Plan, adj: dict, free: list, kinds: dict, seeds: list[int], cap: int, want: list[int] | None = None) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _more_halls(plan: Plan, adj: dict, free: list, kinds: dict, seeds: list[int], cap: int, want: list[int] | None = None) -> int: """Rooms turned into halls until the rest (or `want`) all open onto one.""" made = 0 while made < cap and free: covered = set(seeds) for i in seeds: covered |= set(adj.get(i, ())) left = [i for i in (free if want is None else want) if i not in covered] if not left: break seed_set = set(seeds) best = max(free, key=lambda i: ( len([n for n in adj.get(i, ()) if n in left]), len(set(adj.get(i, ())) & seed_set), plan.rooms[i - 1].area)) if not any(n in left for n in adj.get(best, ())): break kinds[best] = "hall" free.remove(best) seeds.append(best) made += 1 return made

nodes.name: _assign_house_kinds
nodes.signature: def _assign_house_kinds(plan: Plan, level: int, levels: int, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None, rng: random.Random | None = None, by_kind: bool = False) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _assign_house_kinds(plan: Plan, level: int, levels: int, stairs: tuple[int, int, str] | None = None, rng: random.Random | None = None, by_kind: bool = False) -> None: """Rooms of a house, placed by what they sit next to. Handing kinds out in size order put the kitchen wherever the second-biggest rectangle fell, bathrooms opening off living rooms, and a kitchen on every storey of a three-storey house. Here the ground floor holds the rooms a household shares - the living room, the kitchen beside it, dining beside that - and upper floors hold bedrooms. Bedrooms go as far from the living room as the plan allows; the bathroom takes the smallest room. A floor cut `by_kind` (_house_by_kind) already has its kinds, open plan included; only a piece the shaft or the footprint split off a room is named here, and a spare room off the hall becomes another hall where bedrooms and bathrooms would otherwise open into each other. """ rng = rng or random.Random(plan.width * 31 + plan.height) if by_kind: for room in plan.rooms: if not room.is_core and not room.fixed: room.kind = "closet" if room.area <= SMALL_ROOM_TILES else "storage" adj = _neighbours(plan) rooms = list(enumerate(plan.rooms, 1)) seeds = [i for i, r in rooms if r.is_core or r.kind in CIRCULATION] near = {n for i in seeds for n in adj[i]} free = [i for i, r in rooms if i in near and not r.is_core and r.kind in ("office", "storage", "laundry")] kinds: dict[int, str] = {} _more_halls(plan, adj, free, kinds, seeds, 1 + len(rooms) // ROOMS_PER_HALL, want=[i for i, r in rooms if r.kind in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bathroom")]) for i, kind in kinds.items(): plan.rooms[i - 1].kind = kind # A bedroom or bathroom still off every hall trades kinds with a # spare room on one that is the right size for it. def off_hall(i: int) -> bool: return not any(plan.rooms[n - 1].is_core or plan.rooms[n - 1].kind in CIRCULATION for n in adj[i]) for i, room in rooms: if room.kind not in ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bathroom") or not off_hall(i): continue size = SIZES[room.kind] swap = [j for j, r in rooms if r.fixed and r.kind in HOUSE_TOP_UP and not off_hall(j) and size.lo <= r.area <= HOUSE_OVERSIZE * size.hi] if swap: j = min(swap, key=lambda j: abs(plan.rooms[j - 1].area - room.area)) room.kind, plan.rooms[j - 1].kind = plan.rooms[j - 1].kind, room.kind return adj = _neighbours(plan) # A room the mapper drew with a kind of its own keeps it; only the rest # are dealt out, and whatever is left out of that is a core, hence the # hall below. free = [i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if not r.is_core and not r.fixed] for i, room in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1): if i not in free and not room.fixed: room.kind = "hall" if not free: return area = {i: plan.rooms[i - 1].area for i in free} kinds: dict[int, str] = {} bedroom_budget, bathroom_budget = _house_room_budgets(plan, levels) ground_bed = level == 0 and _ground_bedroom(bedroom_budget, levels, _footprint(plan), rng) bedroom_quota = _house_floor_bedrooms(bedroom_budget, levels, level) + ground_bed # A bathroom on every floor with a bedroom, and on the ground floor too # when the house has one to spare. bathroom_floors = {n for n in range(levels) if _house_floor_bedrooms(bedroom_budget, levels, n)} if bathroom_budget > len(bathroom_floors) or ground_bed: bathroom_floors.add(0) def take(i: int, kind: str) -> None: kinds[i] = kind free.remove(i) if level == 0: living = max(free, key=lambda i: area[i]) take(living, "livingroom") if free: near = [n for n in adj[living] if n in free] or free kitchen = max(near, key=lambda i: area[i]) take(kitchen, "kitchen") near = [n for n in adj[kitchen] if n in free] # A separate dining room is the exception: Knox County has one in # 13% of its houses, the rest eating in the kitchen or the living # room. Taking one whenever there was a room to spare gave ours # one in 93%. if near and len(free) >= 3 and rng.random() < _house_dining_share(plan.profile): take(max(near, key=lambda i: area[i]), "dining") if free and level in bathroom_floors and (levels == 1 or len(free) >= 2): take(min(free, key=lambda i: area[i]), "bathroom") # A small room beside the kitchen is its laundry. near = [n for n in adj.get(kitchens[0], ()) if n in free and area[n] <= SMALL_ROOM_TILES] if (kitchens := [i for i, k in kinds.items() if k == "kitchen"]) else [] if near: take(min(near, key=lambda i: area[i]), "laundry") _more_halls(plan, adj, free, kinds, [living] + [i for i, k in kinds.items() if k == "hall"], len(free) // ROOMS_PER_HALL) dist = _graph_distance(adj, living) rest = sorted(free, key=lambda i: -dist.get(i, 99)) bedroom_count = min(bedroom_quota, len(rest)) kids_room = bedroom_count > 1 and rng.random() < 0.4 for n, i in enumerate(rest): if n < bedroom_count: kinds[i] = "kidsbedroom" if kids_room and n == bedroom_count - 1 else "bedroom" elif area[i] <= SMALL_ROOM_TILES: kinds[i] = "closet" elif n == bedroom_count: kinds[i] = ("office" if rng.random() < _house_study_share(plan.profile) else "storage") else: kinds[i] =

nodes.name: off_hall
