Cycling the list instead # handed cells and cupboards whatever room came next, so a # station's cells averaged 24 m2 against the game's 15 while its # storerooms took the big ones. start = (i - len(mix)) % len(fill) ready = [fill[(start + k) % len(fill)] for k in range(len(fill)) if spare(fill[(start + k) % len(fill)])] if ready and any(k in ROOM_MEDIAN_AREA for k in ready): kind = min(ready, key=lambda k: abs( ROOM_MEDIAN_AREA.get(k, 25) - room.area)) else: # Every fill kind is spent. Carry on round the list from # where this room falls rather than dropping the whole # remainder on the first entry: a big building has far more # rooms than the mix and the caps together cover, and that # gave a stadium sixteen identical corridors and a castle a # floor of beds. kind = ready[0] if ready else fill[start] room.kind = kind used[kind] += 1 # The smallest room makes a far more convincing bathroom than a hall. It # trades kinds with whatever the mix made the bathroom rather than adding # one, or a nine-room church came out with two lavatories in it. Fixed # rooms - drawn with a kind of their own - are neither moved into nor out # of: the smallest one the mix still owns takes the trade. swappable = [r for r in order if not r.fixed] if len(order) >= 3 and "bathroom" in mix and swappable \ and swappable[-1].kind != "bathroom": swap = next((r for r in swappable if r.kind == "bathroom"), None) if swap is not None: swap.kind = swappable[-1].kind swappable[-1].kind = "bathroom"

nodes.name: spare
nodes.body_text: def spare(kind: str) -> bool: per = ROOM_CAP_PER.get(kind) return per is None or used[kind] < max(1, total // per)

nodes.name: _arrange_business_rooms
nodes.body_text: def _arrange_business_rooms(plan: Plan, kind: str) -> None: """Improve related-room adjacency without changing the mix or circulation.""" pairs = BUSINESS_NEIGHBOURS.get(kind, ()) if not pairs: return adj = _neighbours(plan) rooms = plan.rooms def satisfied(pair): a, b = pair return any(rooms[i - 1].kind == a and any(rooms[j - 1].kind == b for j in neighbours) for i, neighbours in adj.items()) for pair in pairs: if satisfied(pair): continue before = sum(satisfied(p) for p in pairs) done = False for i, room in enumerate(rooms, 1): if room.kind != pair[0]: continue for j in sorted(adj[i]): candidate = rooms[j - 1] if candidate.fixed or candidate.is_core or candidate.is_shaft or candidate.kind in CIRCULATION: continue for other in rooms: if (other.kind != pair[1] or other.fixed or other.is_core or other.is_shaft or other.kind in CIRCULATION): continue if max(candidate.area, other.area) > 2 * min(candidate.area, other.area): continue candidate.kind, other.kind = other.kind, candidate.kind if satisfied(pair) and sum(satisfied(p) for p in pairs) > before: done = True break candidate.kind, other.kind = other.kind, candidate.kind if done: break if done: break

nodes.name: satisfied
nodes.body_text: def satisfied(pair): a, b = pair return any(rooms[i - 1].kind == a and any(rooms[j - 1].kind == b for j in neighbours) for i, neighbours in adj.items())

nodes.name: _circulation
nodes.body_text: def _circulation(plan: Plan, rooms: list[Room]) -> int: """Rooms turned into halls until the rest all open onto one.""" adj = _neighbours(plan) where = {id(r): i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1)} protected = set() for kind, minimum in MIN_SPECIAL_ROOMS.get(plan.kind or "", {}).items(): matches = sorted((r for r in rooms if r.kind == kind), key=lambda r: -r.area) protected.update(id(r) for r in matches[:minimum]) free = [where[id(r)] for r in rooms if (r.kind or "") not in CIRCULATION and id(r) not in protected] seeds = [where[id(r)] for r in rooms if (r.kind or "") in CIRCULATION] kinds: dict[int, str] = {} made = _more_halls(plan, adj, free, kinds, seeds, len(free) // ROOMS_PER_HALL) for i, kind in kinds.items(): plan.rooms[i - 1].kind = kind return made

nodes.name: layout_preview.py
nodes.body_text: """A picture of what the building step decided, to look at before compiling. Compiling a big map takes the best part of an hour, and the settings that shape it (spawn density, apartment share, street scale) are only judged by looking at the result. This draws the ground, every building coloured by what it is, and optionally how many zombies each part of the map will start with, from files the build already wrote - so it takes a second and needs no WorldEd. """ from __future__ import annotations import csv import json import os import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from .bitmaps import read_rgb MAX_SIDE = 2400 # Kinds the build makes, with fixed colours so a colour means the same thing on # every map. Anything else gets the grey at the end. KIND_COLOURS = { "house": (240, 200, 80), "apartment": (230, 120, 60), "shop": (70, 140, 230), "restaurant": (230, 80, 160), "shed": (170, 170, 170), "school": (90, 200, 120), "civic": (150, 110, 220), "church": (250, 250, 250), "medical": (230, 60, 60), "industrial": (110, 90, 70), "fire": (255, 120, 0), "police": (40, 70, 200), "library": (120, 220, 220), "stadium": (60, 160, 90), "mall": (200, 60, 200), } OTHER = (200, 200, 200) LAYERS = ("kinds", "zombies")

nodes.name: _info
nodes.body_text: def _info(map_dir: str) -> tuple[str, dict]: name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(map_dir)) with open(os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}_info.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f: return name, json.load(f)

nodes.name: _step
nodes.body_text: def _step(width: int, height: int) -> int: return max(1, -(-max(width, height) // MAX_SIDE))

nodes.name: draw
nodes.signature: def draw(map_dir: str, layer: str = "kinds") -> Image.Image
nodes.body_text: def draw(map_dir: str, layer: str = "kinds") -> Image.Image: """The preview as a PIL image. `layer` is "kinds" (buildings by use) or "zombies" (buildings in outline over a heat map of the spawn map).""" name, info = _info(map_dir) width, height = info["width_tiles"], info["height_tiles"] step = _step(width, height) base = Image.fromarray(read_rgb(os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}.bmp"), step=step)) # Washed out: the colours drawn on top are what is being looked at. base = Image.blend(base, Image.new("RGB", base.size, (235, 235, 235)), 0.55) rows = [] csv_path = os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}_placements.csv") if os.path.exists(csv_path): with open(csv_path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f: rows = list(csv.DictReader(f)) if layer == "zombies": spawn_path = os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}_ZombieSpawnMap.bmp") if os.path.exists(spawn_path): # Written as a grey picture the size of the map in tenths, but # stored as 24-bit, so the red channel is the level. spawn = read_rgb(spawn_path)[:, :, 0] top = max(1, int(spawn.max())) heat = Image.fromarray((spawn.astype(np.float32) / top * 255).astype(np.uint8)) heat = heat.resize(base.size, Image.BILINEAR) h = np.asarray(heat).astype(np.float32) / 255.0 arr = np.asarray(base).astype(np.float32) red = np.array([220, 30, 30], dtype=np.float32) arr = arr * (1 - 0.8 * h[..., None]) + red * (0.8 * h[..., None]) base = Image.fromarray(arr.astype(np.uint8)) pen = ImageDraw.Draw(base) used: dict[str, int] = {} for r in rows: kind = r.get("kind") or "house" used[kind] = used.get(kind, 0) + 1 x0, y0 = int(r["tile_x"]) // step, int(r["tile_y"]) // step x1 = max(x0 + 1, (int(r["tile_x"]) + int(r["width"])) // step) y1 = max(y0 + 1, (int(r["tile_y"]) + int(r["height"])) // step) if layer == "zombies": pen.rectangle([x0, y0, x1, y1], outline=(30, 30, 30)) else: pen.rectangle([x0, y0, x1, y1], fill=KIND_COLOURS.get(kind, OTHER), outline=(40, 40, 40)) _legend(pen, base.size, used, layer) return base

nodes.name: _legend
nodes.signature: def _legend(pen: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, size: tuple[int, int], used: dict, layer: str) -> None
nodes.body_text: def _legend(pen: ImageDraw.ImageDraw, size: tuple[int, int], used: dict, layer: str) -> None: try: font = ImageFont.load_default(size=max(12, size[0] // 90)) except TypeError: # an older Pillow has one size only font = ImageFont.load_default() if layer == "zombies": items = [("more zombies = redder", (220, 30, 30), None)] else: items = [(k, KIND_COLOURS.get(k, OTHER), n) for k, n in sorted(used.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])] line = max(14, size[0] // 80) pad = line // 2 pen.rectangle([pad, pad, pad + line * 12, pad * 2 + line * len(items) + pad], fill=(255, 255, 255), outline=(60, 60, 60)) for i, (label, colour, n) in enumerate(items): y = pad * 2 + i * line pen.rectangle([pad * 2, y, pad * 2 + line - 4, y + line - 4], fill=colour, outline=(40, 40, 40)) pen.text((pad * 2 + line, y - 1), label if n is None else f"{label} {n}", fill=(20, 20, 20), font=font)

nodes.name: render_to
nodes.signature: def render_to(map_dir: str, layer: str = "kinds") -> str
nodes.body_text: def render_to(map_dir: str, layer: str = "kinds") -> str: """Write the preview next to the map and return its path. It is drawn again only when something it is made from is newer.""" if layer not in LAYERS: raise ValueError(f"unknown layer {layer!r}") name, _info_ = _info(map_dir) out = os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}_layout_{layer}.png") sources = [os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}{s}") for s in (".bmp", "_placements.csv", "_ZombieSpawnMap.bmp", "_info.json")] newest = max((os.path.getmtime(p) for p in sources if os.path.exists(p)), default=0) if not os.path.exists(out) or os.path.getmtime(out) < newest: draw(map_dir, layer).save(out, format="PNG") return out

If not, leave the flag alone: the next container -- in the same building gets the chance instead. local fits, capacity = pcall(function() return container:getMaxWeight() end) if fits and capacity and capacity < NEEDED_CAPACITY then return end for _, item in ipairs(box.items or KnoxMapGunCache.ITEMS) do container:AddItem(item) end filled[box.id] = true print("KnoxMap: left a rifle in " .. tostring(box.id) .. " (" .. tostring(box.kind) .. ") at " .. tostring(square:getX()) .. "," .. tostring(square:getY())) end

nodes.name: inBuilding
nodes.body_text: function KnoxMapResetLoot.inBuilding(square) local building = square and square:getBuilding() local def = building and building:getDef() if not def then return nil end local found = {} for x = def:getX(), def:getX2() do for y = def:getY(), def:getY2() do for z = def:getMinLevel(), def:getMaxLevel() do local at = getCell():getGridSquare(x, y, z) -- Its own tiles only: a building's box can take in the one -- next door, and a terrace is a row of them. if at and at:getBuilding() == building then eachContainer(at, found) end end end end return found end

nodes.name: around
nodes.body_text: function KnoxMapResetLoot.around(square, radius) local found = {} if not square then return found end local cx, cy = square:getX(), square:getY() for x = cx - radius, cx + radius do for y = cy - radius, cy + radius do for z = 0, KnoxMapResetLoot.LEVELS - 1 do eachContainer(getCell():getGridSquare(x, y, z), found) end end end return found end

nodes.body_text: function KnoxMapResetLoot.refill(containers, player) local done = 0 for _, container in ipairs(containers) do refill(container, player) done = done + 1 end return done end

nodes.body_text: local function confirm(player, what, containers) -- The game fills containers on the server, and a client cannot ask it to -- do it again; this is for a game you host yourself. if isClient() then player:Say("Resetting loot only works in single player.") return end if #containers == 0 then player:Say("Nothing to refill here.") return end local text = string.format( "Reset the loot in %d containers %s?\nAnything stored in them is lost.", #containers, what) local modal = ISModalDialog:new(0, 0, 320, 140, text, true, nil, function(_, button) if button.internal ~= "YES" then return end local filled = KnoxMapResetLoot.refill(containers, player) player:Say(string.format("Refilled %d containers.", filled)) end) modal:initialise() modal:addToUIManager() modal.moveWithMouse = true modal:setAlwaysOnTop(true) end

nodes.name: mapstate.py
nodes.body_text: """Which KnoxMap made a map, and what a newer one needs redone. A map is built in four steps - generate, build, compile, install - and a release rarely changes all of them. Cars, for instance, were a missing file that install writes, so a map made with an older KnoxMap only has to be installed again; the Knox County roads setting changes the terrain, so that one starts from Generate. Every step writes the version that ran it into knoxmap_map.json beside the map. Opening a map made by an older release, the window can then say exactly what is out of date - and offer to bring it up to date without starting over. {"stages": {"generate": {"version": "1.3.2", "at": "2026-09-16T20:11:04"}, "build": ..., "compile": ..., "install": ...}} """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import time import knoxfiles STATE_FILE = "knoxmap_map.json" STAGES = ("generate", "build", "compile", "install") # The release that last changed what a step writes. A map whose step ran on # anything older is redone by that step - and by the ones after it, since each # works on what the one before produced. CHANGED_IN = { # 1.3.6: houses where the map has only an address, trees and scrub over # open country, military sites read from military=* as well as landuse. "generate": "1.3.6", # 1.3.9: every wall carries a cut-out for every window style, so a window # has a wall behind it. 1.3.6: rows of shops cut into their units, rooms # small enough for the game to fill every container in them, police # stations, libraries and fire stations, headstones in the churchyards, a # place of its own in the world so two maps can be installed at once. "build": "1.3.9", # 1.3.1: the project is repaired before compiling. "compile": "1.3.1", # 1.3.6: the old map's cells are cleared out before the new ones go in. "install": "1.3.6", } # What each step is called in the window, for the message. LABELS = {"generate": "Generate map", "build": "Build", "compile": "Compile", "install": "Install"}

nodes.name: _parse
nodes.body_text: def _parse(version: str) -> tuple[int, ...]: import re return tuple(int(p) for p in re.findall(r"\d+", version or "")[:4]) or (0,)

nodes.name: _path
nodes.body_text: def _path(map_dir: str) -> str: return os.path.join(map_dir, STATE_FILE)

nodes.name: read
nodes.body_text: def read(map_dir: str) -> dict: try: with open(_path(map_dir), encoding="utf-8") as f: data = json.load(f) return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {} except (OSError, ValueError): return {}

nodes.name: stamp
nodes.signature: def stamp(map_dir: str, stage: str, version: str | None = None) -> None
nodes.body_text: def stamp(map_dir: str, stage: str, version: str | None = None) -> None: """Record that `stage` just ran, with this KnoxMap's version.""" if version is None: import knoxlog version = knoxlog.version() state = read(map_dir) stages = state.setdefault("stages", {}) stages[stage] = {"version": version, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")} # A step invalidates whatever was made from its output. for later in STAGES[STAGES.index(stage) + 1:]: stages.pop(later, None) try: knoxfiles.write(_path(map_dir), state, indent=2) except OSError: pass # a map whose stamp cannot be written still works

nodes.name: record_install
nodes.signature: def record_install(map_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str, title: str = "") -> None
nodes.body_text: def record_install(map_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str, title: str = "") -> None: """Remember which mod folder this map was installed into, so the window can show it, check it is current and take it out again.""" state = read(map_dir) state["installed"] = {"modRoot": mod_root, "modId": mod_id, "title": title, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")} try: knoxfiles.write(_path(map_dir), state, indent=2) except OSError: pass

nodes.name: installed
nodes.body_text: def installed(map_dir: str) -> dict | None: """Where this map is installed, or None when it is not - or when that mod folder has since been deleted or moved by hand.""" rec = read(map_dir).get("installed") if not isinstance(rec, dict) or not rec.get("modRoot"): return None if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(str(rec["modRoot"]), "mod.info")): return None return rec

nodes.name: forget_install
nodes.body_text: def forget_install(map_dir: str) -> None: state = read(map_dir) if state.pop("installed", None) is None: return try: knoxfiles.write(_path(map_dir), state, indent=2) except OSError: pass

nodes.name: done
nodes.body_text: def done(map_dir: str) -> dict: """What has been done to this map, from its files where there is no stamp: maps made before stamps existed still have to be recognised.""" from pathlib import Path path = Path(map_dir) name = path.name stages = dict(read(map_dir).get("stages") or {}) # Nothing stamped maps before 1.3.5, so read what is there. A terrain with # the bridges and monuments file was drawn by 1.1 or later; a project from # before the stamps is older than the parking spaces and pumps (1.3.3), # which is what the steps after it would be redone for anyway. compiled = any((path / "lots").glob("*.lotheader")) if (path / "lots").is_dir() else False guesses = { "generate": ((path / f"{name}_info.json").exists(), "1.1" if (path / f"{name}_structures.json").exists() else "0"), "build": ((path / f"{name}.pzw").exists(), "0"), "compile": (compiled, "0"), # Nothing here says whether it was installed, and the step that puts # the cars and the in-game map into a map made before 1.3.5 is exactly # that one - so a compiled map is taken to want installing. "install": (compiled, "0"), } for stage, (there, version) in guesses.items(): if there and stage not in stages: stages[stage] = {"version": version, "at": None, "guessed": True} return stages

nodes.name: needs
nodes.body_text: def needs(map_dir: str) -> list[str]: """The steps to run to bring this map up to this KnoxMap, in order. Empty when the map is up to date. A step is in the list when it ran on an older release than the one that last changed it - and then so is every step after it, which was made from its output. """ stages = done(map_dir) if not stages: return [] out: list[str] = [] for stage in STAGES: if out: # something earlier is being redone if stage in stages: out.append(stage) continue ran = stages.get(stage) if ran is None: continue # never done; not out of date either if _parse(ran.get("version", "0")) < _parse(CHANGED_IN[stage]): out.append(stage) return out

nodes.name: made_with
nodes.body_text: def made_with(map_dir: str) -> str | None: """The oldest KnoxMap that made part of this map, for the message. Only versions a step wrote down count: before 1.3.5 nothing was stamped, and what is read from the files is a guess at what is missing, not a version to name.""" stages = done(map_dir) stamped = [s.get("version") for s in stages.values() if not s.get("guessed") and s.get("version")] if stamped: return min(stamped, key=_parse) return "an early release" if stages else None

nodes.name: picture.py
nodes.body_text: """A picture of a finished map, ready to show somebody. tools/render_lots.py draws a compiled map the way the game draws it, but it draws exactly the tiles you ask for at exactly the scale you ask for, and getting something worth looking at out of it means knowing the map's size, picking a window on it, choosing a scale that is neither a postage stamp nor a 300-megapixel canvas, and then trimming the empty diagonal corners off the result. That is what this does. from knoxbuild.picture import picture picture("output/mytown", "mytown.png") # the whole town picture("output/mytown", "inside.png", roofs=False) # every room shown An isometric view is a diamond, so the corners of the image are always empty; they are cropped away, and what is left is centred on the project's own background at the size asked for. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import sys from pathlib import Path from PIL import Image BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent if str(BASE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR)) # The background the rest of the project's art sits on. BACKGROUND = (20, 24, 15) SIZE = (1920, 1080) # Drawing is done larger than the picture and shrunk down, which is what makes # the tiles read cleanly; beyond about twice there is nothing left to gain. OVERSAMPLE = 2.0 # A whole town at 1x is a canvas of a hundred million pixels and several # gigabytes. Past this the scale comes down instead. MAX_PIXELS = 60_000_000 # render_lots clamps a tile to 4 pixels wide, so there is no point asking for # less, and 1.0 is the game at its own size. MIN_SCALE, MAX_SCALE = 4 / 64, 1.0

nodes.name: map_size
nodes.signature: def map_size(map_dir: str | Path) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def map_size(map_dir: str | Path) -> tuple[int, int]: """How many tiles across and down the map is.""" map_dir = Path(map_dir) name = map_dir.name info = json.loads((map_dir / f"{name}_info.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) return int(info["width_tiles"]), int(info["height_tiles"])

nodes.name: compiled
nodes.body_text: def compiled(map_dir: str | Path) -> bool: """Whether there is anything to draw yet.""" return any(Path(map_dir, "lots").glob("*.lotheader"))

nodes.name: _pixels
nodes.signature: def _pixels(w: int, h: int, scale: float) -> int
nodes.body_text: def _pixels(w: int, h: int, scale: float) -> int: """How big a canvas render_lots would build for this.""" tile = max(4, round(64 * scale)) return ((w + h) * tile // 2 + tile) * ((w + h) * tile // 4 + 8 * tile)

nodes.name: _within_budget
nodes.signature: def _within_budget(x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int, scale: float) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]
nodes.body_text: def _within_budget(x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int, scale: float) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]: """A window that can actually be drawn, keeping the middle of this one. The tiles cannot be made smaller than four pixels, so past a certain size there is no scale that helps and the only thing left is to draw less. A map of a whole county would otherwise ask for a canvas of several gigabytes and take the window down with it. """ while _pixels(w, h, scale) > MAX_PIXELS and (w > 64 or h > 64): x, y = x + w // 8, y + h // 8 w, h = max(64, w - w // 4), max(64, h - h // 4) return x, y, w, h

nodes.name: _scale_for
nodes.signature: def _scale_for(w: int, h: int, size: tuple[int, int]) -> float
nodes.body_text: def _scale_for(w: int, h: int, size: tuple[int, int]) -> float: """A scale that fills the picture without building a canvas nothing can hold. The drawn width is about (w + h) * 32 * scale.""" want = max(1.0, size[0] * OVERSAMPLE) scale = want / max(1, (w + h) * 32) scale = min(MAX_SCALE, max(MIN_SCALE, scale)) # ...and if that is still too much canvas, come down until it is not. while scale > MIN_SCALE and _pixels(w, h, scale) > MAX_PIXELS: scale /= 1.3 return round(max(MIN_SCALE, scale), 4)

nodes.name: _trim
nodes.body_text: def _trim(picture: Image.Image) -> Image.Image: """The diagonal border of nothing an isometric view always has.""" if picture.mode != "RGBA": return picture box = picture.getbbox() return picture.crop(box) if box else picture

nodes.name: _on_background
nodes.signature: def _on_background(picture: Image.Image, size: tuple[int, int]) -> Image.Image
nodes.body_text: def _on_background(picture: Image.Image, size: tuple[int, int]) -> Image.Image: """The whole picture, centred, never blown up past its own size.""" flat = Image.new("RGB", picture.size, BACKGROUND) flat.paste(picture, mask=picture.split()[3] if picture.mode == "RGBA" else None) scale = min(size[0] / flat.width, size[1] / flat.height, 1.0) if scale < 1.0: flat = flat.resize((max(1, round(flat.width * scale)), max(1, round(flat.height * scale))), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS) out = Image.new("RGB", size, BACKGROUND) out.paste(flat, ((size[0] - flat.width) // 2, (size[1] - flat.height) // 2)) return out

nodes.name: picture
nodes.signature: def picture(map_dir: str | Path, out_png: str | Path | None = None, box: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None, roofs: bool = True, size: tuple[int, int] = SIZE, scale: float | None = None) -> Image.Image
nodes.body_text: def picture(map_dir: str | Path, out_png: str | Path | None = None, box: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None, roofs: bool = True, size: tuple[int, int] = SIZE, scale: float | None = None) -> Image.Image: """A picture of the map, or of `box` (x, y, width, height) of it. `roofs=False` takes the top off, which is how every room and everything in it becomes visible - the view worth sending somebody. `scale` is chosen to suit the area unless you name one. Raises FileNotFoundError when the map has not been compiled: there is nothing to draw until then, and the terrain on its own is the preview picture the generator already writes. """ from tools import render_lots map_dir = Path(map_dir) if not compiled(map_dir): raise FileNotFoundError( f"{map_dir.name} has not been compiled yet - there is nothing to draw. " "Run Compile first.") if box is None: box = (0, 0, *map_size(map_dir)) x, y, w, h = (int(v) for v in box) w, h = max(1, w), max(1, h) if scale is None: scale = _scale_for(w, h, size) x, y, w, h = _within_budget(x, y, w, h, scale) drawn = render_lots.render(str(map_dir), x, y, w, h, max_level=None if roofs else 0, scale=scale) if drawn is None: raise FileNotFoundError( f"nothing of {map_dir.name} is compiled at {x},{y} {w}x{h}.") out = _on_background(_trim(drawn), size) if out_png: Path(out_png).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) out.save(out_png) return out

nodes.name: pictures_of
nodes.signature: def pictures_of(map_dir: str | Path, into: str | Path | None = None, size: tuple[int, int] = SIZE) -> list[Path]
nodes.body_text: def pictures_of(map_dir: str | Path, into: str | Path | None = None, size: tuple[int, int] = SIZE) -> list[Path]: """The set worth having of a finished map, written into the map's folder. The whole town, then the middle of it close enough to see, then the same middle with the roofs off. A town has a middle worth looking at far more often than it has an interesting corner, and anyone who wants a different part can name a box. """ map_dir = Path(map_dir) into = Path(into) if into else map_dir / "pictures" into.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) w, h = map_size(map_dir) close = min(320, max(120, min(w, h) // 3)) middle = (max(0, w // 2 - close // 2), max(0, h // 2 - close // 2), close, close) wanted = [("town.png", (0, 0, w, h), True), ("close.png", middle, True), ("inside.png", middle, False)] made = [] for filename, box, roofs in wanted: try: picture(map_dir, into / filename, box=box, roofs=roofs, size=size) except FileNotFoundError: continue made.append(into / filename) return made

nodes.name: placement.py
nodes.body_text: """Where a map stands in the game's world, chosen rather than guessed. Project Zomboid's world is one grid shared by every map installed. Knox County sits in the corner of it, and KnoxMap has always dropped a generated map east of the vanilla map and east again of any other KnoxMap map already installed (knoxbuild/world.py, choose_origin), which keeps maps from landing on top of each other and is the one thing nobody gets to decide: whether the new town is north of Louisville or two counties west of it, whether two of your own maps sit side by side as one sprawl or at opposite ends of the world. This is that decision, handed over. A place chosen here is remembered beside the map (`placement.json`) and the build uses it instead of packing the map in automatically. Moving one that is already built is three small rewrites, because everything in the project is written relative to its own corner and the world origin is added at the end: the .pzw <worldOrigin origin="x,y"/>, in 300-tile cells worldmap.xml <cell x= y=>, the same cells; its points are cell-relative streets.xml and worldmap-annotations.lua world tiles and then the map has to be compiled again, because the compiled files are named for the 256-tile cells they land in and 300 does not divide into 256. With the Rust compiler that is a minute on a map that took an hour to build, which is why choosing the place afterwards is worth doing at all. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import re import knoxfiles from .world import CELL_SIZE, _installed_boxes, _project_box # Knox County, in 300-tile cells. The vanilla map is 78 x 63 compiled cells of # 256 tiles - 19968 x 16128 tiles - which is 67 x 54 cells of 300. VANILLA_BOX = (0, 0, 67, 54) VANILLA_NAME = "Knox County (the vanilla map)" # How far out a map may be put. The game holds a grid covering every cell any # map uses, so a map parked at cell 10,000 is a world almost entirely of # nothing, and the paper map draws the town as a speck in the corner of it. MAX_CELL = 400 PLACEMENT_FILE = "placement.json" LOT_NAME = re.compile(r"^(?:world_)?(?:.*?_)?(\d+)_(\d+)\.(lotheader|lotpack)$") # ---- the world as it really is ---------------------------------------------- # # Boxes are enough to put a map somewhere, and not enough to see what you are # putting it next to: Knox County is not a rectangle, it is 4,065 cells with # bites out of it, and the vanilla world is eight maps rather than one. These # read the cells on disk - the game's own folders and every map installed - # and hand the window their real shape. COMPILED_CELL = 256 CELL_NAME = re.compile(r"^(\d+)_(\d+)\.lotheader$") TILE_NAME = re.compile(r"(\d+)/tile(\d+)x(\d+)\.png") # The game draws its own map from a pyramid of tiles shipped beside it: # # media/maps/<map>/pyramid.zip # pyramid.txt VERSION=1 / bounds=0 0 19968 16128 / imageSize=... # <level>/tile<x>x<y>.png 256 px tiles, each level half the one # before it # # so the picture of Knox County - and of any installed map that ships one - # can be put on the world exactly where it belongs, instead of a grey box the # shape of its cells. It is the player's own copy of the game being read, and # the picture never leaves their PC: it is assembled into the app's cache and # shown in the window. PYRAMID = "pyramid.zip" PICTURE_MAX_PX = 1600 # a world picture bigger than this is wasted # ---- moving one that has already been built --------------------------------- # ---- a road from one map to the next ---------------------------------------- # # Two maps in one world have empty grid between them: no ground, no road, # nothing to drive along. A road drawn across that gap becomes a map of its own # - a strip of country with that road down it - built, compiled and installed # by the same steps as any other map. # # Two things decide whether it looks like anywhere. It is built at the scale of # the map it joins, so its road is the same width in tiles as the roads it # meets - a road built at a metre a tile against a map built at two is twice as # wide as the street it runs into. And it is not a road on bare grass: a road # between two towns runs past woods, fields and hedges, which is what the land # either side of it is made of here. LINK_MARGIN_CELLS = 1 # cells of ground either side of the road LINK_MAX_CELLS = 2500 # a link bigger than this is a map, not a road VERGE_M = 14.0 # grass between the road and whatever is beyond SCENERY_STEP_M = 150.0 # how often the land either side changes SCENERY_DEPTH_M = (60.0, 230.0) # What the country between two towns is made of, and how much of each. SCENERY = (("forest", 34), ("farmland", 26), ("scrub", 12), ("grass", 10), ("orchard", 6), ("forest", 12))

nodes.name: saved
nodes.signature: def saved(out_dir: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def saved(out_dir: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """The place chosen for this map, or None while it is packed in for you.""" try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, PLACEMENT_FILE), encoding="utf-8") as f: data = json.load(f) return int(data["cell_x"]), int(data["cell_y"]) except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError): return None

nodes.name: standalone
nodes.body_text: def standalone(out_dir: str) -> bool: """Whether this map is built to be played without Knox County.""" try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, PLACEMENT_FILE), encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f).get("standalone") is True except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError): return False

nodes.name: save
nodes.signature: def save(out_dir: str, cells, standalone_flag: bool | None = None) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def save(out_dir: str, cells, standalone_flag: bool | None = None) -> tuple[int, int]: """Remember the place chosen; the standalone choice is kept unless one is given.""" x, y = clamp(cells) keep = standalone(out_dir) if standalone_flag is None else bool(standalone_flag) os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True) path = os.path.join(out_dir, PLACEMENT_FILE) tmp = path + ".part" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"cell_x": x, "cell_y": y, "standalone": keep}, f) os.replace(tmp, path) return x, y

nodes.name: set_standalone
nodes.signature: def set_standalone(out_dir: str, map_name: str, on: bool) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def set_standalone(out_dir: str, map_name: str, on: bool) -> dict: """Make the map standalone, or take it back to sharing the world. A standalone map is the only one in its world, so it goes to the corner, cell 0,0, where the world is smallest. Taking it back leaves it where it stands: the player picks a new place, or has one picked for them.""" if on: save(out_dir, (0, 0), standalone_flag=True) return move(out_dir, map_name, (0, 0), remember=False) here = where_is(out_dir, map_name, automatic=False) where, was = here["cell"] or (0, 0), here["built"] save(out_dir, where, standalone_flag=False) # Standing it back down leaves it parked where standalone put it, but the # lots in `lots/` are named for wherever it was last compiled - cell 0,0 is # not where they are - so this is the same question `move` asks, and not a # "no" written down here. Install refuses a map whose lots name another # place as "moved since it was last compiled", and said so however often it # was compiled again. return {"origin": list(where), "was": list(was) if was else None, "rewrote": [], "needsBuild": False, "needsCompile": not lots_match(out_dir, where)}

nodes.name: forget
nodes.body_text: def forget(out_dir: str) -> bool: """Back to being packed in beside whatever else is installed.""" try: os.remove(os.path.join(out_dir, PLACEMENT_FILE)) return True except OSError: return False

nodes.name: clamp
nodes.signature: def clamp(cells) -> tuple[int, int]: # A string is a sequence too, and "70,0" read as a pair of items is cell # 7,0 - a map quietly put somewhere nobody asked for, on top of Knox # County. Only a real pair of numbers is a place.
nodes.body_text: def clamp(cells) -> tuple[int, int]: # A string is a sequence too, and "70,0" read as a pair of items is cell # 7,0 - a map quietly put somewhere nobody asked for, on top of Knox # County. Only a real pair of numbers is a place. if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)) or len(cells) != 2: raise ValueError("A place is two whole numbers: the cell across and down.") try: x, y = int(cells[0]), int(cells[1]) except (TypeError, ValueError): raise ValueError("A place is two whole numbers: the cell across and down.") if not (0 <= x <= MAX_CELL and 0 <= y <= MAX_CELL): raise ValueError(f"A map goes between cell 0 and cell {MAX_CELL}; " f"further out is a world of empty grid.") return x, y

nodes.name: project_origin
nodes.signature: def project_origin(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def project_origin(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """Where the project on disk was last built, from its .pzw.""" box = _project_box(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.pzw")) return (box[0], box[1]) if box else None

nodes.name: project_size
nodes.signature: def project_size(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def project_size(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int]: """How many cells across and down this map is.""" box = _project_box(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.pzw")) if box: return box[2], box[3] try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_info.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f: info = json.load(f) return int(info.get("cells_x") or 0), int(info.get("cells_y") or 0) except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError): return 0, 0

nodes.name: compiled_corner
nodes.signature: def compiled_corner(out_dir: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def compiled_corner(out_dir: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None: """The north-west compiled cell on disk, or None if nothing is compiled. Compiled files are named for the 256-tile cell they hold, so this is what says where the lots in `lots/` actually are - whatever the project now says about where the map should be. """ lots = os.path.join(out_dir, "lots") found = [] try: entries = os.listdir(lots) except OSError: return None for entry in entries: m = LOT_NAME.match(entry) if m: found.append((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))) if not found: return None return min(c[0] for c in found), min(c[1] for c in found)

nodes.name: lots_match
nodes.signature: def lots_match(out_dir: str, cells: tuple[int, int] | None) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def lots_match(out_dir: str, cells: tuple[int, int] | None) -> bool: """Do the compiled lots sit where the map is now meant to be? False means the map has been moved since it was compiled, so installing it as it stands would ship cells under one set of names and a paper map and spawn points pointing somewhere else. """ corner = compiled_corner(out_dir) if corner is None or cells is None: return True tx, ty = cells[0] * CELL_SIZE, cells[1] * CELL_SIZE return corner == (tx // 256, ty // 256)

nodes.name: where_is
nodes.signature: def where_is(out_dir: str, map_name: str, automatic: bool = True) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def where_is(out_dir: str, map_name: str, automatic: bool = True) -> dict: """Where this map stands, and which record says so - the one answer. Three things know where a map is: the place chosen for it (`placement.json`), the world origin its own `.pzw` was last built with, and the names of the compiled lots in `lots/`. They disagree, by design - a map moved after it was compiled has lots naming the old place, and one that has never been compiled has none at all - but each caller used to read them itself, in its own order. That is how one of them could believe the map was at 70,0 while another read 0,0, and why install refused a map as "moved since it was last compiled" while the window said it was ready. chosen what the player picked (standalone parks at 0,0) built what the project itself was last built at automatic a free cell, when neither of those says anything compiled where the lots really are, in compiled cells matches whether the lots are where the map is going Every caller asks this instead of reading the three, so there is one order of precedence rather than four. """ from .world import choose_origin width, height = project_size(out_dir, map_name) chosen = saved(out_dir) built = project_origin(out_dir, map_name) cell = chosen or built if cell is None and automatic: cell = choose_origin(out_dir, width, height) return { "cell": cell, "chosen": chosen, "built": built, "source": "chosen" if chosen else "built" if built else "automatic", "size": (width, height), "compiled": compiled_corner(out_dir), "matches": lots_match(out_dir, cell), }

nodes.name: _cells_of
nodes.body_text: def _cells_of(folder: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """Every compiled cell in a map folder, from the names of its headers.""" out = [] try: entries = os.listdir(folder) except OSError: return out for entry in entries: m = CELL_NAME.match(entry) if m: out.append((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))) return out

nodes.name: _runs
nodes.body_text: def _runs(cells: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[list[int]]: """Cells as [row, first, last] runs: a map's shape without listing every one of its four thousand cells.""" by_row: dict[int, list[int]] = {} for x, y in cells: by_row.setdefault(y, []).append(x) out = [] for y in sorted(by_row): xs = sorted(by_row[y]) start = last = xs[0] for x in xs[1:]: if x == last + 1: last = x continue out.append([y, start, last]) start = last = x out.append([y, start, last]) return out

nodes.name: _map_folder
nodes.signature: def _map_folder(folder: str, kind: str, name: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def _map_folder(folder: str, kind: str, name: str) -> dict | None: cells = _cells_of(folder) if not cells: return None x0 = min(c[0] for c in cells) y0 = min(c[1] for c in cells) return {"name": name, "kind": kind, "cells": len(cells), "x": x0, "y": y0, "w": max(c[0] for c in cells) - x0 + 1, "h": max(c[1] for c in cells) - y0 + 1, "runs": _runs(cells)}

nodes.name: safe_file
nodes.body_text: def safe_file(name: str) -> str: return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "_", name).strip("_") or "map"

nodes.name: _map_folders
nodes.body_text: def _map_folders(): """(folder, kind, name) for every map on this PC: the game's own first.""" try: import knoxpaths except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no paths, no world return try: media = knoxpaths.pz_media_dir() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 media = None if media: maps = os.path.join(str(media), "maps") if os.path.isdir(maps): for entry in sorted(os.listdir(maps)): yield os.path.join(maps, entry), "vanilla", entry try: mods = knoxpaths.zomboid_user_dir() / "mods" except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return if mods.is_dir(): for folder in sorted(mods.glob("*/common/media/maps/*")): yield str(folder), "installed", folder.name

nodes.name: _pyramid_bounds
nodes.signature: def _pyramid_bounds(text: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def _pyramid_bounds(text: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None: """The world tiles a pyramid covers, from its own pyramid.txt.""" for line in text.splitlines(): if line.startswith("bounds="): parts = line.split("=", 1)[1].split() if len(parts) == 4: try: return tuple(int(float(v)) for v in parts) # type: ignore except ValueError: return None return None

nodes.name: build_picture
nodes.signature: def build_picture(folder: str, into: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def build_picture(folder: str, into: str) -> dict | None: """Assemble a map's picture from the smallest level of its pyramid. Twenty tiles rather than the 4,914 of the full one, which is as much picture as a window the size of a postcard can show. """ import io import zipfile from PIL import Image path = os.path.join(folder, PYRAMID) if not os.path.exists(path): return None try: with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf: bounds = _pyramid_bounds(zf.read("pyramid.txt").decode("utf-8", "replace")) if not bounds: return None x0, y0, x1, y1 = bounds levels: dict[int, list[tuple[int, int]]] = {} for name in zf.namelist(): m = TILE_NAME.fullmatch(name) if m: levels.setdefault(int(m.group(1)), []).append( (int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))) if not levels or x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0: return None # Each level is half the one before, so the highest number is the # smallest picture of the whole map. level = max(levels) step = 2 ** level width, height = max(1, (x1 - x0) // step), max(1, (y1 - y0) // step) canvas = Image.new("RGB", (width, height), (16, 18, 15)) for tx, ty in levels[level]: with zf.open(f"{level}/tile{tx}x{ty}.png") as f: with Image.open(io.BytesIO(f.read())) as page: tile = page.convert("RGB") canvas.paste(tile, (tx * 256, ty * 256)) except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError, zipfile.BadZipFile): return None os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(into), exist_ok=True) tmp = into + ".part" canvas.save(tmp, format="PNG") os.replace(tmp, into) return {"file": into, "x": x0, "y": y0, "w": x1 - x0, "h": y1 - y0, "px": [width, height]}

nodes.name: picture_for
nodes.signature: def picture_for(name: str, cache_dir: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def picture_for(name: str, cache_dir: str) -> dict | None: """A map's picture by name, assembled on the first ask and kept.""" for folder, _kind, found in _map_folders(): if found != name: continue into = os.path.join(cache_dir, "world", f"{safe_file(found)}.png") source = os.path.join(folder, PYRAMID) try: if os.path.getmtime(into) >= os.path.getmtime(source): import zipfile from PIL import Image with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as zf: bounds = _pyramid_bounds( zf.read("pyramid.txt").decode("utf-8", "replace")) with Image.open(into) as im: size = im.size if bounds: return {"file": into, "x": bounds[0], "y": bounds[1], "w": bounds[2] - bounds[0], "h": bounds[3] - bounds[1], "px": list(size)} except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no cache, build it pass return build_picture(folder, into) return None

nodes.name: _with_pictures
nodes.signature: def _with_pictures(maps: list[dict], cache_dir: str | None) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def _with_pictures(maps: list[dict], cache_dir: str | None) -> list[dict]: """Each map that has a picture, with the world tiles it covers. Done here rather than when the window asks for each one, because a picture is only worth drawing if the window knows where to put it, and that is the same answer every time. """ if not cache_dir: for found in maps: found["picture"] = False return maps for found in maps: if not found.get("picture"): continue where = picture_for(found["name"], cache_dir) found["picture"] = bool(where) if where: found["pictureBox"] = {k: where[k] for k in ("x", "y", "w", "h")} return maps

nodes.name: world_maps
nodes.signature: def world_maps(own_mod: str | None = None) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def world_maps(own_mod: str | None = None) -> list[dict]: """Every map on this PC, in compiled cells: the game's own and the installed mods. What the window draws the world from. `own_mod` is the mod folder the map being placed was installed into: its own installed copy is not another map, and was drawn as one, a second square of the same town behind it.""" own = os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(own_mod)) + os.sep if own_mod else None out = [] for folder, kind, name in _map_folders(): if own and os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(folder)).startswith(own): continue found = _map_folder(folder, kind, name) if found: # Whether the game ships a picture of it, which the window asks # for separately. found["picture"] = os.path.exists(os.path.join(folder, PYRAMID)) out.append(found) return out

nodes.name: installed_maps
nodes.body_text: def installed_maps() -> list[dict]: """Every map already installed on this PC, in cells.""" out = [] for x, y, w, h in _installed_boxes(): out.append({"x": x, "y": y, "w": w, "h": h}) return out

nodes.name: overlaps
nodes.signature: def overlaps(box: dict, other: dict) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def overlaps(box: dict, other: dict) -> bool: return (box["x"] < other["x"] + other["w"] and other["x"] < box["x"] + box["w"] and box["y"] < other["y"] + other["h"] and other["y"] < box["y"] + box["h"])

nodes.name: layout
nodes.signature: def layout(out_dir: str, map_name: str, cache_dir: str | None = None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def layout(out_dir: str, map_name: str, cache_dir: str | None = None) -> dict: """Everything the window needs to show the world and this map in it. `cache_dir` is where the pictures of the maps are kept; without one the world is drawn as the shape of its cells and nothing else. """ from . import mapstate from .world import choose_origin here = where_is(out_dir, map_name) inst = mapstate.installed(out_dir) width, height = here["size"] chosen, built, where = here["chosen"], here["built"], here["cell"] vx, vy, vw, vh = VANILLA_BOX mine = {"x": where[0], "y": where[1], "w": width, "h": height} taken = [m for m in installed_maps() if not (built and m["x"] == built[0] and m["y"] == built[1])] alone = standalone(out_dir) return { "vanilla": {"x": vx, "y": vy, "w": vw, "h": vh, "name": VANILLA_NAME}, # The world as it really is, in compiled cells, for the picture. "maps": _with_pictures(world_maps(inst and inst.get("modRoot")), cache_dir), "compiledCell": COMPILED_CELL, "installed": taken, "map": mine, "chosen": bool(chosen), "built": list(built) if built else None, "compiled": here["compiled"] is not None, "lotsMatch": here["matches"], "source": here["source"], "cellTiles": CELL_SIZE, "maxCell": MAX_CELL, "standalone": alone, # A standalone map is the only one in its world: nothing to clash with. "clash": [] if alone else ( ([VANILLA_NAME] if width and height and overlaps(mine, {"x": vx, "y": vy, "w": vw, "h": vh}) else []) + [f"a map at cell {m['x']},{m['y']}" for m in taken if width and height and overlaps(mine, m)]), }

nodes.name: _shift_pzw
nodes.signature: def _shift_pzw(path: str, cells: tuple[int, int]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _shift_pzw(path: str, cells: tuple[int, int]) -> bool: try: with open(path, "rb") as f: text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") except OSError: return False new, n = re.subn(r'<worldOrigin origin="-?\d+,-?\d+"/>', f'<worldOrigin origin="{cells[0]},{cells[1]}"/>', text, count=1) if not n: return False knoxfiles.write_text(path, new) return True

nodes.name: _shift_worldmap
nodes.signature: def _shift_worldmap(path: str, delta: tuple[int, int]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _shift_worldmap(path: str, delta: tuple[int, int]) -> bool: """The paper map's cells. Its points are relative to the cell they are in, so only the cell numbers move.""" dx, dy = delta try: with open(path, "rb") as f: text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") except OSError: return False def one(m): return f'<cell x="{int(m.group(1)) + dx}" y="{int(m.group(2)) + dy}">' new, n = re.subn(r'<cell x="(-?\d+)" y="(-?\d+)">', one, text) if not n: return False knoxfiles.write_text(path, new) return True

nodes.name: one
nodes.body_text: def one(m): return f'<cell x="{int(m.group(1)) + dx}" y="{int(m.group(2)) + dy}">'

nodes.name: _shift_points
nodes.signature: def _shift_points(path: str, delta_tiles: tuple[int, int]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _shift_points(path: str, delta_tiles: tuple[int, int]) -> bool: """Street lines, which are world tiles to one decimal place.""" dx, dy = delta_tiles try: with open(path, "rb") as f: text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") except OSError: return False def one(m): return (f'<point x="{float(m.group(1)) + dx:.1f}" ' f'y="{float(m.group(2)) + dy:.1f}"/>') new, n = re.subn(r'<point x="(-?[\d.]+)" y="(-?[\d.]+)"/>', one, text) if not n: return False knoxfiles.write_text(path, new) return True

nodes.name: one
nodes.body_text: def one(m): return (f'<point x="{float(m.group(1)) + dx:.1f}" ' f'y="{float(m.group(2)) + dy:.1f}"/>')

nodes.name: _shift_annotations
nodes.signature: def _shift_annotations(path: str, delta_tiles: tuple[int, int]) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _shift_annotations(path: str, delta_tiles: tuple[int, int]) -> bool: """The text on the paper map: addUntranslatedText(name, layer, x, y).""" dx, dy = delta_tiles try: with open(path, "rb") as f: text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace") except OSError: return False def one(m): return f'{m.group(1)}{int(m.group(2)) + dx}, {int(m.group(3)) + dy})' new, n = re.subn(r'(addUntranslatedText\(.*?,\s*"[^"]*",\s*)(-?\d+),\s*(-?\d+)\)', one, text) if not n: return False knoxfiles.write_text(path, new) return True

nodes.name: one
nodes.body_text: def one(m): return f'{m.group(1)}{int(m.group(2)) + dx}, {int(m.group(3)) + dy})'

nodes.name: automatic
nodes.signature: def automatic(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def automatic(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> tuple[int, int]: """Where this map would be put if nobody had placed it: east of the vanilla map and of anything else installed (knoxbuild/world.py).""" from .world import choose_origin width, height = project_size(out_dir, map_name) return choose_origin(out_dir, width, height, keep_place=False)

nodes.name: unplace
nodes.signature: def unplace(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def unplace(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> dict: """Hand the choice back to the app, and put the map where it would go. Forgetting the choice alone would leave a map that had been moved sitting wherever it was moved to - the project itself says where it is - so the map goes back to the place it would have been packed into. """ forget(out_dir) done = move(out_dir, map_name, automatic(out_dir, map_name), remember=False) done["automatic"] = True return done

nodes.name: settled_origin
nodes.signature: def settled_origin(out_dir: str, map_name: str, width: int, height: int) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def settled_origin(out_dir: str, map_name: str, width: int, height: int) -> tuple[int, int]: """Where to build this map: the place picked for it, else where its own files already stand, else a free cell. A build used to pick a fresh place every time and ignore the choice, so a map the window had placed at 0,0 was built at 70,0: the compiled cells named for one origin and install refusing it against the other, for ever. """ # Same answer as everywhere else: the choice, else where it was built, # else a free cell (see where_is). return where_is(out_dir, map_name)["cell"]

nodes.name: move
nodes.signature: def move(out_dir: str, map_name: str, cells, remember: bool = True) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def move(out_dir: str, map_name: str, cells, remember: bool = True) -> dict: """Put a built map somewhere else. Says what was rewritten. Only the files that carry the world origin are touched; the buildings, the ground and the zombies are all relative to the map's own corner and do not know where in the world they are. The compiled lots do - they are named for it - so they have to be made again, which the window says. """ want = save(out_dir, cells) if remember else clamp(cells) was = where_is(out_dir, map_name, automatic=False)["built"] done = {"origin": list(want), "was": list(was) if was else None, "rewrote": [], "needsBuild": was is None, "needsCompile": False} if was is None or was == want: done["needsCompile"] = not lots_match(out_dir, want) return done delta = (want[0] - was[0], want[1] - was[1]) tiles = (delta[0] * CELL_SIZE, delta[1] * CELL_SIZE) if _shift_pzw(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.pzw"), want): done["rewrote"].append(f"{map_name}.pzw") if _shift_worldmap(os.path.join(out_dir, "worldmap.xml"), delta): done["rewrote"].append("worldmap.xml") if _shift_points(os.path.join(out_dir, "streets.xml"), tiles): done["rewrote"].append("streets.xml") if _shift_annotations(os.path.join(out_dir, "worldmap-annotations.lua"), tiles): done["rewrote"].append("worldmap-annotations.lua") done["needsCompile"] = not lots_match(out_dir, want) return done

nodes.name: _clip_to_box
nodes.body_text: def _clip_to_box(points, width, height): """A line cut to the sheet, as however many runs of it are inside.""" def inside(p): return 0 <= p[0] <= width and 0 <= p[1] <= height def cross(a, b): lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0 for _ in range(24): mid = (lo + hi) / 2 at = (a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * mid, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * mid) if inside(at): lo = mid else: hi = mid return (a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * lo, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * lo) out, run = [], [] for i, here in enumerate(points): if inside(here): if not run and i: run.append(cross(here, points[i - 1])) run.append(here) continue if run: run.append(cross(run[-1], here)) if len(run) > 1: out.append(run) run = [] if len(run) > 1: out.append(run) return out

nodes.name: inside
nodes.body_text: def inside(p): return 0 <= p[0] <= width and 0 <= p[1] <= height

nodes.name: cross
nodes.body_text: def cross(a, b): lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0 for _ in range(24): mid = (lo + hi) / 2 at = (a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * mid, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * mid) if inside(at): lo = mid else: hi = mid return (a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * lo, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * lo)

nodes.name: _along
nodes.body_text: def _along(points, step): """Walk a line, giving (x, y, along, dx, dy) every `step` metres.""" import math out = [] walked = 0.0 for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(points, points[1:]): run = math.hypot(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) if run <= 0: continue ux, uy = (x1 - x0) / run, (y1 - y0) / run at = 0.0 while at < run: out.append((x0 + ux * at, y0 + uy * at, walked + at, ux, uy)) at += step walked += run return out

nodes.name: _jitter
nodes.body_text: def _jitter(ring, rng, by): """Corners nudged about, so a field is not a stencil of the last one.""" return [[round(x + rng.uniform(-by, by), 1), round(y + rng.uniform(-by, by), 1)] for x, y in ring]

nodes.name: _scenery
nodes.signature: def _scenery(points, width, height, seed: int) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def _scenery(points, width, height, seed: int) -> list[dict]: """Woods, fields, hedges, trees and the odd farm either side of the road. Laid along the road rather than scattered over the sheet: what a road between two towns runs past is a hedge, then a field, then a wood, in lengths of a hundred metres or two, with a farm standing back from it every so often. Bare grass with a road down the middle reads as a runway, which is what the first version of this looked like. """ import random rng = random.Random(seed) out: list[dict] = [] kinds = [kind for kind, _n in SCENERY] weights = [n for _kind, n in SCENERY] inside = lambda ring: all(0 <= px <= width and 0 <= py <= height for px, py in ring) for x, y, _walked, ux, uy in _along(points, SCENERY_STEP_M): nx, ny = -uy, ux # square to the road for side in (1, -1): if rng.random() < 0.15: continue # a gap: a view across the fields kind = rng.choices(kinds, weights=weights, k=1)[0] near = VERGE_M + rng.uniform(0, 26) deep = rng.uniform(*SCENERY_DEPTH_M) run = SCENERY_STEP_M * rng.uniform(0.75, 1.15) a = (x + nx * side * near, y + ny * side * near) b = (a[0] + ux * run, a[1] + uy * run) c = (b[0] + nx * side * deep, b[1] + ny * side * deep) d = (a[0] + nx * side * deep, a[1] + ny * side * deep) ring = _jitter([a, b, c, d], rng, min(run, deep) * 0.12) if inside(ring): out.append({"kind": kind, "points": ring}) # A farm, a barn or a house standing back from the road, with a # track up to it. A road with nothing on it for two miles is a # road nobody has any reason to drive down. if rng.random() < 0.22: building = rng.choices(("barn", "house", "shed"), weights=(5, 4, 3), k=1)[0] back = near + rng.uniform(30, 90) size = {"barn": (22, 14), "house": (12, 9), "shed": (7, 5)}[building] along = rng.uniform(20, max(21, run - size[0])) p0 = (x + ux * along + nx * side * back, y + uy * along + ny * side * back) plot = [p0, (p0[0] + ux * size[0], p0[1] + uy * size[0]), (p0[0] + ux * size[0] + nx * side * size[1], p0[1] + uy * size[0] + ny * side * size[1]), (p0[0] + nx * side * size[1], p0[1] + ny * side * size[1])] drive = [[round(p0[0] + ux * size[0] / 2, 1), round(p0[1] + uy * size[0] / 2, 1)], [round(x + ux * along + ux * size[0] / 2, 1), round(y + uy * along + uy * size[0] / 2, 1)]] if inside(plot) and inside(drive): out.append({"kind": "track", "points": drive}) out.append({"kind": building, "points": [[round(px, 1), round(py, 1)] for px, py in plot]}) # A hedge along the verge, in runs, which is what a country road has # between it and the field beyond. if rng.random() < 0.55: side = rng.choice((1, -1)) near = VERGE_M * rng.uniform(0.6, 0.9) a = (x + nx * side * near, y + ny * side * near) b = (a[0] + ux * SCENERY_STEP_M * 0.9, a[1] + uy * SCENERY_STEP_M * 0.9) if inside((a, b)): out.append({"kind": "hedge", "points": [[round(a[0], 1), round(a[1], 1)], [round(b[0], 1), round(b[1], 1)]]}) # Trees along the verge, thicker than the woods are even: a lane is lined # with them long after the wood it came out of has ended. for x, y, _walked, ux, uy in _along(points, 26.0): nx, ny = -uy, ux for side in (1, -1): if rng.random() > 0.38: continue at = (x + nx * side * (VERGE_M * rng.uniform(0.5, 1.4)) + ux * rng.uniform(-8, 8), y + ny * side * (VERGE_M * rng.uniform(0.5, 1.4)) + uy * rng.uniform(-8, 8)) if inside((at,)): out.append({"kind": "tree", "points": [[round(at[0], 1), round(at[1], 1)]]}) return out

nodes.name: link_design
nodes.signature: def link_design(out_dir: str, map_name: str, points, kind: str = "primary", scenery: bool = True) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def link_design(out_dir: str, map_name: str, points, kind: str = "primary", scenery: bool = True) -> dict: """The road drawn between two maps, as a map of its own. `points` are where it was drawn, in world tiles. What comes back is the sheet to build (generator/sketch.py), the cells it covers and the scale it is built at - the same as the map it joins, so its road is the same width in tiles as the streets it runs into. """ import json kinds = {entry[0] for entry in __import__("generator.sketch", fromlist=["sketch"]).PALETTE} if kind not in kinds: raise ValueError(f"No such thing to draw: {kind}") line = [] if not isinstance(points, (list, tuple)): raise ValueError("A road is a list of points in world tiles.") for point in points: try: line.append((float(point[0]), float(point[1]))) except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError): raise ValueError("A road is a list of points in world tiles.") if len(line) < 2: raise ValueError("A road needs at least two points.") metres = 1.0 try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_info.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f: metres = float(json.load(f).get("meters_per_tile") or 1.0) except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError): pass box = _link_box(line, out_dir, map_name) if box is None: raise ValueError("There is no room for a road there: every cell it " "crosses belongs to a map already.") if box["w"] * box["h"] > LINK_MAX_CELLS: raise ValueError(f"{box['w']}x{box['h']} cells of ground is a map, not " f"a road. Draw a straighter one.") # Onto the sheet: metres from its bottom-left corner, y north, which is # upside down from the world grid the road was drawn on. width = box["w"] * CELL_SIZE * metres height = box["h"] * CELL_SIZE * metres sheet = [((x - box["x"] * CELL_SIZE) * metres, ((box["y"] + box["h"]) * CELL_SIZE - y) * metres) for x, y in line] runs = _clip_to_box(sheet, width, height) if not runs: raise ValueError("None of that road is on ground that can be built.") features = [] for run in runs: features.append({"kind": kind, "points": [[round(x, 1), round(y, 1)] for x, y in run]}) if scenery: features += _scenery(run, width, height, seed=int(abs(run[0][0]) + abs(run[0][1])) + box["x"]) return {"design": {"width_m": round(width, 1), "height_m": round(height, 1), "anchor": {"lat": 0.0, "lon": 0.0}, "features": features}, "box": box, "metersPerTile": metres, "cells": box["w"] * box["h"], "roads": len(runs), "scenery": len(features) - len(runs)}

nodes.name: _link_box
nodes.signature: def _link_box(line, out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def _link_box(line, out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> dict | None: """The cells a road may be built on: round the road, out of every map. Two maps may not share a cell - whichever the game reads second wins and the other's ground is simply not there - so the strip is trimmed back out of everything already on the world, including the map it is joining. """ import math xs = [p[0] for p in line] ys = [p[1] for p in line] x0 = max(0, int(math.floor(min(xs) / CELL_SIZE)) - LINK_MARGIN_CELLS) y0 = max(0, int(math.floor(min(ys) / CELL_SIZE)) - LINK_MARGIN_CELLS) x1 = int(math.ceil(max(xs) / CELL_SIZE)) + LINK_MARGIN_CELLS y1 = int(math.ceil(max(ys) / CELL_SIZE)) + LINK_MARGIN_CELLS box = {"x": x0, "y": y0, "w": max(1, x1 - x0), "h": max(1, y1 - y0)} taken = [] for found in world_maps(): c = COMPILED_CELL taken.append({"x": found["x"] * c, "y": found["y"] * c, "w": found["w"] * c, "h": found["h"] * c}) where = saved(out_dir) or project_origin(out_dir, map_name) width, height = project_size(out_dir, map_name) if where and width and height: taken.append({"x": where[0] * CELL_SIZE, "y": where[1] * CELL_SIZE, "w": width * CELL_SIZE, "h": height * CELL_SIZE}) for _pass in range(8): me = {"x": box["x"] * CELL_SIZE, "y": box["y"] * CELL_SIZE, "w": box["w"] * CELL_SIZE, "h": box["h"] * CELL_SIZE} hit = next((t for t in taken if overlaps(me, t)), None) if hit is None: return box sides = sorted( (by, side) for side, by in ( ("left", -(-(hit["x"] + hit["w"] - me["x"]) // CELL_SIZE)), ("right", -(-(me["x"] + me["w"] - hit["x"]) // CELL_SIZE)), ("top", -(-(hit["y"] + hit["h"] - me["y"]) // CELL_SIZE)), ("bottom", -(-(me["y"] + me["h"] - hit["y"]) // CELL_SIZE)), ) if by > 0) if not sides: return None by, side = sides[0] if side == "left": box["x"] += by box["w"] -= by elif side == "right": box["w"] -= by elif side == "top": box["y"] += by box["h"] -= by else: box["h"] -= by if box["w"] <= 0 or box["h"] <= 0: return None return None

nodes.name: population.py
nodes.body_text: """A zombie spawn map drawn from who actually lived and worked there. The first spawn map was painted from ground colour alone: tarmac got crowds, grass got stragglers. That treats a car park and a street of five-storey flats as the same place, and a town's busiest blocks no busier than its bypass. Every building has already been placed on its real footprint with a storey count and a kind by the time this runs, which is enough to estimate how many people were in it. Homes are counted by floor area over the living space one person has. Everything else - shops, schools, clinics, works - by how crowded that kind of place is during the day, because the outbreak did not wait for people to go home. Those people are spread over the map's 10x10-tile chunks, softened a little so zombies spill into the streets around busy blocks, and scaled into the spawn values the game reads. What the game does with a spawn value is not something this can see: the game's own Zombie Population sandbox setting multiplies everything again. So the scale is anchored to the one thing that can be checked - vanilla Knox County, whose spawn map runs 1 to 10 - and left adjustable. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import numpy as np from PIL import Image import knoxfiles from generator import pz_colors as C CHUNK = C.SPAWN_MAP_SCALE # tiles per spawn-map pixel, each way # People per square metre of floor, for buildings nobody lives in. Daytime # figures: a school is packed, a warehouse nearly empty. DAYTIME_M2_PER_PERSON = { "school": 8, "restaurant": 10, "church": 6, "shop": 15, "medical": 15, "civic": 20, "industrial": 60, "barn": 250, } RESIDENTIAL = {"house", "apartment"} # Spawn value per person in a chunk, before the zombies-per-person dial. Set so # a chunk wholly covered by five storeys of flats - about 500 m2 of floor, or # 11 people at the default 45 m2 each - reaches 10, the densest value vanilla # Knox County uses anywhere. Everything else scales down from there. # # Living space was 35 m2 (25 for a city), which is floor per person as a # census counts it - net, in homes. Footprint floor area is gross: stairs, # walls, shops and offices on the ground floor. Measured against real # densities the old figures counted two to seven times the people: central # Paris at 140,000 a km2 where the 4th arrondissement has 17,000, Kadikoy at # 76,000, Tokyo's Nakano at 50,000 against 21,000. At 45 and 50 the census # lands within reach of the real numbers, and this value moved with it so a # town's zombies are exactly what they were. VALUE_PER_PERSON = 0.9 # Share of each chunk's people who are out in the chunks around it rather # than indoors, as a light blur. Without it the map is dotted with isolated # hot spots exactly the shape of buildings, and the streets between them empty. SPILL = 0.3 # People out on the street, per chunk of made ground, before the dials. # # Every zombie used to come from a building, so a town OpenStreetMap has the # roads of but not the houses - which is most of the world outside Europe and # the cities - came out empty: "there's not really any zombies where there # aren't any houses, and all the zombies are heavily concentrated inside". # The streets themselves say a place was lived in, so paved ground carries # its own few, in proportion to how much of the chunk is made ground. STREET_PEOPLE_PER_CHUNK = 1.3 # What counts as made ground: carriageway, pavement, car park, plaza. STREET_COLOURS = (C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.LIGHT_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE, C.PALE_CONCRETE, C.PAVING) # Rows of the map measured at a time, so a town's bitmap is never held in # memory twice over (see renderer.BOX_STRIP_ROWS). GROUND_STRIP_CHUNKS = 64

nodes.name: _ground_shares
nodes.signature: def _ground_shares(path: str, gw: int, gh: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
nodes.body_text: def _ground_shares(path: str, gw: int, gh: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]: """(paved share, water share) of every chunk, 0..1.""" from .bitmaps import read_rgb_rows, same_colour paved = np.zeros((gh, gw), dtype=float) water = np.zeros((gh, gw), dtype=float) for top in range(0, gh, GROUND_STRIP_CHUNKS): rows = min(GROUND_STRIP_CHUNKS, gh - top) # Only this strip is read. The picture used to be opened and converted # whole first, which held it twice over - what the strips were there # to avoid. strip = read_rgb_rows(path, top * CHUNK, (top + rows) * CHUNK, gw * CHUNK) if strip.shape[:2] != (rows * CHUNK, gw * CHUNK): continue is_paved = np.zeros(strip.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for colour in STREET_COLOURS: is_paved |= same_colour(strip, colour) is_water = same_colour(strip, C.WATER) shape = (rows, CHUNK, gw, CHUNK) paved[top:top + rows] = is_paved.reshape(shape).mean(axis=(1, 3)) water[top:top + rows] = is_water.reshape(shape).mean(axis=(1, 3)) del strip, is_paved, is_water return paved, water

nodes.name: _split_scale
nodes.body_text: def _split_scale(kind: str) -> tuple[str, float]: """('medical', 2.5) from 'medical:2.5'; ('medical', 0.25) from '...:closed'. Set by knoxbuild/hospitals.py from HIFLD BEDS, so a real hospital is stocked with more or fewer people than a generic medical building. """ if ":" not in kind: return kind, 1.0 base, _, suffix = kind.partition(":") if base != "medical": return kind, 1.0 if suffix == "closed": return base, 0.25 try: return base, max(0.1, float(suffix)) except ValueError: return base, 1.0

nodes.name: occupants
nodes.signature: def occupants(kind: str, tiles: int, levels: int, metres_per_tile: float, m2_per_person: float) -> tuple[float, float]
nodes.body_text: def occupants(kind: str, tiles: int, levels: int, metres_per_tile: float, m2_per_person: float) -> tuple[float, float]: """(residents, daytime occupants) for one building.""" if kind == "shed": return 0.0, 0.0 kind, scale = _split_scale(kind) floor = tiles * metres_per_tile * metres_per_tile * max(1, levels) if kind in RESIDENTIAL: return floor / m2_per_person, 0.0 return 0.0, scale * floor / DAYTIME_M2_PER_PERSON.get(kind, 25)

nodes.name: _soften
nodes.body_text: def _soften(grid: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """A small separable blur, [1 4 6 4 1] each way, that keeps the total.""" k = np.array([1, 4, 6, 4, 1], dtype=float) / 16.0 padded = np.pad(grid, 2, mode="constant") rows = sum(k[i] * padded[:, i:i + grid.shape[1]] for i in range(5)) cols = sum(k[i] * rows[i:i + grid.shape[0], :] for i in range(5)) total = grid.sum() return cols * (total / cols.sum()) if cols.sum() > 0 else cols

nodes.name: build_spawn_map
nodes.signature: def build_spawn_map(buildings: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]], map_w: int, map_h: int, metres_per_tile: float, landscape_path: str | None, settings, zoning=None) -> tuple[Image.Image, dict]
nodes.body_text: def build_spawn_map(buildings: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]], map_w: int, map_h: int, metres_per_tile: float, landscape_path: str | None, settings, zoning=None) -> tuple[Image.Image, dict]: """Spawn map image and a summary, from placed buildings. `buildings` holds (x0, y0, mask, levels, kind) in tiles. """ gw, gh = map_w // CHUNK, map_h // CHUNK people = np.zeros((gh, gw), dtype=float) residents_total = 0.0 daytime_total = 0.0 for x0, y0, mask, levels, kind in buildings: tiles = int(mask.sum()) if not tiles: continue res, day = occupants(kind, tiles, levels, metres_per_tile, settings.m2_per_person) residents_total += res daytime_total += day per_tile = (res + day) / tiles ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask) cx = np.clip((x0 + xs) // CHUNK, 0, gw - 1) cy = np.clip((y0 + ys) // CHUNK, 0, gh - 1) np.add.at(people, (cy, cx), per_tile) density = (1 - SPILL) * people + SPILL * _soften(people) street_total = 0.0 if landscape_path and os.path.exists(landscape_path): paved, water = _ground_shares(landscape_path, gw, gh) # The people who were out when it happened, wherever there is a # street to be out on - even where nobody drew the buildings. street = STREET_PEOPLE_PER_CHUNK * paved street_total = float(street.sum()) density = density + street # No zombies standing in rivers and lakes. density[water > 0.5] = 0.0 # How many zombies each person becomes, and the most one chunk may hold - # both per chunk, because a zone may say something different about its own # part of the map. Outside every zone these are the map's own numbers # repeated, so a map with no zones gets exactly what it always did. per_resident = settings.zombies_per_resident cap = settings.spawn_density if zoning is not None and len(zoning): dials = zoning.chunk_values(("zombies_per_resident", "spawn_density"), gw, gh, CHUNK) per_resident = dials["zombies_per_resident"] cap = dials["spawn_density"] value = density * VALUE_PER_PERSON * per_resident # Round at random in proportion to the fraction, so a quiet street worth # 0.3 of a zombie still gets one now and then instead of never. rng = np.random.default_rng(settings.seed) whole = np.floor(value) value = whole + (rng.random(value.shape) < (value - whole)) value = np.clip(value, 0, cap).astype(np.uint8) img = Image.fromarray(np.stack([value] * 3, axis=2), mode="RGB") populated = int((value > 0).sum()) summary = { "residents": int(round(residents_total)), "daytime_occupants": int(round(daytime_total)), "on_the_street": int(round(street_total)), "people": int(round(residents_total + daytime_total + street_total)), "zombies_per_resident": settings.zombies_per_resident, "m2_per_person": settings.m2_per_person, "horde_cap": settings.spawn_density, "chunks": int(value.size), "chunks_with_zombies": populated, "share_with_zombies": round(populated / value.size, 4) if value.size else 0, "peak_value": int(value.max()) if value.size else 0, "chunks_at_cap": int((value >= cap).sum()), "spawn_total": int(value.sum()), # A person-for-zombie reading of the dial, for the page. The game # scales the real number again with its Zombie Population setting. "zombie_estimate": int(round((residents_total + daytime_total) * settings.zombies_per_resident)), } return img, summary

nodes.name: save_footprints
nodes.signature: def save_footprints(path: str, buildings: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]]) -> None
nodes.body_text: def save_footprints(path: str, buildings: list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]]) -> None: """Keep every building's footprint, so zombies can be recounted alone. Redrawing the spawn map needs nothing but where the buildings are, how tall and what they are - but getting that again meant rebuilding every building in town, minutes of work, to change one small image. Masks are packed to bits and stored end to end. """ header = np.array([(x0, y0, m.shape[1], m.shape[0], lv) for x0, y0, m, lv, _k in buildings], dtype=np.int32).reshape(-1, 5) bits = np.packbits(np.concatenate([b[2].ravel() for b in buildings]) if buildings else np.zeros(0, dtype=bool)) kinds = np.array([k for *_, k in buildings]) np.savez_compressed(path, header=header, bits=bits, kinds=kinds)

nodes.name: load_footprints
nodes.signature: def load_footprints(path: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]]
nodes.body_text: def load_footprints(path: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray, int, str]]: data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=False) header, kinds = data["header"], data["kinds"] total = int(sum(int(w) * int(h) for _x, _y, w, h, _l in header)) flat = np.unpackbits(data["bits"])[:total].astype(bool) out, at = [], 0 for (x0, y0, w, h, lv), kind in zip(header, kinds): n = int(w) * int(h) out.append((int(x0), int(y0), flat[at:at + n].reshape(int(h), int(w)), int(lv), str(kind))) at += n return out

nodes.name: recount
nodes.body_text: def recount(out_dir: str, settings) -> dict: """Redraw a built map's spawn map from its saved footprints, in seconds.""" names = [f for f in os.listdir(out_dir) if f.endswith("_info.json")] if not names: raise FileNotFoundError("not a generated map folder") map_name = names[0][: -len("_info.json")] fp_path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_footprints.npz") if not os.path.exists(fp_path): raise FileNotFoundError("generate the buildings first") info = knoxfiles.read(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_info.json"), "what the map is") or {} img, summary = build_spawn_map(load_footprints(fp_path), info["width_tiles"], info["height_tiles"], info["meters_per_tile"], os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.bmp"), settings) knoxfiles.save(img, os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_ZombieSpawnMap.bmp"), format="BMP") summary["official"] = [p for p in official_population(out_dir, map_name) if p.get("inside")][:5] knoxfiles.write(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_population.json"), summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) return summary

nodes.name: official_population
nodes.signature: def official_population(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> list[dict]
nodes.body_text: def official_population(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> list[dict]: """Places OpenStreetMap gives a population for, largest first.""" path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_places.json") places = knoxfiles.read(path, "the towns and villages on the map", default=[]) if not places: return [] return sorted(places, key=lambda p: -p.get("population", 0))

nodes.name: presets.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings built by hand, kept and used again. The generator lays out every building from scratch, which is what makes a map of ten thousand of them possible and is also its limit: it will never produce the one house somebody drew themselves, or the terrace they have been perfecting in BuildingEd for a month. A preset is that building, saved whole and stamped onto a footprint instead of a generated one. A preset is a `.tbx` file - the same thing the generator writes and the same thing BuildingEd reads and writes - so anything that can make one can make a preset: a building out of a map that came out well, or one drawn by hand in the game's own editor and dropped into the folder. Nothing is converted, and nothing is re-rendered: the file that goes in is the file that comes out, which is the whole point of hand-building one. There are two ways one gets used. A zone names the presets it draws from (knoxbuild/zones.py), which is how a particular estate is built of particular houses. And a preset says what kind of building it stands in for - a police station, a church, a shop - and the kinds that are switched on here are used wherever the map has a building of that kind: turn "police" on and every police station on the map is the one that was built by hand, not an arranged set of offices that happens to be called a police station. Either way a footprint takes a preset that fits inside it, chosen from its own seed so a rebuild puts the same building on the same spot; a footprint nothing fits goes back to the generator, because a town with holes in it where no preset fitted is worse than one with some generated houses in it. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import re import unicodedata # The .tbx header: <building version="4" width="12" height="10" ...> _SIZE = re.compile(r'<building\b[^>]*\bwidth="(\d+)"[^>]*\bheight="(\d+)"') _ROOM = re.compile(r"<room\b") _FLOOR = re.compile(r"<floor>") # The generator writes a <floor> for each storey and one more for the roof, so # a two-storey house has three. Counted against the levels recorded beside the # buildings of a built map: of 61 buildings of Manhattan, every 5-storey one # has 6 <floor> and every 6-storey one has 7.
