nodes.body_text: def demo_houses(): """Made-up houses (street at the bottom of the page, "S").""" out = [] # Victorian mid terrace, 5 x 9 main range + 3 x 4 back addition (north = back) w, h = 5, 13 m = _box(w, h, [(3, 0, 4, 3)]) out.append(("vic_mid_terrace", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW") - {(4, y, "E") for y in range(4)}), "terrace_victorian")) # inter-war semi 7 x 8, party wall east w, h = 7, 8 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("iw_semi", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "E")), "semi_interwar")) # 1970s council terrace end 6 x 8 w, h = 6, 8 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("council_end", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "W")), "council")) # 1980s starter home, mid terrace 5 x 7 w, h = 5, 7 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("starter_mid", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "starter_80s")) # detached 1980s, 10 x 8 with an integral garage 3 x 6 at the front west w, h = 10, 8 m = _box(w, h) up = _box(w, h) out.append(("detached_garage", House(w, h, [m, up], "S", set(), garage=(0, 2, 2, 7)), "detached_80s")) # bungalow 11 x 8 w, h = 11, 8 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("bungalow", House(w, h, [m], "S"), "bungalow")) # L-shaped detached 9 x 9 with the back corner out w, h = 9, 9 m = _box(w, h, [(6, 0, 8, 2)]) out.append(("l_detached", House(w, h, [m, m], "S"), "detached_80s")) # semi with street to the north, party wall west w, h = 7, 8 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("semi_north", House(w, h, [m, m], "N", _party(w, h, "W")), "semi_interwar")) # homes over shops (street to the south; party walls both sides, as on a High Street) w, h = 6, 12 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("shop_home", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_house")) w, h = 7, 12 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("shop_flats_3", House(w, h, [m, m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_flats")) w, h = 11, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("shop_two_flats", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "W")), "shop_flats2")) # businesses by class: no homes over them, or a home w, h = 6, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("shop_one_storey", House(w, h, [m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_only@retail")) w, h = 6, 12 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("shop_stores_over", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_only@retail")) out.append(("takeaway_home", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_house@food")) w, h = 9, 12 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("bank", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "W")), "shop_only@bank")) w, h = 10, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("surgery", House(w, h, [m, m], "S"), "shop_only@surgery")) w, h = 5, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("estate_agent", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "EW")), "shop_only@office")) # pubs: a town pub with two bars and the landlord's flat; a village pub, nobody over it w, h = 13, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("pub_two_bars", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "W")), "shop_house@pub")) w, h = 9, 9 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("pub_function_room", House(w, h, [m, m], "S"), "shop_only@pub")) # blocks of flats w, h = 10, 8 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("flats_four_block", House(w, h, [m, m], "S", homes=4), "flats_block")) w, h = 14, 10 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("flats_80s_block", House(w, h, [m, m, m], "S", homes=6), "flats_block")) w, h = 7, 11 m = _box(w, h) out.append(("flats_conversion", House(w, h, [m, m, m], "S", _party(w, h, "E"), homes=3), "flats_block")) return out

nodes.name: programme_by_area
nodes.signature: def programme_by_area(storeys: int, ground_m2: int, style: str = "") -> str
nodes.body_text: def programme_by_area(storeys: int, ground_m2: int, style: str = "") -> str: """A programme when the sub-type gives none (rules.programme_by_area); a large house in a period style (rules.period_styles) is a period one.""" period = style in RULES["period_styles"] or "__" in style if storeys == 1: return "bungalow_large" if ground_m2 >= RULES["programme_by_area"][-2][1] else "bungalow" if storeys >= 3: big = ground_m2 >= RULES["townhouse_large_m2"] return ("period_large" if big else "townhouse_period") if period else ("executive_large" if big else "townhouse_modern") name = RULES["programme_by_area"][-1][0] for n, below in RULES["programme_by_area"]: if ground_m2 < below: name = n break if name == "executive_large" and period: return "period_large" return name

nodes.name: choose_programme
nodes.signature: def choose_programme(look: str, storeys: int, ground_m2: int, style: str = "") -> str | None
nodes.body_text: def choose_programme(look: str, storeys: int, ground_m2: int, style: str = "") -> str | None: """A house's programme: its 1993 look (rules.look_programmes), then its storeys and size; None for what the room solver leaves to Build (flats).""" looks = RULES["look_programmes"] if look in looks and looks[look] is None: return None period = look in RULES["period_looks"] or style in RULES["period_styles"] or "__" in style if storeys == 1: return "bungalow_large" if ground_m2 >= RULES["programme_by_area"][-2][1] else "bungalow" if storeys >= 3: big = ground_m2 >= RULES["townhouse_large_m2"] return ("period_large" if big else "townhouse_period") if period else \ ("executive_large" if big else "townhouse_modern") if ground_m2 >= RULES["programme_by_area"][-2][1]: return "period_large" if period else "executive_large" if look in looks and any(len(v) == storeys for v in programme_tables(looks[look])[0]): return looks[look] # the look's programme has no variant of this many storeys (a bungalow # look with rooms in the roof: a chalet bungalow): by size return programme_by_area(storeys, ground_m2, style)

nodes.name: _pubs
nodes.body_text: def _pubs(): """KnoxMap UK's pub fittings (knoxbuild/pub_uk.py), or None where it is not installed.""" try: from . import pub_uk except ImportError: return None return pub_uk

nodes.name: shop_use_of
nodes.body_text: def shop_use_of(uses) -> tuple | None: """The one business the solver lays a ground floor out for: a pub's bar when it has one (its food hygiene record or business rates are the same pub), else the building's only use; None for several (Build's own, for now).""" uses = list(uses or []) pubs = _pubs() pub = pubs.pub_use(uses) if pubs else None if pub: return pub return tuple(uses[0]) if len(uses) == 1 else None

nodes.name: shop_programme
nodes.signature: def shop_programme(storeys: int, homes: int, cls: str = "retail") -> str | None
nodes.body_text: def shop_programme(storeys: int, homes: int, cls: str = "retail") -> str | None: """A business by its homes: none (shop_only@class: store rooms and a break room upstairs), one (a house's rooms above, a maisonette over two floors), a flat a floor, or two flats a floor. The ground floor is its class's (room_solver.json shops); a retail one with homes keeps its first programmes' names (shop_house...).""" upper = storeys - 1 if upper < 0 or upper > 3 or cls not in SHOPS["grounds"]: return None # (a guest house not in a house: Build's) if not homes: return f"{SHOP_ONLY}@{cls}" if upper < 1: return None base = "shop_house" if homes <= 1 else "shop_flats" if homes <= upper else "shop_flats2" return base if cls == "retail" else f"{base}@{cls}"

nodes.name: house_from_job
nodes.signature: def house_from_job(job: tuple, roof: dict | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def house_from_job(job: tuple, roof: dict | None = None): """Build's job for one building (build._make_one) as (House, programme, building id), or None when the room solver is not for it: not a house, a block of flats or a business with one use (or a pub) with or without homes over it (those three need KnoxMap UK's regional record); rooms mapped from OSM, a landmark, a hotel; the room_solver setting off.""" (w, h, levels, commercial, seed, kind, mask, settings, style, label, path, street, retail, uses, hotel, entrances, profile, mapped, garage_door, preset_file, party, *planned) = job roof = roof if roof is not None else (planned[0] if planned else None) style = style or {} if not wanted(settings): return None # KnoxMap UK's regional record (age, dwelling, rooms); without one, a house is # laid out by its footprint and storeys alone info = style.get("uk_rooms") or {} if preset_file or style.get("landmark") or style.get("superstore"): return None # a business with or without homes over it (shops.py's shop_flats, shop): # one use, or a pub (a building tagged as one is Build's "restaurant") use = shop_use_of(uses) if info.get("dwelling") in ("shop_flats", "shop") else None shop = (info.get("dwelling") in ("shop_flats", "shop") and kind in ("apartment", "shop", "restaurant") and not hotel and use is not None) # a block of flats: shops.py's flats, no shop under it (a lift block, 5+ storeys, is Build's) block = info.get("dwelling") == "flats" and kind == "apartment" and not uses and not hotel if not shop and not block and (kind not in (None, "house") or commercial or uses): return None if any(k != "garage" for _, k in (mapped or [])): return None # no mask: a plain rectangle, every square base = [[bool(v) for v in row] for row in mask] if mask is not None else [[True] * w for _ in range(h)] if roof and roof.get("level_masks"): masks = [[[bool(v) and bool(base[y][x]) for x, v in enumerate(row)] for y, row in enumerate(lm)] for lm in roof["level_masks"]] else: masks = [[row[:] for row in base] for _ in range(max(1, levels))] masks = [mk for mk in masks if any(any(r) for r in mk)] if not masks or len(masks) > 4: return None # Build's party edges (x, y, "N"|"W") as the square sides behind them sides = set() for (x, y, d) in (party or {}): a, b = ((x, y - 1), (x, y)) if d == "N" else ((x - 1, y), (x, y)) inside = lambda q: 0 <= q[0] < w and 0 <= q[1] < h and base[q[1]][q[0]] # noqa: E731 if inside(b) and not inside(a): sides.add((b[0], b[1], d)) elif inside(a) and not inside(b): sides.add((a[0], a[1], "S" if d == "N" else "E")) g = (style.get("garage") or {}).get("rect") if g and not all(0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and base[y][x] for x in range(g[0], g[2] + 1) for y in range(g[1], g[3] + 1)): g = None # a garage reaching past the footprint: the solver leaves it out house = House(w, h, masks, street or "S", sides, tuple(g) if g else None, None if (shop or block) else info.get("epc_rooms"), info.get("homes") if block else None) ground = sum(v for row in masks[0] for v in row) if block: prog = "flats_block" elif shop and conversion(info, use): # an office, surgery or guest house in a house: the house's own plan # (renamed in to_building); a period house cut into flats by its size prog = choose_programme(info.get("look", ""), len(masks), ground, style.get("name", "")) \ or programme_by_area(len(masks), ground, style.get("name", "")) elif shop: # shops.py's "shop" has no homes; "shop_flats" at least one homes = (info.get("homes") or 1) if info.get("dwelling") == "shop_flats" else 0 prog = shop_programme(len(masks), homes, use_class(use)) else: prog = choose_programme(info.get("look", ""), len(masks), ground, style.get("name", "")) if prog is None: return None return house, prog, info.get("osm_id") or label

nodes.name: wanted
nodes.body_text: def wanted(settings) -> bool: """The room solver for this building's settings (Settings.room_solver; a zone may set it), unless KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER says otherwise.""" env = os.environ.get(ENV) if env is not None and env.strip(): return env.strip().lower() not in OFF return bool(getattr(settings, "room_solver", 0))

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.signature: def prepare(jobs: list, processes: int | None = None) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def prepare(jobs: list, processes: int | None = None) -> dict | None: """Before Build's pool starts: every house's footprint the cache lacks, solved in parallel here, so the workers only read it.""" if not any(wanted(job[7]) for job in jobs): return None try: from ortools.sat.python import cp_model # noqa: F401 except ImportError: print("room_solver: OR-Tools is not installed; Build's own layouts") return None todo = [] for job in jobs: try: got = house_from_job(job) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - that house keeps Build's layout got = None if got: todo.append((got[0], got[1])) cache = LayoutCache() dropped = cache.prune() processes = processes or max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 4) // 4) got = prewarm(todo, cache, processes=processes, workers=4, progress=lambda i, n, t: print(f" room_solver: {i}/{n} footprints solved, {t:.0f}s", flush=True)) os.environ[PREPARED] = "1" # Build's workers: the cache only (PREPARED) got["houses"] = len(todo) got["stale_dropped"] = dropped print("room_solver:", got) return got

nodes.name: plan_for_job
nodes.signature: def plan_for_job(job: tuple, roof: dict | None = None)
nodes.body_text: def plan_for_job(job: tuple, roof: dict | None = None): """A house's Building from its cached layout (Build's _make_one), or None to leave it to Build's own layout.""" global _CACHE got = house_from_job(job, roof) if got is None: return None house, prog, bid = got if _CACHE is None: _CACHE = LayoutCache() lay = layout_for(house, prog, bid, _CACHE, solve_missing=not os.environ.get(PREPARED)) if lay is None: return None seed, profile, party, uses = job[4], job[16], job[20], job[13] info = (job[8] or {}).get("uk_rooms") or {} converted = conversion(info, shop_use_of(uses)) if info.get("dwelling") in ("shop", "shop_flats") else None return to_building(lay, seed=seed, profile=profile, party=party or {}, uses=uses, converted=converted, homes=info.get("dwelling") == "shop_flats")

nodes.name: dump_job
nodes.signature: def dump_job(path: str, job: tuple, roof: dict | None = None) -> None

nodes.name: load_dump
nodes.body_text: def load_dump(path: str) -> list: """The houses a Build run wrote with KNOXMAP_ROOMS_DUMP: [(House, programme, record)].""" import glob out = [] for fn in sorted(glob.glob(path + ".*")): if not fn.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].isdigit(): continue # .skipped, .errors: not houses with open(fn, encoding="utf-8") as f: for line in f: r = json.loads(line) masks = [[[c == "1" for c in row] for row in m.split("/")] for m in r["masks"]] house = House(r["width"], r["height"], masks, r["street"], {tuple(e) for e in r["party"]}, tuple(r["garage"]) if r["garage"] else None, r.get("epc_rooms"), r.get("homes")) out.append((house, r["programme"], r)) return out

nodes.name: map_houses
nodes.signature: def map_houses(map_dir: str, limit: int | None = None, seed: int = 1)
nodes.body_text: def map_houses(map_dir: str, limit: int | None = None, seed: int = 1): """Real footprints from a built map's .tbx files, for timing: (house, programme, name). Approximate: the street is taken as S and there are no party walls (the .tbx keeps neither); the programme by storeys and size.""" import csv import random from . import buildtiles name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(map_dir)) with open(os.path.join(map_dir, f"{name}_placements.csv"), encoding="utf-8") as f: rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(f) if r["kind"] == "house"] if limit: rows = random.Random(seed).sample(rows, min(limit, len(rows))) out = [] for r in rows: path = os.path.join(map_dir, "buildings", r["file"]) if not os.path.exists(path): continue with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: b = buildtiles.parse_tbx(f.read()) floors = [[[bool(v) for v in row] for row in fl.rooms] for fl in b.floors if any(any(row) for row in fl.rooms)] if not floors or len(floors) > 4 or r["style"].startswith("uk_flats"): continue # flats in a house's outline: a flats programme, later ys = [y for m in floors for y, row in enumerate(m) if any(row)] xs = [x for m in floors for row in m for x, v in enumerate(row) if v] x0, x1, y0, y1 = min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys) masks = [[row[x0:x1 + 1] for row in m[y0:y1 + 1]] for m in floors] area = sum(v for row in masks[0] for v in row) prog = programme_by_area(len(masks), area, r.get("style", "")) out.append((House(x1 - x0 + 1, y1 - y0 + 1, masks, "S"), prog, r["name"])) return out

nodes.name: main
nodes.body_text: def main(argv=None): import argparse ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--demo", nargs="?", const=os.path.join(HERE, "..", "output", "rooms_demo")) ap.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=5.0) ap.add_argument("--only") ap.add_argument("--bench", help="a built map: time solving its houses' footprints into the cache") ap.add_argument("--sample", type=int, default=None) ap.add_argument("--processes", type=int, default=4) ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4) ap.add_argument("--cache", help="cache folder (default cache/room_solver)") a = ap.parse_args(argv) if a.bench: houses = map_houses(a.bench, a.sample) cache = LayoutCache(a.cache) print("stale entries dropped:", cache.prune()) jobs = [(h, p) for h, p, _ in houses] print(f"{len(jobs)} houses; {len({house_key(h, p) for h, p in jobs})} footprints") got = prewarm(jobs, cache, processes=a.processes, seconds=a.seconds, workers=a.workers, progress=lambda i, n, t: print(f" {i}/{n} footprints, {t:.0f}s", flush=True)) print(got) t = time.time() found = sum(1 for i, (h, p) in enumerate(jobs) if layout_for(h, p, i, cache) is not None) print(f"from the cache: {found}/{len(jobs)} houses laid out in {time.time() - t:.1f}s") return 0 if not a.demo: ap.print_help() return 1 os.makedirs(a.demo, exist_ok=True) for name, house, prog in demo_houses(): if a.only and a.only != name: continue lay = solve(house, prog, seconds=a.seconds, workers=8) if lay is None: print(f"{name}: no layout") continue broken = check(lay) render(lay, os.path.join(a.demo, f"{name}.png"), name) print(f"{name}: {prog} v{lay.variant} {lay.seconds:.1f}s stairs={lay.stairs} " f"{'OK' if not broken else broken}") return 0

nodes.name: rules.py
nodes.body_text: """The colour-to-tile rules (Rules.txt) that turn the landscape bitmaps into tiles. Rules.txt is a data file that ships with the mapping tools. Its layout: alias { name = darkgrass tiles = [ blends_natural_01_16 ... ] } rule { label = ... bitmap = 0|1 color = r g b tiles = name | [ names ] layer = 0_Floor condition = r g b } `bitmap` 0 is the landscape picture and 1 the vegetation picture. `condition`, when there is one, is a landscape colour the rule only applies on. A tile entry is a tile or an alias; a tile is picked by choosing an entry (repeats count as weight), then, if it is an alias, one of its tiles. """ from __future__ import annotations import re from dataclasses import dataclass, field @dataclass @dataclass

nodes.name: Rule
nodes.body_text: class Rule: label: str bitmap: int color: tuple[int, int, int] entries: list[str] layer: str condition: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None

nodes.name: Ruleset
nodes.body_text: class Ruleset: aliases: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict) rules: list[Rule] = field(default_factory=list) def for_bitmap(self, bitmap: int) -> list[Rule]: return [r for r in self.rules if r.bitmap == bitmap]

nodes.name: for_bitmap
nodes.body_text: def for_bitmap(self, bitmap: int) -> list[Rule]: return [r for r in self.rules if r.bitmap == bitmap]

nodes.name: _blocks
nodes.body_text: def _blocks(text: str): """(kind, {key: str | list[str]}) for every `alias {}` / `rule {}` block.""" lines = [ln.split("//")[0].strip() for ln in text.splitlines()] i = 0 while i < len(lines): kind = lines[i] if kind in ("alias", "rule") and i + 1 < len(lines) and lines[i + 1] == "{": i += 2 body: dict = {} while i < len(lines) and lines[i] != "}": m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*=\s*(.*)$", lines[i]) if m: key, value = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip() if value == "[": items = [] i += 1 while i < len(lines) and lines[i] != "]": if lines[i]: items.append(lines[i]) i += 1 body[key] = items else: body[key] = value i += 1 yield kind, body i += 1

nodes.name: _triple
nodes.body_text: def _triple(v: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]: r, g, b = (int(t) for t in v.split()) return r, g, b

nodes.name: parse_rules
nodes.body_text: def parse_rules(text: str) -> Ruleset: rs = Ruleset() for kind, b in _blocks(text): tiles = b.get("tiles", []) entries = tiles if isinstance(tiles, list) else [tiles] if kind == "alias": rs.aliases[b["name"]] = entries else: rs.rules.append(Rule( label=b.get("label", ""), bitmap=int(b["bitmap"]), color=_triple(b["color"]), entries=entries, layer=b["layer"], condition=_triple(b["condition"]) if "condition" in b else None)) return rs

nodes.name: load_rules
nodes.body_text: def load_rules(path: str) -> Ruleset: with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: return parse_rules(f.read())

nodes.name: settings.py
nodes.body_text: """Every knob the generator exposes, in one place. These started life as module-level constants scattered across the renderer, the layout code and the zone detector. That was fine while they were my guesses, but they encode taste - how dense a town is, how tall, how glassy, how many zombies - and taste belongs to whoever is building the map. Values arriving from the UI are untrusted: `from_dict` ignores anything it does not recognise and clamps the rest into a range that still produces a loadable map, so a hand-edited settings file cannot turn into a WorldEd crash. """ from __future__ import annotations from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, fields @dataclass(frozen=True) # name -> (minimum, maximum). Wider than anyone sensibly wants, narrow enough # that nothing here can produce a building the .tbx reader rejects. LIMITS = { "spawn_density": (0, 60), "zombies_per_resident": (0.0, 5.0), "m2_per_person": (10.0, 150.0), "tree_density": (0.0, 3.0), "forest_density": (0.0, 3.0), "seed": (0, 2 ** 31 - 1), "true_map": (0, 1), "fill_gaps": (0, 1), "fill_frontage": (0, 1), "guaranteed_rifle": (0, 1), # MIN_ROOM in layout.py is 3, and a building has to hold at least one room # plus its walls. MAX_BUILDING_DIMENSION in the reader is 300. "min_size": (3, 40), "align_streets": (0, 1), # Past 45 either way it is the same grid again, a quarter turn round. "rotate_degrees": (-45.0, 45.0), "straight_roads": (0, 4), "include_proposed_roads": (0, 1), "max_size": (8, 250), "apartment_footprint": (16, 4000), "apartment_chance": (0.0, 1.0), # Build 42 has 32 levels above ground (WorldEd's MAX_WORLD_LEVELS is 64, # -32 to 31), and the vanilla map's tallest tower reaches level 29. tbx.py # always puts a roof floor on top of the last storey, and the roof takes # one of the 32 levels, so 31 storeys is the most that fits. Every storey # is a full floor of rooms and furniture, so tall towns cost build and # compile time - the presets stay low. "max_levels": (1, 31), "vanilla_tiles": (0, 1), "room_size": (16, 400), "room_solver": (0, 1), "building_alignment": (0, 3), "square_buildings": (0, 45), "neighbourhood_tiles": (20, 2000), "style_oddity": (0.0, 1.0), "parking_density": (0.0, 4.0), "basement_share": (0.0, 1.0), "max_basement_depth": (0, 32), # Not a range at all - the page asks /api/settings for the options - # but every knob gets an entry so the settings form can be built blind. "arch_style": (0, 3), "height_mix": (0, 4), # The enrichment layers. String knobs carry an entry for the form's sake. "landcover": (0, 3), "elevation": (0, 2), "max_relief": (0, 12), "ne_context": (0, 1), "region_override": (0, 3), "hospitals": (0, 3), "hospitals_place_missing": (0, 1), "climate_flavor": (0, 1), "winter_look": (0, 3), } BUILDING_ALIGNMENT_OPTIONS = ("real", "smart", "rectilinear", "rectangle") ARCH_STYLE_OPTIONS = ("auto", "cn", "off") HEIGHT_MIX_OPTIONS = ("auto", "low", "middle", "tall", "even") LANDCOVER_OPTIONS = ("worldcover", "osm", "off") ELEVATION_OPTIONS = ("3dep", "flat") HOSPITALS_OPTIONS = ("hifld", "osm", "off") WINTER_LOOK_OPTIONS = ("auto", "on", "off") PRESETS = { # A small American-style town: detached houses, low, plenty of parking. "suburb": Settings(apartment_footprint=600, apartment_chance=0.1, max_levels=2, parking_density=1.4, neighbourhood_tiles=140, tree_density=1.3, m2_per_person=60.0), # The default, and what a European or Turkish town centre looks like. "town": Settings(), # Dense and tall: most large footprints become blocks of flats. "city": Settings(apartment_footprint=90, apartment_chance=0.85, max_levels=6, neighbourhood_tiles=70, spawn_density=14, tree_density=0.6, m2_per_person=50.0), # Scattered farms and barns under heavy tree cover. "rural": Settings(apartment_footprint=2000, apartment_chance=0.0, max_levels=2, spawn_density=4, tree_density=2.0, m2_per_person=70.0, parking_density=0.4, neighbourhood_tiles=300), } DEFAULT = Settings()

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.signature: class Settings: # --- zombies --------------------------------------------------------- # The most zombies one 10x10-tile chunk can be given. Vanilla Knox County # peaks at 10 and leaves 97% of its map empty; 96 here once buried a town.
nodes.body_text: class Settings: # --- zombies --------------------------------------------------------- # The most zombies one 10x10-tile chunk can be given. Vanilla Knox County # peaks at 10 and leaves 97% of its map empty; 96 here once buried a town. spawn_density: int = 10 # How many zombies each person who lived or worked here becomes. The # spawn map is drawn from an estimate of where people were; this scales it. zombies_per_resident: float = 1.0 # Floor area per resident, in square metres. It is what turns a # building's floor area into a head count. The floor area is gross - the # whole footprint on every storey, stairs and shop fronts included - so # this runs higher than the living space a census quotes: about 50 in a # dense city, 45 in a town, 60 or more in American suburbs. See # VALUE_PER_PERSON in population.py for how these were checked. m2_per_person: float = 45.0 # Turn the map so the town's main street grid runs along the tile grid # (1) or keep north straight up (0). Diagonal streets become staircases of # tiles; turning the map straightens every street on the grid. align_streets: int = 1 # Turn the map by hand, on top of whatever straightening did. A city # whose streets run at 30 degrees has every road as a staircase; turned # 30 degrees it is laid out along the tiles. Straighten streets finds the # angle itself where there is one grid to find; this is for the places # where the automatic answer is wrong, or where there are two grids and # the mapper wants to pick which one wins. rotate_degrees: float = 0.0 # How the roads are laid: as mapped (0); in straight runs along the tiles # and on 45-degree diagonals, like Knox County's (1); routed in vanilla # B42's sixteen directions with its own street shapes and curves (2); or # that, with built-up streets kept on the grid and off the buildings (3); # or Knox County straight with the short kinks between runs squared off and # a street kept to one grid line or one diagonal (4, the default). # 2 and 3 take minutes on a town (generator/roadgraph). straight_roads: int = 4 include_proposed_roads: int = 0 # --- terrain --------------------------------------------------------- # Multiplies how much tree cover the map gets: the woods the mapper drew, # the trees in gardens, and the scrub scattered over open ground. tree_density: float = 1.0 # ...and this scales the woods on top of it, so the two can differ. A # mapped forest and a tree in somebody's garden are not the same thing to # play in - one is cover for miles, the other is a yard with a tree in it # - and a map wanted thick woods round a thinly planted town had no way # to say so. forest_density: float = 1.0 # --- buildings ------------------------------------------------------- seed: int = 1 # Rebuild every address the map has (1), or read the map for what is # there and lay the housing out to suit the game (0). # # OpenStreetMap draws a town at its real density. At 2 m a tile that is a # street of five-by-four-tile houses standing shoulder to shoulder, which # is accurate and is not a place anyone wants to loot: a Knox County house # is four or five proper rooms with a yard round it. With this off, about # half the ordinary houses are left out and the ones that stay grow into # the gap. Roads, rivers, woods and the terrain are still exactly as # mapped - only the housing is the game's rather than the survey's. true_map: int = 1 # Fill in the buildings OpenStreetMap has not got, from Overture Maps # (generator/overture.py). OSM is drawn by people, so how much of a town # is on it depends on who lives there: all of a German one, the high # street and little else in plenty of the world. Overture publishes # machine-detected roofprints under the same licence, and where OSM is # blank they are the difference between a town and a few streets. # # Off by default, because where OSM is complete this adds sheds and costs # a few minutes: measured over the same size of box, 60 buildings in # Gifhorn against 761 in Urgup. Needs DuckDB installed. fill_gaps: int = 0 # Build into the gaps along a street that has buildings either side of # them (generator/rendering/infill.py): the shop missing from a row of # shops, the houses missing from a run of houses, built like the ones # beside them. It needs no data from anywhere, only the streets and # buildings already on the map. fill_frontage: int = 0 # Put one military rifle somewhere on the map, come what may. A real town # has no army checkpoint in it, so the game's rifles - which spawn from # army and police loot - may have nowhere at all to appear. guaranteed_rifle: int = 1 min_size: int = 3 # skip footprints narrower than this, in tiles # and larger than this. It was 60, which threw away the largest # buildings in town - the factory, the cultural centre - which are # exactly the landmarks a place is recognised by. max_size: int = 200 # An untagged footprint at least this big is read as a block of flats, # this often. OSM rarely says, so these two decide a town's characte

nodes.name: to_dict
nodes.body_text: def to_dict(self) -> dict: return asdict(self)

nodes.name: from_dict
nodes.body_text: def from_dict(cls, data: dict | None) -> "Settings": """Build from untrusted input, ignoring junk and clamping the rest.""" data = data if isinstance(data, dict) else {} preset = PRESETS.get(str(data.get("preset", "")).lower()) base = preset.to_dict() if preset else {} kept: dict = {} types = {f.name: f.type for f in fields(cls)} enum_options = {"building_alignment": BUILDING_ALIGNMENT_OPTIONS, "arch_style": ARCH_STYLE_OPTIONS, "height_mix": HEIGHT_MIX_OPTIONS, "landcover": LANDCOVER_OPTIONS, "elevation": ELEVATION_OPTIONS, "hospitals": HOSPITALS_OPTIONS, "winter_look": WINTER_LOOK_OPTIONS} for name, raw in list(base.items()) + list(data.items()): if name not in types: continue # unknown key, including "preset" itself if name in enum_options: value = str(raw).strip().lower() if value in enum_options[name]: kept[name] = value continue if name == "region_override": # "auto" or a short country code; anything else keeps the default. value = str(raw).strip() if value == "auto": kept[name] = value elif value.isalpha() and len(value) <= 3: kept[name] = value.upper() continue try: value = int(raw) if types[name] == "int" else float(raw) except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError): continue # unparseable, keep the default if value != value: continue # NaN compares false with everything; keep the default lo, hi = LIMITS[name] kept[name] = min(max(value, lo), hi) # Only a settings file from before building_alignment existed names these; anything # else, a preset or a bare request, takes the default as it stands. if "building_alignment" not in data and ("square_buildings" in data or "straight_roads" in data): old_square = data.get("square_buildings", base.get("square_buildings", cls().square_buildings)) old_straight = data.get("straight_roads", base.get("straight_roads", 0)) try: old_square = float(old_square) old_straight = int(old_straight) except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError): old_square, old_straight = 15.0, 0 kept["building_alignment"] = ( "rectangle" if old_straight or old_square >= 45 else "real" if old_square <= 0 else "smart") return cls(**kept)

nodes.name: share.py
nodes.body_text: """A hand-built building in one file, to send to somebody else. A preset lives in two or three files beside the app - the .tbx, the drawing it was made from, and a line in presets.json saying what kind of building it stands in for (knoxbuild/presets.py). That is fine for a building that stays where it was made and no use at all for one somebody wants to show another player, which is how the asking began: people build a house they are proud of and there is nowhere for it to go. So: one JSON file holding all of it, named `<building>.knoxbuilding.json`, which can be sent over Discord and dropped back into any copy of KnoxMap. Beyond passing it round, it is also how a building reaches the library that ships with KnoxMap - somebody sends one in, and `tools/add_shared_building.py` puts it in `presets/library/`, where every later release carries it and every map can be built from it. Everything here treats what it is given as untrusted. A share file arrives from a stranger over a chat program; `read` is the one door it comes through, and nothing past that door has to wonder whether the name is a path, whether the .tbx is a building at all, or whether the thing is a hundred megabytes of XML entities pointed at themselves. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import re import time from . import presets as P FORMAT = "knoxmap-building" VERSION = 1 SUFFIX = ".knoxbuilding.json" # Caps. A hand-built building of 150x150 over 8 storeys writes about a # megabyte of .tbx, so four is room for anything the editor can make and far # less than a file meant to tie the parser in knots. MAX_TBX_CHARS = 4_000_000 MAX_DESIGN_CHARS = 1_000_000 MAX_SIDE = 300 # a cell; nothing that does not fit on the map MAX_STOREYS = 32 MAX_AUTHOR = 60 MAX_NOTES = 500 # A document type declaration is the one piece of XML a .tbx never needs and # the one an attack is written with: a few nested entities expand into # gigabytes in the parser (knoxbuild/buildtiles.py reads these with # ElementTree, which expands them). A building that has one is refused rather # than parsed, here at the door, so nothing downstream has to defend itself. _DANGEROUS = re.compile(r"<!\s*(?:DOCTYPE|ENTITY)", re.I)

nodes.name: _text
nodes.body_text: def _text(value, limit: int) -> str: return str(value or "").strip()[:limit]

nodes.name: file_name
nodes.body_text: def file_name(name: str) -> str: """What a share file for this building is called.""" safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "_", P.safe_name(name)).strip("_") return f"{safe or 'building'}{SUFFIX}"

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.signature: def wrap(name: str, tbx: str, design: dict | None = None, kind: str = "", author: str = "", notes: str = "") -> dict
nodes.body_text: def wrap(name: str, tbx: str, design: dict | None = None, kind: str = "", author: str = "", notes: str = "") -> dict: """The share file for a building, as data ready to be written out.""" out = { "format": FORMAT, "version": VERSION, "name": P.safe_name(name), "kind": str(kind or ""), "author": _text(author, MAX_AUTHOR), "notes": _text(notes, MAX_NOTES), "made": int(time.time()), "tbx": tbx, } if design: out["design"] = design try: import knoxlog out["knoxmap"] = knoxlog.version() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - the version is a courtesy pass return out

nodes.name: of_preset
nodes.signature: def of_preset(base_dir, name: str, author: str = "", notes: str = "") -> dict
nodes.body_text: def of_preset(base_dir, name: str, author: str = "", notes: str = "") -> dict: """Wrap a preset that is already saved here. Raises if there is none.""" from . import designer as D clean = P.safe_name(name) text = P.read(base_dir, clean) if text is None: raise ValueError(f'There is no hand-built building called "{name}".') entry = next((p for p in P.library(base_dir) if p["name"] == clean), {}) # Whoever built it keeps their name on it when it is passed on again. return wrap(clean, text, D.load_design(base_dir, clean), kind=entry.get("kind") or "", author=author or entry.get("author") or "", notes=notes or entry.get("notes") or "")

nodes.name: read
nodes.signature: def read(data) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]
nodes.body_text: def read(data) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]: """Check a share file. Returns (building, None) or (None, what is wrong). What comes back is built from scratch out of what was in the file, so anything else it carried - a key we have never heard of, a kind this version does not have - is left outside rather than passed along. """ from . import designer as D if not isinstance(data, dict): return None, "That file does not hold a building." if data.get("format") != FORMAT: return None, "That is not a building shared from KnoxMap." if data.get("version") != VERSION: return None, (f"That building was shared by another version of " f"KnoxMap (version {data.get('version')!r}, this one " f"reads {VERSION}).") name = P.safe_name(data.get("name") or "") if not name: return None, "The building in that file has no name." tbx = data.get("tbx") if not isinstance(tbx, str) or not tbx.strip(): return None, "That file holds no building: there is no .tbx in it." if len(tbx) > MAX_TBX_CHARS: return None, (f"That building is {len(tbx):,} characters of .tbx, " f"past the {MAX_TBX_CHARS:,} a shared one may be.") if _DANGEROUS.search(tbx): return None, ("That building carries an XML document type " "declaration, which a building file never needs. It has " "not been opened.") about = P.measure(tbx) if about is None: return None, ("That is not a building file: no <building> with a " "width and a height in it.") if about["width"] > MAX_SIDE or about["height"] > MAX_SIDE: return None, (f"That building is {about['width']}x{about['height']} " f"tiles, and a shared one may be {MAX_SIDE} a side.") if about["storeys"] > MAX_STOREYS: return None, f"That building has {about['storeys']} storeys." kind = str(data.get("kind") or "").strip().lower() if kind and kind not in {entry["id"] for entry in P.kinds()}: kind = P.ANY # a kind this version does not know is no kind design = data.get("design") if design is not None: if not isinstance(design, dict): design = None elif len(json.dumps(design, default=str)) > MAX_DESIGN_CHARS: return None, "The drawing in that file is too big to read." else: try: design = D.clean(design) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a drawing we cannot read is design = None # no reason to refuse the building itself return {"format": FORMAT, "version": VERSION, "name": name, "kind": kind, "author": _text(data.get("author"), MAX_AUTHOR), "notes": _text(data.get("notes"), MAX_NOTES), "made": data.get("made") if isinstance(data.get("made"), int) else None, "knoxmap": _text(data.get("knoxmap"), 20), "tbx": tbx, "design": design, "width": about["width"], "height": about["height"], "storeys": about["storeys"], "rooms": about["rooms"]}, None

nodes.name: load
nodes.signature: def load(path) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]
nodes.body_text: def load(path) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]: """Read and check a share file on disk.""" try: size = os.path.getsize(path) except OSError as exc: return None, f"Could not open that file: {exc}" if size > MAX_TBX_CHARS + MAX_DESIGN_CHARS: return None, f"That file is {size:,} bytes, which is too big to be one." try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: data = json.load(f) except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc: return None, f"That file could not be read: {exc}" return read(data)

nodes.name: install
nodes.signature: def install(base_dir, entry: dict, folder: str | None = None) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def install(base_dir, entry: dict, folder: str | None = None) -> dict: """Put a checked building into a preset folder. Returns what it is. `folder` is where it goes; the default is where somebody's own buildings live. `tools/add_shared_building.py` passes the library that ships with KnoxMap instead. """ from . import designer as D if folder is None: about = P.save(base_dir, entry["name"], entry["tbx"], kind=entry.get("kind") or P.ANY) if entry.get("design"): D.save_design(base_dir, entry["name"], entry["design"]) about["editable"] = True return about os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True) name = P.safe_name(entry["name"]) path = os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.tbx") tmp = path + ".part" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f: f.write(entry["tbx"]) os.replace(tmp, path) if entry.get("design"): design_path = os.path.join(folder, f"{name}{P.DESIGN_SUFFIX}") tmp = design_path + ".part" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f: json.dump({**entry["design"], "name": name}, f, indent=1) os.replace(tmp, design_path) return {"name": name, "file": path, "width": entry["width"], "height": entry["height"], "storeys": entry["storeys"], "rooms": entry["rooms"], "kind": entry.get("kind") or P.ANY}

nodes.name: sizing.py
nodes.body_text: """Room sizes in tiles, and what a flat or a house floor contains by its area. Sizes come from the "kinds" table in room_solver.json (square metres), so the two room models agree. Programmes are lists of Build room kinds, living room first; split_by_targets cuts a box in proportion to their targets. """ import json import os import random from dataclasses import dataclass TILES_PER_M2 = 1.5 # Settings.room_size: 16 m2 = 24 tiles @dataclass(frozen=True) # Build kind -> the room_solver.json kind that sets its size. _FROM_JSON = { "bathroom": "bathroom", "bedroom": "bed_double", "kidsbedroom": "bed_single", "kitchen": "kitchen", "livingroom": "living", "openplan": "openplan", "dining": "dining", "laundry": "utility", "office": "study", } # Kinds the json has no single size for (its hall and cupboards are 0-2 m2). _FALLBACK = { "hall": Size(3, 6, 12, 4.0), "closet": Size(2, 3, 6, 2.0), "storage": Size(3, 6, 12, 3.0), } SIZES: dict[str, Size] = _load() _BEDS = ("bedroom", "kidsbedroom") # Rooms that take up a floor's spare tiles. The rest - bathroom, hall, # laundry, storage, closet - stay at their target however big the floor. GROWS = {"livingroom", "openplan", "dining", "kitchen", "bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "office"} _FLOOR = 9 # MIN_ROOM squared: no room is cut smaller

nodes.name: Size
nodes.body_text: class Size: lo: int target: int hi: int aspect: float

nodes.name: _load
nodes.body_text: def _load() -> dict[str, Size]: with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "room_solver.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f: kinds = json.load(f)["kinds"] out = dict(_FALLBACK) for build, key in _FROM_JSON.items(): k = kinds[key] lo, hi = k["area"] out[build] = Size(*(round(m * TILES_PER_M2) for m in (lo, k["target"], hi)), float(k["aspect"])) return out

nodes.name: min_area
nodes.body_text: def min_area(programme: list[str]) -> int: """Tiles a programme needs for every room to reach its lo.""" return sum(SIZES[k].lo for k in programme)

nodes.name: capacity
nodes.body_text: def capacity(programme: list[str]) -> int: """Tiles a programme fills with its rooms that grow at their hi and the rest at target: past this, a floor wants another room, not bigger ones.""" return sum(SIZES[k].hi if k in GROWS else max(SIZES[k].target, _FLOOR) for k in programme)

nodes.name: room_areas
nodes.signature: def room_areas(kinds: list[str], area: float) -> list[float]
nodes.body_text: def room_areas(kinds: list[str], area: float) -> list[float]: """Each room's share of `area` tiles, by water-filling from the targets. Spare tiles go to the rooms that grow, in proportion to their target and each only up to its hi; past every hi they grow on rather than a bathroom growing at all. Short of tiles, the big rooms give way first, down to their lo, then the small ones; past every lo all shrink alike. """ t = [max(SIZES[k].target, _FLOOR) for k in kinds] lo = [min(max(SIZES[k].lo, _FLOOR), v) for k, v in zip(kinds, t)] hi = [max(SIZES[k].hi, v) for k, v in zip(kinds, t)] big = [i for i, k in enumerate(kinds) if k in GROWS] or list(range(len(kinds))) out = list(t) gap = area - sum(t) if gap > 0: free = list(big) while gap > 1e-9 and free: step = gap / sum(t[i] for i in free) full = [i for i in free if out[i] + t[i] * step >= hi[i]] if not full: for i in free: out[i] += t[i] * step return out for i in full: gap -= hi[i] - out[i] out[i] = hi[i] free.remove(i) if gap > 1e-9: for i in big: out[i] += gap * t[i] / sum(t[j] for j in big) return out small = [i for i in range(len(kinds)) if i not in big] for group in (big, small): slack = sum(out[i] - lo[i] for i in group) if gap >= 0 or slack <= 0: continue take = min(-gap, slack) for i in group: out[i] -= take * (out[i] - lo[i]) / slack gap += take if gap < 0: out = [v * area / sum(out) for v in out] return out

nodes.name: programme_for_flat
nodes.signature: def programme_for_flat(area: int, rng: random.Random, open_plan: bool = False) -> list[str] | None
nodes.body_text: def programme_for_flat(area: int, rng: random.Random, open_plan: bool = False) -> list[str] | None: """Studio, 1-, 2- or 3-bed flat by area; None when below a studio's lo sum. A studio is always open plan: one room with its kitchen, and a bathroom. """ living = "openplan" if open_plan else "livingroom" kitchen = [] if open_plan else ["kitchen"] plans = [ ["openplan", "bathroom"], [living, *kitchen, "bedroom", "bathroom"], [living, *kitchen, "bedroom", rng.choice(_BEDS), "bathroom"], ["hall", living, *kitchen, "bedroom", "bedroom", "kidsbedroom", "bathroom", "bathroom"], ] fit = [i for i, p in enumerate(plans) if area >= min_area(p)] if not fit: return None i = fit[-1] # ponytail: a flat just over its minimum sometimes takes the smaller plan. if i and area < min_area(plans[i]) * 1.15 and rng.random() < 0.5: i -= 1 return plans[i]

nodes.name: programme_for_house_floor
nodes.signature: def programme_for_house_floor(area: int, level: int, levels: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[str] | None
nodes.body_text: def programme_for_house_floor(area: int, level: int, levels: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[str] | None: """Rooms of one house floor (level 0 = ground); None when below its lo sum.""" if levels == 1: rooms = ["hall", "livingroom", "kitchen", "bedroom", "bathroom"] extra = [(55, "bedroom")] elif level == 0: rooms = ["hall", "livingroom", "kitchen"] extra = [(60, "laundry")] else: rooms = ["hall", "bedroom", "bathroom"] extra = [(40, "bedroom"), (55, rng.choice(_BEDS))] if area < min_area(rooms): return None for a, k in extra: if area >= max(a, min_area(rooms + [k])): rooms.append(k) return rooms

nodes.name: split_by_targets
nodes.signature: def split_by_targets(box: tuple[int, int, int, int], kinds: list[str], rng: random.Random, mask: list[list[bool]] | None = None, first_edge: str | None = None, area: float | None = None, touch: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None) -> list | None
nodes.body_text: def split_by_targets(box: tuple[int, int, int, int], kinds: list[str], rng: random.Random, mask: list[list[bool]] | None = None, first_edge: str | None = None, area: float | None = None, touch: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None) -> list | None: """Cut box (x0, y0, x1, y1, inclusive) into one room per kind, sized by target. Recursive guillotine: kinds (first kept first, the rest shuffled by rng) split into two groups, a cut along the longer axis at the ratio of the groups' areas, then each side again. The areas are room_areas of the box's tiles: a bathroom stays near its target while the living room and bedrooms take what is spare. Every side stays >= MIN_ROOM; None when no cut allows it. first_edge ("N" = y0, "S" = y1, "W" = x0, "E" = x1) makes the first kind's room touch that edge of the box. With a mask every room lies wholly inside it and the rooms cover exactly the box's masked tiles: a cut is kept only where each piece, trimmed to its masked bounding box, ends up as whole rectangles - a footprint no guillotine cut can carve gives None (fall back). `area` is the tiles the rooms are sized for, when not the box's own: a box the footprint will clip is sized for the floor inside it, so every room - the bathroom too - is drawn that much bigger and keeps about its size once clipped. `touch` (x0, y0, x1, y1) makes the first kind's room overlap that rectangle or share a wall with it: a hall by the stairs. Rooms come back in kinds order, kind set, fixed=True. """ from .layout import MIN_ROOM as M, Room if not kinds: return None order = [0] + rng.sample(range(1, len(kinds)), len(kinds) - 1) side = {"W": 0, "N": 1, "E": 2, "S": 3}.get(first_edge) # ponytail: node cap, backtracking only happens on masked boxes; a mask # that needs deeper search falls back instead of stalling the build. budget = [400] # Masked tiles of any rectangle in O(1): sums over (0, 0)..(x - 1, y - 1). pre = None if mask is not None: pre = [[0] * (box[2] + 2) for _ in range(box[3] + 2)] for y in range(box[3] + 1): for x in range(box[2] + 1): pre[y + 1][x + 1] = (mask[y][x] + pre[y][x + 1] + pre[y + 1][x] - pre[y][x]) def tiles(r): x0, y0, x1, y1 = r if pre is None: return (x1 - x0 + 1) * (y1 - y0 + 1) return pre[y1 + 1][x1 + 1] - pre[y0][x1 + 1] - pre[y1 + 1][x0] + pre[y0][x0] def trim(r): if pre is None: return r x0, y0, x1, y1 = r ys = [y for y in range(y0, y1 + 1) if tiles((x0, y, x1, y))] xs = [x for x in range(x0, x1 + 1) if tiles((x, y0, x, y1))] return (xs[0], ys[0], xs[-1], ys[-1]) if ys else None def fits(r, idx): w, h = r[2] - r[0] + 1, r[3] - r[1] + 1 if side is not None and 0 in idx and r[side] != box[side]: return False if touch is not None and 0 in idx: # Sharing a wall of two tiles at least, or a door has no room to # go in it and the stairs open onto a bedroom instead. ox = min(r[2], touch[2]) - max(r[0], touch[0]) + 1 oy = min(r[3], touch[3]) - max(r[1], touch[1]) + 1 if not ((ox > 0 and oy > 0) or (ox >= 2 and (r[1] == touch[3] + 1 or r[3] == touch[1] - 1)) or (oy >= 2 and (r[0] == touch[2] + 1 or r[2] == touch[0] - 1))): return False return (w // M) * (h // M) >= len(idx) and tiles(r) >= len(idx) * M * M def solve(r, idx): budget[0] -= 1 if budget[0] < 0: return None w, h = r[2] - r[0] + 1, r[3] - r[1] + 1 if len(idx) == 1: return [(idx[0], r)] if tiles(r) == w * h else None whole, total = tiles(r), sum(t[i] for i in idx) cands = [] for k in range(1, len(idx)): a, b = idx[:k], idx[k:] share = sum(t[i] for i in a) / total for vertical in (True, False): lo, hi = (r[0], r[2]) if vertical else (r[1], r[3]) for p in range(lo + M, hi - M + 2): low = (r[0], r[1], p - 1, r[3]) if vertical else (r[0], r[1], r[2], p - 1) high = (p, r[1], r[2], r[3]) if vertical else (r[0], p, r[2], r[3]) got = tiles(low) / whole low, high = trim(low), trim(high) if low is None or high is None: continue longer = vertical == (w >= h) for g_lo, g_hi, want in ((a, b, share), (b, a, 1 - share)): if fits(low, g_lo) and fits(high, g_hi): cands.append((not longer, abs(got - want), rng.random(), low, g_lo, high, g_hi)) cands.sort(key=lambda c: c[:3]) for *_, low, g_lo, high, g_hi in cands: one = solve(low, g_lo) two = one and solve(high, g_hi) if two: return one + two if budget[0] < 0: return None return None start = trim(box) t = room_areas(kinds, area or tiles(start)) if start else [] got = start and fits(start, order) and solve(start, order) if not got: return None return [Room(*r, kind=kinds[i], fixed=True) for i, r in sorted(got)]

nodes.name: tiles
nodes.body_text: def tiles(r): x0, y0, x1, y1 = r if pre is None: return (x1 - x0 + 1) * (y1 - y0 + 1) return pre[y1 + 1][x1 + 1] - pre[y0][x1 + 1] - pre[y1 + 1][x0] + pre[y0][x0]

nodes.name: trim
nodes.body_text: def trim(r): if pre is None: return r x0, y0, x1, y1 = r ys = [y for y in range(y0, y1 + 1) if tiles((x0, y, x1, y))] xs = [x for x in range(x0, x1 + 1) if tiles((x, y0, x, y1))] return (xs[0], ys[0], xs[-1], ys[-1]) if ys else None

nodes.name: fits
nodes.body_text: def fits(r, idx): w, h = r[2] - r[0] + 1, r[3] - r[1] + 1 if side is not None and 0 in idx and r[side] != box[side]: return False if touch is not None and 0 in idx: # Sharing a wall of two tiles at least, or a door has no room to # go in it and the stairs open onto a bedroom instead. ox = min(r[2], touch[2]) - max(r[0], touch[0]) + 1 oy = min(r[3], touch[3]) - max(r[1], touch[1]) + 1 if not ((ox > 0 and oy > 0) or (ox >= 2 and (r[1] == touch[3] + 1 or r[3] == touch[1] - 1)) or (oy >= 2 and (r[0] == touch[2] + 1 or r[2] == touch[0] - 1))): return False return (w // M) * (h // M) >= len(idx) and tiles(r) >= len(idx) * M * M

nodes.name: solve
nodes.body_text: def solve(r, idx): budget[0] -= 1 if budget[0] < 0: return None w, h = r[2] - r[0] + 1, r[3] - r[1] + 1 if len(idx) == 1: return [(idx[0], r)] if tiles(r) == w * h else None whole, total = tiles(r), sum(t[i] for i in idx) cands = [] for k in range(1, len(idx)): a, b = idx[:k], idx[k:] share = sum(t[i] for i in a) / total for vertical in (True, False): lo, hi = (r[0], r[2]) if vertical else (r[1], r[3]) for p in range(lo + M, hi - M + 2): low = (r[0], r[1], p - 1, r[3]) if vertical else (r[0], r[1], r[2], p - 1) high = (p, r[1], r[2], r[3]) if vertical else (r[0], p, r[2], r[3]) got = tiles(low) / whole low, high = trim(low), trim(high) if low is None or high is None: continue longer = vertical == (w >= h) for g_lo, g_hi, want in ((a, b, share), (b, a, 1 - share)): if fits(low, g_lo) and fits(high, g_hi): cands.append((not longer, abs(got - want), rng.random(), low, g_lo, high, g_hi)) cands.sort(key=lambda c: c[:3]) for *_, low, g_lo, high, g_hi in cands: one = solve(low, g_lo) two = one and solve(high, g_hi) if two: return one + two if budget[0] < 0: return None return None

nodes.name: structures.py
nodes.body_text: """Write the bridges, overpasses and monuments generator/structures.py planned. The renderer leaves a list of tiles, each on a storey and a layer. They go into buildings with no rooms, one per map cell, the way fences do (see fences.py), drawn as the building's user tiles: BuildingEd keeps a grid of those per layer name per floor, and WorldEd lays them over the ground when it compiles the lots. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os from xml.sax.saxutils import escape, quoteattr import knoxfiles from . import catalog as C CELL = 300

nodes.name: build_structures
nodes.signature: def build_structures(out_dir: str, map_name: str, bdir: str) -> tuple[list, dict]
nodes.body_text: def build_structures(out_dir: str, map_name: str, bdir: str) -> tuple[list, dict]: from .world import Placement path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_structures.json") data = knoxfiles.read(path, "the bridges and monuments") if not data: return [], {"bridges": 0, "monuments": 0, "tiles": 0} rows = data.get("tiles") or [] try: with open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_info.json"), encoding="utf-8") as f: info = json.load(f) width, height = info["width_tiles"], info["height_tiles"] except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError): width = height = None by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} for x, y, z, layer, tile in rows: # Only what lies on the map. A railing along the far edge of a bridge # at the map's bottom row stood on the tile below it - in a cell the # map does not have, and WorldEd refused the whole project: "error # reading world, invalid cell coordinates". if x < 0 or y < 0 or z < 0: continue if width is not None and (x >= width or y >= height): continue by_cell.setdefault((x // CELL, y // CELL), []).append((x, y, z, layer, tile)) placements = [] for (cx, cy), tiles in sorted(by_cell.items()): x0 = min(t[0] for t in tiles) y0 = min(t[1] for t in tiles) w = max(t[0] for t in tiles) - x0 + 1 h = max(t[1] for t in tiles) - y0 + 1 fname = f"{map_name}_structures_{cx}_{cy}.tbx" with open(os.path.join(bdir, fname), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(render_tiles_tbx(w, h, [(x - x0, y - y0, z, layer, tile) for x, y, z, layer, tile in tiles])) placements.append(Placement(f"buildings/{fname}", x0, y0, w, h)) return placements, {"bridges": data.get("bridges", 0), "monuments": data.get("monuments", 0), "tiles": len(rows)}

nodes.name: pack_loose
nodes.signature: def pack_loose(bdir: str, map_name: str, tag: str, tiles: list, on_top: bool = False) -> list
nodes.body_text: def pack_loose(bdir: str, map_name: str, tag: str, tiles: list, on_top: bool = False) -> list: """Loose (x, y, level, layer, tile) squares written as one .tbx per cell. A lot spanning cells is refused by WorldEd, so they are grouped by the cell they fall in and each group placed at its own corner. """ from .world import Placement by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} for t in tiles: by_cell.setdefault((t[0] // CELL, t[1] // CELL), []).append(t) placements = [] for (cx, cy), group in sorted(by_cell.items()): gx0 = min(t[0] for t in group) gy0 = min(t[1] for t in group) gw = max(t[0] for t in group) - gx0 + 1 gh = max(t[1] for t in group) - gy0 + 1 fname = f"{map_name}_{tag}_{cx}_{cy}.tbx" with open(os.path.join(bdir, fname), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(render_tiles_tbx(gw, gh, [(x - gx0, y - gy0, z, layer, tile) for x, y, z, layer, tile in group])) placements.append(Placement(f"buildings/{fname}", gx0, gy0, gw, gh, on_top=on_top)) return placements

nodes.name: render_tiles_tbx
nodes.signature: def render_tiles_tbx(width: int, height: int, tiles: list) -> str
nodes.body_text:
def render_tiles_tbx(width: int, height: int, tiles: list) -> str: """A building with no rooms whose floors hold only user-drawn tiles.""" names = sorted({t[4] for t in tiles}) number = {n: i + 1 for i, n in enumerate(names)} levels = max(t[2] for t in tiles) + 1 grids: dict[int, dict[str, dict]] = {} for x, y, z, layer, tile in tiles: grids.setdefault(z, {}).setdefault(layer, {})[(x, y)] = number[tile] out = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>'] attrs = [("version", 4), ("width", width), ("height", height), ("ExteriorWall", C.EXTERIOR_WALL), ("ExteriorWallTrim", 0), ("Door", C.DOOR), ("DoorFrame", C.DOOR_FRAME), ("Window", C.WINDOW), ("Curtains", C.CURTAINS), ("Shutters", 0), ("Stairs", C.STAIRS), ("RoofCap", C.ROOF_CAP), ("RoofSlope", C.ROOF_SLOPE), ("RoofTop", C.ROOF_TOP), ("GrimeWall", 0)] out.append("<building" + "".join(f" {k}={quoteattr(str(v))}" for k, v in attrs) + ">") for entry in C.TILE_ENTRIES: out.append(f' <tile_entry category={quoteattr(entry["category"])}>') for enum_name, tile in entry["tiles"].items(): out.append(f' <tile enum={quoteattr(enum_name)} tile={quoteattr(tile)}/>') out.append(" </tile_entry>") out.append(" <user_tiles>") out.extend(f" <tile tile={quoteattr(n)}/>" for n in names) out.append(" </user_tiles>") out.append(" <used_tiles>" + " ".join(str(i) for i in range(1, len(C.TILE_ENTRIES) + 1)) + "</used_tiles>") out.append(" <used_furniture></used_furniture>") rooms = "
" + "
".join(",".join("0" for _ in range(width)) + ("," if y < height - 1 else "") for y in range(height)) + "
" for z in range(levels): out.append(" <floor>") out.append(" <rooms>" + rooms + "</rooms>") for layer, cells in sorted(grids.get(z, {}).items()): # BuildingFloor's user tile grids are one wider and taller than the # building, so a wall piece can sit on the far edge. text = ["
"] for y in range(height + 1): row = [str(cells.get((x, y), 0)) for x in range(width + 1)] text.append(",".join(row) + ("," if y < height else "") + "
") out.append(f' <tiles layer={quoteattr(layer)}>' + escape("".join(text)) + "</tiles>") out.append(" </floor>") out.append("</building>") return "
".join(out) + "
"

nodes.name: tbx.py
nodes.body_text: """Serialise a Plan to BuildingEd's .tbx format. Schema taken from BuildingWriter in timbaker/buildinged. Two index conventions differ and are easy to get backwards: tile entries 1-based, and 0 means "none" (entryIndex) furniture 0-based, no null form (furnitureIndex) Element order inside <building> follows the writer: tile entries, furniture, user_tiles, used_tiles, used_furniture, the <room> list, then <floor>. """ from __future__ import annotations import random import zlib from xml.sax.saxutils import escape, quoteattr from . import catalog as C from .layout import ROOM_STYLE, Building, Plan, _erika_ready, roof_rects # Version 4 is the first that carries a per-room Ceiling tile. Writing 3 still # loads - the reader accepts 1..7 - but then it silently back-fills ceilings # itself, so we may as well state them. VERSION = 4 # A pitched roof needs room for two slopes; a narrower strip of a house (a # porch, one step of a turned footprint) keeps a flat roof. PEAK_MIN_TILES = 4 # The 30-degree roofs the game's own houses wear, which BuildingEd sizes to an # odd number of tiles across, 3 to 11; a house up to two tiles wider takes an # 11 and a flat strip. Wider than that, the steep 45-degree gable with a flat # top in the middle is all the editor offers. PEAK30_MAX_ACROSS = 11 HIP_MAX_ACROSS = 7 _PEAK_DEPTHS = {1: "Point5", 2: "One", 3: "OnePoint5", 4: "Two", 5: "TwoPoint5"} _NO_CAPS = {"cappedW": False, "cappedN": False, "cappedE": False, "cappedS": False} _SHALLOW_DEPTH = "OnePoint5" # A one-storey part of a two-storey house is pitched too (it was always flat); only a strip # narrower than NARROW_PEAK_MIN stays flat. Set PITCH_LOWER_ROOFS = False for the old roofs. PITCH_LOWER_ROOFS = True NARROW_PEAK_MIN = 2 # A footprint of many wings gives each its own roof, and a steep 30-degree one over a wide # block rises twice as high as the 45-degree roofs of the wings beside it. Past # MANY_WING_RECTS pieces a block wider than MANY_WING_PEAK30_MAX across takes the 45-degree # roof too, whose height stops at three levels. MANY_WING_RECTS = 3 MANY_WING_PEAK30_MAX = 7 # On a diagonal edge the same footprint breaks into many tiny rectangles, and a gable on each # reads as a row of teeth along the eave. In such a footprint a piece under this many tiles # stays flat, level with the wall top, so the eave is one line. MANY_WING_MIN_PITCHED_AREA = 8 # Flat roofs carry plant: bare tar from edge to edge read as unfinished. One # air-conditioning unit per ROOF_AC_EVERY tiles of roof, a vent per # ROOF_VENT_EVERY, and a hatch, kept off the edges and off each other. ROOF_MIN_TILES = 60 ROOF_AC_EVERY = 90 ROOF_VENT_EVERY = 60 # How many room kinds in a building carry wall trim. Knox County's schools # How many different interior wall sets one building uses. Knox County's # figure, measured over 77 buildings in Muldraugh, is 4.48. # # A mall is the exception: every unit in it is let to somebody else and # painted to suit, and the game's own runs to 117 different wall tiles in the # one building where an ordinary house has a dozen. It gets one per room kind # instead, out of the whole list. INTERIOR_WALLS_PER_BUILDING = 4 # One per storey for a mall concourse, so the ground floor seen through the # atrium is plainly a different floor from the gallery you are standing on. CONCOURSE_FLOORS = ("tile_cream", "tile_grey", "civic_pale", "tile_white") WALLS_PER_KIND = {"mall": 99} # run to 0.25 pieces of walls_interior_detailing per 10 m2 and ours to 2.43 # with every room trimmed, so about one kind in ten keeps it. TRIM_SHARE = 0.12

nodes.name: _stable_seed
nodes.body_text: def _stable_seed(*parts) -> int: """A seed that is the same in every process. hash() of a string is not: Python randomises it per process, so two builds of one map picked different floors and trims, and the build could not be repeated.""" return zlib.crc32(repr(parts).encode("utf-8"))

nodes.name: _attrs
nodes.signature: def _attrs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> str: # Nearly every value is a coordinate or an index. Quoting those through # quoteattr, nine million calls for a town, was 40% of the time spent # writing buildings; numbers never need escaping.
nodes.body_text: def _attrs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> str: # Nearly every value is a coordinate or an index. Quoting those through # quoteattr, nine million calls for a town, was 40% of the time spent # writing buildings; numbers never need escaping. return "".join(f' {k}="{v}"' if type(v) is int else f" {k}={quoteattr(str(v))}" for k, v in pairs)

nodes.name: _peak_depth
nodes.signature: def _peak_depth(across: int, shallow: bool = False) -> str
nodes.body_text: def _peak_depth(across: int, shallow: bool = False) -> str: """BuildingEd's depth for a 45-degree peaked roof this many tiles across. `shallow` lowers it: on a garage the full depth is a roof taller than the walls beneath it. """ depth = _PEAK_DEPTHS.get(across, "Three") if shallow and depth in ("Three", "TwoPoint5", "Two"): return _SHALLOW_DEPTH return depth

nodes.name: _roof_pieces
nodes.signature: def _roof_pieces(rects, peaked: bool, roof30: bool = True, shallow: bool = False, gable_only: bool = False)
nodes.body_text: def _roof_pieces(rects, peaked: bool, roof30: bool = True, shallow: bool = False, gable_only: bool = False): """(RoofType, Depth, caps, (x, y, w, h)) for each roof over a footprint. Flat roofs are never capped: at depth three a cap is a storey-high wall of roof tiles laid over the top storey's own walls. A pitched roof is capped at its gable ends where they are the outside of the house, and left open where it runs into the next roof. 30-degree roofs need an odd width across their slopes. On an even one the roof covers one tile less and a flat strip takes the last row, on the side away from the camera (north or west) where it shows least. A house that is a single rectangle gets a hip roof about half the time, as Knox County's do; an L-shape keeps gables, whose ends meet cleanly. """ out = [] single = len(rects) == 1 for rx, ry, rw, rh, caps in rects: across = min(rw, rh) tooth = len(rects) >= MANY_WING_RECTS and rw * rh < MANY_WING_MIN_PITCHED_AREA if not peaked or across < NARROW_PEAK_MIN or tooth: out.append(("FlatTop", "Three", dict(_NO_CAPS), (rx, ry, rw, rh))) continue along_x = rw >= rh # a narrow wing (2-3 across) takes a low 45-degree roof rather than a flat one steep_block = len(rects) >= MANY_WING_RECTS and across > MANY_WING_PEAK30_MAX if not roof30 or across < 3 or (not gable_only and ( steep_block or across > PEAK30_MAX_ACROSS + 2 or across < PEAK_MIN_TILES)): cap = dict(_NO_CAPS) if along_x: cap["cappedW"], cap["cappedE"] = caps["cappedW"], caps["cappedE"] out.append(("PeakWE", _peak_depth(rh, shallow), cap, (rx, ry, rw, rh))) else: cap["cappedN"], cap["cappedS"] = caps["cappedN"], caps["cappedS"] out.append(("PeakNS", _peak_depth(rw, shallow), cap, (rx, ry, rw, rh))) continue odd = across if across % 2 else across - 1 if gable_only: # Stock shallow gables stop at eleven; surplus stays behind the far eave. odd = min(odd, PEAK30_MAX_ACROSS) # Hips only on small houses: across a wide one the four slopes meet # in a tall point that looks like a hat. A quad is cut from the square # of the longer side of its rectangle, so that side has to be odd or # buildroofs paints nothing at all and the house loses its whole roof. hip = (not gable_only and single and odd <= HIP_MAX_ACROSS and max(rw, odd) % 2 == 1 and (rx * 31 + ry * 17 + rw * 7 + rh) % 2 == 0) cap = dict(_NO_CAPS) if along_x: box = (rx, ry + (rh - odd), rw, odd) if rh != odd: out.append(("FlatTop", "Three", dict(_NO_CAPS), (rx, ry, rw, rh - odd))) if not hip: cap["cappedW"], cap["cappedE"] = caps["cappedW"], caps["cappedE"] out.append(("Peak30Quad" if hip else "Peak30WE", "Zero", cap, box)) else: box = (rx + (rw - odd), ry, odd, rh) if rw != odd: out.append(("FlatTop", "Three", dict(_NO_CAPS), (rx, ry, rw - odd, rh))) if not hip: cap["cappedN"], cap["cappedS"] = caps["cappedN"], caps["cappedS"] out.append(("Peak30Quad" if hip else "Peak30NS", "Zero", cap, box)) return out

nodes.name: floor_options
nodes.signature: def floor_options(kind: str, of_kind: dict, mansion: bool = False) -> list[str]
nodes.body_text: def floor_options(kind: str, of_kind: dict, mansion: bool = False) -> list[str]: """The finishes a room of `kind` may be laid in: a mansion's own where it has them for that room, the building kind's or the room kind's otherwise. Only names the catalogue has a tile entry for.""" from .layout import FLOOR_CHOICES, MANSION_FLOORS if mansion: own = [o for o in MANSION_FLOORS.get(kind, ()) if o in C.EXTRA_FLOORS] if own: return own return [o for o in of_kind.get(kind, FLOOR_CHOICES.get(kind, ())) if o in C.EXTRA_FLOORS]

nodes.name: _rooftop
nodes.signature: def _rooftop(grid: list[list[int]], width: int, height: int, seed: str | int = 0) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, str]]
nodes.body_text: def _rooftop(grid: list[list[int]], width: int, height: int, seed: str | int = 0) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, str]]: import random tiles = [(x, y) for y in range(1, height - 1) for x in range(1, width - 1) if all(grid[y + dy][x + dx] for dy in (-1, 0, 1) for dx in (-1, 0, 1))] area = sum(1 for row in grid for v in row if v) if area < ROOF_MIN_TILES or not tiles: return [] rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:{width}:{height}:{area}") # Only the air-conditioning unit stands on a roof. Every other tile in # rooftop_furniture (the vents at 014/015, the hatch at 016/022/023) is # attachedCeiling or a wall-mounted Conditioner, and the game hangs a # ceiling tile from the ceiling of the level it sits on - on the roof floor # that is a storey above the roof, so they floated over the building. The # count is kept, so a roof still carries as many pieces as it did. wanted = ["roof_ac"] * (1 + max(1, area // ROOF_AC_EVERY) + area // ROOF_VENT_EVERY) taken: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() out = [] rng.shuffle(tiles) for role in wanted: for x, y in tiles: if any((x + dx, y + dy) in taken for dx in (-1, 0, 1) for dy in (-1, 0, 1)): continue taken.add((x, y)) out.append((role, x, y, rng.choice(("W", "N")))) break return out

nodes.name: _storefront_runs
nodes.signature: def _storefront_runs(storey, doors) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _storefront_runs(storey, doors) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, int]]: """The ground floor's shop glass as straight runs of wall: (edge dir, fixed coordinate, first tile along, length). A run spans from its first glazed tile to its last, taking in the doors and the bits of wall beside them, and stops wherever the line is no longer an outside wall.""" grid = storey.grid h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0]) def cell(x, y): return grid[y][x] if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h else 0 def outside(d, fixed, t): x, y = (fixed, t) if d == "W" else (t, fixed) a, b = (cell(x - 1, y), cell(x, y)) if d == "W" else (cell(x, y - 1), cell(x, y)) return bool(a) != bool(b) lines: dict[tuple[str, int], list[int]] = {} for x, y, d in storey.shop_front: lines.setdefault((d, x if d == "W" else y), []).append(y if d == "W" else x) door_at = {(d, x if d == "W" else y, y if d == "W" else x) for x, y, d in doors} runs = [] for (d, fixed), along in sorted(lines.items()): lo, hi = min(along), max(along) # A shop door just past the last pane belongs to the shop front too. for step in (-1, 1): end = lo if step < 0 else hi for k in (1, 2): if (d, fixed, end + k * step) in door_at and all( outside(d, fixed, end + i * step) for i in range(1, k + 1)): end += k * step break lo, hi = (end, hi) if step < 0 else (lo, end) start = None for t in range(lo, hi + 2): if t <= hi and outside(d, fixed, t): start = t if start is None else start elif start is not None: runs.append((d, fixed, start, t - start)) start = None return runs

nodes.name: cell
nodes.body_text: def cell(x, y): return grid[y][x] if 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h else 0

nodes.name: outside

Taller buildings of a kind take bigger windows: the last row whose # storey count this building reaches. for levels, entry, curtains in style.get("windows_by_levels") or (): if len(storeys) >= levels and levels > 1: window_idx = _add(entries, entry) curtains_idx = _add(entries, curtains) trim_idx = _add(entries, style.get("trim")) shutters_idx = _add(entries, style.get("shutters")) grime_idx = _add(entries, style.get("grime")) if style.get("roof"): kit = style["roof"] if kit.get("slopes"): slope_idx = _add(entries, kit["slopes"]) top_idx = _add(entries, kit["tops"]) peaked = bool(kit.get("peaked")) # nodes.name: terrain.py
nodes.body_text: """Tiles for the ground, from the landscape and vegetation pictures and Rules.txt. For every rule the pixels of its colour get a tile from its list. The pick is a hash of the pixel's position, the rule and a seed, so the same map always gets the same tiles and a cell can be made without making the ones around it. Only the rules are applied here, not the blends along edges between two ground kinds. """ from __future__ import annotations import numpy as np from .rules import Rule, Ruleset # Bottom of the stack first. Layers not listed go after these, by name. LAYER_ORDER = ["0_Floor", "0_FloorOverlay", "0_FloorOverlay2", "0_FloorOverlay3", "0_FloorOverlay4", "0_FloorOverlay5", "0_FloorOverlay6", "0_Curbs", "0_Furniture", "0_Vegetation"] _M = np.uint64(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

nodes.name: mix
nodes.signature: def mix(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, salt: int) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def mix(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, salt: int) -> np.ndarray: """A well-mixed 64-bit number for every (x, y): splitmix64 on the position.""" z = (x.astype(np.uint64) * np.uint64(0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)) ^ (y.astype(np.uint64) * np.uint64(0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4F)) z = z + np.uint64((salt * 0x165667B19E3779F9) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) z = (z ^ (z >> np.uint64(30))) * np.uint64(0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) z = (z ^ (z >> np.uint64(27))) * np.uint64(0x94D049BB133111EB) return z ^ (z >> np.uint64(31))

nodes.name: Palette
nodes.body_text: class Palette: """Tile names to small numbers, shared by every cell of a map.""" def __init__(self): self.names: list[str] = [""] # 0 means no tile self.index: dict[str, int] = {"": 0} def of(self, name: str) -> int: i = self.index.get(name) if i is None: i = self.index[name] = len(self.names) self.names.append(name) return i

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.body_text: def __init__(self): self.names: list[str] = [""] # 0 means no tile self.index: dict[str, int] = {"": 0}

nodes.name: of
nodes.body_text: def of(self, name: str) -> int: i = self.index.get(name) if i is None: i = self.index[name] = len(self.names) self.names.append(name) return i

nodes.name: _pick
nodes.signature: def _pick(rule: Rule, rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray, seed: int, salt: int) -> np.ndarray
nodes.body_text: def _pick(rule: Rule, rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, xs: np.ndarray, ys: np.ndarray, seed: int, salt: int) -> np.ndarray: """Palette numbers for the tiles of `rule` at these positions.""" n = len(rule.entries) h1 = mix(xs, ys, seed * 1000003 + salt) entry = (h1 % np.uint64(n)).astype(np.int64) out = np.zeros(len(xs), np.int64) h2 = mix(xs, ys, seed * 1000003 + salt + 7919) for e, name in enumerate(rule.entries): sel = entry == e if not sel.any(): continue if name in rules.aliases: sub = rules.aliases[name] j = (h2[sel] % np.uint64(len(sub))).astype(np.int64) out[sel] = np.array([pal.of(t) for t in sub], np.int64)[j] else: out[sel] = pal.of(name) return out

nodes.name: colour_keys
nodes.body_text: def colour_keys(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: """A colour picture (h, w, 3) as one number per pixel, r * 65536 + g * 256 + b.""" return (img[..., 0].astype(np.uint32) << 16) | (img[..., 1].astype(np.uint32) << 8) | img[..., 2]

nodes.name: _key
nodes.body_text: def _key(c) -> int: return (c[0] << 16) | (c[1] << 8) | c[2]

nodes.name: ground_layers
nodes.signature: def ground_layers(land: np.ndarray, veg: np.ndarray, rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, seed: int, x0: int = 0, y0: int = 0) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
nodes.body_text: def ground_layers(land: np.ndarray, veg: np.ndarray, rules: Ruleset, pal: Palette, seed: int, x0: int = 0, y0: int = 0) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]: """{layer: (h, w) palette numbers} for a window of the pictures. `land` and `veg` are (h, w, 3) uint8; (x0, y0) is where the window starts in the world, so the picks do not depend on how the world was cut up.""" h, w = land.shape[:2] gy, gx = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w] gx = gx.astype(np.int64) + x0 gy = gy.astype(np.int64) + y0 layers: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {} def paint(rule: Rule, mask: np.ndarray, salt: int) -> None: if not mask.any(): return layer = layers.setdefault(rule.layer, np.zeros((h, w), np.int64)) layer[mask] = _pick(rule, rules, pal, gx[mask], gy[mask], seed, salt) # Colours as single numbers, and only the rules whose colour is in the picture at all # (a window holds a handful of the 148). land_key, veg_key = colour_keys(land), colour_keys(veg) in_land, in_veg = set(np.unique(land_key).tolist()), set(np.unique(veg_key).tolist()) for n, rule in enumerate(rules.rules): key = _key(rule.color) if key not in (in_land if rule.bitmap == 0 else in_veg): continue if rule.condition is not None and _key(rule.condition) not in in_land: continue mask = (land_key if rule.bitmap == 0 else veg_key) == key if rule.condition is not None: mask &= land_key == _key(rule.condition) paint(rule, mask, n) return layers
