nodes.signature: def paint(rule: Rule, mask: np.ndarray, salt: int) -> None
nodes.body_text: def paint(rule: Rule, mask: np.ndarray, salt: int) -> None: if not mask.any(): return layer = layers.setdefault(rule.layer, np.zeros((h, w), np.int64)) layer[mask] = _pick(rule, rules, pal, gx[mask], gy[mask], seed, salt)

nodes.name: stack_order
nodes.body_text: def stack_order(layer_names) -> list[str]: known = [n for n in LAYER_ORDER if n in layer_names] return known + sorted(n for n in layer_names if n not in LAYER_ORDER)

nodes.name: tower.py
nodes.body_text: """Office-tower interiors: which buildings qualify and where the core goes. A tower core is one block near the middle of the floor, the same on every storey: a stair hall (the lift lobby), a row of lifts along one long side of it with their doors on the hall, and a toilet plus a riser room on the other. """ from __future__ import annotations import random from dataclasses import dataclass, field from . import layout TOWER_FROM_LEVELS = 12 TOWER_MIN_SIDE = 14 PLANT_SHARE = 0.9 # the plant floor sits this far up the building SERVICE_WIDE = 4 # toilet and riser: deep enough to be rooms HALL_MIN_LONG = layout.STAIR_RUN + 1 # A core further than this from the middle is not a tower core: no fit, no tower. CENTRE_SLACK = 4 Rect = tuple[int, int, int, int] Door = tuple[int, int, str] @dataclass

nodes.name: qualifies
nodes.signature: def qualifies(kind: str | None, levels: int, width: int, height: int) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def qualifies(kind: str | None, levels: int, width: int, height: int) -> bool: return (kind == "civic" and levels >= TOWER_FROM_LEVELS and min(width, height) >= TOWER_MIN_SIDE)

nodes.name: plant_level
nodes.body_text: def plant_level(levels: int) -> int: return round(levels * PLANT_SHARE)

nodes.name: TowerCore
nodes.body_text: class TowerCore: stair: Rect lifts: list[tuple[Rect, Door]] = field(default_factory=list) service: list[tuple[Rect, str]] = field(default_factory=list)

nodes.name: _lift_count
nodes.body_text: def _lift_count(width: int, height: int) -> int: area = width * height return 2 if area < 400 else 3 if area < 700 else 4

nodes.name: _shape
nodes.body_text: def _shape(n: int, lifts_west: bool) -> TowerCore: """The core of an N-S hall with its top-left corner at (0, 0).""" s, wide = layout.SHAFT_SIZE, layout.CORE_WIDE long_ = max(HALL_MIN_LONG, s * n) hx = s if lifts_west else SERVICE_WIDE svc_x = hx + wide if lifts_west else 0 lift_x = 0 if lifts_west else hx + wide door_x = hx if lifts_west else lift_x core = TowerCore(stair=(hx, 0, hx + wide - 1, long_ - 1)) for i in range(n): y = s * i core.lifts.append(((lift_x, y, lift_x + s - 1, y + s - 1), (door_x, y, "W"))) # One toilet and the riser, stacked down the far side. Every tower gets # exactly these two: the hall is at most 8 long (4 lifts of 2), and a # third room would make each thinner than MIN_ROOM, a sliver that # layout._mend_fragments folds away. kinds = ("bathroom", "storage") each = long_ // len(kinds) for i, kind in enumerate(kinds): y = each * i h = each if i < len(kinds) - 1 else long_ - y core.service.append(((svc_x, y, svc_x + SERVICE_WIDE - 1, y + h - 1), kind)) return core

nodes.name: _moved
nodes.signature: def _moved(core: TowerCore, ox: int, oy: int, across: bool) -> TowerCore
nodes.body_text: def _moved(core: TowerCore, ox: int, oy: int, across: bool) -> TowerCore: """Shift to (ox, oy); `across` turns it to run east-west (x and y swap).""" def mv(rc: Rect) -> Rect: x0, y0, x1, y1 = rc if across: x0, y0, x1, y1 = y0, x0, y1, x1 return x0 + ox, y0 + oy, x1 + ox, y1 + oy def door(d: Door) -> Door: x, y, o = d return (y + ox, x + oy, "N") if across else (x + ox, y + oy, o) return TowerCore(mv(core.stair), [(mv(rc), door(d)) for rc, d in core.lifts], [(mv(rc), k) for rc, k in core.service])

nodes.name: mv
nodes.body_text: def mv(rc: Rect) -> Rect: x0, y0, x1, y1 = rc if across: x0, y0, x1, y1 = y0, x0, y1, x1 return x0 + ox, y0 + oy, x1 + ox, y1 + oy

nodes.name: door
nodes.body_text: def door(d: Door) -> Door: x, y, o = d return (y + ox, x + oy, "N") if across else (x + ox, y + oy, o)

nodes.name: pick_core
nodes.signature: def pick_core(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random) -> TowerCore | None
nodes.body_text: def pick_core(width: int, height: int, mask: list[list[bool]] | None, rng: random.Random) -> TowerCore | None: """The tower core nearest the middle of the footprint, or None if the mask has no room for the whole core block (it is one rectangle, as the spec has it, so a notch in its corner rules it out).""" for n in range(_lift_count(width, height), 1, -1): best: list[TowerCore] = [] best_score = None for west in (True, False): base = _shape(n, west) bw = SERVICE_WIDE + layout.CORE_WIDE + layout.SHAFT_SIZE bl = base.stair[3] + 1 for across in (False, True): w, h = (bl, bw) if across else (bw, bl) for oy in range(height - h + 1): for ox in range(width - w + 1): core = _moved(base, ox, oy, across) sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1 = core.stair dx = abs((sx0 + sx1 + 1) / 2 - width / 2) dy = abs((sy0 + sy1 + 1) / 2 - height / 2) if dx > CENTRE_SLACK or dy > CENTRE_SLACK: continue score = dx + dy if best_score is not None and score > best_score + 1e-9: continue if mask is not None and not all( mask[y][x] for y in range(oy, oy + h) for x in range(ox, ox + w)): continue if best_score is None or score < best_score - 1e-9: best_score, best = score, [core] else: best.append(core) if best: return rng.choice(best) return None

"guest_house": ("lobby", "office"), "museum": ("lobby", "storage"), "gallery": ("giftstore", "storage")} OFFICE_USE = ("office", "office") # Rooms on the street a shop front is glazed for and a door goes into. FRONT_ROOMS = {front for table in (AMENITY_USES, SHOP_USES, HEALTHCARE_USES, LEISURE_USES, TOURISM_USES) for front, _back in table.values()} \ - {"library", "theatre", "policeoffice", "daycare", "mechanic", "office"} \ | {"italianrestaurant", "chineserestaurant"} # The keys of the OSM tags this reads; the overpass query asks for points # with any of them (generator/osm.py). USE_KEYS = ("amenity", "shop", "healthcare", "leisure", "tourism", "office", "craft") # Food rooms; the others are sold from. FOOD_FRONTS = {"restaurantdining", "italianrestaurant", "chineserestaurant", "cafe", "icecream", "bar", "bakery"}

nodes.name: use_of
nodes.signature: def use_of(tags: dict) -> tuple[str, str] | None
nodes.body_text: def use_of(tags: dict) -> tuple[str, str] | None: """The (front room, back room) one set of OSM tags makes, or None.""" amenity = (tags.get("amenity") or "").strip().lower() cuisine = (tags.get("cuisine") or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower() if amenity in ("restaurant", "fast_food", "food_court", "cafe"): front, back = AMENITY_USES[amenity] if cuisine in KITCHEN_BY_CUISINE and amenity != "cafe": back = KITCHEN_BY_CUISINE[cuisine] front = DINING_BY_CUISINE.get(cuisine, front) return front, back if amenity in AMENITY_USES: return AMENITY_USES[amenity] shop = (tags.get("shop") or "").strip().lower() if shop in SHOP_USES: return SHOP_USES[shop] if shop and shop not in ("no", "vacant", "yes"): return ("generalstore", "storage") for key, table in (("healthcare", HEALTHCARE_USES), ("leisure", LEISURE_USES), ("tourism", TOURISM_USES)): value = (tags.get(key) or "").strip().lower() if value in table: return table[value] if tags.get("office") or tags.get("craft"): return OFFICE_USE return None

nodes.name: uses_of
nodes.signature: def uses_of(tag_sets: list[dict], limit: int = 8) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
nodes.body_text: def uses_of(tag_sets: list[dict], limit: int = 8) -> list[tuple[str, str]]: """The uses of a building's own tags and the points inside it, in order, each once.""" out: list[tuple[str, str]] = [] for tags in tag_sets: use = use_of(tags) if use and use not in out: out.append(use) return out[:limit]

nodes.name: is_hotel
nodes.body_text: def is_hotel(tag_sets: list[dict]) -> bool: return any((t.get("tourism") or "") in ("hotel", "motel", "hostel") or (t.get("building") or "") == "hotel" for t in tag_sets)

nodes.name: works.py
nodes.body_text: """Works yards: the paved yard round each industrial building and what stands in it. An industrial estate used to be gravel from fence to fence, a beige plain with the works standing in it and nothing else. The estate's land is grass now (generator/rendering/landcover.py), and each works gets what Knox County's have: a tarmac yard round it, worn at the edges where it meets the grass, a drive out to the road, cars parked in front, a dumpster by the wall, and pallets, drums, barrels, crates and tyres stood along it. Run from yards.paint_paths, on the same ground and vegetation bitmaps, after the houses. """ from __future__ import annotations import math from collections import deque from generator import pz_colors as C WORKS_KINDS = ("industrial",) YARD_MIN, YARD_MAX = 6, 10 # tiles of yard out from the walls YARD_EDGE = 3 # worn ground past the yard: gravel, dirt, weeds EDGE_WEAR = (0.55, 0.3, 0.12) # how much of each row of it is worn, nearest first DRIVE_MAX = 120 DRIVE_WIDTH = 3 CLUTTER_EVERY = 9 # tiles of wall per stack of clutter # Wear on the yard's tarmac, as the street pass has it on the roads. GRIME_SHARE = 0.0 # no dark patches on the tarmac, as on the roads CRACK_SHARE = 1 / 14 # (colour, fewest and most in a row along the wall) CLUTTER = [(C.WORKS_PALLET, (2, 4)), (C.WORKS_BRICKS, (1, 3)), (C.WORKS_DRUM, (2, 4)), (C.WORKS_BARREL, (2, 3)), (C.WORKS_CRATE, (2, 4)), (C.WORKS_TIRES, (1, 3))] # A dumpster is two tiles and the game has it facing two ways: along a wall # that runs east-west (S) or north-south (E), first tile then second. DUMPSTERS = [{"S": (C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_S0, C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_S1), "E": (C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_E0, C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_E1)}, {"S": (C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S0, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S1), "E": (C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E0, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E1)}] PARKING_DEPTH = 5

nodes.name: yard_width
nodes.signature: def yard_width(bw: int, bh: int) -> int
nodes.body_text: def yard_width(bw: int, bh: int) -> int: """How far the yard runs out from the walls: wider round a bigger works.""" return max(YARD_MIN, min(YARD_MAX, round(math.sqrt(bw * bh) / 4)))

nodes.name: dress_works
nodes.signature: def dress_works(rows: list[dict], door_lists: dict, cv, drives: list | None, rng) -> int
nodes.body_text: def dress_works(rows: list[dict], door_lists: dict, cv, drives: list | None, rng) -> int: """Yards for the works in `rows`. `cv` is paint_paths' canvas: ground, veg, w, h, free(x, y), paint(x, y, colour), paved_at, occupied_at and claimed_bytes. Returns the works given a yard.""" w, h = cv.w, cv.h done = 0 for row in rows: if row.get("kind") not in WORKS_KINDS: continue x0, y0, bw, bh = row["tile_x"], row["tile_y"], row["width"], row["height"] doors = door_lists.get(row["file"], []) r = yard_width(bw, bh) def ring(x, y): """How many tiles out from the building's rectangle a square is.""" return max(x0 - x, x - (x0 + bw - 1), y0 - y, y - (y0 + bh - 1), 0) yard = {(x, y) for y in range(y0 - r, y0 + bh + r) for x in range(x0 - r, x0 + bw + r) if cv.free(x, y)} if not yard: continue # The squares at the doors, two out, and either side of the step, # where nothing is stood. fronts = set() for ox, oy, ix, iy in doors: dx, dy = ox - ix, oy - iy sx, sy = x0 + ox, y0 + oy fronts |= {(sx + dx * k, sy + dy * k) for k in range(3)} fronts |= {(sx - dy, sy + dx), (sx + dy, sy - dx)} # The drive: from the yard to the nearest road or paving, unless the # yard is on one already. door = (x0 + doors[0][0], y0 + doors[0][1]) if doors else (x0, y0) drive = _drive(yard, cv, door) for x, y in yard: cv.paint(x, y, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT) cv.paved_at[y * w + x] = True for x, y in drive: cv.paint(x, y, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT) cv.paved_at[y * w + x] = True # Where the tarmac gives out: gravel, dirt and weeds into the grass. for y in range(y0 - r - YARD_EDGE, y0 + bh + r + YARD_EDGE): for x in range(x0 - r - YARD_EDGE, x0 + bw + r + YARD_EDGE): k = ring(x, y) - r - 1 if not 0 <= k < YARD_EDGE or not cv.free(x, y): continue roll = rng.random() if roll < EDGE_WEAR[k]: cv.paint(x, y, C.LIGHT_ASPHALT if rng.random() < 0.65 else C.DIRT) elif roll < EDGE_WEAR[k] + 0.25 and cv.veg is not None: cv.veg[y, x] = C.SHORT_GRASS taken = set(fronts) def can(x, y): return (x, y) in yard and (x, y) not in taken and cv.veg is not None def stand(x, y, colour): if not can(x, y): return False cv.veg[y, x] = colour taken.add((x, y)) return True # Along the walls: the squares of the yard next to the building. wall = [(x, y) for x, y in yard if ring(x, y) == 1] cx, cy = x0 + bw / 2, y0 + bh / 2 wall.sort(key=lambda p: math.atan2(p[1] - cy, p[0] - cx)) _dumpster(wall, x0, y0, bw, bh, doors, can, stand, rng) i = rng.randrange(CLUTTER_EVERY) while i < len(wall): colour, (lo, hi) = rng.choice(CLUTTER) n, run = rng.randint(lo, hi), [] for p in wall[i:i + hi + 2]: if len(run) == n: break if p in taken: continue if run and abs(p[0] - run[-1][0]) + abs(p[1] - run[-1][1]) != 1: break run.append(p) for p in run: stand(*p, colour) i += CLUTTER_EVERY + rng.randrange(-2, 3) # Lights at two corners of the yard, their arms over it. for (x, y), lamp in (((x0 - r, y0 - r), C.LAMP_S), ((x0 + bw + r - 1, y0 + bh + r - 1), C.LAMP_N)): stand(x, y, lamp) # Cars parked in front of the first door, past its step. if drives is not None and doors: ox, oy, ix, iy = doors[0] dx, dy = ox - ix, oy - iy sx, sy = x0 + ox, y0 + oy depth = min(PARKING_DEPTH, r - 3) if depth > 0: if dy: a, b = sorted((sy + dy * 3, sy + dy * (2 + depth))) spot = (max(x0, sx - 6), a, min(12, bw), b - a + 1) else: a, b = sorted((sx + dx * 3, sx + dx * (2 + depth))) spot = (a, max(y0, sy - 6), b - a + 1, min(12, bh)) drives.append(spot) px, py, pw, ph = spot taken |= {(x, y) for x in range(px, px + pw) for y in range(py, py + ph)} # Wear on the rest of the tarmac. if cv.veg is not None: for x, y in yard: if (x, y) in taken: continue roll = rng.random() if roll < GRIME_SHARE: cv.veg[y, x] = C.ASPHALT_GRIME elif roll < GRIME_SHARE + CRACK_SHARE: cv.veg[y, x] = C.ASPHALT_CRACKS done += 1 return done

nodes.name: ring
nodes.body_text: def ring(x, y): """How many tiles out from the building's rectangle a square is.""" return max(x0 - x, x - (x0 + bw - 1), y0 - y, y - (y0 + bh - 1), 0)

nodes.name: can
nodes.body_text: def can(x, y): return (x, y) in yard and (x, y) not in taken and cv.veg is not None

nodes.name: stand
nodes.body_text: def stand(x, y, colour): if not can(x, y): return False cv.veg[y, x] = colour taken.add((x, y)) return True

nodes.name: _drive
nodes.signature: def _drive(yard: set, cv, door: tuple[int, int]) -> list
nodes.body_text: def _drive(yard: set, cv, door: tuple[int, int]) -> list: """The squares of a drive from `yard` to the nearest road or paving, three wide, leaving the yard as near the front door as it can; none when the yard already meets one or none is in reach.""" w, h = cv.w, cv.h paved_at = cv.paved_at queue = deque() prev = {} # Searched from the squares nearest the door first, so of the ways out # that are equally short the one from the front wins. for x, y in sorted(yard, key=lambda p: (abs(p[0] - door[0]) + abs(p[1] - door[1]), p)): for nx, ny in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if (nx, ny) in yard or not (0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h): continue if paved_at[ny * w + nx] and not cv.occupied_at[ny * w + nx]: return [] prev[(x, y)] = None queue.append((x, y, 0)) end = None while queue: x, y, n = queue.popleft() if (x, y) not in yard and paved_at[y * w + x]: end = (x, y) break if n >= DRIVE_MAX: continue for nx, ny in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if (nx, ny) in prev or not (0 <= nx < w and 0 <= ny < h): continue if paved_at[ny * w + nx] and not cv.occupied_at[ny * w + nx] or cv.free(nx, ny): prev[(nx, ny)] = (x, y) queue.append((nx, ny, n + 1)) if end is None: return [] route = [] step = prev[end] while step is not None and step not in yard: route.append(step) step = prev[step] out = [] for i, (x, y) in enumerate(route): before, after = route[max(0, i - 1)], route[min(len(route) - 1, i + 1)] across = ((x, y - 1), (x, y), (x, y + 1)) if before[0] != after[0] else \ ((x - 1, y), (x, y), (x + 1, y)) out += [p for p in across[:DRIVE_WIDTH] if cv.free(*p)] return out

nodes.name: _dumpster
nodes.signature: def _dumpster(wall, x0, y0, bw, bh, doors, can, stand, rng) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def _dumpster(wall, x0, y0, bw, bh, doors, can, stand, rng) -> bool: """One dumpster against the wall, as near a door as it can stand without being in the way of one.""" near = [(x0 + ox, y0 + oy) for ox, oy, _ix, _iy in doors] or [(x0, y0)] spots = [] on_wall = set(wall) for x, y in wall: if (x + 1, y) in on_wall and (y == y0 - 1 or y == y0 + bh): spots.append(((x, y), (x + 1, y), "S")) if (x, y + 1) in on_wall and (x == x0 - 1 or x == x0 + bw): spots.append(((x, y), (x, y + 1), "E")) spots.sort(key=lambda s: min(abs(s[0][0] - a) + abs(s[0][1] - b) for a, b in near)) colours = rng.choice(DUMPSTERS) for a, b, facing in spots: if can(*a) and can(*b): first, second = colours[facing] stand(*a, first) stand(*b, second) return True return False

nodes.name: world.py
nodes.body_text: """Write a WorldEd project (.pzw) with every generated building pre-placed. Schema from WorldWriter in timbaker/pzworlded. A <lot>'s x/y are relative to the cell that holds it, so a building at map tile (tx, ty) lands in cell (tx // 300, ty // 300) at offset (tx % 300, ty % 300). Only <bmp> and <cell> are emitted. WorldEd's reader routes anything it does not recognise through readUnknownElement() and applies defaults for the settings blocks we leave out, so a minimal project opens cleanly. """ from __future__ import annotations import os from dataclasses import dataclass from xml.sax.saxutils import quoteattr CELL_SIZE = 300 # Where the generated map sits in the shared world, in source (300-tile) cells. # # Vanilla "Muldraugh, KY" occupies compiled cells 0..77 x 0..62 — the whole of # Knox County. A map generated at origin 0,0 lands on top of it: a tiny one can # get away with it by landing in an empty corner, but anything the size of a # real town collides and the region never shows up. 70 source cells is 21000 # tiles, which starts past vanilla's eastern edge (77 * 256 = 19712) with room # to spare. WORLD_ORIGIN_CELLS = (70, 0) # ...and where the *next* map sits, because two of them cannot sit in the # same place. Every map used to be built at 70,0, so a player with two # KnoxMap maps installed had both claiming the same cells: the game reads # one cell's header and the other cell's data and falls over on the way in. # # So each map is given the first free run of cells east of the maps already # installed, with a cell or two of empty ground between. They stay packed # tight on purpose - the game lays out one grid covering every cell any map # uses, so maps scattered across the world would be a grid mostly made of # nothing, and the paper map draws the town smaller the further out it sits. # A map with no other installed beside it lands on 70,0. ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS = 2 _ORIGIN = list(WORLD_ORIGIN_CELLS) # Lot-export worker threads. # # WorldEd defaults to one per core, up to 16. Each worker holds a whole # combined cell - four source cells and every building map placed on them - # so on a real town the count is a memory multiplier, not just a speed dial: # 16 workers on downtown Pergamon reached 11 GB inside a single batch. Four # keeps the peak near a gigabyte and still saturates the disk. GENERATE_LOTS_THREADS = 4 # Zones the game reads out of the world: ParkingStall is where vehicles spawn, # TownZone marks built-up ground. Vanilla Knox County carries 9694 parking # stalls and 2715 town zones - without them the streets are bare tarmac and # nothing drives or parks anywhere. ZONE_GROUPS = [ ("ParkingStall", "#ff007f"), ("TownZone", "#aa0000"), ] @dataclass @dataclass

nodes.name: origin
nodes.body_text: def origin() -> tuple[int, int]: """Where the map being built now sits, in 300-tile cells.""" return (_ORIGIN[0], _ORIGIN[1])

nodes.name: set_origin
nodes.body_text: def set_origin(value) -> None: _ORIGIN[0], _ORIGIN[1] = int(value[0]), int(value[1])

nodes.name: _project_box
nodes.signature: def _project_box(pzw_path: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def _project_box(pzw_path: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None: """(origin x, origin y, cells across, cells down) out of a .pzw.""" import re try: with open(pzw_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: text = f.read() except OSError: return None o = re.search(r'<worldOrigin origin="(-?\d+),(-?\d+)"', text) w = re.search(r'<world version="[^"]*" width="(\d+)" height="(\d+)"', text) if not (o and w): return None return int(o.group(1)), int(o.group(2)), int(w.group(1)), int(w.group(2))

nodes.name: _installed_boxes
nodes.body_text: def _installed_boxes() -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]: """Where the maps already installed on this PC sit, from the names of their compiled cells (<base>_<cell x>_<cell y>.lotheader). Compiled cells are 256 tiles, not 300, so they are converted back.""" import os import re try: import knoxpaths mods = knoxpaths.zomboid_user_dir() / "mods" except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no Zomboid folder, nothing installed return [] boxes = [] if not mods.is_dir(): return [] for maps in mods.glob("*/common/media/maps/*"): cells = [] try: entries = os.listdir(maps) except OSError: continue for entry in entries: m = re.fullmatch(r".*_(\d+)_(\d+)\.lotheader", entry) if m: cells.append((int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)))) if not cells: continue x0 = min(c[0] for c in cells) * 256 // CELL_SIZE y0 = min(c[1] for c in cells) * 256 // CELL_SIZE x1 = (max(c[0] for c in cells) + 1) * 256 y1 = (max(c[1] for c in cells) + 1) * 256 boxes.append((x0, y0, -(-x1 // CELL_SIZE) - x0, -(-y1 // CELL_SIZE) - y0)) return boxes

nodes.name: choose_origin
nodes.signature: def choose_origin(out_dir: str, cells_x: int, cells_y: int, keep_place: bool = True) -> tuple[int, int]
nodes.body_text: def choose_origin(out_dir: str, cells_x: int, cells_y: int, keep_place: bool = True) -> tuple[int, int]: """A run of free cells for this map, keeping the one it already has. A map that has been built before keeps its place, so rebuilding it does not move a town out from under anybody's save. `keep_place` off is the answer to "where would this map go if it had never been placed", which is what handing the choice back to the app has to mean. """ import os here = os.path.abspath(out_dir) name = os.path.basename(here.rstrip(os.sep)) if keep_place: # Somewhere the mapper picked themselves beats anything worked out # here: where a town sits is theirs to decide (knoxbuild/placement.py). from .placement import saved chosen = saved(here) if chosen: return chosen mine = _project_box(os.path.join(here, f"{name}.pzw")) if mine: return mine[0], mine[1] # Only what is installed holds a place. Every generation makes a new # output folder, and those used to claim their cells for good: the tenth # map a PC built started ninety cells further east than the first, and the # paper map is one grid from cell 0, so the town drew as a speck in the # corner of an empty world. A folder nobody installed is a project on # disk, not something in anybody's game, and uninstalling a map now hands # its cells back. taken = _installed_boxes() ox, oy = WORLD_ORIGIN_CELLS for _ in range(len(taken) + 1): clash = [b for b in taken if b[0] < ox + cells_x + ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS and ox < b[0] + b[2] + ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS and b[1] < oy + cells_y + ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS and oy < b[1] + b[3] + ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS] if not clash: break ox = max(b[0] + b[2] for b in clash) + ORIGIN_GAP_CELLS return ox, oy

nodes.name: Zone
nodes.body_text: class Zone: kind: str # "ParkingStall" | "TownZone" tile_x: int # absolute tile coords tile_y: int width: int height: int @property def cell_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x // CELL_SIZE @property def cell_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y // CELL_SIZE @property def offset_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x % CELL_SIZE @property def offset_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y % CELL_SIZE

nodes.body_text: def cell_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x // CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: cell_y
nodes.body_text: def cell_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y // CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: offset_x

nodes.name: offset_y

nodes.name: Placement
nodes.body_text: class Placement: tbx_path: str # relative to the .pzw tile_x: int # absolute tile coords in the whole map tile_y: int width: int height: int # WorldEd lays a cell's lots down in the order this file lists them, and # what is laid last is drawn last. A porch light stands on the tile the # house wall is on, so sorted by position it went down before the wall # and the wall covered it. Anything that hangs on a building goes last. on_top: bool = False # Storeys. A taller building is laid after a lower one beside it: the lower one's # ceiling and roof tiles take the squares they are on, and that took the taller # one's upper-floor wall with them when it was laid first (a wall missing over a # neighbour's roof). Laid after, its wall is added to what is there. levels: int = 1 # The level its first floor stands on: below 0 for a basement # (knoxbuild/basements.py), whose top floor is at -1. base_level: int = 0 @property def cell_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x // CELL_SIZE @property def cell_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y // CELL_SIZE @property def offset_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x % CELL_SIZE @property def offset_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y % CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: cell_x
nodes.body_text: def cell_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x // CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: cell_y
nodes.body_text: def cell_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y // CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: offset_x
nodes.body_text: def offset_x(self) -> int: return self.tile_x % CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: offset_y
nodes.body_text: def offset_y(self) -> int: return self.tile_y % CELL_SIZE

nodes.name: _tool_path
nodes.body_text: def _tool_path(path: str) -> str: """A folder as the map tools read it: forward slashes on Windows, and otherwise whatever the compiler in use can open - the machine's own name for a build made for it, a Wine name for the Windows one (knoxpaths.tool_path).""" if os.name == "nt": return path.replace("\\", "/") import knoxpaths return knoxpaths.tool_path(path)

nodes.name: render_pzw
nodes.signature: def render_pzw(cells_x: int, cells_y: int, bmp_name: str, placements: list[Placement], map_name: str = "", project_dir: str = "", zones: list[Zone] | None = None) -> str: # Nothing may name a cell outside the world: WorldEd rejects the whole # project over one ("error reading world, invalid cell coordinates").
nodes.body_text: def render_pzw(cells_x: int, cells_y: int, bmp_name: str, placements: list[Placement], map_name: str = "", project_dir: str = "", zones: list[Zone] | None = None) -> str: # Nothing may name a cell outside the world: WorldEd rejects the whole # project over one ("error reading world, invalid cell coordinates"). def on_grid(cx: int, cy: int) -> bool: return 0 <= cx < cells_x and 0 <= cy < cells_y by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list[Placement]] = {} for p in placements: if on_grid(p.cell_x, p.cell_y): by_cell.setdefault((p.cell_x, p.cell_y), []).append(p) # The zombie spawn map, absolute for the same reason the export folders # below are. # # It sat in the same <GenerateLots> block as <exportdir> and was a bare # file name, so WorldEd looked for it next to its own executable, found # nothing, and baked a town with no zombies in it at all - "I did not # encounter a single one". The name is filled in further down, once the # project folder is known. spawn_map = f"{map_name}_ZombieSpawnMap.bmp" if map_name else "" out = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>', f'<world version="1.0" width="{cells_x}" height="{cells_y}">'] # Pre-fill the conversion settings so BMP -> TMX and Generate Lots are # ready to run without visiting their dialogs first. ' <update-existing checked="false"/>', " </BMPToTMX>", " <TMXToBMP>", ' <mainImage generate="true"/>', ' <vegetationImage generate="true"/>', ' <buildingsImage path="" generate="false"/>', " </TMXToBMP>", " <GenerateLots>", f' <exportdir path={quoteattr(lots_dir)}/>', f' <ZombieSpawnMap path={quoteattr(spawn_map)}/>', ' <TileDefFolder path=""/>', f' <worldOrigin origin="{origin()[0]},{origin()[1]}"/>', f' <numberOfThreads count="{GENERATE_LOTS_THREADS}"/>', " </GenerateLots>", " <LuaSettings>", ' <spawnPointsFile path="spawnpoints.lua"/>', ' <worldObjectsFile path="objects.lua"/>', " </LuaSettings>", ] # Types must be declared before groups, and both before any object # references them - WorldReader errors out otherwise. for name, _colour in ZONE_GROUPS: out.append(f' <objecttype name={quoteattr(name)}/>') for name, colour in ZONE_GROUPS: out.append(f' <objectgroup name={quoteattr(name)}' f' color={quoteattr(colour)}' f' defaulttype={quoteattr(name)}/>') out.append(f' <bmp path={quoteattr(bmp_name)} x="0" y="0"' f' width="{cells_x}" height="{cells_y}"/>') zones_by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list[Zone]] = {} for z in zones or []: if on_grid(z.cell_x, z.cell_y): zones_by_cell.setdefault((z.cell_x, z.cell_y), []).append(z) # Point each cell at its TMX when that file already exists. # # BMP to TMX assigns these in memory and they are only persisted when the # project is saved; a headless run that dies before saving leaves every # cell at map="" and Generate Lots then refuses with "missing reference". # Writing the paths here means a re-run can skip conversion entirely and go # straight to compiling. nodes.name: worldmap.py
nodes.body_text: """The in-game paper map and its street names. Project Zomboid draws the map a player opens with M from two files in the map folder: worldmap.xml, polygons tagged with what they are, and streets.xml, named centre lines. Without them a generated map opens as a blank sheet - the one place in the game where the real town should be most recognisable. Both are written the way the vanilla Muldraugh files are laid out (Build 42): worldmap.xml <world version="1.0"> of <cell x y> blocks, one per 300-tile cell in world cell numbers. Each <feature> is a polygon in that cell's own coordinates, 0-300, with a property the map style filters on: building=Residential/RetailAndCommercial/..., highway=primary/secondary/tertiary/trail, water=river, natural=forest. Everything is a polygon - roads included, as strips as wide as the road. streets.xml <streets version="1"> of <street name width> with <point x y> in absolute world tiles. worldmap-annotations.lua a function adding text labels through the map's symbols API, in absolute world tiles: the town's name, its parks and squares, rivers and lakes, and its best-known buildings. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os from xml.sax.saxutils import quoteattr from shapely.geometry import LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, box from shapely.ops import linemerge, unary_union from generator import osm from generator.renderer import (THROUGH_ROADS, _is_polygon, _way_width_m, sea_polygons, shape_px) from .world import origin CELL = 300 # What each generated building kind is on the map. These are the categories # the vanilla style colours; a shed is drawn as a plain building. BUILDING_VALUE = { "house": "Residential", "apartment": "Residential", "shop": "RetailAndCommercial", "mall": "RetailAndCommercial", "restaurant": "RestaurantsAndEntertainment", "school": "CommunityServices", "civic": "CommunityServices", "church": "CommunityServices", "medical": "Medical", "industrial": "Industrial", "barn": "Industrial", "shed": "yes", } # Road classes as the map style knows them. It has no class for a service # lane, so those draw as the smallest street. HIGHWAY_VALUE = { "road_major": "primary", "road_medium": "secondary", "road_minor": "tertiary", "road_service": "tertiary", "pedestrian": "tertiary", "dirt_path": "trail", "paved_path": "trail", } RAIL_WIDTH_M = 4.0 AREA_VALUE = {"water": ("water", "river"), "pool": ("water", "river"), "forest": ("natural", "forest")} # Streets worth a name on the map. Footpaths carry names too, but labelling # every alley and pavement buries the streets people navigate by. NAMED_CLASSES = {"road_major", "road_medium", "road_minor", "road_service", "pedestrian"} # The credit lines under the OpenStreetMap note on the paper map: names to a line, # and tiles between lines. CREDIT_NAMES_PER_LINE = 4 CREDIT_LINE_GAP = 8 SIMPLIFY = 0.5 # tiles; the map is drawn far smaller than one tile per pixel # Points in one <street> of streets.xml, at most. Project Zomboid (Build 42) builds # each street's outline for the paper map in one shared 3 KB buffer # (IsoMetaGrid.clipperBuffer, in WorldMapStreet.createPolygon and # clipToObscuredCells) and never makes it bigger there. A street of more than # about 190 points overflows it: BufferOverflowException is thrown inside the # map's render, and the whole map window - streets, legend, buttons - draws # nothing for as long as that street is under the mouse, so the M map looks # broken for the rest of the session. Long country roads in OpenStreetMap get # there. 32 keeps a piece's outline and its triangles under 3 KB even with every corner mitred. # The map joins pieces of one name that share an end, so a road still highlights as one. MAX_STREET_POINTS = 32 # Labels: the style layer each goes on and how large, as the vanilla # Muldraugh annotations use them. TOWN_SCALE = {"city": 4.5, "town": 3.5, "village": 2.5, "suburb": 2.0, "quarter": 1.5, "neighbourhood": 1.2, "hamlet": 1.2} PLACE_SCALE = 0.6 BUILDING_SCALE = 0.6 # Only buildings people would give directions by, and not every one of them: # a label per corner shop buries the map. LABELLED_KINDS = {"school", "church", "medical", "civic", "industrial", "shop", "restaurant", "house", "apartment"} MIN_LABELLED_TILES = 150 MAX_BUILDING_LABELS = 40 MIN_PLACE_TILES = 400 PLACE_CATEGORIES = {"park", "plaza", "cemetery", "sports", "grass"}

nodes.signature: def write(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, info: dict, buildings: list[tuple[list[tuple[float, float]], str, str]]) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def write(out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, info: dict, buildings: list[tuple[list[tuple[float, float]], str, str]]) -> dict: """Write worldmap.xml and streets.xml into `out_dir`. Returns counts. `buildings` holds each placed building's projected outline and its kind. Roads, water and woodland come from the OSM download cached beside the map; a map folder without one still gets its buildings. """ metres_per_tile = info["meters_per_tile"] width, height = proj.width, proj.height features: list[tuple[Polygon, str, str]] = [] labels: list[tuple[str, str, float, float, float]] = [] named_buildings = [] for outline, kind, name in buildings: poly = _clean(Polygon(outline)) if poly is not None: features.append((poly, "building", BUILDING_VALUE.get(kind, "yes"))) if name and kind in LABELLED_KINDS and poly.area >= MIN_LABELLED_TILES: named_buildings.append((poly.area, name, poly)) named_buildings.sort(key=lambda b: -b[0]) for _area, name, poly in named_buildings[:MAX_BUILDING_LABELS]: spot = poly.representative_point() labels.append((name, "text-building", BUILDING_SCALE, spot.x, spot.y)) bbox = info.get("bbox") or {} cache = os.path.join(out_dir, info["osm_cache"]) if info.get("osm_cache") \ else osm.cache_path(out_dir, map_name) wanted = tuple(info["osm_bbox"]) if info.get("osm_bbox") else \ (bbox.get("south"), bbox.get("west"), bbox.get("north"), bbox.get("east")) # Whatever download is beside the map, however old the filter list it was # fetched with. This step never fetches one, so turning an older file away # does not get the newer tags - it writes a map with the buildings on it # and not one road, river or wood. feats = osm.load_cache(cache, wanted, filters=None) or [] feats = osm.proposed_roads(feats, info.get("include_proposed_roads", 0)) if not feats: print(f" paper map : no download beside the map " f"({os.path.basename(cache)}), so it has buildings only - " f"generate the map again to put the streets back") if info.get("straight_roads"): # The streets as the map drew them, not as they are. from generator.octilinear import replay from generator.renderer import classify replay(feats, proj, classify, _is_polygon, info, out_dir, map_name) clip = shape_px(info.get("shape"), proj) streets: dict[str, list[tuple[LineString, float]]] = {} railways = [] for feat in feats: if feat.kind == "node": continue cat = osm.classify(feat.tags, _is_polygon(feat)) if cat in HIGHWAY_VALUE and not _is_polygon(feat): line = _line(feat, proj) if line is None: continue if clip is not None and cat not in THROUGH_ROADS: # The drawn shape's side streets only, as on the ground. line = line.intersection(clip) if line.is_empty or line.length < 1: continue if not isinstance(line, LineString): parts = [g for g in getattr(line, "geoms", []) if isinstance(g, LineString)] if not parts: continue line = max(parts, key=lambda g: g.length) width_tiles = _way_width_m(feat, cat) / metres_per_tile strip = line.buffer(width_tiles / 2, cap_style=2, join_style=2) poly = _clean(strip) if poly is not None: features.append((poly, "highway", HIGHWAY_VALUE[cat])) name = (feat.tags.get("name") or "").strip() if name and cat in NAMED_CLASSES: streets.setdefault(name, []).append((line, width_tiles)) elif cat == "railway" and not _is_polygon(feat): railways.append(feat) elif cat in AREA_VALUE and _is_polygon(feat): key, value = AREA_VALUE[cat] for ring in _outer_rings(feat, proj): poly = _clean(Polygon(ring)) if poly is not None: features.append((poly, key, value)) name = (feat.tags.get("name") or "").strip() if name and key == "water" and poly.area >= MIN_PLACE_TILES: spot = poly.representative_point() labels.append((name, "text-water-medium", 1.0, spot.x, spot.y)) elif cat in PLACE_CATEGORIES and _is_polygon(feat) and "highway" not in feat.tags: name = (feat.tags.get("name") or "").strip() rings = _outer_rings(feat, proj) if name and rings: poly = _clean(Polygon(rings[0])) if poly is not None and poly.area >= MIN_PLACE_TILES: spot = poly.representative_point() labels.append((name, "text-place", PLACE_SCALE, spot.x, spot.y)) from generator.rendering.rails import rail_paths for path in rail_paths(railways, proj): poly = _clean(LineString(path).buffer(RAIL_WIDTH_M / metres_per_tile / 2, cap_style=2, join_style=2)) if poly is not None: features.append((poly, "railway", "rail")) for sea in sea_polygons(feats, proj): for part in getattr(sea, "geoms", None) or [sea]: poly = _clean(part) if hasattr(part, "exterior") else None if poly is not None: features.append((poly, "water", "river")) cells = _write_worldmap(os.path.join(out_dir, "worldmap.xml"), features, width, height) named = _write_streets(os.path.join(out_dir, "streets.xml"), streets) places_path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_places.json") if os.path.exists(places_path): with open(places_path, encoding="utf-8") as f: for place in json.load(f): if place.get("inside") and place.get("name"): labels.append((place["name"], "text-town", TOWN_SCALE.get(place.get("place"), 2.0), place["tile_x"], place["tile_

def _write_annotations(path: str, labels: list[tuple[str, str, float, float, float]], width: int, height: int) -> None: """Text on the paper map, the way vanilla's worldmap-annotations.lua adds it.""" ox, oy = origin()[0] * CELL, origin()[1] * CELL seen = set() lines = ["return function(mapUI)", "	local mapAPI = mapUI.javaObject:getAPIv3()", "	local symbolsAPI = mapAPI:getSymbolsAPIv2()", "	local symbol"] for name, layer, scale, x, y in labels: if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height) or (name, layer) in seen: continue seen.add((name, layer)) lines += [ f"	symbol = symbolsAPI:addUntranslatedText({_lua_string(name)}, " f'"{layer}", {round(x + ox)}, {round(y + oy)})', "	symbol:setRGBA(0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.000)", f"	symbol:setScale({scale:.3f})", "	symbol:setAnchor(0.50, 0.50)", "	symbol:setRotation(0.0)", "	symbol:setMatchPerspective(true)", "	symbol:setApplyZoom(true)", "	symbol:setMinZoom(0.00)", "	symbol:setMaxZoom(24.00)", "	symbol:setUserDefined(false)", ""] lines.append("end") with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="
") as f: f.write("
".join(lines) + "
")

nodes.name: _clean
nodes.body_text: def _clean(poly) -> Polygon | None: if poly.is_empty: return None if not poly.is_valid: poly = poly.buffer(0) poly = poly.simplify(SIMPLIFY, preserve_topology=True) return None if poly.is_empty or poly.area < 1 else poly

nodes.name: _line
nodes.body_text: def _line(feat, proj) -> LineString | None: pts = [proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in feat.geometry] return LineString(pts) if len(pts) >= 2 else None

nodes.name: _outer_rings
nodes.body_text: def _outer_rings(feat, proj) -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]: if feat.kind == "way": return [[proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in feat.geometry]] return [[proj.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in ring] for role, ring in feat.role_geoms if role in ("outer", "") and len(ring) >= 3]

nodes.body_text: def _parts(geom) -> list[Polygon]: if geom.is_empty: return [] if isinstance(geom, Polygon): return [geom] return [g for g in getattr(geom, "geoms", []) if isinstance(g, Polygon)]

def _write_worldmap(path: str, features: list[tuple[Polygon, str, str]], width: int, height: int) -> int: """Clip every feature to the cells it crosses, in cell coordinates.""" ox, oy = origin() by_cell: dict[tuple[int, int], list[str]] = {} for poly, key, value in features: minx, miny, maxx, maxy = poly.bounds for cy in range(max(0, int(miny // CELL)), min(height // CELL, int(maxy // CELL) + 1)): for cx in range(max(0, int(minx // CELL)), min(width // CELL, int(maxx // CELL) + 1)): x0, y0 = cx * CELL, cy * CELL if minx >= x0 and maxx <= x0 + CELL and miny >= y0 and maxy <= y0 + CELL: clipped = poly else: clipped = poly.intersection(box(x0, y0, x0 + CELL, y0 + CELL)) for part in _parts(clipped): if part.area < 1: continue ring = list(part.exterior.coords)[:-1] pts = "
".join( f' <point x="{round(x - x0)}" y="{round(y - y0)}"/>' for x, y in ring) by_cell.setdefault((cx, cy), []).append( ' <feature>
 <geometry type="Polygon">
' f' <coordinates>
{pts}
 </coordinates>
' ' </geometry>
 <properties>
' f' <property name="{key}" value={quoteattr(value)}/>
' ' </properties>
 </feature>') with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="
") as f: f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<world version="1.0">
') for (cx, cy) in sorted(by_cell, key=lambda c: (c[1], c[0])): f.write(f' <cell x="{ox + cx}" y="{oy + cy}">
') f.write("
".join(by_cell[(cx, cy)])) f.write("
 </cell>
") f.write("</world>
") return len(by_cell)

nodes.body_text: def _street_pieces(coords: list, most: int = MAX_STREET_POINTS) -> list[list]: """`coords` cut into runs of at most `most` points, each starting on the last one's final point, so together they are the same line (see MAX_STREET_POINTS).""" if len(coords) <= most: return [coords] pieces, i = [], 0 while i < len(coords) - 1: pieces.append(coords[i:i + most]) i += most - 1 return pieces

def _write_streets(path: str, streets: dict[str, list[tuple[LineString, float]]]) -> int: """One entry per continuous stretch of each named street.""" ox, oy = origin()[0] * CELL, origin()[1] * CELL count = 0 with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="
") as f: f.write('<streets version="1">
') for name in sorted(streets): pieces = streets[name] width = max(3, round(max(w for _l, w in pieces))) joined = unary_union([l for l, _w in pieces]) merged = linemerge(joined) if isinstance(joined, MultiLineString) else joined lines = [merged] if isinstance(merged, LineString) else \ list(getattr(merged, "geoms", [])) for line in lines: line = line.simplify(SIMPLIFY) if line.length < 10: continue for coords in _street_pieces(list(line.coords)): pts = "
".join(f' <point x="{x + ox:.1f}" y="{y + oy:.1f}"/>' for x, y in coords) f.write(f' <street name={quoteattr(name)} width="{width}">
' f' <points>
{pts}
 </points>
 </street>
') count += 1 f.write("</streets>
") return count

nodes.name: worldmap_bin.py
nodes.body_text: """worldmap.xml.bin: the paper map in the form Build 42 actually reads. The in-game map (M) showed street names and nothing else - no roads, no buildings, no water. worldmap.xml was being read, but Build 42 no longer loads that format properly: its XML reader stores each outline's length in coordinates rather than points, reads twice as far as it wrote, and every outline fails with an IndexOutOfBoundsException (console.txt: "Error while parsing xml element: geometry"). The game's own maps, and every working Build 42 map mod, ship the binary file beside the XML, and when it is there the game reads that instead. It also uses the new 256-tile cells, where the XML is in the old 300-tile ones. The layout, from the game's WorldMapBinary reader and checked against Muldraugh's own file (every byte of it parses): "IGMB" int version = 2 int cell size = 256 int width, int height cells, counted from cell 0, 0 int n, n x (short length, UTF-8 bytes) the string table width x height cells, row by row: int -1 no data in this cell, or int x, int y, int features, then per feature: short type (a string index: "Polygon") byte rings, per ring: short points, points x (short x, short y) byte properties, per property: short key, short value (indices) Points are in tiles from the cell's corner. Everything is little-endian. The binary is converted from worldmap.xml, so a map built before this gets its paper map back when it is installed again. """ from __future__ import annotations import struct import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET from shapely.geometry import Polygon, box from shapely.validation import make_valid XML_CELL = 300 BIN_CELL = 256 # A polygon smaller than this draws as nothing and is not worth the risk. MIN_AREA = 1.0 # The game keeps all of a cell's points in one buffer and remembers where each # outline starts in it as a 16-bit number: past 32767 values - 16383 points - # the start wraps negative and every outline after it fails to load. Knox # County's densest cell has about 1600. A packed city centre can have more. CELL_POINT_BUDGET = 15000 # The triangles are kept the same way: every outline's triangles go into one # buffer per cell whose start the game also keeps as a 16-bit number # (WorldMapGeometry.triangulate), so past 32767 indices the start wraps # negative and WorldMapRenderer.fillPolygon reads outside the buffer - the M # map stops drawing and throws every frame ("forgot to call endRun()"). A # polygon of n points is about 3n indices, so the point budget alone let a # packed city cell reach 45,000 (Hamburg). A road is triangulated again at # each of the five zoom levels it is simplified for, so it counts six times. CELL_INDEX_BUDGET = 30000 HIGHWAY_COPIES = 6 # What goes first when a cell is over it: the small things. KEEP_ORDER = ("water", "highway", "railway", "building", "natural")

nodes.name: _features
nodes.body_text: def _features(xml_path: str): """(rings in world tiles, [(key, value)]) for every feature in the XML.""" root = ET.parse(xml_path).getroot() for cell in root.iter("cell"): ox = int(cell.get("x")) * XML_CELL oy = int(cell.get("y")) * XML_CELL for feature in cell.iter("feature"): geometry = feature.find("geometry") if geometry is None or geometry.get("type", "Polygon") != "Polygon": continue rings = [] for coords in geometry.iter("coordinates"): ring = [(ox + int(float(p.get("x"))), oy + int(float(p.get("y")))) for p in coords.iter("point")] if len(ring) >= 3: rings.append(ring) if not rings: continue props = [(p.get("name"), p.get("value")) for p in feature.iter("property") if p.get("name")] yield rings, props

nodes.name: _polygons
nodes.body_text: def _polygons(shape): """Every polygon in whatever a clip or a repair handed back. make_valid can answer with a collection holding loose lines beside the shapes.""" if shape.geom_type == "Polygon": if not shape.is_empty: yield shape elif hasattr(shape, "geoms"): for part in shape.geoms: yield from _polygons(part)

nodes.name: _ring
nodes.body_text: def _ring(points) -> list | None: """One ring at whole tiles, or None if rounding has collapsed it.""" out = [] for x, y in points: point = (round(x), round(y)) if not out or point != out[-1]: out.append(point) while len(out) > 1 and out[0] == out[-1]: out.pop() return out if len(set(out)) >= 3 else None

nodes.name: _clean
nodes.body_text: def _clean(rings) -> list[list]: """Rings rounded to whole tiles, checked again after the rounding. Rounding is what breaks them: corners land on the same tile and the shape collapses, or edges cross. The game cannot triangulate either, and throws in WorldMapRenderer.fillPolygon when the map is zoomed out. """ tidy = [r for r in (_ring(ring) for ring in rings) if r] if not tidy: return [] try: shape = Polygon(tidy[0], tidy[1:]) if not shape.is_valid: # make_valid over buffer(0): buffer keeps only the lobes that wind # the right way, so half of a crossed outline would disappear. shape = make_valid(shape) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a broken outline is left off, not fatal return [] out = [] for part in _polygons(shape): if part.area < MIN_AREA: continue piece = [r for r in (_ring(ring.coords) for ring in [part.exterior, *part.interiors]) if r] if not piece: continue # A repair can put a corner on a half tile, so the rounding above may # have broken it again. Whatever is left is what gets written. try: final = Polygon(piece[0], piece[1:]) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 continue if final.is_valid and not final.is_empty and final.area >= MIN_AREA: out.append(piece) return out

nodes.name: _pieces
nodes.body_text: def _pieces(rings, cell_x, cell_y): """The part of a polygon inside one 256-tile cell, as ring lists.""" x0, y0 = cell_x * BIN_CELL, cell_y * BIN_CELL try: shape = Polygon(rings[0], rings[1:]) if not shape.is_valid: shape = make_valid(shape) clipped = shape.intersection(box(x0, y0, x0 + BIN_CELL, y0 + BIN_CELL)) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a broken outline is left off, not fatal return [] out = [] for part in _polygons(clipped): out.extend(_clean([[(x - x0, y - y0) for x, y in ring.coords] for ring in [part.exterior, *part.interiors]])) return out

nodes.name: _points
nodes.body_text: def _points(piece) -> int: return sum(len(ring) for ring in piece)

nodes.name: _indices
nodes.body_text: def _indices(piece, props) -> int: """Triangle indices the game will keep for this outline (see CELL_INDEX_BUDGET).""" copies = HIGHWAY_COPIES if any(k == "highway" for k, _ in props) else 1 return 3 * _points(piece) * copies

nodes.name: _fits
nodes.body_text: def _fits(features: list) -> bool: return (sum(_points(p) for p, _ in features) <= CELL_POINT_BUDGET and sum(_indices(p, props) for p, props in features) <= CELL_INDEX_BUDGET)

nodes.name: _within_budget
nodes.body_text: def _within_budget(features: list) -> list: """A cell's features, simplified and then thinned until they fit.""" if _fits(features): return features for tolerance in (0.75, 1.5, 3.0): simpler = [] for piece, props in features: try: shape = Polygon(piece[0], piece[1:]).simplify(tolerance, preserve_topology=True) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 simpler.append((piece, props)) continue if shape.is_empty or shape.geom_type != "Polygon" or len(shape.exterior.coords) < 4: continue for cleaned in _clean([r.coords for r in [shape.exterior, *shape.interiors]]): simpler.append((cleaned, props)) features = simpler if _fits(features): return features def rank(item): piece, props = item keys = [k for k, _ in props] kind = min((KEEP_ORDER.index(k) for k in keys if k in KEEP_ORDER), default=len(KEEP_ORDER)) xs = [x for x, _ in piece[0]] ys = [y for _, y in piece[0]] return (kind, -(max(xs) - min(xs)) * (max(ys) - min(ys))) kept, total, tris = [], 0, 0 for item in sorted(features, key=rank): n, t = _points(item[0]), _indices(*item) if total + n <= CELL_POINT_BUDGET and tris + t <= CELL_INDEX_BUDGET: kept.append(item) total += n tris += t return kept

nodes.name: rank
nodes.body_text: def rank(item): piece, props = item keys = [k for k, _ in props] kind = min((KEEP_ORDER.index(k) for k in keys if k in KEEP_ORDER), default=len(KEEP_ORDER)) xs = [x for x, _ in piece[0]] ys = [y for _, y in piece[0]] return (kind, -(max(xs) - min(xs)) * (max(ys) - min(ys)))

nodes.name: write_bin
nodes.signature: def write_bin(xml_path: str, bin_path: str) -> int
nodes.body_text: def write_bin(xml_path: str, bin_path: str) -> int: """Convert worldmap.xml to worldmap.xml.bin. Returns features written.""" cells: dict[tuple[int, int], list] = {} for rings, props in _features(xml_path): xs = [x for x, _ in rings[0]] ys = [y for _, y in rings[0]] cx0, cx1 = min(xs) // BIN_CELL, max(xs) // BIN_CELL cy0, cy1 = min(ys) // BIN_CELL, max(ys) // BIN_CELL if cx0 == cx1 and cy0 == cy1: if cx0 < 0 or cy0 < 0: continue local = [[(x - cx0 * BIN_CELL, y - cy0 * BIN_CELL) for x, y in r] for r in rings] for piece in _clean(local): cells.setdefault((cx0, cy0), []).append((piece, props)) continue for cy in range(max(0, cy0), cy1 + 1): for cx in range(max(0, cx0), cx1 + 1): for piece in _pieces(rings, cx, cy): cells.setdefault((cx, cy), []).append((piece, props)) for key in list(cells): cells[key] = _within_budget(cells[key]) strings: dict[str, int] = {} def index(text: str) -> int: if text not in strings: strings[text] = len(strings) return strings[text] index("Polygon") body = bytearray() width = max((x for x, _ in cells), default=-1) + 1 height = max((y for _, y in cells), default=-1) + 1 count = 0 for y in range(height): for x in range(width): features = cells.get((x, y)) if not features: body += struct.pack("<i", -1) continue features = features[:0x7FFFFFFF] body += struct.pack("<iii", x, y, len(features)) for piece, props in features: body += struct.pack("<hB", index("Polygon"), min(len(piece), 255)) for ring in piece[:255]: ring = ring[:32767] body += struct.pack("<h", len(ring)) for px, py in ring: body += struct.pack("<hh", max(-32768, min(32767, px)), max(-32768, min(32767, py))) props = props[:255] body += struct.pack("<B", len(props)) for key, value in props: body += struct.pack("<hh", index(key), index(value or "")) count += 1 head = bytearray(b"IGMB") head += struct.pack("<iiii", 2, BIN_CELL, width, height) head += struct.pack("<i", len(strings)) for text in sorted(strings, key=strings.get): raw = text.encode("utf-8") head += struct.pack("<h", len(raw)) + raw with open(bin_path, "wb") as f: f.write(head + body) return count

nodes.name: index
nodes.body_text: def index(text: str) -> int: if text not in strings: strings[text] = len(strings) return strings[text]

nodes.name: read_bin
nodes.body_text: def read_bin(bin_path: str) -> dict: """The file read back the way the game reads it, for the self-test: {(cell x, cell y): [(rings, {key: value})]}.""" with open(bin_path, "rb") as f: data = f.read() pos = 0 def take(fmt): nonlocal pos values = struct.unpack_from(fmt, data, pos) pos += struct.calcsize(fmt) return values if len(values) > 1 else values[0] if data[:4] != b"IGMB": raise ValueError("invalid format (magic doesn't match)") pos = 4 version, cell, width, height = take("<iiii") if version != 2 or cell != 256: raise ValueError(f"version {version}, cell size {cell}") strings = [] for _ in range(take("<i")): n = take("<h") strings.append(data[pos:pos + n].decode("utf-8")) pos += n out = {} for _ in range(width * height): x = take("<i") if x == -1: continue y, n = take("<ii") feats = [] for _ in range(n): kind = strings[take("<h")] rings = [] for _ in range(take("<B")): rings.append([take("<hh") for _ in range(take("<h"))]) props = {strings[take("<h")]: strings[take("<h")] for _ in range(take("<B"))} feats.append((kind, rings, props)) out[(x, y)] = feats if pos != len(data): raise ValueError(f"{len(data) - pos} bytes left over") return out

nodes.name: take
nodes.body_text: def take(fmt): nonlocal pos values = struct.unpack_from(fmt, data, pos) pos += struct.calcsize(fmt) return values if len(values) > 1 else values[0]

nodes.name: yards.py
nodes.body_text: """The front and back of every house: path, stoop, drive, mailbox, bin, fence. Knox County's houses have all of these and generated ones stood in unbroken lawn with the front door opening onto grass. The door is only known once the building is laid out, after the terrain was drawn, so they are painted into the terrain and vegetation bitmaps here, starting from the renderer's untouched copy of the ground (<map>_ground_base.bmp) so that building again does not keep old paths. Back-yard fences are returned as lines for the fence builder (knoxbuild/fences.py). Measured on the vanilla map's outdoor squares: stone slabs (floors_exterior_tilesandstone_01) are its commonest outdoor floor after grass, dark tarmac drives the next, then wooden fences. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import random import re import shutil from collections import deque import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from .bitmaps import read_rgb, same_colour # A farmhouse stands well back from its road, and its drive and front path run # that far. The path stops at the drive when it meets it first. On Piqua 383 # houses were a median 61 tiles from the pavement with no straight drive. PATH_MAX_TILES = 120 GARAGE_DRIVE_MAX_TILES = 40 # A house the terrain already gave a drive to (generator/rendering/homesteads.py: # a house in the woods) gets no second one beside it: tarmac this near its walls. DRIVE_THERE_TILES = 3 # Who gets a front path, a stoop and a porch light. Only houses get the drive # and the yard: flats and public buildings have lots of their own. On Piqua # 91% of the flats had no way to the street before this. FRONT_PATH_KINDS = ("house", "apartment", "church", "civic", "medical", "library") DRIVE_WIDTH = 3 DRIVE_EXTRA = 5 # how far the drive runs past the front of the house YARD_DEPTH = 9 # back yard, from the back wall to the back fence YARD_MIN_DEPTH = 4 YARD_SIDE = 2 # how far the fence stands out past the house's sides PAVED = (C.PALE_CONCRETE, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT) CROSSABLE = (C.DARK_GRASS, C.MEDIUM_GRASS, C.LIGHT_GRASS, C.DIRT, C.DIRT_ROWS_H, C.DIRT_ROWS_V) YARD_FENCE_STYLES = ("tall_wooden", "short_wooden", "white_picket", "short_chainlink") YARD_ARCHETYPES = ("family", "grill", "laundry", "garden", "bare") YARD_ARCHETYPE_WEIGHTS = (30, 22, 18, 18, 12) YARD_FENCE_WEIGHTS = (40, 30, 18, 12) FENCED_SHARE = 0.85 # A light by the front door. Knox County has one on 92% of its houses and a # railing on 71%; generated ones had a light on 1%, which is most of why they # read as unfinished from the street. Seven in ten of the game's sit within a # tile of a door, all but 3% on the ground outside the wall rather than on the # building's own tiles, so that is where these go. # # Which sprite goes on which wall was read off the vanilla map, not guessed: # for every outdoor light standing outside a house with house tiles on exactly # one side, that side. The five sets below each came back 96-100% one-sided # over 60 to 140 sightings. The key is the side the house is on, seen from the # light's own tile. PORCH_LIGHTS = [ {"N": "lighting_outdoor_01_24", "W": "lighting_outdoor_01_25", "S": "lighting_outdoor_01_28", "E": "lighting_outdoor_01_29"}, {"N": "lighting_outdoor_01_26", "W": "lighting_outdoor_01_27", "S": "lighting_outdoor_01_30", "E": "lighting_outdoor_01_31"}, {"N": "lighting_outdoor_01_32", "W": "lighting_outdoor_01_33", "S": "lighting_outdoor_01_36", "E": "lighting_outdoor_01_37"}, {"N": "lighting_outdoor_01_34", "W": "lighting_outdoor_01_35", "S": "lighting_outdoor_01_39", "E": "lighting_outdoor_01_38"}, {"N": "lighting_outdoor_01_40", "W": "lighting_outdoor_01_41", "S": "lighting_outdoor_01_44", "E": "lighting_outdoor_01_45"}, ] PORCH_LIGHT_SHARE = 0.92 # The square the light stands on usually carries the house wall as well, and # what is written last is drawn last: on the Furniture layer the wall went on # top and the light was invisible. Every one of the 659 vanilla porch lights # that shares a square with an exterior wall is written after it. PORCH_LIGHT_LAYER = "WallFurniture" # The side the house is on, from the tile the light stands on. _SIDE = {(0, -1): "N", (0, 1): "S", (-1, 0): "W", (1, 0): "E"} _OUTSIDE_DOORS_CACHE: dict[tuple[str, int], list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]] = {} DOOR_FRONT_DEPTH = 2

nodes.name: yard_plan
nodes.signature: def yard_plan(bx0: int, by0: int) -> tuple[str, bool, str]
nodes.body_text: def yard_plan(bx0: int, by0: int) -> tuple[str, bool, str]: """(fence style, fenced, archetype) for the house at bx0,by0. Stable per house so a rebuild is the same map, and independent of the order houses are visited in. """ rng = random.Random((bx0 * 73856093) ^ (by0 * 19349663) ^ 0x9E3779B9) style = rng.choices(YARD_FENCE_STYLES, weights=YARD_FENCE_WEIGHTS)[0] fenced = rng.random() < FENCED_SHARE archetype = rng.choices(YARD_ARCHETYPES, weights=YARD_ARCHETYPE_WEIGHTS)[0] return style, fenced, archetype

nodes.name: _outside_doors
nodes.signature: def _outside_doors(tbx_path: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _outside_doors(tbx_path: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int]]: """(outside x, y, inside x, y) of each ground-floor outside door, front first.""" try: key = (tbx_path, os.stat(tbx_path).st_mtime_ns) except OSError: key = None if key is not None and key in _OUTSIDE_DOORS_CACHE: return _OUTSIDE_DOORS_CACHE[key] with open(tbx_path, encoding="utf-8") as f: text = f.read() first = text.split("<floor>", 2) if len(first) < 2: return [] floor = first[1] grid_text = re.search(r"<rooms>(.*?)</rooms>", floor, re.S) if not grid_text: return [] grid = [[int(v) for v in row.strip().strip(",").split(",")] for row in grid_text.group(1).strip().splitlines() if row.strip()] h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0]) def inside(x, y): return 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and grid[y][x] != 0 found = [] for m in re.finditer(r'type="door"[^>]*? x="(\d+)" y="(\d+)" dir="([NW])"', floor): x, y, d = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3) a, b = ((x, y - 1), (x, y)) if d == "N" else ((x - 1, y), (x, y)) if inside(*a) != inside(*b): out, into = (a, b) if inside(*b) else (b, a) found.append((out[0], out[1], into[0], into[1])) if key is not None: _OUTSIDE_DOORS_CACHE[key] = found return found

nodes.name: inside
nodes.body_text: def inside(x, y): return 0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and grid[y][x] != 0

nodes.name: door_fronts
nodes.signature: def door_fronts(out_dir: str, rows: list[dict]) -> set[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def door_fronts(out_dir: str, rows: list[dict]) -> set[tuple[int, int]]: """The squares in front of every ground-floor outside door, DOOR_FRONT_DEPTH deep, as map tiles: where nothing that blocks (a tree, a fence) may stand.""" from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: lists = list(pool.map(lambda r: _outside_doors(os.path.join(out_dir, "buildings", r["file"])), rows)) out: set[tuple[int, int]] = set() for row, doors in zip(rows, lists): for ox, oy, ix, iy in doors: dx, dy = ox - ix, oy - iy for k in range(DOOR_FRONT_DEPTH): out.add((row["tile_x"] + ox + dx * k, row["tile_y"] + oy + dy * k)) return out

nodes.name: _pave_patio
nodes.signature: def _pave_patio(ground, veg, crossable, claimed, cells, colour=C.PAVING_STONE)
nodes.body_text: def _pave_patio(ground, veg, crossable, claimed, cells, colour=C.PAVING_STONE): """Pave only unclaimed lawn so one home's patio cannot overwrite a neighbor's path.""" h, w = crossable.shape paved = [] for x, y in cells: if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h) or not crossable[y, x] or claimed[y, x]: continue ground[y, x] = colour if veg is not None: veg[y, x] = C.VEG_NOTHING paved.append((x, y)) return paved

nodes.name: paint_paths
nodes.signature: def paint_paths(out_dir: str, map_name: str, rows: list[dict], occupied, drives: list | None = None, lights: list | None = None, fronts: set | None = None) -> tuple[int, list]
nodes.body_text: def paint_paths(out_dir: str, map_name: str, rows: list[dict], occupied, drives: list | None = None, lights: list | None = None, fronts: set | None = None) -> tuple[int, list]: """Dress houses and connect mapped garages. Return houses dressed and fences. Each drive's parking space, (x, y, width, height) at its house end, is added to `drives` when it is given: the car belongs there. Porch lights are added to `lights` the same way, as (x, y, level, layer, tile) for whoever writes them into a .tbx.""" bmp = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}.bmp") base = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_ground_base.bmp") veg_path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_veg.bmp") veg_base = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{map_name}_veg_base.bmp") if not os.path.exists(bmp): return 0, [] if not os.path.exists(base): shutil.copyfile(bmp, base) if os.path.exists(veg_path) and not os.path.exists(veg_base): shutil.copyfile(veg_path, veg_base) ground = read_rgb(base) veg = read_rgb(veg_base) if os.path.exists(veg_base) else None h, w = ground.shape[:2] def match(colours): mask = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool) for c in colours: mask |= same_colour(ground, c) return mask paved = match(PAVED) road = match((C.DARK_ASPHALT, C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, C.LIGHT_ASPHALT, C.DARKEST_ASPHALT, C.DARK_POTHOLE, C.LIGHT_POTHOLE)) crossable = match(CROSSABLE) & ~occupied # Painted for some house already. One block of memory seen two ways: as an # array for the whole-map work, and as bytes for the tile-at-a-time loops # below, where reading a numpy element costs several times what a list # does. The masks that never change are read the same way, as flat lists # indexed y * w + x. claimed_bytes = bytearray(h * w) claimed = np.frombuffer(claimed_bytes, dtype=bool).reshape(h, w) crossable_at = crossable.ravel().tolist() paved_at = paved.ravel().tolist() occupied_at = np.asarray(occupied, dtype=bool).ravel().tolist() road_at = road.ravel().tolist() walkable_at = ((crossable | paved | road) & ~occupied).ravel().tolist() # Drives the terrain laid already, read before any are painted here. laid = same_colour(ground, C.DARK_ASPHALT) def drive_there(bx0, by0, bw, bh): """Tiles of a drive already reaching this house, nearest first, or [].""" r = DRIVE_THERE_TILES x0, y0 = max(0, bx0 - r), max(0, by0 - r) x1, y1 = min(w, bx0 + bw + r), min(h, by0 + bh + r) ys, xs = np.nonzero(laid[y0:y1, x0:x1]) if not len(xs): return [] xs, ys = xs + x0, ys + y0 dx = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(bx0 - xs, xs - (bx0 + bw - 1))) dy = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(by0 - ys, ys - (by0 + bh - 1))) order = np.argsort(dx + dy, kind="stable") return [(int(xs[i]), int(ys[i])) for i in order] def free(x, y): return (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and crossable_at[y * w + x] and not claimed_bytes[y * w + x]) def paint(x, y, colour): ground[y, x] = colour claimed_bytes[y * w + x] = 1 if veg is not None: veg[y, x] = 0 def put(x, y, colour): if veg is not None and free(x, y): veg[y, x] = colour claimed_bytes[y * w + x] = 1 dressed = 0 fences = [] rng = random.Random(0xB17E) # Reading a thousand freshly written .tbx files is mostly waiting on the # disk, so it is done on threads up front; the loop below still runs in # order, which keeps the random choices the same. from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor house_files = [r["file"] for r in rows if r.get("kind") in FRONT_PATH_KINDS] with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool: door_lists = dict(zip(house_files, pool.map( lambda f: _outside_doors(os.path.join(out_dir, "buildings", f)), house_files))) for row in rows: if row.get("kind") not in FRONT_PATH_KINDS: continue home = row["kind"] == "house" doors = door_lists[row["file"]] if not doors: continue ox, oy, ix, iy = doors[0] bx0, by0 = row["tile_x"], row["tile_y"] bw, bh = row["width"], row["height"] sx, sy = bx0 + ox, by0 + oy dx, dy = ox - ix, oy - iy # out of the door, towards the street px, py = -dy, dx # along the front of the house # A light on the wall beside the door. It goes outside the building, # past the edge of the house's own .tbx, so it is written as a loose # tile. Ahead of the path and the stoop because it does not depend on # either: a house with nowhere to run a path still has a front light. side = _SIDE.get((-dx, -dy)) if lights is not None and side and rng.random() < PORCH_LIGHT_SHARE: style = rng.choice(PORCH_LIGHTS) for k in (1, -1): lx, ly = sx + px * k, sy + py * k if not (0 <= lx < w and 0 <= ly < h) or occupied_at[ly * w + lx]: continue # Only where the house really is behind it: beside a door in a # corner, one of the two faces open ground. wx, wy = lx - dx, ly - dy if not (0 <= wx < w and 0 <= wy < h and occupied_at[wy * w + wx]): continue lights.append((lx, ly, 0, PORCH_LIGHT_LAYER, style[side])) break if not free(sx, sy): continue # The drive: beside the house, from the street past the front wall. # Ahead of the path, so that a house far back from the street can walk # to its own drive. there = drive_there(bx0, by0, bw, bh) if home else [] if not home: lanes = [] elif there: # The

nodes.name: match
nodes.body_text: def match(colours): mask = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool) for c in colours: mask |= same_colour(ground, c) return mask

nodes.name: drive_there
nodes.body_text: def drive_there(bx0, by0, bw, bh): """Tiles of a drive already reaching this house, nearest first, or [].""" r = DRIVE_THERE_TILES x0, y0 = max(0, bx0 - r), max(0, by0 - r) x1, y1 = min(w, bx0 + bw + r), min(h, by0 + bh + r) ys, xs = np.nonzero(laid[y0:y1, x0:x1]) if not len(xs): return [] xs, ys = xs + x0, ys + y0 dx = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(bx0 - xs, xs - (bx0 + bw - 1))) dy = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(by0 - ys, ys - (by0 + bh - 1))) order = np.argsort(dx + dy, kind="stable") return [(int(xs[i]), int(ys[i])) for i in order]

nodes.name: free
nodes.body_text: def free(x, y): return (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h and crossable_at[y * w + x] and not claimed_bytes[y * w + x])

nodes.name: paint
nodes.body_text: def paint(x, y, colour): ground[y, x] = colour claimed_bytes[y * w + x] = 1 if veg is not None: veg[y, x] = 0

nodes.name: put
nodes.body_text: def put(x, y, colour): if veg is not None and free(x, y): veg[y, x] = colour claimed_bytes[y * w + x] = 1

nodes.name: at
nodes.body_text: def at(u, v, u0=u0): """World tile u along the back wall, v rows back from it.""" return ((u0 + u, back + bdy * v) if dy else (back + bdx * v, u0 + u))

nodes.name: place
nodes.body_text: def place(u, v, colour, ground_colour=None): x, y = at(u, v) if (x, y) in taken or not free(x, y): return False taken.add((x, y)) if ground_colour is not None: paint(x, y, ground_colour) if colour is not None and veg is not None: veg[y, x] = colour claimed_bytes[y * w + x] = 1 return True

nodes.name: place_pair
nodes.body_text: def place_pair(first, second): """Both halves of one two-tile sprite, or neither: a half alone is half a deck chair.""" for u, v, _c in (first, second): x, y = at(u, v) if (x, y) in taken or not free(x, y): return False return place(*first) and place(*second)

nodes.name: veg_bed

nodes.name: zones.py
nodes.body_text: """Zones the mapper draws, each with its own settings. One set of settings for a whole map makes one kind of town. A real one is not one kind: the centre is taller and denser than the edge, the estate on the hill is all the same brick, the industrial end has no houses in it and the quarantine block has ten times the zombies. Until now the only way to get any of that was to build two maps and hope they met in the middle. A zone is a polygon with a few settings written on it. Anything inside it is built to those; anything outside is built to the map's own. Only the settings that can sensibly differ from one part of a town to another are allowed (OVERRIDABLE) - a zone cannot change the scale or the seed, because those decide what the whole map is - and a zone may also name the wall style its buildings are built in, which is the one thing that is not an ordinary setting. Zones nest, and the smallest one containing a point wins, the way knoxbuild/areas.py does it: a street of shops inside a town centre inside a map is read from the inside out. """ from __future__ import annotations import os from dataclasses import replace import knoxfiles from shapely import STRtree from shapely.geometry import Point, Polygon from .areas import parts from .settings import LIMITS, Settings # What a zone may say about itself. These are the settings whose answer can # honestly differ between two parts of one town; the rest decide what the map # is rather than what a district is like, and are left alone: # # seed the map is one map, and a zone with its own seed would # rebuild differently every time the zone was nudged # align_streets the whole map is turned, or none of it is # rotate_degrees the same # straight_roads the roads are drawn once, before any zone is read # fill_gaps the download happens before there are zones to read # fill_frontage the buildings are added while the ground is drawn # building_alignment a footprint is squared up before its centre is known OVERRIDABLE = ( # --- what is built --- "max_levels", "apartment_chance", "apartment_footprint", "true_map", "min_size", "max_size", "room_size", "neighbourhood_tiles", "style_oddity", "vanilla_tiles", "room_solver", # --- who is in it --- "spawn_density", "zombies_per_resident", "m2_per_person", # --- what is around it --- "tree_density", "parking_density", ) # A zone may also pin the walls its buildings are built in - "the estate on # the hill is all the same brick" - which is not a setting but a style name # out of the catalogue (knoxbuild/build.py, pick_style). STYLE_KEY = "wall_style" # And the hand-built buildings it draws from, by name (knoxbuild/presets.py). # A footprint in the zone takes one that fits inside it; one that nothing fits # is laid out by the generator as usual, because a town with holes in it where # no preset fitted is worse than one with generated houses among the built. PRESETS_KEY = "presets"

nodes.name: overridable
nodes.body_text: def overridable() -> list[dict]: """The settings a zone may set, with their limits, for the window.""" base = Settings().to_dict() out = [] for name in OVERRIDABLE: lo, hi = LIMITS[name] out.append({"id": name, "default": base[name], "min": lo, "max": hi, "int": isinstance(base[name], int)}) return out

nodes.name: _listed
nodes.body_text: def _listed(value) -> list: """A list of whatever was sent, or nothing. A cleaner never throws: this reads what the window posts and what is on disk, and a number where a list was expected used to come back as a Python TypeError.""" return list(value) if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) else []

nodes.name: _table
nodes.body_text: def _table(value) -> dict: return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}

nodes.name: clean
nodes.body_text: def clean(raw) -> list[dict]: """Zones from untrusted input: a ring and the settings on it. A zone is kept as drawn - a ring of (lon, lat) - because that is what it was drawn as and what it has to be drawn as again. """ out = [] for item in raw if isinstance(raw, list) else []: if not isinstance(item, dict): continue ring = [] for point in _listed(item.get("ring")): try: ring.append((float(point[0]), float(point[1]))) except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError): ring = [] break if len(ring) < 3: continue values = {} for key, value in _table(item.get("settings")).items(): if key not in OVERRIDABLE: continue try: number = float(value) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue if number != number: # NaN compares false with everything continue lo, hi = LIMITS[key] values[key] = min(max(number, lo), hi) style = item.get(STYLE_KEY) zone = {"name": str(item.get("name") or "")[:60], "ring": ring, "settings": values} if isinstance(style, str) and style.strip(): zone[STYLE_KEY] = style.strip()[:40] chosen = item.get(PRESETS_KEY) if isinstance(chosen, list): names = [str(n).strip()[:60] for n in chosen if str(n).strip()] if names: zone[PRESETS_KEY] = names[:200] out.append(zone) return out

nodes.signature: def load(out_dir: str, map_name: str) -> list[dict]: # A damaged zones file is said rather than swallowed: a build that drops # the zones is a map built to the wrong numbers everywhere they were.
