nodes.name: Zoning
nodes.body_text: class Zoning: """The zones of one map, ready to be asked about a point. Built once and asked once per building, so the polygons are projected into tile coordinates up front and indexed; asking is a tree lookup and a `contains`, not a walk through every zone. """ def __init__(self, items: list[tuple[Polygon, dict]], settings: Settings): self._items = items self._tree = STRtree([p for p, _ in items]) if items else None # A zone drawn over itself comes in in pieces; it is still one zone, # and both "the smallest zone here wins" and the order they are # painted in go by the whole of it, not by the piece. self._whole: dict[int, float] = {} for shape, zone in items: self._whole[id(zone)] = self._whole.get(id(zone), 0.0) + shape.area self._base = settings # The same zone is asked about over and over - every building in a # district, every chunk of the spawn map - and a Settings is frozen, # so each zone's answer is worked out once. self._settled: dict[int, Settings] = {} @classmethod def build(cls, zones, proj, settings: Settings) -> "Zoning": items = [] for zone in clean(zones): ring = [proj.to_px(lat, lon) for lon, lat in zone["ring"]] shape = Polygon(ring) if not shape.is_valid: shape = shape.buffer(0) # A zone whose outline crosses itself mends into several # polygons, and one of those in the index has no ring to draw. for part in parts(shape): if part.area <= 0: continue items.append((part, zone)) return cls(items, settings) @classmethod def load(cls, out_dir: str, map_name: str, proj, settings: Settings) -> "Zoning": return cls.build(load(out_dir, map_name), proj, settings) def __len__(self) -> int: return len(self._items) def at(self, x: float, y: float) -> dict | None: """The zone a point is in: the smallest one, so zones can nest.""" if self._tree is None: return None point = Point(x, y) best = None for i in self._tree.query(point): shape, zone = self._items[int(i)] size = self._whole.get(id(zone), shape.area) if shape.contains(point) and (best is None or size < best[0]): best = (size, zone) return best[1] if best else None def settings_at(self, x: float, y: float) -> Settings: """The map's settings, with whatever the zone here says on top.""" zone = self.at(x, y) if zone is None or not zone["settings"]: return self._base key = id(zone) settled = self._settled.get(key) if settled is None: fields = {f: type(getattr(self._base, f))(v) for f, v in zone["settings"].items()} settled = self._settled[key] = replace(self._base, **fields) return settled def style_at(self, x: float, y: float) -> str | None: """The wall style this zone pins its buildings to, if it pins one.""" zone = self.at(x, y) return zone.get(STYLE_KEY) if zone else None def presets_at(self, x: float, y: float) -> list[str]: """The hand-built buildings this zone draws from, by name.""" zone = self.at(x, y) return list(zone.get(PRESETS_KEY) or ()) if zone else [] def any_presets(self) -> bool: """Whether any zone names a preset, so the library is read once.""" return any(z.get(PRESETS_KEY) for _shape, z in self._items) def chunk_values(self, keys, gw: int, gh: int, tiles_per_chunk: int) -> dict: """One value per chunk for each named setting, as arrays. The spawn map is drawn a chunk at a time over the whole map, and asking `settings_at` for every chunk of a big one is millions of point-in-polygon tests. The zones are painted into the chunk grid once instead, biggest first so a zone inside another one wins, and the answer is read off. """ import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw out = {key: np.full((gh, gw), float(getattr(self._base, key)), dtype=float) for key in keys} if not self._items: return out for shape, zone in sorted( self._items, key=lambda it: -self._whole.get(id(it[1]), it[0].area)): values = {k: zone["settings"][k] for k in keys if k in zone["settings"]} if not values: continue mask = Image.new("1", (gw, gh), 0) pen = ImageDraw.Draw(mask) for part in parts(shape): ring = [(x / tiles_per_chunk, y / tiles_per_chunk) for x, y in part.exterior.coords] if len(ring) >= 3: pen.polygon(ring, fill=1) inside = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool) if not inside.any(): continue for key, value in values.items(): out[key][inside] = float(value) return out

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.body_text: """Optional enrichment layers from data outside OpenStreetMap. Each dataset is a module implementing DatasetSource: it says whether it can run here, downloads to a cache, builds a layer and applies it. A layer that cannot run is logged and skipped; a map is never lost to a dataset. OSM and hand-authored data always win. See docs/DATASETS.md. Heavy dependencies (rasterio, pyarrow) are imported inside the modules that need them, never here, so the package imports on a bare install. """ from __future__ import annotations import time from abc import ABC, abstractmethod from dataclasses import dataclass, field from pathlib import Path try: # the app's logger, so lines land in the log import knoxlog log = knoxlog.setup("knoxdata") except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a missing logger is not fatal import logging log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata") # The order layers apply in: terrain first, then what stands on it. ORDER = ("elevation_3dep", "worldcover", "natural_earth", "hifld_hospitals", "climate_normals") @dataclass _SOURCES: dict | None = None

nodes.name: DatasetSource
nodes.body_text: class DatasetSource(ABC): """One optional dataset. Subclasses gate themselves out when they cannot run.""" name: str = "" license: str = "" attribution: str = "" # the line a map carries when this applied setting: str = "" # Settings field that turns it on off_values: tuple = ("off", "", 0, None, False) def enabled(self, settings) -> bool: return getattr(settings, self.setting, None) not in self.off_values def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: """Is what this layer needs already on disk, so applying it costs no download? The pipeline calls run_layers(require_cache=True): a map is never slowed or failed by a dataset fetch.""" return True @abstractmethod def available(self, bbox) -> bool: """Can this layer run here (dependency present, bbox in coverage)?""" @abstractmethod def why_unavailable(self) -> str: """One sentence for the log when available() is false.""" @abstractmethod def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir, progress_cb=None): """Download to cache_dir and return a Path (or raise).""" @abstractmethod def build_layer(self, map_ctx): """Read the cache into a Layer.""" @abstractmethod def apply(self, map_ctx, layer) -> None: """Fold the layer into the map."""

nodes.name: run_layers
nodes.signature: def run_layers(settings, bbox, map_dir, map_name="", features=None, progress=None, ctx=None, require_cache=False)
nodes.body_text: def run_layers(settings, bbox, map_dir, map_name="", features=None, progress=None, ctx=None, require_cache=False): """Apply every enabled layer in ORDER; never raise for want of a dataset. Pass `ctx` to have the caller's MapContext filled in (region, labels, climate). With `require_cache` a layer is skipped unless its data is already on disk, so the build path never waits on a download; call refresh() first to populate the cache. Returns the report. """ if ctx is None: ctx = MapContext(bbox=tuple(bbox), settings=settings, map_dir=Path(map_dir), map_name=map_name, features=features if features is not None else []) elif features is not None: ctx.features = features used: list[str] = [] for name in ORDER: source = sources().get(name) if source is None or not source.enabled(settings): continue if not source.available(bbox): why = source.why_unavailable() log.info("knoxdata: %s skipped - %s", name, why) ctx.report[name] = {"used": False, "why": why} continue if require_cache and not source.cached(bbox): log.info("knoxdata: %s skipped - not cached; run refresh to fetch it", name) ctx.report[name] = {"used": False, "why": "not cached"} continue try: layer = source.build_layer(ctx) source.apply(ctx, layer) used.append(name) # Kept beside what apply() reported (WorldCover's class fractions). ctx.report[name] = {**ctx.report.get(name, {}), "used": True} except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - one layer never sinks a map log.warning("knoxdata: %s failed - %s: %s; continuing without it", name, type(exc).__name__, exc) ctx.report[name] = {"used": False, "why": str(exc)} ctx.report["used"] = used return ctx.report

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.body_text: def refresh(settings, bbox, progress=None) -> dict: """Download the enabled layers into the cache. The explicit fetch step: the generate path only ever reads what this put on disk.""" out = {} for name in ORDER: source = sources().get(name) if source is None or not source.enabled(settings): continue if not source.available(bbox): out[name] = {"fetched": False, "why": source.why_unavailable()} continue try: source.fetch(tuple(bbox), cache_dir=None, progress_cb=progress) out[name] = {"fetched": True} except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 log.info("knoxdata: %s refresh failed - %s", name, exc) out[name] = {"fetched": False, "why": str(exc)} return out

nodes.name: landcover_for
nodes.body_text: def landcover_for(settings, bbox): """A callable the renderer uses to lay WorldCover ground, or None. Only when the worldcover layer is on, in coverage, and already cached: the build path never downloads. """ source = sources().get("worldcover") if (source is None or not source.enabled(settings) or not source.available(bbox) or not source.cached(bbox)): return None box = tuple(bbox) def grid(width, height, bounds=None): # `bounds` is what the map image covers, which is padded to whole # cells past the bbox; without it the bbox is stretched over the image. return source.rasterise(tuple(bounds) if bounds else box, width, height) return grid

nodes.name: status
nodes.body_text: def status(settings=None, bbox=None) -> dict: """Which layers are on, and which cannot run here. For Setup and the UI.""" rows = {} for name in ORDER: source = sources().get(name) if source is None: continue on = bool(settings is None or source.enabled(settings)) # Coverage only means something for a real bbox; without one report # what can be known from this machine (a missing dependency). can = source.available(bbox) if bbox is not None else not _needs_missing_source(source) rows[name] = {"enabled": on, "available": can, "license": source.license, "why": "" if can else source.why_unavailable()} return rows

nodes.name: _needs_missing_source
nodes.body_text: def _needs_missing_source(source) -> bool: """True when the layer is blocked by a dependency this machine lacks.""" try: return "not installed" in source.why_unavailable() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return False

nodes.name: cache.py
nodes.body_text: """Two cache tiers, mirroring the OSM cache's lifetime rule. Dataset-wide files (a national hospitals list, a world tile) are shared by every map and expire on a TTL. Per-map products live beside the map and are reused on rebuild. Cache keys carry the dataset version so an update does not read yesterday's answer. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os import time from pathlib import Path BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent # Big shared downloads; never inside a map folder, never copied into a mod. DATASET_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_DATASET_CACHE") or (BASE_DIR / "cache" / "datasets")) # Politeness and safety: the same three tries the Overpass client makes, and a # ceiling so a wrong URL can never fill the disk. MAX_BYTES = int(os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES") or 2 * 1024 ** 3) ATTEMPTS = 3 # A ceiling on the whole dataset cache, not just on one file. The per-download # cap stops one wrong URL filling the disk; nothing stopped ten right ones - # a few national extracts, a world raster or two, and the cache was however big # the last month of maps made it. The oldest files go first. MAX_CACHE_BYTES = int(os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_CACHE_MAX_BYTES") or 8 * 1024 ** 3)

nodes.name: dataset_dir
nodes.body_text: def dataset_dir(*parts: str) -> Path: d = DATASET_DIR.joinpath(*parts) d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) return d

nodes.name: map_dir
nodes.body_text: def map_dir(map_folder) -> Path: """Per-map processed cache beside the map's other data.""" d = Path(map_folder) / ".knoxdata" d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) return d

nodes.name: total_bytes
nodes.body_text: def total_bytes(folder=None) -> int: """How much the dataset cache (or `folder`) holds.""" folder = Path(folder or DATASET_DIR) total = 0 if not folder.is_dir(): return 0 for p in folder.rglob("*"): try: if p.is_file(): total += p.stat().st_size except OSError: continue return total

nodes.name: prune
nodes.signature: def prune(keep_bytes: int | None = None, folder=None, keep=None) -> int
nodes.body_text: def prune(keep_bytes: int | None = None, folder=None, keep=None) -> int: """Delete the oldest cached files until the cache is under its ceiling. `keep` - the file just downloaded - is never one of them, so a download that takes the cache over the limit cannot delete what it just fetched. Returns how many files went. Best effort: a file somebody else has open is left alone and counted as still there. """ folder = Path(folder or DATASET_DIR) limit = MAX_CACHE_BYTES if keep_bytes is None else keep_bytes if not folder.is_dir(): return 0 held = Path(keep) if keep else None files = [] total = 0 for p in folder.rglob("*"): try: if not p.is_file(): continue size = p.stat().st_size total += size if p != held: files.append((p.stat().st_mtime, size, p)) except OSError: continue if total <= limit: return 0 files.sort() removed = 0 for _when, size, p in files: if total <= limit: break try: p.unlink() except OSError: continue total -= size removed += 1 return removed

nodes.name: age_days
nodes.body_text: def age_days(path) -> float: try: return (time.time() - Path(path).stat().st_mtime) / 86400.0 except OSError: return float("inf")

nodes.name: fresh
nodes.body_text: def fresh(path, ttl_days: float) -> bool: """True when `path` exists and is younger than `ttl_days`.""" return Path(path).exists() and age_days(path) < ttl_days

nodes.name: stamp
nodes.body_text: def stamp() -> str: return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

nodes.name: write_json
nodes.body_text: def write_json(path, payload) -> None: path = Path(path) path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".part") with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh: json.dump(payload, fh, ensure_ascii=False) os.replace(tmp, path)

nodes.name: read_json
nodes.body_text: def read_json(path): try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh: return json.load(fh) except (OSError, ValueError): return None

nodes.name: download
nodes.signature: def download(url: str, path, progress_cb=None, chunk: int = 1 << 20, timeout: int = 120, attempts: int = ATTEMPTS, max_bytes: int = MAX_BYTES) -> Path
nodes.body_text: def download(url: str, path, progress_cb=None, chunk: int = 1 << 20, timeout: int = 120, attempts: int = ATTEMPTS, max_bytes: int = MAX_BYTES) -> Path: """Stream `url` to `path` atomically, retrying with backoff. Raises on the last failure; the caller logs and skips. Retries match the Overpass client's politeness (three), and a size cap means a wrong URL cannot fill the disk. """ import urllib.request path = Path(path) path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) part = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".part") req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "KnoxMap/knoxdata"}) last: Exception | None = None for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1): try: done = 0 with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp: total = int(resp.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0) if total and total > max_bytes: raise ValueError(f"{url} is {total} bytes, over the " f"{max_bytes}-byte cap") with open(part, "wb") as out: while True: block = resp.read(chunk) if not block: break done += len(block) if done > max_bytes: raise ValueError(f"download of {url} passed the " f"{max_bytes}-byte cap") out.write(block) if progress_cb is not None: progress_cb(done, total) os.replace(part, path) # The cache has a ceiling of its own (MAX_CACHE_BYTES): this # download may be the one that took it over, and the file it just # wrote is the one that must survive. gone = prune(keep=path) if gone: import knoxlog knoxlog.log.info("cache: removed %d older downloads; the cache is " "capped at %d bytes", gone, MAX_CACHE_BYTES) return path except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - retried, then caller skips last = exc try: if part.exists(): part.unlink() except OSError: pass if attempt < attempts: time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, 30)) raise last if last is not None else RuntimeError(f"could not download {url}")

nodes.name: climate_normals.py
nodes.body_text: """NOAA U.S. Climate Normals: region-correct flavour (US only). The tabular 1991-2020 collection is a GeoParquet of ~15k stations; the nearest station (with inverse-distance weighting over the nearest three) gives a compact profile. Needs pyarrow; without it the map keeps its default look and one line says so. """ from __future__ import annotations import logging import math import os from . import DatasetSource, Layer from . import cache log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata.climate_normals") BASE = os.environ.get( "KNOXMAP_NOAA_URL", "https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/oceans/archive/arc0216/0253808/2.2/data" "/0-data/parquet/normals-monthly-1991-2020.parquet") VERSION = "1991-2020" TTL_DAYS = 3650

nodes.name: _pyarrow
nodes.body_text: def _pyarrow(): try: import pyarrow.parquet # noqa: F401 return True except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return False

nodes.name: in_coverage
nodes.body_text: def in_coverage(bbox) -> bool: s, w, n, e = bbox return w <= -65 and e >= -180 and s <= 72 and n >= 17

nodes.name: _haversine_m
nodes.body_text: def _haversine_m(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) -> float: r = 6371000.0 p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2) dp = math.radians(lat2 - lat1) dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1) a = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2 return 2 * r * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

nodes.name: classify
nodes.signature: def classify(precip_mm: float, jan_c: float) -> str
nodes.body_text: def classify(precip_mm: float, jan_c: float) -> str: if precip_mm < 400: return "arid" if jan_c < -3: return "cold continental" if precip_mm > 1000: return "humid" return "temperate"

"climate_flavor" off_values = ("off", "", 0, None, False) def available(self, bbox) -> bool: return _pyarrow() and in_coverage(bbox) def why_unavailable(self) -> str: if not _pyarrow(): return "pyarrow is not installed (pip install pyarrow)" return "NOAA normals cover the United States only; default look kept." def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: return self._file().exists() def _file(self): return cache.DATASET_DIR / "noaa" / f"normals-monthly-{VERSION}.parquet" def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None): path = self._file() if not cache.fresh(path, TTL_DAYS): cache.download(BASE, path, progress_cb=progress_cb) return path def build_layer(self, ctx) -> Layer: import pyarrow.parquet as pq path = self.fetch(ctx.bbox) table = pq.read_table(path) rows = table.to_pylist() s, w, n, e = ctx.bbox lat, lon = (s + n) / 2.0, (w + e) / 2.0 def coord(row, *keys): for key in keys: if row.get(key) is not None: try: return float(row[key]) except (TypeError, ValueError): continue return None by_station: dict[tuple[float, float], dict] = {} for row in rows: la = coord(row, "LATITUDE", "latitude", "lat") lo = coord(row, "LONGITUDE", "longitude", "lon") if la is None or lo is None: continue key = (round(la, 5), round(lo, 5)) st = by_station.get(key) if st is None: st = dict(row) st["_precip_sum"] = 0.0 st["_has_months"] = False by_station[key] = st month = coord(row, "month", "MONTH") if month is not None: st["_has_months"] = True m = int(round(month)) tavg = coord(row, "MLY-TAVG-NORMAL", "tavg", "TAVG") if m == 1 and tavg is not None and st.get("JAN_MEAN_TMP") is None: st["JAN_MEAN_TMP"] = tavg elif m == 7 and tavg is not None and st.get("JUL_MEAN_TMP") is None: st["JUL_MEAN_TMP"] = tavg prcp = coord(row, "MLY-PRCP-NORMAL", "precip", "PRCP") if prcp is not None: st["_precip_sum"] += prcp ranked = [] for (la, lo), st in by_station.items(): if st.get("_has_months") and st["_precip_sum"] > 0: st["MLY-PRCP-NORMAL"] = st["_precip_sum"] ranked.append((_haversine_m(lat, lon, la, lo), st)) ranked.sort(key=lambda t: t[0]) nearest = ranked[:3] if not nearest: return Layer(profile=None) weights = [1.0 / max(d, 1.0) for d, _ in nearest] total = sum(weights) def avg(*keys): value = 0.0 for weight, (_d, row) in zip(weights, nearest): value += weight * float(coord(row, *keys) or 0.0) return value / total jan = avg("JAN_MEAN_TMP", "jan_mean_tmp", "MLY-TAVG-NORMAL") jul = avg("JUL_MEAN_TMP", "jul_mean_tmp", "MLY-TAVG-NORMAL") precip = avg("MLY-PRCP-NORMAL", "precip", "PRCP") profile = {"jan_c": round(jan, 1), "jul_c": round(jul, 1), "precip_mm": round(precip, 0), "class": classify(precip, jan), "version": VERSION} return Layer(profile=profile) def apply(self, ctx, layer) -> None: profile = layer.data.get("profile") if profile: ctx.climate = profile ctx.report.setdefault("climate_normals", {})["profile"] = profile

nodes.name: elevation_3dep.py
nodes.body_text: """USGS 3DEP elevation (US only): gentle real relief within the z budget. Default path is the 10 m (1/3 arc-second) DEM; raw lidar point clouds are an advanced mode this module does not attempt. The layer reports why when rasterio is absent or the area is outside 3DEP coverage, and the map is built flat as before. Grading is left to the pipeline: this supplies metres per tile. """ from __future__ import annotations import logging import os from . import DatasetSource, Layer from . import cache log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata.elevation_3dep") # The National Map staged-product layout; overridable because it moves. BASE = os.environ.get( "KNOXMAP_3DEP_URL", "https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/13/TIFF/current") TTL_DAYS = 3650

nodes.name: _rasterio
nodes.body_text: def _rasterio(): try: import rasterio # noqa: F401 return True except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return False

nodes.name: in_coverage
nodes.body_text: def in_coverage(bbox) -> bool: """CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands.""" s, w, n, e = bbox conus = (w <= -66 and e >= -125 and s <= 50 and n >= 24) alaska = (w <= -129 and e >= -170 and s <= 72 and n >= 51) islands = (w <= -64 and e >= -161 and s <= 23 and n >= 17) return conus or alaska or islands

nodes.name: _cell
nodes.body_text: def _cell(lat: float, lon: float) -> str: import math lat_nw = int(math.ceil(lat)) lon_nw = int(math.floor(lon)) ns = ("n" if lat_nw >= 0 else "s") + str(abs(lat_nw)).zfill(2) ew = ("w" if lon_nw < 0 else "e") + str(abs(lon_nw)).zfill(3) return ns + ew

nodes.name: tile_name
nodes.signature: def tile_name(lat: float, lon: float) -> str
nodes.body_text: def tile_name(lat: float, lon: float) -> str: return f"USGS_13_{_cell(lat, lon)}.tif"

nodes.name: Elevation3DEP
nodes.body_text: class Elevation3DEP(DatasetSource): name = "elevation_3dep" license = "USGS 3DEP (public domain)" attribution = "USGS 3DEP elevation (public domain)" setting = "elevation" off_values = ("flat", "off", "", None, False) def available(self, bbox) -> bool: return _rasterio() and in_coverage(bbox) def why_unavailable(self) -> str: if not _rasterio(): return "rasterio is not installed (pip install rasterio)" return "the area is outside USGS 3DEP coverage; terrain stays flat." def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: s, w, n, e = bbox return (cache.DATASET_DIR / "3dep" / tile_name((s + n) / 2.0, (w + e) / 2.0)).exists() def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None): root = cache.DATASET_DIR / "3dep" s, w, n, e = bbox lat = (s + n) / 2.0 lon = (w + e) / 2.0 name = tile_name(lat, lon) path = root / name if not cache.fresh(path, TTL_DAYS): folder = _cell(lat, lon) cache.download(f"{BASE}/{folder}/{name}", path, progress_cb=progress_cb) return path def build_layer(self, ctx) -> Layer: """One elevation sample per map tile, normalised and clamped.""" import numpy as np import rasterio from rasterio.windows import from_bounds path = self.fetch(ctx.bbox) proj = getattr(ctx, "proj", None) width = getattr(proj, "width", 256) height = getattr(proj, "height", 256) s, w, n, e = ctx.bbox with rasterio.open(path) as src: data = src.read(1, window=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, src.transform), out_shape=(height, width), resampling=rasterio.enums.Resampling.average) metres = np.asarray(data, dtype="float32") finite = metres[np.isfinite(metres)] if finite.size == 0: return Layer(metres=None) lo, hi = float(finite.min()), float(finite.max()) max_relief = int(getattr(ctx.settings, "max_relief", 4) or 4) if hi - lo > 0: metres = (metres - lo) / (hi - lo) * max_relief return Layer(metres=metres, span=(lo, hi)) def apply(self, ctx, layer) -> None: ctx.elevation = layer.data.get("metres") ctx.report.setdefault("elevation_3dep", {})["span_m"] = layer.data.get("span")

nodes.name: hifld_hospitals.py
nodes.body_text: """HIFLD hospitals: make generated hospitals match the real facilities (US). The national file is small and updated weekly, so it is one dataset-wide download on a 7-day TTL, indexed once per process. Matching prefers a name match, then the nearest tagged hospital, then the nearest candidate building; only the best tier is applied. See docs/DATASETS.md. """ from __future__ import annotations import logging import math import os import re from . import DatasetSource, Layer from . import cache log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata.hifld") # HIFLD publishes on ArcGIS Hub; the layer id can move, so this is overridable. DEFAULT_URL = os.environ.get( "KNOXMAP_HIFLD_URL", "https://services1.arcgis.com/Hp6G80Pky0om7QvQ/arcgis/rest/services/" "Hospitals/FeatureServer/0/query" "?where=1%3D1&outFields=NAME,ADDRESS,CITY,STATE,TYPE,STATUS,BEDS," "TTL_STAFF,HELIPAD,OWNER,LATITUDE,LONGITUDE&f=geojson&outSR=4326") TTL_DAYS = 7 MATCH_M = 150.0 _VERSION = "hifld-2024"

nodes.name: _norm
nodes.body_text: def _norm(text: str) -> str: return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]+", " ", str(text or "").lower()).strip()

nodes.name: _tokens
nodes.body_text: def _tokens(text: str) -> set[str]: ignored = {"hospital", "medical", "center", "centre", "health", "the", "of"} return {w for w in _norm(text).split() if w and w not in ignored}

nodes.name: name_score
nodes.signature: def name_score(a: str, b: str) -> float
nodes.body_text: def name_score(a: str, b: str) -> float: """Jaccard overlap of the words that matter, 0..1.""" ta, tb = _tokens(a), _tokens(b) if not ta or not tb: return 0.0 return len(ta & tb) / len(ta | tb)

nodes.name: _haversine_m
nodes.body_text: def _haversine_m(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) -> float: r = 6371000.0 p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2) dp = math.radians(lat2 - lat1) dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1) a = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2 return 2 * r * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

nodes.name: _centroid
nodes.body_text: def _centroid(feature): """(lat, lon) centre of an OSM way's ring, or None.""" ring = getattr(feature, "geometry", None) or [] if not isinstance(ring, list) or len(ring) < 3: return None lat = sum(float(p[0]) for p in ring) / len(ring) lon = sum(float(p[1]) for p in ring) / len(ring) return lat, lon

nodes.name: _passes
nodes.body_text: def _passes(feature) -> bool: tags = getattr(feature, "tags", None) or {} return (tags.get("amenity") == "hospital" or tags.get("healthcare") == "hospital" or tags.get("building") == "hospital")

nodes.name: _key
nodes.body_text: def _key(prop, *names): for name in names: if name in prop and prop[name] not in (None, ""): return prop[name] return None

nodes.name: HIFLDHospitals
nodes.body_text: class HIFLDHospitals(DatasetSource): name = "hifld_hospitals" license = "US Government Open Data (public domain)" attribution = "HIFLD Hospitals (US Government, public domain)" setting = "hospitals" off_values = ("off", "", "osm", None, False) def _file(self): return cache.DATASET_DIR / "hifld" / "hospitals.geojson" def available(self, bbox) -> bool: # US coverage only: CONUS, AK/HI/PR/VI are all in -180..-65, 17..72. s, w, n, e = bbox in_us = (w <= -65 and e >= -180 and s <= 72 and n >= 17) return in_us and (self._file().exists() or self._can_reach()) @staticmethod def _can_reach() -> bool: return True # fetch() degrades on its own; this only gates coverage def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: return self._file().exists() def why_unavailable(self) -> str: return "HIFLD covers the United States only, and the hospitals list is not cached." def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None): path = self._file() if cache.fresh(path, TTL_DAYS): return path cache.download(DEFAULT_URL, path, progress_cb=progress_cb) return path def _rows(self): payload = cache.read_json(self._file()) if payload is None: try: self.fetch(None) except Exception as exc: # nodes.name: natural_earth.py
nodes.body_text: """Natural Earth 1:110m context: country, coastline fallback, place labels. Public domain (CC0), so the small themes ship cached on demand. This is the one layer that needs no dependency beyond shapely, so it is the reference implementation of the DatasetSource contract. OSM is the source of truth wherever it has the feature; this only fills gaps: a country/region for regional defaults, a coastline where Overpass truncated it at the bbox edge, and names for the paper map where OSM has no place tag. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import logging from . import DatasetSource, Layer from . import cache log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata.natural_earth") BASE = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/martynafford/" "natural-earth-geojson/master") VERSION = "110m-2024" TTL_DAYS = 30 # theme -> path under BASE. Only what a map actually reads. THEMES = { "countries": "110m/cultural/ne_110m_admin_0_countries.json", "places": "110m/cultural/ne_110m_populated_places.json", "coastline": "110m/physical/ne_110m_coastline.json", } # Parsed geometry, kept for the process's life: a rebuild is one load. _LOADED: dict = {}

nodes.name: _url
nodes.body_text: def _url(theme: str) -> str: return f"{BASE}/{THEMES[theme]}"

nodes.name: _file
nodes.body_text: def _file(theme: str): return cache.DATASET_DIR / "natural_earth" / f"ne_{VERSION.split('-')[0]}_{theme}.json"

nodes.name: _load
nodes.body_text: def _load(theme: str): """The theme's GeoJSON, from cache or download, parsed once per process.""" if theme in _LOADED: return _LOADED[theme] path = _file(theme) if not cache.fresh(path, TTL_DAYS): try: cache.download(_url(theme), path) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - caller degrades log.info("knoxdata: Natural Earth %s unavailable - %s", theme, exc) if not path.exists(): return None payload = cache.read_json(path) _LOADED[theme] = payload return payload

nodes.name: _geoms
nodes.body_text: def _geoms(theme: str): """[(shapely geometry, properties)] for a theme, or [].""" from shapely.geometry import shape payload = _load(theme) out = [] for feat in (payload or {}).get("features", []): try: geom = shape(feat["geometry"]) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a broken feature is skipped continue if not geom.is_empty: out.append((geom, feat.get("properties") or {})) return out

nodes.name: country_at
nodes.signature: def country_at(lat: float, lon: float) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def country_at(lat: float, lon: float) -> dict | None: """The country containing a point, as {iso, name}, or None.""" from shapely.geometry import Point here = Point(lon, lat) for geom, props in _geoms("countries"): if geom.contains(here): iso = props.get("ISO_A2") or props.get("WB_A2") or "" return {"iso": str(iso).upper() if iso else "", "name": str(props.get("NAME") or props.get("ADMIN") or "")} return None

nodes.name: places_in
nodes.body_text: def places_in(bbox, limit: int = 200) -> list[dict]: """Populated places inside the box, biggest first.""" from shapely.geometry import Point, box s, w, n, e = bbox area = box(w, s, e, n) found = [] for geom, props in _geoms("places"): if not isinstance(geom, Point) or geom.is_empty: continue if area.contains(geom): found.append({"name": str(props.get("NAME") or ""), "lat": float(props.get("LATITUDE") or geom.y), "lon": float(props.get("LONGITUDE") or geom.x), "pop": int(props.get("POP_MAX") or 0)}) found.sort(key=lambda p: -p["pop"]) return [p for p in found if p["name"]][:limit]

nodes.name: coastline_in
nodes.body_text: def coastline_in(bbox) -> list: """Coastline clipped to the box, as shapely geometries.""" from shapely.geometry import box s, w, n, e = bbox clip = box(w, s, e, n) out = [] for geom, _props in _geoms("coastline"): try: piece = geom.intersection(clip) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 continue if not piece.is_empty: out.append(piece) return out

nodes.body_text: class NaturalEarth(DatasetSource): name = "natural_earth" license = "CC0 1.0 (public domain)" attribution = "Natural Earth (public domain)" setting = "ne_context" off_values = ("off", "", 0, None, False) def available(self, bbox) -> bool: return True # bounded, public, cached; download failures degrade def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: return all(_file(theme).exists() for theme in THEMES) def why_unavailable(self) -> str: return "Natural Earth themes could not be read." def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None): for theme in THEMES: _load(theme) return cache.DATASET_DIR / "natural_earth" def build_layer(self, ctx) -> Layer: s, w, n, e = ctx.bbox center = ((s + n) / 2.0, (w + e) / 2.0) return Layer(country=country_at(*center), places=places_in(ctx.bbox), coastline=coastline_in(ctx.bbox)) def apply(self, ctx, layer) -> None: country = layer.data.get("country") if layer.data else None if country and country.get("iso"): ctx.region = country["iso"] ctx.report.setdefault("natural_earth", {})["country"] = country places = layer.data.get("places") or [] # Labels only where OSM left a name blank; the caller decides that. for i, place in enumerate(places): ctx.labels[f"ne-place-{i}"] = place coast = layer.data.get("coastline") or [] ctx.report.setdefault("natural_earth", {})["coastline_km"] = round( sum(getattr(g, "length", 0.0) for g in coast) * 111.0, 1)

nodes.name: worldcover.py
nodes.body_text: """ESA WorldCover 10 m land cover, for ground OSM leaves blank. OSM polygons always win; this only fills tiles nothing else claimed. The class -> behaviour table is data (data/worldcover_classes.json), not code. Needs rasterio + numpy; without them the layer reports why and is skipped. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import logging import math import os from pathlib import Path from . import DatasetSource, Layer from . import cache log = logging.getLogger("knoxdata.worldcover") TILE_DEG = 3 VERSION = "2021_v200" BASE = os.environ.get( "KNOXMAP_WORLDCOVER_URL", "https://esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/v200/2021/map") TTL_DAYS = 3650 # a published year does not change _DATA = Path(__file__).with_name("data") / "worldcover_classes.json"

nodes.name: classes
nodes.body_text: def classes() -> dict: with open(_DATA, encoding="utf-8") as fh: return json.load(fh)

nodes.name: _corner
nodes.body_text: def _corner(deg: float) -> str: deg = int(math.floor(deg / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG) return (f"N{deg:02d}" if deg >= 0 else f"S{-deg:02d}")

nodes.name: _lon
nodes.body_text: def _lon(deg: float) -> str: deg = int(math.floor(deg / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG) return (f"E{deg:03d}" if deg >= 0 else f"W{-deg:03d}")

nodes.name: tile_names
nodes.body_text: def tile_names(bbox) -> list[str]: """The 3-degree WorldCover tiles a box touches, by their SW corner.""" s, w, n, e = bbox names = [] lat = math.floor(s / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG while lat <= math.floor(n / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG: lon = math.floor(w / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG while lon <= math.floor(e / TILE_DEG) * TILE_DEG: names.append(f"ESA_WorldCover_10m_{VERSION}_{_corner(lat)}{_lon(lon)}_Map.tif") lon += TILE_DEG lat += TILE_DEG return names

nodes.name: _rasterio
nodes.body_text: def _rasterio(): try: import rasterio # noqa: F401 return True except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 return False

nodes.name: _majority3
nodes.body_text: def _majority3(grid): """3x3 majority filter, to take the speckle out of a resampled 10 m grid.""" import numpy as np if grid.size > 4_000_000: # ponytail: O(classes * pixels) is minutes on a 100 km map; skip the # filter there. Add a windowed/GPU pass if big maps need it. return grid padded = np.pad(grid, 1, mode="edge") windows = np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(padded, (3, 3)) codes = np.unique(grid) counts = np.stack([(windows == code).sum(axis=(-1, -2)) for code in codes]) return codes[np.argmax(counts, axis=0)].astype(grid.dtype)

nodes.name: suggest_preset
nodes.body_text: def suggest_preset(fractions: dict) -> str: """Rural/Town/Suburb/City from how much of the area is built up.""" built = float(fractions.get("Built-up", 0.0) or 0.0) if built > 0.35: return "city" if built > 0.18: return "suburb" if built > 0.07: return "town" return "rural"

nodes.name: WorldCover
nodes.body_text: class WorldCover(DatasetSource): name = "worldcover" license = "CC-BY 4.0" attribution = "Contains modified Copernicus/ESA WorldCover data 2021" setting = "landcover" # "OpenStreetMap only" is off too: the ground OSM leaves blank stays grass # with KnoxMap's own scattered woods, as before WorldCover. off_values = ("off", "", "osm", None, False) def available(self, bbox) -> bool: s, w, n, e = bbox return (_rasterio() and -90 <= s < n <= 90 and -180 <= w < e <= 180) def why_unavailable(self) -> str: if not _rasterio(): return "rasterio is not installed (pip install rasterio)" return "the area is outside WorldCover coverage." def cached(self, bbox) -> bool: root = cache.DATASET_DIR / "worldcover" / VERSION return all((root / name).exists() for name in tile_names(bbox)) def rasterise(self, bbox, width: int, height: int): """WorldCover class at one sample per map tile. Read at WorldCover's own 10 m, 3x3-majority filtered there to take the speckle out, then sampled per tile: filtered after the stretch to map tiles, a 10 m pixel is ten tiles across and the filter changed nothing. Only tiles already on disk are read - this is the build path, and the generate step fetched what it needs.""" import numpy as np import rasterio from rasterio.enums import Resampling from rasterio.windows import from_bounds root = self.tile_dir() s, w, n, e = bbox native = None for name in tile_names(bbox): path = root / name if not path.exists(): continue with rasterio.open(path) as src: if native is None: rx, ry = abs(src.transform.a), abs(src.transform.e) native = np.zeros((max(1, round((n - s) / ry)), max(1, round((e - w) / rx))), dtype="uint8") data = src.read(1, window=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, src.transform), out_shape=native.shape, resampling=Resampling.nearest, boundless=True, fill_value=0) native[data > 0] = data[data > 0] # OSM still paints over this if native is None: return np.zeros((height, width), dtype="uint8") native = _majority3(native) rows = np.minimum((np.arange(height) + 0.5) * native.shape[0] / height, native.shape[0] - 1).astype(np.int64) cols = np.minimum((np.arange(width) + 0.5) * native.shape[1] / width, native.shape[1] - 1).astype(np.int64) return native[rows[:, None], cols[None, :]] def tile_dir(self): """Where the downloaded tiles are kept.""" return cache.DATASET_DIR / "worldcover" / VERSION def fetch(self, bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None): root = self.tile_dir() for name in tile_names(bbox): path = root / name if not cache.fresh(path, TTL_DAYS): cache.download(f"{BASE}/{name}", path, progress_cb=progress_cb) return root def build_layer(self, ctx) -> Layer: """Fraction of the AOI in each class, for the preset suggestion.""" import numpy as np import rasterio from rasterio.windows import from_bounds root = self.fetch(ctx.bbox) table = classes() counts: dict[int, int] = {} for name in tile_names(ctx.bbox): with rasterio.open(root / name) as src: s, w, n, e = ctx.bbox window = from_bounds(w, s, e, n, src.transform) data = src.read(1, window=window) values, nvs = np.unique(data, return_counts=True) for value, count in zip(values.tolist(), nvs.tolist()): counts[int(value)] = counts.get(int(value), 0) + int(count) total = sum(counts.values()) or 1 fractions = {table[str(k)]["name"]: round(v / total, 4) for k, v in counts.items() if str(k) in table} return Layer(fractions=fractions, counts=counts, table=table) def apply(self, ctx, layer) -> None: ctx.report.setdefault("worldcover", {})["fractions"] = layer.data.get("fractions", {})

Only tiles already on disk are read - this is the build path, and the generate step fetched what it needs.""" import numpy as np import rasterio from rasterio.enums import Resampling from rasterio.windows import from_bounds root = self.tile_dir() s, w, n, e = bbox native = None for name in tile_names(bbox): path = root / name if not path.exists(): continue with rasterio.open(path) as src: if native is None: rx, ry = abs(src.transform.a), abs(src.transform.e) native = np.zeros((max(1, round((n - s) / ry)), max(1, round((e - w) / rx))), dtype="uint8") data = src.read(1, window=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, src.transform), out_shape=native.shape, resampling=Resampling.nearest, boundless=True, fill_value=0) native[data > 0] = data[data > 0] # OSM still paints over this if native is None: return np.zeros((height, width), dtype="uint8") native = _majority3(native) rows = np.minimum((np.arange(height) + 0.5) * native.shape[0] / height, native.shape[0] - 1).astype(np.int64) cols = np.minimum((np.arange(width) + 0.5) * native.shape[1] / width, native.shape[1] - 1).astype(np.int64) return native[rows[:, None], cols[None, :]]

nodes.name: knoxfiles.py
nodes.body_text: """The map's own files, written whole and read with a straight answer. A map folder holds the ground as bitmaps and a dozen small JSON files beside them - its buildings, its land use, its fences, what it is and how big. Each was written straight to its own name, so a generate that was stopped, crashed or had the window closed on it left one of them half written, and the next Build died on the half: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 32790 (char 32789) Nobody can act on that. Each file is now written beside itself and moved into place, which is one step on every system this runs on: what is on disk is either the file from before or the new one, never half of either. And reading one says which file it is, what it holds and what to do about it. """ from __future__ import annotations import json import os

nodes.body_text: class Damaged(ValueError): """A map file that is there but cannot be read."""

nodes.name: _forget
nodes.body_text: def _forget(part: str) -> None: """Take away what was half written, so the folder is left as it was.""" try: os.remove(part) except OSError: pass

nodes.name: write
nodes.body_text: def write(path: str, payload, **dump) -> None: """Write `payload` to `path` as JSON: all of it, or none of it.""" part = f"{path}.part" try: with open(part, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(payload, f, **dump) os.replace(part, path) except BaseException: _forget(part) raise

nodes.name: save
nodes.body_text: def save(image, path: str, **options) -> None: """The same for a bitmap: a map's ground is the biggest file it writes.""" part = f"{path}.part" try: image.save(part, **options) os.replace(part, path) except BaseException: _forget(part) raise

nodes.name: write_text
nodes.signature: def write_text(path: str, text: str) -> None
nodes.body_text: def write_text(path: str, text: str) -> None: """The same for a file of text the map carries. Where a map stands in the world is written into the project, the paper map, the street lines and the labels, all four rewritten in place when a map is moved. Half of any one of them is a map the game will not open. """ part = f"{path}.part" try: with open(part, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f: f.write(text) os.replace(part, path) except BaseException: _forget(part) raise

nodes.name: read
nodes.signature: def read(path: str, what: str, default=None)
nodes.body_text: def read(path: str, what: str, default=None): """What is in this file. `default` when there is no such file at all. A file that is there and will not read is not a file that is missing - something went wrong while it was written - so this says so instead of quietly building a town with no fences in it. """ try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f) except FileNotFoundError: return default except (OSError, ValueError) as exc: raise Damaged( f"{os.path.basename(path)} ({what}) cannot be read: {exc}. " f"That happens when making the map was interrupted and the file " f"was left half written. Generate the map again to write it " f"afresh - the OpenStreetMap download beside it is kept, so it " f"starts from what is already on disk." ) from exc

nodes.name: knoxlog.py
nodes.body_text: """KnoxMap's logs: one folder, everything that goes wrong, and a report to send. Before this, a failure left at most one line in the window - "Generation failed" or "<!doctype ... is not valid JSON" - and nothing on disk, so a bug report on the Discord was a screenshot of a message that said nothing. Now: * logs/knoxmap.log records every run: a header describing the PC (Windows version and code page, Python, memory, disk, where the game and the map tools are), each step of generating, building, compiling and installing, and the full traceback of every error, whether it happened in a request, a background compile, the page itself or at start-up. It rolls over at 2 MB, keeping five. * Each error gets a short id (E-7F3A2C) that is shown in the app next to the message and written beside the traceback, so "I got E-7F3A2C" finds it. * WorldEd's own output from every compile batch is kept in logs/worlded/. * Setup writes logs/setup.log. * report_zip() bundles all of it with a system summary into one zip for #bug-reports, with the user's name taken out of every path. """ from __future__ import annotations import io import json import logging import logging.handlers import os import platform import re import secrets import sys import threading import time import traceback import zipfile from pathlib import Path BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent # KNOXMAP_LOG_DIR moves them, so the self-test does not write into a real log. LOG_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_LOG_DIR") or BASE_DIR / "logs") MAIN_LOG = LOG_DIR / "knoxmap.log" WORLDED_DIR = LOG_DIR / "worlded" KEEP_WORLDED_LOGS = 40 MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024 BACKUPS = 5 log = logging.getLogger("knoxmap") _ready = threading.Lock() _configured: list[str] = [] # --- the PC this is running on --------------------------------------------- # --- WorldEd's output -------------------------------------------------------- # Windows reports a crashed program by the exception that killed it. _EXIT_CODES = { 0: "finished", -1073741819: "crashed: access violation (0xC0000005)", 3221225477: "crashed: access violation (0xC0000005)", -1073741571: "crashed: stack overflow (0xC00000FD)", 3221225725: "crashed: stack overflow (0xC00000FD)", -1073740791: "crashed: internal error (0xC0000409)", 3221226505: "crashed: internal error (0xC0000409)", -1073741515: "could not start: a DLL is missing (0xC0000135)", 3221225781: "could not start: a DLL is missing (0xC0000135)", -1073741510: "closed from outside (0xC000013A)", 3221225786: "closed from outside (0xC000013A)", -1073741801: "ran out of memory (0xC0000017)", 3221225495: "ran out of memory (0xC0000017)", 65: "stalled or timed out", 124: "hung and was stopped", } # --- the report --------------------------------------------------------------

nodes.name: setup
nodes.signature: def setup(program: str = "app", console: bool = False) -> logging.Logger
nodes.body_text: def setup(program: str = "app", console: bool = False) -> logging.Logger: """Send KnoxMap's logging to logs/knoxmap.log (once per process) and write the header for this run.""" with _ready: if _configured: return log _configured.append(program) try: LOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True) handler: logging.Handler = logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler( MAIN_LOG, maxBytes=MAX_BYTES, backupCount=BACKUPS, encoding="utf-8", delay=True) except OSError: # A read-only folder (a zip opened in place): log nowhere rather # than not start. handler = logging.NullHandler() fmt = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)-7s [%(threadName)s] %(message)s", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") handler.setFormatter(fmt) log.addHandler(handler) if console: stream = logging.StreamHandler() stream.setFormatter(fmt) log.addHandler(stream) log.setLevel(logging.INFO) log.propagate = False _install_hooks() log.info("=" * 70) log.info("KnoxMap %s started (%s)", version(), program) for line in system_summary().splitlines(): log.info(" %s", line) return log

nodes.name: _install_hooks
nodes.body_text: def _install_hooks() -> None: """Uncaught errors anywhere - the main thread, a compile thread - go to the log as well as wherever they went before.""" previous = sys.excepthook def on_error(kind, value, tb): log.critical("Uncaught error\n%s", "".join(traceback.format_exception(kind, value, tb))) previous(kind, value, tb) sys.excepthook = on_error previous_thread = threading.excepthook def on_thread_error(args): if args.exc_type is not SystemExit: log.critical("Uncaught error in thread %s\n%s", getattr(args.thread, "name", "?"), "".join(traceback.format_exception(args.exc_type, args.exc_value, args.exc_traceback))) previous_thread(args) threading.excepthook = on_thread_error

nodes.name: on_error
nodes.body_text: def on_error(kind, value, tb): log.critical("Uncaught error\n%s", "".join(traceback.format_exception(kind, value, tb))) previous(kind, value, tb)

nodes.name: on_thread_error
nodes.body_text: def on_thread_error(args): if args.exc_type is not SystemExit: log.critical("Uncaught error in thread %s\n%s", getattr(args.thread, "name", "?"), "".join(traceback.format_exception(args.exc_type, args.exc_value, args.exc_traceback))) previous_thread(args)

nodes.name: error_id
nodes.body_text: def error_id() -> str: return "E-" + secrets.token_hex(3).upper()

nodes.name: record
nodes.signature: def record(exc: BaseException | None = None, where: str = "", **context) -> str
nodes.body_text: def record(exc: BaseException | None = None, where: str = "", **context) -> str: """Log an error with its traceback and context. Returns the id to show.""" eid = error_id() detail = "" if exc is not None: detail = "".join(traceback.format_exception(type(exc), exc, exc.__traceback__)) extra = " ".join(f"{k}={_short(v)}" for k, v in context.items() if v not in (None, "")) log.error("%s %s %s\n%s", eid, where, extra, detail) return eid

nodes.name: _short
nodes.body_text: def _short(value, limit: int = 300) -> str: text = value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value, default=str, ensure_ascii=False) return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit] + "..."

nodes.name: version
nodes.body_text: def version() -> str: try: for line in (BASE_DIR / "CHANGELOG.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(): # "1.3.9", and also "1.3.9 mc1" - a release for one system only, # which carries the platform and its number after the version. m = re.match(r"##\s+(\d[\w.]*(?:\s+[a-z]+\d*)?)", line) if m: return m.group(1) except OSError: pass return "unknown"

nodes.name: memory_status
nodes.signature: def memory_status() -> tuple[int, int, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def memory_status() -> tuple[int, int, int] | None: """(total, free, room this process has left) in bytes, or None elsewhere. The last one is the address space: on a 32-bit Python it is about 2 GB however much memory the PC has, which is what a big map runs out of. """ if os.name != "nt": return _memory_status_posix() try: import ctypes class Status(ctypes.Structure): _fields_ = [("length", ctypes.c_ulong), ("load", ctypes.c_ulong), ("total", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("avail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("pagetotal", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("pageavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("virttotal", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("virtavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("extavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong)] st = Status() st.length = ctypes.sizeof(Status) if ctypes.windll.kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx(ctypes.byref(st)): return int(st.total), int(st.avail), int(st.virtavail) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - not Windows pass return None

nodes.name: Status
nodes.body_text: class Status(ctypes.Structure): _fields_ = [("length", ctypes.c_ulong), ("load", ctypes.c_ulong), ("total", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("avail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("pagetotal", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("pageavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("virttotal", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("virtavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("extavail", ctypes.c_ulonglong)]

nodes.name: _memory_status_posix
nodes.body_text: def _memory_status_posix() -> tuple[int, int, int] | None: """The same three numbers from /proc/meminfo, on Linux.""" try: values = {} with open("/proc/meminfo", encoding="utf-8") as f: for line in f: key, _, rest = line.partition(":") values[key] = int(rest.split()[0]) * 1024 total = values.get("MemTotal", 0) free = values.get("MemAvailable", values.get("MemFree", 0)) if total: # 64-bit address space is effectively unlimited here; a 32-bit # build is capped, which is what the room figure is for. room = free if sys.maxsize > 2 ** 32 else min(free, 2 ** 31) return total, free, room except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError): pass return None

nodes.name: _memory
nodes.body_text: def _memory() -> str: status = memory_status() if status: total, free, _room = status return f"{total / 2**30:.1f} GB, {free / 2**30:.1f} GB free" return "unknown"

nodes.name: _road_router
nodes.body_text: def _road_router() -> str: """Whether knoxroute is here: without it one road layout is a hundred times slower, so a report about a slow map should say at once which it was.""" try: from generator.roadgraph import rustsearch return "found" if rustsearch.available() else "not found (slow roads)" except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - the summary must never fail return "unknown"

nodes.name: system_summary
nodes.body_text: def system_summary() -> str: import locale import shutil lines = [ f"KnoxMap: {version()}", f"OS: {platform.platform()} ({platform.version()})", f"Python: {sys.version.split()[0]} {platform.architecture()[0]}, " f"UTF-8 mode {'on' if sys.flags.utf8_mode else 'OFF'}, " f"code page {locale.getpreferredencoding(False)}", f"Memory: {_memory()}", ] try: free = shutil.disk_usage(BASE_DIR).free / 2**30 lines.append(f"Disk: {free:.1f} GB free where KnoxMap is") except OSError: pass try: import knoxpaths lines += [ f"Game: {knoxpaths.pz_install_dir() or 'not found'}" f" (Build 42: {knoxpaths.is_build42(knoxpaths.pz_install_dir())})", f"Tools: {knoxpaths.mapping_tools_dir() or 'not installed'}", f"Compiler: {'found' if knoxpaths.worlded_cli() else 'not found'}", f"Road router: {_road_router()}", f"Erika's Tiles: {'yes' if knoxpaths.erikas_tiles_ready() else 'no'}, " f"Elevators: {'yes' if knoxpaths.elevators_mod_installed() else 'no'}, " f"Spawn Selector: {'yes' if knoxpaths.spawn_selector_installed() else 'no'}", ] except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - the summary must never fail lines.append(f"Paths: could not be checked ({exc})") return redact("\n".join(lines))

nodes.name: save_tool_output
nodes.signature: def save_tool_output(tool: str, map_name: str, label: str, returncode: int, stdout: str, stderr: str) -> Path | None

nodes.name: explain_exit
nodes.body_text: def explain_exit(code: int) -> str: return _EXIT_CODES.get(code, "failed")

nodes.name: _safe
nodes.body_text: def _safe(text: str) -> str: return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "_", text)[:60] or "x"

nodes.name: redact
nodes.body_text: def redact(text: str) -> str: """The user's name out of paths: C:\\Users\\alice\\... becomes C:\\Users\\<you>\\...""" home = str(Path.home()) user = os.environ.get("USERNAME") or os.environ.get("USER") or "" for form in {home, home.replace("\\", "/")}: if form and len(form) > 3: text = text.replace(form, "<home>") text = re.sub(r"(?i)([\\/]Users[\\/])[^\\/\s\"']+", r"\1<you>", text) if user and len(user) > 2: text = re.sub(re.escape(user), "<you>", text, flags=re.I) return text

nodes.name: report_zip
nodes.signature: def report_zip(output_dir: Path | None = None, recent_maps: int = 3) -> bytes
nodes.body_text:
def report_zip(output_dir: Path | None = None, recent_maps: int = 3) -> bytes: """Everything a bug report needs, in one zip.""" buf = io.BytesIO() with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z: z.writestr("system.txt", system_summary() + "
") for path in sorted(LOG_DIR.glob("knoxmap.log*")) + sorted(LOG_DIR.glob("setup.log*")): z.writestr(f"logs/{path.name}", redact(_tail(path))) for path in sorted(WORLDED_DIR.glob("*.log"))[-10:]: z.writestr(f"logs/worlded/{path.name}", redact(_tail(path))) # WorldEd's own logs: the one place that says why it would not open a # project, which its console output does not. try: import knoxpaths tools = knoxpaths.mapping_tools_dir() if tools: for path in sorted((tools / "settings" / "logs").glob("PZWorldEd-*.log"))[-5:]: z.writestr(f"logs/worlded-app/{path.name}", redact(_tail(path, 1024 * 1024))) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - the report goes out without them pass old_log = BASE_DIR / "knoxmap_error.log" if old_log.exists(): z.writestr("logs/knoxmap_error.log", redact(_tail(old_log))) if output_dir and output_dir.is_dir(): maps = sorted((d for d in output_dir.iterdir() if d.is_dir()), key=lambda d: d.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True)[:recent_maps] for d in maps: for name in (f"{d.name}_info.json", "settings.json", f"{d.name}_population.json"): p = d / name if p.exists(): z.writestr(f"maps/{d.name}/{name}", redact(_tail(p))) listing = "
".join(f"{f.name}	{f.stat().st_size}" for f in sorted(d.iterdir()) if f.is_file()) lots = d / "lots" count = len(list(lots.glob("*.lotheader"))) if lots.is_dir() else 0 z.writestr(f"maps/{d.name}/files.txt", f"{listing}
lots: {count} cells
") return buf.getvalue()

nodes.name: _tail
nodes.body_text: def _tail(path: Path, limit: int = 3 * 1024 * 1024) -> str: try: with open(path, "rb") as f: size = f.seek(0, 2) f.seek(max(0, size - limit)) return f.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace") except OSError as exc: return f"(could not read: {exc})"

nodes.name: open_folder
nodes.body_text: def open_folder(path=None) -> bool: """Show a file or folder in Explorer; the logs folder by default.""" import subprocess try: if path is None: LOG_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True) os.startfile(str(LOG_DIR)) # type: ignore[attr-defined] return True path = Path(path) if os.name != "nt": # No Explorer: open the folder it is in with whatever the desktop # uses. Nothing is selected, which is as close as this gets. folder = path if path.is_dir() else path.parent opener = "open" if sys.platform == "darwin" else "xdg-open" subprocess.Popen([opener, str(folder)]) return True if path.is_dir(): os.startfile(str(path)) # type: ignore[attr-defined] else: # Explorer wants the comma joined to the switch, and the path as # its own argument, or it opens Documents instead. subprocess.Popen(["explorer", "/select,", str(path)]) return True except (OSError, AttributeError): return False

nodes.name: knoxmap.py
nodes.body_text: """KnoxMap — the whole pipeline in one native window. A real place becomes a playable Project Zomboid map: draw an area -> terrain -> buildings -> compile -> install This is a thin shell. It starts the Flask app on a loopback port and shows it in a native window (Edge WebView2 via pywebview), so the window gets the real Leaflet map with the rectangle tool, place search and landmark lookup, rather than a second UI that would drift from the web one. Compiling uses the patched PZWorldEd_cli.exe that Setup installs (see worlded/README.md); without it the app opens WorldEd on the project instead. Run it with: pythonw knoxmap.py (or double-click KnoxMap.exe) On Linux or macOS: ./knoxmap.sh """ from __future__ import annotations import os import socket import sys import threading import time from pathlib import Path BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR)) TITLE = "KnoxMap — real places into Project Zomboid" if __name__ == "__main__": try: raise SystemExit(main()) except SystemExit: raise except BaseException: # noqa: BLE001 report_crash() raise SystemExit(1)

nodes.name: free_port
nodes.body_text: def free_port() -> int: with socket.socket() as s: s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)) return s.getsockname()[1]

nodes.name: serve
nodes.body_text: def serve(port: int) -> None: from app import app # threaded so the long Overpass calls don't block the UI's polling requests. app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=port, debug=False, use_reloader=False, threaded=True)

nodes.name: wait_for
nodes.signature: def wait_for(port: int, timeout: float = 20.0) -> bool
nodes.body_text: def wait_for(port: int, timeout: float = 20.0) -> bool: deadline = time.time() + timeout while time.time() < deadline: try: with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=0.5): return True except OSError: time.sleep(0.1) return False

nodes.name: main
nodes.body_text: def main() -> int: import knoxlog knoxlog.setup("window") import updater # A downloaded update goes in before any of KnoxMap's code is loaded, and # the new version starts in a fresh process. if updater.apply_staged(): updater.relaunch() return 0 os.environ["KNOXMAP_WINDOW"] = "1" import app # noqa: F401 - fail here, where it can be reported, not in the thread port = free_port() threading.Thread(target=serve, args=(port,), daemon=True).start() if not wait_for(port): raise RuntimeError("the local server did not start within 20 seconds") updater.check_in_background() # The window is up: say so on Discord, if it was asked to. Everything in # knoxpresence fails quietly and on its own thread, so a Discord that is # closed, restarting or refusing the socket costs the window nothing. try: import knoxpresence knoxpresence.idle() except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - presence is never worth a failure knoxlog.log.debug("discord presence: %s", exc) url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/" if in_a_browser(): return show_in_browser(url) try: import webview # Painted the page's own near-black before anything loads, so the # window does not flash white for the second it takes Flask to answer. webview.create_window(f"{TITLE} ({knoxlog.version()})", url, width=1440, height=920, min_size=(1000, 680), background_color="#07090B") webview.start() except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - see in_a_browser knoxlog.log.warning("no native window (%s); opening a browser instead", exc) return show_in_browser(url) end_jobs() return 0

nodes.name: _busy_threads
nodes.body_text: def _busy_threads() -> list[threading.Thread]: """Threads doing a job for the window: requests, and the compile's worker.""" return [t for t in threading.enumerate() if t is not threading.current_thread() and t.is_alive() and ("process_request_thread" in t.name or t.name.endswith("(worker)"))]

nodes.name: end_jobs
nodes.body_text: def end_jobs(grace: float = 15.0) -> None: """The window is gone: stop whatever it left running, and leave. Python will not exit while a process pool still has work queued, so a window closed while a city's buildings were being laid out left KnoxMap running unseen for hours - holding memory, and building the same map alongside the next window opened on it. Every job is asked to stop, as the Stop button does (it keeps what is finished), given a few seconds to do so, and whatever is left of its worker processes is ended with it. """ import multiprocessing import knoxlog if not _busy_threads() and not multiprocessing.active_children(): return # nothing running: leave the usual way from web import jobs jobs.stop_all() # Until the jobs have stopped and saved what they had. A stopped pool's # worker processes idle on after it, so they are not waited for. deadline = time.time() + grace while time.time() < deadline and _busy_threads(): time.sleep(0.25) for child in multiprocessing.active_children(): child.terminate() knoxlog.log.info("window closed: running jobs stopped") import logging logging.shutdown() os._exit(0)

nodes.name: in_a_browser
nodes.body_text: def in_a_browser() -> bool: """Whether to skip the native window and use the player's browser. KnoxMap is a web page either way, so a browser tab is a perfectly good window - and on Linux it is often the only one there is. pywebview needs a system toolkit behind it (WebKitGTK through PyGObject, or Qt WebEngine) that pip cannot install, and a machine without one has no window at all. KNOXMAP_BROWSER=1 forces this on any system. """ if os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_BROWSER") == "1": return True if os.name == "nt" or sys.platform == "darwin": return False # WebView2 and WKWebView ship with the system try: import webview # noqa: F401 except ImportError: return True # pywebview picks its toolkit at import time and raises on start when # there is none; asking it now says so before the page is served. try: from webview import guilib guilib.initialize() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no toolkit, or a broken one return True return False

nodes.name: show_in_browser
nodes.body_text: def show_in_browser(url: str) -> int: """Serve KnoxMap and open it in the default browser, in the foreground. The window is what usually keeps the process alive; without one this waits instead, so closing the terminal is what ends KnoxMap. """ import webbrowser # Downloads go through the browser here, not through /api/save, which is # the app window's way round having nowhere to put a file. os.environ["KNOXMAP_WINDOW"] = "0" print(f"KnoxMap is running at {url}", flush=True) print("Leave this window open while you use it; press Ctrl+C to stop.", flush=True) try: webbrowser.open(url) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no browser configured; the URL is printed pass try: while True: time.sleep(3600) except KeyboardInterrupt: end_jobs() return 0

nodes.name: report_crash
nodes.body_text:
def report_crash() -> None: """pythonw has no console, so a failed start would just vanish. Write the traceback next to the app and say where it is in a message box. """ import traceback where = BASE_DIR / "logs" / "knoxmap.log" try: import knoxlog knoxlog.setup("window") eid = " as " + knoxlog.record(sys.exc_info()[1], "KnoxMap could not start") except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - the logger itself may be what broke eid = "" where = BASE_DIR / "knoxmap_error.log" where.write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8") setup = "Setup.bat" if os.name == "nt" else "./setup.sh" text = (f"KnoxMap could not start:

{sys.exc_info()[1]}

" f"Details were saved to {where}{eid}.
" f"Running {setup} again fixes most problems. If it does not, post " "that file in #bug-reports on the KnoxMap Discord.") try: import ctypes ctypes.windll.user32.MessageBoxW(None, text, "KnoxMap", 0x10) except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - not on Windows; the log is enough print(text, file=sys.stderr)

nodes.name: knoxmap_setup.py
nodes.body_text: """KnoxMap setup: everything a fresh PC needs, in one go. Setup.bat (or: python knoxmap_setup.py) Safe to run again at any time; every step checks first and skips what is already done. What it does: 1. Downloads PZ Mapping Tools (the community map editor, GPL) into vendor/. 2. Downloads the patched PZWorldEd_cli.exe that lets KnoxMap compile maps without clicking through WorldEd's menus, and checks its fingerprint. 3. Finds your Project Zomboid install and extracts the tile artwork the map tools need from *your own copy of the game*. Game artwork is never downloaded or redistributed - it only ever comes from your install. 4. Adjusts the tool configuration for Build 42 and points it at this PC's folders. Nothing is installed outside this folder, and nothing needs admin rights. """ from __future__ import annotations import contextlib import hashlib import io import os import platform import shutil import subprocess import sys import tempfile import zipfile from pathlib import Path BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR)) import knoxpaths # noqa: E402 # The exact PZ Mapping Tools release the patched compiler was built from. The # compiler links against this release's Qt and editor libraries, so the two # are pinned together rather than following "latest". TOOLS_RELEASE = "43.00B260909" TOOLS_URL = ("https://github.com/Unjammer/PZ_Mapping_Tools/releases/download/" "43.00B260909/PZ_Mapping_Tools_build20260909f.zip") REPO = "spytheeuclidean-a11y/knoxmap" CLI_URL = (f"https://github.com/{REPO}/releases/download/" "worlded-cli-20260909f/PZWorldEd_cli.exe") CLI_SHA256 = "dbae186f1f1f541decd123604ec9fc822d930f8f7c1ec8b17c1b89874628f3e2" # The same compiler built for Linux, from the same source at the same commit, # so that making a map there does not go through Wine at all. Upstream # publishes Windows binaries only, so this one is KnoxMap's: it carries its # own Qt and its complete source (.github/workflows/worlded-linux.yml). CLI_LINUX_URL = (f"https://github.com/{REPO}/releases/download/" "worlded-cli-linux-20260909f/PZWorldEd_cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz") CLI_LINUX_SHA256 = "9ef88e23cb58e3fe3e1f9b5d901244b59203ec15d1a456f9f5e16d33164bf3af" USER_AGENT = f"KnoxMap-setup (+https://github.com/{REPO})" # What this run could not do. The exit code says whether it is empty, because # a run that says "Setup complete" must leave nothing for the window's setup # card to complain about, and Setup.bat turns a non-zero exit into "Setup # stopped with an error" instead of a window that lies. Only things that # damage nothing - a rule file that could not be written yet - go here: the app # still draws terrain and builds houses without them. PROBLEMS: list[str] = [] # ---- 1. mapping tools --------------------------------------------------------------- # ---- 2. patched compiler ------------------------------------------------------------ # ---- 3 & 4. game artwork and configuration ------------------------------------------ # ---- 5. where the game keeps mods --------------------------------------------------- if __name__ == "__main__": import traceback _log_to_file() try: raise SystemExit(main()) except SystemExit: raise except BaseException: # noqa: BLE001 traceback.print_exc() print("\nSetup failed. The details are in logs/setup.log - post that file in " "#bug-reports on the KnoxMap Discord if running Setup.bat again does not help.") raise SystemExit(1)

nodes.name: download
nodes.signature: def download(url: str, what: str) -> bytes
nodes.body_text: def download(url: str, what: str) -> bytes: import requests say(f" downloading {what} ...") with requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT}, stream=True, timeout=60) as r: r.raise_for_status() total = int(r.headers.get("content-length") or 0) buf = io.BytesIO() done = 0 for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 16): buf.write(chunk) done += len(chunk) if total: print(f"\r {done / total:5.0%} of {total / 1e6:.0f} MB", end="", flush=True) print() return buf.getvalue()

nodes.name: ensure_mapping_tools
nodes.body_text: def ensure_mapping_tools() -> Path: step(1, "PZ Mapping Tools") existing = knoxpaths.mapping_tools_dir() # worlded_gui finds either the Windows build or one compiled for this # system, so a native build is not thrown away and downloaded over. if existing and knoxpaths.worlded_gui(): say(f" found at {existing}") return existing data = download(TOOLS_URL, f"PZ Mapping Tools {TOOLS_RELEASE} (~40 MB)") target = knoxpaths.VENDOR_DIR / "PZMappingTools" with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)).extractall(tmp) # The archive may or may not wrap everything in a top-level folder. root = next((p.parent.parent for p in Path(tmp).rglob("PZWorldEd.exe") if p.parent.name == "bin"), None) if root is None: raise SystemExit("The downloaded archive has no bin/PZWorldEd.exe - " "the release layout may have changed.") target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if target.exists(): shutil.rmtree(target) shutil.copytree(root, target) say(f" installed to {target}") return target

nodes.name: sha256
nodes.body_text: def sha256(path: Path) -> str: h = hashlib.sha256() with open(path, "rb") as f: for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""): h.update(chunk) return h.hexdigest()

nodes.name: _install_linux_cli
nodes.body_text: def _install_linux_cli(tools: Path) -> bool: """The compiler built for Linux, unpacked into the tools' bin folder. It brings its own Qt, so there is nothing to install and no Wine in the way. It goes in bin/ beside where the Windows one would be because WorldEd takes the folder above the binary as its installation root, and that is where its configuration and the tile artwork live. """ import tarfile try: data = download(CLI_LINUX_URL, "the compiler built for Linux (~29 MB)") except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - any failure means "use Wine" say(f" could not download it: {exc}") return False if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != CLI_LINUX_SHA256: say(" the download does not match the expected fingerprint - not installed.") return False with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data), mode="r:gz") as tar: try: tar.extractall(tmp, filter="data") except TypeError: # Python older than 3.12 has no filter tar.extractall(tmp) program = next((p for p in Path(tmp).rglob("PZWorldEd_cli") if p.is_file()), None) if program is None: say(" the archive has no PZWorldEd_cli - the layout may have changed.") return False bin_dir = tools / "bin" bin_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) for item in program.parent.iterdir(): target = bin_dir / item.name if item.is_dir(): if target.exists(): shutil.rmtree(target) shutil.copytree(item, target, symlinks=True) else: shutil.copy2(item, target) (bin_dir / "PZWorldEd_cli").chmod(0o755) say(f" installed to {bin_dir / 'PZWorldEd_cli'} - no Wine needed") return True

nodes.name: _say_if_it_will_not_start
nodes.body_text: def _say_if_it_will_not_start() -> None: """Check the compiler starts, and say what is wrong if it does not. A compiler that cannot load its Qt does not fail politely: Qt aborts inside its own start-up and the compile dies with exit -6 on the first batch of cells, with two version numbers and nothing to act on. Whoever hits that has already drawn a map and waited through a build, and the answer has nothing to do with the map. Better to find it here, in the seconds after the compiler is installed, and say it in words. """ # Before asking, make the bundled Qt outrank anything LD_LIBRARY_PATH # names. It is what the check would otherwise catch it failing on. fixed = knoxpaths.force_bundled_qt() if fixed: say(f" pointed {fixed} files at the Qt they ship with") trouble = knoxpaths.compiler_trouble() if trouble: say("") say(f" WARNING: {trouble}.") say(" Compile will fail until that is sorted; everything else works.")

nodes.name: ensure_patched_cli
nodes.body_text: def ensure_patched_cli(tools: Path) -> bool: step(2, "Patched map compiler (PZWorldEd_cli)") native = knoxpaths.worlded_cli() if native and not str(native).lower().endswith(".exe"): say(f" found a build for this system at {native}") _say_if_it_will_not_start() return True # On Linux the compiler is fetched for this system rather than run # through Wine. Anywhere else, and on any other processor, the Windows # build is still the one there is. if sys.platform.startswith("linux") and platform.machine() in ("x86_64", "AMD64"): if _install_linux_cli(tools): _say_if_it_will_not_start() return True say(" falling back to the Windows build, which needs Wine") exe = tools / "bin" / "PZWorldEd_cli.exe" if exe.exists(): have = sha256(exe) previous = knoxpaths.load_config().get("cli_sha256") # A compiler this setup installed, from an older release, is replaced # by the new one; one somebody built themselves is left alone. if have != CLI_SHA256 and have == previous: say(" a newer compiler is available - updating") else: say(f" found ({'verified' if have == CLI_SHA256 else 'custom build'})") if have == CLI_SHA256 and previous != CLI_SHA256: knoxpaths.save_config({"cli_sha256": CLI_SHA256}) return True try: data = download(CLI_URL, "the patched compiler (~6 MB)") except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 - any failure means "build it yourself" say(f" could not download it: {exc}") say(" You can still use KnoxMap: compile with 'Open in WorldEd' instead,") say(" or build the compiler yourself - see worlded/README.md.") return False if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != CLI_SHA256: say(" the download does not match the expected fingerprint - not installed.") return False exe.write_bytes(data) knoxpaths.save_config({"cli_sha256": CLI_SHA256}) say(" installed and verified") return True

nodes.name: _warn_if_not_build42
nodes.body_text: def _warn_if_not_build42(game: Path) -> None: if knoxpaths.is_build42(game): return say("") say(" !! This looks like Build 41. KnoxMap makes Build 42 maps, which") say(" Build 41 cannot load. In Steam: right-click Project Zomboid >") say(" Properties > Betas, choose the Build 42 (unstable) branch, let") say(" it update, then run Setup.bat again.") say("")

nodes.name: _ask
nodes.body_text: def _ask(prompt: str) -> str: """input(), or nothing when there is no one to answer (no console).""" try: return input(prompt) except (EOFError, OSError): say("") return ""

nodes.name: choose_steam_folders
nodes.body_text: def choose_steam_folders() -> None: """Show the Steam libraries found on their own, and let the player add a drive or folder they were not found on (games and Workshop mods on another drive). Also chosen later in the app, under Steam libraries.""" found = knoxpaths.steam_libraries_found() say(" Steam libraries: " + (", ".join(f["path"] for f in found) or "none found")) if os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_UNATTENDED") == "1": return while True: answer = _ask(" Games or Workshop mods on another drive? Type the drive or folder\n" " (like E: or E:\\Games\\Steam, several separated by ;),\n" " or press Enter to go on: ").strip() if not answer: return folders = [a.strip().strip('"') for a in answer.split(";") if a.strip()] bad = [f for f in folders if not knoxpaths.library_of(f)] if bad: say(f" No Steam library in {', '.join(bad)} - try again.") continue saved = knoxpaths.load_config().get("steam_folders") or [] knoxpaths.save_steam_folders(list(saved) + folders) say(" Steam libraries: " + ", ".join(f["path"] for f in knoxpaths.steam_libraries_found())) return

nodes.name: find_game
nodes.body_text: def find_game() -> Path | None: step(3, "Project Zomboid install") choose_steam_folders() game = knoxpaths.pz_install_dir() if game: say(f" found at {game}") _warn_if_not_build42(game) return game say(" Could not find Project Zomboid in your Steam libraries.") if os.environ.get("KNOXMAP_UNATTENDED") == "1": # Run by the updater, with nobody to answer: keep the folder set before. saved = knoxpaths.load_config().get("pz_install") return Path(saved) if saved else None if sys.platform == "darwin": say(" On a Mac the game lives inside ProjectZomboid.app. If you do not") say(" know where, this prints it:") say(" find ~/Library/Application\\ Support/Steam -type d -name texturepacks") say(" Any of these will do: the Steam library, the ProjectZomboid folder,") say(" the .app on a Mac, or the media folder itself.") while True: answer = _ask(" Paste the path (or press Enter to skip): ").strip().strip('"') if not answer: return None found = knoxpaths.pz_install_from(answer) if found: say(f" using {found}") _warn_if_not_build42(found) return found say(f" No Project Zomboid there: nothing under {answer} holds a") say(" media/texturepacks folder. Try again, or press Enter to skip.")
