nodes.name: Reserving
nodes.body_text: class Reserving(unittest.TestCase): def test_underground_squares_are_taken_once(self): u = Underground() m = np.ones((4, 4), dtype=bool) self.assertTrue(u.fits(30, 30, m, 2)) u.take(30, 30, m, 2) self.assertFalse(u.fits(33, 33, m, 1)) self.assertTrue(u.fits(34, 30, m, 2)) def test_a_house_basement_stays_a_tile_inside_its_walls(self): spec = reserve([row("house", 10, 10, 6, 5)], Settings(basement_share=1.0), None, None, random.Random(1), (100, 100))[0] self.assertEqual((spec.tier, spec.kind, spec.levels, spec.dx, spec.dy), ("house", "house", 1, 0, 0)) self.assertEqual(int(spec.mask.sum()), 4 * 3) self.assertFalse(spec.mask[0].any() or spec.mask[:, 0].any()) def test_basements_never_join_buildings_that_stand_apart(self): a, b = row("house", 10, 10, 6, 6), row("house", 17, 10, 6, 6) # a tile apart specs = reserve([a, b], Settings(basement_share=1.0), None, None, random.Random(1), (100, 100)) lots = [(as_building(a["mask"], "hall"), 10, 10, 0), (as_building(b["mask"], "hall"), 17, 10, 0), (as_building(specs[0].mask, "storage"), 10 + specs[0].dx, 10 + specs[0].dy, -1), (as_building(specs[1].mask, "storage"), 17 + specs[1].dx, 10 + specs[1].dy, -1)] self.assertEqual(len(placed_rooms(lots[:2])), 2) # Nor the house above: in the game's maps a basement is always a # building of its own, and joined the house lost its roof. self.assertEqual(len(placed_rooms(lots)), 4) def test_an_installation_spreads_over_its_site_but_not_past_it(self): base = row("military", 40, 40, 10, 8) spec = reserve([base], Settings(), None, Sites((20, 30, 120, 90)), random.Random(1), (300, 300))[0] self.assertEqual(spec.tier, "installation") self.assertGreater(int(spec.mask.sum()), 80) ys, xs = np.nonzero(spec.mask) x0, y0 = 40 + spec.dx, 40 + spec.dy self.assertTrue(x0 + xs.min() >= 20 and x0 + xs.max() < 120) self.assertTrue(y0 + ys.min() >= 30 and y0 + ys.max() < 90) self.assertEqual(spec.levels, 2 + 0) # 100 x 60 = 6,000 m2: the fewest levels def test_an_installation_is_cropped_to_its_ceiling(self): spec = reserve([row("military", 900, 900, 10, 10)], Settings(), None, Sites((0, 0, 2000, 2000)), random.Random(1), (2000, 2000))[0] self.assertLessEqual(int(spec.mask.sum()), 40_000) self.assertEqual(spec.levels, 8) def test_a_second_installation_on_the_same_squares_shrinks_then_drops(self): sites = Sites((0, 0, 100, 100), (50, 0, 150, 100)) rows = [row("military", 20, 40, 10, 10), # takes the whole first site row("military", 120, 40, 10, 10), # its site overlaps: shrinks to its footprint row("military", 60, 40, 10, 10)] # inside the first site: nowhere to go specs = reserve(rows, Settings(), None, sites, random.Random(1), (300, 300)) self.assertGreater(int(specs[0].mask.sum()), 1000) self.assertEqual(int(specs[1].mask.sum()), 8 * 8) self.assertIsNone(specs[2]) # Under its own footprint it is a building's basement, not the base's bunker. self.assertEqual((specs[0].tier, specs[1].tier), ("installation", "large")) self.assertEqual(specs[1].levels, levels_for("large", 100, 0, 8)) def test_share_zero_reserves_no_house_basement(self): rows = [row("house", 10 * i, 10, 6, 6) for i in range(20)] self.assertEqual(reserve(rows, Settings(basement_share=0.0), None, None, random.Random(1), (300, 300)), [None] * 20) def test_east_asian_region_quarters_the_house_share(self): rows = [row("house", 4 * (i % 500), 4 * (i // 500), 3, 3) for i in range(4000)] got = reserve(rows, Settings(basement_share=0.4), "jp", None, random.Random(1), (2000, 40)) self.assertTrue(300 <= sum(s is not None for s in got) <= 500)

A basement is for knoxlots.""" def _files(self, d): import os parent = build_building(12, 10, seed=3) b = plan_basement(parent, house_spec(parent), 3, Settings()) from knoxbuild.tbx import render_tbx out = {} for name, text in (("t.tbx", render_tbx(parent, "t")), ("t_bsmt.tbx", render_basement(b, "t", None))): out[name] = os.path.join(d, name) with open(out[name], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(text) return out def test_the_validator_takes_basements_for_knoxlots_only(self): import sys import tempfile sys.path.insert(0, "tools") import validate_tbx with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d: for path in self._files(d).values(): self.assertTrue(validate_tbx.check(path, knoxlots=False), path) self.assertEqual(validate_tbx.check(path, knoxlots=True), [], path) @NEEDS_KNOXLOTS def test_worlded_refuses_a_map_with_basements(self): import os from tools.compile_map import compile_map out = BuildingWithBasements._build(self._town, "worlded", basement_share=1.0) with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as got: compile_map(out, backend="worlded") self.assertIn("basement", str(got.exception)) def test_no_basements_when_worlded_would_compile(self): import os from unittest import mock with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"KNOXMAP_BACKEND": "worlded"}): out = BuildingWithBasements._build(self._town, "plain", basement_share=1.0, compile_lots=False) self.assertEqual(BuildingWithBasements._bsmt_files(out), []) @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): import tempfile cls._town = SimpleNamespace(work=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="bsmt-only-")) @classmethod def tearDownClass(cls): import shutil shutil.rmtree(cls._town.work, ignore_errors=True)

nodes.body_text: class NoGhostRooms(unittest.TestCase): def test_every_basement_room_has_squares(self): """The audit's own buildings (tools/audit_layouts.py), as far as the police station whose basement once kept a room with no squares.""" import sys from collections import Counter sys.path.insert(0, "tools") import audit_layouts as A rng = random.Random(4242) for i in range(88): kind = A.KINDS[i % len(A.KINDS)] w, h = rng.randint(9, 40), rng.randint(9, 40) roll, mask = rng.random(), None if roll < 0.3: mask = A.irregular_mask(w, h, rng) elif roll < 0.65: fp = A.rotated_mask(rng) if fp is not None: w, h, mask = fp.width, fp.height, fp.mask_list() levels = rng.choice((1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12)) if i < 87: continue b = build_building(w, h, levels=levels, seed=i, kind=kind, mask=mask, commercial=kind not in (None, "apartment")) ground = np.array([[bool(v) for v in row] for row in b.storeys[0].grid]) spec = BasementSpec("large", kind, 1, 0, 0, _inside(ground)) below = plan_basement(b, spec, i, Settings()) for st in below.building.storeys: owned = Counter(v for row in st.grid for v in row if v) self.assertEqual([n for n in range(1, len(st.rooms) + 1) if not owned[n]], [])

nodes.body_text: class BathroomSize(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_big_bathroom_becomes_a_bathroom_and_a_store(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 15, 7, kind="bathroom") plan = layout.Plan(16, 8, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 16 for _ in range(8)]) layout._trim_bathroom(plan, 0) self.assertEqual([r.kind for r in plan.rooms], ["bathroom", "storage"]) self.assertLessEqual(plan.rooms[0].area, layout.BATHROOM_MAX_AREA) self.assertEqual(sum(row.count(1) for row in plan.grid), plan.rooms[0].area) def test_no_public_building_has_a_bathroom_hall(self): for kind in ("church", "library", "school", "fire"): for seed in range(8): b = layout.build_building(19 + seed, 15 + seed, levels=2, seed=seed, kind=kind, commercial=True) for s in b.storeys: for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if r.kind == "bathroom": self.assertLessEqual(sum(row.count(i) for row in s.grid), 40, (kind, seed))

nodes.body_text: class BathroomFloor(unittest.TestCase): def houses(self): for seed in range(60): for w, h in ((17, 7), (12, 10), (14, 12)): b = layout.build_building(w, h, seed=seed) for st in b.storeys: yield seed, st def test_a_bathroom_has_no_dresser(self): for seed, st in self.houses(): for role, x, y, o in st.furniture: r = layout._room_at(st, x, y) if r and st.rooms[r - 1].kind == "bathroom": self.assertFalse(role.startswith("dresser"), (seed, role, x, y)) def test_only_the_bathroom_s_own_fittings_stand_in_front_of_a_toilet(self): """A tight bathroom may have its basin there; nothing else.""" from knoxbuild import furnish_rules as FR for seed, st in self.houses(): solid = {c: role for role, x, y, o in st.furniture if layout._blocks(role) for c in layout._cells_for(role, x, y, o)} for role, x, y, o in st.furniture: if role != "toilet" or o not in layout._STEP: continue front = solid.get((x - layout._STEP[o][0], y - layout._STEP[o][1])) if front is not None: self.assertTrue(front.startswith("counter") or FR.priority(front, "bathroom") == FR.ESSENTIAL, (seed, x, y, o, front))

nodes.body_text: """Big house floors cut into rooms, and no room reached through a bathroom. A closet the cut made room-sized failed the whole floor, so two in three big house floors went to the plain splitter; such a closet is now the storage room or study it looks like. A flat bedroom whose only other walls were the outside or the corridor was entered through the bathroom; the two now swap. """ import random import unittest from knoxbuild import layout as L if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: BigHouses
nodes.body_text: class BigHouses(unittest.TestCase): def test_most_big_floors_are_cut_by_kind(self): seen = {"floors": 0, "cut": 0} orig = L._house_by_kind def spy(plan, level, levels, rng): got = orig(plan, level, levels, rng) seen["floors"] += 1 seen["cut"] += got is not None return got L._house_by_kind = spy try: rng = random.Random(1) for i in range(24): L.build_building(rng.randint(20, 30), rng.randint(20, 28), levels=rng.choice((1, 2)), seed=i, kind=None) finally: L._house_by_kind = orig self.assertGreater(seen["floors"], 20) # 36% before; 77% over 119 floors after. self.assertGreater(seen["cut"] / seen["floors"], 0.6)

nodes.body_text: class ThroughBathrooms(unittest.TestCase): def test_flat_rooms_are_not_entered_through_the_bathroom(self): rooms = through = 0 rng = random.Random(7) for i in range(30): b = L.build_building(rng.randint(14, 34), rng.randint(14, 30), levels=rng.choice((2, 3, 4)), seed=i, kind="apartment") for s in b.storeys: links = {} for x, y, d in s.doors: a = L._room_at(s, x - 1, y) if d == "W" else L._room_at(s, x, y - 1) c = L._room_at(s, x, y) if a and c and a != c: links.setdefault(a, set()).add(c) links.setdefault(c, set()).add(a) baths = {j for j, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "bathroom"} for j, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if j in baths or r.is_shaft: continue rooms += 1 through += bool(links.get(j)) and links[j] <= baths self.assertGreater(rooms, 500) # Flats only, the worst case: 1.70% without the swap, 0.64% with it. self.assertLess(through / rooms, 0.01) def test_a_swap_keeps_one_bathroom_and_its_door(self): # A bedroom reached only through the bathroom, which opens on a hall. hall = L.Room(0, 0, 2, 5, kind="hall", unit=1) bath = L.Room(3, 0, 6, 5, kind="bathroom", unit=1) bed = L.Room(7, 0, 9, 5, kind="bedroom", unit=1) plan = L.Plan(10, 6, rooms=[hall, bath, bed], grid=[[1] * 3 + [2] * 4 + [3] * 3 for _ in range(6)], doors=[(3, 2, "W"), (7, 2, "W")]) self.assertEqual(L._swap_through_bathrooms(plan), 1) self.assertEqual([r.kind for r in plan.rooms], ["hall", "bedroom", "bathroom"])

nodes.name: test_big_trees.py
nodes.body_text: """The big trees, and the trees round a park. Every tree KnoxMap placed was one tile of a species sheet at an index Build 42 has no tile definition for - a picture with no `tree` property behind it, so scenery rather than a tree - and the jumbo sheets, which are what the game fills its own woods with, were never used at all. Reported from a generated map: "big trees seem to almost never generate, leading to very disappointing results. in areas such as parks more big trees should probably generate, especially around the edges". """ import os import subprocess import sys import tempfile import unittest from pathlib import Path from unittest import mock import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.rendering import vegetation as V ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent PATCHER = ROOT / "worlded" / "patch_rules_b42_trees.py" RULES = """alias { name = darkgrass tiles = [ blends_natural_01_16 ] } rule { label = Trees bitmap = 1 color = 255 0 0 tiles = [ vegetation_trees_01_8 vegetation_trees_01_9 vegetation_trees_01_10 vegetation_trees_01_11 ] layer = 0_Vegetation } rule { label = Sparse Trees + Grass bitmap = 1 color = 64 0 0 tiles = [ vegetation_trees_01_8 darkgrass vegetation_trees_01_10 ] layer = 0_Vegetation } rule { label = Fir Trees + Dark grass bitmap = 1 color = 64 0 0 tiles = [ vegetation_trees_01_8 darkgrass ] layer = 0_Vegetation condition = 90 100 35 } """ ROADS_PATCHER = ROOT / "worlded" / "patch_rules_roads.py" if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: tools_dir
nodes.body_text: def tools_dir(path: Path) -> Path: """A map-tools folder with just enough in it to be patched.""" (path / "config").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (path / "Tiles" / "2x").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (path / "config" / "Rules.txt").write_text(RULES, encoding="utf-8") (path / "config" / "Tilesets.txt").write_text("", encoding="utf-8") # The patcher refuses to name a sheet that is not on disk; only the name # is read, never the picture. import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher sheets = set(patcher.DECIDUOUS) | set(patcher.EVERGREEN) | {patcher.FLOWER_SHEET} for _label, _colour, tiles in patcher.TREE_RULES: sheets |= {t.rsplit("_", 1)[0] for t in tiles} for sheet in sheets: (path / "Tiles" / "2x" / f"{sheet}.png").write_bytes(b"") return path

nodes.name: patch
nodes.body_text: def patch(path: Path) -> str: out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(PATCHER), str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False) assert out.returncode == 0, out.stderr return (path / "config" / "Rules.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

nodes.name: patch_both
nodes.body_text: def patch_both(path: Path) -> str: """A Setup's worth of rule patching, in Setup's own order.""" for script in (PATCHER, ROADS_PATCHER): out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(script), str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False) assert out.returncode == 0, out.stderr return (path / "config" / "Rules.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

BothPatchersLeaveTheFileAlone
nodes.body_text: class BothPatchersLeaveTheFileAlone(unittest.TestCase): """The trees and the roads patch the same file, one after the other. Each used to strip its own rules and append the new ones to the end. The trees ran first and the roads second, so by the next run the trees' rules were no longer last: each put its own back at the end, past the other's, and the two swapped places on every run. Rules.txt is hashed to decide what an incremental compile may keep (tools/compile_state.py), so every Setup meant a full recompile of every map - and for a map that had been moved, "compile it again" looked like it did nothing, because compiling was not the part that was stale. Running one of them twice cannot see this: the swap needs both. """ def setUp(self): self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() self.tools = tools_dir(Path(self.tmp.name)) self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup) def test_a_second_setup_writes_nothing(self): settled = patch_both(self.tools) for run in (2, 3): with self.subTest(run=run): self.assertEqual(patch_both(self.tools), settled) def test_settled_still_holds_both_patchers_rules(self): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as trees import worlded.patch_rules_roads as roads text = patch_both(self.tools) self.assertIn(f"label = {trees.MARKER} Giant tree", text) self.assertIn(f"label = {roads.MARKER} Yard bed_soil", text) def test_the_rules_are_not_laid_down_twice(self): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as trees text = patch_both(self.tools) self.assertEqual(text.count(f"label = {trees.MARKER} "), len(trees.TREE_RULES))

class TheRulesPlaceTreesTheGameKnows(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() self.tools = tools_dir(Path(self.tmp.name)) self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup) def entries(self, text: str) -> list[str]: import re return re.findall(r" (e_\w+_1_\d+) ", text) def test_no_tree_lands_on_a_picture_with_no_definition_behind_it(self): # Of the 24 pictures on a species sheet the game defines the first # eight, four sizes in two seasons, and it is the definition that # carries `tree = 1..4`. The old rules asked for 8 to 11. for tile in self.entries(patch(self.tools)): sheet, index = tile.rsplit("_", 1) if "JUMBO" in sheet: continue with self.subTest(tile=tile): self.assertLess(int(index), 4, f"{tile} is not a tree the game defines") def test_a_wood_gets_more_than_one_size_of_tree(self): sizes = {int(t.rsplit("_", 1)[1]) for t in self.entries(patch(self.tools)) if "JUMBO" not in t} self.assertGreater(len(sizes), 1, f"every tree the same size ({sizes})") def test_the_fir_rules_get_firs(self): text = patch(self.tools) fir = text.split("label = Fir Trees", 1)[1].split("}", 1)[0] import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher self.assertTrue(any(sheet in fir for sheet in patcher.EVERGREEN), fir) def test_every_colour_the_renderer_paints_has_a_rule(self): text = patch(self.tools) for colour in (C.TREE_SMALL, C.TREE_BIG, C.TREE_HUGE, C.TREE_GIANT): with self.subTest(colour=colour): self.assertIn("color = {} {} {}".format(*colour), text) def test_the_small_trees_are_the_small_sizes(self): text = patch(self.tools) small = text.split("label = KnoxMap tree Small tree", 1)[1].split("]", 1)[0] import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher indices = {int(t.rsplit("_", 1)[1]) for t in small.split() if t.startswith("e_")} self.assertEqual(indices, {patcher.SIZE_INDEX[1], patcher.SIZE_INDEX[2]}) def wood(self, text): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher found = set() for block in text.split("rule
{")[1:]: if patcher.MARKER in block or "Fir" in block: continue found |= {t.rsplit("_", 1)[0] for t in self.entries(block)} return found def blocks(self, text): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher out = {} for block in text.split("rule
{")[1:]: label = block.split("label = ", 1)[1].split("
", 1)[0].strip() if label.startswith(patcher.MARKER): continue tiles = block.split("tiles = [", 1)[1].split("]", 1)[0].split() out[label] = tiles return out def test_every_wood_rule_has_every_species(self): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher for label, tiles in self.blocks(patch(self.tools)).items(): species = {t.rsplit("_", 1)[0] for t in tiles if t.startswith("e_")} want = set(patcher.EVERGREEN if "Fir" in label else patcher.MIXED) with self.subTest(label=label): self.assertEqual(species, want) def test_and_each_keeps_its_share_of_trees(self): import re tree = re.compile(r"^(?:vegetation_trees_01_\d+|e_[a-z]+_1_\d+)$") before = self.blocks(RULES) after = self.blocks(patch(self.tools)) for label, tiles in before.items(): share = sum(bool(tree.match(t)) for t in tiles) / len(tiles) new = after[label] with self.subTest(label=label): self.assertAlmostEqual( sum(bool(tree.match(t)) for t in new) / len(new), share) def test_a_wood_is_every_species_broadleaf_and_evergreen(self): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher found = self.wood(patch(self.tools)) self.assertTrue(found & set(patcher.EVERGREEN), found) self.assertTrue(found & set(patcher.DECIDUOUS), found) def test_an_install_patched_broadleaf_only_gets_the_mixture(self): import worlded.patch_rules_b42_trees as patcher once = patch(self.tools) broadleaf = once for sheet in patcher.EVERGREEN: broadleaf = broadleaf.replace(sheet + "_", "e_redmaple_1_") # ...but only in the woods: our own rules are rewritten whole anyway. (self.tools / "config" / "Rules.txt").write_text(broadleaf, encoding="utf-8") self.assertEqual(patch(self.tools), once) def test_running_it_again_changes_nothing(self): once = patch(self.tools) self.assertEqual(patch(self.tools), once) def test_and_it_mends_what_an_older_version_wrote(self): # The first version substituted index for index, so an install set up # then has species sheets at 8 to 11: scenery, not trees. (self.tools / "config" / "Rules.txt").write_text( RULES.replace("vegetation_trees_01_8", "e_redmaple_1_8") .replace("vegetation_trees_01_11", "e_dogwood_1_11"), encoding="utf-8") text = patch(self.tools) self.assertNotIn("e_redmaple_1_8", text) self.assertNotIn("e_dogwood_1_11", text)

nodes.body_text: class BigTreesStandApart(unittest.TestCase): def grow(self, veg=None, land=None, **kw): veg = veg or planted() land = land or ground(veg.size) with mock.patch.object(V, "tree_rules_ready", return_value=True): V._plant_big_trees(veg, land, [], [], [], Projector(), **kw) return veg def test_a_block_of_wood_grows_some_big_ones(self): self.assertTrue(big_trees(self.grow())) def test_none_of_them_stands_in_another_one_s_square(self): veg = self.grow() taken: set = set() for (x, y), colour in big_trees(veg).items(): side = C.BIG_TREE_ROOM[colour] reach = side // 2 if side % 2 else 0 square = {(fx, fy) for fy in range(y - reach, y - reach + side) for fx in range(x - reach, x - reach + side)} with self.subTest(at=(x, y)): self.assertFalse(square & taken, f"{colour} at {x},{y} overlaps") taken |= square def test_the_rest_of_the_square_is_cleared_for_it(self): veg = self.grow() px = veg.load() for (x, y), colour in big_trees(veg).items(): side = C.BIG_TREE_ROOM[colour] reach = side // 2 if side % 2 else 0 for fy in range(y - reach, y - reach + side): for fx in range(x - reach, x - reach + side): if (fx, fy) != (x, y): with self.subTest(at=(fx, fy)): self.assertEqual(px[fx, fy], C.VEG_NOTHING) def test_none_of_them_hangs_off_the_edge_of_the_map(self): veg = self.grow() w, h = veg.size for (x, y), colour in big_trees(veg).items(): side = C.BIG_TREE_ROOM[colour] reach = side // 2 if side % 2 else 0 self.assertTrue(0 <= x - reach and x - reach + side <= w and 0 <= y - reach and y - reach + side <= h) def test_a_hedge_is_not_cleared_to_make_room(self): veg = planted() for y in range(veg.size[1]): veg.putpixel((30, y), C.BUSHES) grown = self.grow(veg=veg) px = grown.load() kept = sum(1 for y in range(grown.size[1]) if px[30, y] == C.BUSHES) self.assertEqual(kept, grown.size[1], "the hedge was cut through") def test_and_none_of_them_stands_in_the_water(self): land = ground() for y in range(30, 60): for x in range(60): land.putpixel((x, y), C.WATER) grown = self.grow(land=land) wet = [(x, y) for (x, y) in big_trees(grown) if y >= 29] self.assertFalse(wet, f"big trees in the river: {wet[:4]}") def test_turning_the_trees_off_leaves_the_map_alone(self): veg = planted() before = list(veg.get_flattened_data() if hasattr(veg, "get_flattened_data") else veg.getdata()) V._plant_big_trees(veg, ground(), [], [], [], Projector(), density=0) self.assertEqual(list(veg.get_flattened_data() if hasattr(veg, "get_flattened_data") else veg.getdata()), before) def test_as_does_an_install_whose_rules_have_no_big_trees_in_them(self): veg = planted() with mock.patch.object(V, "tree_rules_ready", return_value=False): V._plant_big_trees(veg, ground(), [], [], [], Projector()) self.assertFalse(big_trees(veg)) def test_a_garden_gets_a_tree_but_never_one_that_swallows_the_house(self): # A jumbo XL leans over three squares and an XXL over five: a house # behind one cannot be seen at all, so a yard gets the small jumbo. house = square({"building": "house"}, 28, 28, 32, 32) veg = planted() with mock.patch.object(V, "tree_rules_ready", return_value=True): V._plant_big_trees(veg, ground(), [], [], [house], Projector()) reach = V.GARDEN_REACH_TILES yard = {at: colour for at, colour in big_trees(veg).items() if max(abs(at[0] - 30), abs(at[1] - 30)) <= reach} self.assertTrue(yard, "nothing was planted in the yard") self.assertEqual({c for c in yard.values()} - {C.TREE_BIG}, set(), f"a yard tree that swallows the house: {yard}")

nodes.body_text: class ParksHaveTreesRoundTheEdge(unittest.TestCase): def park(self, size=(120, 120), rules=True): veg = Image.new("RGB", size, C.VEG_NOTHING) land = ground(size, C.MEDIUM_GRASS) feats = [square({"leisure": "park"}, 5, 5, size[0] - 5, size[1] - 5)] with mock.patch.object(V, "tree_rules_ready", return_value=rules): V._paint_parks(veg, land, feats, Projector()) return veg, land def colours(self, veg) -> set: px = veg.load() w, h = veg.size return {px[x, y] for y in range(h) for x in range(w)} def test_not_every_tree_in_a_park_is_the_same_height(self): # Which size a tree comes out is the rule's to say, and the rule a # park tree falls under calls for a grown one. self.assertIn(C.TREE_SMALL, self.colours(self.park()[0])) def test_and_an_install_without_the_rules_plants_plain_trees(self): colours = self.colours(self.park(rules=False)[0]) self.assertNotIn(C.TREE_SMALL, colours) self.assertIn(C.TREES, colours) def density(self, veg, where) -> float: px = veg.load() inside = [(x, y) for x, y in where] grown = sum(1 for x, y in inside if px[x, y] != C.VEG_NOTHING) return grown / max(1, len(inside)) def test_the_belt_round_the_edge_is_thicker_than_the_middle(self): veg, _land = self.park() deep = int(V.PARK_EDGE_M) belt = [(x, y) for y in range(6, 114) for x in range(6, 114) if min(x - 5, y - 5, 114 - x, 114 - y) <= deep] middle = [(x, y) for y in range(6, 114) for x in range(6, 114) if min(x - 5, y - 5, 114 - x, 114 - y) > deep] self.assertGreater(self.density(veg, belt), 2 * self.density(veg, middle)) def test_the_middle_is_not_left_bare_either(self): veg, _land = self.park() middle = [(x, y) for y in range(40, 80) for x in range(40, 80)] self.assertGreater(self.density(veg, middle), 0) def test_a_path_through_a_park_keeps_its_width(self): veg = Image.new("RGB", (120, 120), C.VEG_NOTHING) land = ground((120, 120), C.MEDIUM_GRASS) for x in range(120): land.putpixel((x, 60), C.PALE_CONCRETE) V._paint_parks(veg, land, [square({"leisure": "park"}, 5, 5, 115, 115)], Projector()) px = veg.load() on_the_path = [(x, y) for x in range(10, 110) for y in (59, 60, 61) if px[x, y] != C.VEG_NOTHING] self.assertFalse(on_the_path, f"planted on the path: {on_the_path[:4]}") def test_nothing_grows_outside_the_park(self): veg, _land = self.park() px = veg.load() outside = [(x, y) for x in range(120) for y in range(120) if (x < 4 or y < 4 or x > 116 or y > 116) and px[x, y] != C.VEG_NOTHING] self.assertFalse(outside, f"planted outside: {outside[:4]}")

nodes.body_text: import unittest import numpy as np from knoxbuild.blends import blend_layers, parse_blends from knoxbuild.rules import parse_rules from knoxbuild.terrain import Palette RULES = """ alias { name = grass tiles = [ g_0 g_1 ] } """ ALL = "".join([ blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_n", "n"), blend("0_FloorOverlay2", "ov_w", "w"), blend("0_FloorOverlay3", "ov_e", "e"), blend("0_FloorOverlay4", "ov_s", "s"), blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_nw", "nw"), blend("0_FloorOverlay2", "ov_ne", "ne"), blend("0_FloorOverlay3", "ov_sw", "sw"), blend("0_FloorOverlay4", "ov_se", "se"), ]) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: blend
nodes.body_text: def blend(layer, tile, d, exclude=""): return f""" blend {{ layer = {layer} mainTile = grass blendTile = {tile} dir = {d} exclude = {exclude} }} """

nodes.name: run
nodes.signature: def run(picture, text=ALL, seam=None, x0=0, y0=0)
nodes.body_text: def run(picture, text=ALL, seam=None, x0=0, y0=0): """picture: rows of 'G' grass, 'R' road, '.' nothing. Returns {(x, y): set of overlay names}.""" rules = parse_rules(RULES) pal = Palette() h, w = len(picture), len(picture[0]) floor = np.zeros((h, w), np.int64) for y, row in enumerate(picture): for x, c in enumerate(row): if c != ".": floor[y, x] = pal.of("g_0" if c == "G" else "road") layers = blend_layers(floor, rules, parse_blends(text), pal, seed=1, x0=x0, y0=y0, seam=seam) out = {} for arr in layers.values(): for y, x in zip(*np.nonzero(arr)): out.setdefault((int(x), int(y)), set()).add(pal.names[arr[y, x]]) return out

nodes.body_text: class BlendTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_parse(self): b = parse_blends(ALL) self.assertEqual(len(b), 8) self.assertEqual((b[4].dir, b[4].tile, b[4].layer), ("nw", "ov_nw", "0_FloorOverlay")) def test_cardinal_neighbour(self): got = run(["...", "GR.", "..."]) self.assertEqual(got, {(1, 1): {"ov_w"}}) def test_two_opposite_neighbours(self): self.assertEqual(run(["GRG"]), {(1, 0): {"ov_w", "ov_e"}}) def test_corner_replaces_the_two_cardinals(self): got = run(["GG.", "GR.", "..."]) self.assertEqual(got[(1, 1)], {"ov_nw"}) def test_a_lone_diagonal_gives_nothing(self): self.assertEqual(run(["G..", ".R.", "..."]).get((1, 1)), None) def test_main_ground_and_empty_squares_get_nothing(self): got = run(["GGG", ".G.", "..."]) self.assertEqual(got, {}) def test_excluded_ground_gets_nothing(self): text = blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_w", "w", exclude="grass") self.assertEqual(run(["GG"], text=text), {}) text2 = blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_w", "w", exclude="g_1") self.assertEqual(run(["GR"], text=text2), {(1, 0): {"ov_w"}}) def test_later_rule_wins_a_shared_layer(self): text = blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_first", "w") + blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_last", "w") self.assertEqual(run(["GR"], text=text), {(1, 0): {"ov_last"}}) def test_seams(self): pic = ["GR"] self.assertEqual(run(pic, x0=299), {(1, 0): {"ov_w"}}) self.assertEqual(run(pic, x0=299, seam=300), {}) # 299 | 300 is a seam self.assertEqual(run(pic, x0=10, seam=300), {(1, 0): {"ov_w"}}) def test_a_cut_out_window_blends_the_same_inside(self): # the picks follow the position, and a margin of one square gives the same neighbours pic = ["GGRGG", "GGRRG", "GRRGG"] text = blend("0_FloorOverlay", "ov_w", "w") + blend("0_FloorOverlay2", "ov_e", "e") whole = run(pic, text=text) part = run([row[1:] for row in pic], text=text, x0=1) for (x, y), kinds in part.items(): if x > 0: # column 0 of the cut-out has lost its west neighbour self.assertEqual(whole.get((x + 1, y)), kinds)

The way in is the side that is not water.""" def ground(self, paint): import os from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C directory = self.enterContext(TemporaryDirectory()) tiles = np.zeros((40, 40, 3), dtype=np.uint8) tiles[:, :] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS paint(tiles, C) Image.fromarray(tiles).save(os.path.join(directory, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") return build._street_finder(directory, "m") def test_a_hut_at_the_water_has_its_door_on_the_landward_side(self): side = self.ground(lambda tiles, C: tiles.__setitem__( (slice(20, None), slice(None)), C.WATER)) self.assertEqual(side(10, 16, 6, 4), "N") def test_a_hut_out_on_a_pier_faces_the_shore(self): def paint(tiles, C): tiles[:, :] = C.WATER tiles[:, :8] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS self.assertEqual(self.ground(paint)(12, 18, 4, 4), "W") def test_inland_with_no_street_is_still_no_answer(self): side = self.ground(lambda tiles, C: None) self.assertIsNone(side(10, 2, 6, 4)) def test_a_street_is_still_what_decides_where_there_is_one(self): def paint(tiles, C): tiles[20:, :] = C.WATER tiles[10:12, :] = C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT # the road along the shore self.assertEqual(self.ground(paint)(10, 16, 6, 4), "N")

nodes.name: TheDoorIsOnTheStreet
nodes.body_text: class TheDoorIsOnTheStreet(unittest.TestCase): """Which room the door is in matters less than which way it faces. The best room to arrive in was chosen first and the street only decided which of that room's walls got the door. A house's hall rarely reaches the street side, so the door went round the back: counted over generated houses, 5 in 100 had a door on the street. Reported in #bug-reports by Zombaxx - "entrance door placement not always facing the closest street". """ def doors_facing(self, kind, street, seeds=range(12)): """How many of these buildings have an outside door on the street.""" from knoxbuild.layout import _outside_runs, build_building facing = built = 0 for seed in seeds: plan = build_building(20, 16, levels=2, seed=seed, street=street, kind=None if kind == "house" else kind, commercial=kind not in ("house", "apartment")) ground = plan.storeys[0] doors = set(ground.doors) sides = {side for idx in range(1, len(ground.rooms) + 1) for side, wall in _outside_runs(ground, idx) for edge in wall if edge in doors for side in (side,)} if not sides: continue built += 1 facing += street in sides return facing, built def test_every_kind_opens_onto_the_street_it_stands_on(self): for kind in ("house", "apartment", "shop", "civic", "school"): for street in ("N", "S", "W", "E"): with self.subTest(kind=kind, street=street): facing, built = self.doors_facing(kind, street) self.assertTrue(built, "nothing was built") self.assertEqual(facing, built, f"{kind}: {facing} of {built} face {street}") def test_with_no_street_it_still_puts_a_door_somewhere(self): from knoxbuild.layout import build_building for seed in range(6): plan = build_building(20, 16, levels=2, seed=seed, kind=None) self.assertTrue(plan.storeys[0].doors)

nodes.body_text: class WorldEdTests(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): sys.path.insert(0, str(FIXTURES)) from bxshow import load sys.path.pop(0) cls.load = staticmethod(load) def check_building(self, folder, name, tx, ty, region=None): b = parse_tbx((folder / "buildings" / (name + ".tbx")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) trim_tiles = entry_tiles(b, "ExteriorWallTrim") grime_tiles = entry_tiles(b, "GrimeWall") cache = {} for z in range(len(b.floors)): pred = level_tiles(b, z) for y in range(-2, b.height + 3): for x in range(-2, b.width + 3): if region and not region(z, x, y): continue cx, cy = (21000 + tx + x) // 256, (ty + y) // 256 if (cx, cy) not in cache: cache[cx, cy] = self.load(str(folder / "lots"), cx, cy)[0] actual = cache[cx, cy].get(((21000 + tx + x) % 256, (ty + y) % 256, z), []) actual = [t for t in actual if not t.startswith(TERRAIN)] want = pred.get((x, y), []) if any(WINDOW_FIXTURE.match(t) for t in want): # WorldEd leaves the trim and grime off a window square; # KnoxMap keeps them so the band and the weathering run # under the window (buildtiles.level_layers). Those # deliberate differences are the only ones allowed here. drop = trim_tiles | grime_tiles elif z > 0: # Grime on every storey is ours too; WorldEd keeps it at # the ground level. drop = grime_tiles else: drop = set() if drop: want = [t for t in want if t not in drop] actual = [t for t in actual if t not in drop] self.assertEqual(want, actual, f"{name}: level {z}, ({x},{y})") def test_all_handmade_cases(self): for folder in sorted((FIXTURES / "bx").iterdir()): if folder.is_dir(): with self.subTest(case=folder.name): self.check_building(folder, folder.name, 40, 40) def test_four_level_house(self): self.check_building(FIXTURES / "exp/house", "house_0000", 269, 592) def test_fresh_custom_walls_and_unusual_windows(self): extra = Path(os.environ.get("KNOXLOTS_EXTRA", FIXTURES / "extra")) if not extra.is_dir(): self.skipTest("additional WorldEd fixtures are not installed") for name in ("wallW", "wallN", "windows"): with self.subTest(case=name): self.check_building(extra / name, "building", 40, 40) def test_fresh_overlaps(self): extra = Path(os.environ.get("KNOXLOTS_EXTRA", FIXTURES / "extra")) if not extra.is_dir(): self.skipTest("additional WorldEd fixtures are not installed") for name in ("overlap", "overlap-small", "overlap-trim"): with self.subTest(case=name): folder = extra / name a, b = [parse_tbx((folder / "buildings" / (n + nodes.name: check_building
nodes.signature: def check_building(self, folder, name, tx, ty, region=None)
nodes.body_text: def check_building(self, folder, name, tx, ty, region=None): b = parse_tbx((folder / "buildings" / (name + ".tbx")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")) trim_tiles = entry_tiles(b, "ExteriorWallTrim") grime_tiles = entry_tiles(b, "GrimeWall") cache = {} for z in range(len(b.floors)): pred = level_tiles(b, z) for y in range(-2, b.height + 3): for x in range(-2, b.width + 3): if region and not region(z, x, y): continue cx, cy = (21000 + tx + x) // 256, (ty + y) // 256 if (cx, cy) not in cache: cache[cx, cy] = self.load(str(folder / "lots"), cx, cy)[0] actual = cache[cx, cy].get(((21000 + tx + x) % 256, (ty + y) % 256, z), []) actual = [t for t in actual if not t.startswith(TERRAIN)] want = pred.get((x, y), []) if any(WINDOW_FIXTURE.match(t) for t in want): # WorldEd leaves the trim and grime off a window square; # KnoxMap keeps them so the band and the weathering run # under the window (buildtiles.level_layers). Those # deliberate differences are the only ones allowed here. drop = trim_tiles | grime_tiles elif z > 0: # Grime on every storey is ours too; WorldEd keeps it at # the ground level. drop = grime_tiles else: drop = set() if drop: want = [t for t in want if t not in drop] actual = [t for t in actual if t not in drop] self.assertEqual(want, actual, f"{name}: level {z}, ({x},{y})")

nodes.body_text: class RectTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_rectangle_is_one_rect(self): self.assertEqual(room_rects(squares(["###", "###"])), [(0, 0, 3, 2)]) def test_a_c_shape_cuts_the_way_worlded_does(self): pic = ["######", "######", "#.....", "#.....", "#.....", "######"] self.assertEqual(room_rects(squares(pic)), [(0, 0, 6, 2), (0, 2, 1, 3), (0, 5, 6, 1)]) def test_a_row_wider_than_the_column_above_ends_the_column(self): pic = [".###", ".###", ".###", "####", "####"] self.assertEqual(room_rects(squares(pic)), [(1, 0, 3, 3), (0, 3, 4, 2)]) def test_the_rects_always_cover_the_squares_exactly_once(self): import random rnd = random.Random(5) for _ in range(200): sq = {(x, y) for x in range(8) for y in range(8) if rnd.random() < 0.6} rects = room_rects(sq) self.assertEqual(covers(rects), sq) self.assertEqual(sum(w * h for _, _, w, h in rects), len(sq))

The project lists the lot in source cell (0, 1) # first (it goes column by column); WorldEd goes across a row first, so the lot in # source cell (0, 0) comes first. lots = [(b, 10, 310, 0), (b, 150, 280, 0)] rooms, buildings = cell_tables(82, 1, placed_rooms(lots)) self.assertEqual([r["rects"][0][:2] for r in rooms], [(158, 24), (18, 54)]) self.assertEqual(buildings, [[0], [1]])

"luxury", "building": "mansion"} profile = BuildingProfile.infer(tags, "house", 0.12, 700, 2, 41) self.assertEqual(profile, BuildingProfile.infer(tags, "house", 0.12, 700, 2, 41)) self.assertEqual(profile.year_built, 1922) self.assertEqual(profile.era, "prewar") self.assertEqual(profile.setting, "suburban") self.assertEqual(profile.wear, 0.76) self.assertGreater(profile.wealth, 0.7) def test_neighborhood_setting_uses_density_and_building_type(self): rural = BuildingProfile.infer({}, "house", 0.02, 100, 1, 4) suburban = BuildingProfile.infer({}, "house", 0.14, 100, 1, 4) urban = BuildingProfile.infer({}, "apartment", 0.4, 100, 4, 4) barn = BuildingProfile.infer({"building": "barn"}, None, 0.2, 100, 1, 4) self.assertEqual((rural.setting, suburban.setting, urban.setting, barn.setting), ("rural", "suburban", "urban", "rural")) def test_profile_weights_shell_furniture_and_floor_families(self): old_worn = BuildingProfile.infer( {"start_date": "1900", self.assertGreater(old_worn.style_weight("brick"), old_worn.style_weight("render")) self.assertGreater(new_clean.furniture_weight("dresser_black"), new_clean.furniture_weight("dresser_pale")) self.assertGreater(old_worn.floor_weight("civic_worn"), old_worn.floor_weight("wood_pale")) self.assertLess(new_clean.clutter, old_worn.clutter) def nodes.body_text: class ThirtyDegreeTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_wide_roofs_keep_the_eleven_square_cross_section_at_the_origin(self): table = {1: {f"{stem}{i}": f"{stem}{i}" for stem in ("Slope30W", "Slope30E", "Slope30N", "Slope30S", "Peak30WE", "Peak30NS") for i in range(1, 7)}, 2: {f"{stem}{i}": f"{stem}{i}" for stem in ("CapSlope30RiseS", "CapSlope30FallS", "CapSlope30RiseE", "CapSlope30FallE", "CapPeak30S", "CapPeak30E") for i in range(1, 7)}} for kind, w, h, caps, peak in (("Peak30WE", 4, 13, "WE", (3, 9)), ("Peak30NS", 13, 4, "NS", (8, 4))): with self.subTest(kind=kind): s = roof_squares(lambda n: table.get(int(n), {}), {}, roof(kind, "Zero", 3, 4, w, h, caps)) self.assertTrue(any("Peak30" in t for t in s[peak])) self.assertNotIn((3, 15) if kind == "Peak30WE" else (14, 4), s) def test_slopes_both_sides_of_a_peak_row(self): s = squares("Peak30WE", "Zero", 0, 0, 2, 5) self.assertEqual([s[(0, y)] for y in range(5)], [["s_Slope30N1"], ["s_Slope30N2"], ["s_Peak30NS3"], ["s_Slope30S2"], ["s_Slope30S1"]]) def test_hip_rings(self): s = squares("Peak30Quad", "Zero", 0, 0, 5, 5) self.assertEqual(s[(0, 0)], ["s_OuterSlope30NW1"]) self.assertEqual(s[(4, 0)], ["s_OuterSlope30NE1"]) self.assertEqual(s[(1, 1)], ["s_OuterSlope30NW2"]) self.assertEqual(s[(2, 2)], ["s_Peak30Quad3"]) self.assertEqual(s[(0, 2)], ["s_Slope30W1"]) self.assertEqual(len(s), 25)

nodes.name: entry
nodes.body_text: def entry(category, **tiles): body = "".join(f'<tile enum="{k}" tile="{v}"/>' for k, v in tiles.items()) return f'<tile_entry category="{category}">{body}</tile_entry>'

nodes.name: tbx
nodes.signature: def tbx(width, height, floors, rooms=2, extra_attrs="")
nodes.body_text:
def tbx(width, height, floors, rooms=2, extra_attrs=""): """Entries, 1-based: 1 exterior wall, 2 trim, 3 grime, 4 door, 5 frame, 6 window, 7 curtains, 8 shutters, 9 floor A, 10 interior wall A, 11 floor B, 12 interior wall B, 13 interior trim.""" entries = [ entry("exterior_walls", West="ew_000", North="ew_001", NorthWest="ew_002", SouthEast="ew_003", WestDoor="ew_010", NorthDoor="ew_011", WestWindow9="ew_020", NorthWindow9="ew_021"), entry("exterior_wall_trim", West="tr_000", North="tr_001", NorthWest="tr_002", SouthEast="tr_003", WestWindow="tr_020", NorthWindow="tr_021", WestDoor="tr_010", NorthDoor="tr_011"), entry("grime_wall", West="gr_000", North="gr_001", NorthWest="gr_002", SouthEast="gr_003", WestWindow="gr_020", NorthWindow="gr_021", WestDoor="gr_010", NorthDoor="gr_011"), entry("doors", West="door_000", North="door_001"), entry("door_frames", West="frame_000", North="frame_001"), entry("windows", West="fixtures_windows_white_016", North="fixtures_windows_white_017"), entry("curtains", West="cur_000", East="cur_001", North="cur_002", South="cur_003"), entry("shutters", WestBelow="sh_000", WestAbove="sh_001", NorthLeft="sh_002", NorthRight="sh_003"), entry("floors", Floor="floorA_000"), entry("interior_walls", West="iwA_000", North="iwA_001", NorthWest="iwA_002", WestDoor="iwA_010", NorthDoor="iwA_011", WestWindow="iwA_020", NorthWindow="iwA_021"), entry("floors", Floor="floorB_000"), entry("interior_walls", West="iwB_000", North="iwB_001", NorthWest="iwB_002"), entry("interior_wall_trim", West="it_000", North="it_001", NorthWest="it_002", NorthWindow="it_021"), ] room_defs = ( '<room Name="a" InteriorWall="10" InteriorWallTrim="0" Floor="9" GrimeFloor="0" GrimeWall="0" Ceiling="0"/>' '<room Name="b" InteriorWall="12" InteriorWallTrim="13" Floor="11" GrimeFloor="0" GrimeWall="0" Ceiling="0"/>') fl = "" for rooms_grid, objects in floors: rows = ",
".join(",".join(str(v) for v in row) for row in rooms_grid) objs = "".join("<object " + " ".join(f'{k}="{v}"' for k, v in o.items()) + "/>" for o in objects) fl += f"<floor>{objs}<rooms>
{rows}
</rooms></floor>" return (f'<building version="4" width="{width}" height="{height}" ExteriorWall="1" ExteriorWallTrim="2" ' f'GrimeWall="3" Door="4" DoorFrame="5" Window="6" {extra_attrs}>' + "".join(entries) + room_defs + fl + "</building>")

nodes.name: grid
nodes.body_text: def grid(w, h, fill=1, **cells): g = [[fill] * w for _ in range(h)] for (x, y), v in cells.items(): g[y][x] = v return g

nodes.name: BuildTilesTests
nodes.body_text: class BuildTilesTests(unittest.TestCase): def square(self, text, x, y, z=0): return level_tiles(parse_tbx(text), z).get((x, y), []) def test_names_lose_their_padding(self): self.assertEqual(tile_name("walls_exterior_house_02_064"), "walls_exterior_house_02_64") self.assertEqual(tile_name("floors_interior_carpet_01_000"), "floors_interior_carpet_01_0") self.assertEqual(tile_name("nothing"), "nothing") def test_a_room_has_floor_and_interior_walls_on_its_north_and_west_edges(self): t = tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 0, 0), ["floorA_0", "iwA_2"]) # both: the corner tile self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 0), ["floorA_0", "iwA_1"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 0, 2), ["floorA_0", "iwA_0"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 2), ["floorA_0"]) def test_exterior_walls_stand_on_the_squares_outside_the_south_and_east(self): t = tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 3), ["ew_1", "tr_1", "gr_1"]) # south side self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 4, 1), ["ew_0", "tr_0", "gr_0"]) # east side self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 4, 3), ["ew_3", "tr_3", "gr_3"]) # the post at the corner self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 5, 5), []) def test_upper_levels_wear_grime_but_no_trim_outside(self): t = tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), []), (grid(4, 3), [])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 3, z=1), ["ew_1", "gr_1"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 3, z=0), ["ew_1", "tr_1", "gr_1"]) def test_a_wall_between_two_rooms_belongs_to_the_room_on_its_south_or_east(self): g = [[1, 1, 2, 2], [1, 1, 2, 2], [1, 1, 2, 2]] t = tbx(4, 3, [(g, [])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 1), ["floorB_0", "iwB_0", "it_0"]) # room b has trim self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 1), ["floorA_0"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 0), ["floorB_0", "iwB_2", "it_2"]) def test_a_door_swaps_the_wall_and_adds_frame_and_door(self): t = tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [dict(type="door", x=2, y=0, dir="N")])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 0), ["floorA_0", "iwA_11", "frame_1", "door_1"]) t = tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [dict(type="door", x=1, y=3, dir="N")])]) # exterior self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 3), ["ew_11", "tr_11", "gr_11", "frame_1", "door_1"]) def test_a_window_with_curtains_and_shutters(self): obj = dict(type="window", x=2, y=3, dir="N", CurtainsTile=7, ShuttersTile=8) t = tbx(5, 3, [(grid(5, 3), [obj])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 3), ["ew_21", "tr_21", "gr_21", "sh_2", "sh_3", "fixtures_windows_white_17"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 1, 3), ["ew_1", "tr_1", "gr_1", "sh_2"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 3, 3), ["ew_1", "tr_1", "gr_1", "sh_3"]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 2), ["floorA_0", "cur_3"]) # on the inside inside = dict(type="window", x=2, y=0, dir="N", CurtainsTile=7) t = tbx(5, 3, [(grid(5, 3), [inside])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 0), ["floorA_0", "iwA_21", "fixtures_windows_white_17", "cur_2"]) def test_a_window_keeps_the_trim_and_grime_of_its_wall(self): # The trim and grime tables name one window tile, not one per cut-out, so a # numbered wall variant falls back to it instead of dropping the overlays. obj = dict(type="window", x=2, y=3, dir="N", Tile=6) t = tbx(5, 3, [(grid(5, 3), [obj])]) self.assertEqual(self.square(t, 2, 3), ["ew_21", "tr_21", "gr_21", "fixtures_windows_white_17"]) b = parse_tbx(t) b.entries[2]["NorthWindow9"] = "gr_029" # a table that does name the variant self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 0)[(2, 3)], ["ew_21", "tr_21", "gr_029", "fixtures_windows_white_17"]) def test_a_floor_with_the_wrong_number_of_rooms_is_refused(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(3, 3), [])]))

nodes.name: small_building
nodes.body_text: def small_building(floors, furniture=()): """A 4 x 3 building of one room whose floor tile is F, with a set of stairs and curtains.""" from knoxbuild.buildtiles import Building entries = [ {"Floor": "F"}, # 1 floor {"West": "iw_w", "North": "iw_n", "NorthWest": "iw_nw"}, # 2 interior walls {"West1": "st1", "West2": "st2", "West3": "st3", "North1": "sn1", "North2": "sn2", "North3": "sn3"}, # 3 {"South": "cur_s", "North": "cur_n", "East": "cur_e", "West": "cur_w"}, # 4 ] room = {"Floor": "1", "InteriorWall": "2", "InteriorWallTrim": "0", "Ceiling": "0"} return Building(4, 3, {"Stairs": "3"}, entries, [room], floors, list(furniture))

nodes.body_text: class FurnitureStairsTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_roof_furniture_stands_above_a_flat_roof(self): furniture = [{"layer": "Roof", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "vent")]}}] b = small_building(self.floors([dict(type="roof", RoofType="FlatTop", x=1, y=1, width=1, height=1, TopTiles=5)], upper=True), furniture) b.entries.append({"West1": "roof_floor"}) b.floors[1].objects.append(dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=0, orient="N", x=1, y=1)) self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 1)[(1, 1)], ["F", "roof_floor", "vent"]) def test_walls_furniture_replaces_only_its_wall_direction(self): furniture = [{"layer": "Walls", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "escalator"), (1, 0, "landing")]}}] objs = [dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=0, orient="N", x=0, y=0)] b = small_building(self.floors(objs), furniture) tiles = level_tiles(b, 0) self.assertEqual(tiles[(0, 0)], ["F", "iw_w", "escalator"]) self.assertEqual(tiles[(1, 0)], ["F", "landing"]) def test_north_curtain_precedes_ordinary_furniture(self): furniture = [{"layer": "", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "table")]}}] objs = [dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=0, orient="N", x=1, y=0), dict(type="window", x=1, y=0, dir="N", CurtainsTile=4, Tile=3)] b = small_building(self.floors(objs), furniture) tiles = level_tiles(b, 0)[(1, 0)] self.assertLess(tiles.index("cur_n"), tiles.index("table")) def floors(self, objects, upper=None): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import Floor full = [[1] * 4 for _ in range(3)] out = [Floor(full, objects)] if upper is not None: out.append(Floor([[1] * 4 for _ in range(3)], [])) return out def test_stairs_make_three_steps_and_a_hole_above(self): b = small_building(self.floors([dict(type="stairs", x=0, y=1, dir="W", Tile=3)], upper=True)) ground = level_tiles(b, 0) self.assertEqual([ground[(x, 1)][-1] for x in (1, 2, 3)], ["st3", "st2", "st1"]) above = level_tiles(b, 1) self.assertTrue(all((x, 1) not in above for x in (1, 2, 3))) # no floor over the stairwell self.assertIn((0, 1), above) b = small_building(self.floors([dict(type="stairs", x=2, y=-1, dir="N", Tile=3)], upper=True)) self.assertEqual([level_tiles(b, 0)[(2, y)][-1] for y in (0, 1, 2)], ["sn3", "sn2", "sn1"]) def test_furniture_layers_stack_in_buildinged_order(self): furn = [ {"layer": "", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "table")]}}, # 0 ordinary {"layer": "WallFurniture", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "paint_n")], "E": [(0, 0, "paint_e")]}}, # 1 {"layer": "FloorFurniture", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "rug")]}}, # 2 {"layer": "", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "big_a"), (1, 0, "big_b")]}}, # 3 two tiles ] objs = [dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=0, orient="N", x=1, y=1), dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=1, orient="E", x=1, y=1), dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=1, orient="N", x=1, y=1), dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=2, orient="N", x=1, y=1)] b = small_building(self.floors(objs), furn) # rug under everything, wall furniture facing north before the table, facing east after it self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 0)[(1, 1)], ["F", "rug", "paint_n", "table", "paint_e"]) # Offsets put the second tile on its own square. objs = [dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=3, orient="N", x=1, y=1), dict(type="window", x=2, y=0, dir="N", CurtainsTile=4, ShuttersTile=0, Tile=3)] b = small_building(self.floors(objs), furn) t = level_tiles(b, 0) self.assertEqual(t[(1, 1)], ["F", "big_a"]) self.assertEqual(t[(2, 1)], ["F", "big_b"]) def test_window_variant_follows_the_sprite_pair(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import _window_variant self.assertEqual([_window_variant(f"fixtures_windows_white_{n}") for n in (16, 17, 10, 11, 24, 25)], [9, 9, 6, 6, 13, 13]) self.assertEqual(_window_variant("fixtures_windows_metal_15"), 8) self.assertEqual(_window_variant("fixtures_windows_wood_9"), 5) self.assertEqual(_window_variant("fixtures_windows_01_24"), 0)

nodes.body_text: class AdditionalBuildingRulesTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_custom_wall_runs_use_their_material_and_end_post(self): for direction, axis in (("W", "North"), ("N", "West")): with self.subTest(direction=direction): obj = dict(type="wall", x=1, y=1, length=2, dir=direction, Tile=1, InteriorTile=12, ExteriorTrim=2, InteriorTrim=13) b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 4, [(grid(4, 4), [obj])])) tiles = level_tiles(b, 0) self.assertEqual(tiles[(1, 1)], ["floorA_0", "iwB_1" if axis == "North" else "iwB_0", "it_1" if axis == "North" else "it_0"]) # Interior palette lacks SouthEast, so no invented post tile. endpoint = (3, 1) if direction == "W" else (1, 3) self.assertEqual(tiles[endpoint], ["floorA_0"]) b.floors[0].rooms = grid(4, 4, fill=0) tiles = level_tiles(b, 0) self.assertEqual(tiles[endpoint], ["ew_3", "tr_3", "gr_3"]) def test_corner_door_preserves_perpendicular_wall_and_duplicate_is_written_once(self): obj = dict(type="door", x=0, y=0, dir="N") b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [obj, obj.copy()])])) self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 0)[(0, 0)], ["floorA_0", "iwA_0", "iwA_11", "frame_1", "door_1"]) def test_unusual_windows_keep_known_variants_and_unknown_fallback(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import _window_variant self.assertEqual(_window_variant("fixtures_windows_church_15"), 8) for n in (40, 42, 48, 50): self.assertEqual(_window_variant(f"fixtures_windows_01_{n}"), 17) for n in (41, 43, 49, 51): self.assertEqual(_window_variant(f"fixtures_windows_01_{n}"), 18) self.assertEqual(_window_variant("fixtures_windows_unknown_40"), 0) def test_secondary_furniture_precedes_south_curtain(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import Floor furn = [{"layer": "", "orients": {"N": [(0, 0, "first"), (1, 0, "second")]}}] objs = [dict(type="furniture", FurnitureTiles=0, orient="N", x=1, y=2), dict(type="window", x=2, y=3, dir="N", CurtainsTile=4, Tile=3)] b = small_building([Floor(grid(4, 3), objs)], furn) self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 0)[(2, 2)], ["F", "second", "cur_s"]) def test_stairs_follow_door_frame_and_door(self): b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [dict(type="stairs", x=0, y=0, dir="W", Tile=14), dict(type="door", x=1, y=0, dir="N")])])) b.entries.append({"West3": "step"}) self.assertEqual(level_tiles(b, 0)[(1, 0)], ["floorA_0", "iwA_11", "frame_1", "door_1", "step"]) def test_composition_preserves_floor_under_later_external_wall_and_sparse_empty_squares(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import compose_lots a = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [])])) sparse = grid(4, 3, fill=0) sparse[0][0] = 2 b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(sparse, [])])) world = compose_lots([(a, 10, 20, 2), (b, 11, 21, 2)]) self.assertEqual(world[(11, 21, 2)], ["floorB_0", "iwB_2", "it_2"]) self.assertEqual(world[(12, 21, 2)], ["floorA_0", "ew_0", "tr_0", "gr_0"]) self.assertEqual(world[(13, 22, 2)], ["floorA_0"]) reverse = compose_lots([(b, 11, 21, 2), (a, 10, 20, 2)]) self.assertEqual(reverse[(11, 21, 2)], ["floorA_0"]) def test_corner_trim_is_replaced_by_north_wall_and_preserved_by_west_wall(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import compose_lots a = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [])])) sparse = grid(4, 3, fill=0) sparse[0][:2] = [2, 2] b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(sparse, [])])) west = compose_lots([(a, 0, 0, 0), (b, 2, 3, 0)]) self.assertEqual(west[(4, 3, 0)], ["tr_3", "ew_0", "tr_0", "gr_0"]) north = compose_lots([(a, 0, 0, 0), (b, 3, 2, 0)]) self.assertEqual(north[(4, 3, 0)], ["gr_3", "ew_1", "tr_1", "gr_1"]) def test_a_west_wall_and_a_north_wall_on_one_square_both_stay(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import compose_lots # `a`'s east wall stands on the square (4, 4); `b` ends one row above it, so its # south wall stands on that same square. They are different walls. a = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 3, [(grid(4, 3), [])])) b = parse_tbx(tbx(4, 4, [(grid(4, 4), [])])) for lots in ([(a, 0, 2, 0), (b, 4, 0, 0)], [(b, 4, 0, 0), (a, 0, 2, 0)]): tiles = compose_lots(lots)[(4, 4, 0)] self.assertIn("ew_0", tiles) # the west wall self.assertIn("ew_1", tiles) # the north wall

nodes.body_text: class BusinessCharacter(unittest.TestCase): def test_furniture_group_obeys_walkway_callback(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 9, 9, kind="office") plan = layout.Plan(10, 10, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 10 for _ in range(10)]) group = [("office_chair", 0, 0, "N")] self.assertEqual(layout._place_group(plan, 1, room, group, 1, set(), set(), lambda cells: False), 0) self.assertEqual(layout._place_group(plan, 1, room, group, 1, set(), set(), lambda cells: True), 1) def test_school_canteen_has_a_kitchen(self): for seed in range(4): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind="school", commercial=True, seed=seed).storeys[0] kinds = {r.kind for r in plan.rooms} self.assertIn("diningroom", kinds) self.assertIn("kitchen", kinds) self.assertIn("classroom", kinds) adj = layout._neighbours(plan) self.assertTrue(any(room.kind == "kitchen" and any(plan.rooms[j - 1].kind == "diningroom" for j in adj[i]) for i, room in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1))) def test_fire_station_is_not_mostly_storage(self): for seed in range(4): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind="fire", commercial=True, seed=seed).storeys[0] kinds = Counter(r.kind for r in plan.rooms if not r.is_core and r.kind != "hall") self.assertIn("firegarage", kinds) self.assertIn("bedroom", kinds) self.assertLessEqual(kinds["firestorage"] * 2, sum(kinds.values())) def test_barn_and_shed_are_not_broken_into_a_grid_of_small_rooms(self): for kind in ("barn", "shed"): for seed in range(4): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind=kind, commercial=True, seed=seed).storeys[0] self.assertLessEqual(len(plan.rooms), 6, (kind, seed)) def test_small_castle_has_a_great_hall(self): plan = layout.build_building(20, 16, kind="castle", commercial=True, seed=0).storeys[0] self.assertIn("hall", {r.kind for r in plan.rooms}) def test_small_stadium_has_a_changing_room(self): plan = layout.build_building(20, 16, kind="stadium", commercial=True, seed=0).storeys[0] self.assertIn("lockerroom", {r.kind for r in plan.rooms})

nodes.body_text: class BusinessLayouts(unittest.TestCase): def test_car_repair_tags_select_a_garage_with_mechanic_use(self): self.assertEqual(use_of({"shop": "car_repair"}), ("mechanic", "storage")) self.assertEqual(build.classify_building({"shop": "car_repair"}), "garage") self.assertEqual(build._business_kind("shop", [("mechanic", "storage")]), "garage") self.assertEqual(build._business_kind("house", [("mechanic", "storage")]), "house") shell = build.pick_style(build.STYLE_AS["garage"], 20, 30, random.Random(8), Settings(), density=0.2) self.assertTrue(shell["name"].startswith("industrial")) def test_mechanic_layout_keeps_a_clear_service_bay(self): building = layout.build_building( 16, 12, kind="garage", uses=[("mechanic", "storage")], street="S", garage_door=True, seed=17) plan = building.storeys[0] self.assertEqual(len(plan.rooms), 1) self.assertEqual(plan.rooms[0].kind, "mechanic") self.assertFalse(plan.shop_front) self.assertFalse(plan.windows) self.assertIn("metal_rack", {role for role, *_ in plan.furniture}) self.assertIn("counter_2", {role for role, *_ in plan.furniture}) south_walls = [wall for room_id in range(1, len(plan.rooms) + 1) for side, wall in layout._outside_runs(plan, room_id) if side == "S"] self.assertTrue(any(sum(edge in plan.doors for edge in wall) >= 3 for wall in south_walls)) for role, x, y, facing in plan.furniture: self.assertFalse(any(4 <= cx <= 11 and 3 <= cy <= 8 for cx, cy in layout._cells_for(role, x, y, facing)))

nodes.body_text: class BusinessSizesAndCirculation(unittest.TestCase): def test_public_buildings_have_compact_bathrooms(self): for kind in ("school", "church", "industrial", "military", "castle", "stadium", "medical", "civic", "police", "library", "fire", "offices"): with self.subTest(kind=kind): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind=kind, commercial=True, seed=0, levels=1).storeys[0] toilets = [room for room in plan.rooms if room.kind == "bathroom"] self.assertTrue(toilets) self.assertLessEqual(min(room.area for room in toilets), 20) def test_school_has_circulation_reaching_classrooms(self): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind="school", commercial=True, seed=0, levels=1).storeys[0] adj = layout._neighbours(plan) halls = {i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if r.kind in layout.CIRCULATION} classrooms = [i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "classroom"] self.assertTrue(classrooms) self.assertGreaterEqual(sum(bool(set(adj[i]) & halls) for i in classrooms) * 2, len(classrooms)) def test_shop_floors_keep_a_compact_bathroom(self): for kind in ("shop", "restaurant", "retail"): with self.subTest(kind=kind): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind=kind, commercial=True, seed=0, street="S").storeys[0] self.assertLessEqual(min(r.area for r in plan.rooms if r.kind == "bathroom"), 20) def test_special_purpose_floors_keep_their_primary_space(self): for kind, primary in (("barn", "warehouse"), ("shed", "shed"), ("garage", "garage"), ("mall", "concourse")): with self.subTest(kind=kind): plan = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind=kind, commercial=True, seed=0, street="S").storeys[0] self.assertIn(primary, {r.kind for r in plan.rooms}) if kind == "garage": self.assertEqual(len(plan.rooms), 1)

nodes.body_text: class CleanRoadRuns(unittest.TestCase): def road(self,number,points): return osm.OSMFeature(number,'way',{'highway':'residential'},[(y,x) for x,y in points]) def straighten(self,roads): projection=SimpleNamespace(width=400,height=400,to_px=lambda lat,lon:(lon,lat), to_latlon=lambda x,y:(y,x)) octilinear.straighten_roads(roads,projection,osm.classify,renderer._is_polygon) return [[(x,y) for y,x in r.geometry] for r in roads] def test_small_sideways_kink_becomes_one_straight_run(self): road=self.road(1,[(10,50),(110,50),(120,60),(230,60)]) points=self.straighten([road])[0] self.assertEqual(len(points),2,points) self.assertEqual(points[0][1],points[1][1]) def test_short_bevel_becomes_square_corner_and_branch_stays_connected(self): main=self.road(1,[(10,50),(110,50),(120,60),(120,200)]) side=self.road(2,[(120,60),(230,60)]) main_points,side_points=self.straighten([main,side]) for a,b in zip(main_points,main_points[1:]): self.assertTrue(a[0]==b[0] or a[1]==b[1],main_points) self.assertLess(Point(side_points[0]).distance(LineString(main_points)),1e-8) def test_major_diagonal_is_retained(self): road=self.road(1,[(10,50),(110,50),(180,120),(300,120)]) points=self.straighten([road])[0] self.assertTrue(any(abs(a[0]-b[0])>30 and abs(a[1]-b[1])>30 for a,b in zip(points,points[1:])),points) def test_all_native_rail_markers_clear_vegetation_but_keep_adjacent_grass(self): import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from generator.rail_tiles import RAIL_RULES from generator.rendering.vegetation import _clear_road_vegetation colours = [colour for _, colour, _ in RAIL_RULES] + [C.DARK_GRASS] ground = Image.fromarray(np.array([colours], dtype=np.uint8)) vegetation = Image.new("RGB", ground.size, (0, 255, 0)) _clear_road_vegetation(vegetation, ground) result = np.array(vegetation) self.assertTrue(np.all(result[0, :-1] == C.VEG_NOTHING)) self.assertEqual(tuple(result[0, -1]), (0, 255, 0)) def test_shared_junctions_move_within_the_existing_cap(self): roads=[self.road(1,[(10,50),(110,55),(230,60)]), self.road(2,[(110,55),(113,180)]), self.road(3,[(10,180),(113,180),(230,185)])] before=[(r.geometry[0],r.geometry[-1]) for r in roads] self.straighten(roads) for r,ends in zip(roads,before): for a,b in zip(ends,(r.geometry[0],r.geometry[-1])): self.assertLessEqual(math.dist(a,b),octilinear.MAX_MOVE_TILES) self.assertLess(Point(roads[1].geometry[0]).distance(LineString(roads[0].geometry)),1e-8) self.assertLess(Point(roads[1].geometry[-1]).distance(LineString(roads[2].geometry)),1e-8) def test_vertical_to_diagonal_corner_has_no_mid_diagonal_shift(self): # North-south road bending 45 degrees into a diagonal road with an # intermediate node must stay on one exact diagonal without a 1-tile step. road = self.road(1, [(100, 20), (100, 80), (130, 111), (160, 141)]) projection = SimpleNamespace(width=400, height=400, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat), to_latlon=lambda x, y: (y, x)) octilinear.straighten_roads([road], projection, osm.classify, renderer._is_polygon, clean=True) points = [(x, y) for y, x in road.geometry] self.assertEqual(len(points), 3, points) (x0, y0), (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = points self.assertEqual(x0, x1) self.assertEqual(abs(x2 - x1), abs(y2 - y1))

nodes.body_text: """A worker that dies in native code must not lose the whole compile. concurrent.futures.BrokenProcessPool was raised out of the row pool and ended the run: with an access violation in one worker (0xC0000005 on Windows) the map could not be compiled at all, and the rows already paid for were only kept if the caller passed resume=True. The rows a broken pool leaves unfinished are now made again one at a time. """ import os import tempfile import unittest from concurrent import futures from unittest import mock from tools import map_source if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: class BrokenPool(unittest.TestCase): def test_the_rows_a_broken_pool_lost_are_made_one_at_a_time(self): made = [] def row(project, out, cy, band, placed, seed, seams, size): made.append(cy) return 1 with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp, \ mock.patch.object(map_source.bitmaps, "_bmp_header", return_value=(600, 600)), \ mock.patch.object(map_source, "project_origin", return_value=(0, 0)), \ mock.patch.object(map_source, "read_lots", return_value=[]), \ mock.patch.object(map_source, "read_buildings", return_value=[]), \ mock.patch.object(map_source, "_row", row), \ mock.patch.object(futures, "ProcessPoolExecutor", _Pool), \ mock.patch.object(map_source, "_gather", side_effect=futures.process.BrokenProcessPool("worker died")): written = map_source.make_map_source(tmp, os.path.join(tmp, "src"), workers=2) self.assertGreater(len(made), 1, "the pool path was taken") self.assertEqual(written, len(made)) self.assertEqual(sorted(made), list(range(len(made))), "every row was made once")

nodes.name: BothCompilersPrepareTheOutput
nodes.body_text: class BothCompilersPrepareTheOutput(unittest.TestCase): """The folders, the repairs and the leftover lots, from one place. Each backend used to do this itself, so pruning the lots a map left behind - the fix for install refusing a map as "moved since it was last compiled" - landed on the WorldEd path only, and knoxlots went on compiling over them. """ class Prepared(Exception): """Raised where the compile would have started.""" def project(self, folder: str) -> Path: project = Path(folder) / "town" project.mkdir() (project / "town.pzw").write_text( '<world version="1.0" width="30" height="30">' '<worldOrigin origin="70,0"/></world>', encoding="utf-8") return project def prepared_flags(self, run) -> list: seen = [] def prepare(*args, **kwargs): seen.append(kwargs.get("knoxlots")) raise self.Prepared with mock.patch.object(compile_map, "prepare_output", side_effect=prepare): with self.assertRaises(self.Prepared): run() return seen def test_knoxlots_prepares_the_output_too(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: project = self.project(folder) with mock.patch.object(compile_map, "knoxlots_exe", return_value=Path("knoxlots")), \ mock.patch.object(compile_map, "ensure_rail_rules"): seen = self.prepared_flags(lambda: compile_map.compile_rust(str(project))) self.assertEqual(seen, [True]) def test_worlded_prepares_the_output(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: project = self.project(folder) exe = Path(folder) / "PZWorldEd_cli.exe" exe.write_bytes(b"") seen = self.prepared_flags( lambda: compile_map.compile_map(str(project), exe=str(exe), backend="worlded")) self.assertEqual(seen, [False])

tracks[1][0][1]), 5) seen = set() for track in tracks: for ox, oy, index in rail_sections(track): self.assertEqual(index, 0) for x, y, sheet, tile in ASSEMBLIES[index][4]: pos = (ox + x, oy + y) self.assertNotIn(pos, seen) seen.add(pos) def test_major_turn_is_kept_as_a_single_corner(self): tracks = list(continuous_tracks([[(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 80)]])) self.assertEqual(len(tracks), 1) self.assertEqual(len(tracks[0]), 3) sections = list(rail_sections(tracks[0])) self.assertTrue(any(index >= 4 for x, y, index in sections)) self.assertLessEqual(sum(index >= 4 for x, y, index in sections), 4) def test_fragment_order_and_direction_do_not_change_two_track_geometry(self): rings = [[(0, 0), (50, 5)], [(50, 5), (100, 10)], [(0, 5), (100, 15)]] first = sorted(tuple(t) for t in continuous_tracks(rings)) second = sorted(tuple(t) for t in continuous_tracks([list(reversed(r)) for r in reversed(rings)])) self.assertEqual(first, second) def test_buildings_keep_off_rail_even_in_industrial_yards(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: colours = [colour for label, colour, tile in RAIL_RULES] ground = np.array([colours + [C.DIRT] * 3], dtype=np.uint8) Image.fromarray(ground).save(Path(folder) / 'map_ground_base.bmp') areas = mock.Mock() areas.mask.return_value = np.ones(ground.shape[:2], dtype=bool) weight = _road_weight(folder, 'map', SimpleNamespace(width=ground.shape[1], height=1), areas=areas) self.assertTrue(np.all(weight[0, :-3] >= 2)) self.assertGreaterEqual(weight[0, -3], 2) self.assertEqual(weight[0, -1], 0)

nodes.name: test_dense_blocks.py
nodes.body_text: """Which city blocks get paved wall to wall (generator/rendering/roads.py). A paved block is a slab of pale concrete, so the two things that keep it from swallowing open country are how built-up a block has to be and how big a block may be. Both are exercised here on synthetic streets, through the real function rather than a copy of its arithmetic. """ import unittest from types import SimpleNamespace from PIL import Image from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.pz_colors import MEDIUM_GRASS, PALE_CONCRETE from generator.rendering import roads W = H = 900 if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: proj
nodes.signature: def proj(): # Geometry is written as (y, x) tile pairs, so projects straight through.
nodes.body_text: def proj(): # Geometry is written as (y, x) tile pairs, so projects straight through. return SimpleNamespace(width=W, height=H, meters_per_tile=1.0, to_px=lambda la, lo: (lo, la))

nodes.name: street
nodes.body_text: def street(ring): return OSMFeature(osm_id=1, kind="way", tags={"highway": "residential"}, geometry=[(y, x) for x, y in ring])

nodes.name: building
nodes.body_text: def building(x, y, w, h): ring = [(x, y), (x + w, y), (x + w, y + h), (x, y + h), (x, y)] return OSMFeature(osm_id=2, kind="way", tags={"building": "yes"}, geometry=[(yy, xx) for xx, yy in ring])

nodes.name: square
nodes.body_text: def square(x0, y0, x1, y1): return [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1), (x0, y0)]

nodes.name: paved_fraction
nodes.body_text: def paved_fraction(im, box): a = im.crop(box).convert("RGB") px = a.load() hit = sum(1 for x in range(a.width) for y in range(a.height) if px[x, y] == PALE_CONCRETE) return hit / (a.width * a.height)

nodes.name: run
nodes.body_text: def run(blocks, houses): landscape = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), MEDIUM_GRASS) buckets = {"road_minor": [street(ring) for ring in blocks]} roads._pave_dense_ground(landscape, houses, buckets, proj()) return landscape

nodes.body_text: class DenseBlocks(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_dense_block_is_paved(self): # Two streets make one block, and two thirds of it is under buildings. im = run([square(100, 100, 300, 100), square(300, 100, 300, 300), square(300, 300, 100, 300), square(100, 300, 100, 100)], [building(110, 110, 160, 160)]) self.assertGreater(paved_fraction(im, (110, 110, 290, 290)), 0.5) def test_an_ordinary_street_is_left_alone(self): # A third under buildings: a suburb, a village high street. It cleared # the old 0.28 line and got paved; the downtown line leaves it grass. im = run([square(100, 100, 300, 100), square(300, 100, 300, 300), square(300, 300, 100, 300), square(100, 300, 100, 100)], [building(130, 130, 115, 115)]) self.assertEqual(paved_fraction(im, (110, 110, 290, 290)), 0.0) def test_a_block_the_size_of_a_field_is_never_paved(self): # 500 x 500: a farm and a works clear the coverage line, and paving # the whole thing is the concrete field the map grew instead of trees. im = run([square(50, 50, 600, 50), square(600, 50, 600, 600), square(600, 600, 50, 600), square(50, 600, 50, 50)], [building(100, 100, 300, 250), building(150, 400, 250, 150)]) self.assertEqual(paved_fraction(im, (60, 60, 590, 590)), 0.0)

nodes.name: test_design.py
nodes.body_text: """The drawing board's sheet: metres on a blank page, into a real map. The sheet is the one place in KnoxMap where somebody says how big a map is in metres and expects that many metres. Everything else rounds up to whole 300-tile cells, which turns a small error into a large one: a 900 m sheet measured as 900.04 m is four cells across instead of three, a third more map from four centimetres. So the size is checked against the same question the renderer asks, not against the arithmetic that produced it. """ import math import unittest from generator import sketch if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: cells
nodes.body_text: def cells(metres: float) -> int: return max(300, math.ceil(metres / 300) * 300)

nodes.name: sheet
nodes.signature: def sheet(width=900, height=900, lat=0.0, lon=0.0, features=None)
nodes.body_text: def sheet(width=900, height=900, lat=0.0, lon=0.0, features=None): return {"width_m": width, "height_m": height, "anchor": {"lat": lat, "lon": lon}, "features": features or []}

nodes.name: SheetSize
nodes.body_text: class SheetSize(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_sheet_is_the_size_it_says(self): for width, height, lat in ((900, 900, 0.0), (900, 700, 42.0), (1500, 1200, 60.0), (300, 300, -35.0), (2400, 600, 12.0)): with self.subTest(width=width, height=height, lat=lat): box = sketch.design_bbox(sheet(width, height, lat)) got_w, got_h = sketch._utm_extent(*box) self.assertAlmostEqual(got_w, width, delta=0.3) self.assertAlmostEqual(got_h, height, delta=0.3) def test_it_never_measures_over_and_so_never_costs_a_whole_cell(self): # The one that matters: at or just over a 300 m boundary. for size in (300, 600, 900, 1200, 3000): for lat in (0.0, 42.0, -35.0, 60.0): with self.subTest(size=size, lat=lat): box = sketch.design_bbox(sheet(size, size, lat)) got_w, got_h = sketch._utm_extent(*box) self.assertLessEqual(got_w, size) self.assertLessEqual(got_h, size) self.assertEqual(cells(got_w), size) self.assertEqual(cells(got_h), size) def test_a_silly_size_is_brought_into_range(self): for asked in (0, -5, 10, 1e9, None, "big"): with self.subTest(asked=asked): w, h = sketch._sheet_size({"width_m": asked, "height_m": asked}) self.assertGreaterEqual(w, sketch.MIN_SHEET_M) self.assertLessEqual(w, sketch.MAX_SHEET_M) self.assertGreaterEqual(h, sketch.MIN_SHEET_M) def test_a_sheet_with_no_corner_still_lands_somewhere(self): south, west, north, east = sketch.design_bbox({"width_m": 500, "height_m": 500}) self.assertEqual((south, west), (0.0, 0.0)) self.assertGreater(north, south) self.assertGreater(east, west) def test_a_corner_off_the_world_is_not_used(self): for bad in ({"lat": 95.0, "lon": 0.0}, {"lat": 0.0, "lon": 400.0}, {"lat": "x", "lon": 0.0}, {}): with self.subTest(bad=bad): self.assertEqual(sketch._anchor({"anchor": bad}), (0.0, 0.0))

nodes.name: test_designer.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings drawn by hand in the window (knoxbuild/designer.py). A design is rectangles somebody dragged on a sheet, which is not what the rest of the pipeline can build from: rooms there are rectangles that do not overlap. So what is worth checking is that whatever is drawn comes out as rooms that really do not overlap, that the building made from it is a building the game can load - walls, doors, a way in, furniture - and that saving one keeps both the .tbx and the drawing it came from. """ import os import tempfile import unittest from knoxbuild import designer as D from knoxbuild import presets as P if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: covered
nodes.body_text: def covered(design, level=0): """Every tile a room of this storey covers, with how many rooms cover it.""" seen = {} for r in design["rooms"]: if r["level"] != level: continue for y in range(r["y"], r["y"] + r["h"]): for x in range(r["x"], r["x"] + r["w"]): seen[(x, y)] = seen.get((x, y), 0) + 1 return seen

nodes.body_text: class TheSheet(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_blank_sheet_has_nothing_on_it(self): design = D.blank("police", 24, 18) self.assertEqual((design["width"], design["height"]), (24, 18)) self.assertEqual(design["rooms"], []) self.assertEqual(design["kind"], "police") def test_a_sheet_is_kept_to_a_size_a_building_can_be(self): self.assertEqual(D.clean({"width": 2, "height": 9999})["width"], D.MIN_SIDE) self.assertEqual(D.clean({"width": 2, "height": 9999})["height"], D.MAX_SIDE) self.assertEqual(D.clean({"storeys": 99})["storeys"], D.MAX_STOREYS) def test_nonsense_is_a_blank_sheet_rather_than_an_error(self): for bad in (None, "hello", 7, [], {"rooms": "nope"}, {"rooms": [None, 3, {"x": "left"}]}): with self.subTest(bad=bad): design = D.clean(bad) self.assertGreaterEqual(design["width"], D.MIN_SIDE) self.assertIsInstance(design["rooms"], list) def test_a_room_that_is_not_a_room_the_game_knows_is_not_drawn(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 5, 5, "sauna")]}) self.assertEqual(design["rooms"], []) def test_a_kind_of_building_the_generator_does_not_know_is_any_building(self): self.assertEqual(D.clean({"kind": "spaceport"})["kind"], "") def test_a_room_is_kept_inside_the_sheet(self): design = D.clean({"width": 10, "height": 10, "rooms": [room(8, 8, 40, 40, "office")]}) self.assertEqual(design["rooms"][0], room(8, 8, 2, 2, "office")) def test_a_design_rebuilt_from_its_own_output_is_the_same_design(self): # The window sends back what it was given, so cleaning has to settle. once = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 16, "kind": "police", "seed": 5, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 8, "policeoffice"), room(5, 4, 10, 8, "policelocker")]}) self.assertEqual(D.clean(once), once)

nodes.body_text: class DrawingOverWhatIsThere(unittest.TestCase): def test_the_newest_room_wins_and_the_old_one_keeps_the_rest(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 10, "office"), room(5, 5, 10, 10, "storage")]}) # Nothing is covered twice, and everything drawn is still covered. self.assertTrue(all(n == 1 for n in covered(design).values())) self.assertEqual(len(covered(design)), 10 * 10 + 10 * 10 - 5 * 5) at = {(x, y): r["kind"] for r in design["rooms"] for y in range(r["y"], r["y"] + r["h"]) for x in range(r["x"], r["x"] + r["w"])} self.assertEqual(at[(7, 7)], "storage") # the newer one self.assertEqual(at[(1, 1)], "office") # what is left of the older def test_a_room_drawn_right_over_another_replaces_it(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(2, 2, 6, 6, "office"), room(2, 2, 6, 6, "kitchen")]}) self.assertEqual([r["kind"] for r in design["rooms"]], ["kitchen"]) def test_a_room_with_no_kind_is_the_eraser(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 10, "office"), room(0, 0, 4, 10, "")]}) self.assertEqual(len(covered(design)), 6 * 10) self.assertNotIn((1, 1), covered(design)) def test_erasing_the_middle_leaves_the_ring_round_it(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 9, 9, "office"), room(3, 3, 3, 3, "")]}) self.assertEqual(len(covered(design)), 9 * 9 - 9) self.assertTrue(all(n == 1 for n in covered(design).values())) def test_a_storey_is_drawn_without_cutting_the_one_below(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "storeys": 2, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 10, "office", level=0), room(0, 0, 10, 10, "bedroom", level=1)]}) self.assertEqual(len(covered(design, 0)), 100) self.assertEqual(len(covered(design, 1)), 100) def test_a_room_drawn_on_a_storey_that_is_not_there_lands_on_the_ground(self): design = D.clean({"width": 20, "height": 20, "storeys": 1, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 4, 4, "office", level=5)]}) self.assertEqual(design["rooms"][0]["level"], 0)
