nodes.name: WhatGetsBuilt
nodes.body_text: class WhatGetsBuilt(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.design = D.clean( {"kind": "police", "width": 20, "height": 14, "seed": 11, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 7, "policeoffice"), room(10, 0, 10, 7, "policelocker"), room(0, 7, 20, 7, "policehall")]}) def test_the_rooms_drawn_are_the_rooms_built(self): built = D.stack(self.design) self.assertEqual(len(built.storeys), 1) kinds = {r.kind for r in built.storeys[0].rooms} self.assertEqual(kinds, {"policeoffice", "policelocker", "policehall"}) def test_the_generator_puts_in_the_walls_doors_windows_and_furniture(self): storey = D.stack(self.design).storeys[0] self.assertTrue(storey.doors, "no doorways between the rooms") self.assertTrue(storey.windows, "no windows in the facade") self.assertTrue(storey.furniture, "nothing in the rooms") def test_there_is_a_way_in_from_outside(self): # A hand-built building with no exterior door is a sealed box. storey = D.stack(self.design).storeys[0] grid = storey.grid outside = [] for x, y, d in storey.doors: near = grid[y][x] if 0 <= y < len(grid) and 0 <= x < len(grid[0]) else 0 far = (grid[y][x - 1] if d == "W" and x else grid[y - 1][x] if d == "N" and y else 0) if not near or not far: outside.append((x, y, d)) self.assertTrue(outside, "nothing opens onto the street") def test_what_was_not_drawn_is_not_part_of_the_building(self): # The footprint is what was painted, so an L-shaped building is drawn # by leaving the corner empty rather than by masking it off. design = D.clean({"kind": "house", "width": 20, "height": 20, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 10, 20, "livingroom"), room(10, 0, 10, 10, "kitchen")]}) grid = D.stack(design).storeys[0].grid self.assertEqual(grid[15][15], 0) # the empty corner self.assertNotEqual(grid[5][5], 0) def test_an_empty_sheet_builds_nothing_rather_than_raising(self): built = D.stack(D.blank("house", 10, 10)) self.assertEqual(built.rooms, []) def test_a_single_tile_room_does_not_stop_the_build(self): design = D.clean({"kind": "house", "width": 12, "height": 12, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 12, 12, "livingroom"), room(5, 5, 1, 1, "closet")]}) self.assertTrue(D.stack(design).storeys[0].furniture) def test_two_storeys_get_one_staircase_in_the_same_place(self): design = dict(self.design, storeys=2) design["rooms"] = design["rooms"] + [ dict(r, level=1) for r in self.design["rooms"]] built = D.stack(D.clean(design)) self.assertEqual(len(built.storeys), 2) self.assertEqual(len(built.stairs), 1) cores = [[r for r in s.rooms if r.is_core] for s in built.storeys] self.assertTrue(all(len(c) == 1 for c in cores)) self.assertEqual({(c[0].x0, c[0].y0, c[0].x1, c[0].y1) for c in cores} .__len__(), 1) def test_the_same_design_builds_the_same_building_every_time(self): first = D.tbx_text(self.design, "Station") again = D.tbx_text(self.design, "Station") self.assertEqual(first, again) def test_a_building_of_a_drawn_design_is_a_building_file(self): about = P.measure(D.tbx_text(self.design, "Station")) self.assertEqual((about["width"], about["height"]), (20, 14)) self.assertEqual(about["storeys"], 1) self.assertGreaterEqual(about["rooms"], 3) def test_a_design_names_the_walls_it_is_built_in(self): name = D.style_choices("police")[0] style = D.style_for(dict(self.design, style=name)) self.assertTrue(style.get("exterior")) # A style the catalogue has nothing for is not an error: the building # keeps whatever its kind would have been built in. self.assertTrue(D.style_for(dict(self.design, style="marzipan")))

nodes.body_text: class ThePicture(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_storey_is_drawn_at_a_size_the_window_can_show(self): design = D.autofill(D.blank("house", 20, 16)) img = D.preview(design) px = D.scale_for(design) self.assertEqual(img.size, (20 * px + 1, 16 * px + 1)) def test_a_big_building_is_drawn_smaller_rather_than_enormous(self): self.assertLessEqual(D.scale_for(D.blank("civic", 150, 150)) * 150, 820) def test_a_room_is_the_same_colour_in_every_picture(self): self.assertEqual(D.room_colour("kitchen"), D.room_colour("kitchen")) self.assertNotEqual(D.room_colour("kitchen"), D.room_colour("bedroom")) def test_an_empty_sheet_is_still_a_picture(self): self.assertTrue(D.preview(D.blank("house", 10, 10)).size) def test_and_it_has_the_grid_on_it_before_anything_is_drawn(self): # Asked for in #suggestions: the grid only turned up under a room # once one was drawn, and the moment it is worth seeing is while you # are deciding how big to make one. px = D.scale_for(D.blank("house", 10, 10)) picture = D.preview(D.blank("house", 10, 10)).convert("RGB") self.assertEqual(picture.getpixel((0, 0)), D.EMPTY_GRID_FIFTH) self.assertEqual(picture.getpixel((px, px // 2)), D.EMPTY_GRID) self.assertEqual(picture.getpixel((px // 2, px // 2)), D.OUTSIDE) def test_the_grid_is_still_there_round_what_is_drawn(self): design = D.clean({"width": 12, "height": 12, "storeys": 1, "rooms": [{"kind": "livingroom", "level": 0, "x": 1, "y": 1, "w": 5, "h": 5}]}) px = D.scale_for(design) picture = D.preview(design).convert("RGB") # Well clear of the room, on a line of the grid. self.assertIn(picture.getpixel((10 * px, 10 * px + px // 2)), (D.EMPTY_GRID, D.EMPTY_GRID_FIFTH)) def test_asking_for_a_storey_that_is_not_there_gives_the_top_one(self): design = D.autofill(D.blank("house", 16, 12)) self.assertEqual(D.preview(design, 9).size, D.preview(design, 0).size) def test_an_ordinary_building_is_drawn_whole(self): # nodes.body_text: class Keeping(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.design = D.clean( {"kind": "police", "width": 18, "height": 12, "rooms": [room(0, 0, 18, 12, "policeoffice")]}) def test_saving_one_keeps_the_building_and_the_drawing(self): about = D.keep(self.dir, "Oak Street Station", self.design) self.assertEqual(about["kind"], "police") self.assertEqual(P.read(self.dir, "Oak Street Station"), D.tbx_text(self.design, "Oak Street Station")) again = D.load_design(self.dir, "Oak Street Station") self.assertEqual(again["rooms"], self.design["rooms"]) def test_a_saved_one_is_offered_as_a_preset_of_its_kind(self): D.keep(self.dir, "Oak Street Station", self.design) entry = P.library(self.dir)[0] self.assertEqual((entry["name"], entry["kind"]), ("Oak Street Station", "police")) self.assertTrue(entry["editable"], "the drawing cannot be opened again") def test_an_empty_sheet_cannot_be_saved(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): D.keep(self.dir, "Nothing", D.blank("house", 10, 10)) def test_a_preset_needs_a_name(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): D.keep(self.dir, " ", self.design) def test_throwing_the_preset_away_throws_the_drawing_away_too(self): D.keep(self.dir, "Gone", self.design) self.assertTrue(P.remove(self.dir, "Gone")) self.assertIsNone(D.load_design(self.dir, "Gone")) self.assertEqual(P.library(self.dir), []) def test_a_drawing_that_is_not_there_is_nothing_rather_than_an_error(self): self.assertIsNone(D.load_design(self.dir, "never existed")) def test_a_name_that_could_escape_the_folder_cannot(self): path = D.design_path(self.dir, "../../etc/passwd") self.assertEqual(os.path.dirname(path), P.folder(self.dir))

nodes.name: TheStaircaseInADrawnBuilding
nodes.body_text: class TheStaircaseInADrawnBuilding(unittest.TestCase): """A building drawn by hand needs its stairs somewhere, and the generator put them in the middle of the floor - which over a drawing means in the middle of a drawn room. A 6x6 room on two storeys came back as two rooms, and a smaller one came back as the staircase and nothing else.""" def built(self, w, h, storeys, sheet=22): design = D.clean({"width": sheet, "height": sheet, "storeys": storeys, "rooms": [room(1, 1, w, h, "livingroom", level) for level in range(storeys)]}) return D.stack(design) def test_a_room_is_not_cut_in_two_by_the_stairs_when_it_need_not_be(self): for w, h in ((7, 7), (10, 10), (20, 16)): with self.subTest(size=(w, h)): rooms = self.built(w, h, 2).storeys[0].rooms living = [r for r in rooms if r.kind == "livingroom"] self.assertEqual(len(living), 1, "the drawn room came back in pieces") # And the shaft is at the edge of it, not through the middle. shaft = [r for r in rooms if r.is_core][0] self.assertTrue(shaft.x0 == 1 or shaft.y0 == 1 or shaft.x1 == w or shaft.y1 == h) def test_a_drawing_with_no_room_for_stairs_is_one_storey(self): # 5x6 is wider than the shaft and not wide enough to keep a room # beside it, so asking for two storeys used to come back as a # staircase where the room had been. built = self.built(5, 6, 2) self.assertEqual(len(built.storeys), 1) self.assertEqual([r.kind for r in built.storeys[0].rooms], ["livingroom"]) def test_one_storey_is_never_touched(self): rooms = self.built(6, 6, 1).storeys[0].rooms self.assertEqual([(r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1, r.kind) for r in rooms], [(1, 1, 6, 6, "livingroom")])

nodes.name: RoomsDrawnAreRoomsKept
nodes.body_text: class RoomsDrawnAreRoomsKept(unittest.TestCase): """The layout folds anything thin or ragged into the room beside it, because the plans it cuts out of a slanted footprint are full of wedges that are not rooms. Over a drawing there are no wedges, only what somebody drew: a room drawn across part of another left the rest of that one as a strip, and the strip was quietly given to the new room under a name nobody picked.""" def built(self, *drawn, sheet=(24, 20)): design = D.clean({"width": sheet[0], "height": sheet[1], "storeys": 1, "rooms": list(drawn)}) return design, D.stack(design) def kinds_of(self, built): return {r.kind for r in built.storeys[0].rooms if not r.is_core} def test_what_is_left_of_a_room_drawn_over_keeps_its_own_name(self): # A dining room, then a laundry across the middle of it: what is left # of the dining room is two strips two tiles thick, and both used to # come back as laundry. design, built = self.built(room(2, 2, 10, 9, "dining"), room(4, 2, 6, 9, "laundry")) self.assertIn("dining", self.kinds_of(built)) self.assertIn("laundry", self.kinds_of(built)) def test_a_corridor_two_tiles_thick_is_a_corridor(self): design, built = self.built(room(2, 2, 10, 8, "livingroom"), room(2, 10, 10, 2, "hall")) self.assertIn("hall", self.kinds_of(built)) def test_a_hallway_stays_a_hallway_and_can_be_walked_down(self): # The one that is felt rather than seen: a hall folded into the living # room beside it is furnished as a living room, so a sofa and a # bookshelf end up standing in the hallway and the rooms beyond it are # behind them. from collections import deque from knoxbuild import layout as L design, built = self.built(room(0, 0, 12, 4, "livingroom"), room(0, 4, 10, 2, "hall"), room(0, 6, 6, 5, "bedroom"), room(6, 6, 6, 5, "kitchen"), sheet=(12, 11)) storey = built.storeys[0] halls = [i for i, r in enumerate(storey.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "hall"] self.assertTrue(halls, "the hallway was swallowed by the room beside it") blocked = set() for role, fx, fy, orient in storey.furniture: if L._blocks(role): blocked.update(L._tiles_under(role, fx, fy, orient)) free = [(x, y) for y in range(storey.height) for x in range(storey.width) if storey.grid[y][x] == halls[0] and (x, y) not in blocked] self.assertTrue(free, "every tile of the hallway has something on it") seen, queue = {free[0]}, deque(free[:1]) while queue: x, y = queue.popleft() for step in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if step in free and step not in seen: seen.add(step) queue.append(step) self.assertEqual(len(seen), len(free), "the hallway is blocked across") def test_a_crumb_of_three_tiles_is_still_not_a_room(self): # Nothing can stand in it and the game would have a room with no way # in; it goes to the room it borders, as it always did. design, built = self.built(room(2, 2, 10, 8, "livingroom"), room(2, 10, 3, 1, "closet")) self.assertNotIn("closet", self.kinds_of(built)) def test_nothing_drawn_is_lost_however_the_drawing_is_built_up(self): import random kinds = ["livingroom", "kitchen", "bedroom", "bathroom", "hall", "dining", "office", "storage"] rng = random.Random(11) for trial in range(12): design = D.clean({"width": 30, "height": 24, "storeys": 1, "rooms": []}) for step in range(10): design["rooms"].append(room(rng.randrange(20), rng.randrange(16), rng.randint(4, 9), rng.randint(4, 9), kinds[step % len(kinds)])) design = D.clean(design) built = D.stack(design) made = self.kinds_of(built) for r in design["rooms"]: # Every piece big enough to be a room is still that room. if r["w"] * r["h"] >= 4 and min(r["w"], r["h"]) >= 2: self.assertIn(r["kind"], made, f"trial {trial} step {step}: {r} went missing")

nodes.name: test_district_grid_angle.py
nodes.body_text: """Per-district street grid rotation (renderer.dominant_road_angle). Run from the KnoxMap folder: python -m unittest discover tests No network: the streets are synthesised here. The two-district case is the measured failure this feature fixes: a town that grew in two phases (one grid over here, another over there) used to be turned by the *average* of the two - an angle that straightens neither district, so both kept their staircases. Now the district holding the most street picks the turn; the losing grid keeps its offset and "Knox County roads" bends it. """ import math import os import sys import unittest sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) from generator import renderer # noqa: E402 from generator.osm import OSMFeature # noqa: E402 # A town near 40N, about 600 m square - the box tools/selftest.py draws. SOUTH, WEST = 40.0000, 20.0000 NORTH, EAST = 40.0054, 20.0070 CX = CY = 300.0 # town centre, metres from the SW corner _ids = iter(range(1, 10 ** 6)) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: ll
nodes.signature: def ll(x_m: float, y_m: float, deg: float = 0.0) -> tuple[float, float]
nodes.body_text: def ll(x_m: float, y_m: float, deg: float = 0.0) -> tuple[float, float]: """Metres east/north of the SW corner, turned by deg about the town centre, to (lat, lon).""" a = math.radians(deg) dx, dy = x_m - CX, y_m - CY rx = CX + dx * math.cos(a) - dy * math.sin(a) ry = CY + dx * math.sin(a) + dy * math.cos(a) return (SOUTH + ry / 111320.0, WEST + rx / (111320.0 * math.cos(math.radians(SOUTH))))

nodes.name: seg
nodes.signature: def seg(x0: float, y0: float, x1: float, y1: float, deg: float = 0.0) -> OSMFeature
nodes.body_text: def seg(x0: float, y0: float, x1: float, y1: float, deg: float = 0.0) -> OSMFeature: """One street: ends in metres, optionally turned by deg about the centre.""" return OSMFeature(next(_ids), "way", {"highway": "residential"}, [ll(x0, y0, deg), ll(x1, y1, deg)])

nodes.name: grid
nodes.signature: def grid(deg: float, spacing: int = 80, half: int = 280) -> list[OSMFeature]
nodes.body_text: def grid(deg: float, spacing: int = 80, half: int = 280) -> list[OSMFeature]: """A whole town on one grid at `deg`, streets every `spacing` metres.""" a = math.radians(deg) ax, ay = math.cos(a), math.sin(a) # along a street px, py = -math.sin(a), math.cos(a) # across the streets out = [] for k in range(-half, half + 1, spacing): # Street running along the grid at cross-offset k... out.append(seg(CX + k * px - half * ax, CY + k * py - half * ay, CX + k * px + half * ax, CY + k * py + half * ay)) # ...and the cross street at along-offset k. out.append(seg(CX - half * px + k * ax, CY - half * py + k * ay, CX + half * px + k * ax, CY + half * py + k * ay)) return out

nodes.name: district_a
nodes.body_text: def district_a() -> list[OSMFeature]: """The west half of town: an axis-aligned grid (0 degrees), the larger phase - 2880 m of east-west streets plus 2080 m of north-south.""" out = [] y = 60 while y <= 540: out.append(seg(40, y, 360, y)) y += 60 # North-south streets stop well left of x=250: the projector fits the # 600 m box into a wider tile canvas with a margin, so metre x is not # tile x - streets near the district edge measured across into the # east cells and their mixed votes muddied both districts. x = 50 while x <= 230: out.append(seg(x, 40, x, 560)) x += 60 return out

nodes.name: district_b
nodes.body_text: def district_b() -> list[OSMFeature]: """The east half: a 30-degree grid, the smaller phase (2400 m).""" a = math.radians(30) ax, ay = math.cos(a), math.sin(a) px, py = -math.sin(a), math.cos(a) cx, cy = 500.0, 300.0 out = [] for u in (-80, -40, 0, 40, 80): # streets running at 30 degrees out.append(seg(cx + u * px - 160 * ax, cy + u * py - 160 * ay, cx + u * px + 160 * ax, cy + u * py + 160 * ay)) for v in (-160, -80, 0, 80, 160): # the cross streets at 120 out.append(seg(cx - 80 * px + v * ax, cy - 80 * py + v * ay, cx + 80 * px + v * ax, cy + 80 * py + v * ay)) return out

nodes.body_text: class Uniform(unittest.TestCase): def test_finds_the_single_grid(self): angle, strength = renderer.dominant_road_angle( grid(30), SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST) self.assertLess(abs(abs(angle) - 30), 2) self.assertGreater(strength, 0.8) def test_flat_grid_reads_zero(self): angle, strength = renderer.dominant_road_angle( grid(0), SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST) self.assertLess(abs(angle), 1) self.assertGreater(strength, 0.8)

nodes.body_text: class TwoDistricts(unittest.TestCase): def test_dominant_district_wins_not_the_average(self): # Averaging the two phases lands near -6.5 degrees - straightens # neither grid. The larger district's own angle must win instead. angle, strength = renderer.dominant_road_angle( district_a() + district_b(), SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST) self.assertLess(abs(angle), 2, f"snapped to the dominant grid, got {angle:.2f}") self.assertGreater(strength, 0.6) def test_smaller_phase_alone_still_found(self): # The losing district is measured correctly when it is all there is. angle, strength = renderer.dominant_road_angle( district_b(), SOUTH, WEST, NORTH, EAST) self.assertLess(abs(abs(angle) - 30), 2) self.assertGreater(strength, 0.8)

nodes.name: test_edits.py
nodes.body_text: """Editing the features a map was built from. The download stays the download and the changes are kept beside it, so the things worth checking are that a change really reaches the features, that it cannot reach anything it should not, and that the original is left alone - a map whose cached download has been quietly rewritten cannot be un-edited. """ import unittest from generator import edits from generator.osm import OSMFeature, classify HOUSE = [(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.001), (0.001, 0.001), (0.001, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0)] ROAD = [(0.0, 0.0), (0.002, 0.002)] if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: town
nodes.body_text: def town(): return [ OSMFeature(1, "way", {"building": "house"}, list(HOUSE)), OSMFeature(2, "way", {"highway": "residential"}, list(ROAD)), OSMFeature(3, "way", {"natural": "wood"}, list(HOUSE)), ]

nodes.name: Cleaning
nodes.body_text: class Cleaning(unittest.TestCase): def test_nothing_is_an_empty_edit_list(self): self.assertEqual(edits.clean(None), edits.empty()) self.assertEqual(edits.count(edits.empty()), 0) def test_ids_arrive_as_numbers_however_they_were_sent(self): # JSON object keys are strings, so a moved feature's id always is. cleaned = edits.clean({"removed": ["7", 8], "moved": {"9": ROAD}}) self.assertEqual(cleaned["removed"], [7, 8]) self.assertIn(9, cleaned["moved"]) def test_rubbish_is_dropped_rather_than_guessed_at(self): cleaned = edits.clean({"removed": ["x", None], "moved": {"a": ROAD}, "tags": {"1": {"amenity": None}}}) self.assertEqual(edits.count(cleaned), 0) def test_the_wrong_shape_of_edit_list_is_dropped_too(self): # A table where a list was expected, or a number where either was. # This reads both what the window posts and the file kept beside the # map, and either can arrive like this; it threw "'str' object has no # attribute 'items'" and the window showed a 500. for raw in ("nonsense", 7, None, [], {"tags": "x"}, {"moved": [1, 2]}, {"removed": 5}, {"tags": {"1": "no"}}, {"moved": {"1": 5}}, {"removed": "12"}, {"moved": {"1": [[0, "a"], 7]}}): with self.subTest(raw=raw): self.assertEqual(edits.count(edits.clean(raw)), 0) def test_a_shape_of_one_point_is_not_a_shape(self): self.assertEqual(edits.clean({"moved": {"1": [[0.0, 0.0]]}})["moved"], {}) def test_only_the_listed_tags_are_taken(self): # These tags reach classify and the renderer; a page cannot be allowed # to set whatever it likes on a feature. cleaned = edits.clean({"tags": {"1": {"building": "retail", "note": "hello", "population": "9999"}}}) self.assertEqual(cleaned["tags"][1], {"building": "retail"})

nodes.name: Applying
nodes.body_text: class Applying(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_removed_feature_is_gone(self): out, used = edits.apply(town(), {"removed": [1]}) self.assertEqual([f.osm_id for f in out], [2, 3]) self.assertEqual(used["removed"], 1) def test_a_moved_feature_keeps_its_tags_and_takes_the_new_shape(self): out, used = edits.apply(town(), {"moved": {"2": [[5.0, 5.0], [6.0, 6.0]]}}) road = next(f for f in out if f.osm_id == 2) self.assertEqual(road.geometry, [(5.0, 5.0), (6.0, 6.0)]) self.assertEqual(road.tags, {"highway": "residential"}) self.assertEqual(used["moved"], 1) def test_an_area_that_was_closed_stays_closed(self): # An open ring is a line, not an area: the house would be painted as a # stripe rather than built. ring = [[9.0, 9.0], [9.0, 9.001], [9.001, 9.001]] out, _used = edits.apply(town(), {"moved": {"1": ring}}) house = next(f for f in out if f.osm_id == 1) self.assertEqual(house.geometry[0], house.geometry[-1]) def test_retagging_a_house_as_a_shop_changes_what_is_built(self): out, used = edits.apply(town(), {"tags": {"1": {"building": "retail", "shop": "yes"}}}) house = next(f for f in out if f.osm_id == 1) self.assertEqual(house.tags["building"], "retail") self.assertEqual(classify(house.tags, area=True), "building") self.assertEqual(used["tags"], 1) def test_the_download_is_never_touched(self): original = town() before = [(f.osm_id, list(f.geometry), dict(f.tags)) for f in original] edits.apply(original, {"removed": [1], "moved": {"2": ROAD}, "tags": {"3": {"natural": "sand"}}}) after = [(f.osm_id, list(f.geometry), dict(f.tags)) for f in original] self.assertEqual(before, after) def test_no_edits_is_the_same_list_of_features(self): out, used = edits.apply(town(), None) self.assertEqual([f.osm_id for f in out], [1, 2, 3]) self.assertEqual(used, {"removed": 0, "moved": 0, "tags": 0}) def test_an_id_that_is_not_there_changes_nothing(self): out, _used = edits.apply(town(), {"removed": [999]}) self.assertEqual(len(out), 3)

nodes.body_text: class ForTheWindow(unittest.TestCase): def test_each_feature_carries_its_own_id_back(self): out = edits.as_geojson(town()) self.assertEqual([f["properties"]["osm_id"] for f in out["features"]], [1, 2, 3]) def test_a_closed_way_is_a_polygon_and_an_open_one_a_line(self): out = edits.as_geojson(town()) kinds = {f["id"]: f["geometry"]["type"] for f in out["features"]} self.assertEqual(kinds[1], "Polygon") self.assertEqual(kinds[2], "LineString") def test_coordinates_go_back_the_way_geojson_wants_them(self): out = edits.as_geojson([town()[1]]) self.assertEqual(out["features"][0]["geometry"]["coordinates"], [[0.0, 0.0], [0.002, 0.002]]) def test_only_what_is_being_looked_at_comes_back(self): far = OSMFeature(4, "way", {"building": "house"}, [(50.0, 50.0), (50.0, 50.001), (50.001, 50.001), (50.0, 50.0)]) out = edits.as_geojson(town() + [far], bbox=(-1.0, -1.0, 1.0, 1.0)) self.assertEqual([f["id"] for f in out["features"]], [1, 2, 3]) def test_a_town_too_big_to_edit_sends_the_biggest_and_says_so(self): many = [OSMFeature(i, "way", {"building": "house"}, [(0.0, 0.0), (0.0, i / 1000), (i / 1000, i / 1000), (0.0, 0.0)]) for i in range(1, 51)] out = edits.as_geojson(many, limit=10) self.assertEqual(out["total"], 50) self.assertEqual(out["shown"], 10) self.assertEqual(len(out["features"]), 10) # Largest first, so what arrives is what is worth editing. self.assertEqual(out["features"][0]["id"], 50) def test_a_node_is_not_offered_for_editing(self): trees = [OSMFeature(9, "node", {"natural": "tree"}, [(0.0, 0.0)])] self.assertEqual(edits.as_geojson(trees)["features"], [])

nodes.name: write_extract
nodes.body_text: def write_extract(path): """A tiny extract: a building, a bakery, a road far away, and a lake that is a relation of one untagged way.""" w = osmium.SimpleWriter(path) def node(i, lat, lon, tags=None): w.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=i, location=(lon, lat), tags=tags or {})) for i, (la, lo) in enumerate(square(10.0, 20.0, 0.001), 1): node(i, la, lo) node(5, 10.0005, 20.0005, {"shop": "bakery"}) node(6, 50.0, 50.0) node(7, 50.001, 50.001) for i, (la, lo) in enumerate(square(10.01, 20.01, 0.01), 10): node(i, la, lo) # A lake of four ways, three of them (one by one) beyond a small box. for i, (la, lo) in zip((30, 31, 32, 33), ((10.5, 20.5), (10.5, 20.51), (10.9, 20.51), (10.9, 20.5))): node(i, la, lo) for wid, (a, b) in zip((110, 111, 112, 113), ((30, 31), (31, 32), (32, 33), (33, 30))): w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=wid, nodes=[a, b], tags={})) w.add_relation(osmium.osm.mutable.Relation( id=201, members=[("w", i, "outer") for i in (110, 111, 112, 113)], tags={"type": "multipolygon", "natural": "water"})) w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=100, nodes=[1, 2, 3, 4, 1], tags={"building": "yes"})) w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=101, nodes=[6, 7], tags={"highway": "residential"})) w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=102, nodes=[10, 11, 12, 13, 10], tags={})) w.add_relation(osmium.osm.mutable.Relation( id=200, members=[("w", 102, "outer")], tags={"type": "multipolygon", "natural": "water"})) w.close()

nodes.name: FilterReading
nodes.body_text: class FilterReading(unittest.TestCase): def test_every_overpass_filter_is_understood(self): filters = extract.parse_filters(osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS) self.assertEqual(len(filters), len(osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS)) def test_equality_regex_and_presence(self): f = extract.Filter('way["natural"="water"]') self.assertTrue(f.matches("way", {"natural": "water"})) self.assertFalse(f.matches("way", {"natural": "wood"})) self.assertFalse(f.matches("node", {"natural": "water"})) f = extract.Filter('way["landuse"~"^(forest|grass)$"]') self.assertTrue(f.matches("way", {"landuse": "forest"})) self.assertFalse(f.matches("way", {"landuse": "forestry"})) f = extract.Filter('way["highway"]') self.assertTrue(f.matches("way", {"highway": "x"})) self.assertFalse(f.matches("way", {})) def test_nwr_is_all_three_and_two_tests_both_hold(self): f = extract.Filter('nwr["amenity"="fountain"]') for kind in ("node", "way", "relation"): self.assertTrue(f.matches(kind, {"amenity": "fountain"})) f = extract.Filter('node["place"~"^(city|town)$"]["population"]') self.assertTrue(f.matches("node", {"place": "town", "population": "9"})) self.assertFalse(f.matches("node", {"place": "town"}))

nodes.body_text: class GeometryBounds(unittest.TestCase): def test_short_and_long_lines_in_either_byte_order(self): for count in (2, 64, 65, 1000): for endian, marker in (("<", 1), (">", 0)): points = [(float(i - 20), float(10 - i)) for i in range(count)] wkb = struct.pack(endian + "BII", marker, 2, count) wkb += struct.pack(endian + f"{count * 2}d", *[v for p in points for v in p]) with self.subTest(count=count, endian=endian): self.assertEqual(extract._line_bounds(wkb.hex()), (-20., float(11 - count), float(count - 21), 10.)) def test_invalid_or_different_geometries_are_rejected(self): for wkb in (b'', b'\x01', struct.pack('<BII', 1, 2, 0), struct.pack('<BII', 1, 3, 1)): with self.subTest(wkb=wkb), self.assertRaises(ValueError): extract._line_bounds(wkb.hex())

nodes.body_text: class WhichExtract(unittest.TestCase): INDEX = {"features": [ {"properties": {"id": "world", "name": "World", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/world.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[-180, -90], [180, -90], [180, 90], [-180, 90], [-180, -90]]]}}, {"properties": {"id": "land", "name": "Land", "parent": "world", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/land.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[0, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10], [0, 10], [0, 0]]]}}, {"properties": {"id": "east", "name": "East", "parent": "land", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/east.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[5, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10], [5, 10], [5, 0]]]}}, {"properties": {"id": "west", "name": "West", "parent": "land", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/west.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[0, 0], [5, 0], [5, 10], [0, 10], [0, 0]]]}}, ]} def test_the_smallest_extract_that_holds_the_box(self): got = extract.regions_for(1, 6, 2, 7, self.INDEX) self.assertEqual([r["id"] for r in got], ["east"]) def test_a_box_across_two_halves_takes_the_parent_that_holds_it(self): got = extract.regions_for(1, 4, 2, 6, self.INDEX) self.assertEqual([r["id"] for r in got], ["land"]) def test_a_box_across_two_extracts_with_no_parent_takes_both(self): halves = {"features": [f for f in self.INDEX["features"] if f["properties"]["id"] in ("east", "west")]} got = extract.regions_for(1, 4, 2, 6, halves) self.assertEqual({r["id"] for r in got}, {"east", "west"}) def test_a_box_across_two_states_takes_the_states_not_the_country(self): # Geofabrik's United States polygon is 3,516 against Indiana's 10 and # Kentucky's 11: a box over the Ohio River is held by no single state # and by the country, and the two states are the cheaper read. The # country used to win this one, which is a 12 GB download. index = {"features": [ {"properties": {"id": "country", "name": "Country", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/country.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[0, 0], [100, 0], [100, 100], [0, 100], [0, 0]]]}}, {"properties": {"id": "a", "name": "A", "parent": "country", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/a.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[0, 0], [5, 0], [5, 10], [0, 10], [0, 0]]]}}, {"properties": {"id": "b", "name": "B", "parent": "country", "urls": {"pbf": "https://x/b.pbf"}}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[5, 0], [10, 0], [10, 10], [5, 10], [5, 0]]]}}, ]} got = extract.regions_for(1, 4, 2, 6, index) self.assertEqual([r["id"] for r in got], ["a", "b"]) def test_a_box_in_the_sea_takes_the_widest_that_holds_it(self): got = extract.regions_for(-50, 100, -49, 101, self.INDEX) self.assertEqual([r["id"] for r in got], ["world"])

nodes.body_text: class Download(unittest.TestCase): REGION = {"id": "land", "name": "Land", "url": "https://x/land.pbf"} def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.patch = mock.patch.object(extract, "cache_dir", lambda: self.dir) self.patch.start() def tearDown(self): self.patch.stop() def response(self, status=200, body=b"data"): r = mock.Mock() r.status_code = status r.headers = {"Content-Length": str(len(body))} r.iter_content = lambda n: iter([body]) r.raise_for_status = lambda: None if status < 400 else (_ for _ in ()).throw( extract.requests.HTTPError(str(status))) return r def test_a_fresh_copy_is_used_without_asking(self): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "land.osm.pbf") with open(path, "wb") as f: f.write(b"x") with mock.patch.object(extract.requests, "get", side_effect=AssertionError("asked")): self.assertEqual(extract._download(self.REGION, lambda *a: None, None), path) def test_a_missing_one_is_downloaded_and_kept(self): with mock.patch.object(extract.requests, "get", lambda *a, **k: self.response()): path = extract._download(self.REGION, lambda *a: None, None) with open(path, "rb") as f: self.assertEqual(f.read(), b"data") self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(path + ".part")) def test_an_old_one_is_asked_about_and_kept_on_304(self): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "land.osm.pbf") with open(path, "wb") as f: f.write(b"old") old = time.time() - 40 * 86400 os.utime(path, (old, old)) seen = {} def get(url, headers=None, **k): seen.update(headers or {}) return self.response(304) with mock.patch.object(extract.requests, "get", get): extract._download(self.REGION, lambda *a: None, None) self.assertIn("If-Modified-Since", seen) with open(path, "rb") as f: self.assertEqual(f.read(), b"old") self.assertLess(time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path), 100) def test_an_old_one_is_used_when_the_server_cannot_be_reached(self): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "land.osm.pbf") with open(path, "wb") as f: f.write(b"old") old = time.time() - 40 * 86400 os.utime(path, (old, old)) with mock.patch.object(extract.requests, "get", side_effect=extract.requests.ConnectionError("down")): self.assertEqual(extract._download(self.REGION, lambda *a: None, None), path) def test_none_and_no_server_is_unavailable(self): with mock.patch.object(extract.requests, "get", side_effect=extract.requests.ConnectionError("down")): with self.assertRaises(extract.ExtractUnavailable): extract._download(self.REGION, lambda *a: None, None)

cls.filters = extract.parse_filters(osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS) def read(self, bbox): with mock.patch.object(extract, "cache_dir", lambda: self.dir): return extract._read(self.path, self.filters, bbox, lambda *a: None, None) @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows native paths") def test_unicode_directory_with_disk_index(self): directory = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=self.dir, prefix="\u00c1rea-\u65e5\u672c-") path = os.path.join(directory, "test.osm.pbf") shutil.copyfile(self.path, path) try: extract._native_path(path) except extract.ExtractUnavailable: self.skipTest("Windows short paths are unavailable on this volume") with mock.patch.object(extract, "cache_dir", return_value=directory), \ mock.patch.object(extract, "BIG_EXTRACT_BYTES", 0): got = extract._read(path, self.filters, (9.99, 19.99, 10.03, 20.03), lambda *a: None, None) self.assertEqual({(e["type"], e["id"]) for e in got}, {("node", 5), ("way", 100), ("relation", 200)}) @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "nt", "Windows native paths") def test_unavailable_short_path_falls_back(self): with mock.patch("ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetShortPathNameW", return_value=0): with self.assertRaisesRegex(extract.ExtractUnavailable, "Overpass"): extract._native_path("C:/\u65e5\u672c/test.osm.pbf") def test_what_is_wanted_and_inside_comes_out(self): got = {(e["type"], e["id"]) for e in self.read((9.99, 19.99, 10.03, 20.03))} self.assertEqual(got, {("node", 5), ("way", 100), ("relation", 200)}) def test_a_file_scan_reports_activity_without_a_guessed_percentage(self): reports = [] with mock.patch.object(extract, "_download", return_value=self.path): extract.elements(9.99, 19.99, 10.03, 20.03, regions=[{"name": "test"}], progress=lambda done, total, note: reports.append((done, total, note))) self.assertTrue(any(total == 0 and "reading the map data" in note for _done, total, note in reports)) def test_what_is_far_away_is_left_out(self): got = {(e["type"], e["id"]) for e in self.read((9.99, 19.99, 10.002, 20.002))} self.assertEqual(got, {("node", 5), ("way", 100)}) def test_the_relation_carries_its_member_ways_geometry(self): rel = next(e for e in self.read((9.99, 19.99, 10.03, 20.03)) if e["type"] == "relation") self.assertEqual(rel["members"][0]["role"], "outer") self.assertEqual(len(rel["members"][0]["geometry"]), 5) def nodes.body_text: class FenceHeights(unittest.TestCase): """The game has a short and a tall version of most of its fences and OSM says which: metal bars two metres tall came out as the waist-high railing because a fence's height was never read.""" def test_metal_bars_are_tall_when_the_mapper_says_they_are(self): self.assertEqual(style_for({"barrier": "fence", "fence_type": "metal_bars", "height": "2"}, None), "tall_metal") self.assertEqual(style_for({"barrier": "fence", "fence_type": "metal_bars", "height": "1"}, None), "black_metal") # Said nothing: as it always was. self.assertEqual(style_for({"barrier": "fence", "fence_type": "metal_bars"}, None), "black_metal") def test_the_other_fences_follow_their_height_too(self): for kind, tall, short in (("chain_link", "tall_chainlink", "short_chainlink"), ("wood", "tall_wooden", "short_wooden"), ("picket", "white_picket", "short_picket")): with self.subTest(kind=kind): self.assertEqual(style_for({"fence_type": kind, "height": "2.0"}, "residential"), tall) self.assertEqual(style_for({"fence_type": kind, "height": "0.9"}, "residential"), short) def test_a_height_is_read_however_it_was_written(self): self.assertAlmostEqual(height_m({"height": "2"}), 2.0) self.assertAlmostEqual(height_m({"height": "1.5 m"}), 1.5) self.assertAlmostEqual(height_m({"height": "1,8m"}), 1.8) self.assertAlmostEqual(height_m({"height": "6'"}), 1.8288, places=3) for bad in ("", "tall", "0.05", "40"): self.assertIsNone(height_m({"height": bad}), bad) def test_every_style_named_by_the_height_rule_is_a_fence_we_have(self): for short, (tall, _at) in TALLER.items(): self.assertIn(short, STYLES) self.assertIn(tall, STYLES)

nodes.body_text: class WaysThroughAFence(unittest.TestCase): """A mapper draws the fence as one line and the gate as a node on it, or runs a footpath through it. Built from the line alone the fence walls off the way in.""" def fence(self, openings, tags=None): directory = self.enterContext(TemporaryDirectory()) bdir = os.path.join(directory, "buildings") os.mkdir(bdir) with open(os.path.join(directory, "map_fences.geojson"), "w") as f: json.dump({"features": [{ "type": "Feature", "properties": tags or {"barrier": "fence", "fence_type": "wood", "height": "1.0"}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[2, 6], [13, 6]]}}]}, f) with open(os.path.join(directory, "map_fence_openings.geojson"), "w") as f: json.dump({"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": openings}, f) projection = SimpleNamespace(width=16, height=16, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat)) placements, _count = build_fences( directory, "map", projection, np.zeros((16, 16), dtype=bool), None, bdir) out = {} for placement in placements: root = ElementTree.parse(os.path.join(directory, placement.tbx_path)) names = [f.find("entry/tile").get("name") for f in root.findall(".//furniture")] for obj in root.findall(".//floor/object"): out[(placement.tile_x + int(obj.get("x")), placement.tile_y + int(obj.get("y")))] = names[int(obj.get("FurnitureTiles"))] return out def test_a_gate_node_hangs_a_gate_and_the_fence_carries_on(self): built = self.fence([{"type": "Feature", "properties": {"opening": "gate"}, "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [7, 6]}}]) gates = [x for (x, y), tile in built.items() if tile.startswith("fixtures_doors_fences")] self.assertEqual(len(gates), 1, "one gate, not a gateway") self.assertLessEqual(abs(gates[0] - 7), 1) # ...and the fence either side of it is still there. self.assertIn((3, 6), built) self.assertIn((11, 6), built) def test_a_footpath_through_a_fence_leaves_a_hole(self): built = self.fence([{"type": "Feature", "properties": {"opening": "path"}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[10, 2], [10, 11]]}}]) self.assertNotIn((10, 6), built) self.assertIn((4, 6), built) def test_a_fence_with_no_gate_tile_gets_a_hole_instead(self): built = self.fence( [{"type": "Feature", "properties": {"opening": "gate"}, "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [7, 6]}}], tags={"barrier": "wall"}) # concrete: the game has no gate self.assertNotIn((7, 6), built) self.assertIn((4, 6), built) def test_nothing_changes_where_no_openings_were_mapped(self): built = self.fence([]) # Eleven tiles of fence from x=2 to x=12, and the post it ends on. self.assertEqual(sorted(x for (x, y) in built if y == 6), list(range(2, 14)))

nodes.name: WhoseFenceItIs
nodes.body_text: class WhoseFenceItIs(unittest.TestCase): """A yard fence is this program's guess; a mapped or drawn one is not. Reported in #bug-reports: the fences put round back yards were laid over the fences in OpenStreetMap and over hedges drawn in the editor, because the made-up ones were built last and the last one to claim an edge kept it. """ def built(self, mapped, yard): directory = self.enterContext(TemporaryDirectory()) bdir = os.path.join(directory, "buildings") os.mkdir(bdir) with open(os.path.join(directory, "map_fences.geojson"), "w") as f: json.dump({"features": [{ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"barrier": "hedge"}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": mapped}}]}, f) projection = SimpleNamespace(width=16, height=16, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat)) placements, count = build_fences( directory, "map", projection, np.zeros((16, 16), dtype=bool), None, bdir, extra=[(yard, "white_picket", [])]) tiles = {} for placement in placements: root = ElementTree.parse(os.path.join(directory, placement.tbx_path)) names = [f.find("entry/tile").get("name") for f in root.findall(".//furniture")] for obj in root.findall(".//floor/object"): tiles[(placement.tile_x + int(obj.get("x")), placement.tile_y + int(obj.get("y")))] = \ names[int(obj.get("FurnitureTiles"))] return tiles, count def test_a_yard_fence_that_crosses_a_mapped_one_is_not_built(self): # The hedge runs across where the yard fence would go. tiles, count = self.built(mapped=[[2, 8], [12, 8]], yard=[(6, 4), (6, 12)]) self.assertTrue(count, "the hedge itself should still be there") # Nothing of the yard fence: no tile of it above or below the hedge. self.assertNotIn((6, 5), tiles) self.assertNotIn((6, 11), tiles) def test_one_that_keeps_out_of_the_way_is_built_as_before(self): tiles, _count = self.built(mapped=[[2, 2], [12, 2]], yard=[(6, 8), (12, 8)]) self.assertTrue(any(y >= 7 for _x, y in tiles), "the yard fence should still be built")

nodes.name: test_flyovers.py
nodes.body_text: """Which crossings get a flyover (generator/structures.py: plan_bridges). A flyover rises on ramps, and the ramps only line up with the deck where the crossing is square to the tile grid. A diagonal one never joins, so it is left at ground level: a junction a player can use, not a bridge they cannot. """ import unittest from types import SimpleNamespace from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.structures import Plan, plan_bridges if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

[np.count_nonzero(row) for row in rectilinear.mask if row.any()] self.assertGreater(len(set(real_left)), 1) self.assertEqual(len(set(rect_left)), 1) self.assertGreater(len(set(widths)), 1) def nodes.name: test_frontend_limits.py
nodes.body_text: """The window and the server must agree about where a map stops being easy. `static/js/app.js` repeats a handful of numbers from `web/checks.py` so the page can say what a big map costs before anything is sent - a browser cannot import a Python module. The copy is a promise, and until now nothing checked it: if one side moved, the note under the size readout would describe a limit the server does not enforce (or the server would enforce one the page never mentions) and every test would still pass. This reads both files and compares them. It is a plain parse of the `const` lines rather than a browser run, so it needs no Node, no server and no map. """ from __future__ import annotations import re import unittest from pathlib import Path from web import checks ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent APP_JS = ROOT / "static" / "js" / "app.js" # The numbers the page mirrors on purpose, and the only ones compared. Anything # else the page declares is the page's own business: SLOW_ABOVE_KM2, for one, # has no server twin - it decides when to add a word to the note, not whether # the server will accept a map. SHARED = ( "BIG_AREA_KM2", "BIG_TILES_PER_SIDE", "BIG_LANDMARK_KM2", "OVERPASS_TILE_KM2", "BUILD_BYTES_PER_TILE", "BUILD_BASE_BYTES", ) CONSTANT = re.compile(r"^const\s+([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*(-?[0-9.]+(?:e[0-9]+)?)\s*;") if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: page_constants
nodes.body_text: def page_constants() -> dict[str, float]: """Every numeric `const NAME = value;` in app.js, by name.""" out = {} for line in APP_JS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(): match = CONSTANT.match(line.strip()) if match: out[match.group(1)] = float(match.group(2)) return out

nodes.name: ThePageMirrorsTheServer
nodes.body_text: class ThePageMirrorsTheServer(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.page = page_constants() def test_every_shared_limit_is_declared_on_both_sides(self): for name in SHARED: with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIn(name, self.page, f"{name} is gone from app.js") self.assertTrue(hasattr(checks, name), f"{name} is gone from web/checks.py") def test_the_values_are_the_same(self): for name in SHARED: with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertEqual(self.page[name], getattr(checks, name), f"app.js and web/checks.py disagree about {name}") def test_the_page_does_not_restate_another_server_limit(self): # The other direction: a number the page copies under a name nobody # listed above would drift just as silently. Anything numeric in both # files is compared, whether or not it is in SHARED. for name, value in self.page.items(): server = getattr(checks, name, None) if isinstance(server, (int, float)): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertEqual(value, float(server), f"app.js and web/checks.py disagree about {name}") def test_every_mirrored_limit_is_actually_used(self): # A constant that is declared and never read is the other half of the # same mistake: the copy would look maintained while the note ignored # it. Each name outside the shared list is the page's own, so only the # shared ones are required to be referenced. source = APP_JS.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for name in SHARED: with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertGreater(source.count(name), 1, f"{name} is declared but never used in app.js")

nodes.name: rect
nodes.body_text: def rect(w, h): return {(x, y) for x in range(w) for y in range(h)}

nodes.name: connected
nodes.body_text: def connected(tiles): if not tiles: return True start = min(tiles) seen, todo = {start}, [start] while todo: x, y = todo.pop() for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if n in tiles and n not in seen: seen.add(n) todo.append(n) return seen == set(tiles)

nodes.name: _sample
nodes.body_text: def _sample(): for kind in ("house", "apartment"): for seed in range(30): rng = random.Random(seed) w = rng.randint(9, 20) h = rng.randint(8, 16) levels = rng.randint(1, 3) if kind == "house" else rng.randint(3, 5) yield kind, seed, dict(width=w, height=h, levels=levels, kind=kind, seed=seed)

nodes.body_text: class Walkway(unittest.TestCase): def test_two_doors_joined_by_shortest_path(self): w = walkway(rect(7, 5), [(0, 2), (6, 2)]) self.assertTrue({(0, 2), (6, 2)} <= w) self.assertTrue(connected(w)) self.assertEqual(len(w), 7) def test_three_doors_all_joined(self): w = walkway(rect(7, 5), [(0, 2), (6, 2), (3, 0)]) self.assertTrue({(0, 2), (6, 2), (3, 0)} <= w) self.assertTrue(connected(w)) self.assertLessEqual(len(w), 10) def test_one_door_gets_a_spine(self): w = walkway(rect(5, 5), [(0, 2)]) self.assertIn((0, 2), w) self.assertIn((3, 1), w) self.assertTrue(connected(w)) self.assertEqual(len(w), 5) def test_spine_keeps_off_walls(self): w = walkway(rect(7, 5), [(0, 2)]) for x, y in w - {(0, 2)}: self.assertTrue(1 <= x <= 5 and 1 <= y <= 3, (x, y)) def test_narrow_room_gets_only_the_door(self): self.assertEqual(walkway(rect(2, 6), [(0, 0)]), {(0, 0)}) def test_three_wide_room_gets_only_the_door(self): # A spine down the one inner row leaves nothing two deep (a double # bed) room on either side. self.assertEqual(walkway(rect(3, 7), [(1, 0)]), {(1, 0)}) def test_no_entries(self): self.assertEqual(walkway(rect(4, 4), []), set()) self.assertEqual(walkway(rect(4, 4), [(9, 9)]), set()) def test_l_shape_stays_inside(self): cells = rect(6, 3) | {(x, y) for x in range(3) for y in range(3, 6)} w = walkway(cells, [(5, 1), (1, 5)]) self.assertTrue(w <= cells) self.assertTrue({(5, 1), (1, 5)} <= w) self.assertTrue(connected(w)) def test_tree_as_one_search_per_way_in(self): # walkway grows its tree from one kept distance field; it must join # the ways in exactly as a fresh _path search per way in did. def reference(cells, entries): terminals = sorted({e for e in entries if e in cells}) depth = FR._depth(cells) tree, pending = {terminals[0]}, set(terminals[1:]) while pending: path = FR._path(cells, depth, tree, pending.__contains__) if path is None: break tree.update(path) pending -= tree return tree rng = random.Random(11) for case in range(400): w, h = rng.randint(2, 12), rng.randint(2, 12) cells = rect(w, h) - {(rng.randrange(w), rng.randrange(h)) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, w * h // 4))} if not cells: continue entries = rng.sample(sorted(cells), min(len(cells), rng.randint(2, 8))) with self.subTest(case=case): self.assertEqual(walkway(cells, entries), reference(cells, entries)) def test_deterministic(self): entries = [(0, 2), (6, 2), (3, 0)] self.assertEqual(walkway(rect(7, 5), entries), walkway(rect(7, 5), entries))

nodes.body_text: class FloorStaysOpen(unittest.TestCase): cells = rect(5, 5) walk = {(2, 4), (2, 3), (2, 2)} def test_walkway_is_never_blocked(self): self.assertIs(keeps_floor_open(self.cells, set(), self.walk, {(2, 3)}, 2), False) def test_corner_cut_off(self): self.assertIs(keeps_floor_open( self.cells, {(2, 0), (2, 1)}, self.walk, {(0, 2), (1, 2)}, 2), False) def test_small_pocket_allowed(self): self.assertIs(keeps_floor_open( self.cells, {(1, 0)}, self.walk, {(0, 1)}, 2), True) def test_nothing_new(self): self.assertIs(keeps_floor_open(self.cells, set(), self.walk, set(), 2), True) def test_small_pockets_add_up(self): """An upstairs bedroom in Piqua: a 4x3 room whose doors open off a one-wide strip at x=3. A double bed and a dresser at the foot left pockets of two squares each; a second dresser at (3, 2), on the one square joining room and strip, shut the room off in pockets of 2, 2 and 1, none of them over the limit alone.""" cells = rect(4, 3) | {(3, 3), (3, 4), (3, 5)} walk = {(3, 3), (3, 4), (3, 5)} bed = {(1, 0), (2, 0), (1, 1), (2, 1)} blocked = bed | {(3, 0), (0, 2)} self.assertIs(keeps_floor_open(cells, blocked, walk, {(3, 2)}, 2), False) def test_open_floor_answers_as_keeps_floor_open(self): # The incremental check must give the same answer for every query, so # a seed lays out the same rooms with it as without. rng = random.Random(5) for case in range(300): w, h = rng.randint(2, 7), rng.randint(2, 7) cells = rect(w, h) - {(rng.randrange(w), rng.randrange(h)) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3))} walk = set(rng.sample(sorted(cells), min(len(cells), rng.randint(0, 3)))) floor = FR.OpenFloor(cells, walk, 2) blocked = set() for _ in range(12): x, y = rng.randrange(-1, w + 1), rng.randrange(-1, h + 1) new = {(x, y)} | ({(x + 1, y)} if rng.random() < 0.3 else set()) with self.subTest(case=case, blocked=sorted(blocked), new=sorted(new)): self.assertIs(floor.keeps_open(new), keeps_floor_open(cells, blocked, walk, new, 2)) if rng.random() < 0.5: blocked |= new floor.block(new)

nodes.body_text: class ClearUpAfterBuild(unittest.TestCase): """Full SAMPLE builds, recording what _open_up takes out.""" @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.removed = [] # (role, room kind, touches a window square) orig = layout._open_up def spy(storey, starts): gone = orig(storey, starts) win = set() for x, y, d in storey.windows: win |= {(x - 1, y), (x, y)} if d == "W" else {(x, y - 1), (x, y)} for i in gone: role, x, y, o = storey.furniture[i] idx = storey.grid[y][x] kind = storey.rooms[idx - 1].kind if idx else "" cls.removed.append( (role, kind, bool(set(layout._tiles_under(role, x, y, o)) & win))) return gone with mock.patch.object(layout.furnishing, "_open_up", spy): cls.builds = [layout.build_building(**args) for _k, _s, args in SAMPLE] cls.placed = len(cls.removed) + sum( len(s.furniture) for b in cls.builds for s in b.storeys) def test_few_pieces_removed(self): self.assertLess(len(self.removed) / self.placed, 0.03) def test_essentials_not_removed(self): # Measured 12 (baseline ~283): 8 from one flat kitchen on 4 storeys, # counter and sink on the window square with no other counter or free # wall; 3 beds/wardrobe on moved doors; 1 sofa knocked on by one. # What is left has three causes, none of them furnish-time placement: # a window square in a corner pocket of a full room (its stack can # neither move nor swap, and the window rule wants the square reached, # so the stack on the way goes too), pieces on the clearance of a door # slid off a corner after furnishing that cannot move (beds, wardrobes, # full rooms), and knock-ons of doors that slid into a corner pocket. lost = [(r, k) for r, k, _w in self.removed if priority(r, k) == ESSENTIAL] self.assertLessEqual(len(lost), 16, lost) def test_route_removals_drop(self): # Pieces taken out that do not touch a window square. Measured 50 of # 13,354 = 0.37% (baseline 166 = 1.25%): 26 on the way to a window # square, 11 on a moved door's clearance, 12 knock-ons of moved doors. # What is left has three causes, none of them furnish-time placement: # a window square in a corner pocket of a full room (its stack can # neither move nor swap, and the window rule wants the square reached, # so the stack on the way goes too), pieces on the clearance of a door # slid off a corner after furnishing that cannot move (beds, wardrobes, # full rooms), and knock-ons of doors that slid into a corner pocket. route = [(r, k) for r, k, w in self.removed if not w] self.assertLess(len(route), 0.0045 * self.placed, route) def test_window_squares_are_not_shut_in(self): # A piece moved off a window square must not box the square in: free # window squares in a pocket of two tiles or fewer. Measured 28 of # 1,993 (136 of 2,013 when the move ignored it); what is left are # squares the plan itself leaves in a corner. free = pocket = 0 for b in self.builds: for s in b.storeys: cover = {c for role, x, y, o in s.furniture if layout._blocks(role) for c in layout._tiles_under(role, x, y, o)} for x, y, d in s.windows: for t in (((x - 1, y), (x, y)) if d == "W" else ((x, y - 1), (x, y))): if not (0 <= t[0] < s.width and 0 <= t[1] < s.height and s.grid[t[1]][t[0]]) or t in cover: continue free += 1 seen, todo = {t}, [t] while todo and len(seen) <= 2: cx, cy = todo.pop() for q in ((cx + 1, cy), (cx - 1, cy), (cx, cy + 1), (cx, cy - 1)): if (0 <= q[0] < s.width and 0 <= q[1] < s.height and s.grid[q[1]][q[0]] == s.grid[t[1]][t[0]] and q not in cover and q not in seen): seen.add(q) todo.append(q) pocket += len(seen) <= 2 self.assertLess(pocket, 0.02 * free, (pocket, free)) def test_kitchens_keep_a_table(self): # 27 of 149 kitchens before the walkway rule (18%), 3 when the table's # aisle could not cross it; the aisle is bare floor, so it may. kitchens = tables = 0 for b in self.builds: for s in b.storeys: for idx, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if r.kind != "kitchen": continue kitchens += 1 tables += any(role in ("round_table", "dining_table", "table") for role, x, y, _o in s.furniture if s.grid[y][x] == idx) self.assertGreaterEqual(tables / kitchens, 0.08) def test_rooms_keep_their_essentials(self): want = {"bathroom": (("toilet",), 0.87), "kitchen": (("fridge",), 0.87), "bedroom": (("bed", "double_bed"), 0.78), "livingroom": (("sofa",), 0.95)} rooms = dict.fromkeys(want, 0) have = dict.fromkeys(want, 0) for b in self.builds: for s in b.storeys: for idx, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if r.kind not in want: continue rooms[r.kind] += 1 have[r.kind] += any(role.startswith(want[r.kind][0]) for role, x, y, _o in s.furniture if s.grid[y][x] == idx) for kind, (_roles, floor) in want.items(): with self.subTest(kind=kind): self.assertGreaterEqual(have[kind] / rooms[kind], floor)

nodes.name: NothingStandsInADoorway
nodes.body_text: class NothingStandsInADoorway(unittest.TestCase): """A door's tiles have no blocking piece on them. Furnishing keeps off them, but the pass that moves a door off the flight can put one back afterwards, and it landed on a bed already made up: a bedroom whose only way in was the foot of its bed. """ SHAPES = ((11, 10, 0), (13, 12, 3), (17, 12, 1), (12, 12, 0), (14, 11, 2)) def test_a_doorway_is_clear_in_every_built_house(self): built = 0 for w, h, seed in self.SHAPES: b = layout.build_building(w, h, levels=1, seed=seed, kind="house") for level, s in enumerate(b.storeys): clear = layout._door_tiles(s) for role, x, y, o in s.furniture: if not layout._blocks(role): continue hit = set(layout._cells_for(role, x, y, o)).intersection(clear) with self.subTest(shape=(w, h, seed), level=level, role=role): self.assertFalse( hit, f"{role} at {(x, y)} stands in a doorway at {sorted(hit)}") built += 1 self.assertGreaterEqual(built, len(self.SHAPES))

nodes.name: test_industrial_yards.py
nodes.body_text: """An industrial estate is ground a building may stand on. The renderer paints a works' yard in the game's beige gravel, which is the same colour it paints a track bed and a service lane. The building placer read that colour as road and refused every footprint inside the estate, so a town's industrial end came out as empty gravel in the exact shape of the landuse polygon - with the Knox County roads setting on or off, which is what made it clear the roads were not to blame. """ import json import os import tempfile import unittest from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from knoxbuild.areas import AreaIndex from knoxbuild.build import YARD_AREAS, _road_weight PROJ = SimpleNamespace(width=40, height=40, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat)) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: YardsAreNotRoads
nodes.body_text: class YardsAreNotRoads(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() ground = np.zeros((40, 40, 3), dtype=np.uint8) ground[:, :] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS ground[10:30, 10:30] = C.LIGHT_ASPHALT # the works' yard ground[:, 34:38] = C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT # a street past it Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(self.dir, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") def areas(self, category="industrial"): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "m_areas.geojson") with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [{ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"category": category}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": ring(10, 10, 30, 30)}}]}, f) return AreaIndex.load(self.dir, "m", PROJ) def test_the_yard_of_an_industrial_estate_is_free_ground(self): weight = _road_weight(self.dir, "m", PROJ, None, self.areas()) self.assertEqual(int(weight[20, 20]), 0, "the yard still reads as road") self.assertEqual(int(weight[20, 35]), 2, "the street stopped being one") def test_without_the_land_use_it_is_the_colour_that_decides(self): # Nothing says the gravel is a yard, so it is treated as it always was. weight = _road_weight(self.dir, "m", PROJ, None, None) self.assertEqual(int(weight[20, 20]), 2) def test_a_road_across_the_yard_is_still_a_road(self): hierarchy = np.zeros((40, 40), dtype=np.uint8) hierarchy[19:22, :] = 3 # the works' access road weight = _road_weight(self.dir, "m", PROJ, hierarchy, self.areas()) self.assertEqual(int(weight[20, 20]), 3) self.assertEqual(int(weight[25, 20]), 0) def test_a_car_park_is_left_alone(self): # A building in the middle of a car park is a kiosk nobody mapped; # keeping footprints off them is right. self.assertNotIn("parking", YARD_AREAS) weight = _road_weight(self.dir, "m", PROJ, None, self.areas("parking")) self.assertEqual(int(weight[20, 20]), 2)

nodes.name: AnEstateDrawnAsOneWayRoundTwoYards
nodes.body_text: class AnEstateDrawnAsOneWayRoundTwoYards(unittest.TestCase): """A landuse ring that touches itself is two yards, not nothing. Mending such a ring gives several polygons back instead of one, and one of those in the index has no outline to ask for: reading the ground under a works threw 'MultiPolygon object has no attribute exterior' and the whole build stopped before a single building was placed. """ # Two squares joined by the line the mapper drew between them. PINCHED = [[[10, 10], [19, 10], [19, 19], [10, 19], [10, 10], [21, 21], [29, 21], [29, 29], [21, 29], [21, 21]]] def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() ground = np.zeros((40, 40, 3), dtype=np.uint8) ground[:, :] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS ground[10:30, 10:30] = C.LIGHT_ASPHALT Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(self.dir, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") path = os.path.join(self.dir, "m_areas.geojson") with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [{ "type": "Feature", "properties": {"category": "industrial"}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": self.PINCHED}}]}, f) self.index = AreaIndex.load(self.dir, "m", PROJ) def test_both_halves_are_in_the_index_as_shapes_of_their_own(self): self.assertEqual(len(self.index._items), 2) self.assertEqual(self.index.category_at(14, 14), "industrial") self.assertEqual(self.index.category_at(25, 25), "industrial") self.assertIsNone(self.index.category_at(35, 35)) def test_the_ground_under_both_of_them_reads_as_yard(self): weight = _road_weight(self.dir, "m", PROJ, None, self.index) self.assertEqual(int(weight[14, 14]), 0) self.assertEqual(int(weight[25, 25]), 0) # The gravel the estate does not cover is still read as it was. self.assertEqual(int(weight[11, 28]), 2)

nodes.name: test_infill.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings invented for gaps along a street (generator/rendering/infill.py).""" import unittest from shapely.geometry import Polygon from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.rendering.infill import _back_sheds, _infill_frontage from generator.rendering.projection import Projector PROJ = Projector.build(35.90, -84.00, 35.92, -83.97, 1.0) Y = 150.0 # the street runs along y = 150 tiles if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: way
nodes.body_text: def way(ident, pts, **tags): return OSMFeature(osm_id=ident, kind="way", tags=tags, geometry=[PROJ.to_latlon(x, y) for x, y in pts])

nodes.name: box
nodes.signature: def box(ident, x0, x1, y0, y1, **tags)
nodes.body_text: def box(ident, x0, x1, y0, y1, **tags): tags.setdefault("building", "house") return way(ident, [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1), (x0, y0)], **tags)

nodes.name: street
nodes.body_text: def street(x0=20, x1=300, y=Y, ident=1): return way(ident, [(x0, y), (x1, y)], highway="residential")

nodes.name: row
nodes.signature: def row(start, count, pitch, width, y0, y1, skip=(), **tags)
nodes.body_text: def row(start, count, pitch, width, y0, y1, skip=(), **tags): return [box(100 + i, start + i * pitch, start + i * pitch + width, y0, y1, **tags) for i in range(count) if i not in skip]

nodes.name: polys
nodes.body_text: def polys(feats): return [Polygon([PROJ.to_px(la, lo) for la, lo in f.geometry]) for f in feats]

nodes.name: in_hole
nodes.body_text: def in_hole(feats): """The new buildings standing in the hole of Houses.scene, not the row carried on past its ends.""" return [f for f, p in zip(feats, polys(feats)) if 109 < p.bounds[0] < 184]

nodes.name: fill
nodes.body_text: def fill(buildings, roads=(), **buckets): roads = list(roads) or [street()] return _infill_frontage({"road_minor": roads, **buckets}, [], buildings, PROJ)

nodes.name: Houses
nodes.signature: class Houses(unittest.TestCase): # 15 m houses on an 18 m pitch, 12 m deep, standing 4 m off the pavement, # with the fifth to the eighth missing: a 70 m hole in a row of houses.
nodes.body_text: class Houses(unittest.TestCase): # 15 m houses on an 18 m pitch, 12 m deep, standing 4 m off the pavement, # with the fifth to the eighth missing: a 70 m hole in a row of houses. def scene(self): return row(40, 14, 18, 15, 130, 142, skip=(4, 5, 6, 7)) def test_a_hole_in_a_row_is_filled(self): made = in_hole(fill(self.scene())) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(made), 3) for p in polys(made): self.assertTrue(112 <= p.bounds[0] and p.bounds[2] <= 192) self.assertAlmostEqual(p.bounds[3] - p.bounds[1], 12, delta=2) def test_they_are_built_like_the_neighbours(self): made = fill(self.scene()) self.assertTrue(all(f.tags["building"] == "house" for f in made)) # standing as far back as the houses either side for p in polys(made): self.assertAlmostEqual(p.bounds[3], 142, delta=1.5) def test_nothing_overlaps_anything(self): existing = self.scene() made = fill(existing) every = polys(existing) + polys(made) for i, a in enumerate(every): for b in every[i + 1:]: self.assertLess(a.intersection(b).area, 1.0) def test_the_other_side_of_the_street_is_left_empty(self): for p in polys(fill(self.scene())): self.assertLess(p.bounds[3], Y) def test_a_lone_house_does_not_start_a_street(self): self.assertEqual(fill([box(1, 100, 115, 130, 142)]), []) def test_a_row_is_carried_on_only_a_little(self): one_end = row(40, 4, 18, 15, 130, 142) made = fill(one_end) self.assertLessEqual(len(made), 3) def test_a_church_beside_the_gap_says_nothing(self): scene = self.scene() scene[3] = box(103, 94, 111, 130, 142, building="church") self.assertEqual([f for f in in_hole(fill(scene)) if polys([f])[0].bounds[0] < 120], []) def test_filling_is_repeatable(self): a = [(f.osm_id, f.geometry) for f in fill(self.scene())] b = [(f.osm_id, f.geometry) for f in fill(self.scene())] self.assertEqual(a, b)

nodes.name: FarWalls
nodes.signature: class FarWalls(unittest.TestCase): # E-429518, a town in Sicily: the building past a gap met the street at a # corner and its wall measured 20 m beyond the gap's last station. The # lots ran off the end of the gap and generate failed on an empty min().
nodes.body_text: class FarWalls(unittest.TestCase): # E-429518, a town in Sicily: the building past a gap met the street at a # corner and its wall measured 20 m beyond the gap's last station. The # lots ran off the end of the gap and generate failed on an empty min(). def scan(self, n=40): import numpy as np from generator.rendering.infill import STEP_M s = np.arange(STEP_M / 2, n * STEP_M, STEP_M) zero, one = np.zeros(n), np.ones(n) return {"s": s, "x": s, "y": zero, "tx": one, "ty": zero, "nx": zero, "ny": -one, "ax": s, "ay": zero, "hard": one * 40, "near_b": one * np.inf, "which": -one} def test_a_wall_far_past_the_gap_is_not_trusted(self): from generator.rendering.infill import STEP_M, _lots_for_gap house = {"width": 30.0, "depth": 12.0, "setback": 4.0, "area": 360.0, "kind": "house", "levels": None} i0, i1 = 10, 13 got = _lots_for_gap(self.scan(), i0, i1, [house, house], [], [40.0] * 40, False, i0 * STEP_M - 1, (i1 + 1) * STEP_M + 20) for corners in (got[0] if got else []): xs = [x for x, _ in corners] self.assertLessEqual(max(xs), (i1 + 1) * STEP_M + 1e-6)

nodes.body_text: class Clutter(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_room_is_not_mostly_furniture(self): fills = {"bedroom": [], "hall": []} for seed in range(40): b = L.build_building(10 + seed % 9, 9 + seed % 7, levels=2, seed=seed) for s in b.storeys: floor = Counter(v for row in s.grid for v in row if v) used = Counter() for role, fx, fy, o in s.furniture: if L._blocks(role): for x, y in L._tiles_under(role, fx, fy, o): if 0 <= x < s.width and 0 <= y < s.height and s.grid[y][x]: used[s.grid[y][x]] += 1 for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if r.kind in fills and not r.is_core: fills[r.kind].append(used[i] / floor[i]) self.assertLessEqual(statistics.median(fills["bedroom"]), 0.48) self.assertLessEqual(statistics.median(fills["hall"]), 0.35)

class IsoViewEndpointTests(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.test_map_name = "_test_iso_map" cls.map_dir = OUTPUT_DIR / cls.test_map_name cls.lots_dir = cls.map_dir / "lots" cls.pics_dir = cls.map_dir / "pictures" cls.lots_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) cls.pics_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) # Create dummy lotheader so map is recognized as compiled (cls.lots_dir / "10_10.lotheader").write_bytes(b"lotheader") # Create dummy info file info = { "width_tiles": 300, "height_tiles": 300, "cells_x": 1, "cells_y": 1, "building_count": 5, } (cls.map_dir / f"{cls.test_map_name}_info.json").write_text(json.dumps(info), encoding="utf-8") # Create dummy town overview picture dummy_pic = Image.new("RGBA", (100, 100), (40, 120, 40, 255)) dummy_pic.save(cls.pics_dir / "town.png") # Mock render_lots.render to return a valid PIL image without requiring actual lots files cls.render_patcher = patch("tools.render_lots.render") cls.mock_render = cls.render_patcher.start() cls.mock_render.return_value = Image.new("RGBA", (200, 150), (100, 150, 200, 255)) @classmethod def tearDownClass(cls): cls.render_patcher.stop() if cls.map_dir.is_dir(): shutil.rmtree(cls.map_dir, ignore_errors=True) def setUp(self): self.client = app.test_client() def test_iso_info_unknown_map(self): resp = self.client.get("/api/iso-info/NonExistentMapName12345") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404) data = resp.get_json() self.assertIn("error", data) def test_iso_info_compiled_map(self): resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-info/{self.test_map_name}") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200) data = resp.get_json() self.assertEqual(data["name"], self.test_map_name) self.assertTrue(data["compiled"]) self.assertEqual(data["width_tiles"], 300) self.assertEqual(data["height_tiles"], 300) self.assertEqual(data["building_count"], 5) self.assertIn("pictures", data) def test_iso_render_unknown_map(self): resp = self.client.get("/api/iso-render/NonExistentMapName12345") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404) def test_iso_render_invalid_box(self): resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=invalid,coords") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400) def test_iso_render_cached_box(self): # Request a valid box render resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=100,100,20,20&scale=1.0&roofs=1") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(resp.content_type, "image/png") self.assertGreater(len(resp.data), 100) # Second request should be served from cache resp_cached = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=100,100,20,20&scale=1.0&roofs=1") self.assertEqual(resp_cached.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(resp_cached.data, resp.data) def test_iso_render_custom_rectangular_box_with_interiors(self): # Request a non-square area with furnished interiors (roofs=0) resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=120,80,40,30&scale=1.0&roofs=0") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(resp.content_type, "image/png") self.assertGreater(len(resp.data), 100) def test_iso_render_custom_rectangular_box_with_roofs(self): # Request the same area with roofs (roofs=1) resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=120,80,40,30&scale=1.0&roofs=1") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(resp.content_type, "image/png") self.assertGreater(len(resp.data), 100) def test_iso_render_empty_area_returns_blank_canvas(self): # When render_lots.render returns None (no buildings/tiles in area), # the endpoint should return a 200 PNG canvas rather than 404 self.mock_render.return_value = None try: resp = self.client.get(f"/api/iso-render/{self.test_map_name}?box=999,999,30,30") self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(resp.content_type, "image/png") self.assertGreater(len(resp.data), 50) finally: self.mock_render.return_value = Image.new("RGBA", (200, 150), (100, 150, 200, 255)) def test_iso_info_calculates_focus_coordinates(self): # nodes.name: test_joins.py
nodes.body_text: """Where a built map's roads reach its edge (knoxbuild/joins.py). The drawing board has no world under it, so a street drawn on a sheet stopped dead at the edge and a map drawn to carry on from another never lined up with it. What is worth checking is that the places its roads leave it are read off the map itself, and that they land on the right side of the new sheet however the two are put together - a sheet east of a map meets its eastern edge on the sheet's own western one, and the distance along the border is measured from the same corner on both. """ import os import tempfile import unittest import numpy as np from PIL import Image from knoxbuild import joins if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: a_map
nodes.body_text: def a_map(width=120, height=80, metres=2.0, roads=()): """A map folder with nothing in it but its size and its roads.""" directory = tempfile.mkdtemp() with open(os.path.join(directory, "m_info.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write('{"width_tiles": %d, "height_tiles": %d, "meters_per_tile": %s}' % (width, height, metres)) picture = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8) for where, which, rank in roads: if which == "row": picture[where[0]:where[1], :] = rank else: picture[:, where[0]:where[1]] = rank Image.fromarray(picture).save(os.path.join(directory, "m_road_hierarchy.bmp"), format="BMP") return directory

nodes.name: WhereTheRoadsComeOut
nodes.body_text: class WhereTheRoadsComeOut(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_road_across_the_map_leaves_both_sides(self): # Four tiles of road at 2 m a tile, across the middle: 8 m wide, and # the middle of it is 80 m down a 160 m map. where = a_map(roads=[((38, 42), "row", 3)]) found = joins.edges(where, "m") self.assertEqual(found["widthM"], 240.0) self.assertEqual(found["heightM"], 160.0) for side in ("W", "E"): self.assertEqual(found["roads"][side], [{"at": 80.0, "width": 8.0, "rank": 3}]) self.assertEqual(found["roads"]["N"], []) self.assertEqual(found["roads"]["S"], []) def test_a_kerb_is_not_a_street_and_neither_is_a_whole_edge(self): thin = a_map(roads=[((0, 1), "row", 2)]) # one tile self.assertEqual(joins.edges(thin, "m")["roads"]["W"], []) broad = a_map(height=400, roads=[((0, 300), "row", 2)]) self.assertEqual(joins.edges(broad, "m")["roads"]["W"], []) def test_a_map_with_no_road_picture_still_gives_its_size(self): # And says that is what it is: a map built before KnoxMap drew the # road picture has streets on its edge like any other, it just cannot # say where they are. Told "no street on that side" people went # looking on the ground for one they had seen there. bare = tempfile.mkdtemp() with open(os.path.join(bare, "m_info.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write('{"width_tiles": 50, "height_tiles": 40, "meters_per_tile": 1}') found = joins.edges(bare, "m") self.assertEqual((found["widthM"], found["heightM"]), (50.0, 40.0)) self.assertEqual(found["roads"], {s: [] for s in joins.SIDES}) self.assertFalse(found["roadsKnown"]) def test_a_map_whose_roads_were_read_says_so_even_with_none_on_a_side(self): where = a_map(roads=[((38, 42), "row", 3)]) found = joins.edges(where, "m") self.assertTrue(found["roadsKnown"]) self.assertEqual(found["roads"]["N"], []) def test_a_map_folder_with_nothing_in_it_is_not_an_error(self): found = joins.edges(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "m") self.assertEqual((found["widthM"], found["heightM"]), (0.0, 0.0))

nodes.name: OnTheNewSheet
nodes.body_text: class OnTheNewSheet(unittest.TestCase): """The sheet is lined up with the map's corner on the side they share.""" def setUp(self): # A road across the middle (east-west) and one down it (north-south). self.dir = a_map(roads=[((38, 42), "row", 3), ((58, 62), "col", 4)]) def test_a_sheet_east_of_it_meets_its_eastern_edge_on_the_sheets_west(self): out = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "E", 500.0, 160.0) self.assertEqual(out["meets"], "W") self.assertEqual(out["joins"], [{"x": 0.0, "y": 80.0, "width": 8.0, "rank": 3, "side": "W"}]) def test_a_sheet_west_of_it_meets_it_on_the_sheets_east(self): out = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "W", 500.0, 160.0) self.assertEqual(out["meets"], "E") self.assertEqual([j["x"] for j in out["joins"]], [500.0]) def test_north_and_south_are_measured_across_from_the_same_corner(self): # A sheet north of the map has the map along its bottom edge, which # on a sheet measured upwards from its own corner is y = 0. north = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "N", 240.0, 300.0) self.assertEqual(north["meets"], "S") self.assertEqual(north["joins"], [{"x": 120.0, "y": 0.0, "width": 8.0, "rank": 4, "side": "S"}]) south = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "S", 240.0, 300.0) self.assertEqual(south["meets"], "N") self.assertEqual([(j["x"], j["y"]) for j in south["joins"]], [(120.0, 300.0)]) def test_a_taller_sheet_measures_down_from_the_edge_they_share(self): # The two are lined up along their northern edge, so a road 80 m down # the map is 80 m down the sheet - not 80 m up from the sheet's own # bottom, which on a sheet of another height is somewhere else # entirely. A 600 m sheet beside a 160 m map used to have the street # marked 440 m out of place. out = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "E", 500.0, 600.0) self.assertEqual([(j["x"], j["y"]) for j in out["joins"]], [(0.0, 520.0)]) # And a sheet shorter than the map: the road is where it is, or off. short = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "W", 500.0, 100.0) self.assertEqual([(j["x"], j["y"]) for j in short["joins"]], [(500.0, 20.0)]) def test_a_road_past_the_end_of_a_short_sheet_is_left_off(self): out = joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "E", 500.0, 40.0) self.assertEqual(out["joins"], []) def test_a_side_that_is_not_a_side(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): joins.sheet_joins(self.dir, "m", "up", 100.0, 100.0)

nodes.name: test_knoxdata.py
nodes.body_text: """Offline tests for the optional enrichment layers (knoxdata/). No network: fetchers are mocked or the layer is gated out. The point is the contract — a disabled, unavailable or failing layer is skipped with a line, never a lost map, and OSM data is never overwritten. """ import io import logging import os import tempfile import unittest from pathlib import Path import knoxdata from knoxbuild.settings import Settings if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: TheCacheHasACeiling
nodes.body_text: class TheCacheHasACeiling(unittest.TestCase): """knoxdata/cache.py caps the whole dataset cache, not just one download. The per-download ceiling stops one wrong URL filling the disk. Nothing stopped ten right ones: a few national extracts and a world raster and the cache was as big as the last month of maps made it. """ def ages(self, folder, *sizes): """Files of the given sizes, oldest first.""" made = [] for i, size in enumerate(sizes): p = Path(folder) / f"set{i}.bin" p.write_bytes(b"x" * size) os.utime(p, (1000 + i, 1000 + i)) made.append(p) return made def test_the_oldest_datasets_go_when_it_is_full(self): from knoxdata import cache with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: made = self.ages(folder, 600, 600, 600) self.assertEqual(cache.prune(keep_bytes=1000, folder=folder), 2) self.assertFalse(made[0].exists()) self.assertTrue(made[2].exists(), "the newest dataset must survive") def test_the_file_just_downloaded_is_never_the_one_deleted(self): from knoxdata import cache with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: old, fresh = self.ages(folder, 600, 600) self.assertEqual(cache.prune(keep_bytes=600, folder=folder, keep=fresh), 1) self.assertFalse(old.exists()) self.assertTrue(fresh.exists()) def test_a_cache_under_its_ceiling_is_left_alone(self): from knoxdata import cache with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: made = self.ages(folder, 10) self.assertEqual(cache.prune(keep_bytes=1000, folder=folder), 0) self.assertTrue(made[0].exists()) def test_an_empty_or_missing_cache_is_not_an_error(self): from knoxdata import cache with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder: self.assertEqual(cache.prune(folder=Path(folder) / "nothing-here"), 0)

These exercise build_layer end to end; only fetch is mocked. """ import tempfile import unittest from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import knoxdata from knoxbuild.settings import Settings try: import rasterio # noqa: F401 HAS_RASTERIO = True except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 HAS_RASTERIO = False try: import pyarrow # noqa: F401 HAS_PYARROW = True except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 HAS_PYARROW = False @unittest.skipUnless(HAS_RASTERIO, "rasterio not installed") @unittest.skipUnless(HAS_RASTERIO, "rasterio not installed") @unittest.skipUnless(HAS_RASTERIO, "rasterio not installed") @unittest.skipUnless(HAS_PYARROW, "pyarrow not installed") if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()
