nodes.body_text: class WorldCoverProcessing(unittest.TestCase): def test_class_fractions(self): import rasterio from rasterio.transform import from_bounds from knoxdata import worldcover s, w, n, e = 32.0, -87.0, 32.5, -86.5 tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) name = worldcover.tile_names((s, w, n, e))[0] data = np.full((10, 10), 10, dtype="uint8") data[:5, :] = 30 # grassland data[:2, :] = 50 # built-up with rasterio.open(tmp / name, "w", driver="GTiff", height=10, width=10, count=1, dtype="uint8", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, 10, 10)) as dst: dst.write(data, 1) src = worldcover.WorldCover() src.fetch = lambda bbox, cache_dir=None, progress_cb=None: tmp ctx = knoxdata.MapContext(bbox=(s, w, n, e), settings=Settings(), map_dir=".") fractions = src.build_layer(ctx).data["fractions"] self.assertAlmostEqual(fractions["Built-up"], 0.20, places=3) self.assertAlmostEqual(fractions["Grassland"], 0.30, places=3) self.assertAlmostEqual(fractions["Tree cover"], 0.50, places=3) def test_rasterise_returns_one_class_per_tile(self): import rasterio from rasterio.transform import from_bounds from knoxdata import worldcover s, w, n, e = 32.0, -87.0, 32.5, -86.5 tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) name = worldcover.tile_names((s, w, n, e))[0] data = np.full((10, 10), 10, dtype="uint8") data[:, :5] = 30 with rasterio.open(tmp / name, "w", driver="GTiff", height=10, width=10, count=1, dtype="uint8", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, 10, 10)) as dst: dst.write(data, 1) src = worldcover.WorldCover() src.tile_dir = lambda: tmp src.fetch = lambda *a, **k: self.fail("rasterise must not download") grid = src.rasterise((s, w, n, e), 10, 10) self.assertEqual(grid.shape, (10, 10)) self.assertTrue(set(np.unique(grid).tolist()) <= {10, 30}) def _tile(self, data, s=32.0, w=-87.0, n=32.5, e=-86.5): import rasterio from rasterio.transform import from_bounds from knoxdata import worldcover tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) name = worldcover.tile_names((s, w, n, e))[0] h, wd = data.shape with rasterio.open(tmp / name, "w", driver="GTiff", height=h, width=wd, count=1, dtype="uint8", crs="EPSG:4326", transform=from_bounds(w, s, e, n, wd, h)) as dst: dst.write(data, 1) src = worldcover.WorldCover() src.tile_dir = lambda: tmp return src def test_speckle_is_filtered_at_10_m_not_at_map_tiles(self): # A lone 10 m pixel of cropland in a wood: noise, gone however finely # the map samples it. Filtered after the stretch, it survived. data = np.full((20, 20), 10, dtype="uint8") data[10, 10] = 40 src = self._tile(data) grid = src.rasterise((32.0, -87.0, 32.5, -86.5), 200, 200) self.assertEqual(set(np.unique(grid).tolist()), {10}) def test_area_past_the_tile_is_left_empty_not_stretched(self): # The east half of the box has no tile on disk: it stays 0 (no data), # and the west half keeps the tile's own split at its own place. data = np.full((20, 20), 10, dtype="uint8") data[:, :10] = 30 src = self._tile(data, s=32.0, w=-87.0, n=32.5, e=-86.5) grid = src.rasterise((32.0, -86.75, 32.5, -86.25), 100, 50) self.assertTrue((grid[:, :45] == 10).all()) self.assertTrue((grid[:, 55:] == 0).all())

nodes.name: test_lang_files.py
nodes.body_text: """The language files and the template they are keyed by. A translation is found by its English side: the left of each "=" in lang/english.txt. Reword a line and every translation of it stops matching - silently, because the window simply shows English again. Until now nothing looked: the only language check was one Russian sentence, and the four files had drifted by 20 dead lines and 48 English lines that were in the window but not in the template. These tests hold the two ends together: * every key a language file translates exists in english.txt, so a renamed line shows up here instead of as a sentence that quietly went back to English, and a dead line gets deleted rather than carried forever; * every placeholder ({area}, {count} ...) on the English side survives on the translated side, because a dropped one is a number the reader never sees. Coverage is printed, not asserted: a half-finished file is by design, and whatever is not translated is simply shown in English. """ from __future__ import annotations import re import unittest from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent LANG = ROOT / "lang" TEMPLATE = LANG / "english.txt" PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\{([A-Za-z_]\w*)\}") if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: entries
nodes.body_text: def entries(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]: """English side -> translated side, as the window reads the file.""" out = {} for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(): line = line.strip() if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line: continue english, _, theirs = line.partition("=") english, theirs = english.strip(), theirs.strip() if english: out[english] = theirs return out

A line whose two sides differ would make English # itself read as another language. for english, theirs in entries(TEMPLATE).items(): with self.subTest(english=english[:50]): self.assertEqual(english, theirs)

nodes.body_text: class TheTranslationFiles(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.english = entries(TEMPLATE) self.files = sorted(p for p in LANG.glob("*.txt") if p.name != "english.txt") def test_there_is_something_to_check(self): self.assertTrue(self.files, "no language files found") def test_every_key_is_in_the_template(self): # The drift check. A key the template no longer has can never match # anything the window says, so it is either a reworded line whose # translation should be moved, or a typo. for path in self.files: stale = sorted(set(entries(path)) - set(self.english)) with self.subTest(file=path.name): self.assertEqual(stale, [], f"{len(stale)} key(s) in {path.name} are not in " f"lang/english.txt: {stale[:5]}") def test_placeholders_survive_translation(self): # "{area} km²" translated without {area} shows a size the map never # fills in. Only the English placeholders are required: a translator # may repeat one, which is fine, and may not invent one. for path in self.files: for english, theirs in entries(path).items(): if not theirs or theirs == english: continue # untranslated: not a translation missing = set(PLACEHOLDER.findall(english)) - set(PLACEHOLDER.findall(theirs)) with self.subTest(file=path.name, english=english[:40]): self.assertEqual(missing, set(), f"{path.name} drops {sorted(missing)} from {english!r}") def test_every_file_translates_something(self): # An empty file still loads and looks like a language that works. for path in self.files: done = sum(1 for key, theirs in entries(path).items() if theirs and theirs != key) with self.subTest(file=path.name): self.assertGreater(done, 0) print(f" {path.name}: {done} of {len(self.english)} lines " f"({100 * done / len(self.english):.0f}%)")

nodes.body_text: """What a city-sized map needs: room tables that fit in memory, buildings made in small batches that can be stopped, a compile that carries on after a crash, and one KnoxMap process at a time on a map.""" import json import os import random import tempfile import time import unittest from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest import mock import numpy as np import knoxstop from knoxbuild import build as B from knoxbuild import repair as R from knoxbuild.buildheader import placed_rooms, room_rects from knoxbuild.settings import Settings from tests.slow import slow from tools import compile_map as C from tools import map_source as M @slow @slow @slow @slow @slow @slow @slow if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: _reference_placed_rooms
nodes.body_text: def _reference_placed_rooms(lots): """placed_rooms as it was before it went level by level, one dict entry per square: the output the per-level rewrite has to match exactly.""" order = sorted(range(len(lots)), key=lambda i: (lots[i][2] // 300, lots[i][1] // 300, i)) owner = {} for i in order: b, tx, ty, base = lots[i] for z, floor in enumerate(b.floors): for y, row in enumerate(floor.rooms): for x, v in enumerate(row): if v > 0: owner[(tx + x, ty + y, base + z)] = (i, v) squares = {} for (x, y, z), (i, rid) in owner.items(): squares.setdefault((i, z, rid), set()).add((x, y)) rank = {lot: n for n, lot in enumerate(order)} parts = sorted(squares, key=lambda k: (rank[k[0]], k[1], k[2])) at = {(x, y, k[1]): k for k in parts for (x, y) in squares[k]} lot_parent = list(range(len(lots))) def lfind(i): while lot_parent[i] != i: lot_parent[i] = lot_parent[lot_parent[i]] i = lot_parent[i] return i for k in parts: for (x, y) in squares[k]: for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, -1)): n = at.get((x + dx, y + dy, k[1])) if n and n[0] != k[0]: lot_parent[lfind(n[0])] = lfind(k[0]) groups = {} for i in order: groups.setdefault(lfind(i), []).append(i) parts_of = {} for k in parts: parts_of.setdefault(k[0], []).append(k) out = [] for members in groups.values(): entries = [{"name": lots[k[0]][0].rooms[k[2] - 1].get("Name", ""), "z": k[1], "rects": room_rects(squares[k])} for lot in members for k in parts_of.get(lot, ())] out.append((lots[members[0]][1], lots[members[0]][2], entries)) return out

nodes.body_text: def _town(rnd, n, arrays=False): lots = [] for _ in range(n): w, h, rooms = rnd.randint(1, 9), rnd.randint(1, 9), rnd.randint(1, 4) floors = [] for _z in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)): grid = [[rnd.choice([0] + list(range(1, rooms + 1))) for _x in range(w)] for _y in range(h)] floors.append(SimpleNamespace(rooms=np.array(grid, np.int32) if arrays else grid)) b = SimpleNamespace(floors=floors, rooms=[{"Name": f"room{k}"} for k in range(rooms)]) # Close enough together to overlap and touch, across 300-tile cells. lots.append((b, rnd.randint(0, 700), rnd.randint(0, 700), rnd.choice([0, 0, -1, 1]))) return lots

nodes.name: StoppingACompile
nodes.body_text: class StoppingACompile(unittest.TestCase): def _pool(self, naps): from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) return pool, {pool.submit(_nap, s): n for n, s in enumerate(naps)} def test_every_job_handed_over(self): pool, pending = self._pool([0.2, 0.0, 0.1]) got = {} M._gather(pool, pending, None, lambda fut, n: got.__setitem__(n, fut.result())) self.assertEqual(got, {0: 0.2, 1: 0.0, 2: 0.1}) def test_a_stop_does_not_wait_for_the_jobs_running(self): # Each job as long as a row of a city's cells: a stop used to wait them out. pool, pending = self._pool([60, 60, 60]) asked = time.time() + 1.0 t0 = time.time() with self.assertRaises(knoxstop.Stopped): M._gather(pool, pending, lambda: time.time() > asked, lambda fut, n: None) self.assertLess(time.time() - t0, 10.0)

nodes.body_text: class CheckingTheBuildings(unittest.TestCase): """The check before a compile: what it drops, and not doing it twice.""" def setUp(self): self._dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() self.base = Path(self._dir.name) (self.base / "buildings").mkdir() self.refs = [] for n in range(5): ref = f"buildings/b{n}.tbx" (self.base / ref).write_text(f"<building {n}/>", encoding="utf-8") self.refs.append(ref) self.read = [] def tearDown(self): self._dir.cleanup() def _check(self, refs=None, should_stop=None): def batch(paths, knoxlots): self.read.extend(Path(p).name for p in paths) return [["broken"] if p.endswith("b3.tbx") else [] for p in paths] with mock.patch.object(R, "_check_batch", batch): return R.check_lot_files(self.base, refs or self.refs, True, should_stop) def test_a_file_checked_before_is_not_read_again(self): first = self._check() self.assertEqual(first["buildings/b3.tbx"], ["broken"]) self.assertEqual(len(self.read), 5) self.read.clear() self.assertEqual(self._check(), first) self.assertEqual(self.read, []) later = time.time() + 5 os.utime(self.base / "buildings" / "b1.tbx", (later, later)) self._check() self.assertEqual(self.read, ["b1.tbx"], "only the one that changed") def test_a_missing_file_is_said_without_reading(self): got = self._check(self.refs + ["buildings/gone.tbx"]) self.assertEqual(got["buildings/gone.tbx"], ["the file is missing"]) self.assertNotIn("gone.tbx", self.read) def test_a_stop_keeps_what_was_checked(self): refs = [] for n in range(120): ref = f"buildings/many{n}.tbx" (self.base / ref).write_text("<building/>", encoding="utf-8") refs.append(ref) with mock.patch.object(R, "PARALLEL_CHECK_FROM", 10 ** 9): with self.assertRaises(knoxstop.Stopped): self._check(refs, should_stop=lambda: len(self.read) > 0) self.assertEqual(len(self.read), 50, "stopped after the first batch") self.read.clear() self._check(refs) self.assertEqual(len(self.read), 70, "the first 50 were kept") def test_furniture_out_of_its_room_does_not_drop_a_building(self): import sys tools = str(Path(R.__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "tools") if tools not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, tools) with mock.patch("validate_tbx.check", return_value=[]) as check: R._check_building(self.base / self.refs[0], True) self.assertIs(check.call_args.kwargs.get("flaws"), False)

nodes.body_text: class FurnishedRoomWalkability(unittest.TestCase): def test_furniture_is_moved_off_the_window_approach(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 4, 4, kind="livingroom") plan = layout.Plan( 5, 5, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 5 for _ in range(5)], doors=[(2, 0, "N")], windows=[(0, 2, "W")], furniture=[("bookshelf", 0, 2, "N")]) building = layout.Building(5, 5, storeys=[plan]) removed = layout._clear_the_way(building) self.assertEqual(removed, 0) shelves = [f for f in plan.furniture if f[0] == "bookshelf"] self.assertEqual(len(shelves), 1) self.assertNotEqual(shelves[0][1:3], (0, 2)) def test_window_square_is_cleared_when_nothing_can_move(self): # Boxed in by fridges: a dresser may stand at a window now (it is # low), so one beside the bookshelf would simply trade places with it. room = layout.Room(0, 0, 2, 2, kind="livingroom") furniture = [("bookshelf", 0, 1, "W")] furniture += [("fridge", x, y, "N") for x, y in ((0, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1), (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2))] plan = layout.Plan( 3, 3, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 3 for _ in range(3)], doors=[(1, 0, "N")], windows=[(0, 1, "W")], furniture=furniture) building = layout.Building(3, 3, storeys=[plan]) removed = layout._clear_the_way(building) self.assertEqual(removed, 1) self.assertFalse([f for f in plan.furniture if f[0] == "bookshelf"]) def test_a_wall_cabinet_keeps_its_counter(self): # Nowhere free to stand the dresser: the bare counter could trade # places with it, but would leave the cabinet over a dresser. room = layout.Room(0, 0, 2, 2, kind="kitchen") furniture = [("dresser", 0, 1, "W"), ("counter", 2, 1, "E"), ("wall_cabinet", 2, 1, "E")] furniture += [("dresser", x, y, "N") for x, y in ((0, 0), (2, 0), (0, 2), (1, 2), (2, 2))] plan = layout.Plan( 3, 3, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 3 for _ in range(3)], doors=[(1, 0, "N")], windows=[(0, 1, "W")], furniture=furniture) layout._make_way_for_windows(plan, None) self.assertIn(("counter", 2, 1, "E"), plan.furniture) def test_furniture_partition_is_opened_for_room_walkability(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 4, 4, kind="livingroom") furniture = [("bookshelf", 2, y, "N") for y in range(5)] plan = layout.Plan( 5, 5, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 5 for _ in range(5)], doors=[(0, 2, "W")], furniture=furniture) building = layout.Building(5, 5, storeys=[plan]) removed = layout._clear_the_way(building) self.assertGreater(removed, 0) self.assertLess(len(plan.furniture), len(furniture))

nodes.name: NothingIsWalledOffByTheLift
nodes.body_text: class NothingIsWalledOffByTheLift(unittest.TestCase): """A lift shaft is sealed, so what it stands across is a wall. A tall building with a narrow arm - an L or a T whose neck is a couple of tiles wide - had the shaft land in the neck, and every room up the arm then had nothing beside it but the shaft: no door anywhere, loot nobody could reach. The arm is taken out of that storey instead, which is what it is from the outside: roof. """ def a_building_with_a_narrow_arm(self): # The shape the layout audit found it on: 16 x 39, a 16-wide body # with a 6-wide arm up the middle - four rooms wide once the arm has # its walls, and the shaft is two of them. mask = [[(y >= 14 or 5 <= x <= 10) for x in range(16)] for y in range(39)] return layout.build_building(16, 39, levels=12, seed=2464, kind="fire", mask=mask, commercial=True) def test_every_room_has_a_way_in(self): building = self.a_building_with_a_narrow_arm() for level, storey in enumerate(building.storeys): rooms = range(1, len(storey.rooms) + 1) shafts = {i for i in rooms if storey.rooms[i - 1].is_shaft} beside = {} for a, b in layout._boundary_edges(storey): if a in shafts or b in shafts: continue beside.setdefault(a, set()).add(b) beside.setdefault(b, set()).add(a) for i in rooms: if i in shafts: continue with self.subTest(level=level, room=storey.rooms[i - 1].kind): self.assertTrue(beside.get(i), "nothing beside it but the lift shaft")

nodes.name: test_malls.py
nodes.body_text: """A mall is one enclosed mall, laid out as a mall (knoxbuild.build, layout). Run from the KnoxMap folder: python -m unittest discover tests No network, no files: footprints placed straight into an empty grid, and buildings laid out directly. """ import os import sys import time import unittest sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) import numpy as np # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild import layout # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild.build import mall_by_name, row_units # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild.footprint import place # noqa: E402 GRID = np.zeros((600, 600), dtype=bool) # Three different shops, as uses_of returns them (one per kind), and the # floor area of a real mall. SHOPS = [("clothingstore", "storage"), ("toystore", "storage"), ("bookstore", "storage")] BIG = 20000.0 # The biggest mall kept whole, two storeys, laid out in this many seconds. # It takes about 40 s on a quiet machine and 70 s on a loaded one - a full suite # running beside it was enough to fail the 60 s budget twice. This is a guard # against a layout going quadratic, not a benchmark, so it is set where a busy # CI box still passes and a real slowdown still trips it. MALL_LAYOUT_BUDGET_S = 120.0 if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: def mall(w=160, h=90, levels=1, seed=0, mask=None): return layout.build_building(w, h, levels=levels, kind="mall", commercial=True, seed=seed, mask=mask)

nodes.name: _tiles
nodes.body_text: def _tiles(p, i): return sum(row.count(i) for row in p.grid)

nodes.name: _anchor_rooms
nodes.body_text: def _anchor_rooms(p): return [p.grid[(y0 + y1) // 2][(x0 + x1) // 2] for x0, y0, x1, y1 in p.anchors]

nodes.name: _touches_rect
nodes.body_text: def _touches_rect(p, i, rect): x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect for y, row in enumerate(p.grid): for x, v in enumerate(row): if v == i and any(x0 <= nx <= x1 and y0 <= ny <= y1 for nx, ny in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1))): return True return False

nodes.name: _door_rooms
nodes.body_text: def _door_rooms(p, door): """The two grid values a door joins; 0 is outside.""" x, y, d = door def at(cx, cy): return p.grid[cy][cx] if 0 <= cx < p.width and 0 <= cy < p.height else 0 return at(x, y), (at(x - 1, y) if d == "W" else at(x, y - 1))

nodes.name: at
nodes.body_text: def at(cx, cy): return p.grid[cy][cx] if 0 <= cx < p.width and 0 <= cy < p.height else 0

nodes.name: _links
nodes.body_text: def _links(p): out = {} for door in p.doors: a, b = _door_rooms(p, door) out.setdefault(a, set()).add(b) out.setdefault(b, set()).add(a) return out

nodes.name: _service_components
nodes.body_text: def _service_components(p): halls = {i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "hall" and not r.is_core} links = _links(p) comps, seen = [], set() for h in halls: if h in seen: continue comp, stack = {h}, [h] while stack: for n in links.get(stack.pop(), ()): if n in halls and n not in comp: comp.add(n) stack.append(n) seen |= comp comps.append(comp) return comps

nodes.name: _concourse_id
nodes.body_text: def _concourse_id(p): return next(i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "concourse")

nodes.name: footprint
nodes.body_text: def footprint(w: int, h: int): ring = [(10.0, 10.0), (10.0 + w, 10.0), (10.0 + w, 10.0 + h), (10.0, 10.0 + h), (10.0, 10.0)] fp, reason = place(ring, GRID.copy(), max_side=1e9) assert fp is not None, reason return fp

260 x 240 = 62,400 m2 at a metre a tile. units = row_units(footprint(260, 240), "mall", "retail", 0, 1.0) self.assertGreater(len(units), 1) def test_mall_past_max_size_is_still_cut(self): units = row_units(footprint(150, 100), "mall", "retail", 0, 1.0, max_side=100) self.assertGreater(len(units), 1) def test_center_with_three_shops_is_a_mall(self): self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("shop", {"name": "Piqua Center"}, SHOPS, BIG), "mall") self.assertEqual(mall_by_name(None, {"name": "Miami Valley Centre"}, SHOPS, BIG), "mall") self.assertEqual(mall_by_name(None, {"name": "Towne Plaza"}, SHOPS, BIG), "mall") def test_plaza_with_two_shops_is_not_a_mall(self): uses = [("clothesstore", "storage"), ("office", "office"), ("office", "office")] self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("civic", {"name": "Main Plaza"}, uses, BIG), "civic") def test_center_not_at_end_of_name_is_not_a_mall(self): self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("shop", {"name": "Center Street Shops"}, SHOPS, BIG), "shop") def test_medical_or_civic_center_is_not_a_mall(self): clinic = [("dentist", "medicaloffice"), ("medicaloffice", "medicaloffice"), ("pharmacy", "storage")] self.assertEqual(mall_by_name(None, {"name": "Riverside Medical Center"}, clinic, BIG), None) civic = [("library", "storage"), ("policeoffice", "office"), ("post", "storage")] self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("civic", {"name": "Government Center"}, civic, BIG), "civic") def test_office_tower_plaza_is_not_a_mall(self): uses = SHOPS + [("office", "office")] self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("civic", {"name": "Commerce Plaza"}, uses, BIG), "civic") tall = {"name": "Commerce Plaza", "building:levels": "12"} self.assertEqual(mall_by_name("shop", tall, SHOPS, BIG), "shop") def test_strip_plaza_stays_a_row_of_shops(self): # nodes.body_text: class FloorPlan(unittest.TestCase): def assert_mall_plan(self, p, msg): conc = [i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "concourse"] self.assertEqual(len(conc), 1, msg) adj = layout._neighbours(p) anchors = set(_anchor_rooms(p)) self.assertEqual(len(anchors), len(p.anchors), msg) for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1): if r.kind in layout.MALL_SHOP_KINDS or i in anchors: self.assertIn(conc[0], adj[i], (msg, i, r.kind)) if r.kind in layout.MALL_SHOP_KINDS: self.assertTrue(40 <= _tiles(p, i) <= 150, (msg, r.kind, _tiles(p, i))) for i in anchors: self.assertTrue(800 <= _tiles(p, i) <= 2500, (msg, _tiles(p, i))) def test_one_concourse_reaches_every_shop_and_anchor(self): for seed in range(6): self.assert_mall_plan(mall(seed=seed).storeys[0], seed) def test_arms_reach_the_wall_and_storerooms_are_and_cut_the_storerooms(self): for w, h in ((160, 90), (240, 130), (245, 245)): p = mall(w, h).storeys[0] total = sum(map(sum, p.mask)) if p.mask is not None else w * h store = sum(_tiles(p, i) for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "storage") if (w, h) == (160, 90): # was 35% before the arms ran through self.assertLess(store / total, 0.25, store / total) c = _concourse_id(p) edge = [(x, y) for y in range(p.height) for x in range(p.width) if p.grid[y][x] == c and (x in (0, p.width - 1) or y in (0, p.height - 1))] self.assertTrue(edge, (w, h)) def test_two_anchors_on_a_small_mall(self): p = mall().storeys[0] # 14,400 tiles self.assertEqual(len(p.anchors), 2) self.assert_mall_plan(p, "small") def test_three_or_four_anchors_on_a_big_mall(self): p = mall(240, 130).storeys[0] # 31,200 tiles self.assertIn(len(p.anchors), (3, 4)) self.assert_mall_plan(p, "big") def test_inline_units_are_mall_sized(self): for seed in range(6): p = mall(seed=seed).storeys[0] shops = [i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind in layout.MALL_SHOP_KINDS] self.assertGreaterEqual(len(shops), 20, seed) for i in shops: self.assertTrue(40 <= _tiles(p, i) <= 150, (seed, _tiles(p, i))) def test_small_multi_storey_mall_gets_no_lift(self): # The old layout's hole runs the length of the spine and only the # stair core is taken out of it: a lift there stood in the hole # with the railing across its doors. for w, h in ((32, 28), (60, 50), (50, 40)): for seed in range(4): b = layout.build_building(w, h, levels=2, kind="mall", commercial=True, seed=seed) self.assertIsNone(b.storeys[0].court, (w, h)) self.assertIsNone(b.storeys[0].shaft, (w, h, seed)) def test_small_mall_keeps_old_layout(self): # 32x28 is below MALL_PLAN_MIN_TILES: the old spine-and-split layout. p = layout.build_building(32, 28, kind="mall", commercial=True, seed=0).storeys[0] self.assertIsNone(p.court) self.assertIn("concourse", {r.kind for r in p.rooms}) def test_l_shaped_mall_has_no_room_outside_mask(self): w, h = 160, 90 mask = [[not (x >= 100 and y < 40) for x in range(w)] for y in range(h)] for seed in range(3): p = mall(w, h, seed=seed, mask=mask).storeys[0] for y in range(h): for x in range(w): if not mask[y][x]: self.assertEqual(p.grid[y][x], 0, (seed, x, y)) for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1): if r.kind in layout.MALL_SHOP_KINDS: self.assertTrue(40 <= _tiles(p, i) <= 150, (seed, _tiles(p, i))) def test_food_court_off_the_court_on_ground_only(self): for seed in range(6): b = mall(levels=2, seed=seed) g, up = b.storeys seats = [i for i, r in enumerate(g.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "foodcourt"] self.assertEqual(len(seats), 1, seed) self.assertTrue(_touches_rect(g, seats[0], g.court), seed) counters = [i for i, r in enumerate(g.rooms, 1) if r.kind in layout.FOOD_COUNTERS] self.assertTrue(3 <= len(counters) <= 5, (seed, len(counters))) adj = layout._neighbours(g) for c in counters: self.assertTrue(20 <= _tiles(g, c) <= 40, (seed, _tiles(g, c))) self.assertIn(seats[0], adj[c], seed) self.assertFalse({"foodcourt", *layout.FOOD_COUNTERS} & {r.kind for r in up.rooms}, seed) def test_tall_mall_same_rules(self): p = mall(90, 160).storeys[0] self.assertEqual(len(p.anchors), 2) self.assert_mall_plan(p, "tall")

nodes.name: _in_rect
nodes.body_text: def _in_rect(cell, rect, grow=0): x, y = cell x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect return x0 - grow <= x <= x1 + grow and y0 - grow <= y <= y1 + grow

nodes.name: _cells
nodes.body_text: def _cells(rect): x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect return [(x, y) for y in range(y0, y1 + 1) for x in range(x0, x1 + 1)]

nodes.body_text: class Doors(unittest.TestCase): def test_service_corridor_reaches_restrooms_office_and_exit(self): for size in ((160, 90), (240, 130), (90, 160)): p = mall(*size).storeys[0] comps = _service_components(p) self.assertTrue(comps, size) links = _links(p) reached = set() for comp in comps: self.assertTrue(any(0 in links.get(h, ()) for h in comp), (size, comp)) for h in comp: reached |= links.get(h, set()) kinds = [p.rooms[i - 1].kind for i in reached if i] self.assertGreaterEqual(kinds.count("bathroom"), 2, size) self.assertIn("office", kinds, size) def test_every_inline_shop_with_a_service_hall_behind_has_a_back_door(self): for seed in range(4): p = mall(seed=seed).storeys[0] adj, links = layout._neighbours(p), _links(p) halls = {i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "hall" and not r.is_core} for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1): if r.kind in layout.MALL_SHOP_KINDS and halls & set(adj[i]): self.assertTrue(halls & links.get(i, set()), (seed, i, r.kind)) def test_food_counters_open_onto_the_seating(self): for seed in range(4): p = mall(seed=seed).storeys[0] links = _links(p) seat = next(i for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1) if r.kind == "foodcourt") for i, r in enumerate(p.rooms, 1): if r.kind in layout.FOOD_COUNTERS: self.assertIn(seat, links.get(i, set()), (seed, r.kind)) def test_each_anchor_has_an_outside_door(self): for size in ((160, 90), (240, 130)): p = mall(*size).storeys[0] links = _links(p) for a in _anchor_rooms(p): self.assertIn(0, links.get(a, set()), (size, a))

tv[1]) * -dy == (sy - tv[2]) * -dx and (sx - tv[1]) * dx + (sy - tv[2]) * dy < 0 for sx, sy in layout._cells_for(*sofa))) def test_full_arrangement_is_tried_before_pair_only_fallback(self): room = layout.Room(0, 0, 6, 6, kind='livingroom') plan = layout.Plan(7, 7, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 7 for _ in range(7)], kind='house') real_fits = layout._living_fits pair_seen = False def blocked_first_table(plan, idx, parts, cells, taken, gap, keeps_open): nonlocal pair_seen if len(parts) == 2: pair_seen = True elif not pair_seen: return False return real_fits(plan, idx, parts, cells, taken, gap, keeps_open) with mock.patch.object(layout.furnishing, '_living_fits', side_effect=blocked_first_table): self.assertTrue(layout._furnish_living(plan, 1, room, set(), set(), {})) self.assertTrue(pair_seen) self.assertIn('coffee_table', [role for role, *_ in plan.furniture]) def test_generated_houses_and_basements_keep_tv_facing_seating(self): checked = 0 for kind in ('house', 'basement_house_rec'): for seed in range(10): plan = layout.build_plan(12, 10, kind=kind, seed=seed) for room_id, room in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1): if room.kind != 'livingroom': continue items = [f for f in plan.furniture if layout._room_at(plan, f[1], f[2]) == room_id] for tv in (f for f in items if f[0] == 'tv'): checked += 1 dx, dy = layout._STEP[tv[3]] self.assertTrue(any( role.startswith('sofa') and orient == layout._OPPOSITE_SIDE[tv[3]] and any((sx - nodes.name: test_mapfiles_whole.py
nodes.body_text: """A map file is written whole, or the one from before is still there. A generate writes a dozen files into the map folder - the ground, the buildings, the land use, the fences - and each used to be written straight to its own name. Stop the generate, close the window or lose the machine halfway through one and what stayed was half a file, which the next Build read as the map and died on: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 32790 (char 32789) What is worth checking is that an interrupted write leaves the file that was there before, that a half-written one is reported as damaged rather than silently read as an empty map, and that a file which is simply not there is still "nothing of that kind here". """ import json import os import tempfile import unittest import knoxfiles from knoxbuild import fences, structures, zones from knoxbuild.areas import AreaIndex from knoxbuild.build import _drawn_features from knoxbuild.population import official_population if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: Unserialisable
nodes.body_text: class Unserialisable: """Stands in for whatever goes wrong halfway down a long write."""

nodes.name: WrittenWholeOrNotAtAll
nodes.body_text: class WrittenWholeOrNotAtAll(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.path = os.path.join(self.dir, "thing.json") def test_a_write_that_fails_leaves_the_one_from_before(self): knoxfiles.write(self.path, {"features": [1, 2, 3]}) with self.assertRaises(TypeError): knoxfiles.write(self.path, {"features": Unserialisable()}) with open(self.path, encoding="utf-8") as f: self.assertEqual(json.load(f), {"features": [1, 2, 3]}) # And the half of it that was written is taken away again rather # than left in the map folder. self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.dir), ["thing.json"]) def test_and_nothing_at_all_when_there_was_nothing_before(self): with self.assertRaises(TypeError): knoxfiles.write(self.path, Unserialisable()) self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.path)) def test_the_half_written_file_is_not_left_lying_in_its_place(self): knoxfiles.write(self.path, {"a": 1}) self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.dir), ["thing.json"]) def test_a_bitmap_is_written_the_same_way(self): from PIL import Image picture = os.path.join(self.dir, "ground.bmp") knoxfiles.save(Image.new("RGB", (4, 4), (1, 2, 3)), picture, format="BMP") self.assertEqual(os.listdir(self.dir), ["ground.bmp"]) with Image.open(picture) as written: self.assertEqual(written.size, (4, 4))

nodes.body_text: class ReadingOneThatWentWrong(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() def half(self, name, text='{"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [{"geo'): path = os.path.join(self.dir, name) with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(text) return path def test_it_says_which_file_it_is_and_what_to_do(self): path = self.half("m_fences.geojson") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged) as caught: knoxfiles.read(path, "the fences") said = str(caught.exception) self.assertIn("m_fences.geojson", said) self.assertIn("the fences", said) self.assertIn("Generate the map again", said) def test_a_file_that_is_not_there_is_not_a_file_that_is_damaged(self): missing = os.path.join(self.dir, "nothing.json") self.assertIsNone(knoxfiles.read(missing, "the fences")) self.assertEqual(knoxfiles.read(missing, "the fences", default=[]), []) def test_the_build_stops_on_a_half_written_layer_rather_than_ignoring_it(self): # Each of these used to be either a raw JSONDecodeError out of the # middle of the build, or - worse - swallowed, so the map came out # with no fences and nobody was told why. self.half("m_fences.geojson") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): fences.build_fences(self.dir, "m", None, None, None, self.dir) self.half("m_areas.geojson") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): AreaIndex.load(self.dir, "m", None) self.half("m_structures.json") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): structures.build_structures(self.dir, "m", self.dir) self.half("m_places.json") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): official_population(self.dir, "m") def test_the_drawing_a_map_is_made_of_is_never_dropped_in_silence(self): # These two were swallowed: a half-written sheet meant a hand-drawn # map built as empty ground, and half a zones file meant a town built # to the map's own numbers everywhere the mapper had set others - # both without a word. self.half("m_design.json") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): _drawn_features(self.dir, "m") os.remove(os.path.join(self.dir, "m_design.json")) self.half("m_zones.json") with self.assertRaises(knoxfiles.Damaged): zones.load(self.dir, "m") def test_a_map_folder_with_none_of_them_still_builds(self): self.assertEqual(AreaIndex.load(self.dir, "m", None)._items, []) self.assertEqual(official_population(self.dir, "m"), []) self.assertEqual(structures.build_structures(self.dir, "m", self.dir), ([], {"bridges": 0, "monuments": 0, "tiles": 0})) self.assertEqual(zones.load(self.dir, "m"), []) self.assertEqual(_drawn_features(self.dir, "m"), [])

nodes.name: test_mapped_rooms.py
nodes.body_text: """Real interiors from OSM indoor=room data (renderer + knoxbuild.layout). Run from the KnoxMap folder: python -m unittest discover tests No network, no files. Two halves: renderer._buildings_geojson attaches each mapped room to the building it stands in, and layout.build_plan cuts the ground floor along those rooms instead of guessing. A building surveyed room by room - a school's classrooms, an office's rooms round its core - keeps that plan. """ import os import sys import unittest sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) from generator import renderer # noqa: E402 from generator.osm import OSMFeature # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild.layout import build_plan # noqa: E402 # A school: a building wide enough to hold the rooms drawn inside it. SCHOOL = OSMFeature(1, "way", {"building": "school", "name": "Test School"}, [(40.000, 20.000), (40.000, 20.0010), (40.0016, 20.0010), (40.0016, 20.000), (40.000, 20.000)]) CLASSROOM = OSMFeature(2, "way", {"indoor": "room", "room": "classroom"}, [(40.0002, 20.0002), (40.0002, 20.0008), (40.0008, 20.0008), (40.0008, 20.0002), (40.0002, 20.0002)]) # A room drawn off in the field, not in any building. STRAY = OSMFeature(3, "way", {"indoor": "room"}, [(40.010, 20.010), (40.010, 20.011), (40.011, 20.011), (40.011, 20.010), (40.010, 20.010)]) # Two rooms as the mapper drew them, in storey tiles: a 8x6 classroom and a # 6x5 bathroom, both small enough that no kind cap cuts them back. CLASSROOM_RING = [(2, 2), (9, 2), (9, 7), (2, 7), (2, 2)] BATHROOM_RING = [(13, 3), (18, 3), (18, 7), (13, 7), (13, 3)] MAPPED = [(CLASSROOM_RING, "classroom"), (BATHROOM_RING, "bathroom")] if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: rooms_property
nodes.body_text: def rooms_property(indoor=(CLASSROOM, STRAY)): g = renderer._buildings_geojson([SCHOOL], list(indoor)) return g["features"][0]["properties"].get("rooms")

nodes.name: Attach
nodes.body_text: class Attach(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_room_lands_on_its_building_with_its_tags(self): rooms = rooms_property() self.assertEqual(len(rooms), 1) self.assertEqual(rooms[0]["room"], "classroom") self.assertEqual(len(rooms[0]["ring"]), 5) def test_a_room_in_no_building_is_dropped(self): # Only the classroom is inside the school; the stray is not attached # to anything and never reaches the build. self.assertEqual(len(rooms_property()), 1) def test_buildings_without_rooms_have_no_property(self): g = renderer._buildings_geojson([SCHOOL], []) self.assertNotIn("rooms", g["features"][0]["properties"])

nodes.name: room_covering
nodes.body_text: def room_covering(plan, x, y): """The room holding (x, y); slivers beside a mapped room may be folded into it (layout._mend_fragments), so the drawn room can cover more than was drawn - never less.""" for r in plan.rooms: if r.x0 <= x <= r.x1 and r.y0 <= y <= r.y1: return r return None

nodes.name: Cut
nodes.body_text: class Cut(unittest.TestCase): def test_the_mapped_rooms_are_cut_as_drawn_with_their_kind(self): plan = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5, mapped=MAPPED) cls = room_covering(plan, 5, 4) # the middle of the classroom self.assertIsNotNone(cls) self.assertTrue(cls.x0 <= 2 and cls.y0 <= 2 and cls.x1 >= 9 and cls.y1 >= 7, vars(cls)) self.assertEqual(cls.kind, "classroom") self.assertTrue(cls.fixed) # The bathroom has no sliver against it and lands exactly as drawn. cls2 = room_covering(plan, 15, 5) self.assertEqual((cls2.x0, cls2.y0, cls2.x1, cls2.y1), (13, 3, 18, 7)) self.assertEqual(cls2.kind, "bathroom") def test_the_rest_of_the_floor_is_still_cut_and_tiled(self): plan = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5, mapped=MAPPED) self.assertGreater(len(plan.rooms), len(MAPPED)) self.assertTrue(all(all(row) for row in plan.grid), "every tile of the floor belongs to some room") def test_untagged_rooms_are_still_placed(self): # A room the game has no name for keeps its walls; the usual rules # furnish it afterwards. bare = [([xy for xy in CLASSROOM_RING], None)] plan = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5, mapped=bare) r = room_covering(plan, 5, 4) self.assertIsNotNone(r) self.assertFalse(r.fixed) self.assertTrue(r.x0 <= 2 and r.y0 <= 2 and r.x1 >= 9 and r.y1 >= 7, vars(r)) def test_upper_floors_are_laid_out_as_ever(self): # The mapper drew one floor; an upper storey is the ordinary plan. with_mapped = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5, ground=False, mapped=MAPPED) without = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5, ground=False) self.assertEqual([(r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1, r.kind) for r in with_mapped.rooms], [(r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1, r.kind) for r in without.rooms]) def test_a_building_without_mapped_rooms_is_cut_as_ever(self): plan = build_plan(40, 24, kind="civic", seed=5) self.assertGreater(len(plan.rooms), 1) self.assertTrue(all(all(row) for row in plan.grid))

nodes.name: OctilinearRoadDefaults
nodes.body_text: class OctilinearRoadDefaults(unittest.TestCase): def test_straight_roads_are_default_but_can_be_disabled(self): self.assertEqual(Settings().straight_roads, 4) self.assertEqual(Settings.from_dict({}).straight_roads, 4) self.assertEqual(Settings.from_dict({"straight_roads": 0}).straight_roads, 0) # By name, not by position: counted off the end of the argument list # this moved every time the renderer gained a knob, and said nothing # about straight roads when it did. straight = inspect.signature(renderer.render).parameters["straight_roads"] self.assertEqual(straight.default, 4) def test_curves_become_straight_runs_and_keep_shared_junctions(self): projection = SimpleNamespace( width=128, height=128, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat), to_latlon=lambda x, y: (y, x), ) main = osm.OSMFeature( 1, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [(10, 10), (20, 18), (30, 25), (40, 34), (50, 45)]) side = osm.OSMFeature( 2, "way", {"highway": "residential"}, [(20, 18), (25, 28), (30, 38)]) count = octilinear.straighten_roads( [main, side], projection, osm.classify, renderer._is_polygon) self.assertEqual(count, 2) self.assertLess(Point(*side.geometry[0]).distance(LineString(main.geometry)), 1e-8) for feature in (main, side): pixels = [projection.to_px(*point) for point in feature.geometry] for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(pixels, pixels[1:]): dx, dy = round(x1 - x0), round(y1 - y0) self.assertTrue(dx == 0 or dy == 0 or abs(dx) == abs(dy))

nodes.name: StraighteningKnowsWhenToStop
nodes.body_text: class StraighteningKnowsWhenToStop(unittest.TestCase): """The fit has no limit of its own on how far it may drag the town, and on a big map it used it: a main road at a slight angle straightened by moving its far end a couple of blocks, which cut the road beyond it off.""" def projection(self, side=4000): return SimpleNamespace(width=side, height=side, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat), to_latlon=lambda x, y: (y, x)) def test_nothing_is_dragged_further_than_the_cap(self): import math projection = self.projection() # Two thousand tiles of road at three degrees: straight on the tiles # only if one end moves fifty tiles. points = [(x, 100 + x * math.tan(math.radians(3))) for x in range(0, 2001, 100)] road = osm.OSMFeature(1, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [(y, x) for x, y in points]) octilinear.straighten_roads([road], projection, osm.classify, renderer._is_polygon) drawn = [projection.to_px(*p) for p in road.geometry] for x, y in ((0, 100.0), (2000, 204.8)): nearest = min(abs(y - py) for px, py in drawn if abs(px - x) < 1e-6) self.assertLessEqual(nearest, octilinear.MAX_MOVE_TILES) # ...and it is still drawn the way the game draws roads. for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(drawn, drawn[1:]): dx, dy = round(x1 - x0), round(y1 - y0) self.assertTrue(dx == 0 or dy == 0 or abs(dx) == abs(dy)) def roundabout(self, tags): import math projection = self.projection(600) ring = [(300 + 7 * math.sin(a * math.pi / 6), 300 + 7 * math.cos(a * math.pi / 6)) for a in range(12)] ring.append(ring[0]) arcs = [osm.OSMFeature(i, "way", dict(tags), [(y, x) for x, y in ring[i * 3:i * 3 + 4]]) for i in range(4)] arms = [] for i, (dx, dy) in enumerate(((1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), (0, -1))): at = ring[i * 3] far = (at[0] + dx * 180 + (4 if dy else 0), at[1] + dy * 180) arms.append(osm.OSMFeature(10 + i, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [(at[1], at[0]), (far[1], far[0])])) was = [list(arc.geometry) for arc in arcs] octilinear.straighten_roads(arcs + arms, projection, osm.classify, renderer._is_polygon) return arcs, arms, was def test_a_roundabout_is_left_exactly_as_it_was_drawn(self): # Fitted to the eight directions a roundabout came out as a few # crossed triangles. It has no straight sides to fit. arcs, arms, was = self.roundabout({"highway": "primary", "junction": "roundabout"}) self.assertEqual([arc.geometry for arc in arcs], was) def test_the_roads_into_a_roundabout_still_meet_it(self): arcs, arms, _was = self.roundabout({"highway": "primary", "junction": "roundabout"}) on_the_ring = {point for arc in arcs for point in arc.geometry} for arm in arms: self.assertIn(arm.geometry[0], on_the_ring)

nodes.body_text: """Three things seen in game in a thin office and a house (Piqua, 2026-10-31). - A whiteboard is three tiles of wall; windows kept off its first tile only and went through the other two. - An office desk against a wall had its chair two tiles off, or across the room. - A kitchen's one-tile tail took counters and a sink, a bathroom's one-square nub the toilet: nowhere to stand to use them. """ import random import unittest from knoxbuild import layout as L SHAPES = [(8, 26), (3, 20), (6, 16), (5, 12), (10, 14), (4, 9), (12, 30), (7, 7)] if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: class OfficeSeating(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.built = list(buildings()) def test_no_window_through_a_wall_piece(self): for b in self.built: for storey in b.storeys: windows = set(storey.windows) for role, x, y, o in storey.furniture: if not L._is_wall_piece(role): continue for cx, cy in L._cells_for(role, x, y, o): self.assertNotIn(L._wall_edge(cx, cy, o), windows, (role, x, y, o)) def test_a_chair_at_every_desk_that_has_one_in_its_room(self): seated = total = 0 for b in self.built: for storey in b.storeys: furn, grid = storey.furniture, storey.grid chairs = {(x, y) for role, x, y, _o in furn if role == "office_chair"} for role, x, y, o in furn: if role not in L.DESK_ROLES: continue here = grid[y][x] if not any(grid[cy][cx] == here for cx, cy in chairs): continue # no chair in its room to give it sx, sy = L._STEP[L._OPPOSITE[o]] front = {(cx + sx, cy + sy) for cx, cy in L._tiles_under(role, x, y, o)} total += 1 seated += bool(front & chairs) # A desk can have no free tile in front of it; nearly all have one. self.assertGreater(total, 20) self.assertGreaterEqual(seated / total, 0.9, (seated, total)) def test_nothing_stands_on_a_one_tile_wide_spot(self): for b in self.built: for storey in b.storeys: g, w, h = storey.grid, storey.width, storey.height for role, x, y, o in storey.furniture: if not L._blocks(role) or role.startswith("elevator"): continue for cx, cy in L._tiles_under(role, x, y, o): if 0 <= cx < w and 0 <= cy < h and g[cy][cx]: self.assertFalse(L._narrow(g, cx, cy), (role, cx, cy))

nodes.body_text: """Offices are fitted out across the floor; clothes racks stand on walls only.""" import unittest from knoxbuild import layout from knoxbuild.uses import use_of if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: touches_wall
nodes.body_text: def touches_wall(plan, cell) -> bool: here = layout._room_at(plan, *cell) return any(layout._room_at(plan, cell[0] + dx, cell[1] + dy) != here for dx, dy in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)))

nodes.body_text: def office_rooms(seeds=range(30), size=(36, 28)): for seed in seeds: plan = layout.build_building(*size, kind="offices", street="S", seed=seed).storeys[0] for idx, room in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1): if room.kind == "office" and min(room.x1 - room.x0, room.y1 - room.y0) + 1 >= 7: yield plan, idx

nodes.name: cells_of
nodes.body_text: def cells_of(plan, idx, prefix): return [c for role, x, y, o in plan.furniture if role.startswith(prefix) for c in layout._cells_for(role, x, y, o) if layout._room_at(plan, *c) == idx]

nodes.name: test_osm_cache_age.py
nodes.body_text: """An older download is still the map's roads. The download kept beside a map is stamped with the filter list it was fetched with, and a map drawn before that list grew has an older stamp. Fetching is right to refuse it - the new filters are there to bring back things the old ones never asked for - but the steps after the map is drawn only ever read this file. Turning it away there did not get the newer tags: the paper map came out with the buildings on it and not one road, river or wood, and every shop and surgery mapped as a point was lost with it. """ import gzip import json import os import tempfile import unittest from generator import osm ROAD = {"osm_id": 1, "kind": "way", "tags": {"highway": "residential"}, "geometry": [[1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 2.0]], "role_geoms": []} BOX = (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: write_cache
nodes.body_text: def write_cache(path, bbox, filters, features=()): with gzip.open(path, "wt", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"filters": filters, "bbox": list(bbox), "features": list(features)}, f)

nodes.name: AnOlderDownload
nodes.body_text: class AnOlderDownload(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "m_osm.json.gz") def test_fetching_still_refuses_one_made_with_an_older_filter_list(self): write_cache(self.path, BOX, osm.FILTERS_VERSION - 1, [ROAD]) self.assertIsNone(osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX)) def test_reading_takes_whatever_is_there(self): write_cache(self.path, BOX, osm.FILTERS_VERSION - 4, [ROAD]) got = osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX, filters=None) self.assertEqual(len(got or []), 1) self.assertEqual(got[0].tags, {"highway": "residential"}) def test_a_download_of_the_current_list_is_taken_either_way(self): write_cache(self.path, BOX, osm.FILTERS_VERSION, [ROAD]) self.assertEqual(len(osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX) or []), 1) self.assertEqual(len(osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX, filters=None) or []), 1) def test_a_download_of_somewhere_else_is_refused_however_it_is_read(self): write_cache(self.path, (9.0, 9.0, 9.5, 9.5), osm.FILTERS_VERSION, [ROAD]) self.assertIsNone(osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX)) self.assertIsNone(osm.load_cache(self.path, BOX, filters=None)) def test_the_steps_that_only_read_ask_for_whatever_is_there(self): # The rule itself, in the two places that read the download: a build # and a paper map never fetch, so neither may insist on a version. import inspect from knoxbuild import build, worldmap for module in (build, worldmap): source = inspect.getsource(module) for line in source.splitlines(): if "load_cache(" in line and "def " not in line: self.assertIn("filters=None", line, f"{module.__name__}: {line}")

One operator counted 22,515 requests in a day, 14,608 of # them 504s, from exactly that. nodes.body_text: """The Overpass client is a guest on shared servers: it rests a server that fails, leaves one that refuses it alone, honours Retry-After and asks one at a time.""" import os import tempfile import time import unittest from unittest import mock from generator import osm A, B = "https://a.example/api/interpreter", "https://b.example/api/interpreter" if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: def reply(status, headers=None, text="", payload=None): r = mock.Mock() r.status_code = status r.headers = headers or {} r.text = text r.json.return_value = payload if payload is not None else {"elements": []} return r

nodes.name: Manners

time.time() osm._note_down(A) second = osm._cooling[A] - time.time() self.assertGreater(second, first * 1.5) osm._note_down(B, retry_after=1800) self.assertGreater(osm._cooling[B] - time.time(), 1700) osm._note_up(A) osm._note_down(A) self.assertLess(osm._cooling[A] - nodes.name: test_pbf_local.py
nodes.body_text: """A picked extract, and the check that says whether it will work. A regional file covers a place; a developer may have cut one by hand, or downloaded a county rather than the state. Choosing it takes the guess out, and checking it says what is in the file before a map is built from nothing. """ import os import shutil import tempfile import unittest from unittest import mock import osmium from generator import extract, pbfcheck if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: tiny_pbf
nodes.body_text: def tiny_pbf(path, buildings=True, roads=True, extra=()): """A square of nodes, one building, one street, inside 10,20.""" w = osmium.SimpleWriter(path) nodes = [(10.000, 20.000), (10.002, 20.000), (10.002, 20.002), (10.000, 20.002)] for i, (lat, lon) in enumerate(nodes, 1): w.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=i, location=(lon, lat))) if buildings: w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=10, nodes=[1, 2, 3, 4, 1], tags={"building": "yes"})) if roads: w.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=5, location=(20.001, 10.001))) w.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=11, nodes=[1, 5], tags={"highway": "residential"})) for osm_id, tags in extra: w.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=osm_id, location=(20.0015, 10.0015), tags=tags)) w.close() return path

nodes.body_text: class TheCheck(Temp): def test_a_good_file_is_usable(self): result = pbfcheck.check(self.build()) self.assertTrue(result["ok"], result["problems"]) self.assertGreaterEqual(result["stats"]["nodes"], 4) self.assertEqual(result["tags"].get("building"), 1) self.assertIn("usable", pbfcheck.report_text(result)) def test_a_file_with_no_buildings_is_refused(self): result = pbfcheck.check(self.build(buildings=False)) self.assertFalse(result["ok"]) self.assertTrue(any("buildings" in p for p in result["problems"])) def test_a_file_with_no_roads_is_refused(self): result = pbfcheck.check(self.build(roads=False)) self.assertTrue(any("roads" in p for p in result["problems"])) def test_an_empty_file_is_refused(self): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "empty.osm.pbf") open(path, "wb").close() result = pbfcheck.check(path) self.assertFalse(result["ok"]) self.assertTrue(any("empty" in p for p in result["problems"])) def test_something_that_is_not_an_extract_is_refused(self): path = os.path.join(self.dir, "notes.osm.pbf") with open(path, "wb") as fh: fh.write(b"this is not an extract, it is a text file\n" * 40) result = pbfcheck.check(path) self.assertFalse(result["ok"]) self.assertTrue(any("header" in p for p in result["problems"])) def test_a_file_that_misses_the_area_is_refused(self): result = pbfcheck.check(self.build(), bbox=(40.0, 50.0, 40.1, 50.1)) self.assertFalse(result["ok"]) self.assertTrue(any("does not overlap" in p for p in result["problems"])) def test_a_file_that_covers_the_area_passes(self): result = pbfcheck.check(self.build(), bbox=(10.0005, 20.0005, 10.0015, 20.0015)) self.assertTrue(result["ok"], result["problems"])

nodes.name: test_place_while_compiling.py
nodes.body_text: """A map cannot be moved while it compiles. The compile reads the map's place once, at the start. Ticking Standalone during it moved the map to cell 0,0 under the running compile, which then wrote lots named for the old place, and the install refused them as "moved since it was last compiled" (West_Union and Washington Court House, 2026-10-30/31). """ import tempfile import unittest from pathlib import Path from unittest import mock import app as A from web import common from web.jobs import _COMPILE, _PROGRESS_LOCK if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: PlaceWhileCompiling
nodes.body_text: class PlaceWhileCompiling(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): A.app.config["TESTING"] = True self.client = A.app.test_client() self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup) out = Path(self.tmp.name) (out / "Town").mkdir() patcher = mock.patch.object(common, "OUTPUT_DIR", out) patcher.start() self.addCleanup(patcher.stop) self.map_dir = out / "Town" def _compiling(self, state): with _PROGRESS_LOCK: _COMPILE["Town"] = {"state": state} self.addCleanup(lambda: _COMPILE.pop("Town", None)) def test_standalone_and_moves_are_refused_while_compiling(self): self._compiling("running") for method, body in (("post", {"standalone": True}), ("post", {"cell_x": 90, "cell_y": 3}), ("delete", None)): res = getattr(self.client, method)("/api/placement/Town", json=body) self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 409, (method, body)) self.assertIn("compiling", res.get_json()["error"]) self.assertFalse((self.map_dir / "placement.json").exists()) def test_allowed_once_the_compile_is_done(self): self._compiling("done") res = self.client.post("/api/placement/Town", json={"standalone": True}) self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 200) self.assertTrue((self.map_dir / "placement.json").exists()) def test_looking_is_always_allowed(self): self._compiling("running") self.assertEqual(self.client.get("/api/placement/Town").status_code, 200)

nodes.name: test_placement.py
nodes.body_text: """Where a map stands in the game's world (knoxbuild/placement.py). Moving a map rewrites files somebody's built town is made of, so what matters is that it changes exactly what carries the world origin and nothing else - the test is a round trip, byte for byte - that it is honest about needing the map compiled again, and that nothing can quietly land one map on top of another. """ import hashlib import json import os import shutil import tempfile import unittest from pathlib import Path from unittest import mock from knoxbuild import placement as P from knoxbuild.world import CELL_SIZE, choose_origin PZW = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <world version="1.0" width="4" height="3"> <GenerateLots> <worldOrigin origin="70,0"/> </GenerateLots> <cell x="0" y="0"> <lot x="12" y="30" level="0" width="20" height="16" map="buildings/a.tbx"/> </cell> </world> """ WORLDMAP = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <world version="1.0"> <cell x="70" y="0"> <feature> <geometry type="Polygon"> <coordinates> <point x="0" y="0"/> <point x="0" y="300"/> </coordinates> </geometry> <properties> <property name="water" value="river"/> </properties> </feature> </cell> <cell x="71" y="2"> </cell> </world> """ STREETS = """<streets version="1"> <street name="Main Street" width="4"> <points> <point x="21000.0" y="150.5"/> <point x="21300.4" y="150.5"/> </points> </street> </streets> """ ANNOTATIONS = """return function(mapUI) \tlocal symbolsAPI = mapUI.javaObject:getAPIv3():getSymbolsAPIv2() \tsymbol = symbolsAPI:addUntranslatedText("St Mary's", "text-building", 21137, 524) \tsymbol:setScale(0.600) end """ if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: sha
nodes.body_text: def sha(path): with open(path, "rb") as f: return hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()

nodes.name: AMapOnDisk
nodes.body_text: class AMapOnDisk(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() for name, text in (("town.pzw", PZW), ("worldmap.xml", WORLDMAP), ("streets.xml", STREETS), ("worldmap-annotations.lua", ANNOTATIONS)): with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f: f.write(text) with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "town_info.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"cells_x": 4, "cells_y": 3}, f) def compiled(self, cell_x=82, cell_y=0): lots = os.path.join(self.dir, "lots") os.makedirs(lots, exist_ok=True) for name in (f"{cell_x}_{cell_y}.lotheader", f"world_{cell_x}_{cell_y}.lotpack", f"chunkdata_{cell_x}_{cell_y}.bin"): open(os.path.join(lots, name), "w").close() def text(self, name): with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name), encoding="utf-8") as f: return f.read() def files(self): return {name: sha(os.path.join(self.dir, name)) for name in sorted(os.listdir(self.dir)) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.dir, name))}

nodes.body_text: class MovingOne(AMapOnDisk): def test_everything_that_carries_the_origin_is_moved(self): done = P.move(self.dir, "town", (120, 40)) self.assertEqual(set(done["rewrote"]), {"town.pzw", "worldmap.xml", "streets.xml", "worldmap-annotations.lua"}) pzw, paper, streets, notes = ( self.text(n) for n in ("town.pzw", "worldmap.xml", "streets.xml", "worldmap-annotations.lua")) self.assertIn('<worldOrigin origin="120,40"/>', pzw) # The paper map's points are relative to their cell, so only the cell # numbers move: 70,0 -> 120,40 and 71,2 -> 121,42. self.assertIn('<cell x="120" y="40">', paper) self.assertIn('<cell x="121" y="42">', paper) self.assertIn('<point x="0" y="300"/>', paper) # Streets and labels are world tiles: 50 cells east, 40 south. self.assertIn(f'<point x="{21000.0 + 50 * CELL_SIZE:.1f}" ' f'y="{150.5 + 40 * CELL_SIZE:.1f}"/>', streets) self.assertIn(f'"text-building", {21137 + 50 * CELL_SIZE}, ' f'{524 + 40 * CELL_SIZE})', notes) def test_nothing_else_in_the_map_is_touched(self): before = self.files() P.move(self.dir, "town", (120, 40)) after = self.files() unchanged = {n for n in before if before[n] == after.get(n)} self.assertIn("town_info.json", unchanged) def test_moving_it_back_gives_exactly_what_was_there(self): # It rewrites somebody's built town in place, so a move has to be a # change of numbers and nothing else - not a reformatting of the file. before = self.files() P.move(self.dir, "town", (133, 41)) P.move(self.dir, "town", (70, 0)) after = self.files() for name, digest in before.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertEqual(after[name], digest) def test_a_map_that_is_compiled_has_to_be_compiled_again(self): self.compiled() self.assertFalse(P.move(self.dir, "town", (70, 0))["needsCompile"]) self.assertTrue(P.move(self.dir, "town", (120, 40))["needsCompile"]) def test_a_map_that_was_never_built_only_needs_building(self): os.remove(os.path.join(self.dir, "town.pzw")) done = P.move(self.dir, "town", (120, 40)) self.assertTrue(done["needsBuild"]) self.assertFalse(done["needsCompile"]) self.assertEqual(done["rewrote"], []) self.assertEqual(P.saved(self.dir), (120, 40)) def test_the_lots_say_where_the_map_really_is(self): self.compiled(cell_x=82, cell_y=0) # 70 cells = 21000 tiles / 256 self.assertEqual(P.compiled_corner(self.dir), (82, 0)) self.assertTrue(P.lots_match(self.dir, (70, 0))) self.assertFalse(P.lots_match(self.dir, (71, 0))) def test_a_build_keeps_the_place_chosen_for_the_map(self): P.save(self.dir, (12, 34)) self.assertEqual(P.settled_origin(self.dir, "town", 5, 5), (12, 34)) def test_a_build_keeps_where_the_map_already_stands(self): self.compiled(cell_x=82, cell_y=0) self.assertEqual(P.settled_origin(self.dir, "town", 70, 1), (70, 0)) def test_handing_the_choice_back_puts_the_map_where_it_would_have_gone(self): # Forgetting the choice is not enough: the project itself says where # the map is, so a map that was moved would stay moved. before = self.files() P.move(self.dir, "town", (150, 80)) done = P.unplace(self.dir, "town") self.assertTrue(done["automatic"]) self.assertIsNone(P.saved(self.dir)) self.assertEqual(P.project_origin(self.dir, "town"), (70, 0)) self.assertEqual(self.files(), before) def test_a_map_with_nothing_compiled_cannot_be_in_the_wrong_place(self): self.assertIsNone(P.compiled_corner(self.dir)) self.assertTrue(P.lots_match(self.dir, (500, 500)))

nodes.body_text:
class LeftoversFromWhereTheMapUsedToBe(unittest.TestCase): """Compiling after a move writes the new lots beside the old ones. The old ones are newer than everything they were compiled from, so nothing called them stale: the corner they named stayed the place the map had left, and install went on refusing it as "moved since it was last compiled" however often it was compiled. Ticking Standalone parks a map at cell 0,0, so putting it back somewhere real is exactly that. """ def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.dir, True) os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.dir, "lots")) # A project's .pzw is named after its folder, everywhere in KnoxMap. self.pzw = os.path.join(self.dir, os.path.basename(self.dir) + ".pzw") self.write_pzw("90,0") def write_pzw(self, origin, width=4, height=3): with open(self.pzw, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
' f'<world version="1.0" width="{width}" height="{height}">
' f' <GenerateLots>
 <worldOrigin origin="{origin}"/>
' ' </GenerateLots>
</world>
') def lots(self, x, y): for name in (f"{x}_{y}.lotheader", f"chunkdata_{x}_{y}.bin", f"world_{x}_{y}.lotpack"): open(os.path.join(self.dir, "lots", name), "w").close() def left(self): return sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(self.dir, "lots"))) def test_lots_from_a_place_the_map_has_left_go(self): from tools.compile_map import clear_outside_world self.lots(0, 0) self.lots(1, 0) # where Standalone had parked the map self.lots(105, 0) # 90 cells = 27000 tiles, over 256 self.assertEqual(clear_outside_world(Path(self.dir)), 6) self.assertEqual(self.left(), ["105_0.lotheader", "chunkdata_105_0.bin", "world_105_0.lotpack"]) def test_the_lots_where_the_map_stands_now_stay(self): from tools.compile_map import clear_outside_world self.lots(105, 0) self.lots(109, 0) # the last of four cells across: 27000..28199 tiles self.assertEqual(clear_outside_world(Path(self.dir)), 0) self.assertEqual(len(self.left()), 6) def test_a_map_at_the_corner_keeps_the_lots_at_the_corner(self): from tools.compile_map import clear_outside_world self.write_pzw("0,0") self.lots(0, 0) self.lots(105, 0) # from before it was put at the corner self.assertEqual(clear_outside_world(Path(self.dir)), 3) self.assertEqual(self.left(), ["0_0.lotheader", "chunkdata_0_0.bin", "world_0_0.lotpack"]) def test_a_project_that_says_nothing_is_left_alone(self): from tools.compile_map import clear_outside_world self.lots(0, 0) os.remove(self.pzw) self.assertEqual(clear_outside_world(Path(self.dir)), 0) self.assertEqual(len(self.left()), 3)

nodes.name: WhereAMapReallyIs
nodes.body_text: class WhereAMapReallyIs(AMapOnDisk): """The choice, the build and the lots, answered in one place. Each caller used to read those three records itself, in its own order, which is how one could believe a map was at 70,0 while another read 0,0 - and why install refused a map as "moved since it was last compiled" while the panel above the button said it was ready. """ def test_where_its_own_files_say_it_is(self): here = P.where_is(self.dir, "town") self.assertEqual(here["cell"], P.project_origin(self.dir, "town")) self.assertEqual(here["source"], "built") self.assertIsNone(here["chosen"]) def test_the_place_chosen_wins_over_where_it_was_built(self): P.save(self.dir, (12, 34)) here = P.where_is(self.dir, "town") self.assertEqual(here["cell"], (12, 34)) self.assertEqual(here["built"], P.project_origin(self.dir, "town")) self.assertEqual(here["chosen"], (12, 34)) self.assertEqual(here["source"], "chosen") def test_the_lots_are_reported_separately_from_where_the_map_is_going(self): # Compiled at the corner, which is where Standalone parks a map; the # project itself says 70,0, whose lots belong at 82,0. self.compiled(cell_x=0, cell_y=0) here = P.where_is(self.dir, "town") self.assertEqual(here["cell"], (70, 0)) self.assertEqual(here["compiled"], (0, 0)) self.assertFalse(here["matches"]) def test_lots_where_the_map_is_going_do_match(self): self.compiled(cell_x=82, cell_y=0) # 70 cells of 300 tiles is lot 82 self.assertTrue(P.where_is(self.dir, "town")["matches"]) def test_moving_it_is_what_changes_the_answer(self): self.compiled() before = P.where_is(self.dir, "town")["cell"] P.move(self.dir, "town", (120, 40)) after = P.where_is(self.dir, "town") self.assertNotEqual(before, after["cell"]) self.assertFalse(after["matches"]) def test_the_window_is_told_which_record_decided(self): P.set_standalone(self.dir, "town", True) world = P.layout(self.dir, "town") self.assertEqual(world["source"], "chosen") self.assertEqual(world["map"]["x"], 0)

nodes.body_text: class TheWorldAsItReallyIs(unittest.TestCase): """Maps are drawn cell by cell: Knox County is 4,065 cells with bites out of it, and a box says nothing about what is free next to it.""" def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() def cells(self, pairs): for x, y in pairs: open(os.path.join(self.dir, f"{x}_{y}.lotheader"), "w").close() def test_its_own_installed_copy_is_not_another_map(self): mods = os.path.join(self.dir, "mods") mine = os.path.join(mods, "town", "common", "media", "maps", "town") other = os.path.join(mods, "village", "common", "media", "maps", "village") for folder in (mine, other): os.makedirs(folder) open(os.path.join(folder, "0_0.lotheader"), "w").close() found = [(mine, "installed", "town"), (other, "installed", "village")] with mock.patch.object(P, "_map_folders", return_value=found): self.assertEqual([m["name"] for m in P.world_maps()], ["town", "village"]) self.assertEqual([m["name"] for m in P.world_maps(os.path.join(mods, "town"))], ["village"]) def test_a_row_of_cells_is_one_run(self): self.assertEqual(P._runs([(3, 0), (4, 0), (5, 0)]), [[0, 3, 5]]) def test_a_gap_in_a_row_is_two_runs(self): self.assertEqual(P._runs([(3, 0), (4, 0), (9, 0)]), [[0, 3, 4], [0, 9, 9]]) def test_every_row_is_its_own_runs_in_order(self): self.assertEqual(P._runs([(1, 2), (0, 1), (1, 1)]), [[1, 0, 1], [2, 1, 1]]) def test_a_map_folder_is_read_as_its_real_shape(self): self.cells([(10, 4), (11, 4), (10, 5), (40, 40)]) found = P._map_folder(self.dir, "installed", "town") self.assertEqual((found["x"], found["y"]), (10, 4)) self.assertEqual((found["w"], found["h"]), (31, 37)) self.assertEqual(found["cells"], 4) self.assertEqual(found["runs"], [[4, 10, 11], [5, 10, 10], [40, 40, 40]]) def test_a_folder_with_no_cells_in_it_is_not_a_map(self): open(os.path.join(self.dir, "map.info"), "w").close() self.assertIsNone(P._map_folder(self.dir, "vanilla", "Brandenburg, KY")) def test_a_folder_that_is_not_there_is_not_a_map(self): self.assertEqual(P._cells_of(os.path.join(self.dir, "nowhere")), []) self.assertIsNone(P._map_folder(os.path.join(self.dir, "nowhere"), "vanilla", "nothing")) def test_the_window_is_given_the_grid_both_sides_are_measured_in(self): # The picture is drawn in tiles because the two grids do not divide # into each other: maps are placed on 300s and compiled into 256s. self.assertEqual(P.COMPILED_CELL, 256) self.assertEqual(CELL_SIZE, 300)

class ThePictureOfAMap(unittest.TestCase): """The game ships a picture of each of its maps as a pyramid of tiles. Putting one on the world is only worth anything if it lands exactly where the map really is, so the bounds are read rather than guessed.""" def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() def pyramid(self, bounds="bounds=0 0 19968 16128", levels=(0, 1, 2), tiles=((0, 0), (1, 0))): import zipfile from PIL import Image path = os.path.join(self.dir, P.PYRAMID) with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as zf: zf.writestr("pyramid.txt", f"VERSION=1
{bounds}
imageSize=1 1
") for level in levels: for x, y in tiles: shot = os.path.join(self.dir, "tile.png") Image.new("RGB", (256, 256), (10 + level, 20, 30)).save(shot) zf.write(shot, f"{level}/tile{x}x{y}.png") return path def test_the_bounds_are_read_from_the_pyramid_itself(self): self.assertEqual(P._pyramid_bounds("VERSION=1
bounds=0 0 19968 16128
"), (0, 0, 19968, 16128)) self.assertEqual(P._pyramid_bounds("bounds=512 256 1024 768"), (512, 256, 1024, 768)) def test_a_pyramid_that_says_nothing_about_bounds_is_not_used(self): for bad in ("", "VERSION=1", "bounds=1 2 3", "bounds=a b c d"): with self.subTest(bad=bad): self.assertIsNone(P._pyramid_bounds(bad)) def test_the_smallest_level_is_the_one_assembled(self): # Every level is the whole map; the highest number is the smallest # picture of it, which is all a window the size of a postcard needs. self.pyramid(levels=(0, 1, 2)) where = P.build_picture(self.dir, os.path.join(self.dir, "out", "m.png")) self.assertEqual((where["x"], where["y"], where["w"], where["h"]), (0, 0, 19968, 16128)) # Level 2 is a quarter of the tiles across: 19968 / 4 = 4992. self.assertEqual(where["px"], [19968 // 4, 16128 // 4]) self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(where["file"])) def test_a_map_with_no_pyramid_has_no_picture(self): self.assertIsNone(P.build_picture(self.dir, os.path.join(self.dir, "x.png"))) def test_a_broken_pyramid_is_no_picture_rather_than_a_crash(self): with open(os.path.join(self.dir, P.PYRAMID), "w") as f: f.write("not a zip") self.assertIsNone(P.build_picture(self.dir, os.path.join(self.dir, "x.png"))) def test_a_pyramid_of_nothing_is_no_picture(self): self.pyramid(bounds="bounds=0 0 0 0") self.assertIsNone(P.build_picture(self.dir, os.path.join(self.dir, "x.png"))) def test_a_name_that_could_escape_the_cache_cannot(self): for bad in ("../../etc/passwd", "Muldraugh, KY", "a/b"): with self.subTest(bad=bad): safe = P.safe_file(bad) self.assertNotIn("/", safe) self.assertNotIn("\", safe) self.assertNotIn("..", safe) def test_the_window_is_only_told_about_pictures_it_can_have(self): # Without a cache to build them in there are no pictures, and the # world is drawn as the shape of its cells. maps = [{"name": "Muldraugh, KY", "picture": True}] self.assertEqual(P._with_pictures(maps, None)[0]["picture"], False)

nodes.name: test_presets.py
nodes.body_text: """Hand-built buildings, kept and stamped onto plots. The promise a preset makes is narrow and absolute: the building somebody built is the building that appears. So what is worth checking is that nothing is done to the file, that one is only chosen where it genuinely fits, and that the same plot gets the same building every time the map is built - a preset that moved around on a rebuild would be worse than no preset at all. """ import os import tempfile import unittest from knoxbuild import presets if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: tbx
nodes.body_text:
def tbx(width, height, floors=3, rooms=4): return ('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
' f'<building version="4" width="{width}" height="{height}" ' 'ExteriorWall="19">
' + "".join(' <room Name="livingroom"/>
' for _ in range(rooms)) + "".join(" <floor>
 </floor>
" for _ in range(floors)) + "</building>
")

nodes.body_text: class Reading(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_building_file_is_measured_off_its_header(self): about = presets.measure(tbx(12, 10, floors=4, rooms=13)) self.assertEqual((about["width"], about["height"]), (12, 10)) self.assertEqual(about["rooms"], 13) # The generator writes a floor per storey and one more for the roof. self.assertEqual(about["storeys"], 3) def test_a_single_storey_building_is_one_storey(self): self.assertEqual(presets.measure(tbx(8, 8, floors=2))["storeys"], 1) def test_anything_that_is_not_a_building_file_is_not_one(self): for bad in ("", "hello", "<building>", '<building width="0" height="5">', '<building height="5">'): with self.subTest(bad=bad): self.assertIsNone(presets.measure(bad)) def test_a_name_that_could_escape_the_folder_cannot(self): for bad in ("../../etc/passwd", "a/b", "a\\b", "..", " "): with self.subTest(bad=bad): clean = presets.safe_name(bad) self.assertNotIn("/", clean) self.assertNotIn("\\", clean) self.assertNotIn("..", clean)

nodes.name: TheLibrary
nodes.body_text: class TheLibrary(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() def test_what_goes_in_is_what_comes_out(self): # The whole point of a hand-built building: nothing happens to it. text = tbx(12, 10) presets.save(self.dir, "Brick Cottage", text) self.assertEqual(presets.read(self.dir, "Brick Cottage"), text) def test_saving_something_that_is_not_a_building_is_refused(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): presets.save(self.dir, "Nope", "hello") def test_a_preset_needs_a_name(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): presets.save(self.dir, " ", tbx(4, 4)) def test_the_library_lists_what_is_there_smallest_first(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Big", tbx(30, 30)) presets.save(self.dir, "Small", tbx(6, 6)) self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in presets.library(self.dir)], ["Small", "Big"]) def test_a_stray_file_in_the_folder_is_not_offered(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Real", tbx(6, 6)) with open(os.path.join(presets.folder(self.dir), "notes.txt"), "w") as f: f.write("shopping list") with open(os.path.join(presets.folder(self.dir), "broken.tbx"), "w") as f: f.write("not a building") self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in presets.library(self.dir)], ["Real"]) def test_a_library_that_is_not_there_is_empty_rather_than_an_error(self): self.assertEqual(presets.library(os.path.join(self.dir, "nowhere")), []) def test_one_can_be_thrown_away(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Gone", tbx(6, 6)) self.assertTrue(presets.remove(self.dir, "Gone")) self.assertEqual(presets.library(self.dir), []) self.assertFalse(presets.remove(self.dir, "Gone"))

nodes.body_text: class Choosing(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.lib = [{"name": "Shed", "width": 4, "height": 4}, {"name": "Cottage", "width": 12, "height": 10}, {"name": "Villa", "width": 12, "height": 10}, {"name": "Hall", "width": 40, "height": 30}] def test_only_what_actually_fits_is_offered(self): fits = presets.fitting(self.lib, 12, 10) self.assertEqual({p["name"] for p in fits}, {"Shed", "Cottage", "Villa"}) def test_a_preset_is_never_stretched_to_fit(self): # It is used at the size it was built, so a plot too small gets none. self.assertEqual(presets.fitting(self.lib, 3, 3), []) self.assertIsNone(presets.choose(self.lib, 3, 3, 0)) def test_the_footprint_has_to_fit_the_way_round_it_is(self): # The .tbx is not rotated, so a 12x10 cottage does not go on a 10x12 # plot however near the two are in area. Only the shed fits there. self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in presets.fitting(self.lib, 10, 12)], ["Shed"]) def test_the_biggest_that_fits_wins(self): # A plot meant for a cottage should not get a shed on it. self.assertIn(presets.choose(self.lib, 12, 10, 0)["name"], ("Cottage", "Villa")) self.assertEqual(presets.choose(self.lib, 40, 30, 0)["name"], "Hall") def test_the_same_plot_gets_the_same_building_every_time(self): # A rebuild that moved the hand-built houses around would be worse # than not having them. for seed in (0, 1, 7, 99, 1234): with self.subTest(seed=seed): first = presets.choose(self.lib, 12, 10, seed)["name"] again = presets.choose(self.lib, 12, 10, seed)["name"] self.assertEqual(first, again) def test_different_plots_do_not_all_get_the_same_one(self): # A street of identical plots should not be a street of one house. picked = {presets.choose(self.lib, 12, 10, s)["name"] for s in range(8)} self.assertEqual(picked, {"Cottage", "Villa"}) def test_an_empty_library_chooses_nothing(self): self.assertIsNone(presets.choose([], 50, 50, 0))
