nodes.name: ForAKindOfBuilding
nodes.body_text: class ForAKindOfBuilding(unittest.TestCase): """A preset that stands in for a sort of building, wherever one is built. The other half of the promise: a hand-built police station should be the police station on every map, without the mapper drawing a zone round each one. So what matters is that the kind is honoured - a shed is not stamped as a police station - and that the switch really is a switch. """ def setUp(self): self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.lib = [{"name": "Shed", "width": 4, "height": 4, "kind": "shed"}, {"name": "Station", "width": 12, "height": 10, "kind": "police"}, {"name": "Big Station", "width": 30, "height": 20, "kind": "police"}, {"name": "Anything", "width": 10, "height": 8, "kind": ""}] def test_every_kind_offered_is_one_the_generator_can_recognise(self): from knoxbuild.build import SPECIAL_BY_VALUE offered = {entry["id"] for entry in presets.kinds()} self.assertEqual(offered, {"house", "shed"} | set(SPECIAL_BY_VALUE.values())) self.assertTrue(all(entry["label"] for entry in presets.kinds())) def test_only_presets_built_for_the_kind_are_used_for_it(self): self.assertEqual([p["name"] for p in presets.for_kind(self.lib, "police")], ["Station", "Big Station"]) self.assertEqual(presets.for_kind(self.lib, "church"), []) def test_the_kind_is_preferred_and_any_building_is_the_fallback(self): # A plot big enough for the station gets the station... self.assertEqual( presets.choose_for_kind(self.lib, "police", 12, 10, 0)["name"], "Station") # ...and one too small for any police station falls back to the # preset built for no kind in particular, rather than to nothing. self.assertEqual( presets.choose_for_kind(self.lib, "police", 10, 8, 0)["name"], "Anything") def test_a_preset_for_another_kind_is_never_stamped_as_this_one(self): # The shed fits every plot here and is still never a police station. for width, height in ((4, 4), (6, 5), (9, 7)): with self.subTest(plot=(width, height)): self.assertIsNone( presets.choose_for_kind(self.lib, "police", width, height, 0)) def test_a_building_with_no_special_kind_is_a_house(self): houses = [{"name": "Cottage", "width": 10, "height": 8, "kind": "house"}] self.assertEqual(presets.choose_for_kind(houses, None, 12, 10, 0)["name"], "Cottage") def test_nothing_is_switched_on_to_begin_with(self): self.assertEqual(presets.using(self.dir), set()) def test_a_kind_can_be_switched_on_and_off_again(self): presets.set_use(self.dir, "police", True) presets.set_use(self.dir, "church", True) self.assertEqual(presets.using(self.dir), {"police", "church"}) presets.set_use(self.dir, "church", False) self.assertEqual(presets.using(self.dir), {"police"}) def test_a_kind_the_generator_does_not_know_cannot_be_switched_on(self): for bad in ("spaceport", "", None, "POLICE STATION"): with self.subTest(bad=bad): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): presets.set_use(self.dir, bad, True) def test_what_a_preset_is_for_is_kept_beside_it_not_in_it(self): text = tbx(12, 10) presets.save(self.dir, "Station", text, kind="police") # The .tbx is untouched: it is used exactly as it was saved. self.assertEqual(presets.read(self.dir, "Station"), text) self.assertEqual(presets.library(self.dir)[0]["kind"], "police") def test_a_preset_saved_without_a_kind_stands_in_for_any_building(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Whatever", tbx(8, 8)) self.assertEqual(presets.library(self.dir)[0]["kind"], presets.ANY) def test_what_a_preset_is_for_can_be_changed(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Station", tbx(12, 10), kind="police") presets.set_kind(self.dir, "Station", "fire") self.assertEqual(presets.library(self.dir)[0]["kind"], "fire") presets.set_kind(self.dir, "Station", "") self.assertEqual(presets.library(self.dir)[0]["kind"], presets.ANY) def test_a_kind_the_generator_does_not_know_cannot_be_recorded(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): presets.save(self.dir, "Station", tbx(12, 10), kind="spaceport") def test_throwing_a_preset_away_forgets_what_it_was_for(self): presets.save(self.dir, "Station", tbx(12, 10), kind="police") presets.remove(self.dir, "Station") self.assertEqual(presets.manifest(self.dir)["kinds"], {}) def test_a_folder_with_no_manifest_is_empty_rather_than_an_error(self): self.assertEqual(presets.manifest(os.path.join(self.dir, "nowhere")), {"kinds": {}, "use": {}}) def test_a_manifest_full_of_nonsense_is_ignored_rather_than_believed(self): os.makedirs(presets.folder(self.dir), exist_ok=True) path = os.path.join(presets.folder(self.dir), presets.MANIFEST) for junk in ("", "[1,2,3]", '{"kinds": 7, "use": "yes"}', "not json"): with self.subTest(junk=junk): with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(junk) self.assertEqual(presets.manifest(self.dir), {"kinds": {}, "use": {}}) self.assertEqual(presets.using(self.dir), set())

def project(d, origin): proj = os.path.join(d, "m") os.makedirs(proj) line = f'<worldOrigin origin="{origin}"/>
' if origin else "" with open(os.path.join(proj, "m.pzw"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(f'<?xml version="1.0"?>
<world version="1.0" width="2" height="2">
{line}</world>
') return proj

nodes.body_text: class ProjectOrigin(unittest.TestCase): def test_read_from_the_project_file_in_tiles(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d: self.assertEqual(project_origin(project(d, "0,0")), (0, 0)) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d: self.assertEqual(project_origin(project(d, "3,2")), (900, 600)) def test_no_file_or_no_line_is_the_vanilla_corner(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d: self.assertEqual(project_origin(project(d, "")), (ORIGIN_X, 0)) self.assertEqual(project_origin(os.path.join(d, "nothing")), (ORIGIN_X, 0)) def test_room_tables_follow_the_origin(self): placed = [(10, 10, [{"name": "kitchen", "z": 0, "rects": [(10, 10, 5, 5)]}])] rooms, _ = cell_tables(0, 0, placed, origin=(0, 0)) self.assertTrue(rooms) # the same building is not in that cell when the world starts 300 tiles east self.assertEqual(cell_tables(0, 0, placed, origin=(300, 0)), ([], []))

nodes.body_text: class ProposedRoads(unittest.TestCase): def test_switch_selects_and_types_proposed_roads_without_mutating_cache(self): features = [ osm.OSMFeature(1, 'way', {'highway': 'residential'}, [(1, 1), (2, 2)]), osm.OSMFeature(2, 'way', {'highway': 'proposed', 'proposed': 'primary'}, [(1, 1), (2, 2)]), osm.OSMFeature(3, 'way', {'proposed:highway': 'footway'}, [(1, 1), (2, 2)]), osm.OSMFeature(4, 'way', {'highway': 'proposed'}, [(1, 1), (2, 2)]), ] with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: cache = str(Path(directory) / 'map.json.gz') box = (0, 0, 3, 3) osm.save_cache(cache, box, features) loaded = osm.load_cache(cache, box) self.assertEqual([f.osm_id for f in osm.proposed_roads(loaded, False)], [1]) selected = osm.proposed_roads(loaded, True) self.assertEqual([osm.classify(f.tags) for f in selected], ['road_minor', 'road_major', 'paved_path', 'road_minor']) self.assertEqual(loaded[1].tags['highway'], 'proposed') self.assertEqual(osm.load_cache(cache, box)[1].tags['highway'], 'proposed') def test_queries_and_settings_include_option(self): self.assertIn('way["proposed:highway"]', osm._build_query(0, 0, 1, 1)) self.assertEqual(Settings().include_proposed_roads, 0) self.assertEqual(Settings.from_dict({'include_proposed_roads': 1}).include_proposed_roads, 1) self.assertIn('include_proposed_roads', RENDER_SETTINGS) self.assertIsNone(osm.classify({'highway': 'proposed'})) @unittest.skipUnless(osmium, 'pyosmium is not installed') def test_extract_finds_prefixed_proposal(self): from generator import extract with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: path = str(Path(directory) / 'map.osm.pbf') with osmium.SimpleWriter(path) as writer: writer.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=1, location=(1, 1))) writer.add_node(osmium.osm.mutable.Node(id=2, location=(1.001, 1.001))) writer.add_way(osmium.osm.mutable.Way(id=3, nodes=[1, 2], tags={'proposed:highway': 'primary'})) found = extract._read(path, extract.parse_filters(osm.OVERPASS_FILTERS), (0, 0, 2, 2), lambda *args: None, None) features = osm.proposed_roads(osm._parse({'elements': found}), True) nodes.body_text: """Petrol station forecourts: pumps on islands, set well back from the shop.""" import os import tempfile import unittest import numpy as np from PIL import Image from generator import pz_colors as C from knoxbuild import pumps from knoxbuild.bitmaps import read_rgb if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: forecourt
nodes.signature: def forecourt(mpt, side="S", w=18, h=8, size=(120, 90), at=(50, 20))
nodes.body_text: def forecourt(mpt, side="S", w=18, h=8, size=(120, 90), at=(50, 20)): d = tempfile.mkdtemp() os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((size[1], size[0], 3), np.uint8) ground[:] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS ground[size[1] - 6:] = C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT # a street along the bottom Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") occupied = np.zeros((size[1], size[0]), bool) x0, y0 = at occupied[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w] = True placements, count = pumps.place_pumps( d, "m", os.path.join(d, "buildings"), occupied, [(x0, y0, w, h, side)], [], metres_per_tile=mpt) return read_rgb(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp")), count, placements, (x0, y0, w, h)

the shop's pavement row island_rows = [r for r in rows if r > front + 1 and r < 80] self.assertTrue(island_rows, "no island was drawn") nearest = (min(island_rows) - (y0 + h)) * mpt self.assertGreaterEqual(nearest, pumps.PUMP_SETBACK_M - mpt, f"mpt {mpt}") def test_the_shop_front_is_paved(self): ground, _count, _p, (x0, y0, w, h) = forecourt(2.0) row = ground[y0 + h + 1, x0:x0 + w] self.assertTrue((row == np.array(C.PALE_CONCRETE)).all(axis=1).sum() >= w // 2) def test_each_island_has_a_roof_on_posts(self): d = tempfile.mkdtemp() os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((90, 120, 3), np.uint8) ground[:] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") occupied = np.zeros((90, 120), bool) occupied[20:28, 50:68] = True pumps.place_pumps(d, "m", os.path.join(d, "buildings"), occupied, [(50, 20, 18, 8, "S")], [], metres_per_tile=2.0) text = "".join(open(os.path.join(d, "buildings", f), encoding="utf-8").read() for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "buildings"))) kit = [pumps.CANOPY[b] for b in pumps.CANOPY if pumps.CANOPY[b]["pillar"][0] in text][0] self.assertIn(kit["edge"], text) self.assertIn(kit["fascia_n"], text) self.assertEqual(text.count("<floor>"), 3) # the roof is two floors up def test_a_mapped_canopy_gets_its_roof(self): # A canopy OpenStreetMap draws, a little askew on a turned map: pumps # under it, a roof over them, and the forecourt one rectangle of # tarmac rather than the outline's jagged inside. d = tempfile.mkdtemp() os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((90, 120, 3), np.uint8) ground[:] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") outline = [(40.0, 30.0), (64.0, 31.0), (63.6, 41.0), (39.6, 40.0)] _p, count = pumps.place_pumps(d, "m", os.path.join(d, "buildings"), np.zeros((90, 120), bool), [], [], canopies=[outline], metres_per_tile=1.0) self.assertGreaterEqual(count, 2) text = "".join(open(os.path.join(d, "buildings", f), encoding="utf-8").read() for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "buildings"))) self.assertTrue(any(pumps.CANOPY[b]["pillar"][0] in text for b in pumps.CANOPY)) self.assertEqual(text.count("<floor>"), 3) g = read_rgb(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp")) box = g[30:41, 40:64] paved = ((box == np.array(C.DARK_ASPHALT)).all(axis=2) | (box == np.array(C.PALE_CONCRETE)).all(axis=2)) self.assertTrue(paved.all()) def test_canopy_is_built_as_the_muldraugh_station(self): # The game's own Fossoil station (Muldraugh, cell 41,38): islands at # x 117-125 on rows 32 and 39, read back from its lot files. tiles = pumps.canopy_tiles([(117, 32, 125, 32), (117, 39, 125, 39)], "fossoil", lambda x, y: True) at = {} for x, y, z, _layer, tile in tiles: at.setdefault((x, y, z), set()).add(tile) f = "location_shop_fossoil_01_" roof = {(x, y) for (x, y, z) in at if z == 2} self.assertEqual(roof, {(x, y) for x in range(116, 129) for y in range(30, 42)}) self.assertEqual(at[(116, 30, 2)], {f + "38"}) self.assertEqual(at[(120, 35, 2)], {f + "39"}) for px, py in ((116, 32), (126, 32), (116, 39), (126, 39)): for z in (0, 1): self.assertEqual(at[(px, py, z)], {f + "4"}) self.assertEqual(at[(px + 1, py, z)], {f + "6"}) self.assertEqual(at[(px, py + 1, z)], {f + "5"}) self.assertEqual(at[(px + 1, py + 1, z)], {f + "7"}) self.assertEqual({(x, y) for (x, y, z), t in at.items() if z == 1 and f + "40" in t}, {(x, 42) for x in range(116, 129)}) self.assertEqual({(x, y) for (x, y, z), t in at.items() if z == 1 and f + "41" in t}, {(129, y) for y in range(30, 42)}) self.assertEqual(at[(129, 42, 1)], {f + "42"}) def test_a_loose_point_gets_pumps_and_no_canopy(self): # A station mapped only as a point has no shop, so it gets pumps on a # pad. Give it a canopy too and the map fills with little stations. d = tempfile.mkdtemp() os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((90, 120, 3), np.uint8) ground[:] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") _p, count = pumps.place_pumps(d, "m", os.path.join(d, "buildings"), np.zeros((90, 120), bool), [], [(60, 40)], metres_per_tile=1.0) self.assertGreaterEqual(count, 1) text = "".join(open(os.path.join(d, "buildings", f), encoding="utf-8").read() for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "buildings"))) self.assertIn("location_shop_", text) # the pump itself self.assertEqual(text.count("<floor>"), 1, "no roof over a pad with no shop") def test_a_point_beside_a_station_is_not_a_second_one(self): d = tempfile.mkdtemp() os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((90, 120, 3), np.uint8) ground[:] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(d, "m.bmp"), format="BMP") occupied = np.zeros((90, 120), bool) occu

nodes.name: test_python_library.py
nodes.body_text: """KnoxMap says when the Python running it is missing part of its own library. Reported from a map that stopped with `No module named 'xml.etree.ElementTree'`. That module is part of Python, not a package KnoxMap installs, so pip cannot put it back and the message means the Python on that PC has been trimmed or had a file taken out of it - antivirus software is the usual reason. Said in the middle of a build it tells the person nothing they can act on, so the setup check looks for it and Setup itself refuses such a Python before it builds anything on top of it. nodes.body_text: class WhatKnoxmapNeedsFromPython(unittest.TestCase): def test_the_list_is_what_the_code_really_imports(self): # Each of these is imported somewhere in KnoxMap; if one were dropped # from the list, a Python without it would pass the check and fail # later in a build. for name in ("xml.etree.ElementTree", "xml.sax.saxutils", "zlib", "hashlib", "zipfile", "tarfile", "ssl", "ctypes"): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIn(name, system.NEEDED_FROM_PYTHON) def test_this_python_has_all_of_it(self): self.assertEqual(system._missing_from_python(), []) def test_one_that_is_missing_is_named(self): def gone(name): if name == "xml.etree.ElementTree": raise ImportError("no such module") return object() with patch("importlib.util.find_spec", gone): self.assertEqual(system._missing_from_python(), ["xml.etree.ElementTree"]) def test_the_setup_check_says_what_to_do_about_it(self): with patch.object(system, "_missing_from_python", lambda: ["xml.etree.ElementTree"]): report = system._setup_report() check = next(c for c in report["checks"] if c["id"] == "python_library") self.assertFalse(check["ok"]) # The name of what is gone, that pip is not the answer, and a way out. self.assertIn("xml.etree.ElementTree", check["fix"]) self.assertIn("pip", check["fix"]) self.assertIn("python.org", check["fix"]) def test_and_passes_quietly_when_nothing_is_missing(self): report = system._setup_report() check = next(c for c in report["checks"] if c["id"] == "python_library") self.assertTrue(check["ok"])

nodes.body_text: class SetupRefusesSuchAPython(unittest.TestCase): """Both setup scripts check before they build an environment on it.""" def script(self, name): # The names as they are spelled in the repository: Windows finds # "setup.bat" whatever the case, and Linux - where this runs in CI - # does not. from pathlib import Path return (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / name).read_text( encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") def test_windows_setup_checks_and_falls_back_to_a_private_copy(self): text = self.script("Setup.bat") self.assertIn("import xml.etree.ElementTree", text) self.assertIn(":python_damaged", text) # It must recover rather than stop: the private copy is fetched again. after = text.split(":python_damaged", 1)[1] self.assertIn("call :portable_python", after) def test_the_other_setup_checks_too_and_names_the_packages(self): text = self.script("setup.sh") self.assertIn("import xml.etree.ElementTree", text) self.assertIn("apt install python3", text)

nodes.body_text: class RailEndpoints(unittest.TestCase): def test_short_straight_fragment_uses_one_piece_instead_of_a_loop(self): for delta in ((1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, -1)): for phase in (0, .2, .5, .8): points = [(10+phase, 20), (10+phase+1.2*delta[0], 20+1.2*delta[1])] for track in continuous_tracks([points]): with self.subTest(delta=delta, phase=phase): sections = list(rail_sections(track, backend="python")) self.assertEqual(len(sections), 1) self.assertLess(sections[0][2], 4) x, y, index = sections[0] ports = [(x+px/2, y+py/2) for px, py in ASSEMBLIES[index][:2]] for endpoint in track: self.assertLessEqual(min(math.dist(p, endpoint) for p in ports), math.sqrt(2.5)+1e-8) def test_scaled_real_fragment_fits_with_connected_ports(self): # A clipped Cookeville diagonal; at 2m/tile its last port overhangs the line. source = [(2185.1667290805053, 1125.3332709194947), (2189.4088189004106, 1121.0911810995894)] for scale in (1, 2, 3): points = [(x / scale, y / scale) for x, y in source] for track in continuous_tracks([points]): with self.subTest(scale=scale): sections = list(rail_sections(track, backend="python")) self.assertTrue(sections) previous = None for x, y, index in sections: ports = {(2*x+px, 2*y+py) for px, py in ASSEMBLIES[index][:2]} if previous is not None: self.assertEqual(len(previous & ports), 1) previous = ports target = max(track[0], track[-1]) self.assertLessEqual(min(math.dist((px/2, py/2), target) for px, py in previous), math.sqrt(2.5)+1e-8) def test_fractional_endpoints_and_fitted_diagonal_fragments(self): cases = [[(0, .1), (4, .1)], [(0, .5), (4, .5)], [(.5, 0), (.5, 4)], [(.5, 1.5), (3.5, 4.5)], [(.5, 0), (3.5, -3)]] cases += [track for points in cases[:] for track in continuous_tracks([points])] for points in cases: with self.subTest(points=points): sections = list(rail_sections(points)) self.assertTrue(sections) self.assertEqual(list(rail_sections(list(reversed(points)))), sections) previous = None for x, y, index in sections: ports = {(2*x+px, 2*y+py) for px, py in ASSEMBLIES[index][:2]} if previous is not None: self.assertEqual(len(previous & ports), 1) previous = ports endpoint = max(points[0], points[-1]) self.assertLessEqual(min(math.dist((px/2, py/2), endpoint) for px, py in previous), math.sqrt(2.5)+1e-8) def test_integer_straight_keeps_its_existing_assembly(self): self.assertEqual(list(rail_sections([(0, 0), (4, 0)])), [(0, -1, 0)])

nodes.body_text: """Regression coverage for solid tracks, linked garage panels and low roofs.""" import contextlib import io from pathlib import Path from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory import unittest from unittest import mock import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET import numpy as np from PIL import Image, ImageDraw from generator import pz_colors as C from generator.osm import OSMFeature from generator.rendering import roads from generator.rendering import rails from knoxbuild import catalog, layout, tbx from knoxbuild.buildtiles import parse_tbx, level_tiles from knoxbuild.rules import load_rules from knoxbuild.terrain import ground_layers, Palette from worlded import patch_rules_roads ROOT = Path(catalog.__file__).resolve().parents[1] TOOLS_RULES = ROOT / "vendor/PZMappingTools/config/Rules.txt" if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: _rules_for
nodes.body_text: def _rules_for(folder: str) -> Path: """A config folder holding the rules KnoxMap writes, without the tools. These tests used to copy the PZMappingTools `Rules.txt` in, which is not in the repository - CI has no vendor folder, so they errored there and only ever ran on a machine with the tools installed. The rules they care about are the ones KnoxMap adds itself, written into an empty file by the same code Setup runs. """ config = Path(folder) / "config" config.mkdir(exist_ok=True) (config / "Rules.txt").write_text("", encoding="utf-8") with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): patch_rules_roads.main(["patch_rules_roads", folder]) return config / "Rules.txt"

Every tile table is the donor's own, unchanged. for key in ("exterior", "interior", "window", "curtains", "trim", "grime"): self.assertEqual(style.get(key), donor.get(key), f"{key} must be the catalog's own") def test_pool_is_flat_roofed_masonry_without_shutters(self): names = [s["name"] for s in cn_house_styles()] self.assertEqual(sorted(names), sorted(f"cn_{base}" for base in CN_BASES)) for style in cn_house_styles(): self.assertFalse(style["roof"]["peaked"]) self.assertNotIn("shutters", style) # And the wood-and-siding styles are not in the pool at all. self.assertFalse(any(base in style["name"] for base in ("clapboard", "logs", "trailer", "siding", "timber"))) def test_cn_style_renders_a_tbx(self): from xml.etree import ElementTree from knoxbuild import layout from knoxbuild.tbx import render_tbx room = layout.Room(0, 0, 4, 5, kind="livingroom") plan = layout.Plan(5, 6, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * 5 for _ in range(6)], windows=[(2, 0, "N")]) style = cn_house_styles()[0] root = ElementTree.fromstring(render_tbx(plan, "cn-style-test", style)) entries = [entry for entry in root.findall("tile_entry") if entry.get("category") in ("exterior_walls", "interior_walls")] self.assertTrue(entries) def test_pick_style_uses_the_cn_pool_for_ordinary_houses(self): rng = random.Random(7) settings = Settings() seen = set() for i in range(40): style = pick_style(None, 10 + (i % 12) * 9, 10 + (i // 12) * 9, rng, settings, density=0.3, region="cn") seen.add(style["name"]) self.assertTrue(seen) self.assertTrue(all(name.startswith("cn_") for name in seen), seen) def test_dated_prewar_buildings_keep_their_pitched_roofs(self): profile = BuildingProfile.infer({"start_date": "1921"}, None, 0.3, 120, 2, 11) self.assertTrue(profile.dated) self.assertEqual(profile.era, "prewar") style = pick_style(None, 40, 40, random.Random(1), Settings(), density=0.3, profile=profile, region="cn") self.assertFalse(style["name"].startswith("cn_")) def test_undated_buildings_do_not_get_the_prewar_exemption(self): profile = BuildingProfile.infer({}, None, 0.3, 120, 2, 11) self.assertFalse(profile.dated) style = pick_style(None, 40, 40, random.Random(1), Settings(), density=0.3, profile=profile, region="cn") self.assertTrue(style["name"].startswith("cn_")) def test_default_maps_are_unchanged(self): rng = random.Random(7) settings = Settings() for i in range(20): style = pick_style(None, 10 + (i % 8) * 9, 10 + (i // 8) * 9, rng, settings, density=0.3) self.assertFalse(style["name"].startswith("cn_"))

nodes.body_text: class RegionalStoreys(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.settings = Settings() self.rng = random.Random(42) def test_cn_houses_run_taller_than_default_ones(self): default = [building_levels({}, None, 30, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0)[0] for i in range(200)] cn = [building_levels({}, None, 30, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region="cn")[0] for i in range(200)] self.assertGreater(max(cn), max(default)) self.assertGreater(sum(cn) / len(cn), sum(default) / len(default)) def test_cn_houses_never_exceed_the_games_house_shape_by_much(self): for i in range(100): levels, measured = building_levels({}, None, 30, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region="cn") self.assertFalse(measured) self.assertLessEqual(levels, 4) def test_cn_apartments_follow_their_own_table(self): got = {building_levels({}, "apartment", 500, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region="cn")[0] for i in range(60)} self.assertTrue(got & {4, 5, 6}, got) def test_small_footprints_stay_low_everywhere(self): # The Arnis-style area table: a kiosk-sized footprint is not a tower. for region in (None, "cn"): for i in range(40): levels, _ = building_levels({}, "shop", 8, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region=region) self.assertLessEqual(levels, 2, (region, levels)) def test_large_houses_read_as_taller_than_small_ones(self): small = {building_levels({}, None, 20, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0)[0] for i in range(80)} large = {building_levels({}, None, 200, random.Random(i), self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0)[0] for i in range(80)} self.assertGreater(max(large), max(small)) def test_osm_levels_beat_every_table(self): for region in (None, "cn"): levels, measured = building_levels( {"building:levels": "5"}, None, 30, self.rng, self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region=region) self.assertTrue(measured) self.assertEqual(levels, 5) def test_levels_respect_max_levels(self): settings = Settings(max_levels=3) for i in range(40): levels, _ = building_levels({}, "apartment", 500, random.Random(i), settings, metres_per_tile=2.0, region="cn") self.assertLessEqual(levels, 3) def test_every_default_kind_still_has_a_pool_or_range(self): for kind in set(DEFAULT_LEVELS) | {None, "mall", "castle"}: pool = area_level_pool(kind, 1000.0) rng = random.Random(0) lo, hi = DEFAULT_LEVELS.get(kind or "", (1, 2)) levels = building_levels({}, kind, 250, rng, self.settings, metres_per_tile=2.0)[0] self.assertGreaterEqual(levels, 1) self.assertLessEqual(levels, max(hi, 12)) if pool is None: self.assertIn(kind, DEFAULT_LEVELS) def test_area_bands_are_ordered(self): for kind, bands in AREA_LEVEL_TABLE.items(): with self.subTest(kind=kind): limits = [limit for limit, _pool in bands] self.assertEqual(limits[-1], None) self.assertEqual([l for l in limits if l is not None], sorted(l for l in limits if l is not None))

nodes.name: test_regression_maps.py
nodes.body_text: """Cheap checks for the committed fixture metadata and golden-hash comparison. The actual render + Rust compile check is `python tools/regression_maps.py`. """ import json import re import unittest from tools.regression_maps import GOLDEN, SCENARIOS, compare, scenario_features if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: RegressionMapTests
nodes.body_text: class RegressionMapTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_fixed_scenarios_have_compiled_file_hashes(self): expected = json.loads(GOLDEN.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) self.assertEqual(set(expected), set(SCENARIOS)) for name, spec in SCENARIOS.items(): case = expected[name] features = scenario_features(name) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(features), spec["min_buildings"]) self.assertEqual(case["seed"], spec["seed"]) self.assertEqual(case["preset"], spec["preset"]) self.assertGreaterEqual(case["buildings"], spec["min_buildings"]) self.assertGreaterEqual(case["cells"], 1) self.assertEqual(len(case["files"]), case["cells"] * 3) self.assertTrue(all(re.fullmatch("[0-9a-f]{64}", digest) for digest in case["files"].values())) def test_compiled_hash_comparison_reports_every_difference(self): self.assertFalse(compare({"same.lotheader": "abc"}, {"same.lotheader": "abc"})) mismatches = compare({"changed.lotheader": "new", "extra.lotpack": "abc"}, {"changed.lotheader": "old", "missing.lotpack": "xyz"}) self.assertEqual(len(mismatches), 3) self.assertTrue(any("changed changed.lotheader" in m for m in mismatches)) self.assertTrue(any("missing missing.lotpack" in m for m in mismatches)) self.assertTrue(any("unexpected extra.lotpack" in m for m in mismatches))

nodes.name: test_release_integrity.py
nodes.body_text: """What a release ships, and what Setup installs on somebody else's PC. `.knoxmap_files.json` is the list an update deletes by, and `requirements.txt` is what Setup installs. Both are easy to leave a version behind, and neither failure can be seen from here: the manifest shows up as a module that never arrives, the requirements as a package that installs itself newer than anything KnoxMap was ever run against. """ import json import re import unittest from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: TheShippedFileList
nodes.body_text: class TheShippedFileList(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.manifest = json.loads((ROOT / ".knoxmap_files.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) self.files = self.manifest["files"] def test_the_tests_do_not_ship(self): # 107 of the files in a download, and the installed app runs none of # them. .gitattributes keeps them out of the zip; this keeps them out of # the list an update deletes by, which is the other half of the same job. self.assertEqual([f for f in self.files if f.startswith("tests/")], []) self.assertNotIn("test_pipeline.py", self.files) def test_every_shipped_file_is_on_disk(self): from tools.check_manifest import ADDED_BY_RELEASE # Source checkouts do not carry the binaries built by release jobs. missing = [f for f in self.files if f not in ADDED_BY_RELEASE and not (ROOT / f).exists()] self.assertEqual(missing, [], "an update cannot put these back") def test_the_list_is_a_set(self): self.assertEqual(len(self.files), len(set(self.files))) def test_the_developer_tooling_does_not_ship(self): # pyproject.toml and requirements-dev.txt are for whoever works on # KnoxMap: a linter and its settings, which a player has no use for. # Keeping them out of the zip is also what keeps check_manifest.py's # comparison exact, since git archive would otherwise ship them. # The frontend's ESLint and node:test setup is the same arrangement. text = (ROOT / ".gitattributes").read_text(encoding="utf-8") for name in ("pyproject.toml", "requirements-dev.txt", "package.json", "package-lock.json", "eslint.config.js"): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIn(f"{name} export-ignore", text) self.assertNotIn(name, self.files) def test_the_binaries_come_from_the_release_and_not_the_repository(self): # It used to be one of each: KnoxMap.exe ignored, knoxlots.exe committed. # Native binaries are built by the launcher/knoxlots workflows and # copied into downloads. The repository carries their source; a copy # built here still works, but is not committed. ignored = (ROOT / ".gitignore").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() for name in ("/KnoxMap.exe", "/knoxlots.exe", "/knoxroute.exe"): self.assertIn(name, ignored) for name in ("KnoxMap.exe", "knoxlots.exe", "knoxroute.exe"): self.assertIn(name, self.files, "a download has to carry every native binary") def test_it_has_a_version(self): # updater.py compares this with the changelog heading; a manifest from a # different version is how a half-applied update reads as complete. self.assertRegex(str(self.manifest.get("version")), r"^\d+(\.\d+)+$")

nodes.name: WhatSetupInstalls
nodes.body_text: class WhatSetupInstalls(unittest.TestCase): def requirements(self) -> list[str]: text = (ROOT / "requirements.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") return [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("#")] def test_every_package_is_pinned(self): # A floor like numpy>=1.26 installs whatever is newest the day somebody # runs Setup - months after this was tested, on their PC, with no way # back. Setup.bat and setup.sh both install this list. unpinned = [line for line in self.requirements() if "==" not in line] self.assertEqual(unpinned, [], "Setup would install a moving target") def test_the_pins_are_versions_and_not_ranges(self): for line in self.requirements(): name, _, version = line.partition("==") self.assertRegex(version, r"^\d+(\.\d+)+$", f"{name} is not pinned to a version") def test_the_window_is_in_there(self): # CI leaves pywebview out (no GUI toolkit on a runner); Setup must not. self.assertTrue(any(line.lower().startswith("pywebview") for line in self.requirements())) def test_nothing_is_listed_twice(self): names = [re.split(r"[=<>!\[]", line, maxsplit=1)[0].lower() for line in self.requirements()] self.assertEqual(len(names), len(set(names)))

nodes.body_text: class TheCatalogGenerator(unittest.TestCase): """The committed catalog is not the generator's output any more. Its own header says so: GAME_WALL_STYLES and the escalators were added by hand and tools/make_catalog.py does not write them. A warning in a docstring is not a guard - the generator would have written straight over them - so writing the committed file now has to be asked for with --force. """ def test_it_refuses_to_overwrite_the_committed_catalog(self): from tools import make_catalog code = make_catalog.main(["make_catalog", "no/such/config", str(ROOT / "knoxbuild" / "catalog.py")]) self.assertEqual(code, 2) def test_it_still_writes_where_it_was_told_to(self): # Past the guard it reads the game's config, which is not there - the # point is that it got that far instead of refusing the destination. from tools import make_catalog with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError): make_catalog.main(["make_catalog", "no/such/config", str(ROOT / "catalog-scratch.py")])

nodes.name: test_render_settings.py
nodes.body_text: """RENDER_SETTINGS has to stay level with what generate() really reads. The page runs only the steps a changed setting needs: one of these and the map is drawn again, anything else and the buildings are laid out afresh on the ground that is already there. If a knob is added to the renderer and not to this list, changing it would appear to do nothing at all - the map would never be redrawn - which is the kind of bug nobody reports because it looks like the setting is just weak. """ import inspect import re import unittest import app from knoxbuild.settings import Settings from web.generation import _generate # Read by generate() and deliberately not in the list: the renderer draws a # first zombie spawn map from the ground colours, and then the building step # throws that away and draws it again from the people in the buildings # (knoxbuild/build.py). Changing it only needs the buildings doing again. REDRAWN_BY_THE_BUILD = {"spawn_density"} if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: _generate_source
nodes.body_text: def _generate_source() -> str: """The function that really reads the settings. The route `generate` only unwraps the request body and hands it to `_generate`; every knob is read in there. """ return inspect.getsource(_generate)

nodes.name: settings_read_by
nodes.body_text: def settings_read_by(source) -> set: """The setting names an object's source reads off `settings`. Narrowed to the real fields, or `settings.to_dict()` counts as a knob. """ if not isinstance(source, str): source = inspect.getsource(source) return {n for n in re.findall(r"settings\.(\w+)", source) if n in Settings().to_dict()}

nodes.name: SmallKitchensAreFitted
nodes.body_text: class SmallKitchensAreFitted(unittest.TestCase): """A restaurant kitchen is worktop wall to wall, however small it is. The commercial run asked for no cupboards and for full coverage, and the cupboard share came out of the same budget anyway - 99 - 99 = 0 - so no run was drawn at all. Every restaurant kitchen had the one counter off its wishlist and bare wall either side of it, which is most obvious in the small ones. """ def kitchens(self, seeds=range(30)): for seed in seeds: for w, h in ((11, 13), (13, 11), (12, 12), (14, 12), (10, 12), (12, 10)): plan = layout.build_building( width=w, height=h, kind="restaurant", seed=seed, levels=1, street="S", uses=[("restaurantdining", "dinerkitchen")]).storeys[0] for idx, room in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1): if room.kind.endswith("kitchen") and room.area <= 20: pieces = [f for f in plan.furniture if plan.grid[f[2]][f[1]] == idx] floor = {(x, y) for y in range(room.y0, room.y1 + 1) for x in range(room.x0, room.x1 + 1) if plan.grid[y][x] == idx} yield seed, room, pieces, floor def test_a_small_kitchen_is_worktop_and_not_bare_wall(self): seen = fitted = 0 for seed, room, pieces, floor in self.kitchens(): seen += 1 counters = [p for p in pieces if p[0].startswith("counter")] if len(counters) >= 3 and len({p[3] for p in counters}) >= 2: fitted += 1 self.assertGreater(seen, 20) self.assertGreater(fitted / seen, 0.9, f"only {fitted} of {seen} small kitchens got a worktop run") def test_a_small_kitchen_keeps_a_way_through(self): for seed, room, pieces, floor in self.kitchens(): taken = {(p[1], p[2]) for p in pieces} self.assertGreaterEqual(len(floor - taken), 2, f"seed {seed}: a kitchen of {room.area} m2 is walled in")

nodes.body_text: class RoadBevels(unittest.TestCase): def paint(self, paths, width=6): image=Image.new('L',(100,100),0) _draw_roads(image,[(width,paths)],255) return np.array(image) def test_even_width_has_no_one_tile_bulge_at_vertices(self): for width in (4,6,8,12): with self.subTest(width=width): road=self.paint([[(10,50),(40,50),(80,50)]],width) for x in (15,39,40,41,75): self.assertEqual(np.count_nonzero(road[:,x]),width) def test_outer_corner_is_a_45_degree_bevel(self): road=self.paint([[(10,50),(50,50),(50,10)]],8) edges=[] for y in (51,52,53,54): xs=np.flatnonzero(road[y]);self.assertTrue(len(xs)) edges.append(int(xs[-1])) self.assertEqual(np.diff(edges).tolist(),[-1,-1,-1],edges) def test_small_diagonal_retains_its_inside_45_degree_cut(self): road=self.paint([[(50,90),(50,53),(53,50),(90,50)]],6) self.assertEqual(road[54,54],255) self.assertEqual(road[55,54],0) self.assertEqual(road[54,55],0) def test_separate_map_ways_make_the_same_corner(self): whole=self.paint([[(10,50),(50,50),(50,10)]],8) split=self.paint([[(10,50),(50,50)],[(50,10),(50,50)]],8) np.testing.assert_array_equal(whole,split) def test_projection_roundoff_cannot_add_an_extra_edge_tile(self): path=[(10,50),(50,50),(50,10)] noisy=[(x+1e-10,y-1e-10) for x,y in path] np.testing.assert_array_equal(self.paint([path]),self.paint([noisy])) def test_closed_road_does_not_fill_its_centre(self): road=self.paint([[(20,20),(80,20),(80,80),(20,80),(20,20)]]) self.assertEqual(road[50,50],0) self.assertEqual(road[20,50],255) def test_narrow_and_clipped_roads_still_draw(self): for width in (1,3,6): road=self.paint([[(-30,0),(40,0),(40,50)]],width) self.assertEqual(road[20,40],255)

nodes.name: test_road_edges.py
nodes.body_text: """Pavement on the edge of a street (generator/rendering/roads.py). A pavement tile with no pavement beside it orthogonally is one step of a diagonal edge. On its own the tile draws with a lip and reads as a spike in the grass, so the tidy-up pass takes it back to the ground it stands in. """ import unittest from PIL import Image from generator.pz_colors import (MEDIUM_GRASS, MEDIUM_ASPHALT, DARK_ASPHALT, DARKEST_ASPHALT, PALE_CONCRETE) from generator.rendering.roads import _smooth_road_edges ASPHALT = (MEDIUM_ASPHALT, DARK_ASPHALT, DARKEST_ASPHALT) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: is_colour
nodes.body_text: def is_colour(ground, colours): import numpy as np mask = np.zeros(ground.shape[:2], dtype=bool) for colour in colours: mask |= np.all(ground == colour, axis=2) return mask

nodes.name: tidy
nodes.body_text: def tidy(im): _smooth_road_edges(im, ASPHALT, is_colour) return im

nodes.name: RoadEdges
nodes.body_text: class RoadEdges(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_straight_street_keeps_its_pavements(self): im = Image.new('RGB', (60, 60), MEDIUM_GRASS) for y in range(10, 50): for x in range(20, 31): im.putpixel((x, y), MEDIUM_ASPHALT) im.putpixel((19, y), PALE_CONCRETE) im.putpixel((31, y), PALE_CONCRETE) tidy(im) self.assertEqual(im.getpixel((19, 30)), PALE_CONCRETE) self.assertEqual(im.getpixel((31, 30)), PALE_CONCRETE) def test_a_stepped_pavement_is_taken_back_to_grass(self): # One tile a step down a diagonal edge: every tile of it stands alone # orthogonally, which is the spike the player sees. im = Image.new('RGB', (60, 60), MEDIUM_GRASS) for i in range(10, 40): for x in range(i, i + 8): im.putpixel((x, i), MEDIUM_ASPHALT) im.putpixel((i - 1, i), PALE_CONCRETE) tidy(im) left = [im.getpixel((i - 1, i)) for i in range(10, 40)] self.assertEqual(left.count(PALE_CONCRETE), 0, "no step of the diagonal stays behind as a slab")

nodes.body_text: """The Road layout setting's vanilla choices (generator/roadgraph): every routed road on vanilla's sixteen directions with its junctions shared; the frontage-density mode (a sparse street keeps its 2:1, a dense one goes on the grid, a terraced street's jog moves to the gap in its frontage, a road keeps off a building on its line); the numpy stand-ins for scipy; the routed roads saved by Generate and read back the same by Build.""" import json import math import os import tempfile import unittest from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np from generator import octilinear, osm, renderer from generator.roadgraph import modes, network, raster, route, rustsearch, snap from knoxbuild.settings import Settings H = W = 200 @unittest.skipUnless(rustsearch.available(), "knoxroute not built") if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: plain_projection
nodes.body_text: def plain_projection(size=400): """1 tile = 1 degree, y down as lat: to_px(lat, lon) = (lon, lat).""" return SimpleNamespace(width=size, height=size, meters_per_tile=1.0, to_px=lambda lat, lon: (lon, lat), to_latlon=lambda x, y: (y, x))

nodes.name: a_route
nodes.signature: def a_route(s, g, pts, h=None, width=4)
nodes.body_text: def a_route(s, g, pts, h=None, width=4): return snap._route(pts, s, g, h, h, 2, snap.min_run(width), {}, 0, road_width=width)

nodes.name: share_2to1
nodes.body_text: def share_2to1(path) -> float: vs = raster.vertices(path) seg = [(math.hypot(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]), a, b) for a, b in zip(vs, vs[1:])] two = sum(L for L, a, b in seg if a[0] != b[0] and a[1] != b[1] and abs(b[0] - a[0]) != abs(b[1] - a[1])) return two / sum(L for L, _a, _b in seg)

nodes.name: town
nodes.body_text: def town(): """A main road on a gentle curve, a side road off it at an angle, a lane off that.""" main = osm.OSMFeature(1, "way", {"highway": "primary", "name": "High Street"}, [(200, 20), (190, 100), (175, 180), (170, 260), (172, 380)]) side = osm.OSMFeature(2, "way", {"highway": "residential", "name": "Mill Lane"}, [(175, 180), (130, 200), (90, 230), (40, 250)]) lane = osm.OSMFeature(3, "way", {"highway": "residential"}, [(90, 230), (60, 200), (40, 160)]) house = osm.OSMFeature(4, "way", {"building": "house"}, [(150, 140), (150, 150), (160, 150), (160, 140), (150, 140)]) return [main, side, lane, house]

nodes.body_text: class Routing(unittest.TestCase): def test_every_road_runs_on_the_sixteen_directions_and_junctions_are_shared(self): feats = town() proj = plain_projection() graph = route.route(feats, proj, "graph", log=lambda *a: None) self.assertEqual(set(graph["ways"]), {"1", "2", "3"}) for w, g in graph["ways"].items(): pts = [proj.to_px(*p) for p in g["geometry"]] for a, b in zip(pts, pts[1:]): dx, dy = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1] k = math.gcd(int(round(dx)), int(round(dy))) or 1 self.assertIn((round(dx) // k, round(dy) // k), snap.STEP, f"way {w}: {a} -> {b}") ends = {w: {tuple(g["geometry"][0]), tuple(g["geometry"][-1])} for w, g in graph["ways"].items()} on = {w: {tuple(p) for p in g["geometry"]} for w, g in graph["ways"].items()} self.assertTrue(ends["2"] & on["1"], "the side road meets the main road at one of its nodes") self.assertTrue(ends["3"] & on["2"], "the lane meets the side road at one of its nodes") self.assertTrue(graph["shift"]) def test_the_graph_moves_the_rest_of_the_town_with_the_roads(self): feats = town() proj = plain_projection() graph = route.route(feats, proj, "graph", log=lambda *a: None) before = list(feats[3].geometry) n = octilinear.apply_road_graph(feats, graph, proj) self.assertEqual(n, 3) self.assertEqual([list(p) for p in feats[0].geometry], graph["ways"]["1"]["geometry"]) self.assertNotEqual(feats[3].geometry, before) # the house moved with its street def test_a_roundabout_stays_as_drawn_and_the_roads_meet_it(self): ring = [(200.3 + 12 * math.sin(a), 199.6 + 12 * math.cos(a)) for a in np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 13)] ring[-1] = ring[0] rb = osm.OSMFeature(9, "way", {"highway": "primary", "junction": "roundabout"}, ring) west = osm.OSMFeature(10, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [(190, 20), (195, 120), ring[9]]) east = osm.OSMFeature(11, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [ring[3], (205, 300), (215, 380)]) proj = plain_projection() graph = route.route([rb, west, east], proj, "graph", log=lambda *a: None) self.assertEqual(graph["ways"]["9"]["geometry"], [list(p) for p in ring]) self.assertEqual(tuple(graph["ways"]["10"]["geometry"][-1]), ring[9]) # off the tile corners self.assertEqual(tuple(graph["ways"]["11"]["geometry"][0]), ring[3]) def test_a_roundabout_mapped_as_arcs_is_one_ring(self): # four quarter arcs; a road leaves straight out east from the eastern node (tile x # is lon here): it must be free to (an arc's own middle once pointed it elsewhere) ring = [(200 + 12 * math.sin(a), 200 + 12 * math.cos(a)) for a in np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 17)] ring[-1] = ring[0] arcs = [osm.OSMFeature(20 + k, "way", {"highway": "primary", "junction": "roundabout"}, ring[4 * k:4 * k + 5]) for k in range(4)] lat, lon = ring[0] out = osm.OSMFeature(30, "way", {"highway": "primary"}, [ring[0], (lat, lon + 40), (lat, lon + 90)]) proj = plain_projection() nodes, links, pins = network.build(arcs + [out], proj) (n,) = [n for n in pins if n in (links[0].u, links[0].v)] self.assertGreater(pins[n][0], 0.9) # outwards: +x graph = route.route(arcs + [out], proj, "graph", log=lambda *a: None) pts = [proj.to_px(*q) for q in graph["ways"]["30"]["geometry"]] self.assertLessEqual(max(abs(y - pts[0][1]) for _x, y in pts), 2) # straight out, no hook def test_a_dual_carriageway_is_one_road(self): a = osm.OSMFeature(1, "way", {"highway": "primary", "oneway": "yes"}, [(100, 20), (100, 380)]) b = osm.OSMFeature(2, "way", {"highway": "primary", "oneway": "yes"}, [(110, 380), (110, 20)]) nodes, links, _pins = network.build([a, b], plain_projection()) self.assertEqual(len(links), 1) self.assertEqual(links[0].tags.get("dual_carriageway"), "yes") graph = route.route([a, b], plain_projection(), "graph", log=lambda *a: None) self.assertEqual(graph["ways"]["1"]["geometry"], graph["ways"]["2"]["geometry"][::-1]) self.assertNotIn("width", graph["ways"]["1"]["tags"]) # drawn as one ordinary road def test_a_width_in_metres_is_tiles_at_the_maps_scale(self): f = osm.OSMFeature(1, "way", {"highway": "residential", "width": "8"}, [(100, 20), (100, 380)]) proj = plain_projection() self.assertEqual(network.build([f], proj)[1][0].width, 8) proj.meters_per_tile = 2.0 self.assertEqual(network.build([f], proj)[1][0].width, 4)

nodes.body_text: class Modes(unittest.TestCase): def tearDown(self): modes.reset() def test_density_is_high_by_a_frontage_and_nothing_far_off(self): edge = np.zeros((H, W), bool) edge[100, 20:180] = True # a long row of house fronts d = modes.density(edge) self.assertGreater(d[100, 100], 0.5) self.assertLess(d[100 - 40, 100], 0.01) self.assertLessEqual(d.max(), 1.0) def test_a_sparse_street_keeps_its_2to1(self): s, g = (20, 50), (140, 110) # a street at 2:1, nothing beside it snap.COST = np.zeros((H, W)) self.assertGreater(share_2to1(a_route(s, g, [s, g], h=1)), 0.9) def test_a_dense_street_is_drawn_on_the_grid(self): s, g = (20, 50), (140, 110) free = a_route(s, g, [s, g]) snap.COST = np.ones((H, W)) # lined with buildings all along dense = a_route(s, g, [s, g]) self.assertLess(share_2to1(dense), share_2to1(free) - 0.5) def test_a_terraced_streets_jog_moves_to_the_gap(self): # The real street steps 10 tiles south at x 40; terraces both sides all along but # for a gap at x 80-105 (no building within JOG_GAP of the road's edge there). s, g = (10, 50), (130, 60) line = [s, (40, 50), (40, 60), g] snap.COST = np.ones((H, W)) dist = np.full((H, W), 3.0) dist[:, 80:106] = 20.0 snap.JOG = {"dist": dist, "plots": None} inner = raster.vertices(a_route(s, g, line, h=0))[1:-1] self.assertTrue(inner) for x, _y in inner: self.assertTrue(78 <= x <= 107, f"a turn at x {x}, not in the gap: {inner}") snap.JOG = None # without the rule it jogs near the real step free = raster.vertices(a_route(s, g, line, h=0))[1:-1] self.assertTrue(any(x < 70 for x, _y in free), free) def test_occupancy_steers_a_road_off_a_building_on_its_line(self): s, g = (20, 100), (180, 100) fp = np.zeros((H, W), bool) fp[97:106, 85:115] = True # a building standing across the real line under = lambda path: snap.occ_field(4)[[y for _x, y in path], [x for x, _y in path]].sum() snap.OCC = fp straight = a_route(s, g, [s, g], h=0) # OCC_WEIGHT 0: through it snap.OCC_WEIGHT = 4.0 try: around = a_route(s, g, [s, g], h=0) finally: snap.OCC_WEIGHT = 0.0 self.assertGreater(under(straight), 0) self.assertLess(under(around), under(straight) / 4) def test_a_modes_constants_are_put_back(self): before = (snap.OCC_WEIGHT, snap.DIR_PENALTY) info = modes.prepare("cost", [], H, W) self.assertEqual(info["mode"], "cost") self.assertEqual(snap.OCC_WEIGHT, 1.0) self.assertIsNotNone(snap.COST) modes.reset() self.assertEqual((snap.OCC_WEIGHT, snap.DIR_PENALTY), before) self.assertIsNone(snap.COST) self.assertIsNone(snap.JOG)

nodes.body_text: class WithoutScipy(unittest.TestCase): def test_distance_is_exact_up_to_its_cap(self): rng = np.random.default_rng(1) fill = rng.random((40, 50)) > 0.97 d = modes.distance(fill, cap=8) ys, xs = np.nonzero(fill) for y in range(40): for x in range(50): want = min(math.hypot(x - xs[k], y - ys[k]) for k in range(len(xs))) self.assertAlmostEqual(d[y, x], min(want, 9.0), places=6) def test_least_squares_matches_numpy(self): rng = np.random.default_rng(2) A = rng.random((30, 12)) * (rng.random((30, 12)) > 0.6) A[np.arange(12), np.arange(12)] += 1.0 b = rng.random(30) rows, cols = np.nonzero(A) got = snap._least_squares(rows, cols, A[rows, cols], b, 12, np.zeros(12)) want = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)[0] self.assertTrue(np.allclose(got, want, atol=1e-6)) def test_convolve_is_the_same_size_and_centred(self): a = np.zeros((9, 9)) a[4, 4] = 1.0 k = np.arange(9, dtype=float).reshape(3, 3) out = snap.convolve(a, k) self.assertEqual(out.shape, a.shape) self.assertAlmostEqual(out[3:6, 3:6].sum(), k.sum()) self.assertAlmostEqual(out[4, 4], k[1, 1])

nodes.body_text: class RouterEquivalence(unittest.TestCase): """The out-of-process search must give exactly the in-process one.""" def test_cost_mode_uses_the_router_and_matches_python(self): import unittest.mock as mock seen = [] original = rustsearch.Router.search def spy(self, **kw): seen.append(1) return original(self, **kw) proj = plain_projection() with mock.patch.object(rustsearch.Router, "search", spy): routed = route.route(town(), proj, "cost", log=lambda *a: None) self.assertTrue(seen, "the Rust router was not used in cost mode") old = snap.BACKEND snap.BACKEND = "python" try: python = route.route(town(), proj, "cost", log=lambda *a: None) finally: snap.BACKEND = old self.assertEqual(routed["ways"], python["ways"])

class RoadRulesTests(unittest.TestCase): def test_patch_rules_roads_b42_soil_resilience(self): """Build 42 lacks floors_exterior_natural_01_18; ensure Yard bed_soil rule survives.""" with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: root = Path(tmp) cfg = root / "config" cfg.mkdir() rules_file = cfg / "Rules.txt" # Start with CRLF and older litter rule containing trash_01_13 rules_file.write_text( "rule
{
 label = KnoxMap road Litter
 bitmap = 1
" " color = 12 36 208
 tiles = [
 trash_01_0
" " trash_01_13
 ]
 layer = 0_FloorOverlay6
}
", encoding="utf-8", ) two_x = root / "Tiles" / "2x" two_x.mkdir(parents=True) # Simulate B42 floors_exterior_natural_01.png where 18 is blank img = Image.new("RGBA", (8 * 128, 7 * 256), (0, 0, 0, 0)) arr = np.array(img) for idx in [8, 9, 10, 11, 16, 17]: r, c = divmod(idx, 8) arr[r * 256 : (r + 1) * 256, c * 128 : (c + 1) * 128, 3] = 255 Image.fromarray(arr).save(two_x / "floors_exterior_natural_01.png") ret = patch_rules_roads.main(["patch_rules_roads.py", str(root)]) self.assertEqual(ret, 0) txt = rules_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") self.assertNotIn("trash_01_13", txt) self.assertIn("KnoxMap road Yard bed_soil", txt) self.assertIn("floors_exterior_natural_01_16", txt) self.assertTrue(knoxpaths.road_rules_ok(root)) def test_ensure_road_catalogue(self): """Verify ensure_road_catalogue adds curb and marking sheets to empty catalogue.""" with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: tilesets = Path(tmp) / "Tilesets.txt" tilesets.write_text("version = 1
", encoding="utf-8") knoxmap_setup.ensure_road_catalogue(tilesets) content = tilesets.read_text(encoding="utf-8") self.assertIn("street_curbs_01", content) self.assertIn("street_trafficlines_01", content) self.assertIn("floors_exterior_natural_01", content)

nodes.body_text: class RoofLayouts(unittest.TestCase): def test_roof_rectangles_cover_an_irregular_footprint_once(self): grid = [[1] * 8 + [0] * 4 for _ in range(4)] grid.extend([[1] * 12 for _ in range(8)]) rects = layout.roof_rects(grid) for peaked, roof30 in ((False, False), (True, False), (True, True)): with self.subTest(peaked=peaked, roof30=roof30): covered = [[0] * 12 for _ in range(12)] for _kind, _depth, _caps, (x0, y0, width, height) in tbx._roof_pieces( rects, peaked, roof30): for y in range(y0, y0 + height): for x in range(x0, x0 + width): covered[y][x] += 1 self.assertEqual(covered, grid) def test_flat_roof_equipment_varies_by_building_without_overlapping(self): grid = [[1] * 10 for _ in range(10)] first = tbx._rooftop(grid, 10, 10, "house-a") second = tbx._rooftop(grid, 10, 10, "house-b") self.assertNotEqual(first, second) for placement in (first, second): for index, (_role, x, y, _orientation) in enumerate(placement): for _other, other_x, other_y, _other_orientation in placement[index + 1:]: self.assertTrue(abs(x - other_x) > 1 or abs(y - other_y) > 1) def test_every_roof_piece_is_one_the_world_painter_can_draw(self): # buildroofs.roof_squares has no branch for a Peak30Quad whose longer # side is even, so such a piece paints nothing: the house keeps its # walls and loses its entire roof (108 houses in one town). from knoxbuild.buildroofs import roof_squares for w in range(3, 14): for h in range(3, 14): grid = [[1] * w for _ in range(h)] for kind, depth, _caps, (x, y, pw, ph) in tbx._roof_pieces( layout.roof_rects(grid), True, True): if kind == "FlatTop": continue with self.subTest(kind=kind, w=w, h=h): self.assertTrue(roof_squares( lambda n: {}, {}, dict(RoofType=kind, Depth=depth, x=x, y=y, width=pw, height=ph))) def test_flat_roof_plant_stands_on_the_roof(self): # The game hangs an attachedCeiling tile from the ceiling of its level: # on the roof floor that is a storey above the roof, which is how the # vents and the hatch came to float over the buildings. Only the # air-conditioning unit stands on the floor, so it is all a roof gets. from knoxbuild import catalog as C grid = [[1] * 12 for _ in range(12)] roles = {role for role, *_rest in tbx._rooftop(grid, 12, 12, "house-a")} self.assertEqual(roles, {"roof_ac"}) tiles = {tile for orients in C.FURNITURE["roof_ac"].values() for tile in orients.values()} self.assertEqual(tiles, {"rooftop_furniture_000", "rooftop_furniture_001"}) def test_a_wide_block_among_many_wings_is_not_given_the_steep_roof(self): # An 11-wide block with two narrow wings: three pieces, so the block takes the # 45-degree roof (three levels at most), not a 30-degree one six levels high. grid = [[1] * 11 for _ in range(12)] for y in range(2, 5): grid[y] += [1] * 3 for y in range(8, 11): grid[y] += [1] * 3 grid = [row + [0] * (14 - len(row)) for row in grid] kinds = [k for k, _d, _c, box in tbx._roof_pieces(layout.roof_rects(grid), True, True) if box[2] * box[3] >= 100] self.assertTrue(kinds and all(not k.startswith("Peak30") for k in kinds), kinds) # Alone, the same block keeps it. alone = tbx._roof_pieces(layout.roof_rects([[1] * 11 for _ in range(12)]), True, True) self.assertTrue(any(k.startswith("Peak30") for k, *_ in alone), alone) def test_tiny_pieces_of_a_many_wing_footprint_stay_flat(self): # A staircase of 2x2 steps: many small rectangles, none worth a gable of its own. grid = [[0] * 12 for _ in range(12)] for i in range(6): for y in range(2 * i, 2 * i + 2): for x in range(2 * i, 12): grid[y][x] = 1 pieces = tbx._roof_pieces(layout.roof_rects(grid), True, True) small = [k for k, _d, _c, (_x, _y, w, h) in pieces if w * h < tbx.MANY_WING_MIN_PITCHED_AREA] self.assertTrue(len(pieces) >= tbx.MANY_WING_RECTS and small) self.assertEqual(set(small), {"FlatTop"}) # One small house on its own keeps its gable. alone = tbx._roof_pieces(layout.roof_rects([[1] * 3 for _ in range(2)]), True, True) self.assertNotEqual(alone[0][0], "FlatTop")

nodes.name: test_room_budget.py
nodes.body_text: """Thinning a building's rooms so the map fits the game's save buffer. The game writes every room and building in the world through one 10 MB buffer (tools/make_map_mod.py). A map past it keeps nothing: the write throws and no save stores which buildings are explored, alarmed or lit. Rather than tell the player to generate a smaller map, the rooms are merged down to what fits - walls, doors, furniture and the buildings themselves stay as they are. """ import csv import glob import os import tempfile import unittest from unittest import mock from knoxbuild import layout, placement, presets from knoxbuild.build import _rooms_that_fit from knoxbuild.layout import build_building from knoxbuild.settings import Settings from tests.basement_town import build_town from tools import make_map_mod if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: tiled
nodes.body_text: def tiled(plan): """The squares this storey gave to a room, as {(x, y)}.""" return {(x, y) for y, row in enumerate(plan.grid) for x, v in enumerate(row) if v}

nodes.name: ThinningOneStorey
nodes.body_text: class ThinningOneStorey(unittest.TestCase): def house(self): return build_building(22, 18, levels=2, seed=5, kind="house").storeys[0] def test_it_merges_down_to_the_limit(self): plan = self.house() was = len(plan.rooms) self.assertGreater(was, 8) merged = layout.thin_plan(plan, was // 2) self.assertGreater(merged, 0) self.assertEqual(len(plan.rooms), was - merged) self.assertLessEqual(len(plan.rooms), was // 2) def test_not_one_square_of_the_plan_is_lost(self): plan = self.house() before = tiled(plan) layout.thin_plan(plan, 6) self.assertEqual(tiled(plan), before) def test_every_room_left_owns_squares_and_is_numbered_in_order(self): plan = self.house() layout.thin_plan(plan, 6) owned = {v for row in plan.grid for v in row if v} self.assertEqual(owned, set(range(1, len(plan.rooms) + 1))) def test_the_walls_doors_and_windows_stay_where_they_were(self): plan = self.house() doors, windows = list(plan.doors), list(plan.windows) furniture = list(plan.furniture) layout.thin_plan(plan, 6) self.assertEqual(plan.doors, doors) self.assertEqual(plan.windows, windows) self.assertEqual(plan.furniture, furniture) def test_a_plan_drawn_by_hand_is_left_alone(self): plan = self.house() plan.drawn = True was = len(plan.rooms) self.assertEqual(layout.thin_plan(plan, 3), 0) self.assertEqual(len(plan.rooms), was) def test_the_stair_core_is_never_merged_away(self): plan = self.house() layout.thin_plan(plan, layout.THIN_MIN_ROOMS) self.assertTrue(any(room.is_core for room in plan.rooms)) def test_two_flats_are_never_joined(self): flats = build_building(30, 26, levels=2, seed=3, kind="apartment").storeys[0] unit_by_tile = {(x, y): flats.rooms[v - 1].unit for y, row in enumerate(flats.grid) for x, v in enumerate(row) if v} layout.thin_plan(flats, 6) dwellings = {} for y, row in enumerate(flats.grid): for x, v in enumerate(row): if v: dwellings.setdefault(v, set()).add(unit_by_tile[(x, y)]) for units in dwellings.values(): self.assertEqual(len(units), 1, "one room spans two dwellings")

nodes.name: AWholeTownFitsTheBuffer
nodes.body_text: class AWholeTownFitsTheBuffer(unittest.TestCase): """The pass that runs once every building is laid out: a town that would not fit is thinned, and what reaches the game fits (knoxbuild/build.py).""" def town(self, folder: str, budget: int | None = None) -> dict: settings = Settings(seed=7) name = os.path.basename(folder) if budget is None: build_town(folder, settings, compile_lots=False) else: with mock.patch.object(make_map_mod, "META_BUDGET", budget): build_town(folder, settings, compile_lots=False) files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(folder, "buildings", "*.tbx"))) rooms = {} for path in files: with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: rooms[os.path.basename(path)] = presets.measure(f.read())["rooms"] with open(os.path.join(folder, f"{name}_placements.csv"), encoding="utf-8") as f: rows = list(csv.DictReader(f)) cells = placement.project_size(folder, name) return {"rooms": rooms, "files": set(rooms), "rows": len(rows), "cells": cells[0] * cells[1], "total": sum(rooms.values()), "cellars": sum(1 for n in rooms if n.endswith("_bsmt.tbx"))} def test_a_town_past_the_buffer_comes_out_thin_and_whole(self): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work: plain = self.town(os.path.join(work, "plain", "town")) self.assertGreater(plain["total"], 200) # A buffer that leaves room for three quarters of the town's rooms, basements # included - the same sum the game's map_meta.bin holds. allowed = plain["total"] * 3 // 4 budget = (10 * allowed + 23 * (plain["rows"] + plain["cellars"]) + 8 * plain["cells"] + make_map_mod.KNOX_COUNTY_META) thin = self.town(os.path.join(work, "thin", "town"), budget) self.assertLess(thin["total"], plain["total"], "nothing was thinned") self.assertLessEqual(thin["total"], allowed, "more rooms than the buffer holds") self.assertEqual(thin["files"], plain["files"], "a building was lost") self.assertEqual(thin["rows"], plain["rows"], "a placement was lost") self.assertEqual(thin["cellars"], plain["cellars"], "a basement was lost")

nodes.body_text: class DemoHouses(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.lays = {name: R.solve(house, prog, seconds=3.0, workers=4) for name, (house, prog) in HOUSES.items() if not prog.startswith("shop") and prog != "flats_block"} def test_every_house_solves_and_keeps_the_rules(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIsNotNone(lay) self.assertEqual(R.check(lay), []) def test_bedrooms_upstairs_except_in_a_bungalow(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): ground = {r["kind"] for r in lay.storeys[0]["rooms"]} with self.subTest(name=name): if len(lay.storeys) > 1: self.assertFalse(ground & set(R.RULES["bedroom_kinds"])) else: self.assertTrue(ground & set(R.RULES["bedroom_kinds"])) self.assertIsNone(lay.stairs) def test_rooms_with_stairs_are_small(self): # the hall and landing: the 5 stair squares and a little passage for name, lay in self.lays.items(): for st in lay.storeys: for room in st["rooms"]: if room["kind"] in R.ROOT_KINDS: with self.subTest(name=name, kind=room["kind"]): self.assertLessEqual(len(room["squares"]), R.STAIR_RUN + 8) def test_stairs_run_along_a_wall(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): if lay.stairs: x, y, d = lay.stairs with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIn((x, y, 1 if d == "N" else 0), R.stair_places(lay.house)) def test_kitchen_at_the_back_with_the_back_door(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIsNotNone(lay.back_door) st = lay.storeys[0] a, b = R._door_squares(lay.back_door) inside = a if R._room_at(st["grid"], *a) else b room = st["rooms"][st["grid"][inside[1]][inside[0]] - 1] self.assertIn(room["kind"], ("kitchen", "kitchen_diner", "kitchen_breakfast", "utility")) def test_windows_are_the_rooms_own(self): # every window: in its room's wall, the room within its cap (the solver's own choice) for name, lay in self.lays.items(): for st in lay.storeys: for room in st["rooms"]: spots = room.get("windows", []) with self.subTest(name=name, kind=room["kind"]): self.assertLessEqual(len(spots), R.KINDS[room["kind"]]["cap"]) for (x, y, _) in spots: self.assertIn((x, y), room["squares"]) def test_bathrooms_are_at_least_two_by_two(self): # the game's bathroom fittings need 2 x 2 (user, 2026-10-20) for name, lay in self.lays.items(): for st in lay.storeys: for room in st["rooms"]: if room["build"] == "bathroom": with self.subTest(name=name, kind=room["kind"]): for x0, y0, x1, y1 in room["rects"]: self.assertGreaterEqual(min(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) + 1, 2) if room["kind"] == "bathroom": # a bath, toilet, sink and cupboard: 3 x 2 at least x0, y0, x1, y1 = room["rects"][0] self.assertGreaterEqual(max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) + 1, 3) def test_windows_stack(self): # most first-floor windows sit over a ground-floor one for name, lay in self.lays.items(): if len(lay.storeys) < 2: continue down = set(lay.storeys[0]["windows"]) up = set(lay.storeys[1]["windows"]) with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertGreaterEqual(len(up & down), len(up) // 2)

nodes.name: Cache
nodes.body_text: class Cache(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): import tempfile self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp() self.house, self.prog = HOUSES["iw_semi"] def test_saved_layouts_come_back_the_same(self): cache = R.LayoutCache(self.dir) first = R.layout_for(self.house, self.prog, "a", cache) cache.save() again = R.layout_for(self.house, self.prog, "a", R.LayoutCache(self.dir)) self.assertEqual([st["grid"] for st in first.storeys], [st["grid"] for st in again.storeys]) self.assertEqual(first.stairs, again.stairs) self.assertEqual(R.check(again), []) def test_the_pair_of_a_semi_comes_from_its_twin(self): cache = R.LayoutCache(self.dir) R.layout_for(self.house, self.prog, "a", cache) twin = R.mirror_house(self.house) self.assertTrue(cache.known(twin, self.prog)) options = cache.options(twin, self.prog) self.assertTrue(options) party_edges = {R._edge(*e) for e in twin.party} for lay in options: self.assertEqual(R.check(lay), []) # the party wall moved to the other side: no window or door in it for st in lay.storeys: self.assertFalse(party_edges & set(st["windows"])) self.assertFalse(party_edges & set(st["doors"])) def test_a_footprint_with_no_layout_is_remembered(self): tiny = R.House(3, 3, [[[True] * 3 for _ in range(3)]] * 2, "S") cache = R.LayoutCache(self.dir) self.assertIsNone(R.layout_for(tiny, "semi_interwar", "a", cache)) self.assertTrue(cache.known(tiny, "semi_interwar")) def test_editing_one_kind_keeps_other_programmes_cached(self): import copy before = {n: R.programme_hash(n) for n in ("semi_interwar", "period_large")} saved = copy.deepcopy(R.KINDS["drawing_room"]) try: R.KINDS["drawing_room"]["target"] += 1 R._PROG_HASH.clear() self.assertEqual(R.programme_hash("semi_interwar"), before["semi_interwar"]) self.assertNotEqual(R.programme_hash("period_large"), before["period_large"]) finally: R.KINDS["drawing_room"] = saved R._PROG_HASH.clear() def test_mirror_twice_is_the_same_layout(self): lay = R.solve(self.house, self.prog) twin = R.mirror_house(self.house) back = R.mirror(R.mirror(lay, twin), self.house) self.assertEqual([st["grid"] for st in back.storeys], [st["grid"] for st in lay.storeys]) self.assertEqual(sorted(back.storeys[0]["windows"]), sorted(lay.storeys[0]["windows"])) self.assertEqual(sorted(back.storeys[0]["doors"]), sorted(lay.storeys[0]["doors"]))

nodes.name: IntoBuild
nodes.body_text: class IntoBuild(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_layout_becomes_a_furnished_building_and_a_tbx(self): from knoxbuild.tbx import render_tbx house, prog = HOUSES["iw_semi"] lay = R.solve(house, prog) # Build's party walls: the neighbour is one storey (a bungalow beside it) party = {R._edge(*e): 1 for e in house.party} b = R.to_building(lay, seed=3, party=party) self.assertEqual(len(b.storeys), 2) self.assertEqual(b.stairs, [lay.stairs]) self.assertTrue(b.storeys[0].party) self.assertFalse(b.storeys[1].party) # above the neighbour: an outside wall self.assertTrue(all(s.furniture for s in b.storeys)) self.assertIn("<room", render_tbx(b, "test", None)) def test_off_unless_the_setting_or_the_environment_says(self): import os from types import SimpleNamespace saved = os.environ.pop("KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER", None) try: self.assertFalse(R.wanted(SimpleNamespace(room_solver=0))) # the default self.assertTrue(R.wanted(SimpleNamespace(room_solver=1))) self.assertFalse(R.wanted(object())) # settings without it os.environ["KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER"] = "0" self.assertFalse(R.wanted(SimpleNamespace(room_solver=1))) os.environ["KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER"] = "1" self.assertTrue(R.wanted(SimpleNamespace(room_solver=0))) finally: os.environ.pop("KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER", None) if saved is not None: os.environ["KNOXMAP_ROOM_SOLVER"] = saved

nodes.body_text: class HomesOverShops(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.lays = {n: R.solve(*HOUSES[n]) for n in ("shop_home", "shop_two_flats")} def test_they_solve(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIsNotNone(lay) self.assertEqual(R.check(lay), []) def test_no_door_between_two_flats(self): lay = self.lays["shop_two_flats"] for st in lay.storeys: for room in st["rooms"]: if room["parent"] is not None: p = st["rooms"][room["parent"]] if room["kind"] != "flat_hall": self.assertEqual(room["unit"], p["unit"]) def test_the_shop_and_the_flats_each_have_a_street_door(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): st = lay.storeys[0] street = [e for e in st["doors"] if e[2] == "N" and e[1] == lay.house.height] # street S with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertGreaterEqual(len(street), 2) self.assertTrue(st.get("shop_front")) def test_build_names_the_shop_and_keeps_the_lobby(self): lay = self.lays["shop_home"] b = R.to_building(lay, seed=1, uses=[("grocery", "grocerystorage")]) ground = b.storeys[0] kinds = {r.kind for r in ground.rooms} self.assertIn("grocery", kinds) self.assertIn("hall", kinds) self.assertEqual(ground.kind, "shop") self.assertTrue(ground.shop_front)

nodes.name: Businesses
nodes.body_text: class Businesses(unittest.TestCase): """Commercial ground floors by class, store rooms over them, pubs.""" @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.lays = {n: R.solve(*HOUSES[n]) for n in BUSINESSES} def test_they_solve_and_keep_the_rules(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIsNotNone(lay) self.assertEqual(R.check(lay), []) def test_rooms_are_named_after_the_business(self): b = R.to_building(self.lays["takeaway_home"], seed=1, uses=[("restaurantdining", "pizzakitchen")]) kinds = {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms} self.assertTrue({"restaurantdining", "pizzakitchen", "hall"} <= kinds) self.assertEqual(b.storeys[1].kind, "apartment") b = R.to_building(self.lays["surgery"], seed=1, uses=[("dentist", "medicaloffice")]) self.assertIn("dentist", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms}) def test_a_pubs_kitchen_stays_a_kitchen(self): lay = self.lays["pub_two_bars"] b = R.to_building(lay, seed=1, uses=[("restaurantdining", "restaurantkitchen"), ("bar", "barstorage")]) kinds = [r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms] self.assertGreaterEqual(kinds.count("bar"), 1) # the bars (the lounge and a snug are optional) self.assertIn("barstorage", kinds) if any(r["kind"] == "shop_kitchen" for r in lay.storeys[0]["rooms"]): self.assertIn("restaurantkitchen", kinds) def test_no_homes_store_rooms_upstairs_and_one_street_door(self): lay = self.lays["shop_stores_over"] b = R.to_building(lay, seed=1, uses=[("generalstore", "storage")]) self.assertEqual(b.storeys[1].kind, "shop") self.assertTrue({r.kind for r in b.storeys[1].rooms} <= {"storage", "breakroom", "bathroom", "closet", "hall"}) st = lay.storeys[0] street = [e for e in st["doors"] if e[2] == "N" and e[1] == lay.house.height] # street S self.assertEqual(street, [lay.front_door]) # the shop's: the stair hall has none def test_the_waiting_room_has_its_own_street_door(self): lay = self.lays["surgery"] waiting = next(r for r in lay.storeys[0]["rooms"] if r["kind"] == "waiting") mine = {R._edge(x, y, "S") for (x, y) in waiting["squares"] if y == lay.house.height - 1} self.assertIn(lay.front_door, mine) def test_programmes_by_homes_and_class(self): self.assertEqual(R.shop_programme(1, 0, "retail"), "shop_only@retail") self.assertEqual(R.shop_programme(2, 1, "retail"), "shop_house") self.assertEqual(R.shop_programme(2, 1, "food"), "shop_house@food") self.assertEqual(R.shop_programme(3, 3, "pub"), "shop_flats2@pub") self.assertIsNone(R.shop_programme(6, 0, "retail")) self.assertEqual(R.use_class(("bar", "barstorage")), "pub") self.assertEqual(R.use_class(("butcher", "storage")), "retail") self.assertEqual(R.shop_use_of([("butcher", "storage")]), ("butcher", "storage")) self.assertIsNone(R.shop_use_of([("butcher", "storage"), ("bank", "office")])) self.assertTrue(R.is_programme("shop_only@bank") and R.is_programme("shop_flats@food")) self.assertFalse(R.is_programme("shop_only@nothing")) self.assertNotEqual(R.programme_hash("shop_only@bank"), R.programme_hash("shop_only@retail"))

nodes.body_text: class BlocksOfFlats(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.lays = {n: R.solve(h, p) for n, (h, p) in HOUSES.items() if p == "flats_block"} def test_they_solve(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): with self.subTest(name=name): self.assertIsNotNone(lay) self.assertEqual(R.check(lay), []) def test_each_flat_has_one_front_door_off_the_shared_hall(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): for st in lay.storeys: flats = {r["unit"] for r in st["rooms"] if r.get("unit")} for u in flats: halls = [r for r in st["rooms"] if r.get("unit") == u and r["kind"] == "flat_hall"] with self.subTest(name=name, flat=u): self.assertEqual(len(halls), 1) self.assertEqual(st["rooms"][halls[0]["parent"]].get("unit", 0), 0) for r in st["rooms"]: if r["parent"] is not None and r["kind"] != "flat_hall": self.assertEqual(r.get("unit", 0), st["rooms"][r["parent"]].get("unit", 0)) def test_each_flat_has_a_bathroom_and_a_living_room(self): for name, lay in self.lays.items(): for st in lay.storeys: for u in {r["unit"] for r in st["rooms"] if r.get("unit")}: kinds = {r["kind"] for r in st["rooms"] if r.get("unit") == u} with self.subTest(name=name, flat=u): self.assertIn("bathroom", kinds) self.assertTrue(kinds & {"living", "openplan"}) def test_floors_of_one_outline_have_the_same_flats(self): lay = self.lays["flats_conversion"] shapes = [sorted((r["kind"], sorted(r["squares"])) for r in st["rooms"] if r.get("unit")) for st in lay.storeys[1:]] self.assertEqual(shapes[0], shapes[1])

nodes.name: test_rooms_together.py
nodes.body_text: """Pieces that belong together are put together. Measured over 60 houses and flats before and after: a bed with a bedside table 19% to 74%, a sofa with a coffee table 34% to 51%, dining tables 2.0 to 2.7 chairs, a kitchen with fridge, stove and sink in one run of worktop 36% to 48%. The thresholds sit under the after figures on a smaller sample. """ import random import unittest from unittest import mock from knoxbuild import interiors as I, layout as L if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: near
nodes.body_text: def near(a, b, d=1): return any(abs(x1 - x2) + abs(y1 - y2) <= d for x1, y1 in L._tiles_under(*a) for x2, y2 in L._tiles_under(*b))

nodes.name: RoomsTogether
nodes.body_text: class RoomsTogether(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.rooms = [] rng = random.Random(3) for i in range(30): kind = rng.choice([None, None, "apartment"]) # Where pieces stand, not which wood they are in: the wood pass # (interiors.one_wood) swaps a bedside chest for a dresser of the # home's wood, which these would not know from any other dresser. with mock.patch.object(I, "one_wood", lambda *a: None): b = L.build_building(rng.randint(10, 22), rng.randint(9, 18), levels=rng.choice((1, 2)), seed=i, kind=kind) for s in b.storeys: for idx, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): fs = [f for f in s.furniture if 0 <= f[2] < s.height and 0 <= f[1] < s.width and s.grid[f[2]][f[1]] == idx] cls.rooms.append((r.kind, fs)) def share(self, pick, ok): got = [ok(p, fs) for _k, fs in self.rooms for p in fs if pick(p)] self.assertGreater(len(got), 10) return sum(got) / len(got) def test_beds_have_a_bedside_table(self): self.assertGreater(self.share( lambda f: f[0].startswith(("bed", "double_bed")), lambda b, fs: any(f[0] in ("nightstand", "sidetable") and near(f, b) for f in fs)), 0.6) def test_sofas_have_a_coffee_table(self): self.assertGreater(self.share( lambda f: f[0] == "sofa" or f[0].startswith("sofa_"), lambda so, fs: any(f[0] == "coffee_table" and near(f, so, 2) for f in fs)), 0.4) def test_kitchens_are_one_run(self): runs = total = 0 for kind, fs in self.rooms: if kind not in ("kitchen", "openplan"): continue pieces = [f for f in fs if f[0].startswith(("counter", "stove", "fridge")) or L._is_sink(f[0])] key = [next((f for f in pieces if f[0].startswith(k)), None) for k in ("fridge", "stove")] key.append(next((f for f in pieces if L._is_sink(f[0])), None)) if None in key: continue total += 1 seen, todo = {0}, [0] while todo: a = todo.pop() for j, p in enumerate(pieces): if j not in seen and near(pieces[a], p): seen.add(j) todo.append(j) runs += all(any(pieces[j] is k for j in seen) for k in key) self.assertGreater(total, 20) self.assertGreater(runs / total, 0.38)

nodes.body_text: class Sea(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_shore_across_the_map_makes_one_sea(self): # land on the left of a line running west to east: the north half is water. faces = sea_polygons([coast(1, [(-5, 50), (105, 50)])], _Proj()) self.assertEqual(len(faces), 1) self.assertAlmostEqual(faces[0].area, 5000, delta=300) def test_a_loose_end_inside_the_map_is_carried_on(self): faces = sea_polygons([coast(1, [(-5, 50), (60, 50)])], _Proj()) self.assertEqual(len(faces), 1) self.assertGreater(faces[0].area, 4000) def test_a_junction_is_not_a_loose_end(self): # Two shores crossing at (50, 50): every end of the pieces they are cut # into at the crossing used to fire a ray across the whole map. shores = [coast(1, [(-5, 50), (105, 50)]), coast(2, [(50, -5), (50, 105)])] faces = sea_polygons(shores, _Proj()) total = sum(f.area for f in faces) # at most the map itself, split along lines that stay on the grid self.assertLessEqual(total, 10000 + 1) for f in faces: minx, miny, maxx, maxy = f.bounds self.assertGreaterEqual(minx, -0.001) self.assertLessEqual(maxx, 100.001)
