nodes.name: test_shared_buildings.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings passed from one person to another, and the library they ship in. A hand-built building lived in two or three files beside the app and could not leave the PC it was made on. It now goes out as one file - the .tbx, the drawing it was made from and what it stands in for - which anyone can take in, and which `tools/add_shared_building.py` can put into the library that ships with KnoxMap (knoxbuild/share.py). What arrives that way came from a stranger over a chat program, so most of this is about what `read` refuses. """ import json import os import tempfile import unittest from knoxbuild import designer as D from knoxbuild import presets as P from knoxbuild import share as S # What `measure` needs to see to call something a building: the header, and a # <floor> per storey plus one for the roof. TBX = ('<building version="4" width="12" height="10">' '<room name="hall"/><room name="kitchen"/>' '<floor></floor><floor></floor><floor></floor>' '</building>') DESIGN = {"width": 12, "height": 10, "storeys": 2, "kind": "police", "rooms": [{"level": 0, "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 6, "h": 10, "kind": "hall"}, {"level": 0, "x": 6, "y": 0, "w": 6, "h": 10, "kind": "office"}]} if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: shared
nodes.body_text: def shared(**changes) -> dict: out = S.wrap("Station House", TBX, D.clean(DESIGN), kind="police", author="Zombaxx", notes="Cells at the back.") out.update(changes) return out

nodes.body_text: class WhatComesInIsChecked(unittest.TestCase): def refused(self, data) -> str: entry, problem = S.read(data) self.assertIsNone(entry) self.assertTrue(problem) return problem def test_a_building_shared_from_knoxmap_is_taken(self): entry, problem = S.read(shared()) self.assertIsNone(problem) self.assertEqual(entry["name"], "Station House") self.assertEqual(entry["kind"], "police") self.assertEqual(entry["author"], "Zombaxx") self.assertEqual((entry["width"], entry["height"], entry["storeys"]), (12, 10, 2)) def test_and_it_survives_being_written_out_and_read_back(self): entry, _ = S.read(json.loads(json.dumps(shared()))) self.assertEqual(entry["tbx"], TBX) self.assertEqual(len(entry["design"]["rooms"]), 2) def test_anything_else_is_not_a_building(self): for what in (None, [], "a string", 7, {}, {"format": "zip"}): with self.subTest(what=what): self.refused(what) def test_a_file_from_another_version_says_so(self): self.assertIn("another version", self.refused(shared(version=99))) def test_a_building_with_no_name_is_refused(self): self.refused(shared(name="")) self.refused(shared(name="///")) def test_so_is_one_with_no_building_in_it(self): self.refused(shared(tbx="")) self.refused(shared(tbx="hello")) self.refused(shared(tbx=None)) def test_and_one_too_big_to_be_a_building(self): self.assertIn("past the", self.refused(shared(tbx="x" * (S.MAX_TBX_CHARS + 1)))) wide = TBX.replace('width="12"', f'width="{S.MAX_SIDE + 1}"') self.assertIn("a side", self.refused(shared(tbx=wide))) def test_an_xml_bomb_is_not_even_opened(self): # A few nested entities expand into gigabytes in the parser, and # knoxbuild/buildtiles.py reads these with ElementTree, which expands # them. A .tbx never needs a doctype, so one that has it is refused. bomb = ('<!DOCTYPE lol [<!ENTITY a "aaaaaaaaaa">' '<!ENTITY b "&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;&a;">]>' + TBX) self.assertIn("document type", self.refused(shared(tbx=bomb))) self.refused(shared(tbx=TBX.replace("<building", "<!ENTITY x><building"))) def test_a_kind_this_version_does_not_have_is_no_kind(self): entry, problem = S.read(shared(kind="spaceport")) self.assertIsNone(problem) self.assertEqual(entry["kind"], P.ANY) def test_a_drawing_that_cannot_be_read_does_not_cost_the_building(self): entry, problem = S.read(shared(design="not a drawing")) self.assertIsNone(problem) self.assertIsNone(entry["design"]) self.assertEqual(entry["tbx"], TBX) def test_the_name_of_the_file_cannot_walk_out_of_the_folder(self): for name in ("../../etc/passwd", "..\\..\\windows", "a/b", "CON"): with self.subTest(name=name): out = S.file_name(name) self.assertTrue(out.endswith(S.SUFFIX)) self.assertNotIn("/", out) self.assertNotIn("\\", out) self.assertNotIn("..", out)

What knoxbuild/build.py asks for a plot the map says is a police # station, with "police" switched on. listed = P.library(self.home) pick = P.choose_for_kind(listed, "police", 20, 16, seed=3) self.assertIsNotNone(pick, "a shipped building was not offered") self.assertEqual(pick["name"], "Station House") self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(pick["file"])) # And not for a plot it does not fit on. self.assertIsNone(P.choose_for_kind(listed, "police", 8, 8, seed=3)) def test_sharing_a_shipped_one_keeps_the_credit_on_it(self): entry = S.of_preset(self.home, "Station House") self.assertEqual(entry["author"], "Zombaxx") self.assertEqual(entry["kind"], "police") self.assertTrue(entry.get("design")) self.assertEqual(entry["tbx"], TBX) def test_and_sharing_one_that_is_not_there_says_so(self): with self.assertRaises(ValueError): S.of_preset(self.home, "No Such Building")

nodes.name: test_shell_menus.py
nodes.body_text: """The window's menu bar (static/js/shell.js) and what the Tools menu opens. A menu with no items is a dead button: `MENUS` builds the bar and a matching `fillMenu` case fills it, and the two are separate lists that can drift. The Tools menu is the map developer's way in to the extract picker and the check. """ import os import re import unittest ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: read
nodes.body_text: def read(*parts) -> str: with open(os.path.join(ROOT, *parts), encoding="utf-8") as fh: return fh.read()

nodes.name: MenuBar
nodes.body_text: class MenuBar(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.shell = read("static", "js", "shell.js") def menus(self) -> list[str]: found = re.search(r"const MENUS = \[([^\]]+)\]", self.shell) self.assertIsNotNone(found, "the menu bar is built from MENUS") return re.findall(r"'([^']+)'", found.group(1)) def test_tools_sits_between_build_and_help(self): menus = self.menus() self.assertEqual(menus[-3:], ["Build", "Tools", "Help"]) def test_every_menu_has_items(self): for name in self.menus(): with self.subTest(menu=name): self.assertRegex(self.shell, rf"\n\s+{name}: \(\) =>", f"no fillMenu case for {name}") def test_the_tools_menu_opens_the_extract_tool(self): self.assertIn("check an openstreetmap extract", self.shell.lower()) self.assertIn("$('toolsBody')", self.shell) def test_the_panel_it_opens_is_in_the_page(self): for element in ("pbfFile", "pbfBrowse", "pbfUse", "pbfClear", "pbfCheck", "pbfReport", "toolsBody"): with self.subTest(element=element): self.assertEqual(read("templates", "index.html").count(f'id="{element}"'), 1) def test_the_panel_hides_outside_the_dialog(self): css = read("static", "css", "app.css") self.assertIn("#toolsBody { display: none; }", css) self.assertIn(".ws-dialog #toolsBody { display: block; }", css)

nodes.body_text: """Regression for the shop floor dropped from a generated map. logs/knoxmap.log.1, 2026-11-03 (1.8.4): "building left out ... IndexError: list index out of range" in _fit_out_sections. _shop_rooms recorded 1-based room numbers before _paint; _paint drops, splits and renumbers rooms, so the numbers were stale by the time _fit_out_sections indexed plan.rooms with them. """ import unittest from knoxbuild import layout if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: _band
nodes.body_text: def _band(w, h, y0, y1): """A footprint mask that leaves most of the shop outside the building.""" return [[y0 <= y < y1 for _ in range(w)] for y in range(h)]

nodes.body_text: class PathGuards(unittest.TestCase): def test_save_refuses_a_sibling_prefix(self): """output/foo is not output/foo2: str.startswith used to say it was.""" import tempfile from pathlib import Path from web import common with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: root = Path(tmp) (root / "foo").mkdir() (root / "foo2").mkdir() (root / "foo2" / "secret.txt").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8") old = common.OUTPUT_DIR common.OUTPUT_DIR = root try: map_dir = common._map_dir("foo") self.assertIsNotNone(map_dir) target = (map_dir / ".." / "foo2" / "secret.txt").resolve() self.assertTrue(str(target).startswith(str(map_dir))) # old bug self.assertFalse(target.is_relative_to(map_dir)) # now refused finally: common.OUTPUT_DIR = old

nodes.body_text: def sales_floor(kind, seed, w=36, h=22): plan = layout.build_building(width=w, height=h, kind="shop", seed=seed, levels=1, street="S", uses=[(kind, "storage")]).storeys[0] idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if r.kind == kind) return plan, idx, [f for f in plan.furniture if plan.grid[f[2]][f[1]] == idx]

nodes.body_text: def is_cooler(role): return "fridge" in role or "freezer" in role

nodes.body_text: class CoolersAreBanks(unittest.TestCase): def test_coolers_stand_side_by_side(self): # Scattered between shelves before: one cooler in three had no cooler # beside it. alone = total = 0 for seed in range(12): for kind in ("grocery", "liquorstore"): plan, idx, furniture = sales_floor(kind, seed) tiles = {c for f in furniture if is_cooler(f[0]) for c in layout._cells_for(*f)} for x, y in tiles: total += 1 alone += not any(n in tiles for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1))) self.assertGreater(total, 0) self.assertLess(alone / total, 0.05) def test_a_grocery_has_produce_stands_by_the_door(self): stands = [sum(1 for f in sales_floor("grocery", s)[2] if f[0] == "shop_bin") for s in range(12)] self.assertGreaterEqual(sum(stands) / len(stands), 4) def test_nothing_stands_in_front_of_a_cooler_or_shelf(self): # A drinks machine stood in front of a fridge door, and a fridge in a # notch of the outline faced the wall. step = {"N": (0, 1), "S": (0, -1), "W": (1, 0), "E": (-1, 0)} for seed in range(10): for kind in ("conveniencestore", "grocery", "liquorstore", "gasstore"): for w, h in ((36, 22), (21, 14), (17, 23)): plan, idx, furniture = sales_floor(kind, seed, w, h) # a till stands on its counter, a light switch on the wall taken = {c for f in plan.furniture if f[0] != "register" and not layout._is_wall_piece(f[0]) for c in layout._cells_for(*f)} for role, x, y, orient in furniture: if not (is_cooler(role) or role == "shop_shelf_red"): continue dx, dy = step[orient] for cx, cy in layout._cells_for(role, x, y, orient): front = (cx + dx, cy + dy) with self.subTest(kind=kind, seed=seed, size=(w, h), piece=(role, x, y)): self.assertEqual(plan.grid[front[1]][front[0]], idx) self.assertNotIn(front, taken) def test_drinks_machines_face_into_the_shop(self): # They stood one tile in from the shop front, turned to the window. step = {"N": (0, 1), "S": (0, -1), "W": (1, 0), "E": (-1, 0)} seen = 0 for seed in range(12): plan, idx, furniture = sales_floor("conveniencestore", seed) for role, x, y, orient in furniture: if role.startswith("vending"): seen += 1 dx, dy = step[orient] # its back is to the shop front: outside is behind it bx, by = x - 2 * dx, y - 2 * dy inside = 0 <= by < len(plan.grid) and 0 <= bx < len(plan.grid[0]) self.assertFalse(inside and plan.grid[by][bx] == idx, (role, x, y, orient)) self.assertGreater(seen, 0) def test_convenience_stores_sell_fresh_produce(self): stands = [sum(1 for f in sales_floor(kind, s)[2] if f[0] == "shop_bin") for s in range(8) for kind in ("conveniencestore", "cornerstore")] self.assertGreaterEqual(sum(stands) / len(stands), 1.5) # and only where it is meant to be for s in range(4): self.assertFalse([f for f in sales_floor("candystore", s)[2] if f[0] == "shop_bin"]) def test_display_cases_are_a_row_or_two(self): for seed in range(6): plan, idx, furniture = sales_floor("butcher", seed) cases = {f[2] for f in furniture if f[0] == "shop_display_butcher"} with self.subTest(seed=seed): self.assertTrue(cases) self.assertLessEqual(len({f[1] for f in furniture if f[0] == "shop_display_butcher"}), 2)

full coverage def test_tiles_box(self): box = {(x, y) for x in range(12) for y in range(10)} ordered = 0 for seed in range(50): rooms = S.split_by_targets((0, 0, 11, 9), FLAT, random.Random(seed)) self.assertIsNotNone(rooms, seed) self.assertEqual([r.kind for r in rooms], FLAT) self.assertTrue(all(r.fixed for r in rooms)) self.assertTrue(all(min(r.w, r.h) >= 3 for r in rooms)) self.assertTiles(rooms, box) a = {r.kind: r.area for r in rooms} ordered += a["bathroom"] < a["bedroom"] < a["livingroom"] self.assertGreaterEqual(ordered, 45) def test_too_small(self): self.assertIsNone(S.split_by_targets((0, 0, 4, 3), FLAT, random.Random(0))) def test_deterministic(self): a = S.split_by_targets((2, 3, 15, 12), FLAT, random.Random(9)) self.assertEqual(a, S.split_by_targets((2, 3, 15, 12), FLAT, random.Random(9))) def test_first_edge(self): x0, y0, x1, y1 = box = (1, 2, 13, 11) on = {"N": lambda r: r.y0 == y0, "S": lambda r: r.y1 == y1, "W": lambda r: r.x0 == x0, "E": lambda r: r.x1 == x1} for edge, touches in on.items(): for seed in range(20): rooms = S.split_by_targets(box, FLAT, random.Random(seed), first_edge=edge) self.assertIsNotNone(rooms, (edge, seed)) self.assertEqual(rooms[0].kind, "livingroom") self.assertTrue(touches(rooms[0]), (edge, seed, rooms[0])) def test_masked_l(self): # 12x10 box with the north-east 5x4 corner outside the building. mask = [[not (x >= 7 and y < 4) for x in range(12)] for y in range(10)] inside = {(x, y) for y in range(10) for x in range(12) if mask[y][x]} for seed in range(20): rooms = S.split_by_targets((0, 0, 11, 9), FLAT, random.Random(seed), mask) self.assertIsNotNone(rooms, seed) self.assertTiles(rooms, inside) self.assertTrue(all(min(r.w, r.h) >= 3 for r in rooms)) def test_mask_hole_none(self): # One tile missing mid-floor: no room may hold it, nothing can cut it out. mask = [[(x, y) != (5, 5) for x in range(12)] for y in range(10)] self.assertIsNone(S.split_by_targets((0, 0, 11, 9), FLAT, random.Random(0), mask))

nodes.name: _flat_floors
nodes.body_text: def _flat_floors(n=100): """Every storey of n flat blocks of varied footprint.""" from knoxbuild import layout as L rng = random.Random(11) for i in range(n): w, h = rng.randint(9, 22), rng.randint(8, 18) b = L.build_building(w, h, levels=rng.randint(2, 4), kind="apartment", seed=i) yield from b.storeys

nodes.name: _touches_corridor
nodes.body_text: def _touches_corridor(plan, idx): for y in range(plan.height): for x in range(plan.width): if plan.grid[y][x] != idx: continue for nx, ny in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if (0 <= nx < plan.width and 0 <= ny < plan.height and plan.grid[ny][nx] and plan.rooms[plan.grid[ny][nx] - 1].unit == 0): return True return False

nodes.name: _masked_flat_floors
nodes.body_text: def _masked_flat_floors(): """(block, storey, plan) of 140 flat blocks on irregular and turned footprints, as tools/audit_layouts.py builds them; built once.""" if not _MASKED: from knoxbuild import layout as L irregular_mask, rotated_mask = _audit_masks() rng = random.Random(4242) for i in range(140): w, h = rng.randint(9, 40), rng.randint(9, 40) if i % 2: mask = irregular_mask(w, h, rng) else: fp = rotated_mask(rng) if fp is None: continue w, h, mask = fp.width, fp.height, fp.mask_list() b = L.build_building(w, h, levels=rng.choice((2, 3, 4, 5)), seed=i, kind="apartment", mask=mask) _MASKED.extend((i, n, plan) for n, plan in enumerate(b.storeys)) return _MASKED

nodes.body_text: class Flats(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.floors = list(_flat_floors()) def test_medians(self): import statistics as st area = {"bath": [], "bed": [], "living": []} for plan in self.floors: for r in plan.rooms: key = ("bath" if r.kind == "bathroom" else "bed" if r.kind == "bedroom" else "living" if r.kind in LIVING else None) if key and not r.is_core: area[key].append(r.area) m = {k: st.median(v) for k, v in area.items()} self.assertLess(m["bath"], m["bed"], m) self.assertLess(m["bed"], m["living"], m) def test_bathrooms_vs_bedrooms(self): baths = beds = flats = 0 for plan in self.floors: baths += sum(r.kind == "bathroom" for r in plan.rooms) beds += sum(r.kind in BEDS for r in plan.rooms) flats += len({r.unit for r in plan.rooms if r.unit}) self.assertLessEqual(baths, beds + flats) def test_living_at_corridor(self): bad = [] for n, plan in enumerate(self.floors): if not plan.corridor: continue units = {r.unit for r in plan.rooms if r.unit} for u in units: if not any(r.unit == u and r.kind in LIVING and _touches_corridor(plan, i) for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1)): bad.append((n, u)) self.assertEqual(bad, []) def test_small_flat_falls_back(self): from knoxbuild import layout as L self.assertIsNone(L._flat_by_kind((0, 0, 4, 3), random.Random(0), False, None, "N")) L._flat_by_kind((0, 0, 5, 4), random.Random(0), False, None, "N") for seed in range(10): b = L.build_building(6, 5, levels=2, kind="apartment", seed=seed) self.assertTrue(all(s.rooms for s in b.storeys)) def test_masked_flats_keep_bathroom(self): bad = [] for i, n, plan in _masked_flat_floors(): for u in {r.unit for r in plan.rooms if r.unit}: rooms = [r for r in plan.rooms if r.unit == u] if (len(rooms) >= 2 and any(r.fixed for r in rooms) and not any(r.kind == "bathroom" for r in rooms)): bad.append((i, n, u)) self.assertEqual(bad, []) def test_masked_flats_living_at_corridor(self): # A flat cut by kind on a clipped footprint (mask plus first_edge) # still mostly has its living room by the front door. flats = at = 0 for _, _, plan in _masked_flat_floors(): if not plan.corridor: continue for u in {r.unit for r in plan.rooms if r.unit}: if not any(r.unit == u and r.fixed for r in plan.rooms): continue flats += 1 at += any(r.unit == u and r.kind in LIVING and _touches_corridor(plan, i) for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1)) self.assertGreater(flats, 100) self.assertGreaterEqual(at, 0.6 * flats, (at, flats)) def test_hotel_unchanged(self): import hashlib from knoxbuild import layout as L out = [] for seed, (w, h) in enumerate([(24, 16), (32, 24), (18, 30)]): b = L.build_building(w, h, levels=3, kind="apartment", hotel=True, seed=seed) out.append(tuple((r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1, r.kind, r.unit) for s in b.storeys for r in s.rooms)) self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(repr(out).encode()).hexdigest(), "645f44026bd40753b1a9617d47707c825d032fcad4d5dcd8e5c06d35c518e3c9")

nodes.body_text: class Houses(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): cls.houses = list(_houses()) def test_medians(self): import statistics as st area: dict[str, list[int]] = {} for b in self.houses: for s in b.storeys: for r in s.rooms: if not r.is_core and not r.is_shaft: area.setdefault(r.kind, []).append(r.area) m = {k: st.median(v) for k, v in area.items()} self.assertLessEqual(m["hall"], m["bedroom"], m) self.assertLess(m["laundry"], m["bedroom"], m) self.assertLess(m["storage"], m["bedroom"], m) self.assertLess(m["bathroom"], m["bedroom"], m) self.assertLess(m["bedroom"], m["livingroom"], m) # A bathroom is not sized like a living room. self.assertLessEqual(m["bathroom"], 0.4 * m["livingroom"], m) # Bedrooms are near their old 20 again, a bathroom 3x4 at most. self.assertLessEqual(m["bathroom"], 0.5 * m["bedroom"], m) self.assertLessEqual(m["bathroom"], 12, m) def test_every_house_has_the_basics(self): for n, b in enumerate(self.houses): kinds = {r.kind for s in b.storeys for r in s.rooms} self.assertTrue(_has_kitchen(kinds), (n, kinds)) self.assertIn("bathroom", kinds, n) self.assertTrue(kinds & set(BEDS), (n, kinds)) def test_small_house(self): from knoxbuild import layout as L for seed in range(10): b = L.build_building(8, 10, levels=1, kind="house", seed=seed) kinds = {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms} self.assertTrue(_has_kitchen(kinds), (seed, kinds)) self.assertIn("bathroom", kinds, seed) self.assertTrue(kinds & set(BEDS), (seed, kinds)) def test_bathroom_on_every_bedroom_floor(self): from knoxbuild import layout as L rng = random.Random(3) for seed in range(20): w, h = rng.randint(9, 20), rng.randint(8, 16) b = L.build_building(w, h, levels=3, kind="house", seed=seed) self.assertEqual(len(b.storeys), 3) for lvl, s in enumerate(b.storeys): kinds = {r.kind for r in s.rooms} if kinds & set(BEDS): self.assertIn("bathroom", kinds, (seed, w, h, lvl, kinds)) def test_upstairs_opens_onto_a_hall(self): # The stairs arrive in a hall, not straight into a bedroom. cores = bad = bed_bed = 0 for b in self.houses: for n, s in enumerate(b.storeys): for a, c in _door_pairs(s): ka, kc = s.rooms[a - 1].kind, s.rooms[c - 1].kind bed_bed += ka in BEDS and kc in BEDS if not n: continue for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if not r.is_core: continue opened = [s.rooms[j - 1] for p in _door_pairs(s) if i in p for j in p if j != i and not s.rooms[j - 1].is_core] cores += 1 bad += bool(opened) and all(o.kind in BEDS + ("bathroom",) for o in opened) self.assertLessEqual(bad, 0.07 * cores, (bad, cores)) self.assertLessEqual(bed_bed, 0.2 * len(self.houses), bed_bed) def test_dining_room_is_the_exception(self): dining = sum(any(r.kind == "dining" for s in b.storeys for r in s.rooms) for b in self.houses) self.assertLessEqual(dining, 0.25 * len(self.houses), dining) def test_some_ground_floors_keep_a_bedroom(self): two = [b for b in self.houses if len(b.storeys) == 2] ground = sum(any(r.kind in BEDS for r in b.storeys[0].rooms) for b in two) self.assertGreater(ground, 0) self.assertLessEqual(ground, 0.4 * len(two), (ground, len(two)))

nodes.name: _door_pairs
nodes.body_text: def _door_pairs(plan): """(room, room) for every door between two rooms of a storey.""" out = [] for x, y, d in plan.doors: a = (plan.grid[y][x - 1] if x > 0 else 0) if d == "W" else ( plan.grid[y - 1][x] if y > 0 else 0) c = plan.grid[y][x] if x < plan.width and y < plan.height else 0 if a and c: out.append((a, c)) return out

nodes.body_text: class OddHouses(unittest.TestCase): """Turned footprints and big rectangles, where a cut sized for the floor but drawn on the whole box made every room twice its size.""" @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): from knoxbuild import layout as L _, rotated_mask = _audit_masks() rng = random.Random(5) cls.turned, cls.big = [], [] for i in range(60): fp = rotated_mask(rng) cls.turned.append(L.build_building( fp.width, fp.height, levels=rng.randint(1, 3), kind="house", seed=i, mask=fp.mask_list())) for i in range(40): w, h = rng.randint(20, 32), rng.randint(16, 24) cls.big.append(L.build_building(w, h, levels=rng.randint(1, 3), kind="house", seed=i)) @staticmethod def _areas(houses): area: dict[str, list[int]] = {} for b in houses: for s in b.storeys: for r in s.rooms: if not r.is_core and not r.is_shaft: area.setdefault(r.kind, []).append(r.area) return area def test_turned(self): import statistics as st a = self._areas(self.turned) self.assertLessEqual(st.median(a["bathroom"]), 14) self.assertLessEqual(max(a["bathroom"]), 30) self.assertLessEqual(max(a["livingroom"]), 120) self.assertLessEqual(st.median(a["livingroom"]), 55) # 1.3 x the old 42 def test_big_rectangles(self): import statistics as st a = self._areas(self.big) self.assertLessEqual(st.median(a["livingroom"]), 47) # 1.3 x the old 36 self.assertLessEqual(st.median(a["bedroom"]), 27) # 1.3 x the old 21

nodes.name: test_sketch.py
nodes.body_text: """A drawn feature has to be a real OSM feature, or it is drawn and then lost. Everything after the drawing - the ground, the buildings, the paper map, the compiled cells - reads tags and nothing else. A palette entry whose tags say nothing to `classify` puts a shape on the page that is simply missing from the finished map, with no error anywhere, so the table is checked against `classify` itself rather than against the comment beside it. """ import unittest from generator import sketch from generator.osm import classify SQUARE = [[[0.0, 0.0], [0.001, 0.0], [0.001, 0.001], [0.0, 0.001], [0.0, 0.0]]] LINE = [[0.0, 0.0], [0.001, 0.001]] # Tools whose mark on the map is not made by `classify`, and why. These are # checked by what they really do instead; anything else that classifies as # nothing is drawn on the page and silently absent from the finished map. NOT_THROUGH_CLASSIFY = { # The ground is not painted for it: the forecourt and its pumps are laid # out round the point by knoxbuild/pumps.py. "fuel", } if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: collection
nodes.body_text: def collection(*features): return {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": list(features)}

nodes.name: drawn
nodes.body_text: def drawn(kind, geometry, coordinates, **props): return {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"kind": kind, **props}, "geometry": {"type": geometry, "coordinates": coordinates}}

nodes.name: Palette
nodes.body_text: class Palette(unittest.TestCase): def test_every_entry_reaches_the_map(self): lost = [e[0] for e in sketch.PALETTE if sketch.category_of(e[0]) is None and e[0] not in NOT_THROUGH_CLASSIFY] self.assertEqual(lost, [], "drawn, then missing from the finished map") def test_the_exceptions_really_are_exceptions(self): # If one of them starts classifying, the excuse above is stale. for entry_id in NOT_THROUGH_CLASSIFY: with self.subTest(entry_id): self.assertIn(entry_id, sketch.BY_ID) self.assertIsNone(sketch.category_of(entry_id)) def test_a_petrol_station_is_a_point_because_the_pumps_need_one(self): # knoxbuild/build.py finds them among the point features; an outline # tagged this way is a building with no forecourt. self.assertEqual(sketch.BY_ID["fuel"][2], "point") def test_ids_are_unique(self): ids = [e[0] for e in sketch.PALETTE] self.assertEqual(len(ids), len(set(ids))) def test_every_tool_is_under_exactly_one_heading(self): # The window builds its palette from these groups; a tool left out of # them is drawn under "Other", and one named here but since removed # leaves a heading with a gap under it. self.assertEqual([e[0] for e in sketch.PALETTE if e[0] not in sketch.GROUP_OF], []) self.assertEqual([i for i in sketch.GROUP_OF if i not in sketch.BY_ID], []) listed = [i for _name, ids in sketch.GROUPS for i in ids] self.assertEqual(len(listed), len(set(listed))) self.assertEqual(len(listed), len(sketch.PALETTE)) def test_the_palette_comes_out_under_one_heading_each(self): # The window starts a heading wherever the group changes, so a group # that appears twice draws two headings with other tools between them. seen, runs = set(), [] for entry in sketch.palette(): if not runs or runs[-1] != entry["group"]: runs.append(entry["group"]) self.assertEqual(len(runs), len(set(runs)), runs) self.assertEqual(runs, [name for name, _ids in sketch.GROUPS]) def test_the_palette_tells_the_window_the_heading(self): groups = {e["group"] for e in sketch.palette()} self.assertNotIn("Other", groups) self.assertEqual(groups, {name for name, _ids in sketch.GROUPS}) def test_geometry_is_one_the_window_can_draw(self): for entry_id, _label, geometry, _tags in sketch.PALETTE: with self.subTest(entry_id): self.assertIn(geometry, ("line", "area", "point")) def test_a_building_entry_is_a_building_to_the_generator(self): # The building generator looks for the tag, not for the category. for entry_id in ("house", "apartments", "school", "church", "shed"): with self.subTest(entry_id): self.assertIn("building", sketch.BY_ID[entry_id][3]) self.assertEqual(sketch.category_of(entry_id), "building") def test_the_road_classes_come_out_in_their_own_classes(self): # A motorway and an alley must not land in the same bucket, or every # drawn road is painted the same width. self.assertEqual(sketch.category_of("motorway"), "road_major") self.assertEqual(sketch.category_of("residential"), "road_minor") self.assertEqual(sketch.category_of("service"), "road_service")

nodes.name: Conversion
nodes.body_text: class Conversion(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_line_keeps_its_points_in_osm_order(self): feats = sketch.features(collection(drawn("residential", "LineString", LINE))) self.assertEqual(len(feats), 1) # GeoJSON is (lon, lat); OSMFeature is (lat, lon), as Overpass gives it. self.assertEqual(feats[0].geometry, [(0.0, 0.0), (0.001, 0.001)]) self.assertEqual(feats[0].tags, {"highway": "residential"}) self.assertEqual(feats[0].kind, "way") def test_an_area_is_a_closed_way(self): feats = sketch.features(collection(drawn("house", "Polygon", SQUARE))) self.assertEqual(feats[0].geometry[0], feats[0].geometry[-1]) self.assertEqual(classify(feats[0].tags, area=True), "building") def test_an_unclosed_ring_is_closed(self): feats = sketch.features(collection( drawn("water", "Polygon", [SQUARE[0][:-1]]))) self.assertEqual(feats[0].geometry[0], feats[0].geometry[-1]) def test_ids_are_negative_and_do_not_repeat(self): feats = sketch.features(collection( drawn("residential", "LineString", LINE), drawn("water", "Polygon", SQUARE), drawn("tree", "Point", [0.0, 0.0]))) ids = [f.osm_id for f in feats] self.assertTrue(all(i < 0 for i in ids), ids) self.assertEqual(len(set(ids)), len(ids)) def test_a_point_is_a_node(self): feats = sketch.features(collection(drawn("tree", "Point", [1.5, 2.5]))) self.assertEqual(feats[0].kind, "node") self.assertEqual(feats[0].geometry, [(2.5, 1.5)]) def test_rubbish_is_left_out_rather_than_guessed_at(self): # None of these can be drawn through the window, but a hand-edited # file or an older release's save can hold them. self.assertEqual(sketch.features(None), []) self.assertEqual(sketch.features(collection()), []) for bad in (drawn("not_a_kind", "LineString", LINE), drawn("residential", "LineString", [[0.0, 0.0]]), drawn("water", "Polygon", [[[0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]]]), drawn("residential", "Circle", LINE), {"type": "Feature", "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": LINE}}): with self.subTest(bad=bad): self.assertEqual(sketch.features(collection(bad)), []) def test_only_the_listed_extra_tags_are_taken(self): # The tags reach classify and the renderer, so a page cannot be allowed # to set whatever it likes on a feature. feats = sketch.features(collection(drawn( "house", "Polygon", SQUARE, tags={"building:levels": 3, "name": "The Arms", "amenity": "bar"}))) self.assertEqual(feats[0].tags["building:levels"], "3") self.assertEqual(feats[0].tags["name"], "The Arms") self.assertNotIn("amenity", feats[0].tags) def test_a_drawn_street_is_the_same_feature_as_a_surveyed_one(self): # The whole point: nothing downstream can tell them apart. from generator.osm import OSMFeature surveyed = OSMFeature(12345, "way", {"highway": "residential"}, [(0.0, 0.0), (0.001, 0.001)]) made = sketch.features(collection(drawn("residential", "LineString", LINE)))[0] self.assertEqual(classify(made.tags), classify(surveyed.tags)) self.assertEqual(made.geometry, surveyed.geometry) self.assertEqual(made.kind, surveyed.kind)

nodes.name: test_split_large_buildings.py
nodes.body_text: """Buildings past settings.max_size are split, not dropped (knoxbuild.build). Run from the KnoxMap folder: python -m unittest discover tests No network, no files: one polygon placed straight into an empty grid. The gate in footprint.place refuses a building whose long side is over max_size - measured on the real polygon, before anything is claimed. build.py answers "large" by placing it again without that gate and passing max_side down to row_units, so every unit comes out inside the cap the gate used to enforce. The factory and the hangar are the landmarks a place is known by; dropping them left a hole in the map. """ import os import sys import unittest sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) import numpy as np # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild.build import row_units # noqa: E402 from knoxbuild.footprint import place # noqa: E402 # 500 x 80 tiles: well over the 200-tile gate on its long side. RECT = [(10.0, 10.0), (510.0, 10.0), (510.0, 90.0), (10.0, 90.0), (10.0, 10.0)] GRID = np.zeros((600, 600), dtype=bool) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: placed
nodes.body_text: def placed(max_side: float): return place(list(RECT), GRID.copy(), max_side=max_side)

nodes.name: Gate

nodes.name: Split
nodes.body_text: class Split(unittest.TestCase): def test_cut_units_fit_inside_the_cap(self): fp, reason = placed(1e9) self.assertIsNotNone(fp, reason) # At a quarter-metre tiles the area rule (BIG_BUILDING_M2, 6000 m2 # = 95481 tiles squared here) stops before 200, so without the cap # this footprint is passed through whole - only the cap splits it. # "industrial" is not a row kind, so this is the plain _cut_big path. units = row_units(fp, "industrial", "industrial", 0, 0.25, max_side=200) self.assertGreater(len(units), 1) self.assertTrue(all(max(u.width, u.height) <= 200 for u in units), [(u.width, u.height) for u in units]) def test_the_cuts_keep_every_tile(self): fp, _ = placed(1e9) units = row_units(fp, "industrial", "industrial", 0, 0.25, max_side=200) self.assertEqual(sum(u.tiles for u in units), fp.tiles) def test_without_the_cap_the_area_rule_is_unchanged(self): fp, _ = placed(1e9) units = row_units(fp, "industrial", "industrial", 0, 0.25) self.assertEqual([(u.width, u.height) for u in units], [(500, 80)]) def test_a_building_that_already_fits_is_cut_exactly_as_before(self): small = [(10.0, 10.0), (160.0, 10.0), (160.0, 60.0), (10.0, 60.0), (10.0, 10.0)] fp, reason = place(list(small), GRID.copy(), max_side=200) self.assertIsNotNone(fp, reason) plain = row_units(fp, "industrial", "industrial", 0, 1.0) capped = row_units(fp, "industrial", "industrial", 0, 1.0, max_side=200) self.assertEqual( [(u.x0, u.y0, u.width, u.height, u.tiles) for u in plain], [(u.x0, u.y0, u.width, u.height, u.tiles) for u in capped])

nodes.body_text: """No door opens onto the steps of a flight of stairs: those squares cannot be walked across, so the door and the rooms behind it are cut off.""" import os import sys import unittest from knoxbuild.layout import build_building sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname( os.path.abspath(__file__))), "tools")) from audit_layouts import audit # noqa: E402 BAD = "door opening onto the stairs" if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: class DoorsClearOfStairs(unittest.TestCase): def check(self, w, h, levels, seed, kind): b = build_building(w, h, levels=levels, seed=seed, kind=kind, commercial=kind not in (None, "apartment")) found = audit(b, kind) self.assertFalse(found.get(BAD), (kind, w, h, levels, seed)) self.assertFalse(found.get("room with no way in"), (kind, seed)) def test_cases_that_failed(self): self.check(21, 37, 2, 60, "apartment") self.check(36, 39, 5, 98, "apartment") self.check(28, 28, 8, 44, "civic") def test_houses_and_flats(self): for seed in range(40): self.check(12 + seed % 20, 14 + seed % 17, 2 + seed % 3, seed, "apartment" if seed % 2 else None)

Each of these came from somebody building maps, so what is worth checking is the thing they asked for rather than the mechanism: that a scale between the whole metres is really kept, that a skyline asked for is the skyline built, that the woods can differ from the trees in the gardens, and that one kind of place cannot take a whole list of landmarks. """ import collections import random import unittest import app as knoxapp from generator import places from knoxbuild.build import building_levels from knoxbuild.settings import HEIGHT_MIX_OPTIONS, LIMITS, Settings if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: class ScalesBetweenWholeMetres(unittest.TestCase): """1 m a tile is a town at full size and 2 m is everything in it half that; the steps in between are where a map is actually tuned.""" def test_a_quarter_metre_is_kept_as_it_was_typed(self): for asked in (1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.25, 3.5): with self.subTest(asked=asked): self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(asked), asked) def test_anything_finer_is_rounded_to_the_nearest_quarter(self): self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(1.37), 1.25) self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(1.4), 1.5) self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(1.0137), 1.0) def test_the_half_metre_is_still_the_finest_there_is(self): for asked in (0.5, 0.4, 0.1, 0.0, -3): with self.subTest(asked=asked): self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(asked), knoxapp.MIN_METERS_PER_TILE) def test_a_scale_past_the_end_is_the_end(self): self.assertEqual(knoxapp.tidy_scale(900), knoxapp.MAX_METERS_PER_TILE)

nodes.body_text: class TheSkylineAsked(unittest.TestCase): """A height mix shapes the buildings OpenStreetMap says nothing about.""" def heights(self, mix, kind=None, area=400, n=2000, **settings): base = {"preset": "city", "height_mix": mix, **settings} rng = random.Random(7) return [building_levels({}, kind, area, rng, Settings.from_dict(base), 1.0)[0] for _ in range(n)] def test_what_the_mapper_counted_is_never_overruled(self): # The whole point of the setting is that it fills in a blank. A tower # somebody counted the floors of stays the height they counted. for mix in HEIGHT_MIX_OPTIONS: with self.subTest(mix=mix): rng = random.Random(1) levels, from_osm = building_levels( {"building:levels": "9"}, "apartment", 400, rng, Settings.from_dict({"preset": "city", "height_mix": mix, "max_levels": 30}), 1.0) self.assertEqual((levels, from_osm), (9, True)) def test_low_builds_lower_than_the_place_is_and_tall_builds_higher(self): low = self.heights("low") auto = self.heights("auto") tall = self.heights("tall") self.assertLess(sum(low) / len(low), sum(auto) / len(auto)) self.assertGreater(sum(tall) / len(tall), sum(auto) / len(auto)) def test_middle_gathers_in_the_middle_rather_than_spreading(self): # It used to average two draws, which rounds the halves of a pool of # 2, 3 and 4 outwards and came out wider than the guess it gathers. middle = collections.Counter(self.heights("middle")) auto = collections.Counter(self.heights("auto")) self.assertGreater(middle.most_common(1)[0][1], auto.most_common(1)[0][1]) def test_even_really_is_every_height_up_to_the_tallest(self): seen = set(self.heights("even", max_levels=8)) self.assertEqual(seen, set(range(1, 9))) def test_as_the_place_is_leaves_the_generator_alone(self): # The default has to be what the generator did before there was a # setting, or every map ever made changes under its mapper. self.assertEqual(Settings().height_mix, "auto") rng = random.Random(3) settings = Settings() was = [building_levels({}, "civic", 900, rng, settings, 1.0)[0] for _ in range(50)] rng = random.Random(3) now = [building_levels({}, "civic", 900, rng, Settings.from_dict({"height_mix": "auto"}), 1.0)[0] for _ in range(50)] self.assertEqual(was, now) def test_a_mix_the_window_does_not_offer_is_refused(self): self.assertEqual(Settings.from_dict({"height_mix": "enormous"}).height_mix, "auto") def test_the_window_is_offered_every_mix_the_generator_knows(self): offered = {value for value, _label in knoxapp.app.test_client().get("/api/settings") .get_json()["options"]["height_mix"]} self.assertEqual(offered, set(HEIGHT_MIX_OPTIONS))

nodes.body_text: class LandmarksNobodyKindTakesOver(unittest.TestCase): """A town of forty churches used to spend a quarter of its list on them.""" def town(self, **counts): rows = [] for value, (key, n) in counts.items(): for i in range(n): rows.append({"name": f"{value} {i}", "kind": key, "value": value, "lat": 0.0, "lon": 0.0, "_rank": places._notability(key, value, {})}) rows.sort(key=lambda d: (-d["_rank"], d["value"], d["name"].lower())) return rows def setUp(self): self.rows = self.town(place_of_worship=("amenity", 400), supermarket=("shop", 40), theatre=("amenity", 5), museum=("tourism", 3), graveyard=("amenity", 1)) def test_the_one_theatre_and_the_one_graveyard_are_in_the_list(self): kept = {d["value"] for d in places._share_out(self.rows, 100)} self.assertEqual(kept, {"place_of_worship", "supermarket", "theatre", "museum", "graveyard"}) def test_no_kind_takes_more_than_its_share_while_others_wait(self): kept = collections.Counter(d["value"] for d in places._share_out(self.rows, 100)) share = max(places.VALUE_MIN, int(100 * places.VALUE_SHARE)) # The churches only pass their share once everything else is in. self.assertGreater(kept["place_of_worship"], share) self.assertEqual(kept["supermarket"], share) def test_the_list_is_still_filled_to_the_limit(self): for limit in (10, 50, 100, 300): with self.subTest(limit=limit): self.assertEqual(len(places._share_out(self.rows, limit)), limit) def test_a_place_that_really_is_all_churches_still_gets_a_full_list(self): only = self.town(place_of_worship=("amenity", 200)) self.assertEqual(len(places._share_out(only, 100)), 100) def test_a_short_list_is_left_exactly_as_it_was_ranked(self): self.assertEqual(places._share_out(self.rows[:20], 100), self.rows[:20]) def test_more_landmarks_are_listed_than_the_old_three_hundred(self): self.assertGreater(places.LANDMARK_LIMIT, 300)

nodes.body_text: class TerrainTests(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.rs = parse_rules(RULES) self.land, self.veg = pictures() def run_layers(self, seed=1, land=None, veg=None, x0=0, y0=0): pal = Palette() layers = ground_layers(self.land if land is None else land, self.veg if veg is None else veg, self.rs, pal, seed, x0, y0) return {k: np.array(pal.names, dtype=object)[v] for k, v in layers.items()} def test_tiles_come_from_the_rules_and_only_where_the_colour_is(self): out = self.run_layers() floor, vegetation = out["0_Floor"], out["0_Vegetation"] self.assertTrue(all(t == "" for t in floor[:, :5].ravel())) self.assertTrue(set(floor[:, 5:].ravel()) <= {"g_0", "g_1", "g_2", "g_3"}) self.assertTrue(all(t == "" for t in vegetation[:10].ravel())) self.assertTrue(set(vegetation[10:20, 10:20].ravel()) <= {"tree_a", "tree_b", "g_0", "g_1", "g_2", "g_3"}) # an alias entry is one entry in three, so a third of the picks, split four ways share = np.mean(np.isin(vegetation[10:20, 10:20], ["g_0", "g_1", "g_2", "g_3"])) self.assertTrue(0.15 < share < 0.5, share) def test_same_seed_same_tiles_and_another_seed_other_tiles(self): a, b, c = self.run_layers(1), self.run_layers(1), self.run_layers(2) self.assertTrue((a["0_Floor"] == b["0_Floor"]).all()) self.assertFalse((a["0_Floor"] == c["0_Floor"]).all()) def test_a_cut_out_window_gets_the_tiles_the_whole_picture_got(self): whole = self.run_layers() part = self.run_layers(land=self.land[8:30, 12:40], veg=self.veg[8:30, 12:40], x0=12, y0=8) self.assertTrue((whole["0_Floor"][8:30, 12:40] == part["0_Floor"]).all()) self.assertTrue((whole["0_Vegetation"][8:30, 12:40] == part["0_Vegetation"]).all()) def test_stack_order(self): self.assertEqual(stack_order({"0_Vegetation", "0_Floor", "0_Zed", "0_Curbs"}), ["0_Floor", "0_Curbs", "0_Vegetation", "0_Zed"])

nodes.name: CellSourceTests
nodes.body_text: class CellSourceTests(unittest.TestCase): def words(self, data, names): """The square records of a one-level source, skipping the header.""" o = 4 + 5 * 4 + 4 for n in names: o += 2 + len(n.encode()) o += 4 + 4 + 1 # no rooms, no buildings, no zombie bytes return np.frombuffer(data[o:], dtype="<u4") def test_header_and_every_square_is_covered(self): a = np.zeros((SIDE, SIDE), np.int64) a[0, :3] = [1, 2, 1] b = np.zeros((SIDE, SIDE), np.int64) b[0, 1] = 2 data = cell_source(83, 2, ["t_a", "t_b"], [[a, b]]) self.assertEqual(data[:4], b"KCEL") self.assertEqual(struct.unpack_from("<5I", data, 4), (1, 83, 2, 0, 1)) w = self.words(data, ["t_a", "t_b"]) # square (0,0): 2 values + room, tile 0 ; (1,0): tiles 1 and 1 ; (2,0): tile 0 ; then empties self.assertEqual(list(w[:3]), [2, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0]) self.assertEqual(list(w[3:7]), [3, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, 1]) self.assertEqual(list(w[7:10]), [2, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0]) self.assertEqual(list(w[10:12]), [0xFFFFFFFF, SIDE * SIDE - 3]) self.assertEqual(len(w), 12) def test_empty_level_is_one_run(self): data = cell_source(0, 0, [], [[np.zeros((SIDE, SIDE), np.int64)]]) w = self.words(data, []) self.assertEqual(list(w), [0xFFFFFFFF, SIDE * SIDE])

x0, y1 - y0) + 1, layout.MIN_ROOM) def test_open_footprint(self): for seed in range(20): core = tower.pick_core(30, 30, None, random.Random(seed)) self.assertIsNotNone(core) self.assertTrue(2 <= len(core.lifts) <= 4) self.check(core, 30, 30) x0, y0, x1, y1 = core.stair self.assertLessEqual(abs((x0 + x1 + 1) / 2 - nodes.name: door_links
nodes.body_text: def door_links(plan): links = {} for x, y, d in plan.doors: a = layout._room_at(plan, x, y) b = layout._room_at(plan, x - 1, y) if d == "W" else layout._room_at(plan, x, y - 1) links.setdefault(a, set()).add(b) links.setdefault(b, set()).add(a) return links

nodes.name: lift_lobby
nodes.body_text: def lift_lobby(plan, links): """Circulation rooms reached from the stair hall through doors.""" core = next(i for i, r in enumerate(plan.rooms, 1) if r.is_core) seen, stack = {core}, [core] while stack: for n in links.get(stack.pop(), ()): if n and n not in seen and plan.rooms[n - 1].kind in ("hall", "lobby"): seen.add(n) stack.append(n) return seen

nodes.body_text: class BuildBuildingTower(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_31_storey_tower_builds(self): b = layout.build_building(30, 40, levels=31, kind="civic", seed=3) self.assertEqual(len(b.storeys), 31) first = lift_rects(b.storeys[0]) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(first), 2) for s in b.storeys: self.assertEqual(lift_rects(s), first) self.assertEqual(sorted((x, y, d) for _, (x, y, d) in s.shafts), sorted((x, y, d) for _, (x, y, d) in b.storeys[0].shafts)) self.assertNotIn("office", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[tower.plant_level(31)].rooms}) self.assertIn("office", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[5].rooms}) self.assertNotIn("retail", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms}) self.assertIn("lobby", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms}) def test_every_room_of_every_storey_is_reachable(self): b = layout.build_building(30, 40, levels=14, kind="civic", seed=3) for lvl, s in enumerate(b.storeys): links = door_links(s) start = next(i for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1) if r.is_core) seen, stack = {start}, [start] while stack: for n in links.get(stack.pop(), ()): if n and n not in seen: seen.add(n) stack.append(n) for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1): if not r.is_shaft: self.assertIn(i, seen, (lvl, i, r.kind)) def test_setback_keeps_core_inside_upper_floors(self): # 20x14 seed 2014 is the footprint whose step cut through the toilet. for w, h, seed in ((30, 40, 3), (20, 14, 2014)): with self.subTest(w=w, h=h, seed=seed): b = layout.build_building(w, h, levels=12, kind="civic", seed=seed) t = tower.pick_core(w, h, None, random.Random(seed ^ 0x70E2)) self.assertIsNotNone(t) upper = b.storeys[-1] cores = [r for r in upper.rooms if r.is_core] service = [r for r, _ in t.service] if upper.mask is None: continue # no step at all keeps the core whole too for rect in (lift_rects(upper) + service + [(c.x0, c.y0, c.x1, c.y1) for c in cores]): for x, y in cells(rect): self.assertTrue(upper.mask[y][x], (rect, x, y)) for rect, kind in t.service: self.assertTrue(any((r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1) == rect and r.kind == kind for r in upper.rooms), (rect, kind)) b = layout.build_building(30, 40, levels=12, kind="civic", seed=3) self.assertIsNotNone(b.storeys[-1].mask) def test_a_footprint_with_no_room_for_a_core_falls_back(self): mask = [[not (x >= 8 and y < 12) for x in range(20)] for y in range(20)] self.assertIsNone(tower.pick_core(20, 20, mask, random.Random(1 ^ 0x70E2))) # The ordinary path: no storey is cut as a tower, and one lift. (The # ordinary civic mix has lobbies of its own, so the kind proves nothing.) with mock.patch.object(layout.assemble, "_tower_rooms", side_effect=AssertionError("tower path ran")): b = layout.build_building(20, 20, levels=14, kind="civic", seed=1, mask=mask) self.assertEqual(len(b.storeys), 14) for s in b.storeys: self.assertEqual(len(s.shafts), 1)

nodes.body_text: class SummerStreetStandIn(unittest.TestCase): """A tower at the 31-storey cap on a stand-in for the 100 Summer Street footprint (32 storeys in life; Build 42 has room for 31 and the roof).""" def test_summer_street_footprint_builds_31_storeys(self): w, h = SUMMER_STREET_STAND_IN b = layout.build_building(w, h, levels=31, kind="civic", seed=3) self.assertEqual(len(b.storeys), 31) first = lift_rects(b.storeys[0]) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(first), 2) for s in b.storeys: self.assertEqual(lift_rects(s), first) self.assertNotIn("office", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[tower.plant_level(31)].rooms}) self.assertIn("lobby", {r.kind for r in b.storeys[0].rooms}) def test_it_serialises_to_a_tbx(self): from knoxbuild.buildtiles import parse_tbx from knoxbuild.tbx import render_tbx w, h = SUMMER_STREET_STAND_IN b = layout.build_building(w, h, levels=31, kind="civic", seed=3) # 31 storeys plus the roof floor render_tbx always adds: all 32 levels self.assertEqual(len(parse_tbx(render_tbx(b, "summer_street")).floors), 32)

The pieces come from the game's own tiles (tools/game_pieces.py).""" import random import unittest from collections import Counter from knoxbuild import catalog as C from knoxbuild import interiors as I from knoxbuild import layout as L if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.body_text: def trade_room(kind, use, seed, w=18, h=13): b = L.build_building(w, h, kind="shop", seed=seed, levels=1, street="S", uses=[(use, "storage")]) s = b.storeys[0] idx = next((i for i, r in enumerate(s.rooms, 1) if r.kind == use), None) roles = Counter(f[0] for f in s.furniture if idx and 0 <= f[2] < s.height and 0 <= f[1] < s.width and s.grid[f[2]][f[1]] == idx) return s, idx, roles

nodes.name: GymIsLaidOutInRows
nodes.body_text: class GymIsLaidOutInRows(unittest.TestCase): """A gym floor is rows: treadmills shoulder to shoulder facing the mirrors, the weights behind them on evenly spaced lines. They used to be scattered - a treadmill every other tile, and three weight machines at odd angles in a whole room - which reads as machinery stood about at random.""" def gym(self, w=18, h=12, seed=0): room = L.Room(0, 0, w, h, kind="gym") room.x0, room.x1, room.y0, room.y1 = 0, w - 1, 0, h - 1 plan = L.Plan(w, h, rooms=[room], grid=[[1] * w for _ in range(h)], doors=[(0, h // 2, "W")], kind="gym") got = I.furnish_gym(plan, 1, room, random.Random(seed), set(), set(), None) self.assertIsNotNone(got) pieces = [(r, x, y, o) for r, x, y, o in plan.furniture if r in ("treadmill", "weight_machine", "weight_machine_alt")] return pieces def test_treadmills_stand_shoulder_to_shoulder_in_one_row(self): for seed in range(4): pieces = self.gym(seed=seed) treads = [(x, y) for r, x, y, _ in pieces if r == "treadmill"] self.assertGreaterEqual(len(treads), 6, f"seed {seed}: {treads}") depths = {y for _, y in treads} self.assertEqual(len(depths), 1, f"seed {seed}: treadmills at {treads}") along = sorted(x for x, _ in treads) self.assertEqual(along[-1] - along[0] + 1, len(along), f"seed {seed}: gaps in the treadmill row {along}") def test_weight_machines_line_up_in_even_rows(self): for seed in range(4): pieces = self.gym(seed=seed) weights = [(x, y, o) for r, x, y, o in pieces if r.startswith("weight")] self.assertGreaterEqual(len(weights), 6, f"seed {seed}: {weights}") rows = {} for x, y, o in weights: rows.setdefault(y, []).append((x, o)) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(rows), 2, f"seed {seed}: one row only {weights}") lines = [] for y, members in rows.items(): self.assertEqual(len({o for _, o in members}), 1, f"seed {seed}: a row faces two ways {members}") xs = sorted(x for x, _ in members) gaps = {b - a for a, b in zip(xs, xs[1:])} self.assertEqual(len(gaps), 1, f"seed {seed}: uneven row {xs}") lines.append(xs) self.assertEqual(len({tuple(l) for l in lines}), 1, f"seed {seed}: rows out of line with each other {lines}")

nodes.name: test_untrusted_input.py
nodes.body_text: """What the window posts, and what is on disk beside a map, is untrusted. Five places read it: the zones drawn on a map, the sheet a map was drawn on, the drawn features themselves, the changes made to the real ones, and a hand-built building. Each is a cleaner whose whole job is to leave out what it cannot use - and each threw a Python error instead when the shape of what it was given was wrong rather than its contents: a number where a list was expected came back as "'int' object is not iterable", and the window showed a 500 with a traceback behind it. A file edited by hand, a save from an older KnoxMap and a page that posts badly are all this - and so is "NaN", which float() takes and nothing after it does. """ import unittest from generator import edits, sketch from knoxbuild import designer, zones # The shapes that broke them: the wrong type at every level, and the numbers # that are not numbers. JUNK = [None, "", "x", [], {}, True, False, 0, -1, 1.5, float("nan"), float("inf"), "NaN", "inf", [[1, 2]], [[1]], [[None]], [[1, 2], [3]], {"a": 1}, [1, 2, 3], 10 ** 12] if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: every
nodes.body_text: def every(raw_for): """The same junk in every slot of whatever that cleaner takes.""" out = [] for i, value in enumerate(JUNK): out.extend(raw_for(value, JUNK[(i + 7) % len(JUNK)])) return out

nodes.body_text: class NothingThrows(unittest.TestCase): def check(self, call, raws): for raw in raws: with self.subTest(raw=repr(raw)[:60]): call(raw) # the test is that this does not throw def test_the_zones_drawn_on_a_map(self): self.check(zones.clean, [None, "x", 5, {}, [1], [None]] + every( lambda a, b: [[{"ring": a, "settings": b}], [{"ring": [[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1]], "settings": a, "style": b, "presets": a}]])) def test_a_hand_built_building(self): self.check(designer.clean, [None, "x", 5, []] + every( lambda a, b: [{"width": a, "height": b, "storeys": a, "kind": b, "rooms": a, "name": b, "seed": a, "style": b}, {"rooms": [{"kind": a, "level": b, "x": a, "y": b, "w": a, "h": b}]}, {"rooms": [a]}])) def test_the_things_drawn_on_a_map(self): self.check(sketch.features, [None, "x", 5, {}] + every( lambda a, b: [{"features": a}, {"features": [{"properties": a, "geometry": b}]}, {"features": [{"properties": {"kind": "residential"}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": a}}]}, {"features": [{"properties": {"kind": "pond"}, "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": a}}]}, {"features": [{"properties": {"kind": "tree"}, "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": a}}]}])) def test_the_sheet_a_map_was_drawn_on(self): def both(raw): sketch.design_to_drawn(raw) sketch.design_bbox(raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {}) self.check(both, [None, "x", 5, []] + every( lambda a, b: [{"width_m": a, "height_m": b, "anchor": a, "features": b}, {"anchor": {"lat": a, "lon": b}, "features": [{"kind": "residential", "points": [[1, 2], [3, 4]]}]}, {"features": [{"kind": a, "points": b}]}])) def test_the_changes_made_to_the_real_features(self): self.check(edits.clean, [None, "x", 5, []] + every( lambda a, b: [{"removed": a, "moved": b, "tags": a}, {"moved": {"1": a}}, {"tags": {"1": a}}]))

nodes.body_text: class AndNothingIsInventedEither(unittest.TestCase): """Dropping what cannot be used is right; reading it as something else is not.""" def test_a_string_of_digits_is_not_a_list_of_ids(self): # "12" is a sequence, so it was read as the two features 1 and 2 and # both were taken off the map. self.assertEqual(edits.clean({"removed": "12"})["removed"], []) def test_a_sheet_measured_in_nan_is_not_a_sheet(self): south, west, north, east = sketch.design_bbox( {"width_m": "NaN", "height_m": float("nan")}) for value in (south, west, north, east): self.assertEqual(value, value) # not NaN self.assertGreater(north, south) self.assertGreater(east, west) def test_a_point_that_is_not_a_pair_of_numbers_is_left_out(self): drawn = {"features": [{"properties": {"kind": "residential"}, "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[0.0, 0.0], [None], [1.0, 1.0]]}}]} made = sketch.features(drawn) self.assertEqual([len(f.geometry) for f in made], [2])

nodes.name: test_updates_api.py
nodes.body_text: """The update routes: what they refuse, and what they must not start. `web/updates.py` is the one screen that can replace the running copy, so its refusals matter more than its successes: a bad version name, a copy that is a git checkout, a restart with nothing downloaded, a restart outside the window. Each is checked here without letting a download begin - `updater.check` and `updater.restart` are the only things that touch the network or the process, and both are stubbed. """ import unittest from unittest import mock import app as A if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: test_window_columns.py
nodes.body_text: """Windows upstairs stand above the windows downstairs. A block of flats repeats its floor plan, so its windows always lined up. A house does not: every storey is laid out room by room, the rooms upstairs are not the rooms downstairs, and the windows went wherever each floor's rooms wanted them. Looking up at a generated house from the street, 27 of every 100 upstairs windows stood above a window - which is what gives a town away, because a real facade is built in columns. Reported in #bug-reports by Zombaxx: "window alignment with the windows above not properly lining up". """ import unittest from knoxbuild.layout import build_building # Measured over the buildings below. Houses were at 0.27 before the floor # below's columns were taken first; the rest were already repeating their # plan and must not get worse. WANTED = {"house": 0.60, "apartment": 0.85, "civic": 0.85, "shop": 0.85} if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: lined_up
nodes.body_text: def lined_up(kind, levels=3, size=(24, 18), seeds=range(8)): """How much of each upper floor's glazing stands above the floor below.""" above = same = 0 for seed in seeds: built = build_building(size[0], size[1], levels=levels, seed=seed, kind=None if kind == "house" else kind, commercial=kind not in ("house", "apartment")) for level in range(1, len(built.storeys)): under = set(built.storeys[level - 1].windows) here = set(built.storeys[level].windows) above += len(here) same += len(here & under) return same / max(1, above), above

nodes.name: WindowsInColumns
nodes.body_text: class WindowsInColumns(unittest.TestCase): def test_most_of_an_upper_floor_sits_above_the_one_below(self): for kind, wanted in WANTED.items(): with self.subTest(kind=kind): share, counted = lined_up(kind) self.assertGreater(counted, 20, "nothing to measure") self.assertGreaterEqual( share, wanted, f"{kind}: only {share:.0%} of upstairs windows are above one") def test_a_tall_house_keeps_its_columns_all_the_way_up(self): share, _counted = lined_up("house", levels=5) self.assertGreaterEqual(share, 0.60) def test_the_windows_are_still_there_to_line_up(self): # Lining them up must not be done by having fewer of them: a house of # this size has windows on every storey. built = build_building(24, 18, levels=3, seed=3) for level, storey in enumerate(built.storeys): with self.subTest(level=level): self.assertGreater(len(storey.windows), 4)

nodes.name: test_windows_open.py
nodes.body_text: """A window on a house has to open. Project Zomboid marks most of each window sheet WindowLocked: those sprites can never be opened, only smashed, and once smashed never shut again. Five of the fourteen house styles were built with them, and a school, a surgery and a town hall too - so about a third of a town's houses had windows nobody could climb through or close behind them. A shop front and a factory's glazing keep theirs. Fixed panes are what those are in the game as well. """ import unittest from knoxbuild import catalog as C from knoxbuild.buildtiles import LOCKED_WINDOWS, window_locked # Buildings people live in or walk into. The ones left out are the shop # fronts (restaurant, shop), a works (industrial) and a barn. MUST_OPEN = {"civic", "medical", "school"} if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: west
nodes.body_text: def west(style): return (style.get("window") or {}).get("tiles", {}).get("West", "")

nodes.name: WindowsPeopleCanOpen
nodes.body_text: class WindowsPeopleCanOpen(unittest.TestCase): def test_every_house_style_has_windows_that_open(self): shut = [s["name"] for s in C.HOUSE_STYLES if window_locked(west(s))] self.assertEqual(shut, [], f"houses with windows that never open: {shut}") def test_so_does_every_building_people_walk_into(self): for kind in sorted(MUST_OPEN): with self.subTest(kind=kind): self.assertFalse(window_locked(west(C.SPECIAL_STYLES[kind])), west(C.SPECIAL_STYLES[kind])) for variant in C.SPECIAL_STYLE_VARIANTS.get(kind, ()): self.assertFalse(window_locked(west(variant)), west(variant)) def test_a_shop_front_is_still_a_fixed_pane(self): # Not every locked window is a mistake: a shop window is one sheet of # glass in the game too, and it is meant to be broken rather than # opened. self.assertTrue(window_locked(west(C.SPECIAL_STYLES["shop"]))) def test_the_rule_reads_a_sprite_number_the_way_the_game_does(self): self.assertTrue(window_locked("fixtures_windows_wood_008")) self.assertTrue(window_locked("fixtures_windows_wood_8")) self.assertFalse(window_locked("fixtures_windows_wood_018")) self.assertFalse(window_locked("fixtures_windows_church_014")) # A sheet nobody recorded, and anything that is not a window at all. self.assertFalse(window_locked("fixtures_windows_curtains_01_040")) self.assertFalse(window_locked("")) self.assertFalse(window_locked("walls_exterior_house_01_032")) def test_the_table_covers_the_sheets_the_styles_are_built_from(self): used = set() for style in list(C.HOUSE_STYLES) + list(C.SPECIAL_STYLES.values()): tile = west(style) if tile: used.add(tile.rsplit("_", 1)[0]) # church is the one sheet with nothing locked in it, so it is not in # the table; everything else a style uses has to be. self.assertTrue(used - set(LOCKED_WINDOWS) <= {"fixtures_windows_church"}, sorted(used - set(LOCKED_WINDOWS)))

nodes.body_text: class Groves(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_share_of_open_ground_is_wood(self): land, veg = _field() _paint_groves(veg, land, Proj(), 1.0) self.assertTrue(0.08 < _share(veg) < 0.22, _share(veg)) def test_density_scales_it_and_zero_is_none(self): shares = [] for d in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0): land, veg = _field() _paint_groves(veg, land, Proj(), d) shares.append(_share(veg)) self.assertEqual(shares[0], 0) self.assertEqual(shares, sorted(shares)) def test_nothing_on_roads_or_water(self): land, veg = _field(400) land.paste(C.MEDIUM_ASPHALT, (0, 0, 400, 400)) self.assertEqual(_paint_groves(veg, land, Proj(), 2.0), 0) self.assertEqual(_share(veg), 0) def test_grass_under_a_wood_is_dark(self): land, veg = _field() _paint_groves(veg, land, Proj(), 1.0) trees = np.array(veg).sum(axis=2) > 0 ground = np.array(land) self.assertTrue((ground[trees] == np.array(C.DARK_GRASS)).all())

nodes.body_text: """Works yards (knoxbuild/works.py): tarmac round a works, a drive to the road, a dumpster and clutter by the walls, grass beyond.""" import unittest from collections import deque import numpy as np from generator import pz_colors as C from knoxbuild.works import YARD_EDGE, yard_width from tests.test_yards import SIZE, _paint X, Y = 16, 20 # the works, SIZE x SIZE, door in its north wall DUMPSTER = {C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_S0, C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_S1, C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_E0, C.DUMPSTER_BLUE_E1, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S0, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_S1, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E0, C.DUMPSTER_ORANGE_E1} OBJECTS = DUMPSTER | {C.WORKS_PALLET, C.WORKS_BRICKS, C.WORKS_DRUM, C.WORKS_BARREL, C.WORKS_CRATE, C.WORKS_TIRES, C.LAMP_N, C.LAMP_S} if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()

nodes.name: _colours
nodes.body_text: def _colours(img): return {tuple(int(v) for v in px) for px in img.reshape(-1, 3)}

nodes.name: WorksYards
nodes.body_text: class WorksYards(unittest.TestCase): @classmethod def setUpClass(cls): works = [("industrial", X, Y)] # The yards on their own: the credit lettered in the ground # (knoxbuild/credit_ground.py) has its own tests, and would be land # beyond the yard that is not grass. from knoxbuild import credit_ground keep, credit_ground.LAYOUTS = credit_ground.LAYOUTS, [] try: cls.ground = _paint(50, 50, works) cls.veg = _paint(50, 50, works, veg=True) finally: credit_ground.LAYOUTS = keep cls.r = yard_width(SIZE, SIZE) def ring(self, x, y): return max(X - x, x - (X + SIZE - 1), Y - y, y - (Y + SIZE - 1), 0) def test_the_yard_is_tarmac_and_the_land_beyond_is_grass(self): for y in range(2, 50): for x in range(50): k = self.ring(x, y) if 1 <= k <= self.r: self.assertNotEqual(tuple(self.ground[y, x]), C.MEDIUM_GRASS, (x, y)) elif k > self.r + YARD_EDGE + 1 and abs(x - (X + 3)) > 3: # (the drive runs north to the pavement past the door) self.assertEqual(tuple(self.ground[y, x]), C.MEDIUM_GRASS, (x, y)) def test_a_drive_reaches_the_pavement(self): hard = ~np.all(self.ground == C.MEDIUM_GRASS, axis=2) start = (X + 3, Y - 1) seen, todo = {start}, deque([start]) while todo: x, y = todo.popleft() if y < 2: return for n in ((x + 1, y), (x - 1, y), (x, y + 1), (x, y - 1)): if 0 <= n[0] < 50 and 0 <= n[1] < 50 and n not in seen and hard[n[1], n[0]]: seen.add(n) todo.append(n) self.fail("no hard ground from the works' door to the pavement") def test_a_dumpster_and_clutter_stand_in_the_yard(self): got = _colours(self.veg) self.assertTrue(got & DUMPSTER) self.assertGreaterEqual(len(got & {C.WORKS_PALLET, C.WORKS_BRICKS, C.WORKS_DRUM, C.WORKS_BARREL, C.WORKS_CRATE, C.WORKS_TIRES}), 1) def test_nothing_stands_at_the_door(self): door = (X + 3, Y - 1) for x, y in [(door[0], door[1] - k) for k in range(3)] + [(door[0] - 1, door[1]), (door[0] + 1, door[1])]: self.assertNotIn(tuple(self.veg[y, x]), OBJECTS, (x, y)) def test_a_house_gets_no_works_yard(self): ground = _paint(50, 50, [("house", X, Y)]) self.assertEqual(tuple(ground[Y + SIZE + 4, X + 3]), C.MEDIUM_GRASS)

When Wine is not installed, subprocess.Popen raises FileNotFoundError inside the request thread and the page got "500 Internal Server Error" with nothing to read - which reads as KnoxMap falling over rather than "install Wine, or set PZWORLDED to a native build". nodes.body_text: class WorldedLaunch(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): self.client = A.app.test_client() self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() self.map_dir = Path(self.tmp.name) / "Tavacare" self.map_dir.mkdir() (self.map_dir / "Tavacare.pzw").write_text("<project/>", encoding="utf-8") def tearDown(self): self.tmp.cleanup() def test_a_worlded_that_cannot_start_is_a_refusal(self): with mock.patch.object(generation, "_map_dir", return_value=self.map_dir), \ mock.patch.object(generation, "_worlded_exe", return_value=Path("C:/nowhere/PZWorldEd.exe")), \ mock.patch.object(subprocess, "Popen", side_effect=FileNotFoundError(2, "No such file", "wine")): out = self.client.post("/api/worlded", json={"mapName": "Tavacare"}) self.assertEqual(out.status_code, 400, out.get_data(as_text=True)) self.assertIn("Could not start PZWorldEd", out.get_json()["error"]) def test_a_map_with_no_project_is_still_a_refusal(self): with mock.patch.object(generation, "_map_dir", return_value=self.map_dir), \ mock.patch.object(generation, "_worlded_exe", return_value=Path("C:/nowhere/PZWorldEd.exe")): (self.map_dir / "Tavacare.pzw").unlink() out = self.client.post("/api/worlded", json={"mapName": "Tavacare"}) self.assertEqual(out.status_code, 400, out.get_data(as_text=True)) self.assertIn("No .pzw", out.get_json()["error"])

nodes.body_text: def square(x, y, side=3, corners=8): """A building-sized outline with `corners` points.""" pts = [(x, y), (x + side, y), (x + side, y + side), (x, y + side)] while len(pts) < corners: (ax, ay), (bx, by) = pts[-1], pts[0] pts.append(((ax + bx) / 2, (ay + by) / 2)) return [pts]

nodes.body_text: class CellBudget(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_packed_city_cell_keeps_its_triangles_under_16_bits(self): # About 2,000 buildings and a few roads in one 256-tile cell, as a # city centre at 2 m a tile has: 16,000 points fit the old point # budget but triangulate to about 48,000 indices, past the 32767 the # game can address. features = [(square(x * 5, y * 5), [("building", "yes")]) for x in range(50) for y in range(40)] features += [(square(0, y * 20, side=250, corners=40), [("highway", "primary")]) for y in range(10)] kept = W._within_budget(features) self.assertTrue(kept) self.assertLessEqual(sum(W._indices(p, props) for p, props in kept), W.CELL_INDEX_BUDGET) self.assertLessEqual(sum(W._points(p) for p, _ in kept), W.CELL_POINT_BUDGET) self.assertLess(W.CELL_INDEX_BUDGET, 32767) def test_an_ordinary_cell_is_left_alone(self): features = [(square(x * 10, y * 10), [("building", "yes")]) for x in range(10) for y in range(10)] self.assertEqual(W._within_budget(features), features)

nodes.signature: def _paint(width, height, buildings, water=(), veg=False, tarmac=())
nodes.body_text: def _paint(width, height, buildings, water=(), veg=False, tarmac=()): """Lawn with a pavement along the top two rows; return the painted ground, or the vegetation layer when `veg`. `buildings` is (kind, tile_x, tile_y[, door]) per building, `water` (x, y) tiles.""" with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as out: os.mkdir(os.path.join(out, "buildings")) ground = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8) ground[:, :] = C.MEDIUM_GRASS ground[:2, :] = C.PALE_CONCRETE for x, y in water: ground[y, x] = C.WATER for x, y in tarmac: ground[y, x] = C.DARK_ASPHALT Image.fromarray(ground).save(os.path.join(out, "t.bmp"), format="BMP") Image.fromarray(np.zeros_like(ground)).save(os.path.join(out, "t_veg.bmp"), format="BMP") occupied = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=bool) rows = [] for n, (kind, x, y, *door) in enumerate(buildings): _building(os.path.join(out, "buildings"), f"b{n}.tbx", *door) occupied[y:y + SIZE, x:x + SIZE] = True rows.append({"file": f"b{n}.tbx", "kind": kind, "building": "yes", "tile_x": x, "tile_y": y, "width": SIZE, "height": SIZE}) paint_paths(out, "t", rows, occupied) return read_rgb(os.path.join(out, "t_veg.bmp" if veg else "t.bmp"))

nodes.body_text: class FrontPaths(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_block_of_flats_gets_a_path_to_the_pavement(self): ground = _paint(30, 30, [("apartment", 10, 10)]) # Straight out of the door at (13, 9) up to the pavement at row 1. for y in range(2, 10): self.assertTrue(_stone(ground, 13, y), f"no path at (13, {y})") def test_a_house_far_back_from_the_street_walks_to_its_drive(self): ground = _paint(30, 80, [("house", 10, 62)]) drive = np.all(ground == C.DARK_ASPHALT, axis=2) self.assertTrue(drive[2:62].any(axis=1).all(), "the drive does not reach the pavement") self.assertTrue(_stone(ground, 13, 61), "no path from the door") def test_a_house_with_a_drive_from_the_terrain_gets_no_second(self): # A drive the woods' clearing laid (generator/rendering/homesteads.py): # down the west side from the pavement, then in to the house's wall. laid = ([(x, y) for x in range(2, 5) for y in range(2, 66)] + [(x, y) for x in range(5, 10) for y in range(63, 66)]) ground = _paint(30, 80, [("house", 10, 62)], tarmac=laid) drive = np.all(ground == C.DARK_ASPHALT, axis=2) extra = drive.copy() for x, y in laid: extra[y, x] = False self.assertFalse(extra.any(), "a second drive was laid beside the first") self.assertTrue(_stone(ground, 13, 61), "no path from the door") def test_a_house_far_back_with_no_drive_still_gets_a_path(self): # A stream with one footbridge-wide gap: no straight drive gets across. stream = [(x, 30) for x in range(30) if x != 13] ground = _paint(30, 80, [("house", 10, 62)], water=stream) for y in range(2, 62): self.assertTrue(_stone(ground, 13, y), f"no path at (13, {y})") def test_a_path_goes_around_the_neighbours_back_yard(self): alone = _paint(40, 40, [("house", 10, 4)]) both = _paint(40, 40, [("house", 10, 4), ("house", 10, 24)]) # The house and the minimum yard every house gets (the yard behind it # starts at row 10); a deeper yard may extend further, but this part is # claimed whatever the depth chosen. yard = (slice(10, 10 + YARD_MIN_DEPTH), slice(8, 18)) self.assertTrue((alone[yard] == both[yard]).all(), "the second house's path was painted over the first one's yard")

nodes.body_text: class Cleaning(unittest.TestCase): def test_a_zone_cannot_set_what_decides_the_whole_map(self): # The seed, the scale and the rotation are what the map is; a zone # with its own would be a different map in the middle of this one. kept = zones.clean([{"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"seed": 7, "align_streets": 0, "rotate_degrees": 45, "max_levels": 9}}]) self.assertEqual(kept[0]["settings"], {"max_levels": 9.0}) def test_values_are_clamped_to_what_the_generator_accepts(self): lo, hi = LIMITS["max_levels"] kept = zones.clean([{"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": hi + 500}}, {"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": lo - 500}}]) self.assertEqual(kept[0]["settings"]["max_levels"], float(hi)) self.assertEqual(kept[1]["settings"]["max_levels"], float(lo)) def test_max_levels_ceiling_is_build_42(self): self.assertEqual(LIMITS["max_levels"], (1, 31)) def test_a_shape_that_is_not_a_shape_is_dropped(self): self.assertEqual(zones.clean([{"ring": [[0, 0], [1, 1]]}]), []) self.assertEqual(zones.clean([{"ring": "nonsense"}]), []) self.assertEqual(zones.clean(["rubbish", 7, None]), []) self.assertEqual(zones.clean(None), []) def test_unreadable_numbers_are_left_out_rather_than_guessed_at(self): kept = zones.clean([{"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": "tall", "spawn_density": float("nan"), "room_size": 20}}]) self.assertEqual(kept[0]["settings"], {"room_size": 20.0}) def test_a_pinned_wall_style_is_kept_as_a_name(self): kept = zones.clean([{"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "wall_style": " brick "}]) self.assertEqual(kept[0][zones.STYLE_KEY], "brick") bare = zones.clean([{"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "wall_style": 5}]) self.assertNotIn(zones.STYLE_KEY, bare[0])

nodes.body_text: class Asking(unittest.TestCase): def test_inside_the_zone_its_settings_answer(self): z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": 12}}) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(500, 500).max_levels, 12) def test_outside_it_the_map_answers_with_its_own_object(self): base = Settings() z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": 12}}, settings=base) # The same object, not a copy: a map with no zones must cost nothing. self.assertIs(z.settings_at(5000, 5000), base) def test_a_zone_leaves_the_settings_it_says_nothing_about_alone(self): base = Settings() z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": 12}}) inside = z.settings_at(500, 500) self.assertEqual(inside.max_levels, 12) self.assertEqual(inside.room_size, base.room_size) self.assertEqual(inside.seed, base.seed) def test_the_smallest_zone_wins_so_they_can_nest(self): z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 10, 10), "settings": {"max_levels": 3}}, {"ring": square(1, 1, 2, 2), "settings": {"max_levels": 9}}) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(1500, 1500).max_levels, 9) # inner self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(5000, 5000).max_levels, 3) # outer def test_an_int_setting_stays_an_int(self): # It is read straight into the generator, which indexes and ranges on # it; a float max_levels raises there rather than here. z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "settings": {"max_levels": 7}}) self.assertIsInstance(z.settings_at(500, 500).max_levels, int) def test_a_pinned_style_is_only_pinned_inside(self): z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 1, 1), "wall_style": "brick"}) self.assertEqual(z.style_at(500, 500), "brick") self.assertIsNone(z.style_at(5000, 5000)) def test_no_zones_is_the_map_everywhere(self): base = Settings() z = zoning(settings=base) self.assertEqual(len(z), 0) self.assertIs(z.settings_at(1, 1), base) self.assertIsNone(z.style_at(1, 1))

nodes.name: AcrossTheWholeMap
nodes.body_text: class AcrossTheWholeMap(unittest.TestCase): def test_the_chunk_grid_says_what_each_part_of_the_map_is_set_to(self): # The spawn map is drawn a chunk at a time, so the zones are painted # into that grid once rather than asked about chunk by chunk. # The projector above makes a degree a thousand tiles, so this zone # is tiles 0-100 of a grid 20 chunks of 10 tiles across: 200 tiles. base = Settings() z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 0.1, 0.1), "settings": {"spawn_density": 60}}, settings=base) grid = z.chunk_values(("spawn_density",), gw=20, gh=20, tiles_per_chunk=10)["spawn_density"] self.assertEqual(grid.shape, (20, 20)) self.assertEqual(grid[5, 5], 60.0) # inside self.assertEqual(grid[19, 19], float(base.spawn_density)) # outside def test_a_zone_inside_another_wins_on_the_grid_too(self): z = zoning({"ring": square(0, 0, 0.2, 0.2), "settings": {"spawn_density": 5}}, {"ring": square(0, 0, 0.05, 0.05), "settings": {"spawn_density": 60}}) grid = z.chunk_values(("spawn_density",), gw=30, gh=30, tiles_per_chunk=10)["spawn_density"] self.assertEqual(grid[2, 2], 60.0) # tiles 20-30: the small one self.assertEqual(grid[15, 15], 5.0) # tiles 150-160: the big one def test_with_no_zones_every_chunk_is_the_map(self): base = Settings() grid = zoning(settings=base).chunk_values( ("spawn_density",), gw=4, gh=4, tiles_per_chunk=10)["spawn_density"] self.assertTrue((grid == float(base.spawn_density)).all())

nodes.name: AZoneDrawnOverItself
nodes.body_text: class AZoneDrawnOverItself(unittest.TestCase): """An outline that crosses itself is still the ground it covers. Mending such an outline gives several polygons back instead of one, and one of those has no ring to paint, so painting the zones into the chunk grid threw 'MultiPolygon object has no attribute exterior'. """ # Two squares joined by the line between them: tiles 0-40 and 60-100. PINCHED = [[0, 0], [0.04, 0], [0.04, 0.04], [0, 0.04], [0, 0], [0.06, 0.06], [0.1, 0.06], [0.1, 0.1], [0.06, 0.1], [0.06, 0.06]] def zoning(self): return zoning({"ring": self.PINCHED, "settings": {"spawn_density": 60}}) def test_each_part_of_it_is_a_zone_of_its_own(self): z = self.zoning() self.assertEqual(len(z), 2) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(20, 20).spawn_density, 60) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(80, 80).spawn_density, 60) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(50, 50).spawn_density, Settings().spawn_density) def test_a_zone_inside_one_of_its_halves_still_wins(self): # Each half is smaller than the zone nested in it, and "the smallest # zone here wins" would hand the ground to the half that contains it. # What decides is the whole of a zone, however many pieces it is in. z = zoning({"ring": self.PINCHED, "settings": {"spawn_density": 5}}, {"ring": square(0.01, 0.01, 0.035, 0.035), "settings": {"spawn_density": 60}}) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(20, 20).spawn_density, 60) self.assertEqual(z.settings_at(5, 5).spawn_density, 5) grid = z.chunk_values(("spawn_density",), gw=20, gh=20, tiles_per_chunk=10)["spawn_density"] self.assertEqual(grid[2, 2], 60.0) # tiles 20-30: the nested one self.assertEqual(grid[0, 0], 5.0) # tiles 0-10: the big one def test_and_both_are_painted_into_the_chunk_grid(self): grid = self.zoning().chunk_values(("spawn_density",), gw=20, gh=20, tiles_per_chunk=10)["spawn_density"] self.assertEqual(grid[1, 1], 60.0) # tiles 10-20 self.assertEqual(grid[8, 8], 60.0) # tiles 80-90 self.assertEqual(grid[5, 5], float(Settings().spawn_density))
