nodes.name: split_name
nodes.signature: def split_name(entry: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None
nodes.body_text: def split_name(entry: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None: """'walls_exterior_house_01_32' -> ('walls_exterior_house_01', 32).""" m = re.match(r"^(.*)_(\d+)$", entry) if not m: return None return m.group(1), int(m.group(2))

nodes.name: read_tilesets_txt
nodes.signature: def read_tilesets_txt(path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int]], dict[str, str]]
nodes.body_text: def read_tilesets_txt(path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int]], dict[str, str]]: """(tileset name -> (columns, rows), tileset name -> pack file name). A "file =" line is either a bare sheet name or "<pack>/<sheet>". The pack half says where to look; a bare name has to be hunted for across all of them. """ sizes: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {} packs: dict[str, str] = {} name = None with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream: lines = stream.readlines() for raw in lines: s = raw.strip() if s.startswith("file = "): ref = s[7:] name = ref.split("/")[-1] if "/" in ref: packs[name] = ref.rsplit("/", 1)[0] elif s.startswith("size = ") and name: cols, rows = s[7:].split(",") sizes[name] = (int(cols), int(rows)) name = None return sizes, packs

nodes.name: extract_pack
nodes.signature: def extract_pack(pack_path: str, catalog: dict, wanted: set, out_dir: str, merge: bool = False) -> set
nodes.body_text: def extract_pack(pack_path: str, catalog: dict, wanted: set, out_dir: str, merge: bool = False) -> set: """Write every wanted sheet this pack holds. Returns the names written. With `merge`, a sheet already on disk is added to rather than replaced. """ os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True) # Pass 1, metadata only: which page does each tileset last appear on? # Extracting all 543 sheets at once would hold several GB of RGBA at peak, # so pass 2 writes each sheet out and frees it as soon as its last page has # been read. Skipping the PNG payloads makes this pass cheap. scout = PackReader(pack_path) last_page: dict[str, int] = {} for page_index, (_name, entries, read_png) in enumerate(scout.pages()): for ename, *_rest in entries: parsed = split_name(ename) if parsed and parsed[0] in wanted: last_page[parsed[0]] = page_index read_png() # keeps the stream aligned scout.f.close() reader = PackReader(pack_path) print(f"pack version {reader.version}, {reader.page_count} pages; " f"want {len(wanted)} tilesets, {len(last_page)} present in this pack") sheets: dict[str, Image.Image] = {} cell: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {} placed = 0 pages_decoded = 0 written = 0 def flush(tname: str) -> None: nonlocal written img = sheets.pop(tname, None) if img is None: return img.save(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{tname}.png")) img.close() written += 1 for page_index, (page_name, entries, read_png) in enumerate(reader.pages()): relevant = [] for ename, x, y, w, h, ox, oy, fx, fy in entries: parsed = split_name(ename) if parsed and parsed[0] in wanted: relevant.append((parsed[0], parsed[1], x, y, w, h, ox, oy, fx, fy)) png = read_png() if not relevant: continue pages_decoded += 1 with Image.open(io.BytesIO(png)) as page: page_img = page.convert("RGBA") for tname, idx, x, y, w, h, ox, oy, fx, fy in relevant: cols, rows = catalog[tname] if tname not in sheets: cell[tname] = (fx, fy) existing = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{tname}.png") if merge and os.path.exists(existing): with Image.open(existing) as old: sheets[tname] = old.convert("RGBA") else: sheets[tname] = Image.new("RGBA", (cols * fx, rows * fy), (0, 0, 0, 0)) cw, ch = cell[tname] col, row = idx % cols, idx // cols if row >= rows: continue crop = page_img.crop((x, y, x + w, y + h)) sheets[tname].paste(crop, (col * cw + ox, row * ch + oy)) placed += 1 page_img.close() # Anything whose last page this was is complete - write it and let go. for tname in [t for t, p in last_page.items() if p == page_index]: flush(tname) if pages_decoded % 25 == 0: print(f" page {page_index}: {pages_decoded} decoded, " f"{placed} tiles, {written} sheets written, " f"{len(sheets)} open") for tname in list(sheets): flush(tname) print(f"decoded {pages_decoded} pages, placed {placed} tiles, " f"wrote {written} sheets to {out_dir}") reader.f.close() return set(last_page)

nodes.name: flush
nodes.body_text: def flush(tname: str) -> None: nonlocal written img = sheets.pop(tname, None) if img is None: return img.save(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{tname}.png")) img.close() written += 1

nodes.name: main
nodes.body_text: def main(argv: list[str]) -> int: if len(argv) < 4: print(__doc__) return 2 packs_arg, tilesets_txt, out_dir = argv[1], argv[2], argv[3] wanted = set(argv[4:]) catalog, pack_of = read_tilesets_txt(tilesets_txt) if not wanted: wanted = set(catalog) unknown = sorted(wanted - set(catalog)) if unknown: print(f"not in Tilesets.txt, skipping: {unknown}") wanted -= set(unknown) if os.path.isdir(packs_arg): available = {os.path.basename(p): os.path.join(packs_arg, p) for p in os.listdir(packs_arg) if p.endswith(".pack")} else: available = {os.path.basename(packs_arg): packs_arg} # Group by the pack each sheet says it lives in. Anything unprefixed has to # be looked for everywhere, so it rides along with every pack. by_pack: dict[str, set] = {} floating = {n for n in wanted if n not in pack_of} for name in wanted - floating: pack = pack_of[name] if pack in available: by_pack.setdefault(pack, set()).add(name) else: print(f"pack not found for {name}: {pack}") for pack in available: if pack in by_pack or floating: by_pack.setdefault(pack, set()).update(floating) found: set = set() for pack in sorted(by_pack): names = by_pack[pack] - found if not names: continue print(f"== {pack}: looking for {len(names)} sheets ==") found |= extract_pack(available[pack], catalog, names, out_dir) # Build 42 moved the floor sheets (grass blends, kerbs, ceilings...) into # "<pack>.floor.pack" while Tilesets.txt still names the old pack. Some # sheets are split between the two: roofs_01 keeps its slopes in Tiles2x # but its flat tops (54, 55) went to the floor pack, so every flat roof # previewed as blank. The 2x floor packs are therefore merged into every # sheet; any other 2x pack is then searched for whatever is still missing. # 1x packs are skipped: their frames would make half-size sheets. for pack in sorted(p for p in available if "2x" in p.lower() and ".floor." in p): print(f"== {pack}: merging floor tiles into {len(wanted)} sheets ==") found |= extract_pack(available[pack], catalog, wanted, out_dir, merge=True) for pack in sorted(p for p in available if "2x" in p.lower() and ".floor." not in p): names = wanted - found if not names: break print(f"== {pack}: retrying {len(names)} missing sheets ==") found |= extract_pack(available[pack], catalog, names, out_dir) absent = sorted(wanted - found) if absent: print() print(f"no tiles in any pack for ({len(absent)}): {absent}") print(f"extracted {len(found)} of {len(wanted)} sheets") return 0

nodes.name: game_pieces.py
nodes.body_text: """Furniture roles read straight off the game's own tile definitions. python tools/game_pieces.py prints the block knoxbuild/catalog.py ends with BuildingEd's furniture file has no pews, pool tables, salon chairs, treadmills or coin laundry machines, so these come from media/newtiledefinitions.tiles.txt instead: each tile's Facing says which wall the piece stands against (the catalog key, FACING_TO_ORIENT) and its SpriteGridPos where it sits in a piece of several tiles. tools/make_catalog.py writes the same block. """ from __future__ import annotations import os import pprint import re # The catalog keys a piece by the wall it stands against; the game by the way # it faces, which is away from that wall. FACING_TO_ORIENT = {"S": "N", "E": "W", "N": "S", "W": "E"} # role: (sheet, tile numbers, layer). A role whose tiles do not cover all four # facings has only the walls they do, which layout.NORTH_WEST_ONLY picks up. GAME_PIECES = { # Churches: a pew of three seats, and the altar facing them. "pew": ("location_community_church_small_01", [48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61], "Furniture"), "altar": ("location_community_church_small_01", [40, 41, 42, 43], "Furniture"), # Bars: the counter, its stools, the bottle shelves behind it, a pool # table, a jukebox and an arcade cabinet. "bar_counter": ("location_restaurant_bar_01", [1, 3, 5, 7], "Furniture"), "bar_shelf": ("location_restaurant_bar_01", [30, 38], "Furniture"), "pool_table": ("recreational_01", [2, 3, 6, 7], "Furniture"), "jukebox": ("recreational_01", [0, 1], "Furniture"), "arcade": ("recreational_01", [20, 21, 22, 23], "Furniture"), # Laundromats. "coin_washer": ("appliances_laundry_01", [4, 5, 6, 7], "Furniture"), "coin_dryer": ("appliances_laundry_01", [12, 13, 14, 15], "Furniture"), # Hair salons: the chair and the hood dryer. "salon_chair": ("location_services_beauty_01", [0, 1, 2, 3], "Furniture"), "hair_dryer": ("location_services_beauty_01", [8, 9, 10, 11], "Furniture"), # Gyms: treadmills and weight machines, two tiles each. "treadmill": ("recreational_sports_01", [28, 29, 30, 31], "Furniture"), "weight_machine": ("recreational_sports_01", [40, 41, 42, 43], "Furniture"), "weight_machine_alt": ("recreational_sports_01", [44, 45, 46, 47], "Furniture"), # Children's rooms. "bunk_bed": ("furniture_bedding_01", [84, 85, 86, 87], "Furniture"), # A home's tables in its other woods (interiors.TONES): low tables the # height of the coffee table (Surface 15), and white and light oak dining # tables. "low_table_tan": ("furniture_tables_low_01", [16, 17], "Furniture"), "low_table_black": ("furniture_tables_low_01", [18, 19], "Furniture"), "low_table_white": ("furniture_tables_low_01", [20, 21], "Furniture"), "dining_table_white": ("furniture_tables_high_01", [44, 45, 46, 47], "Furniture"), "dining_table_oak": ("furniture_tables_high_01", [60, 61, 62, 63], "Furniture"), # The small things a home has (interiors.dress_room): a toaster and a # coffee maker on the worktop, a radio on a chest, a mirrored vanity in a # bedroom, a cot in a baby's room, and a small mirror over a basin and a # clock over a worktop on the north and west walls. "coffee_maker": ("appliances_cooking_01", [56, 57, 58, 59], "Furniture"), "toaster": ("appliances_cooking_01", [32, 33], "Furniture"), "radio": ("appliances_radio_01", [0, 1, 2, 3], "Furniture"), "vanity": ("furniture_storage_01", [40, 41, 42, 43], "Furniture"), "crib": ("furniture_bedding_01", [88, 89, 90, 91], "Furniture"), "mirror_small": ("walls_decoration_01", [10, 11], "WallFurniture"), "clock": ("walls_decoration_01", [104, 105], "WallFurniture"), # The rest of a home's and a shop's (interiors.dress_room): a telephone, # a coat rack by the door, cardboard boxes in a closet or a stockroom, a # laundry hamper, an air vent on the wall, a sale sign in a shop. "phone": ("location_business_office_generic_02", [0, 1, 2, 3], "Furniture"), "coat_rack": ("location_community_school_01", [36, 37, 38, 39], "Furniture"), "box": ("trashcontainers_01", [24, 25], "Furniture"), "box_battered": ("trashcontainers_01", [26, 27], "Furniture"), "hamper": ("appliances_laundry_01", [24, 25], "Furniture"), "wall_vent": ("rooftop_furniture", [34, 35], "WallFurniture"), "sale_sign": ("location_shop_generic_01", [70, 71], "Furniture"), } # A bar stool is round: the one sprite, whichever way. ROUND = {"bar_stool": ("location_restaurant_bar_01_26", "Furniture"), # A kitchen's or a bathroom's waste bin. "bin": ("trashcontainers_01_20", "Furniture")} # The door mat has no Facing in the game's definitions: its two halves are # laid out as the bath mat's are (floors_rugs_01 48-51), so it is set the same. FIXED = {"door_mat": ({"W": {"0,0": "floors_rugs_01_059", "0,1": "floors_rugs_01_058"}, "N": {"0,0": "floors_rugs_01_056", "1,0": "floors_rugs_01_057"}}, "FloorFurniture"), # A house plant in a floor pot: Ficus, Snake Plant, Dragon Tree and # Cast Iron Plant (vegetation_indoor_01, IsLow, not a tabletop # piece). A pot looks the same from every side, so the wall it # stands by picks the plant. It was d_plants_1_016, an outdoor # shrub with no pot, growing out of the floor. "plant": ({"W": {"0,0": "vegetation_indoor_01_012"}, "N": {"0,0": "vegetation_indoor_01_010"}, "E": {"0,0": "vegetation_indoor_01_009"}, "S": {"0,0": "vegetation_indoor_01_011"}}, "Furniture")} # Posters for a teenager's room: walls_decoration_05 0-7 face south (a north # wall) and 8-15 are the same posters facing east (a west wall). POSTERS = [(f"walls_decoration_05_{n:03d}", f"walls_decoration_05_{n + 8:03d}") for n in range(8)] if __name__ == "__main__": print(block())

nodes.name: tiledefs_path
nodes.body_text: def tiledefs_path() -> str: try: import knoxpaths media = knoxpaths.pz_media_dir() if media and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(str(media), "newtiledefinitions.tiles.txt")): return os.path.join(str(media), "newtiledefinitions.tiles.txt") game = knoxpaths.pz_install_dir() except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no game found: the default Steam folder game = None game = game or r"C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\ProjectZomboid" return os.path.join(str(game), "media", "newtiledefinitions.tiles.txt")

nodes.name: _props
nodes.body_text: def _props(txt: str) -> dict[str, dict]: out = {} for name, body in re.findall(r"// (\S+)\s*\n\s*tile\s*\{(.*?)\n\s*\}", txt, re.S): out[name] = dict(re.findall(r"^[ \t]*(\w+)[ \t]*=[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", body, re.M)) return out

nodes.name: build
nodes.signature: def build(path: str | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict]
nodes.body_text: def build(path: str | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict]: """(furniture, layers) for every role above.""" txt = open(path or tiledefs_path(), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() props = _props(txt) furniture: dict = {} layers: dict = {} for role, (sheet, numbers, layer) in GAME_PIECES.items(): piece: dict = {} for n in numbers: p = props.get(f"{sheet}_{n}") if not p or p.get("Facing") not in FACING_TO_ORIENT: raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: {sheet}_{n} has no Facing") orient = FACING_TO_ORIENT[p["Facing"]] at = (p.get("SpriteGridPos") or "0,0").replace(" ", "") piece.setdefault(orient, {}).setdefault(at, f"{sheet}_{n:03d}") furniture[role] = piece layers[role] = layer for role, (tile, layer) in ROUND.items(): furniture[role] = {o: {"0,0": tile} for o in ("W", "N", "E", "S")} layers[role] = layer for role, (piece, layer) in FIXED.items(): furniture[role] = piece layers[role] = layer for i, (north, west) in enumerate(POSTERS): furniture[f"poster_{i}"] = {"N": {"0,0": north}, "W": {"0,0": west}} layers[f"poster_{i}"] = "WallFurniture" return furniture, layers

")

nodes.name: large_compile_check.py
nodes.body_text: """Scale check for the Rust compiler: tile a real map's cell sources out to 51 x 48 cells and compile. python tools/large_compile_check.py <map folder> [--work DIR] [--cols 51] [--rows 48] [--threads 4] Makes the cell sources of a real KnoxMap map (tools/map_source.py), repeats them across the grid with new cell positions, compiles with knoxlots and reports time and the compiler's own peak memory (Windows only for the memory figure). Then runs `knoxlots verify` on the result. Needs about 4 GB of disk for 2,448 cells; the work folder is left in place so the lots can be inspected. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import json import shutil import struct import subprocess import sys import tempfile import time from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT)) if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())

nodes.name: peak_memory_mib
nodes.body_text: def peak_memory_mib(proc: subprocess.Popen) -> float | None: """Poll a running process until it exits; its peak working set in MiB (None off Windows).""" if sys.platform != "win32": proc.wait() return None import ctypes import ctypes.wintypes as wt class PMC(ctypes.Structure): _fields_ = [("cb", wt.DWORD), ("PageFaultCount", wt.DWORD), ("PeakWorkingSetSize", ctypes.c_size_t)] + \ [(n, ctypes.c_size_t) for n in ("WorkingSetSize", "QP", "QPP", "QNP", "QNPP", "Pagefile", "PeakPagefile")] handle = ctypes.windll.kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000 | 0x0400 | 0x0010, False, proc.pid) peak = 0 while proc.poll() is None: m = PMC() m.cb = ctypes.sizeof(m) if ctypes.windll.psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo(handle, ctypes.byref(m), m.cb): peak = max(peak, m.PeakWorkingSetSize) time.sleep(0.05) return round(peak / 2**20, 1)

nodes.name: main
nodes.body_text: def main() -> int: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("project") ap.add_argument("--work") ap.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=51) ap.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=48) ap.add_argument("--threads", type=int, default=4) a = ap.parse_args() from compile_map import knoxlots_exe # tools/ is on sys.path when run as a script exe = knoxlots_exe() if exe is None: sys.exit("knoxlots not found - cargo build --release in rust/knoxlots") from tools.map_source import make_map_source work = Path(a.work) if a.work else Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="knoxlots_scale_")) base, tiled, lots = work / "base_src", work / "tiled_src", work / "lots" for d in (base, tiled, lots): shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True) make_map_source(a.project, str(base), seams=True) cells = {tuple(map(int, c.stem.split("_")[1:])): c for c in base.glob("cell_*.kcell")} x0, y0 = min(x for x, _ in cells), min(y for _, y in cells) bw, bh = max(x for x, _ in cells) - x0 + 1, max(y for _, y in cells) - y0 + 1 tiled.mkdir() for f in base.iterdir(): if f.suffix.lower() in (".bmp", ".txt"): shutil.copy(f, tiled / f.name) made = 0 for gx in range(a.cols): for gy in range(a.rows): src = cells.get((x0 + gx % bw, y0 + gy % bh)) if src is None: continue b = bytearray(src.read_bytes()) b[8:16] = struct.pack("<II", x0 + gx, y0 + gy) # cell_x, cell_y follow the magic and version (tiled / f"cell_{x0 + gx}_{y0 + gy}.kcell").write_bytes(b) made += 1 t = time.time() p = subprocess.Popen([str(exe), "compile", str(tiled), str(lots), "--threads", str(a.threads)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True) peak = peak_memory_mib(p) out, err = p.communicate() seconds = round(time.time() - t, 1) verify = subprocess.run([str(exe), "verify", str(lots)], capture_output=True, text=True) res = {"exit_code": p.returncode, "seconds": seconds, "compiler_peak_working_set_mib": peak, "source_cells": made, "lotheaders": len(list(lots.glob("*.lotheader"))), "verify_exit_code": verify.returncode, "verify": verify.stdout.strip(), "stderr": err.strip()[-300:], "work": str(work)} print(json.dumps(res, indent=2)) return 0 if p.returncode == 0 and verify.returncode == 0 else 1

nodes.name: make_catalog.py
nodes.body_text: """Generate knoxbuild/catalog.py from the PZ mapping tools' own config files. Point this at the `config` folder of a PZ_Mapping_Tools install, so the tile names come from the same data BuildingEd itself loads: python tools/make_catalog.py ../PZMappingTools/config /tmp/catalog_gen.py This is a starting point, not a round trip. The committed `knoxbuild/catalog.py` was generated here once and then extended by hand - GAME_WALL_STYLES, the escalators, the interior wall sets and others are not in this script's output - so running it over the committed file would drop those sections. Write somewhere else and diff, never in place. Entries are selected by tile NAME, never by position. An earlier version indexed into BuildingTemplates.txt numerically, which silently pointed at the wrong entries when run against a different revision of the file - and picked `walls_interior_house_01_020`, which the Build 42 config does not contain at all. A missing anchor is now a hard error. """ from __future__ import annotations import collections import os import pprint import re import sys from pathlib import Path ERIKA_TILES_TXT = ("D:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/workshop/content/108600/3346506593/" "mods/Erikas Tiles/common/media/Erikas_Tiles.tiles.txt") # The object's Facing in a tile definition is the way it looks; the tbx orient # is the wall it stands against. A picture facing south hangs on a north wall. FACING_TO_ORIENT = {"S": "N", "E": "W", "N": "S", "W": "E"} # Shop fronts: Erika's glass shop walls, nine frame colours. Each design is a # block of four tiles - west pane, north pane, the corner, the south-east post - # starting at one of these. (The rest of each sheet is the same panes smashed # or with the glass out, frosted glass, and door frames: 4 and 5 hold a door # under a glass transom.) STOREFRONT_SHEETS = [f"walls_commercial_erika_{n:02d}" for n in range(1, 10)] STOREFRONT_DESIGNS = (24, 48, 64, 72, 96, 112) # The glass shop door (fixtures_doors_erika_01) nearest each frame colour: # black, maroon, grey, white, green, red, blue, rust, brown. DOOR_SHEET = "fixtures_doors_erika_01" STOREFRONT_DOORS = [116, 112, 116, 120, 124, 112, 116, 112, 112] # Shop signs, strips of tiles hung along a wall: (sheet, wall, tiles). Tiles # run east along a north wall and south along a west one, the order the # lettering needs. SHOP_SIGNS = [ ("signs_erika_01", "N", [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]), # Zac's Hardware ("signs_erika_01", "N", [5, 6, 7]), # Coin-op Laundromat ("signs_erika_01", "N", [10, 11, 12]), # Legal Services ("signs_erika_01", "N", [13, 14, 15]), # Discount Account ("signs_erika_01", "N", [16, 17, 18]), # Value Insurance ("signs_erika_01", "N", [24, 25, 26]), # Bail Bonds ("signs_erika_01", "N", [48, 49, 50]), # Evan Philips Tax & Accounting ("signs_erika_02", "N", [8, 9, 10, 11]), # Farming Supply ("signs_erika_02", "N", [20, 21, 22, 23]), # Dog Grooming ("signs_erika_01", "W", [58, 57, 56]), # Value Insurance ("signs_erika_02", "W", [19, 18, 17, 16]), # Dog Grooming ("signs_erika_02", "W", [27, 26, 25, 24]), # Sure Fitness ] # Where the extracted tile artwork is, once main() knows. A sheet often has # fewer pictures in it than its declared grid has cells, and the leftovers are # transparent: a tile named for one of those draws as a question mark in game # (CellLoader: missing tile) or as nothing at all. Every tile taken here is # checked against the artwork first. TILES_2X: str | None = None _SHEET_ALPHA: dict = {} # The committed catalog is not this generator's output any more: whole sections # (GAME_WALL_STYLES, the escalators) were added by hand and nothing here writes # them. Regenerating straight over it would drop them without a word - which is # the trap knoxbuild/catalog.py's own header warns about, and a warning in a # docstring nobody reads is not a guard. So the one path that would do it has to # be asked for out loud. COMMITTED = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "knoxbuild" / "catalog.py" if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

nodes.name: parse_tile_entries
nodes.body_text: def parse_tile_entries(path: str) -> list[dict]: txt = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() out = [] for m in re.finditer(r'TileEntry\s*\{(.*?)\n\}', txt, re.S): d = {} for line in m.group(1).strip().splitlines(): if "=" in line: k, v = line.split("=", 1) d[k.strip()] = v.strip() out.append(d) return out

nodes.name: parse_furniture
nodes.body_text: def parse_furniture(path: str) -> dict[str, list[dict]]: groups: dict[str, list[dict]] = {} g = fur = ent = None for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines(): s = raw.strip() if s == "group": g = {"label": None, "furniture": []} elif s.startswith("label = ") and g is not None and g["label"] is None: g["label"] = s[8:] groups[g["label"]] = g["furniture"] elif s == "furniture" and g is not None: fur = {"entries": [], "layer": "Furniture"} g["furniture"].append(fur) ent = None elif s.startswith("layer = ") and fur is not None and ent is None: fur["layer"] = s[8:] elif s == "entry" and fur is not None: ent = {"orient": None, "tiles": {}} fur["entries"].append(ent) elif s.startswith("orient = ") and ent is not None: ent["orient"] = s[9:] elif re.match(r"^\d+,\d+ = ", s) and ent is not None: k, v = s.split(" = ", 1) ent["tiles"][k] = v return groups

def parse_room_names(path: str) -> dict[str, str]: """internal name -> 'r g b', from the tools' RoomNames.txt.""" txt = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() out = {} for m in re.finditer(r'internal = (\S+)\s*
\s*label = [^
]*
\s*color = #([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})', txt): name, hexv = m.group(1), m.group(2) r, g, b = (int(hexv[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)) out[name] = f"{r} {g} {b}" return out

nodes.name: _tile_props
nodes.signature: def _tile_props(body: str) -> dict: # [ \t], not \s: a property with no value would swallow the next line.
nodes.body_text: def _tile_props(body: str) -> dict: # [ \t], not \s: a property with no value would swallow the next line. return dict(re.findall(r"^[ \t]*(\w+)[ \t]*=[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", body, re.M))

nodes.name: _blank
nodes.body_text: def _blank(tile: str) -> bool: """Whether `sheet_012` is an empty square in its sheet. False when the artwork is not on this PC, so the catalog still builds without the game.""" import re as _re if not TILES_2X: return False m = _re.fullmatch(r"(.+)_(\d+)", tile) if not m: return False sheet, idx = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)) if sheet not in _SHEET_ALPHA: _SHEET_ALPHA[sheet] = None try: import numpy as _np from PIL import Image as _Image path = os.path.join(TILES_2X, sheet + ".png") if os.path.exists(path): with _Image.open(path) as img: _SHEET_ALPHA[sheet] = _np.asarray(img.convert("RGBA"))[:, :, 3] except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - no PIL, no check pass alpha = _SHEET_ALPHA[sheet] if alpha is None: return False cols = max(1, alpha.shape[1] // 128) th = 256 r, c = divmod(idx, cols) cell = alpha[r * th:(r + 1) * th, c * 128:(c + 1) * 128] return cell.size == 0 or not cell.any()

nodes.name: erika_roles
nodes.signature: def erika_roles(furniture: dict, layers: dict) -> dict
nodes.body_text:
def erika_roles(furniture: dict, layers: dict) -> dict: """Pieces from Erika's Tiles, added to `furniture` as roles, by group: "art" (paintings, posters, mirrors), "plants", "shop_ads" (posters for shop walls), "vending" (drinks machines), "shelves" (bookcases), plus "storefronts" (exterior/interior wall entries of shop glass) and "signs" ({"N": [...], "W": [...]} strips of shop sign tiles). Empty when the mod's tile definitions are not on this PC.""" import os as _os path = _os.environ.get("ERIKAS_TILES_TXT") or ERIKA_TILES_TXT out: dict = {"art": [], "plants": [], "shop_ads": [], "vending": [], "shelves": [], "storefronts": [], "signs": {"N": [], "W": []}} if not _os.path.exists(path): return out txt = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() for block in re.split(r"
tileset\s*
", txt)[1:]: sheet = re.search(r"file\s*=\s*(\S+)", block).group(1) if sheet.startswith(("walls_decoration_paintings_erika", "walls_decoration_posters_erika", "walls_decoration_mirrors_erika")): group = "art" elif sheet.startswith("vegetation_indoor_erika"): group = "plants" elif sheet == "location_shop_accessories_erika_01": group = "shop" elif sheet == "furniture_shelving_erika_01": group = "shelves" else: continue pieces: dict[tuple, dict] = {} for idx, body in re.findall(r"// \S+_(\d+)\s*
\s*tile\s*\{(.*?)
\s*\}", block, re.S): props = _tile_props(body) n = int(idx) facing = props.get("Facing") if facing not in FACING_TO_ORIENT or "SpriteGridPos" in props: continue # multi-tile pieces are left out if group == "shelves" and not (n < 16 or 104 <= n < 128): continue # tall bookcases only kind = group if group == "shop": # Drinks machines come in blocks of four facings, the posters # that go with them in pairs for a north and a west wall. if "container" in props: kind = "vending" elif props.get("MoveType") == "WallObject": kind = "shop_ads" else: continue # standing signs if kind in ("vending", "shelves"): key = (kind, n // 4) elif kind == "shop_ads": key = (kind, n // 2) else: key = (kind, props.get("GroupName", ""), props.get("CustomName", "")) pieces.setdefault(key, {})[FACING_TO_ORIENT[facing]] = f"{sheet}_{n:03d}" for key, by_orient in pieces.items(): kind = key[0] if any(_blank(t) for t in by_orient.values()): continue # blank squares in the sheet prefix = {"art": "erika_art", "plants": "erika_plant", "shop_ads": "erika_ad", "vending": "erika_vending", "shelves": "erika_shelves"}[kind] role = f"{prefix}_{len(out[kind])}" if kind in ("art", "shop_ads") and {"N", "W"} <= set(by_orient): furniture[role] = {o: {"0,0": t} for o, t in by_orient.items() if o in ("N", "W")} layers[role] = "WallFurniture" elif kind in ("plants", "vending", "shelves") and len(by_orient) == 4: furniture[role] = {o: {"0,0": t} for o, t in by_orient.items()} layers[role] = "Furniture" else: continue out[kind].append(role) for sheet, door in zip(STOREFRONT_SHEETS, STOREFRONT_DOORS): if not re.search(rf"file\s*=\s*{sheet}\s*
", txt): continue doors = {"category": "doors", "tiles": {"West": f"{DOOR_SHEET}_{door:03d}", "North": f"{DOOR_SHEET}_{door + 1:03d}", "WestOpen": f"{DOOR_SHEET}_{door + 2:03d}", "NorthOpen": f"{DOOR_SHEET}_{door + 3:03d}"}} for base in STOREFRONT_DESIGNS: tiles = {"West": f"{sheet}_{base:03d}", "North": f"{sheet}_{base + 1:03d}", "NorthWest": f"{sheet}_{base + 2:03d}", "SouthEast": f"{sheet}_{base + 3:03d}", "WestWindow": f"{sheet}_{base:03d}", "NorthWindow": f"{sheet}_{base + 1:03d}", "WestDoor": f"{sheet}_004", "NorthDoor": f"{sheet}_005"} # A cut-out for every window style, or a window in the glass has # no wall behind it at all. The glass is the same either way. for n in range(1, 20): tiles[f"WestWindow{n}"] = tiles["WestWindow"] tiles[f"NorthWindow{n}"] = tiles["NorthWindow"] out["storefronts"].append([{"category": "exterior_walls", "tiles": tiles}, {"category": "interior_walls", "tiles": dict(tiles)}, doors]) for sheet, wall, idx in SHOP_SIGNS: if re.search(rf"file\s*=\s*{sheet}\s*
", txt): out["signs"][wall].append([f"{sheet}_{i:03d}" for i in idx]) return out

tile_keys
nodes.body_text: def tile_keys(e: dict) -> dict: """Just the enum -> tile-name pairs. Roof entries also carry `offset = SlopePt5S 1 1`, which is a property, not a tile. Copying it through made BuildingEd reject every building with "Unknown roof_slopes enum 'offset'". A real tile value is a single token, so anything with whitespace is not one. """ return {k: v for k, v in e.items() if k not in ("category", "offset") and v and " " not in v}

nodes.name: pick
nodes.signature: def pick(category: str, anchor: str) -> dict
nodes.body_text: def pick(category: str, anchor: str) -> dict: """The entry of `category` whose first tile value is `anchor`.""" for e in entries: if e.get("category") != category: continue out = tile_keys(e) vals = list(out.values()) if vals and vals[0] == anchor: return {"category": category, "tiles": out} raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: no {category} entry anchored at {anchor!r}. " f"The config may have changed - pick a new anchor from " f"tools/make_catalog.py.")

nodes.body_text: def bt_lookup(category: str, anchor: str) -> dict | None: """bt_entry, but nothing rather than a hard stop when it is not there.""" try: return bt_entry(category, anchor) except (SystemExit, ValueError): return None

nodes.name: with_cutouts
nodes.signature: def with_cutouts(entry: dict | None) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def with_cutouts(entry: dict | None) -> dict | None: """A wall entry that has a cut-out for every window style.""" if not entry or not entry.get("category", "").endswith("_walls"): return entry tiles = dict(entry["tiles"]) if "WestWindow1" in tiles: return entry anchor = next(iter(tiles.values()), None) full = bt_lookup(entry["category"], anchor) if anchor else None if full: tiles = dict(full["tiles"]) if "WestWindow1" in tiles: return {"category": entry["category"], "tiles": tiles} # The editor's list has no alternates for this wall either - a shop # front, or one of the sheets that carries a single opening. Every # window then opens the same one, which is wrong by a few pixels and # right by a whole wall. for side in ("West", "North"): plain = tiles.get(f"{side}Window") or tiles.get(side) if plain: for n in range(1, ALT_WINDOWS + 1): tiles[f"{side}Window{n}"] = plain return {"category": entry["category"], "tiles": tiles}

nodes.name: wall_entry
nodes.body_text: def wall_entry(anchor: str) -> dict: """An exterior wall from the templates, or the editor's full list.""" for e in entries: if e.get("category") == "exterior_walls": vals = list(tile_keys(e).values()) if vals and vals[0] == anchor: return with_cutouts({"category": "exterior_walls", "tiles": tile_keys(e)}) return with_cutouts(bt_entry("exterior_walls", anchor))

def caps_for(wall: str, fallback: str | None) -> dict | None: """The gable-end set the editor pairs with this exterior wall: each of its roof_caps entries names the wall it belongs to in CapGapE3.""" start = tiles_txt.index("name = roof_caps
") nxt = tiles_txt.find("
 name = ", start + 10) for body in re.findall(r"entry\s*\{(.*?)\}", tiles_txt[start:nxt], re.S): pairs = dict((k, v.strip()) for k, v in re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+) = ([^
]*)$", body, re.M)) if pairs.get("CapGapE3") == wall and pairs.get("CapPeak30S1"): tiles = {k: v for k, v in pairs.items() if k != "offset" and v} return {"category": "roof_caps", "tiles": tiles} return bt_entry("roof_caps", fallback) if fallback else None

nodes.signature: def curtains(anchor: str | None) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def curtains(anchor: str | None) -> dict | None: """A curtains entry from its West tile: East, North, South follow it.""" if not anchor: return None sheet, idx = anchor.rsplit("_", 1) n = int(idx) names = [f"{sheet}_{n + i:03d}" for i in range(4)] if names[0] not in tiles_txt: raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: no curtains {anchor!r} in BuildingTiles.txt.") return {"category": "curtains", "tiles": dict(zip(("West", "East", "North", "South"), names))}

nodes.body_text: def roof(slopes: str | None, top: str, peaked: bool) -> dict: """Roof materials: a slope family from the templates, and a flat-top tile used for all three depths (the templates' roofs_01_054 entry has the same tile in every slot too).""" # From BuildingTiles.txt: its slope entries carry the 30-degree # tiles as well, which the templates' copies leave out. return {"slopes": bt_entry("roof_slopes", slopes) if slopes else None, "tops": {"category": "roof_tops", "tiles": {k: top for k in ("West1", "West2", "West3", "North1", "North2", "North3")}}, "peaked": peaked}

nodes.body_text: def window(anchor: str) -> dict: if anchor not in window_pairs: raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: no window {anchor!r} in BuildingTiles.txt.") return {"category": "windows", "tiles": {"West": anchor, "North": window_pairs[anchor]}}

nodes.name: find_furniture
nodes.body_text: def find_furniture(anchor: str) -> dict: """All four facings for a piece, keyed by orientation. Keeping only W and N was a real bug: a sofa placed against the south wall with orient N has its back to the room, which is what "the props are rotated wrong" looks like in game. The source defines E and S for most pieces (1301 and 1231 entries), so take whatever is there. """ for furs in groups.values(): for f in furs: for e in f["entries"]: if e["orient"] == "W" and e["tiles"].get("0,0") == anchor: out = {} for e2 in f["entries"]: if e2["orient"] in ("W", "N", "E", "S") \ and e2["orient"] not in out: out[e2["orient"]] = e2["tiles"] if "W" in out and "N" in out: layers[anchor] = f["layer"] return out raise SystemExit(f"ERROR: furniture anchor not found: {anchor!r}")

nodes.name: make_lang_template.py
nodes.body_text: """Write lang/english.txt: every line of the window, ready to be translated. python tools/make_lang_template.py Anyone can put KnoxMap in their language without touching the code: copy lang/english.txt to lang/<their language>.txt, translate the right-hand side of each line, and pick the language at the top of the window. The name of the file is the name in the menu, so russian.txt appears as "Russian". The English side is what the window actually says, so this is generated rather than typed: the text of every element in templates/index.html, its placeholders and titles, and the messages static/js writes into the page. A line whose translation is left as the English is simply not translated, which is what an untouched template does. """ from __future__ import annotations import html as html_mod import os import re import sys ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) PAGE = os.path.join(ROOT, "templates", "index.html") SCRIPTS = (os.path.join(ROOT, "static", "js", "app.js"), os.path.join(ROOT, "static", "js", "fx.js"), os.path.join(ROOT, "static", "js", "shell.js")) OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "lang", "english.txt") HEADER = """\ # KnoxMap in your language # # Copy this file, name it after the language - russian.txt, deutsch.txt, # turkce.txt - and translate the right of each "=" only. Leave the left alone: # that is what KnoxMap says in English, and how it finds your translation. # Whatever is still in English is shown in English, so a half-finished file # works. Lines starting with # are notes and are ignored. # # Then start KnoxMap and pick the language at the top of the window. # # Written by tools/make_lang_template.py from the window itself - run it again # after a KnoxMap update to pick up anything new. """ # Text that is not worth translating: names, symbols and numbers. SKIP = {"KnoxMap", "discord", "OpenStreetMap", "Leaflet", "×", "→", "?"} # These preset validation errors come from web/presets.py rather than a page script. # They are shown in the Saved areas panel just like client-side messages. PRESET_ERRORS = ( "This is not a KnoxMap preset version 1.", "The preset needs a valid area and scale.", "The preset area or scale is outside the map's limits.", "The preset outline is not a polygon.", "The preset outline falls outside its area.", "The preset outline could not be read.", "The preset needs map settings.", ) # Runtime messages use named placeholders; the translator keeps their names. EXTRA_MESSAGES = ( 'Rotate area', 'Rotate area (drag to rotate, Shift to snap, or click to turn 45°)', 'Shape area', 'Map area', 'Cells', 'Tiles', 'Bitmap', 'MB', 'km²', 'OSM query', 'OSM queries', 'OpenStreetMap data source', 'Online queries', 'Extract / Live', 'Regional dump', 'Overpass server addresses', 'Fast', 'Default', 'Offline', 'Auto', '⚡ Overpass API — Online queries', 'Downloads the selected area from the servers below. Busy servers get a limited number of retries; downloaded parts are kept. If the servers are unreachable, choose Auto or Geofabrik.', '⚙ Auto mode', 'Reads regional Geofabrik data when pyosmium is installed. The file is downloaded once and cached. Reading reports its current stage and object count. Falls back to Overpass if the extract is unavailable.', '📦 Geofabrik — Local data', 'Downloads and caches a Geofabrik region, then selects objects for your area. Works without Overpass after the download. The first read of a large region takes time; the current stage is shown in the window.', 'Map data source set to {source}', 'Only the drawn shape is built:', '{area} km²', '(bounding box: {area} km², {columns}×{rows} cells). Outside it the land turns back to countryside, with the main roads and rivers running on.', 'reading the relations', 'reading the map data', 'reading the map data: {count} tagged nodes and ways checked', 'reading the rest of the larger areas', 'finding the OpenStreetMap extract that covers this place', 'reading the {region} extract', 'downloading the {region} extract from Geofabrik, {downloaded} of {total} MB', 'downloading the {region} extract from Geofabrik, {downloaded} MB', 'no extract ({reason}) - asking the Overpass servers instead', 'the Overpass servers are busy — waiting {seconds}s, then trying again ({attempt} of {attempts})', 'the Overpass servers did not answer — {count} of {total} tiles come from an earlier download and may be out of date', 'server is resting', 'expected Overpass JSON, received {details}', 'invalid Overpass JSON: missing elements list', 'partial answer — {details}', 'every Overpass endpoint failed — {details}', 'the Overpass servers are resting after refusing or failing to answer', 'the Overpass servers are resting after refusing or failing to answer - asking again in about {seconds}s', '"{url}" is not an http(s) server address.', 'The OpenStreetMap extract could not be used: {reason}', 'All Overpass endpoints failed: {details}', 'Lookup failed: {details}', 'no answer within {seconds}s', 'The free OpenStreetMap servers are busy or not answering right now. The public Overpass servers are shared and go busy; waiting a few minutes and generating again usually works, and a smaller area always does. {details}', ) # Anything that is code rather than words: a selector, a path, a template. CODE = re.compile(r"^[#./]|[\[\]{}<>$`|]| https?:|^\w+-\w+$") if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())

nodes.name: is_words
nodes.body_text: def is_words(text: str) -> bool: """Whether this looks like something a person reads, not code.""" if len(text) < 3 or CODE.search(text): return False if not re.search(r"[A-Za-z]{2}", text): return False # A lone lower-case word or two is a key or a class name, not a message. words = text.split() return len(words) >= 3 or text[0].isupper() or text[0].isdigit()

nodes.name: page_strings
nodes.body_text: def page_strings(path: str) -> list[str]: text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read() body = re.sub(r"<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>|<!--.*?-->", "", text, flags=re.S) found = [] for piece in re.split(r"<[^>]+>", body): piece = " ".join(html_mod.unescape(piece).split()) if "{{" not in piece and is_words(piece): found.append(piece) for attr in re.findall(r'(?:placeholder|title|aria-label)="([^"]+)"', text): attr = html_mod.unescape(attr) if "{{" not in attr and is_words(attr): found.append(attr) return found

nodes.name: script_strings
nodes.body_text: def script_strings(paths) -> list[str]: """Sentences the scripts put on the page. Only plain quoted text of a few words: enough to catch the notes, the buttons and the settings, without dragging in every css class and key. """ found = [] for path in paths: text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read() for quote in ("'", '"'): for piece in re.findall(rf"{quote}([^{quote}\\\n]{{6,1000}}){quote}", text): piece = piece.strip() if is_words(piece) and re.search(r"[A-Za-z]{2,}\s+[A-Za-z]", piece): found.append(piece) return found

nodes.body_text:
def main() -> int: strings = page_strings(PAGE) + script_strings(SCRIPTS) + list(PRESET_ERRORS) + list(EXTRA_MESSAGES) seen, lines = set(), [] for text in strings: if text in SKIP or text in seen or "=" in text: continue # "=" is the separator; skip those seen.add(text) lines.append(f"{text} = {text}") lines.sort(key=str.lower) os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True) with open(OUT, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(HEADER + "
" + "
".join(lines) + "
") print(f"wrote {OUT} with {len(lines)} lines") return 0

nodes.name: make_map_mod.py
nodes.body_text: """Package a compiled map into a Project Zomboid map mod. Run this AFTER WorldEd's Generate Lots. It collects the compiled cell data and the Lua files WorldEd wrote, and lays them out the way Build 42 map mods do: <mods>/<id>/ mod.info common/media/maps/<Map Name>/ *.lotheader *.lotpack chunkdata_*.bin map.info spawnpoints.lua objects.lua Layout and map.info fields follow an installed B42 workshop map (New Hartburg). python tools/make_map_mod.py output/mytown --name "My Town, KY" --id mytown """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import os import shutil import sys LOT_PATTERNS = (".lotheader", ".lotpack") EXTRA_FILES = ("spawnpoints.lua", "objects.lua", "roomtones.lua", "worldmap.xml", "streets.xml", "worldmap-annotations.lua") # The new-game spawn picker draws a map with no image of its own from its # paper-map data, and to do that it sizes the "visited" overlay from a world # that has not been loaded yet: IsoMetaGrid still holds its 10,000,000 and # -10,000,000 placeholders, the size comes to -127246320, and the picker # throws NegativeArraySizeException and draws nothing (WorldMapVisited, # MapSpawnSelect.lua). Knox County avoids it by shipping a picture, # spawnSelectImagePyramid.zip, which the picker shows instead. So do these: # the map's own top-down preview, cut the same way - 256-pixel tiles named # tile<column>x<row>.png, each level half the one before, down to three # tiles a side. The picker only needs an overview, so it is drawn at most # this many pixels across rather than Knox County's 158 MB. SPAWN_PICTURE_MAX_PX = 4096 PYRAMID_TILE = 256 SPAWN_SELECTOR_MAX_POIS = 80 # Paper-map label styles that name somewhere a player might want to start. SPAWN_SELECTOR_STYLES = {"text-building": "landmark", "text-place": "landmark"} KNOXMAP_URL = "https://github.com/spytheeuclidean-a11y/knoxmap" # The Workshop shows the preview square and small, and refuses a big file # (tools/workshop_check.py). The mod list shows poster.png the same way. PREVIEW_SIDE = 512 # A map of this many compiled cells or more needs more memory than Project # Zomboid gives itself by default. One player watched a big map "seize and # start to visually glitch out" before the game fell over, and found the # game's own maximum had been left at 3 GB; nothing had told them to look. BIG_MAP_CELLS = 40 # Every save, the game writes each room's and each building's state - seen, # explored, alarmed, lights on - into map_meta.bin through one 10 MB buffer # that never grows (SliceY.SliceBuffer, IsoMetaGrid.savePart): 8 bytes a # cell, 10 a room, 23 a building. Hamburg's 1.6 million rooms came to 21 MB, # and every save and hot-save threw BufferOverflowException and wrote # nothing. Knox County itself is 1.2 MB, which a map that is not standalone # shares the buffer with. The budget leaves room for what else goes in. SAVE_BUFFER = 10_485_760 META_BUDGET = 9_000_000 META_CELL, META_ROOM, META_BUILDING = 8, 10, 23 KNOX_COUNTY_META = 1_160_348 if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())

nodes.name: worlds_already_made
nodes.body_text: def worlds_already_made() -> list[str]: """Saves that exist on this PC, newest first. A world is written to disk cell by cell as players walk into it, built from whatever map was loaded at the time, so a map added or changed afterwards leaves old cells beside new ones that do not match. There is no repair; the answer is a new world. Worth saying at the moment the map is installed, while there is still a choice about which save to start. """ try: root = knoxpaths_module().zomboid_user_dir() / "Saves" if not root.is_dir(): return [] found = [(save.stat().st_mtime, f"{mode.name}/{save.name}") for mode in root.iterdir() if mode.is_dir() for save in mode.iterdir() if save.is_dir()] except OSError: return [] return [name for _when, name in sorted(found, reverse=True)]

nodes.name: collect
nodes.signature: def collect(project_dir: str, lots_dir: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]
nodes.body_text: def collect(project_dir: str, lots_dir: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]: """Compiled cell files, and the loose Lua/XML files WorldEd wrote.""" cells = [] if os.path.isdir(lots_dir): for f in sorted(os.listdir(lots_dir)): if f.endswith(LOT_PATTERNS) or f.startswith("chunkdata"): cells.append(os.path.join(lots_dir, f)) extras = [] for folder in (lots_dir, project_dir): if not os.path.isdir(folder): continue for name in EXTRA_FILES: p = os.path.join(folder, name) if os.path.exists(p) and not any( os.path.basename(e) == name for e in extras): extras.append(p) return cells, extras

nodes.name: _world_origin_tiles
nodes.body_text: def _world_origin_tiles(project_dir: str) -> tuple[int, int]: """The map's world origin in tiles, read back from the .pzw it came from.""" import re for entry in os.listdir(project_dir): if not entry.endswith(".pzw"): continue with open(os.path.join(project_dir, entry), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: text = f.read() m = re.search(r'<worldOrigin origin="(-?\d+),(-?\d+)"', text) if m: return int(m.group(1)) * 300, int(m.group(2)) * 300 return 0, 0

nodes.name: _spawn_tiles
nodes.signature: def _spawn_tiles(project_dir: str, limit: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]
nodes.body_text: def _spawn_tiles(project_dir: str, limit: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """Map tiles to start on: inside homes, as far apart as the town allows. These used to be the middle of each building's bounding box, taken from every n-th row of the placements file. For an L-shaped or turned building that middle is often outside it - a start in the yard or inside a wall - and the rows are in file order, so the picks could bunch up in one street or land in a church. Now they come from the real footprints: homes first, each pick the building furthest from those already chosen, and within it a tile with floor on every side, away from the walls the furniture lines. """ import numpy as np sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) from knoxbuild.population import load_footprints saved = [os.path.join(project_dir, e) for e in os.listdir(project_dir) if e.endswith("_footprints.npz")] if not saved: return [] buildings = load_footprints(saved[0]) homes = [b for b in buildings if b[4] in ("house", "apartment")] pool = homes or [b for b in buildings if b[4] != "shed"] or buildings if not pool: return [] def inner_tile(x0, y0, mask): # Tiles whose eight neighbours are all floor, nearest the middle. m = mask.astype(bool) core = m.copy() core[1:, :] &= m[:-1, :] core[:-1, :] &= m[1:, :] core[:, 1:] &= m[:, :-1] core[:, :-1] &= m[:, 1:] core[1:, 1:] &= m[:-1, :-1] core[:-1, :-1] &= m[1:, 1:] core[1:, :-1] &= m[:-1, 1:] core[:-1, 1:] &= m[1:, :-1] ys, xs = np.nonzero(core if core.any() else m) if len(xs) == 0: return None cy, cx = ys.mean(), xs.mean() i = int(np.argmin((xs - cx) ** 2 + (ys - cy) ** 2)) return x0 + int(xs[i]), y0 + int(ys[i]) spots = [s for s in (inner_tile(x0, y0, m) for x0, y0, m, _l, _k in pool) if s] if not spots: return [] arr = np.array(spots, dtype=float) centre = arr.mean(axis=0) chosen = [int(np.argmin(((arr - centre) ** 2).sum(axis=1)))] nearest = ((arr - arr[chosen[0]]) ** 2).sum(axis=1) while len(chosen) < min(limit, len(spots)): nxt = int(np.argmax(nearest)) if nearest[nxt] == 0: break chosen.append(nxt) nearest = np.minimum(nearest, ((arr - arr[nxt]) ** 2).sum(axis=1)) return [spots[i] for i in chosen]

nodes.name: inner_tile
nodes.signature: def inner_tile(x0, y0, mask): # Tiles whose eight neighbours are all floor, nearest the middle.
nodes.body_text: def inner_tile(x0, y0, mask): # Tiles whose eight neighbours are all floor, nearest the middle. m = mask.astype(bool) core = m.copy() core[1:, :] &= m[:-1, :] core[:-1, :] &= m[1:, :] core[:, 1:] &= m[:, :-1] core[:, :-1] &= m[:, 1:] core[1:, 1:] &= m[:-1, :-1] core[:-1, :-1] &= m[1:, 1:] core[1:, :-1] &= m[:-1, 1:] core[:-1, 1:] &= m[1:, :-1] ys, xs = np.nonzero(core if core.any() else m) if len(xs) == 0: return None cy, cx = ys.mean(), xs.mean() i = int(np.argmin((xs - cx) ** 2 + (ys - cy) ** 2)) return x0 + int(xs[i]), y0 + int(ys[i])

nodes.name: write_reset_loot
nodes.body_text: def write_reset_loot(mod_root: str) -> bool: """Ship the "Reset loot" right-click menu with the map. The game fills a container once and remembers it, so a map installed again keeps the loot it rolled the first time and the only cure used to be a new save. knoxbuild/lua/resetloot.lua puts it back, building by building. Every KnoxMap map carries the same file and the first one loaded claims it. """ source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "knoxbuild", "lua", "resetloot.lua") if not os.path.exists(source): return False lua_dir = os.path.join(mod_root, "common", "media", "lua", "client", "KnoxMap") os.makedirs(lua_dir, exist_ok=True) shutil.copy2(source, os.path.join(lua_dir, "KnoxMapResetLoot.lua")) return True

nodes.name: write_gun_cache
nodes.signature: def write_gun_cache(project_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str) -> dict | None
nodes.body_text: def write_gun_cache(project_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str) -> dict | None: """Ship the map's one guaranteed military rifle. knoxbuild/guns.py picked the building while the map was built and left <name>_guncache.json beside it. Two files go out: the handler, which every KnoxMap map carries and the first one loaded claims, and this map's own file registering its building's box. Either may load first - both create the table if it is not there yet - so no load order has to be arranged. """ import json as _json import re as _re found = None for entry in sorted(os.listdir(project_dir)): if entry.endswith("_guncache.json"): found = os.path.join(project_dir, entry) break if not found: return None try: with open(found, encoding="utf-8") as f: box = _json.load(f) except (OSError, ValueError): return None handler = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "knoxbuild", "lua", "guncache.lua") if not os.path.exists(handler): return None lua_dir = os.path.join(mod_root, "common", "media", "lua", "server", "KnoxMap") os.makedirs(lua_dir, exist_ok=True) shutil.copy2(handler, os.path.join(lua_dir, "KnoxMapGunCache.lua")) items = ", ".join(_lua_string(i) for i in box.get("items") or []) safe_id = _re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", mod_id) or "map" lines = [ "-- This map's box, for KnoxMapGunCache.lua. Generated by KnoxMap.", "-- " + " ".join(f"{box.get('kind', '?')}: " f"{box.get('name') or box.get('building', '')}".split()), "KnoxMapGunCache = KnoxMapGunCache or { boxes = {} }", "table.insert(KnoxMapGunCache.boxes, {", f" id = {_lua_string(mod_id)},", f" kind = {_lua_string(str(box.get('kind') or ''))},", f" x = {int(box['x'])}, y = {int(box['y'])},", f" w = {int(box['w'])}, h = {int(box['h'])},", f" items = {{ {items} }},", "})", "", ] with open(os.path.join(lua_dir, f"KnoxMapGunCache_{safe_id}.lua"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n".join(lines)) return box

nodes.name: _lua_string
nodes.body_text: def _lua_string(value: str) -> str: """A Lua string literal. Map names carry apostrophes and backslashes.""" return '"' + str(value).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'

nodes.name: write_spawn_selector
nodes.signature: def write_spawn_selector(project_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str, name: str) -> int
nodes.body_text: def write_spawn_selector(project_dir: str, mod_root: str, mod_id: str, name: str) -> int: """Put this map into Spawn Selector, if the player has that mod. Spawn Selector (workshop 3772052709) lets a new character pick a starting spot on the world map, but its regions and points of interest are a fixed list for Knox County, so a generated town elsewhere in the world could not be picked. This adds a Lua file that, only when Spawn Selector is loaded, adds the map's area to its random-start regions and its named buildings and places - the same ones labelled on the paper map - to its points of interest. Without the mod the file does nothing, so it adds no dependency. The tables are filled at OnGameBoot, after every mod's Lua has run: Spawn Selector assigns its lists outright, so adding to them any earlier could be wiped out by load order. Returns how many points were added. """ import json as _json import re as _re annotations = os.path.join(project_dir, "worldmap-annotations.lua") pois, town = [], name if os.path.exists(annotations): with open(annotations, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: text = f.read() found = _re.findall(r'addUntranslatedText\("((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)", "([a-z-]+)", ' r'(-?[\d.]+), (-?[\d.]+)\)', text) for label, style, x, y in found: label = label.replace('\\"', '"').replace("\\\\", "\\") if style == "text-town": town = label elif style in SPAWN_SELECTOR_STYLES and len(pois) < SPAWN_SELECTOR_MAX_POIS: pois.append((label, SPAWN_SELECTOR_STYLES[style], float(x), float(y))) width = height = 0 for entry in os.listdir(project_dir): if entry.endswith("_info.json"): with open(os.path.join(project_dir, entry), encoding="utf-8") as f: meta = _json.load(f) width, height = meta.get("width_tiles", 0), meta.get("height_tiles", 0) if not width or not height: return 0 ox, oy = _world_origin_tiles(project_dir) def lua_str(s: str) -> str: return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", " ") + '"' entries = "\n".join( f' {{ type = "custom_poi", group = {lua_str(group)}, name = {lua_str(label)}, ' f'location = {lua_str(town)}, x = {x:.1f}, y = {y:.1f}, z = 0, placement = "building" }},' for label, group, x, y in pois) guard = _re.sub(r"\W", "_", mod_id) lua = f"""-- Written by KnoxMap for {name}. -- Adds this map to Spawn Selector (Steam workshop 3772052709) when it is -- installed. Does nothing otherwise. local function addToSpawnSelector() if not (SpawnSelector and SpawnSelector.RANDOM_REGIONS and SpawnSelectorPOIs and SpawnSelectorPOIs.entries) then return end if SpawnSelector.KnoxMapAdded_{guard} then return end SpawnSelector.KnoxMapAdded_{guard} = true table.insert(SpawnSelector.RANDOM_REGIONS, {{ minX = {ox}, minY = {oy}, maxX = {ox + width - 1}, maxY = {oy + height - 1} }}) local pois = {{ {entries} }} for _, poi in ipairs(pois) do table.insert(SpawnSelectorPOIs.entries, poi) end end Events.OnGameBoot.Add(addToSpawnSelector) """ folder = os.path.join(mod_root, "common", "media", "lua", "shared", "KnoxMap") os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True) with open(os.path.join(folder, f"{guard}_SpawnSelector.lua"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(lua) return len(pois)
